Canic Code Review
Code review · 29 September 2026

Canic Code Review

Single-operation journalling is careful, but one critical and 44 high findings, many of them durable states that routine events wedge permanently, keep Canic from being ready for production Fleets.
Commit 06d73694d · v0.110.469 crates · ~585k lines of Rust49 review areas · 319 agents28 findings retested with failing tests

Verdict

Canic is careful at the level of a single operation. Root capability handlers mark replay receipts ExternalEffectInFlight before any effectful await, fleet ensure persists each Intent before it observes or issues an effect, and the backup and restore runners claim each step Pending before it runs. The management-canister and ledger adapters in canic-core use unbounded wait. Ledger effects are deduplicated with a fixed created_at_time, plus a memo on the canister paths, and adopt Duplicate replies. Root accepts a Coordinator grant in one message with no await and replays with zero cycles. Registry, Coordinator and funding state commit by compare-and-swap against the exact prior record, and Component Registry transitions contain no await. The delegated-auth chain fails closed, no reviewer found a way to forge a token, and every Root, Store and Coordinator command variant is authorized before any effect. A survey of about 1,500 panic, cast and arithmetic sites found no caller-reachable overflow or panic on paths that move cycles or ICP, configuration parsing stays out of canister Wasm, and a CI script enforces the pre-1.0 hard cut.

The critical defect is in the cost guard. It builds a new quota key for every 60-second window and writes it into the durable committed-totals map, which never reclaims a committed row and caps identities at 1,000. A test with one legitimate reserve per window failed at window 999 with CAPACITY_LIMIT. Each later window is a new key, so every later cost-guarded reserve fails the same way, and the finding traces how child funding, Component provisioning and ICP refill on Root then fail for good. Among the other reproduced defects, a caller with no template made five calls, drove five batch signatures of another issuer's batches, each a paid threshold-ECDSA signature in production, and got no proof. Most of the rest leave durable state stuck after a routine event. Registry records crossed the 4,096-byte Storable bound after the paid creation effect and trapped again on retry. A second recycle of one pool asset under one Component left it stuck in Recycling. When a Root opened a funding request during a funding-policy rotation, the rotation fence and the Root's pending request blocked each other on both sides. A fleet ensure plan applied 48 hours after review wedged in its InProgress journal, and a completed clean reinstall captured every later ensure. In backup and restore, prune deleted a directory holding an in-flight restore journal, restore loaded a partial upload as complete, and a retried backup combined snapshots from two stop windows in one crash-consistent unit.

After merging 67 duplicates and dropping 8 refuted findings, 401 remain, of which 1 is critical, 44 high, 105 medium, 220 low and 31 info. The 44 high findings share a few mechanisms. The most common is a journal that freezes evidence and later requires live state to match it exactly. Conservation checks compare balances frozen at intent time with balances that anyone can raise through deposit_cycles or icrc1_transfer and that idle burn or Root's own pool creation lowers. Operations bind a whole Registry version or hash, so an admission change or another root's removal invalidates them, and in multi-root Fleets nothing resyncs a lagging mirror. Ledger timestamps, ingress expiry and certified block windows lapse while a host journal waits. Many of these states have no abort, successor or operator-clear transition, so recovery usually means reinstalling a Root or the Fleet, or deleting journal files the docs forbid touching. A second group concerns background work. Retry classifiers treat every transport reject as permanent. Lifecycle timer chains are neither deduplicated nor bounded below the 64-entry ic-timers registry, and a full registry makes registration trap. A trap after an await leaves a Running entry that nothing re-arms. A third group burns or strands cycles or ICP through bounded-wait value transfers, reconcile paths that record a rejection after cycles may have moved, a Root deletion that never evacuates its ICP account, and a clean reinstall that does not check that the seed covers every Root-controlled canister.

Of the 28 review findings retested with focused tests, 16 reproduced in full, 11 partially and 1 could not be tested natively, and none was disproved. Most partial results stop at the same place, because timer loops, inter-canister awaits, Ledger replies and the ic-timers registry do not run natively. One reproduction had to vendor ic-timers 0.8.0 to reach its test platform, and the downstream wedges still need PocketIC tests. The same pass found that canic-host, and so the canic CLI, does not compile on macOS, since durable_io passes a u32 mode where rustix expects the platform's u16 mode_t. Every CI job runs on ubuntu-24.04, so nothing caught it. CI does run PocketIC lanes, but the governed lane executes only registered cases, so unregistered tests never run and a renamed suite would pass with zero tests. Reviewers also report that the MSRV job never checks wasm32 and that no lane runs doctests. cargo audit over 567 crates found no vulnerabilities and no yanked crates, and warned only that paste (a compile-time proc-macro through candid) and serde_cbor (host-side through ic-agent) are unmaintained.

Reproduced with tests

Static findings were re-tested by writing focused tests in isolated worktrees and running them against the current code. A test was written to assert the correct behaviour, so a failing test confirms the bug.

FindingOutcomeEvidence
canic-host, and therefore the canic CLI, does not compile on macOS: durable_io passes a u32 file mode where rustix expects the platform mode_t, which is u16 on Darwin
reproduced
cargo test -p canic-host --lib --no-run (unmodified 06d73694d, macOS)
On the unmodified commit, building canic-host on macOS fails with the type error below. With the one-line cast applied, canic-host, canic-cli and canic compile, and every host and CLI reproduction in this review ran with it.
Committed resource totals are never reclaimed while cost-guard quota keys are per-60-second bucket, so the 1,000-identity cap permanently blocks every cost-guarded operation on root after about 1,000 active quota minutes
reproduced
crates/canic-core/src/ops/cost_guard.rs::ops::cost_guard::tests::repro_quota_buckets_exhaust_totals_cap
The test lives in the existing cost_guard tests module and calls the production CostGuardOps::reserve and CostGuardOps::complete. It uses the module's `request()` helper: 60 s window, max 1 operation per window, with the cycle balance raised to 1000. It runs one ordinary reserve+complete in each of 1,100 separate 60-second windows (now = window*60+10) and asserts that every reserve succeeds. Each window's reserve is legitimate: it uses a new quota bucket key, so enforce_quota sees used = 0. Result: windows 0 to 998 succeed. The reserve in window 999 fails with CostGuardReserveError::Store(InternalError E81). E81 is CAPACITY_LIMIT. At that point IntentStore::totals_len() is 1000 (999 committed quota-bucket rows plus the one shared cycle-reservation row) and pending_total is 0. Because the error is the Store variant and not the QuotaExceeded variant, it comes from IntentStoreOps::try_reserve -> ensure_resource_total_admission (ResourceTotalRecordCapacityReached), not from the quota check. This confirms the core claim. Committed rows for past quota buckets are never reclaimed, and after about 1,000 active windows every new-window cost-guarded reserve is rejected. Every later window is also a new key, so the block is permanent. The test did not exercise the downstream effects the finding describes (child top-up stopping, other root workflows blocked). Those follow from the same rejection but would need workflow- or PocketIC-level tests.
`canic backup prune` deletes backup directories that hold an unfinished restore apply journal and staged artifacts, stranding an in-flight production restore.
reproduced
crates/canic-cli/src/backup/tests/prune.rs::repro_prune_preserves_backup_with_unfinished_restore_journal
The test builds a backup root with two Complete layouts using the existing prune fixtures: a newer backup-newest and an older backup-restoring. The older one has a restore-ready manifest and a real artifact whose checksum matches. It then runs the production `canic restore prepare --backup-dir <older> --require-restore-ready` through crate::restore::run. By default that writes restore-plan.json and restore-apply-journal.json into the backup directory itself. Next the test uses the production journal API (mark_next_operation_pending_at, write_restore_apply_journal) to move the restore journal to an in-flight state with 1 of 5 operations pending. That is the state an interrupted or paused `restore run --execute --max-steps 1` leaves behind. Finally it calls backup_prune with keep=1 and dry_run=false, and asserts that the directory and the journal still exist. The test fails. backup_list still shows the restoring layout as Complete, because status ignores the restore files. Prune selects it, calls remove_dir_all, and reports it as Removed. Afterwards the directory and restore-apply-journal.json are both gone. This confirms the finding's core claim in full: prune deletes a backup directory that holds a non-terminal restore apply journal. It checks no lock and no restore state. The test does not exercise the downstream consequences, stopped canisters and a later PreparedJournalMissing from `restore run`, but they follow directly once the journal file no longer exists.
Upload reconciliation adopts any single new snapshot as the completed upload, so a partially uploaded snapshot left by a failed or interrupted upload is recorded as done and later loaded.
reproduced
crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/tests.rs::repro_failed_upload_retry_adopts_partial_snapshot
The test builds a two-operation restore journal (UploadSnapshot seq 0, then LoadSnapshot seq 1) with a real staged artifact. The backup root is canonicalized because macOS temp_dir sits under the /var symlink, which the stager rejects. It uses a fake executor, PartialUploadExecutor. Run 1 goes through restore_run_execute_result_with_executor. The inventory is empty, and the upload command exits 1 after adding "partial-upload" to the target inventory, which models a metadata-phase ID with failed data chunks. The op becomes Failed and keeps snapshot_ids_before=[]. Next the test calls the production restore_run_retry_failed, which moves the op back to Ready and still keeps the baseline. Run 2: reconcile_upload_operation sees the single inventory delta and records "partial-upload" as the uploaded ID. The upload command is never re-executed. The runner then issues `canister snapshot restore <target> partial-upload` and reports the restore complete. The test asserts that the partial snapshot is not recorded as the upload, and that assertion fails. So the runner-side claim holds in full: after a failed upload, a partial snapshot is recorded as done and later loaded. The existing test execute_preserves_pending_operation_while_command_is_in_flight already asserts the same adoption for the interrupted Pending path. What the IC does when it loads an incomplete snapshot (reject, or zero-filled memory) cannot be exercised natively. The finding presents that part as conditional anyway.
A backup retried after failure containment mixes two stop windows: snapshots taken before containment restarted the fleet are kept while the remaining members are snapshotted in a later window.
reproduced
crates/canic-backup/src/runner/tests.rs::repro_retry_after_containment_mixes_stop_windows
The test builds a real Subtree plan: APP is the selected parent and WORKER is its child. It runs backup_run_execute_with_executor through a wrapper around the existing FakeBackupRunnerExecutor. The wrapper counts stop windows (one per stop of APP), gives each snapshot the id of the window it was taken in, and fails CreateSnapshot only for WORKER. First run: APP is snapshotted in window 1, WORKER's snapshot fails, and containment restarts both canisters. Afterwards snapshot-APP stays Completed and only the Stop/Start rows go back to Ready. Retry (same layout, failure removed): both canisters are stopped again, but only WORKER is snapshotted, and the next step downloads APP's window-1 snapshot. The test then builds the manifest with build_manifest_for_test from the resulting download journal. It shows one backup unit of kind Subtree, pairing APP from window 1 with WORKER from window 2. The assertion that all members of the unit come from one stop window fails. Setup caveat: the retry stops after 6 steps (max_steps) and marks the artifacts Durable in memory. On macOS, VerifyArtifact fails with a checksum IO error (ENOTDIR) in every runner test, including the existing runner_records_failed_operation_and_retries_from_that_operation. That macOS error is unrelated to this finding. The snapshot ids never change during download or verify. The finding's claim holds in full.
GetOrCreateDelegationProof forces a new paid threshold-ECDSA batch signature on every call from any active Component that is not in the in-flight batch, whenever any template is due
reproduced
crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegation/chain_key_batch/tests.rs::repro_non_member_get_or_create_forces_paid_signature_for_other_issuers
The test sets up issuer B (p(200)) with a root issuer policy and an enabled renewal template, and no renewal state, which is the situation when B's installs keep failing. Caller C (p(201)) has no template. The test calls the existing helper prepare_sign_and_find_test_issuer_proof five times with required_issuer_pid = C at increasing now_ns. That helper runs the same ops sequence as the workflow's get_or_create_chain_key_delegation_proof_for_issuer_root: plan, commit, then sign_chain_key_root_delegation_batch, then signed_chain_key_delegation_proof_for_issuer. Signing goes through a counting DynamicMockSigner. After each call the test records an install failure (CallFailed) for B on every Signed batch. It asserts that C gets zero signer calls and zero new batches. Result: each call made one signer call (the paid sign_with_ecdsa in production), for 5 in total. Five distinct B-only batches were committed and signed, and the proof epoch went from 0 to 14. Every call still returned no proof for C, which is auth_proof_pending in production. The recorded install failures did not stop B's template from being due. So the core claim holds: a caller with no template can drive repeated paid signatures of other issuers' batches. Not exercised: the root endpoint gate, the real management-canister cycle cost, and the 128-pending cap. The test also shows distinct batch ids per call, which matches the verifier's correction of the duplicate-id claim.
Funding-policy rotation holds an irrevocable Fleet-wide fence that deadlocks with a Root's unresolved local funding request, freezing all funding and all Registry commits
reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/tests.rs::repro_rotation_fence_blocks_exact_root_funding_replay (plus ::repro_rotation_fence_deadlocks_root_with_unresolved_request)
Both tests reuse the existing fixtures (activate_two_roots, funding_rotation_plan, root_funding_request) and call the production ops directly. Test 1 (lost response): a Root is granted through prepare_root_funding and record_root_funding_acceptance. Before any rotation, replaying the exact request returns Current(Granted). With the correct predecessor usage in the plan, begin_funding_policy_rotation succeeds, because the Coordinator holds no `current` for that Root. After that, the same exact replay returns Err(STATE_CONFLICT, E132) instead of Current(Granted). This matches the claim: the rotation_current fence at root_funding.rs:98 runs before the replay checks for `current` and `last`. The store is left unchanged. Test 2 (second trigger, both sides): the Root's own RootFundingStore opens a request with RootFundingOps::prepare_request after Begin. The Coordinator returns conflict. After stage and apply, funding_policy_rotation_step asks for PrepareRoot(R), and RootFundingOps::prepare_policy_rotation also returns conflict. The Root keeps its request, and its retry to the Coordinator conflicts again. As a control, clearing only the Root's local `current` makes PrepareRoot return Ok, so the unresolved request is the only obstacle. The test asserts that at least one side can make progress, and it fails. Not exercised: the 1 s timer retry loop, the missing abort command, and fencing of Registry commits. These follow from the code structure. The deadlock itself is shown natively on both sides.
Root reservation and draining are allowed during an active fresh-install or scale-out, which permanently wedges that operation's service publication
reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/tests.rs::repro_spare_root_draining_during_scale_out_must_not_wedge_service_publication
The test activates three roots with the scale-out config and drives a fresh install through the existing helpers to RuntimesActivated, with one placement on R0 and empty batches on R1 and R2. It then prepares a scale-out on R1 whose confirmation roots are {R0, R1}, and drives it to ComponentsProvisioned at Registry revision 6. R2 is a spare Active root outside every batch, confirmation root, placement and service. The admission-idle check passes. prepare_root_draining_reservation(R2) is accepted, and publish_root_draining moves the Registry from revision 6 to 7. After that, publish_component_provisioning_services returns STATE_CONFLICT (E132) on every retry, and the scale-out stays in ComponentsProvisioned. As a control, the saved pre-removal state publishes to ServiceTopologyPublished, so the draining revision is the cause. While the operation is stuck, starting an admission transition and preparing another scale-out both return E132. The test asserts that either the fence rejects the removal or publication still succeeds; it fails on the publication assertion. This confirms the verifier-corrected scale-out case, including the blocked admission and the blocked follow-up scale-out. Not exercised: the fresh-install variant, which the verifier says is narrow or unreachable after acceptance; the Root side accepting R2's draining (the Root's draining response is synthesized); and the real 1s timer retry loop.
Recycling completion is idempotent on component ID only, so a second recycle of the same asset under the same component silently does nothing and leaves the asset stuck in Recycling forever
reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/mod.rs::ops::canister_pool::tests::repro_second_recycle_same_component_settles_to_ready
The test sets up one imported Ready asset A (100 cycles) and one Component C. It then runs the production ops sequence that the workflow drives twice, with child operations 0x11 and 0x22: claim_smallest_sufficient_ready, finalize_claim, register_recycled_pending, mark_ready, validate_complete_recycling, complete_recycling. The first cycle settles A to Ready with last_recycle=C/0x11. The second cycle reclaims the same asset, because it is the only Ready one. validate_complete_recycling returns Ok, but complete_recycling returns early at recycling_completion's component-only last_recycle check. A stays Recycling{claim: C/0x22, reset: Ready}, and last_recycle is still C/0x11. After that, ready_count is 0, response.recycling is 1 and non_store_asset_count is 1. Recovery probes both fail with public code E132, which the code path makes the conflict error: retry_reset falls to its conflict arm and begin_handoff needs Ready or Failed. The assertion that the second recycle settles to Ready fails for exactly the claimed reason. The core defect and the stuck, unrecoverable pool row are confirmed natively. The downstream finalize_inventory stall is a workflow consequence that I did not exercise; it follows from non_store_asset_count staying at 1.
Record growth is never checked against the 4096-byte Storable bound, so install or commit can trap after the paid creation effect and permanently wedge the allocation
reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/tests/repro_record_bound/mod.rs::repro_child_record_growth_traps_after_paid_creation (also ::repro_child_record_trap_is_deterministic_and_wedges_retirement and ::repro_top_level_record_growth_traps_after_paid_creation)
The fixture is the same single active partition used by child_reservation_is_parent_indexed_idempotent_and_capacity_bounded. The child test runs the real ops lifecycle: reserve, validate_creation, begin_creation, mark_created, validate_install, begin_install, installed, verified, commit, directory_prepared, runtime_activated and membership. It uses 5 pseudo-random chunk hashes and init args of 0 to 1536 bytes, runs each step under catch_unwind, and prints the stored value size after each step. It asserts that a step either finishes or returns a typed error at an admission check, and never traps. Every admission check passed, and every step after begin_creation (the paid creation effect) then trapped at the ic-stable-structures bound assert (storable.rs:63): membership at 512B of init args, commit at 768B, begin_install at 1024B and above. The wedge test starts from the 768B case. Retrying commit traps again with the same record size. The allocation stays Verified with reserved_descendants=1, and begin_component_draining returns unavailable (E140). The top-level test uses prepared_created_allocation: 32 chunks trap at activate_membership and 48 chunks trap at begin_install, both after the creation effect. So the finding holds in full: no ops path checks the 4096-byte value bound, the trap is deterministic, and the Component can no longer retire. The only difference from the finding is which phase traps first, which depends on size, as the verifier noted.
An approved capacity import has no abort path, and its 2-attempt per-step budgets are spent before local prechecks, so ordinary transient failures permanently wedge Root and the host Fleet.
reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/capacity_import/repro_tests.rs::repro_step_budget_not_spent_by_failed_free_precheck
The test runs the production workflow finish_root (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs) against a real ic-agent Agent. The Agent points at an in-process fake replica, and query-signature verification is off. The fake Root answers the PoolImport status query (source AwaitingHandoff, phase Reserved) and the PoolImportContext query. The Coordinator registry query returns HTTP 500. The journal is built with the existing ops helpers: bound, approved, Root-reserved, and custody-ready. Each finish_root call charges the "0:controllers" submission allowance first. It then calls advance_root, root_command and verify_destination, and fails with CoordinatorUnavailable before any update is sent. The fake replica recorded 0 /call requests. Results: - Attempts 1 and 2 persisted submissions of 1 and then 2. - Attempt 3 returned BudgetExhausted{step:"0:controllers"}. That fails the assertion that an allowance must not be spent when no update was submitted. - After exhaustion, staging a fresh review returned Conflict, because the approved journal was not released. This confirms the host is wedged. Not exercised natively: - The slow-stop path, where Root returns Unavailable and then Conflict. That needs PocketIC. - Root's allocation fence. - The lock_operation refusal. - The absence of an abort command, which I checked only by reading the code (PoolImportCommand has no abort variant). The core claim holds: the allowance is charged before free prechecks, so two failures that never reach Root permanently exhaust the step. The same pattern appears in reserve and release.
Any credit to a source or the destination Root is treated as a conservation failure, so a permissionless deposit_cycles can block approval or permanently stall a reserved import.
reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/capacity_import/publication/tests.rs::repro_third_party_credit_is_not_a_conservation_failure
The test reuses the existing publication fixture, which is a bound, operation-carrying journal on disk, and drives production code in three places. (1) It calls retained_source_debit with the source's reviewed balance plus a 500-cycle deposit. (2) It calls admit_handoffs with the destination Root's controlled_cycles raised by 500. (3) It follows the handoff workflow's own inspection spending: one inspection for the approval sample, then approve and reserve, one inspection for the intent sample, then prepare_handoff and issue_handoff. It then plays the workflow's Completed branch (reserve_inspection followed by observe_handoff) against a post-handoff sample whose controllers are already transitional, whose version is +1, and whose balance includes a 500-cycle third-party deposit. It asserts that a credit counts as zero debit, that approval is admitted, and that the handoff is recorded as Applied. All three checks fail as the finding claims. retained_source_debit returns ConservationUnproven. admit_handoffs returns InvalidCycleBounds. Both observe_handoff attempts fail with ConservationUnproven, and the third reserve_inspection fails with BudgetExhausted. So the handoff that was already executed can never be recorded, because the 4-inspection budget cannot be reset. The host-side claim holds in full. The Root-side reserve_call rejection was not run by this test. The existing control-plane test capacity_import_root_paid_attempts_survive_replay_without_budget_rebase already asserts that reserve_paid_call(identity(), 1, 10_001) errors, which corroborates it. The "no abort path" part of the permanence claim was not tested separately.
Ledger effects reuse the review-time created_at_time, and the InProgress journal is written first, so applying a plan more than 24h after review (or resuming a lost Ledger reply after the window) permanently wedges the operation
reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/tests.rs::repro_stale_review_time_ledger_effects_wedge_operation
The test uses the existing fleet_ensure fixture() and MockPlatform, with a Create for "created" and Funds for "app" and "replaced". It calls production workflow::plan with planned_at_time set to wall-clock now minus 48h. It then models the Cycles Ledger's TooOld rule in the mock: every Ledger action whose created_at_time is more than 24h old gets stall_before_mutation(u32::MAX), so it errors every time without executing. Then it calls production workflow::apply, applies again, re-plans with a fresh clock, and calls plan_reinstall. What happened: apply ran no plan-age check. It wrote the InProgress journal and sent one Ledger request carrying the timestamp from 48h earlier. That request was rejected, and the only effect was stalled_observations=1. The second apply returned Stalled, and the journal stayed InProgress. Planning with the fresh clock returned the same plan digest with the same frozen created_at_time values. plan_reinstall returned RetainedOperationRecoveryRequired. No real mutation ever happened, so the operation is wedged with no supported exit. The test asserts the correct behaviour: a stale plan must not reach InProgress, no out-of-window Ledger request may be sent, and fresh planning must give in-window timestamps. It fails on the first of these. The main claim holds in full. Two caveats: the Ledger's TooOld reply is simulated by the mock, because a real Ledger is not available natively, and the lost-reply-after-24h variant was not exercised.
Retirement Transfer requires an exact treasury credit with no allowance for the treasury's own burn, so routine idle charges turn a conserved drain into a permanent UnbalancedTransfer
reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs::repro_treasury_idle_burn_after_drain_is_conserved (plus companion repro_treasury_idle_burn_before_drain_stays_pending)
Both tests reuse the existing ProtocolOwnersFixture in the platform tests module, which runs a fake `icp` script that serves per-canister status JSON. Each test registers a "treasury" principal and gives the source "coordinator" 20T and the treasury 50T. It builds a Transfer of 10T with a source burn bound of 1M, then calls the production prepare_effect, which records the intent baseline pre=20T and destination_pre=50T. After that it calls the real IcpEnsurePlatform::observe_effect. (1) Before the drain, the treasury pays a 20k idle charge and the source is untouched. The correct result would be Pending, but observe_effect returns Err(InvalidTransferBalance). This happens because destination_after < destination_before hits BalanceMovedInInvalidDirection. (2) After an exactly conserved drain, the source is debited 10T+1M, which is inside its allowance, and the treasury is credited 10T-20k. The correct result would be applied, but observe_effect returns Err(UnbalancedTransfer), because the destination credit must equal the amount exactly. This confirms that the destination side has no burn allowance and that the frozen intent baseline is what gets compared. I checked the resume claim by reading the code only; no test exercises it. merge_observed_cycles updates only the post fields, and the pre-apply observe_effect in the workflow (mod.rs:1531-1540) uses the same record. So re-observing would give the same error every time, and the core claim holds.
After a clean reinstall completes, clean-reinstall.json keeps capturing all later Ensure invocations, so a changed desired can never be applied and --reinstall no longer starts a new reset
reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/tests.rs::repro_completed_clean_reinstall_does_not_capture_later_ordinary_ensure
The test reuses the MockPlatform fixture from the existing fresh_logical_controller test. It models a finished clean reset: ops::clean_reinstall::bind freezes the reset desired in clean-reinstall.json, then workflow::plan/apply converge phase 3 under a stand-in convergence digest. That run is terminal. Before any new plan exists, selected(review) is false, as the finding says. The operator then adds a canister and runs the ordinary workflow::plan with a new desired hash, which writes plan X (1 create). Next the test checks the routing the CLI's run_if_selected would do, with the platform bound to the changed desired (as the CLI does). The review, --apply and --reinstall calls all route to the clean reinstall. With --reinstall, retained_desired returns the frozen reset desired. clean_reinstall::review returns the never-applied plan X with terminal=true. clean_reinstall::apply(X) fails with DriftedBeforeApply and applies nothing. As a control on the same state, ordinary workflow::apply(X, changed desired) returns Ok(true), so the failure comes from the routing, not from the fixture. The finding holds in full: once a plan is written after a completed reset, clean-reinstall.json captures every later Ensure, the changed desired cannot be applied through the routed path, and --reinstall returns the stale plan instead of starting a new reset. The one step not driven here is the actual canic-cli binary. Its routing was reproduced by calling the same host selected/retained_desired/review/apply functions in the order the CLI calls them.
A root Fleet-state cascade that reaches a committed but still-Prepared Component records a prepared state-snapshot hash that activate_component_runtime rejects as obsolete evidence, so that Component can never be activated
reproduced
crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs::ops::storage::fleet_activation::tests::repro_state_cascade_before_configure_runtime_blocks_component_activation
The test sets up a Prepared managed Component runtime with initialize_nonroot_prepared and an UngroupedOrdinary deployment. It then makes the same two calls that StateCascadeWorkflow::apply_state_with_activation makes in managed mode when a root SynchronizeState cascade reaches a node: prepare_applied_state_snapshot(H) followed by commit_prepared_snapshot. Next it runs the ConfigureRuntime ops sequence: prepare_component_runtime_directory succeeds with DirectoryPrepared, then activate_component_runtime is called twice (once, then as a retry). The test asserts that the first activation transitions to Active. Result: prepare_applied_state_snapshot accepts the Component-runtime record and stores prepared_state_snapshot_hash = Some(H). Both activation attempts return InvalidRecord("managed Component runtime retains obsolete cascade or credential evidence"), and the hash is still present afterwards. So the member is permanently unable to activate; the only code that clears the hash is FleetActivationOps::activate, which rejects Component runtimes. The core defect and the permanent wedge are both confirmed natively. The upstream reachability was checked by reading code, not by running it: - RootStateCascadeTargets::current adds every Registry partition, with no status filter (root_component_canisters). - The Prepared non-root fence admits CANIC_COMMAND updates. The downstream consequence, that provisioning never reaches RuntimesActive, needs PocketIC and was not exercised.
Retirement leaves material_threshold + maximum_execution_burn_cycles in the source, but Delete allows at most material_threshold, so every drained retirement or replacement fails at Delete and cannot be replanned
reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/tests.rs::repro_retirement_delete_admits_unspent_drain_reserve
The test uses the existing fleet_ensure fixture: "retired" is an Absent Auxiliary canister holding 100 cycles, with material_threshold 5 and drain maximum_execution_burn 2. It compiles the reviewed plan through production workflow::plan and gets Transfer amount=93 and Delete maximum_remaining_cycles=5. It then models a drain that burns 1 cycle, below the bound of 2. Production reconcile_retirement_transfer accepts this as Conserved, with source_debit 94 and treasury credit 93. The test then drives the production IcpEnsurePlatform::apply(Delete) against a fake icp CLI script. The script reports the source as Stopped with the remaining 6 cycles. The test asserts that Delete succeeds. It fails because Delete returns MaterialCycles { actual: 6, maximum: 5 }. That confirms the plan leaves material + max_burn in the source, reconciliation admits any smaller burn, and Delete admits only material. A probe with a fresh plan against the stopped source holding 6 returns Policy(NoSafeDrain), so the canister cannot be replanned. This matches the verifier's correction: replanning fails at plan time, before the missing Start would matter, so the "drain on a Stopped canister" path from the finding never runs. The wedged-journal resume loop was not exercised end to end. The core claim holds in full.
canic_command caps root-to-child ConfigureRuntime at 16 KiB, but the request carries the full Fleet and Group directories plus every direct child, so larger Components can never be configured or resynchronized
partially reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/repro_tests.rs::repro_configure_runtime_fits_canic_command_payload_limit
The test builds a config with a 64-member Component Group (the per-declaration cap is 256) and runs it through production parse_config_model and compile_component_group_deployment_topology. The validator accepts it. From the compiled members it builds a ComponentGroupDirectory with ComponentBindings shaped like production ones: 10-byte canister ids, 29-byte subnet ids, no recovery controllers. That directory goes into a ComponentRuntimeDirectoryPreparationRequest using the smallest realistic envelope: one fleet root, no services, no direct children. The request is wrapped in the production root-side CanisterCommandFragment::ConfigureRuntime and candid::encode_one'd, which produces the same bytes CallOps::with_arg sends. The test asserts the result is at most DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES (16384), the explicit limit on the target's canic_command. It fails. One member encodes to 2040 bytes, each extra member adds 376 bytes, and 64 members come to 25728 bytes. The limit is first exceeded at 40 members, which matches the finding's estimate of about 40. So the core claim holds: config-valid groups produce a root-to-child ConfigureRuntime that is larger than the target's cap. Not exercised natively: - The target-side trap. By inspection, the macro raw adapter traps when msg_arg_data_size is above max_bytes (canic-macros expand/mod.rs:364-370). - The retry and reconciliation wedge. - The hub case with about 250 direct children. All three need PocketIC. A PocketIC test would provision a group with 40 or more members and assert that publication completes.
A deposit_cycles failure marks the child-funding receipt RecoveryRequired, which blocks all later funding for that child and has no resume or clear path
partially reproduced
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs::repro_tests::repro_deposit_failure_wedges_child_funding_receipt
The test drives the production helpers in the same order execute_authorized_request_cycles uses them. First the replay::check_replay admission. Then a 2T value-transfer cost guard reserved against a 3T total balance, through request_cycles_cost_guard_request plus CostGuardOps::reserve. CostGuardWorkflow::reserve fails natively when it schedules its cleanup timer (E137), so the test calls the ops-level reserve instead. Then mark_request_cycles_external_effect and record_child_grant. The deposit result is a real InternalError converted from CallFailed::InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance. On that error the test runs the handler's failure branch as written: restore_child_snapshot, CostGuardWorkflow::recover_after_failure, the private preserve_request_cycles_recovery_required, and then replay::abort_replay_after_failure. What was observed: the cost guard was recovered (0 pending intents) and the ledger was restored, so the handler did treat the deposit as not executed. Even so, the receipt stayed RecoveryRequired{ExternalEffectStatusUnknown}. A retry with the same op id failed with REQUEST_INCOMPLETE (E124). reject_competing_funding_operation refused a new op id with E124. One hour later, after purge_expired, the receipt was still there and new op ids were still refused. The core wedge claim holds in full. The outcome is partial because the real async deposit, the ic-cdk liquid-balance refusal, and CycleWorkflow::reconcile_after_transfer cannot run natively (ic0 panics). The Err is injected, and the few lines of the handler's failure branch are replayed in the test.
Root-removal timer uses the reservation-time Registry version as the compare-and-swap version for both publications, so any unrelated Registry revision permanently wedges the removal and admission
partially reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/tests.rs::repro_root_removal_timer_draining_cas_wedges_after_unrelated_revision
Setup: the test activates two roots at Registry revision V=4. It reserves RemoveRoot for A and for B at V through FleetCoordinatorWorkflow::prepare_root_draining_reservation, and both commits succeed. For each root it builds the draining publication the way advance_coordinator_root_removal_once does (mod.rs:840-845): the CAS version comes from `current.reservation.request.expected_registry`, and the status is read with FleetCoordinatorOps::operation_status. That timer function is async and awaits query_root_removal, an inter-canister call, before it publishes. It cannot run natively, so the test copies that one construction and calls the production FleetCoordinatorOps::publish_root_draining. Result: A publishes and moves the head to 5. B's request uses revision 4 and gets STATE_CONFLICT (E132). A retry builds an identical request against unchanged durable state and gets E132 again, so every timer tick fails the same way. Replaying RemoveRoot(B) returns the same reservation, still at revision 4. The admission start gate returns E132 because B is still Active. As a control, the same receipt published with CAS on the current head succeeds. Not exercised: the 1 s reschedule loop itself, Root B being stuck draining on the Root side, and the removal-step and funding-rotation variants.
Grant revocation rejects a previous allocation's disabled grant tombstone, so a canister reused by a non-fixture role can never be recycled again, and the pool maintenance timer disables itself
partially reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/repro_tests.rs::repro_reused_asset_tombstone_blocks_recycling
The test runs the scenario from the finding using production pool ops and Store ops. It imports a Ready asset A and puts a complete fixture source in the Store. Allocation C/op1 claims A and is granted revision 1 through set_grant. C is then recycled: revocation_request is applied, the Store keeps a revision 2 disabled tombstone, mark_ready and complete_recycling run, and A goes back to Ready. Allocation D/op2 then claims the same A (claim_smallest_sufficient_ready ignores role) and writes no grant, as a non-fixture role would. Finally D is recycled: the test takes the pending claim D/op2 and the grant_status(A) tombstone and passes them to fixture_grant::revocation_request, the same way revoke_before_reset does. It asserts Ok(None), because a disabled tombstone gives no access. The test fails as the finding predicts: the call returns Err(E132), which is STATE_CONFLICT. When that same error goes through the workflow's maintenance classifiers, it is not retryable and both classifiers return InvariantFailure. This is the branch where finish_maintenance_timer clears MAINTENANCE_ENABLED. The asset stays in Recycling{Pending}. The core defect is fully confirmed. Some async glue was not run natively, because it needs a Store inter-canister call and real timers (PocketIC): revoke_before_reset awaiting the Store, reset_asset returning with `?` before mark_failed, and the timer actually cancelling itself.
The subtree removal timer spins forever at 1 s when it finds an already-Completed removal, which a routine RemoveSubtree retry triggers, and the perpetual timer blocks root authority snapshots
partially reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/lifecycle_drivers/repro_tests.rs::repro_completed_subtree_removal_advance_terminates
I added a test helper, repro_import_completed_subtree_removal, to the ops component_registry tests module. It runs the same production ops sequence as subtree_removal_target_finalization_is_terminal_and_releases_the_live_fence: drain, quiesce, fence, select, stop, delete, remove membership, sync the directory, finalize. That leaves one retained Completed subtree removal in the store. To make the helper reachable from workflow, I changed `mod tests` to `pub(crate) mod tests` in ops/component_registry/mod.rs. The workflow test first confirms that ComponentRegistryOps::subtree_removal still returns the Completed record, which is what a replay or duplicate chain sees. It then calls advance_existing_subtree_removal once with a noop waker. That is the exact call the schedule_subtree_removal_after timer body makes. The test asserts Ok with phase Completed, the only result that stops the chain. Observed: the future resolves straight away with Err(InternalError E137 STATE_INVALID, i.e. InternalError::invariant()). This confirms the core defect: advancing an already-Completed removal fails instead of reporting completion, and the scheduler re-arms after 1 s on any Err. Not exercised natively: the timer loop itself, the missing chain dedup, the endpoint replay scheduling a new chain, and suspend_root / prepare_root_snapshot failing with UnmanagedClaim. Those need real IC timers, so PocketIC. A PocketIC test would replay RemoveSubtree after Completed, then check that lifecycle timers stay registered and that PrepareAuthoritySnapshot fails.
Root ledger retirement stores an immutable transfer intent and then requires an exactly-zero ledger balance, so dust, any later third-party deposit, or a retry after the 24-hour ledger window permanently wedges Root deletion
partially reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/tests/repro_root_ledger_sweep/mod.rs::repro_root_ledger_sweep_reobserves_balance_after_third_party_deposit
The test runs the same production ComponentRegistryOps chain as the existing end-to-end root retirement test: prepare, draining, funding fence, final inventory, removal publication, Store reclamation, binding finalization, Store deletion, and begin_root_deletion_preparation for operation [10;32]. It then persists the first sweep intent the way evacuate does, with balance 100, fee 10, t=35. After a restart, the retry view still holds that same intent, and cycle reclamation without a receipt returns STATE_CONFLICT (E132). To model a third-party deposit, it tries to record a successor intent for the new balance of 200 at t=40, once with no receipt and once after recording the first transfer's block-7 receipt. Both return STATE_CONFLICT, and the stored intent stays at balance_before=100, so the assertion fails. This confirms the core defect natively. The recorded intent can never be replaced, so there is no durable way to sweep a later deposit. Because evacuate re-dispatches only the stored intent and require_empty_source needs a zero balance, every retry fails. The async parts could not be run natively: the Ledger Duplicate/TooOld responses, require_empty_source itself, and the fleet-level wedge. Those would need a PocketIC test that deposits into (root, None) partway through preparation. The dust case matches the verifier's correction: begin_root_ledger_transfer(50, fee 100) is rejected at the store with STATE_CONFLICT and never reaches InvalidTransfer, and a top-up can recover it.
Component operations bind the SHA-256 of the entire live Coordinator FleetRegistry, so a routine admission change blocks every existing and in-flight Component operation
partially reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/component_operation/tests.rs::repro_admission_only_registry_change_keeps_component_operation_authority
The test builds a retained FleetRegistry that matches the existing test authority() fixture: the Root entry, the Spec entry and an admission policy with one principal. It binds the record's registry_sha256 with the same SHA-256-over-serde_json expression that IcpComponentTransport::authority and observe use. It then produces the successor that the Coordinator publishes on `canic admission apply`, using the production canic-core helpers mutate_fleet_admission_membership (Add, Fleet selector) and compile_installed_fleet_admission_policy at generation+1, with revision+1. The test asserts that authority, component_specs and fleet_subnet_roots stay unchanged. Using the existing TransportProbe, it plans and submits once, then sets the observed authority to the one re-derived over the current Registry (only the digest differs) and reports an in-flight Installed progress. Result: the whole-Registry digest changed. policy::validate_authority, workflow::status and workflow::apply all rejected with Authority{"reviewed binding"}, so the in-flight operation can be neither observed nor resumed. This confirms the core claim: an admission-only change permanently invalidates the immutable binding. What was not exercised: IcpComponentTransport::observe itself, whose "live Registry" rejection at transport/mod.rs:288 runs against the unrefreshed retained copy. Running it needs a converged Ensure workspace, protocol sidecars, a fake ICP CLI and Candid Coordinator/Root query responses. The test only prints that the equality observe checks is false. The Root-restart consequence is also inferred, not executed.
FundEstate completion requires an untouched Root Ledger balance, so Root's own autonomous creation (or any third-party credit) after the transfer makes the paid effect permanently unprovable and wedges the operation
partially reproduced
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/tests.rs::repro_estate_funding_consumed_by_root_creation_remains_provable
The test follows the existing lost_estate_funding_response_reuses_the_exact_ledger_transfer flow, with the finding's numbers scaled to 0.1T units: operator 1000, Root Ledger 10, FundEstate amount 50, fee 1, expected_post 60. The production prepare_effect freezes source_before=1000 and destination_before=10 in the Intent. The first MockPlatform apply loses its response; the replay returns the Duplicate receipt, and the record becomes Issued. The test then simulates Root's WaitingForFunding creation debiting 41 from Root's Ledger account, leaving 19. It asserts the correct behaviour: a receipted transfer with an exact source debit (51 = amount + fee) is still provable after Root spends the credit. It calls the production estate_funding_applied directly and also calls observe_effect three times. The mock's FundEstate observation copies the production composition at platform.rs:4477-4506 (receipt present AND estate_funding_applied on live balances), and production also returns retry None for FundEstate. Result: estate_funding_applied returns false. All three observations are identical: applied=false, retry=None, same progress_identity. So the frozen baselines make the effect permanently unprovable, and the core claim holds. The wedge consequence was not driven through workflow::apply: Stalled on every resume, and the InProgress journal blocking reinstall. Building a mock plan that contains a primary-path FundEstate was out of scope. That consequence follows from workflow/mod.rs:1824-1899, which counts repeated identical progress identities with no retry as stalled.
One trap after an await permanently disables retained core timer owners (automatic cycle top-up, placement acknowledgement drain, Root issuer renewal, pool maintenance), because the watchdog recovers only the expired attempt and never re-establishes the stuck registration
partially reproduced
repro-vendor/ic-timers/src/runtime/repro_tests.rs::repro_retained_once_trapped_after_await_is_never_rearmed (plus ::repro_retained_once_trapped_before_await_absorbs_earliest_ensure)
canic-core cannot drive ic-timers natively: its non-test platform calls ic0, which panics off-wasm, and recover_expired_timer needs ic_cdk spawn plus a parent call. So I copied ic-timers 0.8.0 byte-for-byte into repro-vendor/ and pointed the workspace at it with a [patch.crates-io] entry. That makes its cfg(test) fake platform usable, and the test drives the real runtime on it. Test 1 sets up a Retained Once registration the way CycleWorkflow::declare_timer does, arms it, and dispatches it. The first callback suspends at an await. I then drop the suspended task, which is what ic-cdk's cleanup does after a trapped response callback. After that it calls the only re-arms Canic makes, reconcile_schedule(At(100)) and ensure_scheduled(At(100)). Both return Ok, but the claim stays Running and no provider task exists. A later wake-up never dispatches (calls=1), so the test fails. Test 2 deletes the provider task before the first await. It confirms that Earliest ensure_scheduled cannot replace the dead Scheduled entry. By code reading, all four recover_expired_timer owners use `let _ = AsyncJobWorkflow::finish(...)` and never touch the registration. That confirms the watchdog discards the directive and never re-declares the claim. Not exercised: Canic's own watchdog code, and the end effects (no further top-up, Root RunningClaim, post_upgrade trap). Those need PocketIC.
Transport failures (PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE) are classified as permanent by the cycle top-up, pool maintenance, auth renewal and placement-ack retry classifiers, so one transient reject permanently stops those background workers
partially reproduced
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/cycles/mod.rs::tests::repro_transport_reject_stops_parent_topup (plus crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/auth/renewal.rs::tests::repro_transport_reject_stops_renewal, crates/canic-core/src/workflow/placement/acknowledgement.rs::tests::repro_transport_reject_stops_placement_ack, crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs::tests::repro_transport_reject_disables_pool_maintenance)
In canic-core, the tests build the real transport error the way CallOps::execute builds it: InternalError::from(OpsError::from(IcInfraError::from(CallFailed::CallRejected(CallRejected::with_rejection(code, msg))))). They cover SysTransient (2), CanisterError (5), SysUnknown (6) and CallPerformFailed. Each one comes out as code E66 (PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE). - Top-up: CycleWorkflow::finish_funding_failure returns InvariantFailure/Stop for all four transport classes. - Renewal: RootIssuerRenewalWorkflow::failed_result, given the Transport projection that into_renewal_error uses, returns InvariantFailure/Stop. - Placement ack: is_retryable_root_failure returns false on the real transport error, so drain_batch returns Err and run_scheduled stops. - Pool (canic-control-plane): IcInfraError is crate-private there, so the test uses InternalError::public(PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE), which the canic-core From impl produces for CallFailed. maintenance_timer_result and timer_result_completion both give InvariantFailure, the completion that makes finish_maintenance_timer set MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=false and cancel the timers. Every test asserts retry or non-Stop, and every one fails. So the core defect holds in all four classifiers. Not exercised natively: that nothing re-arms the stopped timers, and the downstream harm (a child draining to its freezing threshold, receipts building up toward the replay caps). Those need PocketIC with the real timer registry. The verifier also noted that placement-ack is re-armed by the next allocation and renewal by a template or policy upsert, so those two are not strictly permanent.
Retirement and deletion intents freeze an observed balance and fail with a conflict forever when anyone deposits cycles or ledger credit, with no path to reclaim or sweep again
partially reproduced
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs::repro_store_deletion_wedged_by_third_party_deposit
The Store deletion path is confirmed. The other three paths are not. Setup: the test builds the terminal publication state and a single Store inventory. It gets the deletion cycle authority from production `store_deletion_cycle_authority` on a 2T-cycle status: retained target 330B. It then builds a durable intent with observed_after = 180B, the Store-side target. `validate_store_deletion_intent_lineage` accepts this fixture. Control: with no deposit, `require_store_deletion_authority` returns Ok. After a 1B third-party deposit, the Store holds 181B, still well under the 330B durable target. Two results: - `require_store_deletion_authority` returns an InvalidState error (E137). This check guards both stop and delete. - Polling `reclaim_single_finalized_root_store_cycles` again on the durable intent returns E137 at once, before any IC call. The lineage and the guard pass, so the error comes from the "already durable" refusal. So the test shows no way forward: stop/delete is refused and no second sweep is allowed. `fleet_subnet_root::delete_store` also skips reclamation once observed_after is set. The claim holds for the cited gc.rs:1006 path. Not exercised: the root native reclaim, the root Cycles Ledger `require_empty_source` and the Coordinator zero-balance check. All three need async IC or ledger calls, so they need PocketIC. Also not shown: whether the wedge is permanent, since idle burn can eventually eat the deposit on native balances. Test-enablement change: I re-exported CanisterSettingsSnapshot, MemoryMetricsSnapshot, QueryStatsSnapshot and LogVisibility from `canic_core::control_plane_support::ops::ic::mgmt`. Without them a CanisterStatus fixture cannot be built. This does not change behaviour.
Lifecycle drivers each take a slot in ic-timers' 64-entry registry with no concurrency bound, and `defer_lifecycle_required` traps when the registry is full, so ordinary concurrency or command replays can kill every Root lifecycle driver and pin their slots until restart
could not test
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/timer/repro_tests.rs::repro_lifecycle_deferrals_are_bounded_and_do_not_trap_when_registry_full (plus ::repro_defer_lifecycle_required_traps_on_any_registration_error as supporting evidence)
I could not test the main claim natively: registering more than 64 lifecycle deferrals and having defer_lifecycle_required trap when the registry is full. Every registration goes through the ic-timers runtime, and only a canister can start it. initialize_runtime calls ic0::canister_version, which panics on the host. ic-timers swaps in its fake platform only under its own cfg(test), which is off when it is built as a dependency. So the first test fails during setup, not at the capacity check. The second test confirms part of the finding. With no runtime on the thread, defer_lifecycle_once returns a typed Err(Provider(NotInitialized)), but TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required turns that same error into a trap (ic0 trap stub panic). From the source, RegisterError::CapacityExceeded reaches the same trap path. It is converted into ic_timers::TimerError::Register and then Canic's TimerError::Provider. Nothing in Canic counts lifecycle identities against the 64-entry cap. A PocketIC test would need a Root or test canister that can call defer_lifecycle_once or schedule_component_removal more than 54 times with a long delay or a pending dependency. It would then check three things: - the next ProvisionComponent/RemoveComponent/SynchronizeRegistry call returns a typed error rather than a trap; - the fixed claims stay registered; - a chain that reschedules after an await does not leave a Running entry behind.

28 findings were tested with focused tests. 16 reproduced in full. 11 reproduced in part: the core defect failed natively, but a consequence that needs PocketIC or real timers was not run. 1 could not be tested natively, and none were disproved. The macOS build failure (repro-build-1) was reproduced by compiling the unmodified commit. Each test patch is shown in its finding's trail and was never applied to the working tree.

Dependency audit

cargo audit 0.22.2 checked Cargo.lock at commit 06d73694d (567 crates) against the RustSec advisory database on 29 September 2026. It found no vulnerabilities and no yanked crates, and warned about two unmaintained crates. Neither is in canister code at runtime: paste is a compile-time proc-macro that candid uses, and serde_cbor reaches only the host side, through ic-agent.

AdvisoryCrateKindHow it enters
RUSTSEC-2024-0436paste 1.0.15UnmaintainedProc-macro used by candid 0.10.37, so it is in the build of every canister and host crate, but only at compile time. No replacement is needed until candid moves off it.
RUSTSEC-2021-0127serde_cbor 0.11.2UnmaintainedComes in through ic-agent 0.49.2 → ic-query 0.44.0 (subnet-catalog-host feature) → canic-host → canic-cli. Host-side only; it is not in canister wasm.

What to fix first

  1. Take cost-guard quota buckets out of the durable committed-totals map. Keep per-window quota counts in a separate bounded structure that drops past windows, or reclaim a quota row once its window has passed and nothing is pending, and reserve capacity for Canic-owned keys so application intents cannot starve them.
    Reproduced: one ordinary reserve and complete per 60-second window fails at window 999 with CAPACITY_LIMIT, because 999 past-window rows plus the cycle row fill the 1,000-identity cap. Every later window is a new key, so the block is permanent, and the finding traces how child funding, Component provisioning and ICP refill on Root then stop after roughly 1,000 active quota minutes, which it estimates a modest Fleet reaches in days.
  2. Close the paths that burn or strand cycles and ICP. In GetOrCreateDelegationProof return auth_proof_pending before any signing when the caller has no enabled template, and stop folding other issuers' due templates into caller-driven batches. Use unbounded wait for AcceptFunding, or probe the Root receipt with zero cycles before attaching a grant on Reconcile, and treat a Root error during Reconcile as retryable. Add an ICP Ledger evacuation step with a durable intent to Root deletion preparation, and give blob-storage project funding an intent record.
    Reproduced: a caller with no template drove five batch signatures of another issuer's batches in five calls, each a paid threshold-ECDSA signature in production, and received no proof. The finding puts each signature at about 26.15B cycles, or up to about 3.3T cycles a minute with a 60 s max_revocation_latency, until 128 pending batches stop the renewal timer. A lost bounded-wait response on the zero-accept replay burns a whole grant, and a deleted Root takes its ICP balance with it.
  3. Build one shared retry classifier that works on the typed IcInfraError before it is flattened to PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE. Treat SysTransient, SysUnknown, CanisterError, perform failures and insufficient liquid cycles as retryable with backoff in cycle top-up, pool maintenance, auth renewal and placement acknowledgement, stop counting transport failures toward ICP refill's five notify attempts, and test it with errors built through IcInfraError::CallFailed.
    Partially reproduced: SysTransient, CanisterError, SysUnknown and perform failures all map to PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE, and every classifier stops its worker. In the traced code nothing re-arms a stopped top-up, so one transient reject from a briefly stopped parent ends a child's automatic funding and the child drifts toward its freezing threshold. On Root, one Coordinator timeout stops funding, and ICP refill can end terminally with transferred ICP left at the CMC.
  4. Give the child-funding receipt an exit. When an unbounded-wait deposit_cycles returns a reject or perform failure, restore the ledger, recover the cost guard and abort the receipt so the same operation can retry. Keep RecoveryRequired for genuinely unknown outcomes and add a reconciliation or operator-clear path for it, and base the parent preflight on canister_liquid_cycle_balance().
    Partially reproduced: after an injected InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance the handler restores the ledger and cost guard, yet the receipt stays RecoveryRequired. Both the same operation ID and a new one get REQUEST_INCOMPLETE, and after purge the receipt is still there and new IDs are still refused. That child can never be funded again, and the only recovery is reinstalling the parent, which for Root means the Fleet.
  5. Rewrite conservation checks as bounds. Accept any source debit up to the reviewed bound and record excess credit as controlled, prove FundEstate and retirement transfers from Ledger receipts with live balances used only as bounded evidence, allow successor sweep intents after a proven terminal outcome, record a remainder at or below the fee as a reviewed terminal residual discard, and let Delete keep the drain's unspent burn reserve.
    Reproduced or partially reproduced in six places: a 1B-cycle deposit blocks Store stop and delete, a successor sweep intent for a new Root ledger balance is refused, a 500-cycle credit makes capacity-import approval and handoff unprovable, Root's own pool creation makes a receipted FundEstate unprovable, a 20k-cycle treasury idle charge turns a conserved drain into UnbalancedTransfer, and a retirement plan fails at Delete with 6 cycles against a maximum of 5. Anyone can deposit to a public principal, so several of these let a third party wedge retirement.
  6. Bound and own the lifecycle timer chains. Keep one owned convergence timer per operation or domain, deduplicate removal, provisioning and admission chains by operation key and clear the key on every exit, and return a typed REQUEST_CAPACITY error before the 64-entry ic-timers registry fills. Move retained owners such as top-up to the Watchdog-plus-spawn pattern, and have a watchdog that recovers an expired lease re-establish the registration and apply its directive. Treat an already-Completed subtree removal as success, and add backoff to the 1-second loops.
    A Coordinator retrying a slow Fence phase at 1 Hz adds a chain per call and fills the registry in about a minute, after which Root lifecycle endpoints and timers trap. Reviewers verified this in code, but no native test could fill the registry. Partially reproduced: advancing a Completed subtree removal returns an invariant error, which the finding traces to a routine RemoveSubtree retry spinning forever and blocking authority snapshots, and after a trap past an await the top-up registration stays Running and never fires again.
  7. Stop binding in-flight work to a whole Registry version. Use the Coordinator's current version for compare-and-swap in the root-removal timer, rebuild allocation and scale-out Directory requests from the current partition and mirror and accept monotonic successors, and bind host component operations to a named struct of the component-relevant Registry facts. Reject root reservations while a Component operation is non-terminal. Then make Registry adoption Fleet-wide with per-root acknowledgements and a Coordinator-authenticated resync, and skip Removed roots in CLI and capacity-import observers.
    Reproduced or partially reproduced: the second of two root removals fails with STATE_CONFLICT and an identical retry fails the same way, a spare root's draining leaves a scale-out stuck in ComponentsProvisioned with admission blocked, and an admission-only change rejects an in-flight component operation. In multi-root Fleets a lagging mirror stops a Root's funding and makes its own removal, and so Fleet retirement, impossible.
  8. Add exits to fences and irrevocable reservations. Move the rotation_current rejection below the exact current and last replay checks and add a controller abort for rotations before any Root has prepared. Give capacity import a journalled abort and charge its step allowance only after local prechecks. Clear the prepared snapshot hash for Component runtimes in prepare_applied_snapshot, and let RemoveRoot reservations and child allocations release when the Root rejects or the parent abandons them.
    Reproduced: after a lost funding response the rotation fence refuses the Root's exact replay, and when the Root holds an open request the Coordinator and the Root refuse each other, which the finding traces to a freeze of all funding and Registry commits. Two Coordinator HTTP 500 replies exhaust a capacity-import step with zero update calls sent, after which a fresh import review is refused with Conflict. A state cascade that reaches a Prepared Component makes both activation attempts fail with InvalidRecord.
  9. Check message and record sizes at admission from the configured maxima. Compute the encoded size of the terminal maximum Registry record and reject with resource_exhausted before any pool claim, bound init args and chunk count, give ConfigureRuntime a variant-dependent limit sized like ProvisionComponents, and add tests that encode the largest message a valid config allows. Extend config validation to member-limit reductions, transitive warm-up trees and per-role initial_cycles across Specs.
    Reproduced: with 768 bytes of init args, commit traps at the 4,096-byte Storable bound after the paid creation effect, a commit retry traps the same way, and draining then returns unavailable, so the Component can never retire. Partially reproduced: a 64-member Component Group, well under the 256 cap, encodes ConfigureRuntime to 25,728 bytes against a 16 KiB limit, so that Component can never be configured.
  10. Fix pool recycling idempotency. Pass the full claim key into complete_recycling and validate_complete_recycling, return Ok(None) from revocation_request for a disabled grant on the same target, mark a single conflicting asset Failed without cancelling maintenance, retry transient reset failures, and delete canister snapshots during reset.
    Reproduced: the second recycle of one asset under one Component leaves it in Recycling with ready_count 0, and both recovery probes fail with a conflict. The finding traces how its cycles leave the pool and Root draining then stalls at finalize_inventory. Partially reproduced: an earlier allocation's disabled tombstone makes revocation return STATE_CONFLICT, which the maintenance classifier treats as fatal.
  11. Scope clean reinstall to its own operation. Route to it only when plan.json is the clean infrastructure plan, a clean import is pending, or the plan digest matches the recorded convergence, and archive clean-reinstall.json with the terminal receipt. Before prepare_bootstrap deletes state, require the seed and desired set to cover the retained inventory and the paged live pool of the old Root, with a typed error that names missing IDs.
    Reproduced: after a completed clean reinstall, review, --apply and --reinstall all route back to the frozen reset, and the changed desired document fails with DriftedBeforeApply. Separately (verified, not yet tested), pool assets the Root created after the last ensure keep their cycles under a Root principal that no registry records, while the reset reports fleet_completed.
  12. Handle IC time windows in host journals. Reject a plan whose earliest Ledger created_at_time is near the 24-hour window before writing the InProgress journal, persist an issued-at-least-once marker before each Ledger call, resolve an expired handoff envelope from certified controllers and version, authenticate mint deposits with a length-1 certified icrc3_get_blocks read, and allow a supplementary conversion or refresh when a credited mint falls short.
    Reproduced: a plan applied 48 hours after review writes its InProgress journal, a second apply returns Stalled, re-planning returns the same frozen timestamps and plan_reinstall refuses, so there is no supported exit. The handoff, deposit and short-credit variants (verified, not yet tested) leave spent ICP unadmitted and Root fenced after an interrupted run.
  13. Make backup and restore refuse inconsistent state. In prune, skip any layout with a non-terminal restore plan, journal or staging directory and take its locks non-blockingly first. In restore, require the adopted snapshot's size to match the artifact, or delete and re-upload after a failed attempt. After failure containment, re-arm every CreateSnapshot in the unit. Bind restore to the current release and target identity, and coordinate member restores with Root so the admission projection is resynchronized.
    Reproduced: prune deleted a backup directory holding an in-flight restore journal, which in the finding's scenario leaves stopped canisters with no journal for lost-response reconciliation; restore recorded a partial upload as done and loaded it; and a retried backup paired a parent snapshot from one stop window with a child snapshot from another in one crash-consistent Subtree unit, which would restore parent and child state that disagree, with no warning.
  14. Re-read placement state after awaits. In index finalize, treat an entry Bound to exactly the returned pid as success and recycle only a different pid. Re-check partition_key_shard after the shard-creation await and use a create-only assign. Admit capacity before persisting the index claim.
    Two resumers of a stale index claim can recycle the live bound child, destroying its application state and leaving the key bound to a deleted canister with no unbind API. A concurrent sharding assign moves a key away from the shard that holds its data. Both survived verification and skeptic review, and neither has a test yet.
  15. Tighten ingress and authentication edges. Reject delegated tokens for the anonymous principal, check callers in every inspect_message hook and refuse ingress to query methods, have Root choose the role-attestation epoch, bind replay slot keys to the actor, and give untrusted callers quotas and log capacity separate from operators.
    Anonymous callers can pass auth::authenticated endpoints and make Root and the Coordinator pay for replicated public queries and megabyte ingress, and free self-authenticating principals can lock every user out of session establishment or flush the operator log.
  16. Fix the macOS build. Type the durable_io permission parameter as rustix::fs::Mode, or pass Mode::from_raw_mode literals, so the platform width of mode_t is inferred, and add a macOS CI job that runs at least cargo check -p canic-cli --locked. Also accept symlinked ancestors such as /tmp and /var in durable writes and artifact hashing.
    Reproduced: on the unmodified commit canic-host fails with E0308 on macOS, so `cargo install --locked canic-cli` as INSTALLING.md describes fails for macOS operators, and canic-testing-internal and canic-tests cannot build either. The fix is one line, and every host and CLI reproduction in this review ran with it applied. Reproductions also had to canonicalize temp paths because the restore stager rejects the /var symlink, and every backup runner test fails VerifyArtifact on macOS.
  17. Close the CI selection gaps. Derive the governed PocketIC selection from the registered cases and fail when zero tests run, add the unregistered governed tests to the registry, check wasm32 at the MSRV, add a doctest lane and a local-fleet feature lane, and land this review's reproduction tests as regressions, with PocketIC versions of the partial ones.
    The governed lane runs only registered case lists, so a Fleet-admission fence proof and the artifact-cache invalidation tests never run, and a module rename would turn roughly 60 recovery, funding and conservation journeys into a passing zero-test run. Most of the eleven partial reproductions stopped where timer loops, inter-canister awaits or Ledger replies would need PocketIC.
  18. Reduce per-message cost on hot paths. Cache validated Coordinator and activation projections instead of re-deriving the history on every call, store immutable provisioning batches apart from their cursors, add indexes for operation-ID and partition-key lookups, fetch the release-set manifest once per operation, and bound thread and subprocess fan-out in `info cycles`, `info metrics` and `info list`.
    These costs grow with Fleet size on paths that run every message, including whole-history validation on each Coordinator call, a clone of an activation record of up to 2 MiB on each managed endpoint call, and linear sharding scans that eventually trap. None of them loses state today, and together they set the ceiling on how large a Fleet can grow.

Recurring themes

Fixed caps that routine traffic exhausts

The cost guard builds a quota key per command, subject and 60-second window and writes it into the durable committed-totals map, which never reclaims a committed row and admits at most 1,000 identities. A reproduction with one legitimate reserve per window failed at window 999 with CAPACITY_LIMIT, and because each later window is a new key, every later cost-guarded Root operation fails the same way. Fixed message and record limits also break under ordinary use, since ConfigureRuntime carries whole Fleet and Group directories under a 16 KiB cap that a 40-member Component Group exceeds, Registry records outgrow the 4,096-byte Storable bound after the paid creation effect, and confirm-deletion ingress is capped at 16 KiB (about 490 roots per call) while the pending-deletion list it drains is unbounded. Shared stores that untrusted or application traffic can fill include the Root replay store, the global prepare and session quotas, the count-bounded runtime log and Root's never-pruned pending-attestation maps. Keep time-bucketed counters out of durable totals, give Canic-owned keys reserved capacity, and derive every cap from the configured maxima with a test that encodes the largest valid message.

Conservation checks demand exact balances

Cycle conservation requires only that every controlled cycle stays controlled or is accounted for, yet many checks compare a balance frozen at intent time with an exact expected value. Root and Coordinator ledger retirement need a zero balance after one immutable transfer intent, Store deletion refuses once a deposit raises the balance, capacity import treats any credit as ConservationUnproven and pins bootstrap-time pool and Root balances, FundEstate completion needs an untouched Root Ledger balance, a retirement drain needs a treasury credit equal to the amount despite the treasury's own idle burn, and host conservation and native funding recovery need the operator's shared account balance to match exactly. Anyone can call deposit_cycles or icrc1_transfer against a public principal, so several of these are permissionless ways to wedge retirement or import, and reproductions confirmed the rejection for a 1B-cycle Store deposit, a 500-cycle credit and a 20k-cycle idle charge. The plan compiler has the mirror problem, since it leaves material_threshold plus the drain's burn bound in a retiring canister while Delete admits only material_threshold (reproduced), and Delete's material-cycles guard ignores the reserved cycles that deletion destroys. Root deletion preparation also folds re-sampled canister_status readings into its retry identity, so ordinary drift turns an expected retry into a permanent conflict. Treat conservation as bounds, with debits up to the reviewed bound and excess credit recorded as controlled, prove transfers from Ledger receipts, allow successor sweep intents, and record dust at or below the fee as a reviewed terminal residual discard.

Registry revisions invalidate in-flight work

Several operations bind a whole Registry version or hash at reservation or commit and later require the live value to match exactly. The root-removal timer uses the reservation-time version for compare-and-swap, allocations re-check a Directory authority frozen at commit against the live mirror and partition head, replays of commit, membership activation and RemoveComponent re-validate against the current Fleet directory instead of returning the retained receipt, and host component operations bind the SHA-256 of the entire FleetRegistry, so an admission change, a sibling child commit or another root's draining wedges them. Reproductions, two of them partial, showed the second of two root removals failing with STATE_CONFLICT again on an identical retry, a spare root's draining leaving a scale-out stuck in ComponentsProvisioned, and an admission-only change rejecting an in-flight component operation. In multi-root Fleets the Coordinator publishes only to the roots a flow calls and an activated root cannot resync, so a lagging Root's funding fails as RegistryStale and its own RemoveRoot can never complete, which also blocks Fleet retirement. Capacity-import observation also requires every Root to be quiet, although only the destination Root is fenced. Bind named structs of the facts each operation depends on, use the current version for compare-and-swap while validators keep the source binding, accept monotonic successors, skip Removed roots in observers, and advance every root's mirror with per-root acknowledgements before the next publication.
