Durable states with no exit

Ordinary failures can leave durable state in a phase that has no resume, abort or operator-clear transition. A clean deposit_cycles failure leaves the child's RequestCycles receipt in RecoveryRequired even though the handler restored the ledger and cost guard, and the partial reproduction showed the same and a new operation ID refused with REQUEST_INCOMPLETE; after the one-hour purge the receipt was still present and new IDs were still refused. The funding-policy rotation fence runs before the replay checks for a Root's current and last request, so after a lost response the Coordinator refuses the Root's exact replay, and a Root request opened during the rotation leaves the Coordinator and the Root refusing each other (both reproduced). An approved capacity import has no abort and spends its two-attempt step budget before local prechecks, which two Coordinator HTTP 500 replies exhausted with no update sent (reproduced), and a state cascade that reaches a still-Prepared Component stores a snapshot hash that activate_component_runtime then rejects on every attempt (reproduced). Reviewers found the same gap in child allocations that have no abandon path, an ack-less Registry mirror candidate that can never complete, a terminal UnresolvedAfterLedgerWindow pool refill, clean-reinstall custody records written create-once before validation, and a Fleet Coordinator with no post_upgrade, whose endpoints all trap after a same-release upgrade until a destructive reinstall. Give every durable state a named exit by aborting effects known not to have executed, ordering replay checks before fences, adding controller aborts for fences that have no effect yet, and charging budgets only after prechecks pass.

Transient rejects stop background workers

Every transport failure (SysTransient, CanisterError, SysUnknown, perform failure) is flattened to PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE, while the classifiers for cycle top-up, pool maintenance, auth renewal and placement acknowledgement retry only PLATFORM_FAILED or STATE_FAILED. The partial reproduction built the real transport errors for the top-up, renewal and placement-acknowledgement classifiers and an equivalent PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE error for pool maintenance, and every classifier stopped its worker. A later allocation re-arms placement acknowledgement, and a template or policy upsert re-arms renewal. A child whose parent is briefly stopped therefore never requests cycles again and drifts toward its freezing threshold, and Root's funding stops after one bounded-wait timeout to the Coordinator. Pool maintenance also disables itself when a single asset returns STATE_CONFLICT, renewal stops on one invalid template or with an invariant failure after an upsert while no template is due, a harmless Root acceptance rejection becomes terminal NoGrant, and ICP refill turns final after five notify attempts that count transport failures. Classify on the typed IcInfraError before it is flattened, share one classifier across workers, retry transient classes with backoff, and mark a single failing item Failed while the loop keeps running.

Unbounded, unrecoverable timer chains

ic-timers keeps a heap-only registry of 64 entries, and TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required traps when a registration fails. Removal, provisioning, Registry synchronization and Root admission drivers each start their own self-rescheduling chain without deduplication, so Coordinator retries at 1 Hz or ordinary command replays can fill the registry and make every lifecycle endpoint trap. A trap after an await leaves the entry Running forever. A partial reproduction against a vendored copy of ic-timers 0.8.0 showed that Canic's re-arm calls on the retained top-up registration are absorbed and it never fires again, and reviewers found in the code that the watchdog finishes the expired attempt without re-establishing the registration. An already-Completed subtree removal returns an invariant error instead of its completion (partially reproduced), so a routine RemoveSubtree retry spins every second and blocks authority snapshots. Give each domain one owned timer keyed by operation, move retained owners to the Watchdog-plus-spawn pattern the fixture importer already uses, treat completed state as success, add backoff to the 1-second loops, and return a typed capacity error instead of trapping.

Paid effects that burn or strand cycles and ICP

A few value paths lack a bound or an exact outcome. GetOrCreateDelegationProof folds other issuers' due templates into a caller-driven batch, so a caller with no template forces a new threshold-ECDSA signature, about 26.15B cycles each by the finding's estimate, on every call, and the reproduction drove five batch signatures from five calls without returning a proof. The Coordinator attaches whole grants to bounded-wait AcceptFunding calls, so a lost response on the zero-accept replay burns the grant, and its reconcile path records RootRejected even when an earlier attempt may already have moved the cycles. Root deletion never evacuates the Root's ICP Ledger account, blob-storage project funding keeps no intent record, and inspect_message admits megabyte ingress and replicated public queries from any caller at Root's and the Coordinator's expense. On the host, a Duplicate reply after FailedToCreate or FailedToWithdraw is misread as a pending creation or a successful withdrawal receipt, and `canic cycles convert` can replay an old completed pending_send record in place of a new conversion. Reject callers without a template before signing, use unbounded wait or a zero-cycle receipt probe for value transfers, make reconcile errors retryable, add an ICP evacuation step with a durable intent, and check callers in inspect_message.

Placement state read before an await

The placement workflows derive allocation identities carefully, but two paths act on state they read before an await. Index finalize recycles the child Root just returned even when the key is already Bound to that same child, so two resumers of a stale claim can destroy the live bound instance and leave the key resolving to a deleted canister with no unbind path. Sharding assigns the key after the shard-creation await without re-checking, so a key assigned to another shard in the meantime is silently moved while its data stays on the old shard. The index claim is also persisted before capacity admission, which leaves an untracked claim when admission fails. Re-read durable state after every await, treat an exact match as success, admit capacity before persisting a claim, and use a create-only assign on the creation path.

Pool recycling and principal reuse

Root's canister pool reuses assets across Components, and its idempotency and grant checks are keyed too loosely for that. Recycling completion checks only the component ID, so a second recycle of the same asset under the same Component returns early and leaves it in Recycling (reproduced with ready_count 0), and the finding traces how that stalls Root draining at finalize_inventory. A disabled grant tombstone from an earlier allocation makes revocation return STATE_CONFLICT, which the maintenance classifiers treat as fatal (partially reproduced). A transient reset failure becomes terminal, a fee change wedges a pending refill, two executors race to reset the same asset, recycled canisters keep the previous workload's snapshots, Root replay receipts and parent placement registries keyed on the raw principal carry over to the next occupant, and on the host one Failed asset that Root cannot reinspect dooms every fleet ensure plan. Key completion on the full claim, ignore disabled tombstones, quarantine a single failed asset, delete snapshots during reset, and clear principal-keyed state when a canister returns to the pool.

Backup and restore produce inconsistent state

The backup persistence primitives are sound, and the defects appear where the flows are composed. `canic backup prune` looks only at backup status and deleted a directory holding an in-flight restore journal (reproduced). Restore adopts any single new snapshot as the completed upload, so a failed partial upload was recorded and loaded (reproduced), and a backup retried after failure containment kept the parent's first-window snapshot and paired it with the child's second-window snapshot in one Subtree unit (reproduced). Restoring a Component that uses Fleet admission re-admits principals removed since the backup and wedges the next admission change at Prepare, restore is bound to neither the current release nor the target identity, and a relocatable restore with --mapping reports success for a member whose runtime rejects every managed call. Snapshots are never deleted, deleting an old one to free space permanently blocks the pending upload, and live `canic backup create` always fails at its stubbed preflight while the full-Fleet scope cannot build a plan. Protect non-terminal restore journals during prune under their locks, prove upload completeness from size or delete and re-upload, re-arm every CreateSnapshot in a unit after containment, and coordinate member restores with Root.

Host reviews outlive IC time windows

Host journals freeze Ledger timestamps, signed ingress and funding reviews, and nothing replaces them once an IC window passes. A plan applied 48 hours after review wrote its InProgress journal and sent a Ledger request that the mock's TooOld rule rejected on every resume, while re-planning returned the same frozen timestamps and plan_reinstall refused (reproduced). A capacity-import handoff envelope expires after 240 s and its reply is pruned within minutes, a mint deposit must be authenticated through a certified hash chain of at most 1024 blocks from the Ledger tip, a credited mint or an unapproved Estate review cannot be refreshed after a CMC rate move or balance change, and a bootstrap review binds its first attempt's time-dependent plan hash. Each case leaves an InProgress or approved journal that blocks new plans, often after ICP or cycles were already spent. Reject stale plans before writing the journal, persist an issued-at-least-once marker before each Ledger call, resolve expired envelopes from certified controllers and version, and authenticate deposit blocks with a length-1 certified icrc3_get_blocks read.

Clean reinstall does not scope its authority

After a clean reinstall converges, clean-reinstall.json keeps capturing every later Ensure, so a changed desired document is routed back to the frozen reset and fails with DriftedBeforeApply while --reinstall returns the stale plan (reproduced). Clean reinstall also erases the old Root and Coordinator registries without checking that the seed covers every Root-controlled canister, so refill-created pool assets or omitted workloads keep their cycles outside every registry and conservation equation. The Root reinstall prerequisite checks completeness only against stale host state, a clean-reinstall review can report an unapplied workload phase as fleet_completed, an ordinary no-effect review over a completed Fleet overwrites plan.json without archiving it, a completed-preparation journal from the obsolete lane wedges newer CLIs, and fleet ensure picks a different reset lane depending on whether --environment was typed. Route to clean reinstall only when the plan digest matches its own convergence, archive the selection with its terminal receipt, and require the seed to cover the paged live pool inventory before any destructive step.

Build validation misses runtime limits

canic::build! validates a great deal, but several runtime limits and lookups are not modeled in it. A config-valid 64-member Component Group produces a 25,728-byte ConfigureRuntime against a 16 KiB cap (partially reproduced; the cap is first exceeded at 40 members), and Registry records exceed their 4,096-byte Storable bound once init args or chunk counts grow, trapping after the paid creation effect (reproduced). Root resolves initial_cycles and funding limits by role alone although cross-Spec role reuse is documented, member-limit reductions and transitive warm-up trees go unchecked, host capacity validation ignores child roles' initial_cycles, and the build accepts trust-anchor configs that verifier canisters trap on at install. Activation has similar gaps. A Root built with init_mode readonly or disabled can never be activated, canisters provisioned after a Fleet-state change start from the compiled init_mode, and a later ConfigureRuntime fails in open_fresh after the runtime change has committed. Derive each runtime cap from the configured maxima during validation, check record size at admission before any pool claim, and add tests that compile maximal configurations and encode their largest messages.

Ingress and authentication edges

The cryptographic chain holds, and the remaining findings concern who can act, who pays and whom verifiers trust. The auth::authenticated predicate accepts delegated tokens minted for the anonymous principal, Root signs a member-chosen role-attestation epoch that bypasses min_accepted_epoch floors, and the replay slot key omits the actor, so one Fleet member can pre-occupy another's deterministic operation IDs. Free self-authenticating principals can fill the global prepare and session quotas, and unauthenticated denied calls can flush the count-bounded runtime log that holds operator history. Delegated-token and role-attestation trust anchors name one App-wide root, so issuers and attestation subjects under any other Fleet Subnet Root always fail verification. On the host, enroll_network accepts the mainnet root key under an environment that icp.yaml classifies as Local, and imported canisters keep their prior allocation, freezing threshold and log visibility settings. Reject anonymous subjects at issuance and verification, set the attestation epoch at Root, bind replay slots to the actor, give untrusted traffic quotas separate from operators and members, and anchor trust per Fleet Subnet Root.

Per-message cost grows with state

Instruction cost grows with Fleet size on paths that run every message. Every Coordinator read and write re-derives and re-validates the whole history, every managed endpoint call deep-clones an activation record of up to 2 MiB and re-hashes the Directory authority twice, Root replay admission fully decodes every receipt in several table scans, and each Root admission journal load re-hashes every participant projection. Removed-Component validation scans every allocation and the whole principal index, operation-status lookups full-decode the Component Registry, sharding assign exports every partition-key assignment and eventually traps, the blob-storage deletion query decodes every pending row into one reply, and root_store::status re-downloads and re-hashes a release-set manifest of up to 16 MiB on each provisioning step. On the host, plan files round-trip chunk bytes through serde_json::Value, and `info cycles`, `info metrics` and `info list` start an unbounded thread and several icp subprocesses per canister. Cache validated projections, store immutable batches apart from their mutable cursors, add indexes for by-operation and by-key lookups, and bound host fan-out.

CI and test blind spots

Every CI job runs on ubuntu-24.04, so nothing caught that canic-host, and with it the canic CLI, stopped compiling on macOS when durable_io began passing a u32 mode to rustix, a form that dates to 0.110.22. The governed PocketIC lane runs only the registered case lists, so non-ignored tests missing from the registry, including a Fleet-admission fence proof and the artifact-cache invalidation tests, never run, and a renamed suite would pass with zero tests. Reviewers also report that the MSRV job checks only the native target, no lane runs doctests, the local-fleet feature tests never compile, two tracked source files are outside the module tree, trap_guard recognizes only one spelling of trap, and the Fleet activation fences compile away on native targets so only PocketIC exercises them. Add a macOS check job, derive the PocketIC selection from the registry with a non-empty assertion, check wasm32 at the MSRV, run doctests, and land this review's reproduction tests as regressions.

Targeted second-pass probes

A completeness critic named the areas that round one had covered least, and each got a dedicated probe. Probe findings went through the same adversarial verification as round one, and they appear in the explorer below with ids starting r2-.

Snapshot capture and restore versus the authority seal, durable journals and cycle conservation

7 findings

I traced every path that captures or loads a snapshot. The authority fence (workflow/runtime/authority_restore.rs, ops/storage/authority_restore/mod.rs) is used in production only by the fleet-ensure reset lane (fleet_ensure/ops/authority_seal). That lane seals Root and the Coordinator before a destructive reinstall. canic-backup and canic-cli never seal anything. The Root and the Coordinator cannot currently be captured through the CLI: the subtree scope rejects Root, MaintenanceRoot is never selected, and the full-Fleet scope fails validation. Live `canic backup create` also always fails at its stubbed preflight, so today the CLI cannot take any live backup. `canic restore` still loads any valid manifest. It uploads, stops, loads, starts and checks canister status, with no step that involves Root. On the IC, a snapshot load runs no lifecycle hook, and the cycle balance is not rolled back. A restored member therefore cannot detect the load, and cycles it received after the capture stay in its live balance. (b)/(d): The paid-effect journals of ordinary Components hold up after a restore. Cycle top-up operation IDs come from a durable generation counter. A restored child reuses those IDs and gets Root's cached receipt instead of a second transfer. Once the receipt is purged, the request is treated as a new, legitimate one. Scaling and sharding placement reuse IDs derived from state, and Root's child-allocation replay returns the child it already retains. Store cycle reclaim and blob-storage funding depend only on the live balance. Components keep no Cycles Ledger or CMC journals. The breaks are elsewhere, in protocols where Root pushes state and each member keeps a strict local predecessor check (c). The worst case is the Fleet admission projection. A restored member re-admits principals that were removed after the backup. The next admission change then gets stuck at Prepare with no way to release it. That stuck transition blocks all provisioning and removal on that Root, which leaves a clean reinstall as the only recovery. Index placement is the one placement strategy with time-derived claim IDs. After a restore it creates duplicate children paid for by Root and leaves orphans that Root still has registered. Restoring onto a different canister (relocation) leaves a canister whose Canic runtime refuses every managed call, while restore verification still reports success. (a)/(e): An unsealed Root snapshot, reachable only through the library's MaintenanceRoot scope, would load as an Open Root. Its drivers would resume, and its registry and pool inventory would be missing every canister created after the capture. A sealed snapshot loads as a Root that stays fenced forever, as designed. For sealed authorities, timer state after a load matches the fence: TIMERS_SUSPENDED and the ic-timers registry are restored together from the heap, and Root timer registrations are rejected while suspended. For unsealed members, the heap-side ic-timers registry is restored as it was. Whether the IC restores the global timer on load is platform behaviour I could not verify from this repository. Canic has no reconcile step after a load. The order in which backup and restore stop and start canisters also makes the known top-up retry classifier failure (xc-async-1) happen deterministically for children that are below their top-up threshold.

Checked and sound
  • A sealed Root or Coordinator loaded from a snapshot can never resume, because the resume check requires the canister-history count recorded at seal time (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/authority_restore/mod.rs:67-91, 121-154). The design doc says this is intentional (docs/design/archive/0.100-.../0.100-design.md:1728-1741), and a PocketIC test covers it (crates/canic-testing-internal/src/pic/fleet_registry/baseline.rs, restored_root_preserves_its_inventory_but_cannot_allocate).
  • Seal preparation rejects running or unmanaged timer claims, active async-job leases, in-flight Root funding requests, resumable ICP refills and funding policy rotation (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/timer/mod.rs:131-160, 471-484; crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:66-73). While suspended, register_lifecycle_once refuses new lifecycle timers (timer/mod.rs:351-356, 400-405), so an interleaved continuation cannot arm a driver after the seal.
  • Once a sealed snapshot is loaded, timers match the fence: the heap flag TIMERS_SUSPENDED and the ic-timers registry are restored together, and suspend_root has already cancelled every core claim (timer/mod.rs:174-187).
  • Child automatic top-up operation IDs come from a durable generation counter (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/async_job_recovery/mod.rs:49-57). A restored child that reuses an ID gets Root's cached receipt instead of a second transfer (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:128-136), and cycles it already received stay in its balance, which a load does not roll back.
  • Root child-allocation replay compares only operation ID, component, role and init args (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/authority_validation/mod.rs:93-117) and returns the retained terminal child (component_registry/mod.rs:1111-1123; workflow/component_rpc/lifecycle.rs:95-105). Restored parents using scaling or sharding placement, whose sequences are derived from state, therefore reconverge on the same child.
  • Component Directory synchronization tolerates a restored member: the progression check only requires a strictly newer revision and synchronization time (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/component_runtime.rs:354-384).
  • Store deletion-cycle reclaim and blob-storage project funding depend only on the live balance and keep no journal that a restore could roll back (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/wasm_store/mod.rs:38-83; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/blob_storage/billing/mod.rs:168-224).
  • Placement-receipt acknowledgement accepts repeats (AlreadyAbsent), so a restored parent that re-acknowledges is harmless (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/execute.rs:83-108).

Resumption of journals and drivers after upgrade, authority resume or a trapped driver, including ic-timers semantics

5 findings

I read the ic-timers 0.8.0 registry, runtime, control and platform code, plus its README. I also read the ic-cdk-timers 1.0.0 global_timer and timer_executor code and ic-cdk-executor 2.0.0's trap cancellation. The dependency facts are these. ic-timers keeps a volatile, heap-only registry capped at MAX_TIMER_REGISTRATIONS = 64. When the registry is full, register returns RegisterError::CapacityExceeded, and TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required turns that into a trap. dispatch_ordinary calls begin_ordinary, which sets the entry to Running, in the same message as the first poll of the consumer future. No Drop guard exists anywhere in ic-timers. ic-cdk-executor handles a trapped callback by cancelling (dropping) the task. Two failure modes follow. (1) A trap after an await leaves the entry Running forever: complete_ordinary never runs, and later schedule or reconcile calls on a Running control return no action and are only recorded as pending. (2) A trap before the first await rolls the registry back to Scheduled with its provider handle restored. ic-cdk-timers, however, gets reject code 5 and deletes the Once task, so the entry is Scheduled with a past deadline and never fires. ensure_scheduled uses Earliest selection and cannot replace it. The README confirms "Once / AfterCompletion: No automatic recovery"; only Watchdog survives failed work. On timer state: ic-timers snapshots (snapshot/model.rs) are inert observations holding identity, generation, state and counters, and carry no authority or Running timestamp. An upgrade wipes the heap and a new TimerEpoch starts. A canister-snapshot load restores the heap verbatim; Canic's prepare fence rejects both unmanaged and Running claims, so a sealed capture contains no lifecycle entries. ic-memory 0.14.3 recovers its ledger from the dual-slot commit store (MemoryManager ID 0) and fails closed on corruption. Sealed declaration snapshots reject duplicate keys and slots, the ledger rejects slot reuse and key moves, and Canic's policy pins disjoint core and control-plane ID ranges. No collision path found. Resumption matrix. Events are: A = Root post_upgrade, B = non-root post_upgrade, C = Coordinator upgrade, D = resume_authority_snapshot, E = trap after an await. For every control-plane family, D never rebuilds anything, but prepare also refuses while any lifecycle entry exists, so this only matters for drivers that are already dead. C loses everything, because the Coordinator has no post_upgrade and its endpoints then trap (already reported). - Registry mirror sync: A no; E replay re-arms, no dedup, so duplicates. New: an ack-less candidate can never complete. - Root removal: A, D and E never re-arm, and a replay does not re-arm either. - Root Component provisioning: A re-arms automatically (resume_after_restart). On E, only a Root upgrade re-arms it, because the Coordinator only polls. - Coordinator admission, rotation, root removal and provisioning: E re-arms only on a host command replay, and each replay adds a chain. - Store GC: B no; the Root's next GC request re-arms it. - Component allocation and bootstrap child allocation: A no; a replay after an upgrade re-arms. On E, a replay does not re-arm, because of the heap dedup set. - Non-bootstrap child allocation: completes synchronously inside the parent's ProvisionChild call, so a parent replay re-drives it. - Component and subtree removal: A no; a replay re-arms subject to the directory revalidation already reported, with duplicate chains. - Root admission: A no; the Coordinator's 1 s retries re-arm it, with duplicates. Core owners: - CycleWorkflow: A, B and D start it again. On E it is stuck until an upgrade (new). - Placement acknowledgement drain: B re-arms via bootstrap start(). On E it is stuck. - Root auth renewal: A and D re-arm it. On E it is stuck. - Pool maintenance: A and D re-arm it. On E its AfterCompletion claim is stuck. - Fixture importer: B re-arms it, and it survives E (Watchdog plus spawn). - ICP refill: Root upgrade is refused while a refill is active. A manual refill resumes only on replay; an automatic one resumes only through the top-up timer. - Blob billing: keeps no journal and is command-driven only. Journals that can stay InProgress with no re-arm path: - Root removal: holds the draining fence, the stopped pool, the funding fence, Store reclamation and deletion intents, the Root and Store cycles, and the Coordinator reservation that fences admission. - Component and child allocations whose driver trapped: they hold claimed or created canisters and install intents until an upgrade plus a replay. - The Root's initial Registry candidate whose acknowledgement failed: it permanently blocks this Root's join. - Root Component provisioning after a trapped driver: needs a Root upgrade, while the Coordinator busy-polls. - Retained core owners after a trap: automatic top-up, the ack drain and renewal stop. On Root, authority snapshots are then blocked. If an automatic ICP refill was left active, the only reset (an upgrade) is refused.

Checked and sound
  • ic-memory ledger recovery fails closed. LedgerCommitStore::recover checks the physical/logical generation match and integrity. recover_or_initialize initializes only an uninitialized store (ic-memory-0.14.3/src/ledger/mod.rs:100-147).
  • Memory-ID collisions are rejected at three layers: duplicate slots and keys at snapshot sealing (declaration.rs:454-470), slot reuse and key moves against history (ledger/claim.rs:38-58), and Canic's disjoint core and control-plane ranges (crates/canic-core/src/memory/policy.rs:67-99).
  • The fixture importer uses the Watchdog policy plus a spawned attempt behind a durable lease. The committed successor survives a trapped work message, and expired leases are abandoned and re-claimed (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/fixture_provisioning/timer/mod.rs:61-100).
  • AsyncJob leases prevent a watchdog-recovered attempt from overlapping a normal timer attempt, because claim returns Busy while an unexpired lease exists (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/async_job_recovery/mod.rs:273-301).
  • Root post_upgrade restores timer suspension from the durable fence before starting any service. It starts core services and the pool only when the Root is active and not sealed (crates/canic-core/src/lifecycle/upgrade/root.rs:74-83, crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/root.rs:167-173, crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/lifecycle.rs:959-989).
  • Root post_upgrade refuses an upgrade while an ICP refill is resumable, so an in-flight refill's heap state cannot be silently dropped (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/mod.rs:152-163).
  • Authority snapshot prepare rejects unmanaged lifecycle entries, Running claims and active async-job leases, so a sealed capture contains no half-run driver (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/timer/mod.rs:132-160, 255-281, 471-484).
  • Root Component provisioning is the one control-plane family resumed automatically on Root post_upgrade. It keeps persisted retry deadlines and ReviewRequired fences (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:180-230).

End-to-end Component-group provisioning: host, Coordinator, Root and members

6 findings

I followed one ProvisionComponents batch through all three stages. The host compiles a plan from the live Registry and sends it to the Coordinator by ingress, replaying the exact issued command at most once per run. The Coordinator validates the plan against the exact Registry version and the compiled configuration, stores the plan and its hash in one record, and accepts Roots one at a time. For each Root it sends the full batch with an unbounded-wait ProvisionComponents call. After that it only polls Root status, one Root at a time, through provisioning, fresh publication and activation. Scale-out synchronization is the only later hop that sends a command. Each Root runs its own timer-driven state machine: reserve, claim, install and Registry-commit one member per step, then finalize Provisioned. It publishes each member's Directory after it sees the Coordinator's published Registry, and it activates members once the Coordinator reports DirectoriesConfirmed. Per-member idempotency holds up well. Member operation IDs are deterministic, cursor checks tolerate one lost reservation or commit, installs record intent first and use Install mode (so a duplicate install cannot be destructive), and publication records a hash-bound intent before the call. Plan hash and member set cannot drift between Coordinator and Root. The request-size risk is also bounded: a per-Root batch is a subset of a plan that already fit through ingress, so the Coordinator-to-Root request cannot exceed the cross-subnet limit. The status reply is not bounded this way. The main defects are at the Coordinator/Root boundary. First, the Root status carries a Root-wide estate_funding_required flag, and the Coordinator handles that flag badly. For a Provisioned Root, the funding pause path tries to store a Provisioned response as the current Accepted cursor, which fails invariant validation. For an Accepted Root, the Root's own recorded wait failure hides the flag from the Coordinator. Either way the pause never commits, so the host is never asked to fund, and a routine post-batch pool refill on mainnet can wedge the operation. Second, every acceptance replay schedules a new Root driver. The Coordinator re-sends the full batch every second while its post-accept status read fails, so Root timer chains keep growing. Third, a ReviewRequired Root failure is terminal. There is no resume, abandon or release path: claimed canisters stay held and the Root and Fleet fences stay closed until a clean reinstall. Lesser issues: publication re-fetches the full Fleet Registry from the Coordinator for every member; an unchanged Root cursor is reported as a STATE_CONFLICT failure, which triggers host replays; and the status reply embeds the full per-member result with no size bound. Group removal and scale-in are absent by design. Root-side progress checks do re-read live authority (mirror version, partition revision, draining), but the known fenced operations keep these stable, apart from draining (cp-fleet-coordinator-3).

Checked and sound
  • Coordinator-to-Root request size is bounded by ingress: a per-Root batch is a subset of the plan the controller already sent by ingress, capped at crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:17-58, and root_acceptance_call adds only fixed fields (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:2685-2700). A request that validates cannot exceed the cross-subnet request limit.
  • All provisioning hops from the Coordinator use unbounded-wait calls and attach no cycles (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1197-1200, 1283-1288, 1336-1340), so provisioning has no lost-response cycle burn.
  • Acceptance is exactly replayable before any live prerequisite is re-read (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:95-99; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:279-292), and the stable store rejects any different record under the same operation ID (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/component_provisioning/mod.rs:463-472).
  • Member allocation identities are derived deterministically from (root, operation, plan_hash, placement, member path) (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:250-265). Reservation and Registry-commit steps tolerate exactly one lost local commit (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:1238-1283).
  • Duplicate installs are not destructive: advance_install records an InstallIntent, checks the observed module hash before re-installing (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/component_installation/mod.rs:771-850), and the management call always uses Install mode (crates/canic-core/src/infra/ic/mgmt/lifecycle.rs:80).
  • Directory publication records an intent before the effect, bound to the exact directory authority hash, and a replay must match it (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:856-941; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/top_level_activation/mod.rs:163-223).
  • Plan hash consistency: the Coordinator stores the hash it validated, and the scale-out exact-retry hash equals the validated scale-out hash (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/deployment_ledger/mod.rs:36-80; crates/canic-core/src/ops/component_provisioning_plan/mod.rs:337-360). Coordinator validators compare every Root response's operation_id, plan_hash, registry, digest and receipt hash (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/component_provisioning_reconciliation/mod.rs:136-214).
  • Cross-domain fences hold: admission transitions and funding rotations cannot start during an active provisioning (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/admission.rs:31-67; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/funding_rotation.rs:214-215). Every Coordinator commit is rejected while a rotation is active (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:2023-2031). Capacity import is mutually exclusive with an active batch (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:167).
  • Grouped Components are kept out of ordinary drivers and removal (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:3905-3910; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/mod.rs:4670-4685). Grouped Roots are kept out of RemoveRoot at the Coordinator (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/root_lifecycle.rs:49-100). This matches the documented absence of scale-in.

Replay-policy manifests versus actual command handler behaviour

5 findings

I traced every row in the Root, Coordinator, managed, Store, root-capability and endpoint manifests (crates/canic-core/src/replay_policy/*.rs) to its dispatch arm in crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/{root,fleet_coordinator,wasm_store,role}.rs and then into the handler. Nothing at runtime reads the manifests. The only runtime use of anything in replay_policy is the CostClass enum, which seven workflows pass to CostGuardOps::reserve with their own hard-coded windows, limits and reservations. No runtime code references the quota and cycle-reserve label constants. The tests check that labels are present (tests/cost.rs:53-78) and that each enum variant has one row, but never compare a row with handler behaviour. So the contract exists only as documentation, and several rows have already drifted from it. For paid effects, the handlers mostly hold up on their own terms. Root-capability ProvisionCanister, AllocatePlacementChild, RecycleCanister and RequestCycles reserve an operation-ID receipt with actor and payload-hash checks before authorization and effect. They mark ExternalEffectInFlight before the await and never delete a receipt once an effect has started. Replays after expiry are deduplicated by the control-plane journals keyed by (component, operation_id). AdoptStore, BootstrapStore, HandoffPoolCanister, ImportPoolCanister, MaintainPool, ReclaimDeletionCycles, RefillCycles, PublishReleaseSet and the root, Coordinator and Store value transfers are either receipt-protected or genuinely convergent. The ones that pay are cost-guarded. Label-to-runtime gaps: the chain-key and canister-signature quota labels map to no CostGuard at all. For GetOrCreateDelegationProof this is already reported as core-auth-1. New defects: (1) PrepareRoleAttestation's ROOT_CANISTER_SIGNATURE_PREPARE_QUOTA_V1 is implemented only as a pending-receipt quota. A synchronous prepare never leaves a pending receipt, so the quota never applies. Its committed receipts share root's replay store with root capabilities, count against root's global 10,000 and per-caller 512 caps, and are purged only by the root-capability path. Any active Component or child can therefore block every root capability request. (2) Exact replays of root ProvisionComponents (labelled response_idempotent) and SynchronizeRegistry (replay_protected) return the stored receipt, but each replay also schedules another self-rescheduling lifecycle timer chain with no deduplication. Replay is therefore not effect-free. (3) The manifest rows drift from runtime. Examples: the managed and Store RespondCapability rows say ManagementDeployment where the runtime is ValueTransfer; RetryPoolRefill says ValueTransfer where the runtime guard is ManagementDeployment; BootstrapStore is labelled as a deployment but has no guard; DEPLOYMENT_RESERVE_V1 reserves zero cycles. (4) The endpoint coverage test scans a hand-maintained list of four files, so the blob-storage endpoints, including the cycle-spending _immutableObjectStorageFundFromProjectCycles, sit outside the contract. (5) All deployment guards use root as the quota subject, so one Component's allocations consume the per-minute budget for the whole root.

Checked and sound
  • Root capability requests reserve a receipt keyed by command kind and operation ID, check actor and payload hash, and reserve before authorization and effect. They mark ExternalEffectInFlight before awaiting the lifecycle call (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/execute.rs:119, :248-254). abort only removes Reserved receipts, so receipts for effects that have started are never deleted (crates/canic-core/src/ops/replay/receipt.rs:474-480).
  • ProvisionCanister and RecycleCanister retries after the 300 s receipt expiry do not repeat the paid effect. The control-plane journals keyed by (component, operation_id) return the terminal binding or the Completed removal (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_rpc/lifecycle.rs:83-135, :148-181).
  • AdoptStore and BootstrapStore look up their retained receipt before any management or Store effect, and return it on an exact replay (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:114-123; crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/bootstrap/root_store/mod.rs:83-85).
  • HandoffPoolCanister is replay-convergent: it checks for a completed-handoff receipt, begin_handoff is idempotent for the same recipient, and it moves no cycles on replay (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:535-554; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1048-1124).
  • Replaying ImportPoolCanister on an already imported Ready asset only re-inspects it. Workload assets and Recycled-origin assets are rejected, so a replay never uninstalls a live workload (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:103-127, :299-337; crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:561-575).
  • ReclaimDeletionCycles converges on the account balance and is guarded as ValueTransfer, with a cycle reservation equal to the maximum transfer (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/wasm_store/mod.rs:37-83, :136-157). PublishReleaseSet reserves a DurablePublish guard: 10 per minute and 1B cycles (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/cost_guard.rs:27-30, :88-108).
  • RequestCycles reserves a ValueTransfer guard: the quota is per caller, the reservation equals the approved cycles, and the settlement identity is persisted in the receipt before deposit_cycles (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:413-420, :560-573).
  • PrepareDelegatedToken uses retention-bounded receipts with per-command purge (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/mod.rs:88-105; crates/canic-core/src/ops/replay/receipt.rs:202-220). PreviewCycleRefill dry-run takes no receipt and has no paid effect (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/manual.rs:26-49). The Component allocation scheduler is deduplicated (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:10-27).
  • Question (e): the variant-coverage tests build their variant sets from the real enum source via include_str!, not from hand-kept lists, and currently every Root, Coordinator, managed, Store and root-capability variant has exactly one row (crates/canic-core/src/replay_policy/tests/mod.rs:23-28, :119-147; tests/role_command.rs:9-43).

Fleet activation protocol and endpoint phase fences on Root, Store and non-root canisters

7 findings

I traced every generated endpoint through dispatch::preflight_endpoint and preflight_store_data_endpoint, the pure allowlists, the root command and status variant fences, the authority-restore fence, the macro Fleet-state guard, and the Store and Component activation state machines (ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs in full, plus mapper.rs, fixture/, workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs, workflow/component_runtime.rs and the control-plane callers). The fence is unconditional in the proc macro, including the `internal` marker and the raw-payload adapter. It is exact on name and call kind, and a contradictory record fails closed. What each role admits: - Prepared Root: public_status, observability, root_operation_status and root_status (queries), root_fixture_status (composite query) and root_command (update). A second, decoded-variant fence then admits only the bootstrap and recovery commands (AcceptFunding, Store and pool commands, ProvisionComponent(s), PublishReleaseSet, RespondCapability, SynchronizeRegistry and a few others). Each of these keeps its own controller, Coordinator or member authentication. - Prepared non-root: public_status, observability, auth_status, admission_status and control_status (queries) and the whole canic_command, with no variant fence. - Prepared Store: effectively its entire surface (all StoreCommand variants and all four data lanes), gated only by per-variant caller checks. - Active: everything is admitted. Non-root non-Store canisters additionally get the fixture-readiness gate, which canic_command bypasses. The Coordinator skip at fleet_activation.rs:414 is justified. The Coordinator has no FleetActivation record, and it commits genesis synchronously in init under a controller check, so there is no pre-authority window. The authority-restore fence still applies to it. Store activation binding is sound: - PrepareFleetCredential and ActivateFleet are root-only. - The operation id must match exactly. - The credential must be exact, or advance by one while Prepared. - The evidence hash is recomputed from the stored identity and cascade. - Root verifies identity, cascade, credential and phase before and after, and reconciles lost responses through status. Component Directory authority cannot be downgraded or swapped. Prepared preparation is set once exactly, and Active synchronization requires stable identity, a strictly advancing Component head and a non-regressing Fleet revision, plus full structural validation. Main defects found: 1. (High) A root Fleet-state cascade (SetCyclesFunding or SetFleetStatus, including an idempotent re-issue) reaches every committed partition, including Components still Prepared. prepare_applied_snapshot writes prepared_state_snapshot_hash into the Component record. activate_component_runtime then rejects that record permanently as obsolete evidence, and nothing clears the hash for Component runtimes. 2. (Medium) Newly provisioned canisters never receive the current Fleet mode or cycles kill switch. They start from the compiled init_mode with funding enabled, so new subtrees ignore a paused-funding or Readonly Fleet. 3. (Medium) The documented `init_mode = "readonly"|"disabled"` deadlocks a fresh root. The Fleet guard blocks every activation and bootstrap command, and the Prepared fence blocks the only two commands that could change the mode. 4. (Low) Smaller issues: ApplicationSession and PrepareDelegatedToken reachable before activation and before fixture readiness; data-lane preflight selected by Rust function name; RespondCapability authorized in workflow rather than at the endpoint; and dead activation code. Not covered: - Whether a demoted or draining Fleet-service Authority keeps require_service_authority true after a Directory it cannot accept. service_authority_matches checks only the immutable deployment and the Active phase. - IC delivery ordering for bounded-wait cascade messages. - The inspect_message cost aspects already reported in round one. - The root_status and root_auth_status variant semantics beyond the fence lists. - PocketIC-level confirmation of findings 1–3.

Checked and sound
  • Fence injection is unconditional: expand() always emits `#preflight(#call_ident)` before the access stage (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:118-123), independent of `internal`/`public`, and the raw payload adapter invokes the wrapper so preflight still runs (expand/mod.rs:348-352).
  • Pure allowlists match exact endpoint name AND call kind and default to Fenced (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/fleet_activation.rs:32-115); composite queries are admitted only for canic_root_fixture_status on a Prepared root.
  • Root multiplexed methods get a second, decoded-variant Prepared fence placed after caller authentication and before any effect (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:371-397; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:457-499), and status selectors reuse it (root.rs:1108-1121).
  • Coordinator fence skip is justified: the Coordinator has no FleetActivation record and commits genesis synchronously in init under a controller check (crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/fleet_coordinator.rs init; crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:182-199); the authority-restore fence still applies to it (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/authority_restore.rs:196-201).
  • Authority-restore composition fails closed: updates only, only the role command endpoint while sealed, then only decoded recovery variants, checked before dispatch on Root and Coordinator (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/authority_restore.rs:19-39; workflow/runtime/authority_restore.rs:89-111; root.rs:362-370; fleet_coordinator.rs:103-110).
  • Store activation binding: ActivateFleet/PrepareFleetCredential are root-only at the endpoint (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/wasm_store.rs:81-94); ops require exact operation id, exact-or-plus-one credential while Prepared and exact when Active, Applied (non-Source) cascade, and an evidence hash recomputed from stored identity/cascade (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:661-790).
  • Root validates the Store's fleet, operation id, release build, cascade, credential, manifests and phase/timestamp consistency before and after each step, and reconciles lost responses via the status query (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:584-610, 699-755); Prepared root cannot change Fleet state between PrepareFleetActivation and Resume because SetFleetStatus/SetCyclesFunding are not Prepared-admitted.
  • Component Directory authority cannot be downgraded or swapped: Prepared preparation is exact-once (ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:293-313); Active sync requires stable Component identity, strictly advancing registry revision/content hash/timestamp and non-regressing Fleet revision (mod.rs:357-386; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/component_runtime.rs:353-383) plus full identity/service/group validation (component_runtime.rs:330-653).
  • State cascades cannot be reordered into a downgrade: each fanout hop re-checks the snapshot against current local Fleet state before every send (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/cascade/state.rs:140-148).
  • The status mapper fails closed on any contradictory role/evidence/manifest combination and fixture assignments are rebound to the installation identity on every read (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mapper.rs:27-215; fixture/mod.rs:24-65).
  • Standalone-local bypass is fail-closed by default (Managed) and only selectable via start_local!, which compile-errors for root (crates/canic-core/src/model/fleet_activation/endpoint_mode.rs:19-22; crates/canic/src/macros/start.rs:651-652).
  • Root Fleet-admission participant compilation requires Active partitions and fences catalog mutation (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:268-300), so Prepared Components are not admission targets.

Application session establishment, subject substitution and scope authorization

4 findings

I traced the whole session lane. It starts at the `canic_command::ApplicationSession` endpoint (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:613), goes through `AuthApi::establish_application_session` (api/auth/application_session.rs:63-159), `AuthOps::verify_token` and the verifier (ops/auth/token/mod.rs:181, ops/auth/delegated/verify.rs:105-290), then `ApplicationSessionWorkflow::establish_verified` (workflow/auth/application_sessions.rs:118-207), the pure admission, narrowing and eligibility policy (domain/policy/pure/auth/application_authorization.rs) and the atomic state ops (ops/storage/auth/application_sessions.rs). On the read side I followed the synchronous `authorize_local_application` access path (access/auth/mod.rs:46-104) into the pure decision. The proof that binds the session key to the subject is the issuer's IC canister signature over the canonical claims hash. The claims carry presenter == subject == the prepare caller (prepare.rs:147-148), the Fleet audience, role grants, expiry and an issuer-derived nonce. The issuer signature is pinned to the issuer canister id and seed. The certificate is pinned by a root chain-key batch signature, the Merkle witness and exact certificate/leaf equality. At establishment the verifier requires presenter == msg_caller == subject. The model constructors reject any session or replay whose transport caller differs from its subject, and so does record decoding (authority.rs:47, 223, 319). Subject substitution in access/auth/mod.rs is therefore the identity: a caller cannot act as another user. Token forwarding by a canister fails on the presenter check. The proof is bound to the Fleet key (which includes the network id), the target role, an expiry of at most 60 s and a nonce. It is not bound to one canister. As the 0.105 design states, one proof can open one session on each canister of the granted role in the Fleet, but only by the same caller. Replay is enforced per target by a tombstone that lasts until the proof expires and survives clear, replacement and generation change. An exact retry returns a session only for the same caller, proof and request hash, in the current generation and before expiry, and never extends it. A cleared session cannot be brought back with the same proof. Requested scopes must be in both the local `allowed_scopes` and the verified grant for the local role, and that grant must be a subset of the root-signed certificate grants. Every authorization (update, query or composite) re-checks expiry, Fleet, role, generation, subject admissibility and scope, without mutating state. No await separates retry resolution, verification and commit. Metrics, replay actors and retention quotas use the caller, which always equals the subject, so caller and subject cannot be mixed up. I found no authentication or authorization bypass. The weaknesses already reported in round one remain the main risks and are not repeated here: self-issuable declared scopes, anonymous callers accepted by the token lane, and global capacity caps. The new defects are lower severity: - (a) Establishment rejects proofs whose issue time is ahead of the verifier clock, ignoring the 60 s skew the verifier itself allows, and reports this as `SECURITY_INVALID`. - (b) Admission counts expired but not yet pruned records, and session pruning is gated behind unrelated intent-cleanup errors. A cleanup outage therefore becomes a login lockout. - (c) Tokens carry the certificate grants twice. With large but policy-valid grant sets they exceed the fixed 16 KiB `canic_command` cap that Establish must fit in. - (d) The operator session audit is reachable only by Root, and nothing relays it. I also noted that the workflow's `CallerMismatch` eligibility check is vacuous, because the workflow derives the caller from the verified presenter. The real binding rests entirely on `verify_token(caller: msg_caller)` in the API adapter. The generation transition table matches the design, but because config is embedded per release build it effectively only acts at initialization.

Checked and sound
  • Caller/subject identity cannot diverge: issuance sets presenter=subject=prepare caller (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/prepare.rs:147-148); verification requires presenter==msg_caller and presenter==subject (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/verify.rs:211-216); VerifiedApplicationAuthority, LocalApplicationSession and LocalApplicationReplay constructors reject mismatches (crates/canic-core/src/model/auth/application_authorization/authority.rs:47-49, 223-225, 319-321), as does record decode (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/auth/application_sessions.rs:654-687). Subject substitution in access/auth/mod.rs:65-80 is therefore the identity.
  • Issuer proof is pinned to the issuer canister id and the fixed seed before BLS canister-signature verification (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/issuer_canister_sig.rs:225-247); the root chain-key proof binds root id, policy, batch/leaf windows, Merkle witness and exact cert/leaf equality including grants and expiry (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/chain_key.rs:173-215, 322-392; crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/token/verification.rs:163-165).
  • Audience is the full FleetKey (network id + fleet id) for both token and cert (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/audience.rs:98-100; verify.rs:271-290); token grants must be a subset of root-signed cert grants and scopes are taken only from the grant for the local compiled role (audience.rs:102-119).
  • Scope composition is closed: requested scopes must be in local allowed_scopes (crates/canic-core/src/api/auth/application_session.rs:291-305, config validated sorted at crates/canic-core/src/config/validation/component_spec.rs:145-156) and a subset of the verified local-role grant (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/auth/application_authorization.rs:218-232); scopes are replaced on renewal, never unioned.
  • Replay semantics match the design: tombstone per consumed proof until proof expiry, retained across clear/replace/generation change; exact retry only for same caller+proof+request hash+current generation+unexpired; conflicting reuse denied before verification (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/auth/application_sessions.rs:270-317, 397-409); proof lifetime capped at 60 s (application_authorization.rs:195-204) and tombstone removal (application_sessions.rs:427) coincides with verifier expiry (verify.rs:246), so there is no resurrection window.
  • Every authorization re-evaluates expiry, Fleet, role, generation, live subject admissibility and scope with no mutation, logging or await, so query and composite callers get the same checks (crates/canic-core/src/access/auth/mod.rs:46-104; application_authorization.rs:129-181).
  • Establishment is fully synchronous inside canic_command (no await between retry resolution, verification and commit) and commits sessions+replay in one validated stable-cell write with full index/invariant rebuild (application_sessions.rs:340-395, 487-494); restore re-validates every bound and binding synchronously in init/post_upgrade (application_sessions.rs:511-652; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/mod.rs:127-134).
  • Positive verification cache key binds proof hash, claims hash, issuer-proof hash and caller, and claim/cert/time/audience/scope checks re-run on every hit (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/cache.rs:32-67; crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/token/verification.rs:107-125).
  • Generation transition table (disable/enable, Fleet, role, verifier root, registry epoch, scope removal, max-TTL reduction) is implemented as specified and reconciled before ingress in init and post_upgrade (application_authorization.rs:30-85; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:243, 372).

Multi-root Fleet trust: cross-root peers, Registry mirrors and per-subtree trust anchors

4 findings

I traced how a Fleet with two or more Fleet Subnet Roots authenticates cross-root callers and keeps its per-root Registry mirrors aligned. (a) Root A authenticates a FleetService ProvisionPeer caller only against its own validated Registry mirror. The caller must be exactly one member of the named service, its owner root must be Active and remote, A must be Active, and the caller's expected_registry must equal A's mirror version exactly. A removed, retired or recycled member cannot pass, even through a stale mirror. Registry services are append-only, grouped (service-member) Components can never be drained, and a root that hosts service members can never be reserved for draining. So a stale mirror can only fail closed: members added after A's mirror are rejected. (b) Delegated tokens and role attestations trust one root_canister_id and one chain-key public key, both taken from App-wide config (or from the canister's own root). Cross-root authorization therefore fails closed and never over-trusts. The cost is that issuers and attestation subjects under every other root are unusable. (c) Coordinator publications are not applied atomically across roots, and are often not applied at all. Admission, root draining and removal, and scale-out publications advance only the roots each flow calls. A scale-out's confirmation set is validated to exactly the batch roots plus the roots that host that service. Once a root is activated it has no resync entry point. Every later root-side check compares the Coordinator's or caller's version for exact equality, or for coverage, against the root's own mirror. A root that falls behind therefore permanently rejects funding requests, component-operation acceptance and directory synchronization, funding-policy rotation, and its own removal. No root ever compares itself with its peers. This is the main new finding. It extends the round-one finding cp-root-admission-funding-3 (admission only) to root removal and scale-out, with consequences for the whole Fleet: a multi-root Fleet can never be retired. (d) I found no reachable root-to-root or Coordinator-to-root message over 2 MiB. The Registry is capped at 2 MiB canonical, and each root batch is a subset of a plan that arrives by ingress. (e) Host and CLI paths fail closed on multi-root Fleets instead of picking the first root: unique_fleet_subnet_root, and explicit root principals for convert and topup. There is one new functional gap: `canic backup create` refuses every multi-root Fleet, including subtree backups, because the backup plan model has a single root. There is also a smaller DoS surface: ProvisionPeer revalidates the whole mirror before it checks the caller. Test coverage is thin in this area. No PocketIC test covers ScaleOut or multi-root root removal, and no Canic client builds the FleetService peer request.

Checked and sound
  • FleetServicePeerOps::resolve accepts a caller only if it is exactly one Registry service member, rejects duplicates, requires the caller's owner root to be Active and different from the target root, requires the target root itself to be Active, and re-derives and topology-validates the requester binding (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_service_peer/mod.rs:36-94, 144-176).
  • Retained FleetService origins are re-checked against the current mirror on every later step: registry coverage must be monotonic and the requester must match exactly (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/authority_validation/mod.rs:149-176). ProvisionPeer also requires the caller's expected_registry to equal the local mirror exactly (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:925).
  • Service members cannot be removed or recycled, so a stale mirror cannot admit a former member. Registry service updates are append-only (crates/canic-core/src/ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:585-668). Grouped Components cannot be drained (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/mod.rs:4661-4684). Roots that host service members cannot be reserved for draining or published as draining or removed (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/root_lifecycle.rs:66-101; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1722, 1763, 1837).
  • Every mirror read is fully revalidated: manifest, version, root entry, derived Directory, and previous revision strictly below the current one (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:58-109). Mirror transitions cannot regress (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:654-675).
  • Initial Fleet activation is atomic across roots. Joining is allowed only before activation, and activation requires every root to acknowledge the exact version (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:389-586; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/root_lifecycle.rs:182-200).
  • Cross-root auth fails closed rather than over-trusting. GetOrCreateDelegationProof requires a local active Component member (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:295-311; crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/component_auth/mod.rs:31-52), and role-attestation proofs are verified against one configured root and the IC root key (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/attestation.rs:156-170).
  • Only controllers and non-Removed snapshot roots can read the Coordinator Registry (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:462-484; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/root_lifecycle.rs:112-124).
  • CLI multi-root handling fails closed instead of picking the first root. unique_fleet_subnet_root returns AmbiguousFleetSubnetRoot (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/inventory/mod.rs:139-150), and cycles convert and topup require an explicit root principal that exists in the topology (crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/convert/mod.rs:39-49; crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/wallet.rs:380-394).
  • Message sizes stay within limits. The Registry is capped at 2 MiB canonical bytes (crates/canic-core/src/ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:43, 943), and each root batch sent to a root is a subset of a plan that already arrived by ingress, so no Coordinator-to-root or root-to-root request exceeds 2 MiB.

Authority and residue that survive canister recycling into the shared pool

5 findings

Recycling a retired Component (delete_component and delete_subtree_leaf, then canister_pool::recycle) fences the asset with a pending recycling claim. It then revokes the Wasm Store fixture grant, stops the canister, rewrites controllers to the exact Root plus recovery set, calls uninstall_code and re-reads the balance. Membership removal deletes the Registry partition and principal index and calls complete_recycling, which turns the asset Ready so any allocation on that Root can claim it. The new claimant gets a fresh CanisterInitPayload with its own binding, root and parent. Everything inside the canister, and controller authority, is therefore reset correctly. Everything outside the canister that is keyed on the raw principal is not reset. I traced the principal-keyed stores across crates. - Root issuer policies and renewal templates have no removal path, and the control plane never touches them. Root keeps signing certs for the principal and installs them on whichever workload next occupies it. That occupant can also request them through GetOrCreateDelegationProof, so it inherits the retired issuer's Fleet-audience token-minting grants (high). While the principal sits empty in the pool, the failed install is classified non-retryable and stops the renewal timer for all issuers. - Root replay receipts bind only (command, operation_id, raw caller) and are served before authorization. Unacknowledged placement, in-flight and RecoveryRequired receipts never expire, and workload-derived operation IDs restart at the same values after reinstall. A new occupant can therefore replay the old occupant's placement result, receiving a foreign child principal that it registers, or be permanently blocked from funding. - Root's lifetime per-child funding ledger (100 TC default cap) is keyed by principal and never cleared. - On the parent side, recycling completes before the still-Active parent's direct-child list is resynchronized. The parent's sharding, index and scaling registries are never pruned, so lookups keep routing to the recycled principal, and an empty children list even disables the sharding filter. - Cashier storage credit, Cycles Ledger and ICP balances, and ICRC-2 approvals owned by the principal are neither observed nor swept. The old tenant's blobs keep billing the account the next tenant inherits. - A recycle whose reset failed before uninstall still completes membership removal, and Root draining then hands the un-reset canister, with the old tenant's state, to the asset recipient. Several areas hold up. FleetService member lists and remote-Root Registry mirrors never name a recycled principal: grouped Components cannot take the ordinary retirement path, and the Coordinator refuses Root removal while grouped placements or service members reference the Root. Role attestations are re-derived from the current Registry binding. Application sessions are self-bound and wiped by uninstall. Canic only ever writes controllers, so freezing threshold, reserved-cycles limit and log visibility stay uniform creation defaults. Chunked installs use the Store's chunk store rather than the target's. One fix covers most findings: bind principal-keyed authority to the managed identity (ComponentInstanceId plus install id), or add a revocation phase that runs before complete_recycling. Not covered: - IC semantics for canister logs and chunk store on uninstall_code, which cannot be verified from the repository. - The external Cashier and gateway protocol, whose behavior I inferred from the client code. - Operator-managed Fleet admission principals, which have the same principal-keyed pattern (no retirement hook) but which I did not trace. - canic-host reuse of principals across clean reinstalls. - Snapshot residue, which was already reported (cp-pool-provisioning-4). Inherited snapshots also consume the next tenant's snapshot quota and storage billing.

Checked and sound
  • Pool reset rewrites controllers to the exact Root plus recovery set and uninstalls before readiness (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:672-689). Reinspection and install both require exact root controllers (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:657-663; component_installation/mod.rs:962-965, 976-989), so a previous owner cannot keep controller authority.
  • Fixture grants are revoked on the Wasm Store before physical reset, and every Store await is fenced by the pending recycling claim (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/fixture/mod.rs:22-70; workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:622-628).
  • For top-level Components, Root's principal index entry is removed in the same transaction as the partition, and complete_recycling runs in the same message (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:5681-5701; workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1607-1626). Child commits reject an already-indexed principal (storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:5265-5270).
  • FleetService members and Component Group members cannot take the ordinary draining path (ops/component_registry/mod.rs:4661-4668; component_retirement/mod.rs:113). The Coordinator refuses Root removal while grouped placements or service members reference the Root (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_lifecycle.rs:66-95). Remote-Root Registry mirrors used by FleetServicePeerOps::resolve (ops/fleet_service_peer/mod.rs:36-94) therefore never name a recycled principal.
  • The new claimant is installed with a freshly built binding, root, parent and install_id (component_installation/mod.rs:370-420, 476-515), and the binding is verified by querying the installed canister (component_installation/mod.rs:741-753, 997-1012). Stale env root and parent bindings do not survive.
  • Role attestation issuance re-derives role and subnet from the caller's current Registry binding (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/admission.rs:44-76). Verification requires subject == caller (access/auth/attestation.rs:21-29), so a new occupant cannot obtain an attestation for the old role.
  • Application sessions require presenter == subject == caller and are revalidated against the current authority generation (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/auth/application_authorization.rs:158-166, 181-184). Sessions held on a recycled verifier are wiped by uninstall.
  • Canic only ever writes the controllers setting: the only CanisterSettings constructions are canister_pool/mod.rs:547 and 678, capacity_import/mod.rs:133 and fleet_subnet_root.rs:210. Workloads are not their own controllers. Freezing threshold, reserved-cycles limit and log visibility of Canic-created assets therefore stay uniform creation defaults, with no tenant-specific residue.
  • The recycled canister's own cycle balance is re-observed after uninstall and recorded on the pool asset (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:631-633, 689), so its residual cycles stay controlled pool inventory.
  • Installs stream from the Wasm Store's chunk store (component_installation/mod.rs:352-368), so Canic leaves no chunk-store residue in the target canister.

Fleet-ensure plan compiler versus canister-side expectations

5 findings

I traced compile_plan end to end in crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/policy/mod.rs. That covers create_plan, reuse_plan, retire_plan/append_retirement_actions, resolved_controllers, append_target_funding, the startup-funding tranche and continuation prepay, pool-reconciliation and estate funding, required_root_pool_creations, maximum_observation_count/effect_observation_policy, and operation_id. I compared each decision with what the executor does (workflow/mod.rs ordered_actions/action_order/apply, ops/platform.rs apply_* and observe_effect) and with what the canisters do (canister_pool refill/reset/claim, component_registry creation plans, fleet_subnet_root Store adoption, and canic-core role-based initial_cycles resolution). The compiler is careful arithmetically. Everything is checked u128. Per-action Ledger timestamps are unique among withdraws. Controllers for Pool, Store and Root match what Root and Coordinator enforce. Create and Fund fee accounting balances against terminal conservation. The defects come from parts of the compiler's model that the runtime does not share. First, retirement reserves material_threshold plus the drain's maximum execution burn inside the source, but Delete allows only material_threshold to remain. Delete therefore always refuses unless the drain happens to burn exactly its bound, and a later replan cannot drain the now-stopped canister. The unit-test mock hides this because it deducts exactly amount plus the maximum burn. Second, creation fee authority is one operator-supplied scalar frozen in the seed, and Root derives its fee at runtime from ic0.cost_create_canister. Any pending or required Root pool creation on two Root subnets makes every compile fail with MixedSubnetCreationFees. So a multi-subnet fleet whose Roots both wait for Ledger funding can never be funded. A fee mismatch likewise blocks all planning, and the CLI refuses to change the fee on a non-fresh estate. Third, host validation checks only each Component Spec's own initial_cycles against the pool readiness floor. Root claims child canisters by the child role's initial_cycles, so larger child roles can never be allocated. Fourth, pool reconciliation strictly takes precedence over all other protocol work. One Failed asset that Root cannot reinspect (the Root-side defect cp-pool-provisioning-3) therefore turns every plan into a funding-plus-import plan that always fails, and the InProgress journal wedges the fleet. On operation_id: reusing it for the same desired is deliberate. It lets the Coordinator's ProvisionComponents status be resumed, and a clean reinstall wipes the Coordinator. Cycles Ledger deduplication does not treat a new review as a duplicate, because created_at_time is the nanosecond review time plus a per-action offset. Within one plan, the pool-reconciliation withdraw and the FundEstate transfer share offsets, but they use different Ledger methods and recipients. The reinstall successor replans with prior.planned_at_time, but the preparation plan contains only SealAuthority actions, so no Ledger collision is possible. Stall bounds count consecutive observations without progress, capped at 64 for paced protocol steps, reset on progress, and Stalled can be resumed. I found no wedge caused by fleet size there.

Checked and sound
  • Create fee accounting matches execution: apply_create sends requested_initial_cycles + management_creation_fee (ops/platform.rs:2725-2734), and the plan counts the initial cycles as new funding and the Ledger and creation fees as unavoidable fees (policy/mod.rs:1531-1534). Terminal conservation subtracts exactly those fees (workflow/mod.rs:3666-3678).
  • When the fees agree, the host's estate creation debit (floor + margin + management fee + Ledger fee, policy/mod.rs:2546-2559) equals Root's required refill funding: ledger_amount = floor + margin + cost_create_canister, plus the Ledger fee (canister_pool/refill.rs:368-379, 448-454).
  • Pool asset controllers in desired match Root's root_controllers (recovery controllers + Root): generate/mod.rs:1290-1299 against ids/fleet_topology/mod.rs:253-259. The temporary operator controller on fresh pool assets is removed by a planned SetControllers (policy/mod.rs:1509-1577).
  • Store controllers (operator + recovery + Root) match Root's sibling-Store adoption expectation of recovery + installation controller + Root (generate/mod.rs:1243-1263; canic-control-plane workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:181-189).
  • Controller canisters must be distinct, earlier desired roles (policy/mod.rs:2122-2141). With action_order sorting all Creates first as a stable sort, a controller always exists before the canisters it controls are created.
  • Every Cycles Ledger withdraw in a plan gets a distinct created_at_time: T+index for configured canisters, and T+N+k for pool reconciliation (policy/mod.rs:380-384, 900-913). Estate transfers share offsets with pool reconciliation but use icrc1_transfer to a different recipient, so deduplication cannot collide.
  • The reinstall successor compiles with prior.planned_at_time (workflow/reinstall/mod.rs:286-296), but the preparation plan holds only SealAuthority actions (policy/reinstall/mod.rs:204-221), so no Ledger identity is reused.
  • Reusing operation_id for an unchanged desired is intentional (workflow/mod.rs:650-657). ProvisionComponents must carry exactly the plan's operation id (policy/mod.rs:551-556), and a retained Coordinator status must equal the newly compiled request (ops/current_protocol/mod.rs:857-882), so a replay cannot be misattributed.
  • The Ledger fee is checked against live observation before compiling (policy/mod.rs:357-362). Estate funding owners are bound to the live Root principal (policy/mod.rs:2643-2680). Pool withdraws first prove Root pool membership (ops/platform.rs:2441-2468; ops/effect_preparation/mod.rs:28-57).
  • Tranche selection drops trailing protocol actions until burn fits the available cycles, and it restores startup funding if provisioning is dropped (policy/mod.rs:3169-3222; startup_funding/planning/mod.rs:37-69).
  • The paced stall limit is max(configured, min(topology_bound, 64)) on a counter of consecutive observations without progress, reset whenever progress_identity changes (policy/mod.rs:3501-3506; workflow/mod.rs:1858-1864). Large fleets do not scale this counter.
  • Host and Root agree on pool capacity: both exclude the Store asset and include pending creations (policy/mod.rs:2975-3016; canic-control-plane ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1256-1277).

Host and CLI Candid mirrors, decode-failure handling and decode quotas versus canister interfaces

5 findings

I compared every hand-written CandidType envelope in canic-host and canic-cli that talks to a Canic canister against the macro_rules unions in crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/{root,role,fleet_coordinator,wasm_store}.rs and the shared DTO unions in canic-control-plane/src/dto.
