That covers about 45 enums across current_inventory, current_inventory/ordinary, current_protocol and its fixture module, capacity_import (transport/root, admission observers), funding_observation, install_history, authority_seal, component_operation, observability, observatory, startup_funding, reinstall membership, generate, platform.rs, and CLI admission, cycles convert, cycles funding, auth, inspect and info_subnets. I also checked the canister-side mirrors in the Coordinator (RemoteRootCommand), root_admission, component_provisioning and core rpc. Variant names, method routing and payload types agree everywhere. Payloads are the shared canic-core/control-plane DTOs, so only the envelopes are mirrored by hand. Candid decodes variants by the value's tag (candid de.rs:1446-1473), so partial mirrors and the merged Status/OperationStatus request enums decode correctly. The one real drift is in Result wrapping: `canic cycles funding` wraps its Registry reply in a second Result. It fails to decode on every run. I traced how a reply that fails to decode is classified for each paid or state-changing caller. Every path treats it as an unknown outcome and replays with the same identity. fleet ensure leaves the effect at Intent and observes before resubmitting (workflow/mod.rs:1776-1796). Component operations query progress before resubmitting the retained operation_id. Capacity import maps the failure to RootResponseInvalid, queries status first and spends its step budget. The Coordinator's AcceptFunding path propagates the error and keeps its intent. CLI convert reuses its pending log. None of these paths completes falsely or resubmits under a new identity just because a reply failed to decode. The failures already reported in round one (bounded-wait cycles, typed Err treated as a rejection, Duplicate misreads) are separate. InspectionReserveRequired is matched on every InspectCanister caller. Capacity import, however, collapses it into a generic ObservationUnavailable without a reserve preflight. On the canister side, no public update or inspect argument type contains a vector whose elements can decode from zero bytes. The only Vec<Option<_>> in the DTOs is in a response. Typed decode cost is therefore proportional to payload bytes, and the update path's 10,000 skipping quota bounds skipping. The inspect_message hooks call candid::decode_one with no quota at all, so a skip bomb (an extra `vec null` field) runs until the inspect-message instruction limit. It costs node compute, not cycles. The more consequential inspect_message gap is different. For every method other than the command union, the hooks accept any payload up to 16 KiB whatever the method is. Public query methods can therefore be invoked as replicated ingress updates, which the canister pays for. On root and the Coordinator that includes status lookups that scan the whole registry or history for anonymous callers. Smaller issues: the observatory asks the Coordinator for Metrics and History variants it does not expose, and capacity import hides a Root that is short of liquid cycles behind a generic observation failure.

Checked and sound
  • Root command/status mirrors match the root macro enums by variant name and payload: current_protocol/mod.rs:167-218 vs root.rs:16-147 and 1054-1103 (MaintainPool, ImportPoolCanister, AdoptStore, BootstrapStore, PrepareStoreFixture with inner Result, PrepareComponentRegistry, SynchronizeRegistry, OperationAccepted); capacity_import/transport/root/mod.rs:23-53 (ImportPoolCapacity, PoolImport, PoolImportContext, Coordinator Registry); install_history/mod.rs:20-27; authority_seal/mod.rs:28-46; component_operation/ops/transport/mod.rs:41-63; generate/mod.rs:734-744
  • Operation-status routing is consistent: every mirror sending OperationStatusRequest targets CANIC_ROOT_OPERATION_STATUS and decodes Operation(dto::root::RootOperationStatusResponse) (current_protocol/mod.rs:1798-1822, ordinary/mod.rs:207-211, startup_funding/observation/binding/mod.rs:30-56, cycles/convert/response.rs:20-28 plus request.rs:17-21, fleet_coordinator workflow mod.rs:112-126 and 1277-1302)
  • Payload types in all mirrors are the shared canic-core/canic-control-plane DTOs, so only the envelope enums are hand-maintained; CLI copies (cycles/funding.rs:64-174) match CoordinatorFundingStatusResponse, FleetFundingPolicyRotationStatusPhase and RootFundingStatusResponse field for field (fleet_coordinator.rs dto:136-223, dto/root.rs:86-112)
  • Candid decodes variants by the value's tag (candid-0.10.37 de.rs:1446-1473), so partial response mirrors and merged request enums such as RootInventoryStatusRequest (current_inventory/mod.rs:100-114) decode correctly as long as the value's variant exists
  • InspectionReserveRequired is handled on every root InspectCanister caller: current_inventory/mod.rs:1605-1611, funding_observation/transport/mod.rs:373-389, observability/mod.rs:151-167, platform.rs:507-525 (into_status), capacity management/mod.rs:97-103
  • fleet ensure treats any platform.apply error, including a reply that fails to decode, as an unknown outcome: the effect stays at Intent, stalled_observations is bounded, and the next pass observes before resubmitting the same identity (workflow/mod.rs:1776-1796, 1824-1856)
  • Component operations observe progress before any submit and replay the retained operation_id, so a lost or undecodable ProvisionComponent reply cannot duplicate the allocation (component_operation/workflow/mod.rs:84-108, ops/mod.rs:143-153)
  • The Coordinator's AcceptFunding and ProvisionComponents paths propagate reply-decode errors with `?` and keep their intent; an unexpected Ok variant becomes conflict, not success (canic-control-plane workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1191-1234)
  • The authority seal checks the exact PrepareAuthoritySnapshot and AuthorityRestore wire types against the bound Candid before any call (authority_seal/contract/mod.rs:33-64)
  • The observatory decodes replies with both decoding and skipping quotas (observatory/ops/transport/mod.rs:369-384)
  • External ICP Ledger, CMC and Cycles Ledger mirrors match the upstream interfaces (operator_mint/wire/mod.rs:6-65, icp/cycles_ledger/mod.rs:6-62, platform.rs:81-91 and 576-615)
  • No public update or inspect argument type has vectors whose elements decode from zero bytes; the only Vec<Option<_>> is in the TemplateStagingStatusResponse response (canic-control-plane dto/template/mod.rs:395), and the update path uses skipping_quota 10_000 (canic-macros expand/mod.rs:333-334; ic-cdk-macros export.rs:258-259)
  • Nested Result replies are decoded with the right nesting where the canister returns them explicitly: canic_wasm_store_publish_fixture and canic_root_fixture_status (fixture/mod.rs:98-104 and 169-175 vs wasm_store.rs:369-373 and root.rs:1200-1206)

criticalreproducedcore-intent-replay-1 · liveness · high confidence
Committed resource totals are never reclaimed while cost-guard quota keys are per-60-second bucket, so the 1,000-identity cap permanently blocks every cost-guarded operation on root after about 1,000 active quota minutes
crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:1670

Failure scenario

1. A root funds 50 children. Each child's automatic top-up calls RequestCycles a few times a day. Each call runs `execute_authorized_request_cycles` -> `CostGuardWorkflow::reserve` and later `complete`, leaving a committed row for (child, minute). 2. After about 1,000 such rows (days for a modest fleet, sooner once provisioning or refill rows are added), `IntentStore::totals_len()` equals 1,000. 3. The next RequestCycles falls in a new minute: `enforce_quota` passes (new key, used = 0), then `try_reserve` returns ResourceTotalRecordCapacityReached (CAPACITY_LIMIT). 4. Every later cost-guarded root operation also fails permanently: child funding, component provisioning, ICP refill, template publication. Each new minute is a new key. 5. Children's top-up treats this as a non-retryable exhaustion and stops. Children drain and freeze. The only recovery is resetting root state.

Evidence

`INTENT_RESOURCE_TOTAL_RECORD_LIMIT = 1_000` (mod.rs:45). `try_reserve` calls `ensure_resource_total_admission` (mod.rs:436), which rejects any key without an existing totals row once `totals_len() >= 1000` (mod.rs:1670-1683). `persist_resource_totals` removes a row only when every field is zero (mod.rs:2023-2033). `committed_qty` is only ever increased (commit_at :512, settle_pair_at :828-835, settle_if_pending :1104-1108) and nothing decrements it, so any key with one commit is permanent. The 0.96 design states that nonzero committed totals are "never time-reclaimed".

The cost guard builds its quota key as `canic:cost:quota:<class>:<cmd>:<subject>:<now_secs / quota_window_secs>` (ops/cost_guard.rs:352-363) and reserves it through `try_reserve` (cost_guard.rs:196-203). `complete`/`recover` commit that quota intent (commit_pair_at / commit_and_abort_pending_pair_at, cost_guard.rs:241-268). Every production window is 60 s (nonroot_cycles.rs:46, fleet_subnet_root.rs:87, deployment.rs:16, wasm_store/mod.rs:34, icp_refill/cost_guard.rs:26, publication/cost_guard.rs:27). So every (command, subject, minute) with one completed or recovered operation leaves a permanent totals row. Application local and receipt keys share the same map.

Recommendation

Do not keep time-bucketed quota counters in the durable committed-totals map. - Either move quota accounting to a separate bounded structure that drops buckets older than the current window, or reclaim a quota key's totals once its bucket is in the past and it has no pending count (a past bucket is never read again). - Keep past-window quota rows from counting toward the 1,000-identity cap, or give Canic-owned cost keys a reserved partition so application intents cannot starve them. - Add a unit test that completes cost-guarded operations across more than 1,000 distinct windows and asserts the next reserve still succeeds.

Verifier (confirmed): The claim holds as described. **Why the rows never go away:** - `quota_resource_key` (crates/canic-core/src/ops/cost_guard.rs:349-360) puts `now_secs / quota_window_secs` into the key, and the window is 60 s at every production call site (nonroot_cycles.rs:46, deployment.rs:16, fleet_subnet_root.rs:87, wasm_store/mod.rs:34, icp_refill/cost_guard.rs:26, publication/cost_guard.rs:27, retirement/mod.rs:63). - `reserve` calls `try_reserve` on that key (cost_guard.rs:196-203). `try_reserve` calls `ensure_resource_total_admission` (intent/mod.rs:436), which rejects any key without a totals row once `totals_len() >= 1_000` (mod.rs:1670-1683). - Both `complete` and `recover` commit the quota intent (cost_guard.rs:241-268, settle_pair_at mod.rs:828-835). A failed deposit still recovers, so it also leaves `committed_qty=1` (nonroot_cycles.rs:436). - `persist_resource_totals` removes a row only when it is all zeros (mod.rs:2023-2033). Nothing ever lowers `committed_qty`. - The cleanup timer only aborts pending intents (workflow/runtime/intent.rs:424-433). `reclaim_due_application_receipts` and `remove_terminal` never touch the totals rows (mod.rs:1038-1064, 1211-1260). So every (command, subject, minute) with at least one settled operation leaves a permanent row. The 0.96 design (0.96-design.md:34; changelog 0.96.md:58-60) never considered time-bucketed keys, whose past buckets are never read again. **Impact:** Once 1,000 rows exist, each new-minute key gets CAPACITY_LIMIT. A child's top-up does not retry that code (cycles/mod.rs:966-970). After one resource-exhaustion attempt the top-up stops with `TimerDirective::Stop` (cycles/mod.rs:592-608). Deployment, ICP refill, publication, placement and app intents on the same canister are blocked too. The only way out is a root reset or reinstall. The capacity status warns at 900 rows but cannot free any.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, critical): I could not refute this. Routine operation reaches it without any special privilege. The mechanism holds: - `quota_resource_key` puts `now_secs / quota_window_secs` into the key (ops/cost_guard.rs:349-360). - `reserve` calls `try_reserve` on that key (cost_guard.rs:196-203). `try_reserve` calls `ensure_resource_total_admission` (intent/mod.rs:436), which rejects any new key once there are 1,000 rows (mod.rs:1670-1683). - Both `complete` and `recover` go through `settle_pair_at`, which adds to `committed_qty` (mod.rs:572-595, 828-835). - `persist_resource_totals` removes a row only when it is all zeros (mod.rs:2023-2033). - The only production callers of `remove_totals`, `import_totals` and `set_totals` are that function and test-only code (api/runtime/mod.rs:887 is a test; mod.rs:649 is cfg(test)). The cleanup timer only aborts pending intents (workflow/runtime/intent.rs:414-433). Reachable entry points: 1. A registered child's automatic top-up timer calls RequestCycles on root. The request passes authorization and then `reserve_request_cycles_cost_guard` with quota_subject = child (nonroot_cycles.rs:436, 543-573). With the defaults (5 TC top-up, 100 TC lifetime per child, 60 s cooldown) that is up to about 20 rows per child, so about 50 children use up the cap by themselves. 2. Root's own provisioning runs pool creation, claim and install. Each command kind in each distinct minute adds a permanent row with subject = root (control-plane deployment.rs:28-50). 3. ICP refill, publication, wasm_store and fleet_subnet_root transfers add rows the same way (all use 60 s windows). Once the cap is reached, CAPACITY_LIMIT (mod.rs:281) blocks every new-minute key. Funding, provisioning and publication on root are wedged permanently. After one recovery attempt the child top-up gives up and stops (cycles/mod.rs:582-608). The only recovery is resetting root state. This is an ordinary-operation path to a permanent root wedge, so critical stands.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): Not refuted: the behaviour is real, and the design does not intend it. The design actually argues against it. The archived 0.96 design (0.96-design.md:34, 1058-1062) sets one shared limit of 1,000 resource-total identities. It says nonzero committed totals stay authoritative, and that a slot reopens only when a row returns exactly to zero. At :141-144 it says the headroom assumes bounded keys, and that keys "must not be unique per mint, token, user, or operation." The cost-guard quota key breaks that assumption. It embeds `now_secs / quota_window_secs` (ops/cost_guard.rs:352-363), so each (command, subject, minute) is a new key. `git log -S` shows the quota key dates from 0.61.5, while the limit arrived in 0.96.7 (commit 3c73d10b8). The 0.96.7 audit report never considers time-bucketed keys. The code confirms the rest of the chain: - The only production removal is `persist_resource_totals` for all-zero rows (intent/mod.rs:2023-2033). `committed_qty` only grows (:512, :828, :1104). - `clear_totals_for_tests` is test-only (:648-651). - New keys are rejected once the map is full (:1670-1683). - The child top-up stops on a second resource exhaustion (runtime/cycles/mod.rs:593-608, 977-980). Nothing in docs/status/current.md, the 0.110 or 0.111 designs, or CHANGELOG lists this as a known limitation. The recommended fix does not conflict with the design: a past bucket is never read again, so reclaiming it cannot enable a second settlement. On severity I would downgrade to high. The runtime status warns at 900 rows. A recovery path also exists: an ID-preserving reset or reinstall that keeps canister IDs and their cycles. AGENTS.md treats that as the normal pre-1.0 path, even though it is destructive. So "no recovery path" overstates the impact. It remains an unavoidable liveness failure of root-funded cycle flows under routine use, which is borderline critical.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test lives in the existing cost_guard tests module and calls the production CostGuardOps::reserve and CostGuardOps::complete. It uses the module's `request()` helper: 60 s window, max 1 operation per window, with the cycle balance raised to 1000. It runs one ordinary reserve+complete in each of 1,100 separate 60-second windows (now = window*60+10) and asserts that every reserve succeeds. Each window's reserve is legitimate: it uses a new quota bucket key, so enforce_quota sees used = 0. Result: windows 0 to 998 succeed. The reserve in window 999 fails with CostGuardReserveError::Store(InternalError E81). E81 is CAPACITY_LIMIT. At that point IntentStore::totals_len() is 1000 (999 committed quota-bucket rows plus the one shared cycle-reservation row) and pending_total is 0. Because the error is the Store variant and not the QuotaExceeded variant, it comes from IntentStoreOps::try_reserve -> ensure_resource_total_admission (ResourceTotalRecordCapacityReached), not from the quota check. This confirms the core claim. Committed rows for past quota buckets are never reclaimed, and after about 1,000 active windows every new-window cost-guarded reserve is rejected. Every later window is also a new key, so the block is permanent. The test did not exercise the downstream effects the finding describes (child top-up stopping, other root workflows blocked). Those follow from the same rejection but would need workflow- or PocketIC-level tests.

highreproducedbackup-persistence-1 · correctness · high confidence
`canic backup prune` deletes backup directories that hold an unfinished restore apply journal and staged artifacts, stranding an in-flight production restore.
crates/canic-cli/src/backup/prune.rs:34

Failure scenario

1. The operator restores production from backup #3 using the documented incremental pattern `canic restore run 3 --execute --max-steps 1`. 2. StopCanister and UploadSnapshot complete. 3. A scheduled `canic backup prune --keep 2` then runs. Backup #3 is Complete and third-newest, so remove_dir_all deletes it together with restore-apply-journal.json, its lock sidecars and the staging directory. 4. The next `restore run 3` fails with PreparedJournalMissing, or resolves to another directory. Result: the target canisters stay stopped with an uploaded but unloaded snapshot. There is no journal for lost-response reconciliation, and the source artifacts are gone.

Evidence

backup_prune (prune.rs:10-30) selects list entries whose status is Complete, skips the newest `--keep`, and calls `fs::remove_dir_all(&entry.dir)` for the rest (prune.rs:32-36). Status comes from reference/entry.rs:78-96, which looks only at the backup plan, execution journal and manifest. By default `canic restore prepare <ref>` writes restore-plan.json and restore-apply-journal.json into that same backup directory (restore/io.rs:112-118, restore/mod.rs:115-122). `canic restore run <ref>` requires the journal at that path (io.rs:120-148). The restore runner stages upload artifacts in `.restore-apply-journal.json.canic-restore-stage`, next to the journal (canic-backup restore/runner/artifact.rs:194-206). The restore JournalLock is held only during a single `restore run` call (restore/runner/execute.rs:83), and prune never checks the lock or the restore files. Restore operations stop target canisters, then upload and load snapshots, then start them (restore/apply/journal/types.rs:416-423). The prune tests state the intent 'prune never deletes failed recovery evidence' (backup/tests/prune.rs:13).

Recommendation

In backup_prune, skip (or require an explicit --force for) any layout that contains a restore-plan.json, restore-apply-journal.json or restore staging directory whose journal is not terminal. Also take the directory's journal and restore-journal locks non-blockingly before deleting, and list protected entries in the report.

Verifier (confirmed): The defect exists as described. backup_prune (crates/canic-cli/src/backup/prune.rs:14-35) selects every entry whose status is Complete beyond `--keep` and calls remove_dir_all on it. It takes no lock and does not look at restore files. Status comes from entry.rs:78-96, which reads only the manifest, the backup plan and the execution journal. Nothing in BackupLayout or canic-backup refers to restore-plan.json or restore-apply-journal.json; only restore/io.rs:18-19 does. `restore prepare` writes both files into the backup dir by default (restore/mod.rs:115-122, io.rs:112-118), and `restore run <ref>` requires that path (io.rs:120-147). Even with `--journal` placed elsewhere, uploads read from journal.backup_root, which validate_backup_root checks (canic-backup restore/runner/artifact.rs:99-125). Deleting the backup dir therefore also breaks restores journalled outside it. JournalLock is held only inside one run (execute.rs:24), and prune never checks it, so prune can delete the dir even during a live run. This goes against the project's own 0.94 fix CANIC-094-PRUNE-001 (P1, in docs/audits/reports/2026-07/2026-07-20/0.94-realistic-recovery-and-closeout-hardening.md:60-69), which says failed and "otherwise recoverable" layouts must not enter the deletion set. A paused (`--max-steps`) or failed restore awaiting `--retry-failed` is exactly such state. The strongest trigger is a restore that failed and is left for investigation while scheduled backup and prune continue. Severity stays high: same-operation restore recovery cannot finish through Canic, and target canisters can stay stopped. Manual recovery with icp commands, or restoring from another backup, is still possible, so this is not critical."
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): The path is reachable. The entry point is the `canic backup prune --keep N` CLI command (options/prune.rs:42-67), run by the host operator or by their cron job. No canister authority is needed. backup_list sorts newest first (reference/list.rs:26-31). prune keeps only `Complete` entries, skips the newest `keep` and calls `fs::remove_dir_all` on the rest (prune.rs:14-35). It takes no lock and does no restore check. Status looks only at the manifest, the backup plan and the execution journal (entry.rs:78-96), so a pending restore journal in the directory does not protect it. By default `restore prepare` writes restore-plan.json and restore-apply-journal.json into the backup directory itself (restore/mod.rs:115-122, io.rs:112-118). `restore run <ref>` needs that file and returns PreparedJournalMissing without it (io.rs:120-147). Uploads read from journal.backup_root, and validate_backup_root fails once that directory is gone (artifact.rs:40-68, 106-123). So even a journal kept outside the backup directory cannot finish. JournalLock covers only one run (execute.rs:83), so prune can also delete the directory while a run is live. The precondition is realistic: restoring an older backup (a rollback), or a paused/failed restore awaiting `--retry-failed` while scheduled backups and prune keep running. Prune is a routine operator action with a documented safety contract. CANIC-094-PRUNE-001 says "otherwise recoverable layouts cannot enter the deletion set", and the 0.99 semantic inventory (line 523) says prune removes "non-protected" directories. So this is not intended behaviour, and the operator's filesystem authority does not make it acceptable. The harm: the only durable restore owner (the journal) and the source artifacts are lost, targets can stay stopped, and same-operation recovery cannot finish. That matches "recovery that cannot complete". Manual `icp` start and snapshot load keep it short of critical, and no cycles are lost. Severity stays high, at its lower edge.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this. Nothing documents the behaviour as intended, and the project's own design says the opposite. The code does what the finding says. `backup_prune` (crates/canic-cli/src/backup/prune.rs:14-35) keeps only entries whose status is `Complete`, skips the newest `--keep`, and calls `remove_dir_all` on the rest. It takes no lock and never looks at restore files. The status check (reference/entry.rs:78-96) reads only the plan, the execution journal and the manifest. `restore prepare` writes restore-plan.json and restore-apply-journal.json into the backup directory by default (restore/mod.rs:115-122, restore/io.rs:112-118). `restore run <ref>` requires that journal to exist (io.rs:120-147). The upload staging directory sits next to the journal (canic-backup restore/runner/artifact.rs:194-206), and upload artifacts are read from `journal.backup_root` (artifact.rs:99-125). `JournalLock` is held only for the length of one run (execute.rs:83). A grep of canic-backup and of the CLI backup module finds no reference to the restore file names outside restore/io.rs. The design intent supports the finding: - The 0.94 status file (docs/design/archive/0.94-backup-restore-operational-readiness/status.md:16) says "restore preparation and pruning preserve recovery evidence". - The fix for CANIC-094-PRUNE-001 (audit report lines 60-69) requires that "Failed, incomplete, invalid, and otherwise recoverable layouts cannot enter the deletion set". - The 0.94 changelog (docs/changelog/0.94.md:113-115) says the same. - AGENTS.md requires same-release restore interruption recovery. A backup whose restore journal is paused by `--max-steps` or failed is recoverable state. Its status is still `Complete`, so prune selects it anyway. There is no known-limitation entry, and no help text warns against pruning during a restore. The recommended fix, protecting layouts that hold a non-terminal restore journal, follows the 0.94 contract rather than contradicting it. On impact: the restore can no longer be completed or reconciled through Canic, and the targets may stay stopped. Manual icp recovery, or restoring from another backup, is still possible, so this is not critical. It matches "recovery that cannot complete" and "operator command destroys state without adequate checks", so it stays high. It is borderline medium, because it needs an operator or scheduled prune while a restore of an older backup is unfinished.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test builds a backup root with two Complete layouts using the existing prune fixtures: a newer backup-newest and an older backup-restoring. The older one has a restore-ready manifest and a real artifact whose checksum matches. It then runs the production `canic restore prepare --backup-dir <older> --require-restore-ready` through crate::restore::run. By default that writes restore-plan.json and restore-apply-journal.json into the backup directory itself. Next the test uses the production journal API (mark_next_operation_pending_at, write_restore_apply_journal) to move the restore journal to an in-flight state with 1 of 5 operations pending. That is the state an interrupted or paused `restore run --execute --max-steps 1` leaves behind. Finally it calls backup_prune with keep=1 and dry_run=false, and asserts that the directory and the journal still exist. The test fails. backup_list still shows the restoring layout as Complete, because status ignores the restore files. Prune selects it, calls remove_dir_all, and reports it as Removed. Afterwards the directory and restore-apply-journal.json are both gone. This confirms the finding's core claim in full: prune deletes a backup directory that holds a non-terminal restore apply journal. It checks no lock and no restore state. The test does not exercise the downstream consequences, stopped canisters and a later PreparedJournalMissing from `restore run`, but they follow directly once the journal file no longer exists.

highreproducedbackup-restore-1 · correctness · medium confidence
Upload reconciliation adopts any single new snapshot as the completed upload, so a partially uploaded snapshot left by a failed or interrupted upload is recorded as done and later loaded.
crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/execute.rs:566

Failure scenario

The operator presses Ctrl-C during `canic restore run --execute`. SIGINT kills the runner and the icp child mid-upload of a multi-GB stable memory, so the metadata and Wasm are uploaded but some memory chunks are not. Alternatively, a network error makes icp exit non-zero and the operator follows next_action=retry-failed. On rerun the partial snapshot is the single inventory delta, it is adopted as uploaded, and all members are then stopped. If the IC rejects loading an incomplete snapshot, the load fails on every retry because the upload cannot be redone: every member is left stopped and the journal is wedged. If the IC accepts the load, the canister restarts with zero-filled memory regions. Status is Running and the module hash matches, so verification passes and the data loss goes undetected.

Evidence

execute.rs:465-467 treats an upload as recovering whenever `snapshot_ids_before.is_some()`, not only when it is Pending. That baseline survives a Failed state and `retry_failed_operation_at` (journal/mod.rs:292-303, which calls transition_operation at 339-369 without clearing it). reconcile_upload_operation (execute.rs:532-577) computes observed minus baseline and, when exactly one snapshot is new, returns a reconciled success with `uploaded_snapshot_id` set to it (566-571). It never checks that the snapshot is complete or matches the artifact: the inventory's `total_size_bytes` is parsed and then discarded (`_total_size_bytes`, 598-599). The IC upload is two-phase. `upload_canister_snapshot_metadata` creates the snapshot ID and data chunks follow (ic-management-canister-types UploadCanisterSnapshotMetadataArgs/UploadCanisterSnapshotDataArgs). Once the upload op is Completed it can never transition again (journal/types.rs:248-279), and LoadSnapshot always uses that ID (commands/mod.rs:175-191, journal/mod.rs:445-460). The 0.94 capability gate itself states that an inventory delta does not bind an uploaded identity to the artifact checksum (docs/audits/reports/2026-07/2026-07-19/0.94-capability-gate.md:71-75). No test covers a failed upload followed by retry.

Recommendation

Do not treat an inventory delta as proof of a complete upload. Either require the adopted snapshot's reported total_size_bytes (and timestamps) to match the size recorded in the artifact metadata, or, when the previous attempt failed or was interrupted, delete the delta snapshot (it is ours under the exclusivity assumption) and re-upload the staged artifact, or use icp's resume support with the recorded ID. Add runner tests for failed-upload-then-retry and interrupted-upload-with-partial-snapshot.

+// Repro for review finding backup-restore-1: a failed upload leaves a partial
+// snapshot on the target (IC upload is two-phase: metadata creates the ID, data
+// chunks follow). After `restore run --retry-failed`, the runner must not adopt
+// that partial snapshot as the completed upload.
+struct PartialUploadExecutor {
+    inventory: Vec<String>,
+    upload_success: bool,
+    commands: Vec<RestoreApplyRunnerCommand>,
+}
+
+impl RestoreRunnerCommandExecutor for PartialUploadExecutor {
+    fn execute(
+        &mut self,
+        command: &RestoreApplyRunnerCommand,
+        _command_lifetime: Option<crate::persistence::CommandLifetimeHandle>,
+    ) -> Result<RestoreRunnerCommandOutput, std::io::Error> {
+        self.commands.push(command.clone());
+        if is_snapshot_inventory_command(command) {
+            return Ok(snapshot_inventory_output(&self.inventory));
+        }
+        if command.args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("status") {
+            return Ok(status_output("Stopped"));
+        }
+        let is_upload = command.args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("snapshot")
+            && command.args.get(2).map(String::as_str) == Some("upload");
+        if is_upload && !self.upload_success {
+            // Metadata phase succeeded (the IC allocated `partial-upload`), a
+            // data chunk failed, so icp exits non-zero.
+            self.inventory.push("partial-upload".to_string());
+            return Ok(RestoreRunnerCommandOutput {
+                success: false,
+                status: "1".to_string(),
+                stdout: Vec::new(),
+                stderr: b"UploadDataChunk failed: network error".to_vec(),
+            });
+        }
+        if is_upload {
+            self.inventory.push("fresh-upload".to_string());
+            return Ok(RestoreRunnerCommandOutput {
+                success: true,
+                status: "0".to_string(),
+                stdout: br#"{"snapshot_id":"fresh-upload"}"#.to_vec(),
+                stderr: Vec::new(),
+            });
+        }
+        Ok(RestoreRunnerCommandOutput {
+            success: true,
+            status: "0".to_string(),
+            stdout: Vec::new(),
+            stderr: Vec::new(),
+        })
+    }
+}

highreproducedbackup-restore-2 · correctness · high confidence
A backup retried after failure containment mixes two stop windows: snapshots taken before containment restarted the fleet are kept while the remaining members are snapshotted in a later window.
crates/canic-backup/src/runner/mod.rs:379

Failure scenario

Root and child are backed up together. The root snapshot succeeds. The child snapshot fails (for example at the per-canister snapshot limit, see the snapshot-accumulation finding). Containment restarts both canisters and root keeps processing updates. The operator frees space and reruns: both are stopped again, but only the child is snapshotted. The manifest pairs root state from time T1 with child state from T2 and is marked as a crash-consistent subtree unit. Restoring it gives root registry and ledger state that disagrees with the child's state: a wrong restored state with no warning.

Evidence

Backup phases stop every target, then snapshot every target, then start them (plan/build/phases.rs:39-62). When CreateSnapshot for target k fails, failure_after_containment runs because restart_required is true (runner/mod.rs:330-357). contain_backup_failure starts each stopped canister, and because the primary op is CreateSnapshot (`rearm_snapshot_phase`, 379-382) it calls rearm_after_failure_containment (443-448). That function resets only the paired Stop and Start of each target to Ready (execution/mod.rs:222-267). Completed CreateSnapshot rows for targets 0..k-1 stay Completed. On the next `backup run`, next_ready_operation picks the rearmed Stops first (execution/mod.rs:142-154), then skips the Completed snapshots and creates only snapshot k onward, and finalize publishes a manifest in which all members share one topology hash and backup unit (runner/manifest.rs:31-46). The only test of this path uses a single target (runner/tests.rs:380-430).

Recommendation

When containment restarts any canister after some CreateSnapshot rows completed, re-arm every CreateSnapshot in that backup unit, not only the stop/start pairs. The discarded snapshots should be recorded for cleanup. Alternatively, refuse to finalize a manifest whose snapshots come from different stop windows. Add a multi-target test where the second snapshot fails.

Verifier (confirmed): The code does what the finding says. plan/build/phases.rs:39-62 orders all Stops, then all CreateSnapshots, then all Starts. If CreateSnapshot k fails, failure_after_containment (runner/mod.rs:315-357) calls contain_backup_failure. Because the failed primary is CreateSnapshot, rearm_snapshot_phase is true (379-382). next_failure_containment_start (execution/mod.rs:157-181) starts every target whose Stop completed, and rearm_after_failure_containment (222-267) resets only that target's Stop and Start to Ready. Snapshot rows 0..k-1 stay Completed. Nothing in validate() (51-89) or BackupExecutionJournalOperation::validate (operation.rs:20-68) checks that snapshots are ordered relative to stops, so this state passes validation. On retry, next_ready_operation (140-154) picks the Ready Stops, skips the Completed snapshots, and redoes only snapshot k (Failed) onward. Downloads use the T1 snapshot ids that persist_created_snapshot and recorded_snapshot_receipt stored (runner/operations/artifacts.rs:60-93). build_manifest (runner/manifest.rs:14-51) records one topology hash and a Subtree backup unit, and never compares snapshot times (taken_at is kept but never checked). This contradicts the stated intent: changelog 0.94.md:130-131 and the CANIC-094-BACKUP-011 audit say retry 'again quiesces the entire selected set', and the 0.34 design says members are 'snapshotted together'. The only test, runner/tests.rs:380-430, uses one target, so it cannot catch this. The trigger is an ordinary later-target snapshot failure (snapshot limit, cycles, transport) followed by a routine retry, and the restore quietly produces an inconsistent state across canisters. That fits high.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. The path runs from a real entry point to the harm. The operator runs `canic backup create <fleet> --out <dir>`, and backup_create calls backup_run_execute_with_executor (canic-cli/src/backup/create/mod.rs:88). Running it again with the same `--out` is the supported resume path: persist_backup_create_layout reuses the existing plan and journal (create/persistence.rs:23-31), and the runner reads the existing journal (runner/mod.rs:64-65). A later snapshot k failing after snapshots 0..k-1 succeed is an ordinary failure (cycles, snapshot limit, transport). failure_after_containment then runs because restart_required is true (mod.rs:330), and rearm_snapshot_phase is set (379-382). rearm_after_failure_containment resets only the Stop and Start rows (execution/mod.rs:222-266). On resume, next_ready_operation picks the Stops (140-154), skips the Completed snapshots 0..k-1, and retakes only snapshot k, whose reconcile against the T1 baseline finds nothing new (mod.rs:634-639). Re-arming the snapshot rows alone would not fix it: recorded_snapshot_receipt reuses the download-journal artifact for the target (artifacts.rs:50-52, 66-80), so the stale T1 artifacts must be cleared too. build_manifest writes a Subtree consistency unit and never compares taken_at (manifest.rs:31-46). This contradicts the stated intent that retry "quiesce the complete selection again" (changelog 0.94.md:130-131). The only test uses a single target (runner/tests.rs:380-430). Who can trigger it: a host operator who already holds controller authority. But no authority is escalated. The harm is a silently inconsistent restore produced by a routine failure-and-resume sequence, which fits "restore that produces a wrong state" (high). One minor inaccuracy in the finding: the scenario names the fleet root, but backup scope is a non-root deployment or a subtree. Any parent and child pair in a subtree gives the same result.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): The design and docs do not treat this as intended, and it is not a documentation error. The archived 0.34 design (docs/design/archive/0.34-backup-restore/0.34-design.md:20) says selected members are "quiesced together, snapshotted together". The BackupUnit type is documented as a group "that must be captured and restored as one consistency unit" (crates/canic-backup/src/manifest/types.rs:73). The 0.94 fix (docs/changelog/0.94.md:130-131, audit CANIC-094-BACKUP-011) re-arms stop/start "so retry again quiesces the entire selected set". Stopping everything again only helps if every member is then snapshotted again. The code does not do that. rearm_after_failure_containment (execution/mod.rs:222-267) resets only the Stop and Start rows. Snapshot rows that already completed are skipped by next_ready_operation (execution/mod.rs:142-154). build_manifest (runner/manifest.rs:14-51) never checks when each snapshot was taken. Neither docs/status/current.md nor the 0.110/0.111 designs list this as a known limitation. The proposed fix (re-arm snapshots, or refuse to publish a manifest that mixes stop windows) matches the design instead of contradicting it. The path is reachable. Retry means running `backup create --out <same dir>` again, which reuses the existing plan and journal (crates/canic-cli/src/backup/create/persistence.rs:23-31). The retry test covers this with a single target (runner/tests.rs:380-430). One thing lowers the odds: without --out, the default output path is timestamped (create/plan.rs:68-74), so an operator who simply reruns the command gets a fresh backup. Resume still has to be requested on purpose. Even so, it is the designed recovery path. The result is a manifest labelled as one crash-consistent unit whose members came from different times, and nothing warns about it. That matches "restore that produces a wrong state", so it stays high.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test builds a real Subtree plan: APP is the selected parent and WORKER is its child. It runs backup_run_execute_with_executor through a wrapper around the existing FakeBackupRunnerExecutor. The wrapper counts stop windows (one per stop of APP), gives each snapshot the id of the window it was taken in, and fails CreateSnapshot only for WORKER. First run: APP is snapshotted in window 1, WORKER's snapshot fails, and containment restarts both canisters. Afterwards snapshot-APP stays Completed and only the Stop/Start rows go back to Ready. Retry (same layout, failure removed): both canisters are stopped again, but only WORKER is snapshotted, and the next step downloads APP's window-1 snapshot. The test then builds the manifest with build_manifest_for_test from the resulting download journal. It shows one backup unit of kind Subtree, pairing APP from window 1 with WORKER from window 2. The assertion that all members of the unit come from one stop window fails. Setup caveat: the retry stops after 6 steps (max_steps) and marks the artifacts Durable in memory. On macOS, VerifyArtifact fails with a checksum IO error (ENOTDIR) in every runner test, including the existing runner_records_failed_operation_and_retries_from_that_operation. That macOS error is unrelated to this finding. The snapshot ids never change during download or verify. The finding's claim holds in full.

diff --git a/crates/canic-backup/src/runner/tests.rs b/crates/canic-backup/src/runner/tests.rs
index 54493c8f7..1952e34b8 100644

     })

+
+// Repro (backup-restore-2): a later-target snapshot failure followed by containment and a
+// retry must not publish a manifest that mixes snapshots from two different stop windows.
+struct StopWindowExecutor {
+    inner: FakeExecutor,
+    fail_snapshot_for: Option<String>,
+    stop_window: usize,
+    snapshot_windows: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
+}
+
+impl BackupRunnerExecutor for StopWindowExecutor {
+    fn preflight_receipts(
+        &mut self,
+        plan: &BackupPlan,
+        preflight_id: &str,
+        validated_at: &str,
+        expires_at: &str,
+    ) -> Result<crate::plan::BackupExecutionPreflightReceipts, BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        self.inner
+            .preflight_receipts(plan, preflight_id, validated_at, expires_at)
+    }
+
+    fn canister_status(
+        &mut self,
+        canister_id: &str,
+    ) -> Result<BackupRunnerCanisterStatus, BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        self.inner.canister_status(canister_id)
+    }
+
+    fn snapshot_inventory(
+        &mut self,
+        canister_id: &str,
+    ) -> Result<Vec<BackupRunnerSnapshot>, BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        self.inner.snapshot_inventory(canister_id)
+    }
+
+    fn stop_canister(
+        &mut self,
+        canister_id: &str,
+        command_lifetime: crate::persistence::CommandLifetimeHandle,
+    ) -> Result<(), BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        // APP is stopped first in every top-down stop window.
+        if canister_id == APP {
+            self.stop_window += 1;
+        }
+        self.inner.stop_canister(canister_id, command_lifetime)
+    }
+
+    fn start_canister(
+        &mut self,
+        canister_id: &str,
+        command_lifetime: crate::persistence::CommandLifetimeHandle,
+    ) -> Result<(), BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        self.inner.start_canister(canister_id, command_lifetime)
+    }
+
+    fn create_snapshot(
+        &mut self,
+        canister_id: &str,
+        _command_lifetime: crate::persistence::CommandLifetimeHandle,
+    ) -> Result<BackupRunnerSnapshot, BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        self.inner.commands.push(format!("snapshot:{canister_id}"));
+        if self.fail_snapshot_for.as_deref() == Some(canister_id) {
+            return Err(BackupRunnerCommandError::failed(
+                "snapshot",
+                "simulated snapshot limit",
+            ));
+        }
+        let snapshot_id = format!("snap-{canister_id}-window-{}", self.stop_window);
+        let snapshot = BackupRunnerSnapshot {
+            snapshot_id: snapshot_id.clone(),
+            taken_at_timestamp: Some(1_778_709_681_000_000_000 + self.stop_window as u64),
+            total_size_bytes: Some(1024),
+        };
+        self.inner
+            .snapshots
+            .entry(canister_id.to_string())
+            .or_default()
+            .push(snapshot.clone());
+        self.snapshot_windows.insert(snapshot_id, self.stop_window);
+        Ok(snapshot)
+    }
+
+    fn download_snapshot(
+        &mut self,
+        canister_id: &str,
+        snapshot_id: &str,
+        artifact_path: &std::path::Path,
+        command_lifetime: crate::persistence::CommandLifetimeHandle,
+    ) -> Result<(), BackupRunnerCommandError> {
+        self.inner
+            .download_snapshot(canister_id, snapshot_id, artifact_path, command_lifetime)
+    }
+}
+
+fn parent_child_subtree_plan() -> BackupPlan {
+    build_backup_plan(BackupPlanBuildInput {
+        plan_id: "plan-test".to_string(),
+        run_id: "run-test".to_string(),
+        fleet: "demo".to_string(),
+        environment: "local".to_string(),
+        root_canister_id: ROOT.to_string(),
+        selected_canister_id: Some(APP.to_string()),
+        selected_scope_kind: BackupScopeKind::Subtree,
+        include_descendants: true,
+        topology_hash_before_quiesce: HASH.to_string(),
+        registry: &[
+            RegistryEntry {
+                pid: ROOT.to_string(),
+                role: Some("root".to_string()),
+                kind: Some("root".to_string()),
+                parent_pid: None,
+                module_hash: None,
+            },
+            RegistryEntry {
+                pid: APP.to_string(),
+                role: Some("app".to_string()),
+                kind: Some("singleton".to_string()),
+                parent_pid: Some(ROOT.to_string()),
+                module_hash: Some(HASH.to_string()),
+            },
+            RegistryEntry {
+                pid: WORKER.to_string(),
+                role: Some("worker".to_string()),
+                kind: Some("singleton".to_string()),
+                parent_pid: Some(APP.to_string()),
+                module_hash: Some(HASH.to_string()),
+            },
+        ],
+        control_authority: ControlAuthority::operator_controller(AuthorityEvidence::Proven),
+        snapshot_read_authority: SnapshotReadAuthority::operator_controller(
+            AuthorityEvidence::Proven,
+        ),
+        quiescence_policy: QuiescencePolicy::CrashConsistent,
+        identity_mode: IdentityMode::Relocatable,
+    })
+    .expect("backup plan")
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_retry_after_containment_mixes_stop_windows() {
+    let root = temp_dir("canic-backup-runner-repro-mixed-windows");
+    let layout = BackupLayout::new(root.clone());
+    let plan = parent_child_subtree_plan();
+    let journal = BackupExecutionJournal::from_plan(&plan).expect("execution journal");
+    layout.write_backup_plan(&plan).expect("write plan");
+    layout
+        .write_execution_journal(&journal)
+        .expect("write execution journal");
+    println!(
+        "plan phases: {:?}",
+        plan.phases
+            .iter()
+            .map(|phase| phase.operation_id.clone())
+            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+    );
+
+    // First run: parent (APP) snapshot succeeds in window 1, child (WORKER) snapshot fails.
+    let mut executor = StopWindowExecutor {
+        inner: FakeExecutor::default(),
+        fail_snapshot_for: Some(WORKER.to_string()),
+        stop_window: 0,
+        snapshot_windows: BTreeMap::new(),
+    };
+    let err = backup_run_execute_with_executor(&runner_config(root.clone(), None), &mut executor)
+        .expect_err("child snapshot failure aborts run");
+    println!("first run error: {err:?}");
+    println!("first run commands: {:?}", executor.inner.commands);
+    let failed_journal = layout.read_execution_journal().expect("read failed journal");
+    for operation in &failed_journal.operations {
+        println!(
+            "after containment: {} -> {:?}",
+            operation.operation_id, operation.state
+        );
+    }
+
+    // Both canisters were restarted by containment and may have processed updates.
+    // Operator fixes the cause and reruns against the same layout. The retry is bounded to
+    // the quiescence window plus the first download: on macOS the VerifyArtifact step fails
+    // with a platform checksum IO error for every runner test (including the existing
+    // single-target retry test), so the manifest is built from the resulting download journal.
+    executor.fail_snapshot_for = None;
+    let retry_start = executor.inner.commands.len();
+    let retry_result =
+        backup_run_execute_with_executor(&runner_config(root.clone(), Some(6)), &mut executor);
+    let retry_commands = executor.inner.commands[retry_start..].to_vec();
+    println!("retry commands: {retry_commands:?}");
+    let response = retry_result.expect("bounded retry run");
+    println!(
+        "retry executed: {:?}",
+        response
+            .executed_operations
+            .iter()
+            .map(|operation| format!("{operation:?}"))
+            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+    );
+
+    let execution_journal = layout.read_execution_journal().expect("read retry journal");
+    for operation in &execution_journal.operations {
+        println!(
+            "after retry: {} -> {:?}",
+            operation.operation_id, operation.state
+        );
+    }
+    let mut download_journal = layout.read_journal().expect("read download journal");
+    for entry in &download_journal.artifacts {
+        println!(
+            "download journal: {} snapshot {} taken_at {:?} state {:?}",
+            entry.canister_id, entry.snapshot_id, entry.snapshot_taken_at_timestamp, entry.state
+        );
+    }
+    // Model download/verify completion without changing snapshot identity, then build the
+    // manifest exactly as FinalizeManifest would.
+    for entry in &mut download_journal.artifacts {
+        entry.state = ArtifactState::Durable;
+        entry.temp_path = None;
+        entry.checksum = Some(HASH.to_string());
+    }
+    let manifest = build_manifest_for_test(&runner_config(root.clone(), None), &plan, &download_journal)
+        .expect("build manifest");
+    println!("backup units: {:?}", manifest.consistency.backup_units);
+    let mut member_windows = BTreeMap::new();
+    for member in &manifest.deployment.members {
+        let window = executor
+            .snapshot_windows
+            .get(&member.source_snapshot.snapshot_id)
+            .copied()
+            .expect("known snapshot id");
+        println!(
+            "manifest member {} ({}) snapshot {} taken in stop window {window}",
+            member.role, member.canister_id, member.source_snapshot.snapshot_id
+        );
+        member_windows.insert(member.canister_id.clone(), window);
+    }
+    fs::remove_dir_all(root).expect("remove temp root");
+
+    let distinct = member_windows.values().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
+    assert_eq!(
+        distinct.len(),
+        1,
+        "every member of one crash-consistent backup unit must be snapshotted in the same \
+         stop window, got {member_windows:?}"
+    );
+}
highreproducedcore-access-endpoints-1 · correctness · medium confidence
canic_command caps root-to-child ConfigureRuntime at 16 KiB, but the request carries the full Fleet and Group directories plus every direct child, so larger Components can never be configured or resynchronized
crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:585

Failure scenario

A Component Group with roughly 40 or more members, or a hub Component with roughly 250 shard children, produces a ConfigureRuntime argument larger than 16 KiB. The target's raw adapter traps with "update payload is N bytes; maximum is 16384". Root's configure_target_component_runtime gets a reject. Its reconciliation re-query finds the directory not covered and returns the call error (component_registry/mod.rs:3071-3085, 4436-4455). Every retry sends identical bytes, so Component activation or directory convergence for that Component never completes, within configuration limits the validator accepted.

Evidence

canic_command is declared with payload(max_bytes = DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES) (role.rs:582-586), which is 16 KiB (ingress/payload.rs:9). Because the limit is explicit, the raw adapter enforces it for inter-canister calls too, and traps before decoding (canic-macros expand/mod.rs:364-372; docs/features/runtime/update-payload-limits.md table).

ConfigureRuntime carries a ComponentRuntimeDirectoryPreparationRequest (dto/component_registry.rs:935-965):
- authority.fleet is a FleetDirectorySnapshot holding Vec fleet_subnet_roots and Vec services (dto/fleet_registry.rs:540-544).
- authority.component_group is an Option<ComponentGroupDirectory>. Its members are ComponentGroupDirectoryMember values, each with up to 32 labels and a full ComponentBinding (dto/component_provisioning.rs:258-285).
- direct_children is a Vec of {principal, role, 32-byte digest}.

Root builds this request with the whole group directory and all active direct children (canic-control-plane workflow/component_provisioning.rs:801-812). It reuses ConfigureRuntime for every later directory sync (component_registry/mod.rs:4485-4527).

Configuration allows 256 members per group (config/component_group/mod.rs:36). No root-side size assertion exists; contrast root_admission/mod.rs:411-419, which asserts its target command fits 16 KiB. By DTO-shape estimate, one ComponentBinding is about 350 bytes (FleetRegistryAuthority with recovery controllers, three 32-byte ids, three principals) and one direct child about 57 bytes.

Recommendation

- Give ConfigureRuntime a variant-dependent limit sized from the configured maxima, as canic_root_command already does for ProvisionComponents (root.rs:149-160, 164-187). - Add a test that encodes a maximal ConfigureRuntime and asserts it fits. - Consider paging directory delivery, or deduplicating the repeated FleetRegistryAuthority out of each member binding. - Have root reject oversize requests with a typed error before provisioning starts.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. canic_command declares payload(max_bytes = DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES) (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:582-586). That constant is 16*1024 (crates/canic-core/src/ingress/payload.rs:9). Any explicit limit makes the macro emit the raw adapter (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:35-36). The adapter checks msg_arg_data_size and traps above the limit for every caller, root's inter-canister call included (expand/mod.rs:364-372). Root sends the whole placement's ComponentGroupDirectory. That directory holds one member per planned entry, each with a full ComponentBinding carrying a FleetRegistryAuthority (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:2560-2596). The request also carries the Fleet directory and every active direct child (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:801-812; component_registry/mod.rs:4206-4243, which has no cap). The send path configure_target_component_runtime has no size check (component_registry/mod.rs:4505-4526). Both retry paths return call_error after reconciliation fails (3071-3085, 4436-4455), and retries resend identical bytes. The per-member estimate of about 350-400 bytes holds: [u8;32] fields cost 33 bytes and a subnet principal 31. That puts the ceiling near 40 members. The design clearly expects larger groups: - It allows 4,096 deployment members (config/component_group_deployment/mod.rs:42). - Provisioning batches get an 8 MiB budget (component_provisioning_plan/mod.rs:60-63). - Target activation storage allows 2 MiB (storage/stable/fleet_activation/mod.rs:29). The 0.109 design calls 16 KiB a frozen role-command limit (0.109-design.md:582). It measures other commands against that limit but not ConfigureRuntime. Canisters are already created and installed when publication wedges. Cycles stay root-controlled, so this is not critical.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. The path from entry point to failure is concrete. The operator runs fleet ensure, which drives the Coordinator to call root's canic_root_command publish. That reaches workflow::component_provisioning::publish (component_provisioning.rs:451-496), which passes the full mirror.directory to publish_component_directory. That function builds a ComponentRuntimeDirectoryPreparationRequest containing: - the complete FleetDirectorySnapshot, with every service and all its members (dto/fleet_registry.rs:522-544); - the whole group directory (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:2560-2596); - all active direct children (component_provisioning.rs:801-812). configure_target_component_runtime sends this with no size check (component_registry/mod.rs:4505-4526). The target's canic_command has an explicit 16 KiB max_bytes (role.rs:582-586, payload.rs:9). Any explicit limit makes the macro use the raw adapter (expand/mod.rs:35-36), and that adapter traps on msg_arg_data_size for inter-canister callers too (expand/mod.rs:364-370). The exposure is wider than the finding says. Child spawns (child_directory_request, component_registry/mod.rs:4170-4190) and ungrouped Components (2606) also carry the full Fleet Directory. My per-value Candid estimate: - Each group member is about 340 bytes, since each ComponentBinding repeats the FleetRegistryAuthority (fleet_topology/mod.rs:278-350). - Each Fleet service member is about 110 bytes. So about 40 group members, or about 150 service members across the fleet, is past 16 KiB. Validated config allows 256 members per group and 4,096 per fleet (component_group/mod.rs:36,42; schema/mod.rs:72). Neither the host nor root checks the size first. The only size assertion is for other commands (root_admission/mod.rs:417). Who triggers it: the operator, or a Component spawning a child, through ordinary operation with a config the validator accepted. Retries resend identical bytes (3071-3085), so the same-operation recovery can never complete. The canisters are already created and paid for when this happens. Cycles stay root-controlled, and a reinstall-only reset is still available, so this is not critical. Recovery that cannot complete, plus a scale-out ceiling far below the validated bounds, fits high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this finding on intent grounds. The mechanism checks out in code: - canic_command declares payload(max_bytes = DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES) (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:582-586), which is 16*1024 (crates/canic-core/src/ingress/payload.rs:9). - An explicit limit selects the raw adapter (canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:35-36). That adapter traps on msg_arg_data_size for inter-canister callers too (expand/mod.rs:364-370). docs/features/runtime/update-payload-limits.md documents this. - Root sends the full FleetDirectorySnapshot, the whole group directory and all direct children (workflow/component_provisioning.rs:801-812). The send path has no size check (component_registry/mod.rs:4505-4526). - The target requires each member's binding.authority to equal its own (component_runtime.rs:640-646), so FleetRegistryAuthority is repeated in every member. No doc treats this as intended: - The 0.109 design calls 16,384 bytes the frozen role-command limit. It says exceeding the envelope "reduces a bound" (0.109-design.md:580-594), but it measures only admission commands, not ConfigureRuntime. - The group limit stays at 256 members (config/component_group/mod.rs:36), with 4,096 deployment members and service targets. - The only envelope measurement, 0.101 Q4 (qualification.md:47-75), covered 15 Components and a 2,854-byte Fleet Directory. - Nothing in 0.110, 0.111, CHANGELOG or current.md tracks this as a known limitation. The impact may be broader than claimed. The Fleet Directory alone grows with service members, so large fleets could hit the limit even without groups. Two caveats on the recommendation: - Paging would contradict the 0.109 rule against adding an "unreviewed paging protocol". - Reducing bounds, or rejecting oversize requests with a typed error before effects, fits the design. So does a variant-dependent limit, which already has a precedent (root.rs:149-160). Severity stays high. A validated configuration passes all checks, then wedges after the paid create and install. Recovery cannot complete without a reset. Cycles stay under root control, so this is not critical.
Reproduction (partially reproduced): The test builds a config with a 64-member Component Group (the per-declaration cap is 256) and runs it through production parse_config_model and compile_component_group_deployment_topology. The validator accepts it. From the compiled members it builds a ComponentGroupDirectory with ComponentBindings shaped like production ones: 10-byte canister ids, 29-byte subnet ids, no recovery controllers. That directory goes into a ComponentRuntimeDirectoryPreparationRequest using the smallest realistic envelope: one fleet root, no services, no direct children. The request is wrapped in the production root-side CanisterCommandFragment::ConfigureRuntime and candid::encode_one'd, which produces the same bytes CallOps::with_arg sends. The test asserts the result is at most DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES (16384), the explicit limit on the target's canic_command. It fails. One member encodes to 2040 bytes, each extra member adds 376 bytes, and 64 members come to 25728 bytes. The limit is first exceeded at 40 members, which matches the finding's estimate of about 40. So the core claim holds: config-valid groups produce a root-to-child ConfigureRuntime that is larger than the target's cap. Not exercised natively: - The target-side trap. By inspection, the macro raw adapter traps when msg_arg_data_size is above max_bytes (canic-macros expand/mod.rs:364-370). - The retry and reconciliation wedge. - The hub case with about 250 direct children. All three need PocketIC. A PocketIC test would provision a group with 40 or more members and assert that publication completes.

+//! Reproduction: root-to-child ConfigureRuntime must fit the target's frozen
+//! 16 KiB `canic_command` payload envelope for configuration-accepted groups.
+
+use super::CanisterCommandFragment;
+use canic_core::{
+    bootstrap::parse_config_model,
+    dto::{
+        component_provisioning::{
+            ComponentGroupDirectory, ComponentGroupDirectoryMember,
+            ComponentGroupDirectoryProvenance,
+        },
+        component_registry::{
+            ComponentDirectoryHead, ComponentDirectoryProvenance,
+            ComponentRuntimeDirectoryAuthority, ComponentRuntimeDirectoryPreparationRequest,
+        },
+        fleet_registry::{
+            FleetDirectoryProvenance, FleetDirectorySnapshot, FleetRegistryVersion,
+            FleetSubnetRootDirectoryEntry, FleetSubnetRootStatus,
+        },
+    },
+    ids::{
+        AppId, CanisterRole, CanonicalNetworkId, ComponentBinding, ComponentGroupPlacementId,
+        ComponentInstanceId, FleetBinding, FleetCoordinatorBinding, FleetId, FleetKey,
+        FleetRegistryAuthority, SubnetId,
+    },
+    ingress::payload::DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES,
+};
+
+const GROUP_MEMBERS: usize = 64;
+
+// Real canister ids are 10 bytes; subnet ids are 29 bytes.
+fn canister(seed: u16) -> candid::Principal {
+    let [hi, lo] = seed.to_be_bytes();
+    candid::Principal::from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, hi, lo, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01])
+}
+
+fn subnet(byte: u8) -> SubnetId {
+    SubnetId::from_principal(candid::Principal::from_slice(&[byte; 29]))
+}
+
+fn group_config(members: usize) -> String {
+    let mut config = String::from(
+        r#"
+[app]
+name = "repro"
+
+[roles.root]
+kind = "root"
+
+[roles.alpha]
+kind = "canister"
+package = "alpha"
+
+[component_specs.alpha]
+component_role = "alpha"
+maximum_instances = 1024
+"#,
+    );
+    for index in 0..members {
+        config.push_str(&format!(
+            "\n[component_groups.cell.components.m{index:03}]\ncomponent_spec = \"alpha\"\nlabels = {{ tier = \"api\" }}\n"
+        ));
+    }
+    config.push_str(
+        r#"
+[component_group_deployments.cells]
+component_group = "cell"
+initial_placements = 1
+maximum_placements = 1
+placement.maximum_per_root = 1
+placement.minimum_distinct_roots = 1
+"#,
+    );
+    config
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_configure_runtime_fits_canic_command_payload_limit() {
+    // Configuration validation accepts a 64-member Component Group (limit is 256).
+    let config = parse_config_model(&group_config(GROUP_MEMBERS)).expect("valid config");
+    let deployments = config
+        .compile_component_group_deployment_topology()
+        .expect("deployment topology accepted by validator");
+    let deployment = deployments
+        .get(&"cells".parse().expect("deployment ID"))
+        .expect("deployment");
+    assert_eq!(deployment.members.len(), GROUP_MEMBERS);
+
+    let placement_subnet = subnet(7);
+    let root = canister(0xfff0);
+    let authority = FleetRegistryAuthority {
+        binding: FleetCoordinatorBinding {
+            fleet: FleetBinding {
+                fleet: FleetKey {
+                    canonical_network_id: CanonicalNetworkId::ic_mainnet(),
+                    fleet_id: FleetId::from_generated_bytes([3; 32]),
+                },
+                app: AppId::from("repro"),
+            },
+            coordinator_subnet: subnet(4),
+            coordinator: canister(0xfff1),
+            recovery_controllers: Vec::new(),
+        },
+        epoch: 1,
+    };
+    let binding_for = |index: usize| {
+        let byte = u8::try_from(index % 250).expect("byte");
+        ComponentBinding {
+            authority: authority.clone(),
+            component: ComponentInstanceId::from_generated_bytes([byte; 32]),
+            component_spec: deployment.members[index].component_spec.clone(),
+            spec_hash: deployment.members[index].component_spec_hash,
+            role: CanisterRole::new("alpha"),
+            placement_subnet,
+            fleet_subnet_root: root,
+            canister_id: canister(u16::try_from(index).expect("index")),
+        }
+    };
+    let members: Vec<ComponentGroupDirectoryMember> = deployment
+        .members
+        .iter()
+        .enumerate()
+        .map(|(index, member)| ComponentGroupDirectoryMember {
+            member_path: member.member_path.clone(),
+            component_spec: member.component_spec.clone(),
+            purpose: member.purpose.clone(),
+            labels: member.labels.clone(),
+            binding: binding_for(index),
+        })
+        .collect();
+
+    // Minimal envelope: one Fleet root, no services, no direct children.
+    let request_for = |member_count: usize| ComponentRuntimeDirectoryPreparationRequest {
+        operation_id: [0x11; 32],
+        authority: ComponentRuntimeDirectoryAuthority {
+            fleet: FleetDirectorySnapshot {
+                provenance: FleetDirectoryProvenance {
+                    registry: FleetRegistryVersion {
+                        authority: authority.clone(),
+                        revision: 3,
+                        content_hash: [0x12; 32],
+                    },
+                    source_fleet_subnet_root: root,
+                },
+                fleet_subnet_roots: vec![FleetSubnetRootDirectoryEntry {
+                    placement_subnet,
+                    fleet_subnet_root: root,
+                    status: FleetSubnetRootStatus::Active,
+                }],
+                services: vec![],
+            },
+            component: ComponentDirectoryHead {
+                provenance: ComponentDirectoryProvenance {
+                    component: binding_for(0),
+                    source_fleet_subnet_root: root,
+                    component_registry_revision: 1,
+                    component_registry_content_hash: [0x13; 32],
+                    synchronized_at_ns: 14,
+                },
+                descendant_count: 0,
+            },
+            component_group: Some(ComponentGroupDirectory {
+                provenance: ComponentGroupDirectoryProvenance {
+                    authority: authority.clone(),
+                    fleet_subnet_root: root,
+                    group_placement: ComponentGroupPlacementId {
+                        deployment: deployment.deployment.clone(),
+                        ordinal: 0,
+                    },
+                    component_group: deployment.component_group.clone(),
+                    operation_id: [0x15; 32],
+                    plan_hash: [0x16; 32],
+                    placement_receipt_content_hash: [0x17; 32],
+                },
+                members: members[..member_count].to_vec(),
+            }),
+        },
+        direct_children: Vec::new(),
+    };
+    // Exactly the bytes root sends through CallOps::with_arg (candid encode_one).
+    let encoded_len = |member_count: usize| {
+        candid::encode_one(CanisterCommandFragment::ConfigureRuntime(request_for(
+            member_count,
+        )))
+        .expect("ConfigureRuntime Candid")
+        .len()
+    };
+
+    let first_overflow =
+        (1..=GROUP_MEMBERS).find(|count| encoded_len(*count) > DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES);
+    let one = encoded_len(1);
+    let two = encoded_len(2);
+    let bytes = encoded_len(GROUP_MEMBERS);
+    eprintln!("canic_command max_bytes: {DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES}");
+    eprintln!("ConfigureRuntime bytes with 1 member: {one}; per extra member: {}", two - one);
+    eprintln!("ConfigureRuntime bytes with {GROUP_MEMBERS} members: {bytes}");
+    eprintln!("first group size exceeding limit: {first_overflow:?}");
+    assert!(
+        bytes <= DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES,
+        "ConfigureRuntime for a validator-accepted {GROUP_MEMBERS}-member group is {bytes} bytes, \
+         above the target canic_command limit of {DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES} bytes \
+         (first overflow at {first_overflow:?} members)"
+    );
+}
