highreproducedcore-auth-1 · cycles · high confidence
GetOrCreateDelegationProof forces a new paid threshold-ECDSA batch signature on every call from any active Component that is not in the in-flight batch, whenever any template is due
crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegation/chain_key_batch/mod.rs:304

Failure scenario

Issuer B is stopped or out of cycles, so its installs fail and its template stays due. A non-issuer app canister calls GetOrCreateDelegationProof in a loop. Alternatively, users log in on an issuer whose template was disabled, and lazy repair calls it as a non-member. Each call in a new round prepares and signs a fresh batch at about 26.15B cycles, then returns SECURITY_UNAVAILABLE. With a 60 s max_revocation_latency that is up to 128 signatures (about 3.3T cycles) per minute. Once 128 batches are pending, the renewal timer's own prepare fails with CAPACITY_LIMIT, which is non-retryable, and the timer stops.

Evidence

The root command gate admits GetOrCreateDelegationProof for any active Component (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:296-310). The workflow passes the transport caller as required_issuer_pid (workflow/runtime/auth/provisioning/mod.rs:71-90). reusable_in_flight_chain_key_batch reuses a batch only if it contains that caller (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:303-310), and it never reuses Installed batches (311-320). Otherwise due_chain_key_templates collects every other enabled template that is due (selection.rs:20-38). A new batch is committed (mod.rs:259-276) with an id derived from now_ns (423-435), and get_or_create immediately signs it (provisioning/mod.rs:95-97). Signing attaches cost_sign_with_ecdsa cycles (infra/ic/mgmt/signing.rs:37-43). Only after that does signed_chain_key_delegation_proof_for_issuer(caller) find nothing and return auth_proof_pending (provisioning/mod.rs:102-104). A template stays due while its installs keep failing: install failures never update RootIssuerRenewalState (install.rs:201-232), and chain_key_template_due is true once refresh_after has passed (selection.rs:46-63). The only bound is 128 pending batches (mod.rs:225-230). Also, a second call in the same round produces the same batch_id, and upsert (mod.rs:274) resets a Signing batch to Prepared, which triggers a second paid signature for the same batch.

Recommendation

If the caller has no enabled template, return auth_proof_pending before any mutation or signing. For member callers, reuse any unexpired Signed, Installing or Installed batch that contains the caller, and only build a new batch if the caller has no valid proof anywhere. Do not fold other issuers' due templates into caller-driven batches; leave those to the timer. Make commit a no-op when a batch with the same id already exists in a non-Prepared state. Consider a per-caller rate limit on GetOrCreate.

Verifier (confirmed): The core claim holds. The root gate only requires an active Component (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:296-310). Neither the workflow (workflow/runtime/auth/provisioning/mod.rs:71-104) nor the plan checks whether the caller has an enabled template before doing paid work. For a non-member caller, reusable_in_flight_chain_key_batch never matches (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:303-310). due_chain_key_templates then collects other templates that are due (selection.rs:20-38). A new batch is committed (mod.rs:259-276) and signed with cost_sign_with_ecdsa cycles (infra/ic/mgmt/signing.rs:37-43). Only after that does the call return auth_proof_pending. B's template stays due while its installs fail, because only install success writes renewal state (install.rs:151-187, 289-312). Untrusted users can also reach this path through public PrepareDelegatedToken lazy repair on an issuer whose template was disabled and whose proof is expired or stale (prepare/mod.rs:320-349). Three corrections. (1) The same-round duplicate batch_id and Signing-to-Prepared reset claim is wrong. advance_delegated_auth_proof_epoch_at_least always increments (storage/stable/auth/mod.rs:317-327), and proof_epoch is hashed into batch_id (batch_id.rs:29), so each commit gets a distinct id. (2) The timer does not stop at the quota. With required_issuer_pid=None, reusable_in_flight returns any in-flight batch (mod.rs:189-203) before the quota check at 225-230. (3) Spend is capped at 128 signatures (about 3.3T cycles) per batch TTL window, where TTL = min(template ttl, max_cert_ttl, max_revocation_latency) (mod.rs:483-500). It still repeats every window, a sustained drain of root cycles.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. There is a concrete path from real entry points. Entry point 1: any active Component calls the root command GetOrCreateDelegationProof. The only gate is registry membership (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:296-310 and crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/component_auth/mod.rs:35-46). An enabled template is not required. The workflow passes the caller as required_issuer_pid (workflow/runtime/auth/provisioning/mod.rs:82-90). For a caller with no template, reusable_in_flight never matches (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:303-310). due_chain_key_templates still collects every other due template (selection.rs:26-36). A new batch is committed, and it is then signed with attached cycles (provisioning/mod.rs:95-97, signing.rs:116-128, infra/ic/mgmt/signing.rs:37-43). Only after that does the call return pending (provisioning/mod.rs:102-104). Entry point 2 needs no Component authority. PrepareDelegatedToken has no caller gate (role.rs:675-679). On SECURITY_CONFLICT or AUTH_CERT_EXPIRED it does a lazy repair that calls root (prepare/mod.rs:330-362). So on an issuer whose template was disabled and whose local proof is stale or expired, every user request costs root one paid signature. A proof that is merely missing does not trigger repair (token/error.rs:14-16). The "other template due" precondition is an ordinary failure. An issuer that is stopped or out of cycles stays due, because only an install success writes renewal state (install.rs:176-179, 267-275). A template is also due in every renewal window. The actor gains authority it does not hold: the ability to spend root's cycles on other issuers' signatures. Member callers are bounded to one signature per install cycle. Non-members are bounded only by the 128-pending cap per TTL window (mod.rs:225-230), and that repeats every window. This drains root cycles, and the fleet depends on root. I accept the verifier's corrections: the duplicate-id claim is wrong, and the timer does not stop. Severity stays high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): Not intended, and the code contradicts the current contract. docs/contracts/AUTH_DELEGATED_SIGNATURES.md:280-284 says root "returns a cached signed proof when possible" and "signs at most one in-flight batch when no valid batch exists". Lines 481-484 say lazy-repair signing is "bounded by delegation epoch rather than login volume". docs/architecture/authentication.md:295-299 and 433-434 say the same. The lazy-repair rules in the archived 0.76 design (docs/design/archive/0.76-auth/0.76-design.md, section 15, rules 3 and 6 plus the forbidden list) require that the caller be "registered and enabled under root issuer policy" and forbid forced fresh signing. Even the API docstring says "registered issuer caller" (api/auth/root.rs:59). In the code, the gate checks only active Component membership (root.rs:296-310; component_auth/mod.rs:34-47). The workflow prepares and signs before it looks up the caller's proof (provisioning/mod.rs:81-104). A non-member caller never matches reusable_in_flight (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:303-310). due_chain_key_templates then collects other templates that are due (selection.rs:20-38). Those templates stay due because failed installs never write renewal state (install.rs:201-232). Only success writes it, at 257-276. I found no known-limitation entry in docs/status/current.md or CHANGELOG.md. The recommended fix (reject callers without an enabled template before any mutation, return cached proofs) matches the design. Impact check: each call pays about 26.15B cycles for sign_with_ecdsa (signing.rs:114-124). The shipped configs use a 60 s max_revocation_latency (apps/test/canic.toml:64), and the 128-pending cap (mod.rs:66, 225-230) resets every TTL window. That allows about 3.3T cycles per minute, sustained, which can drain root. I accept the verifier's corrections: batch ids are distinct, and the timer does not stop. The trigger needs a fleet-internal Component, or a public login on a misconfigured issuer, which fits the high tier for a reachable authorization weakness that burns cycles.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test sets up issuer B (p(200)) with a root issuer policy and an enabled renewal template, and no renewal state, which is the situation when B's installs keep failing. Caller C (p(201)) has no template. The test calls the existing helper prepare_sign_and_find_test_issuer_proof five times with required_issuer_pid = C at increasing now_ns. That helper runs the same ops sequence as the workflow's get_or_create_chain_key_delegation_proof_for_issuer_root: plan, commit, then sign_chain_key_root_delegation_batch, then signed_chain_key_delegation_proof_for_issuer. Signing goes through a counting DynamicMockSigner. After each call the test records an install failure (CallFailed) for B on every Signed batch. It asserts that C gets zero signer calls and zero new batches. Result: each call made one signer call (the paid sign_with_ecdsa in production), for 5 in total. Five distinct B-only batches were committed and signed, and the proof epoch went from 0 to 14. Every call still returned no proof for C, which is auth_proof_pending in production. The recorded install failures did not stop B's template from being due. So the core claim holds: a caller with no template can drive repeated paid signatures of other issuers' batches. Not exercised: the root endpoint gate, the real management-canister cycle cost, and the 128-pending cap. The test also shows distinct batch ids per call, which matches the verifier's correction of the duplicate-id claim.

highreproducedcore-rpc-ic-1 · liveness · high confidence
A deposit_cycles failure marks the child-funding receipt RecoveryRequired, which blocks all later funding for that child and has no resume or clear path
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:437

Failure scenario

A parent holds 3T native cycles and its freezing reserve is 2.5T. A child requests 2T. The preflight passes (2T <= 3T) and the cost guard passes (3T >= 2T + 1B). ic-cdk then finds only 0.5T liquid and returns InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance. The receipt becomes RecoveryRequired for good. Every later attempt from the child, with the same op id or a new one, returns REQUEST_INCOMPLETE. The child retries every 30 minutes and is never funded until it freezes. The only recovery is reinstalling the parent; if the parent is root, that means the whole fleet.

Evidence

The deposit uses unbounded wait (infra/ic/mgmt/cycles.rs:43), so any Err means the transfer did not execute. At nonroot_cycles.rs:434-438 the handler treats it that way: it restores the funding ledger and releases the cycle reservation, but it also marks the receipt RecoveryRequired{ExternalEffectStatusUnknown} (lines 615-627). The resulting state:
- abort only removes Reserved receipts (ops/replay/receipt.rs:474-480), and RecoveryRequired survives expiry and counts as pending (storage/stable/replay.rs:401-416).
- A retry with the same op id falls through to ReplayDuplicateSame (handler/replay.rs:176-183). Any new op id is refused with FundingOperationInProgress (nonroot_cycles.rs:395-409).
- Only three places remove receipts (receipt.rs:301, 477, 490): the placement acknowledgement and the two abort paths. None applies here.
- The child treats remote rejections as retryable, because observed_public sets code PLATFORM_FAILED (error.rs:68-73, cycles/mod.rs:966-970), and it reuses the same operation generation (async_job_recovery/mod.rs:320-371).
The trigger is ordinary. The preflight and cost guard use native canister_cycle_balance with only a 1B-cycle margin (nonroot_cycles.rs:48, 367, 551), but ic-cdk 0.20.3 refuses the call when the liquid balance is too low (call.rs:753-763, 904). A second path wedges the same way: when stage_response fails (lines 452-459), recovery later finds StagedResponseMissing on every retry. By contrast, ICP refill resumes ExternalEffectStatusUnknown (icp_refill/replay.rs:79-86).

Recommendation

When an unbounded-wait deposit returns any CallFailed, treat it as not executed. Restore the ledger, recover the cost guard, and remove the receipt (for example with abort_uncommitted_receipt) so the same op id can retry fresh. Reserve RecoveryRequired for true unknowns such as a trap after the await, and give those a resume or clear path that does not block every other operation. Base the parent preflight and cost-guard balance on canister_liquid_cycle_balance(). Add a regression test in which the deposit fails with InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance.

highreproducedcp-fleet-coordinator-1 · liveness · high confidence
Root-removal timer uses the reservation-time Registry version as the compare-and-swap version for both publications, so any unrelated Registry revision permanently wedges the removal and admission
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:842

Failure scenario

An operator issues RemoveRoot for root A (op1) and root B (op2) while the Registry is at version V. Both reservations commit at V, and both Roots accept and start draining (fleet_subnet_root.rs:270-299). A's timer publishes A Draining, moving the Registry to V+1. B's timer calls `publish_root_draining(expected_registry = V)`, gets STATE_CONFLICT, and repeats every second forever. B remains Active with a reservation, so `require_admission_transition_start_allowed` rejects every admission mutation permanently. Root B stays stuck in draining. Resubmitting RemoveRoot replays the same reservation and the same stale version. The same thing happens if a scale-out on another root or a funding rotation publishes between B's reservation and its draining publication.

Evidence

`advance_coordinator_root_removal_once` builds the draining publication with `expected_registry: current.reservation.request.expected_registry` (mod.rs:841-844). It builds the removal publication with `expected_registry: final_inventory.registry.clone()` (851-857). Both ops require `request.expected_registry == previous_version`, the current head (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1784-1786, 1855-1857). The ops layer is designed to consume an older reservation after unrelated revisions: the test at workflow/fleet_coordinator/tests.rs:1113-1134 sets `publication.expected_registry` to the current version, while `root_draining.active_registry` keeps the reservation version, which `validate_draining_publication_request` checks separately (root_lifecycle.rs:427-436). Nothing serializes Registry writers. `prepare_root_draining_reservation` accepts a second reservation for another root at the same version (mod.rs:1690-1739). Scale-out publication (mod.rs:1255-1258) and funding rotation (funding_rotation.rs:487-511) can revise the Registry while a reservation exists. Admission unblocks as soon as the root is Draining, because `root_removal_active` counts only Active roots (admission.rs:43-52). On conflict the timer reschedules every 1 s forever (mod.rs:806-815). The reservation is immutable (mod.rs:1701-1709), the only publication entry points outside tests are this timer, and no cancel command exists.

Recommendation

In the timer, pass the Coordinator's current version (`FleetCoordinatorOps::version()`) as `expected_registry` for both publications. Keep reservation and source-version binding in `root_draining.active_registry` and `final_inventory.registry`, which the validators already check. Add a workflow test that interleaves an unrelated Registry revision before each publication step. Alternatively, reject a new reservation, scale-out or rotation while any removal is between reservation and Removed.

The ops test at tests.rs:1113-1134 shows the intended use: CAS on the current version, with the reservation version carried in `active_registry` (root_lifecycle.rs:427-436). highreproducedcp-fleet-coordinator-2 · liveness · medium confidence
Funding-policy rotation holds an irrevocable Fleet-wide fence that deadlocks with a Root's unresolved local funding request, freezing all funding and all Registry commits
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:98

Failure scenario

Root R's RequestRootFunding reaches the Coordinator, which records a terminal Granted `last`. R's bounded-wait call to the Coordinator (fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:108) times out with SysUnknown, so R keeps its request in GrantAccepted. Alternatively, R has just prepared a request that the Coordinator has not processed yet. A controller now runs BeginFundingPolicyRotation, which succeeds because the Coordinator has no `current` for R. R retries and gets a conflict before the Coordinator replays `last`. After stage and apply, the timer's PrepareRoot(R) gets a conflict because R still holds its request. Neither side can progress. No Root in the Fleet can receive a grant, no Registry transition can commit, and no command can clear the rotation.

Evidence

`begin_funding_policy_rotation` looks only for in-flight grants on the Coordinator side (`current.roots.iter().any(|root| root.current.is_some())`, funding_rotation.rs:204). It commits `rotation_current` already in Staging (219-229). While that record exists, `prepare_root_funding` returns conflict (root_funding.rs:98-103), and this check comes before the exact-replay checks of `current` and `last` (128-138). Every Registry commit also fails (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:2027-2032). On the Root side, `prepare_policy_rotation` rejects when the Root has its own unresolved request (`current.current.is_some()`, ops/root_funding/mod.rs:179). The Root clears that request only after recording a terminal Coordinator response (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:457-487); on error it keeps the request and retries (canic-core workflow/runtime/cycles/mod.rs:660-667). The rotation timer retries PrepareRoot every 1 s forever (workflow mod.rs:729-739). CoordinatorCommand has no abort or cancel variant (dto/fleet_coordinator.rs:65-82). Begin also does not check `root_draining_reservations`, whereas design 0.108 requires 'response-loss replay' and 'exact root retry' to be preserved.

Recommendation

Move the `rotation_current` rejection in `prepare_root_funding` below the exact `current` and `last` replay checks, so pending Root journals can always settle during a rotation. Make PrepareRoot report, or let the Coordinator resolve, a Root's pending request instead of failing forever. Add a controller abort for rotations in Staging and PreparingRoots that clears the fence when no Root has prepared. Make begin reject while any root removal is in progress.

Verifier (confirmed): The deadlock is real, and it is easier to reach than the finding says. `begin_funding_policy_rotation` rejects only when the Coordinator itself holds a `current` grant (funding_rotation.rs:204). It commits `rotation_current` in Staging (219-229). `prepare_root_funding` then returns conflict at root_funding.rs:98-103, before the `current` and `last` replay checks at 128-138. As a result, a Root whose Granted response was lost (a bounded-wait call, fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:108) can never collect its replay. There is a second trigger the finding does not mention. Before its own PrepareRoot runs, a Root still has no local fence, so `RootFundingOps::prepare_request` (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:53) checks only root-local `rotation_current`. Any Root at or below its threshold between Begin and its PrepareRoot therefore creates a new `current`, gets a conflict and keeps the request. Conflict counts as retryable (cycles/mod.rs:969). Root retries run every 1-30 minutes (lines 64-65). PrepareRoot then fails every time at ops/root_funding/mod.rs:179 (`current.current.is_some()`). The workflow only calls `reconcile()`, which re-arms the Root timer (workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:90-102). The Coordinator timer retries every second, forever (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:729-739). Nothing can clear the fence. CoordinatorCommand has no abort (dto:65-82). SetRootFunding is also fenced (root_funding.rs:208-213). Registry commits fail (mod.rs:2027-2032), and authority snapshots are refused (root_funding.rs:233). Design 0.108 M8 requires response-loss replay and preserved current/last replay evidence, so this is not intended. Recovery needs out-of-band code or snapshot intervention. The trigger is privileged and rare, so high fits.

The controller holds no power here that is being abused. The problem is that a routine rotation races with ordinary Root timer behavior. Path: 1. A Root timer fires while the Root is at or below its threshold. `prepare_request` (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:46-104) checks only the Root's own `rotation_current`. It commits `current` whenever the Root has not yet been prepared for the rotation. On the Coordinator, `prepare_root_funding` rejects with conflict at root_funding.rs:98-103. This check runs before the `current` and `last` replay checks (128-138), so the Root never gets to see its `last` replay. 3. `record_response` (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:457-495) accepts only Granted or NoGrant responses. It is also the only place that clears `current` (line 490). A conflict therefore leaves `current` in place, and the Root retries every 1 to 30 minutes (cycles/mod.rs:64-65). 4. The Coordinator timer's PrepareRoot step calls the Root's `prepare_policy_rotation`. SetRootFunding is also fenced (root_funding.rs:208-213), and so are all Registry commits (mod.rs:2027-2032). Design 0.108 M8 (lines 1511-1526) requires response-loss replay and preserved current/last replay evidence. This deadlock is therefore not intended behavior. Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): The design intent supports the finding and nothing documents this as a limitation. Design 0.108 M8 (docs/design/0.108-coordinator-backed-root-funding/0.108-design.md:1519-1566) requires the operation to "prepare every affected Root" and to "preserve ... prior current/last replay evidence". +    let coordinator_balance = 2_000_000_000_000_000;
+
+    // Root R (= `second`) keeps its own local journal.
+    RootFundingStore::import(RootFundingData::default());
+    RootFundingOps::commit_genesis(RootFundingOps::compile_genesis()).expect("Root genesis");
+    let root_authority = RootFundingAuthorityView {
+        registry: predecessor_registry.clone(),
+        fleet_subnet_root: second.fleet_subnet_root,
+        status: FleetSubnetRootStatus::Active,
+        funding_eligible: true,
+        funding: second.funding.clone(),
+    };
+
+    // Controller begins a rotation; the Coordinator has no unresolved grant anywhere.
+    let plan = funding_rotation_plan(predecessor_registry, [&first, &second]);
+    let plan_digest = fleet_funding_policy_rotation_plan_digest(&plan);
+    let operation_id = fleet_funding_policy_rotation_operation_id(coordinator, plan_digest);
+    FleetCoordinatorOps::begin_funding_policy_rotation(
+        FleetFundingPolicyRotationBeginRequest {
+            operation_id,
+            plan_digest,
+            header: plan.header.clone(),
+        },
+        10,
+    )
+    .expect("begin rotation");
+
+    // R's timer fires below threshold before PrepareRoot(R): the Root is not yet fenced locally.
+    let root_request = RootFundingOps::prepare_request(&root_authority, 42_200_000_000, 11)
+        .expect("Root opens a fresh local request before its PrepareRoot");
+    let first_attempt = FleetCoordinatorOps::prepare_root_funding(
+        second.fleet_subnet_root,
+        root_request.clone(),
+        coordinator_balance,
+        12,
+    );
+    println!(
+        "coordinator response to R's request: {}",
+        match &first_attempt {
+            Ok(_) => "Ok".to_string(),
+            Err(error) => format!("Err(code = {:?})", error.public_error().code()),
+        }
+    );
+
+    for root in &plan.roots {
+        FleetCoordinatorOps::stage_funding_policy_rotation_root(
+            FleetFundingPolicyRotationStageRootRequest {
+                operation_id,
+                plan_digest,
+                root: root.clone(),
+            },
+            13,
+        )
+        .expect("stage Root");
+    }
+    FleetCoordinatorOps::apply_funding_policy_rotation(
+        FleetFundingPolicyRotationApplyRequest {
+            operation_id,
+            plan_digest,
+            expected_predecessor_generation: 1,
+        },
+        14,
+    )
+    .expect("apply rotation");
+
+    // Drive the Coordinator rotation step until it asks R to prepare.
+    let mut root_prepare = None;
+    let mut root_prepare_request = None;
+    for attempt in 0..4_u64 {
+        match FleetCoordinatorOps::funding_policy_rotation_step().expect("rotation step") {
+            FleetFundingPolicyRotationStep::PrepareRoot {
+                fleet_subnet_root,
+                request,
+            } if fleet_subnet_root == second.fleet_subnet_root => {
+                root_prepare = Some(RootFundingOps::prepare_policy_rotation(
+                    &root_authority,
+                    request.clone(),
+                    20 + attempt,
+                ));
+                root_prepare_request = Some(request);
+                break;
+            }
+            FleetFundingPolicyRotationStep::PrepareRoot { request, .. } => {
+                FleetCoordinatorOps::record_funding_policy_rotation_root_prepared(
+                    rotation_root_receipt(&request, false, 20 + attempt),
+                    20 + attempt,
+                )
+                .expect("record other Root prepared");
+            }
+            _ => panic!("rotation must prepare R before publication"),
+        }
+    }
+    let root_prepare = root_prepare.expect("Coordinator asked R to prepare");
+    println!(
+        "PrepareRoot(R) on the Root: {}",
+        match &root_prepare {
+            Ok(_) => "Ok".to_string(),
+            Err(error) => format!("Err(code = {:?})", error.public_error().code()),
+        }
+    );
+    println!(
+        "Root still holds unresolved request: {}",
+        RootFundingOps::current_request(&root_authority)
+            .expect("Root current request")
+            .is_some()
+    );
+
+    // R's scheduled retry of its exact request after the fence was applied.
+    let retry = FleetCoordinatorOps::prepare_root_funding(
+        second.fleet_subnet_root,
+        root_request,
+        coordinator_balance,
+        30,
+    );
+    println!(
+        "coordinator response to R's retry: {}",
+        match &retry {
+            Ok(_) => "Ok".to_string(),
+            Err(error) => format!("Err(code = {:?})", error.public_error().code()),
+        }
+    );
+
+    // Control probe: the Root's unresolved `current` is the sole PrepareRoot obstacle.
+    let root_snapshot = RootFundingStore::export();
+    let mut cleared = root_snapshot.clone();
+    cleared.current.as_mut().expect("Root record").current = None;
+    RootFundingStore::import(cleared);
+    let control = RootFundingOps::prepare_policy_rotation(
+        &root_authority,
+        root_prepare_request.clone().expect("PrepareRoot request"),
+        40,
+    );
+    println!(
+        "control PrepareRoot(R) with local current cleared: {}",
+        match &control {
+            Ok(_) => "Ok".to_string(),
+            Err(error) => format!("Err(code = {:?})", error.public_error().code()),
+        }
+    );
+    RootFundingStore::import(root_snapshot);
+
+    let coordinator_progress = first_attempt.is_ok() || retry.is_ok();
+    let root_progress = root_prepare.is_ok();
+    assert!(
+        coordinator_progress || root_progress,
+        "rotation deadlock: Coordinator fences R's request and R rejects PrepareRoot"
+    );

highreproducedcp-fleet-coordinator-3 · liveness · high confidence
Root reservation and draining are allowed during an active fresh-install or scale-out, which permanently wedges that operation's service publication
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/service_publication/mod.rs:231

Failure scenario

A fresh install is provisioning across roots R1 and R2, and R2's batch has no placements. The operator removes spare root R2. The reservation succeeds, and R2's draining publication moves the Registry to V+1. After all roots report Provisioned, `publish_component_provisioning_services` sees `current.registry != source_registry` and returns conflict, repeating forever. The fresh install never reaches RuntimesActivated, the deployment ledger never exists, scale-out can never start, and admission stays blocked. Components already created and installed on R1 remain unpublished.

Evidence

`compile_service_publication` requires `current.registry == source_registry` (service_publication/mod.rs:231-233) and `previous_version == record.plan.fleet_registry` (255-257). Every Component operation is therefore bound to the exact Registry at plan time. The reservation guards only exclude roots that receive placements. `require_component_plan_roots_unreserved` skips batches with empty placements (root_lifecycle.rs:49-64). `require_grouped_root_lifecycle_open`, which `prepare_root_draining_reservation` and `publish_root_draining` use, only counts journal batches with `!batch.placements.is_empty()` (root_lifecycle.rs:103-109). Yet a fresh-install plan must contain a batch for every root (component_provisioning_plan/mod.rs:710-717), and its `directory_confirmation_roots` must be every Active root (703-708). A root with an empty batch can therefore be reserved and published Draining in the middle of the operation, and that revision breaks the equality check. The provisioning loop then logs, records a failure and retries every second (workflow mod.rs:939-971). No abort exists, only one scale-out may be active (mod.rs:669-691), and admission stays blocked while a Component operation is non-terminal (admission.rs:33-42).

Recommendation

Reject root reservations and lifecycle publications while any Component operation is non-terminal, or at least for every root in `plan.batches` or `plan.directory_confirmation_roots`. Mirror the rule in `prepare_component_provisioning`. Add tests for reserve-then-publish during each Component phase.

Verifier (confirmed): The core defect is real, but the stated scenario needs a correction. Coordinator side: `prepare_root_draining_reservation` (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1690-1722) and `publish_root_draining` (1759-1763) check only `require_admission_transition_idle` and `require_grouped_root_lifecycle_open`. That fence ignores empty batches (root_lifecycle.rs:103-109). Admission, by contrast, explicitly blocks while a Component operation is active (admission.rs:33-42). Neither `validate_current` nor the history replay rejects a draining receipt committed before a pending publication. `compile_service_publication` then requires `current.registry == source_registry` (service_publication/mod.rs:231-233), and no abort exists. Correction for fresh install: once R2 has accepted its empty batch, the Root refuses draining. `require_root_draining_open` rejects while `active_operation_id` is Some (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:1191-1197), and that value stays set until RuntimesActive (1650-1656). So the finding's 'after all roots Provisioned' case is not reachable. The fresh-install window runs only until R2's acceptance commits, but that window includes the awaits inside root `accept` (workflow/component_provisioning.rs:125-140). The scale-out window is wider. Any spare Active root outside batches, confirmation roots, placements and services stays lifecycle-open on both sides for the whole period before publication. This matches the design intent to leave 'unrelated empty roots lifecycle-open' (docs/design/archive/0.101-.../status.md:553-555). Draining such a root moves the Registry and permanently wedges the operation. Recovery needs a reinstall, so high rather than critical. Separate lead: history replay applies all service receipts before lifecycle receipts (registry_history.rs:80-99).
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. I traced a concrete path from the entry point to the wedge. Entry point: `canic_coordinator_command(RemoveRoot)`, which only a Coordinator controller can call (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:81-100). That call goes to `accept_root_removal` (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:497-501), which checks only `require_admission_transition_idle`. That check covers admission transitions only (ops/fleet_admission/mod.rs:271-277). It then calls `prepare_root_draining_reservation`, which checks `require_grouped_root_lifecycle_open` (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1721). That fence ignores roots that are not named by a non-empty batch, a placement or a service member (root_lifecycle.rs:103-109). In a scale-out, a spare Active root is outside `plan.batches` and the confirmation roots (scale_out/mod.rs:146-153, 284-312). On the Root side, `require_root_draining_open` sees no active operation and zero placements (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:1191-1197), so the Root accepts. The removal timer then calls `publish_root_draining` (workflow mod.rs:840-845), and the Registry revision advances. At publication, `compile_service_publication` requires `current.registry == source_registry` and `previous_version == plan.fleet_registry` (service_publication/mod.rs:231-233, 255-257). Both checks now fail permanently, because draining is one-way. The retry loop reschedules every second (workflow mod.rs:939-971). No abort exists. Admission stays blocked because the operation never reaches RuntimesActivated (admission.rs:33-42). The design explicitly sanctions this concurrency: it says unrelated empty roots stay "lifecycle-open" and names "later unrelated Registry revisions" (0.101 status.md:553-560). The trigger is therefore a supported, fenced command, not an abuse of controller power. That the controller holds greater authority does not excuse a wedge the fences were meant to prevent. I agree with the verifier's correction. The fresh-install window is narrow and closes once the Root accepts its batch. The scale-out window covers the whole period before publication. The trigger is controller-only and there is no CLI surface, and recovery means reinstalling the fleet, so this is high rather than critical.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): The fence itself is intended, but the wedge it allows is not. The archived 0.101 design deliberately fences only "a root named by a nonempty operation batch, committed placement or Fleet-service binding, leaving unrelated empty roots lifecycle-open" (docs/design/archive/0.101-.../status.md:553-555). Changelog 0.101.37 (docs/changelog/0.101.md:650-653) goes further and says in-progress references "do not globally block an unrelated empty root." So the design expects an unrelated root to be drained while a Component operation is running. Nothing reconciles that with publication. `compile_service_publication` still demands `current.registry == source_registry` and `previous_version == plan.fleet_registry` (service_publication/mod.rs:231-233, 255-257). The source is fixed at plan time (registry_history.rs:448-457). `publish_root_draining` checks only `require_grouped_root_lifecycle_open` (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1763), which ignores empty batches (root_lifecycle.rs:103-109). Scale-out has no rebase and no abort, and any other state is `conflict` (mod.rs:689-691). Admission stays blocked (admission.rs:33-42). The reverse ordering also wedges. If service publication lands first, the draining publication fails its exact `expected_registry` check (mod.rs:1785-1787, root_lifecycle.rs:424-425). The Root has already stopped its pool (fleet_subnet_root.rs:276). No doc, status note or CHANGELOG entry records this as a known limitation. I agree with the verifier's correction that the fresh-install window closes once the Root accepts (component_provisioning/mod.rs:1191-1197). The scale-out window stays open until publication. Calibration: RemoveRoot is controller-only (macros/endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:81-100) and has no canic-cli or canic-host exposure, so it is not a routine CLI action. Reinstall is the pre-1.0 recovery. That keeps this high, not critical. The recommended global fence would contradict the documented lifecycle-open intent, so this is a design decision. The alternative fix is to rebase publication over unrelated lifecycle revisions.

Grant revocation rejects a previous allocation's disabled grant tombstone, so a canister reused by a non-fixture role can never be recycled again, and the pool maintenance timer disables itself
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fixture_grant/mod.rs:289

Failure scenario

A Root release has a fixture-bearing role T and a plain role U. Allocation C/op1 (role T) gets asset A and receives grant rev 1. C is deleted: the grant is revoked (rev 2, disabled, binding C/op1) and A returns to Ready. Allocation D/op2 (role U) claims A as the smallest sufficient asset; no grant is written. When D is deleted, recycle(A) reaches revoke_before_reset, sees the C/op1 tombstone, and revocation_request returns conflict. D's deletion fails on every retry. The next timer pass picks A, gets the same conflict, and permanently disables pool maintenance: no resets, no refill. Root retirement can never finish (non_store_asset_count stays above 0). The same happens if a fixture-role allocation is recycled before its own grant was issued.

Evidence

revocation_request builds granted_claim from the observed grant's binding (component, installation) and returns Err(conflict) when it differs from the current recycling claim (fixture_grant/mod.rs:285-291). The `!grant.enabled => Ok(None)` short-circuit only runs afterwards (292-294). The Store keeps revoked grants as disabled tombstones keyed by target Principal (ops/fixture_store/mod.rs:109-135; storage/stable/fixture_store/mod.rs:119-124,218-224). Roles without a fixture source never touch the Store grant: installation() returns None and select/ensure_component do nothing (component_installation/fixture/mod.rs:46-50,86-89). revoke_before_reset reads the grant for every recycling asset whenever the Root release has any fixtures (fixture/mod.rs:23-58; root_wasm_store.rs:195-199). reset_asset propagates that error with `?` before mark_failed (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:622), so the asset stays Recycling{Pending}. Maintenance always picks the first pending reset (270-277). STATE_CONFLICT is not retryable (492-501), so the pass counts as InvariantFailure, and finish_maintenance_timer clears MAINTENANCE_ENABLED and cancels both timers (448-451).

Recommendation

In revocation_request, return Ok(None) for a disabled grant on the same target before comparing claims, or accept a disabled grant whose installation differs from the claim, since it grants no access. Keep the conflict only for an enabled grant that belongs to a different claim. Separately, stop treating a single asset's STATE_CONFLICT as grounds to cancel the whole maintenance loop: mark that asset Failed and move on.

Verifier (confirmed): I could not refute this; every link in the chain holds. `revocation_request` compares the observed grant's (component, installation) with the pending claim and returns `conflict` (fixture_grant/mod.rs:285-291) before it reaches the `!grant.enabled => Ok(None)` check at 292-294. Revocation only writes a disabled tombstone; nothing deletes it except Store GC clearing (ops/fixture_store/mod.rs:124-135,164-175; stable/fixture_store:153-178). The grant `installation` is the allocation's `operation_id` (component_installation/mod.rs:412,507), which is also the claim key (23-26). `claim_smallest_sufficient_ready` picks any Ready asset whatever its role (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:386-409), and `recycling_completion` returns Recycling{Ready} assets to Ready (1641-1655). Roles without a fixture source never read or write the grant (component_installation/fixture/mod.rs:46-50,86-89). `revoke_before_reset` reads the grant for every recycling asset once `fixture_delivery_store()` is Some, which is true whenever the release has any fixtures (root_wasm_store.rs:195-199). `reset_asset` then fails with `?` at canister_pool/mod.rs:622, before `mark_failed`, so the asset stays Recycling{Pending}. `retry_reset` is a no-op for that state (ops:249-253), and handoff accepts only Ready or Failed (ops:1075-1078). `conflict()` is STATE_CONFLICT (canic-core/src/error.rs:129-131), which is not retryable (mod.rs:492-501), so the timer clears MAINTENANCE_ENABLED and cancels itself (448-451). Manual Maintain also fails, because a pending reset is handled before refill (270-277). The design doc says the fixture feature and mixed fleets are qualified (design.md:780-798), so this is reachable in production. Cycles are stranded, not lost, and a clean reinstall recovers, so high is right rather than critical.

+//! Reproduction: a pool asset reused by a non-fixture role cannot be recycled
+//! because the previous allocation's disabled grant tombstone is rejected.

+use super::*;
+use crate::{
+    ops::{
+        canister_pool::CanisterPoolClaimKey,
+        fixture_grant,
+        fixture_store::{grant_status, prepare, set_grant, upload},
+    },

+        fixture_store::{FixtureStore, FixtureStoreData},
+        template::WasmStoreGcStateStore,
+    },
+};
+use canic_core::{
+    dto::fixture_provisioning::{
+        FixtureChunkDescriptor, FixtureChunkUpload, FixtureDescriptor, FixtureGrantRequest,
+        FixtureTargetBinding,
+    },
+    ids::{
+        CanisterRole, ComponentBinding, ComponentInstanceId, FleetSubnetWasmStoreAuthority,
+        ManagedCanisterBinding, ReleaseBuildId, ReleaseBuildNonce,
+    },
+};
+use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
+
+fn principal(byte: u8) -> Principal {
+    Principal::from_slice(&[byte; 29])
+}
+
+fn pool_config() -> FleetSubnetCanisterPoolConfig {
+    FleetSubnetCanisterPoolConfig {
+        minimum_size: 1,
+        maximum_size: 4,
+        canister_cycles: Cycles::new(100),
+        creation_execution_margin: Cycles::new(20),
+    }
+}
+
+fn store_authority() -> FleetSubnetWasmStoreAuthority {
+    FleetSubnetWasmStoreAuthority {
+        authority: crate::test_support::root_funding_request_fixture(1)
+            .expected_registry
+            .authority,
+        placement_subnet: SubnetId::from_principal(principal(9)),
+        fleet_subnet_root: principal(10),
+        wasm_store: principal(11),
+        installation_controller: principal(12),
+        release_build_id: ReleaseBuildId::from_nonce(ReleaseBuildNonce::from_random_bytes(
+            [13; 32],
+        )),
+        wasm_module_hash: [14; 32],
+    }
+}
+
+fn reset_state() {
+    CanisterPoolOps::clear_for_test();
+    FixtureStore::import(FixtureStoreData::default());
+    WasmStoreGcStateStore::clear_for_test();
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_reused_asset_tombstone_blocks_recycling() {
+    reset_state();
+    let now = 1;
+    let asset = principal(30);
+    let config = pool_config();
+
+    // One Ready pool asset A.
+    CanisterPoolOps::initialize_imports(&config, &[asset], now).expect("import asset");
+    CanisterPoolOps::mark_ready(asset, Cycles::new(100), now).expect("ready asset");
+
+    // Store holds one complete fixture source for fixture-bearing role T.
+    let bytes = vec![1u8; 16];
+    let descriptor = FixtureDescriptor {
+        schema_version: 1,
+        format_hash: [7; 32],
+        encoded_length: bytes.len() as u64,
+        chunks: vec![FixtureChunkDescriptor {
+            digest: Sha256::digest(&bytes).into(),
+            length: u32::try_from(bytes.len()).unwrap(),
+        }],
+        completion_summary: [8; 32],
+    };
+    let content = prepare(descriptor, u64::MAX, 0).unwrap().content_id;
+    upload(
+        FixtureChunkUpload {
+            content_id: content,
+            index: 0,
+            bytes,
+        },
+        u64::MAX,
+        0,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let authority = store_authority();
+
+    // Allocation C/op1 (role T, fixture-bearing) claims A and is granted rev 1.
+    let claim_c = CanisterPoolClaimKey {
+        component: ComponentInstanceId::from_generated_bytes([41; 32]),
+        operation_id: [42; 32],
+    };
+    assert_eq!(
+        CanisterPoolOps::claim_smallest_sufficient_ready(&claim_c, &Cycles::new(100), now)
+            .unwrap(),
+        Some(asset)
+    );
+    CanisterPoolOps::finalize_claim(&claim_c, asset, now).unwrap();
+    let binding_c = FixtureTargetBinding {
+        target: ManagedCanisterBinding::Component(ComponentBinding {
+            authority: authority.authority.clone(),
+            component: claim_c.component,
+            component_spec: "fixture".parse().unwrap(),
+            spec_hash: [16; 32],
+            role: CanisterRole::from("fixture"),
+            placement_subnet: authority.placement_subnet,
+            fleet_subnet_root: authority.fleet_subnet_root,
+            canister_id: asset,
+        }),
+        installation: claim_c.operation_id,
+        release_build_id: authority.release_build_id,
+        content_id: content,
+    };
+    let issued = set_grant(
+        FixtureGrantRequest {
+            expected_revision: 0,
+            binding: binding_c,
+            enabled: true,
+        },
+        &authority,
+        u64::MAX,
+        0,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+
+    // C is deleted: recycling revokes its grant (Store keeps a disabled tombstone),
+    // the reset completes and A returns to Ready.
+    CanisterPoolOps::register_recycled_pending(asset, now).unwrap();
+    let pending_c = CanisterPoolOps::pending_recycling_claim(asset)
+        .unwrap()
+        .unwrap();
+    let revoke = fixture_grant::revocation_request(asset, &pending_c, Some(&issued))
+        .unwrap()
+        .expect("C's own grant is revoked");
+    let tombstone = set_grant(revoke, &authority, u64::MAX, 0).unwrap();

+    CanisterPoolOps::complete_recycling(asset, claim_c.component, now).unwrap();
+
+    // Allocation D/op2 (plain role U, no fixture source) reuses A; no grant is written.

+        component: ComponentInstanceId::from_generated_bytes([51; 32]),
+        operation_id: [52; 32],

+            .unwrap(),
+        Some(asset),
+        "D reuses the same physical asset"
+    );
+    CanisterPoolOps::finalize_claim(&claim_d, asset, now).unwrap();
+
+    // D is deleted: revoke_before_reset reads the Store grant for A and asks
+    // revocation_request whether an effect is needed for claim D/op2.
+    CanisterPoolOps::register_recycled_pending(asset, now).unwrap();
+    let pending_d = CanisterPoolOps::pending_recycling_claim(asset)
+        .unwrap()
+        .unwrap();
+    let observed = grant_status(asset);
+    println!("tombstone written by C's revocation: {tombstone:?}");
+    println!(
+        "observed grant for A during D's recycle: revision={:?} enabled={:?} installation={:?}",
+        observed.as_ref().map(|g| g.revision),
+        observed.as_ref().map(|g| g.enabled),
+        observed.as_ref().map(|g| g.binding.installation[0]),
+    );
+    println!(
+        "pending recycling claim: operation_id[0]={}",
+        pending_d.operation_id[0]
+    );
+    let result = fixture_grant::revocation_request(asset, &pending_d, observed.as_ref());
+    println!(
+        "revocation_request result: {:?}",
+        result.as_ref().map_err(InternalError::code)
+    );

+    // pass classifier (the error is not Clone, so reproduce it deterministically).

+    // no access, so recycling D needs no Store effect and must not conflict.
+    assert!(
+        matches!(result, Ok(None)),
+        "revocation of a reused asset must accept the previous allocation's disabled tombstone, got {:?}",
+        result.map_err(|error| error.code())

highreproducedcp-pool-provisioning-2 · correctness · high confidence
Recycling completion is idempotent on component ID only, so a second recycle of the same asset under the same component silently does nothing and leaves the asset stuck in Recycling forever
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1637

Failure scenario

Active Component C has child X on asset A (claim C/opX). A caller-selected subtree removal (allowed while Active) recycles A: it returns to Ready with last_recycle=C/opX. C then creates child Z, which claims A again (C/opZ). When Z is removed, recycle(A) resets it to Recycling{C/opZ, Ready}. validate_complete_recycling returns Ok, Z's Registry membership is removed, and complete_recycling returns early. A is never Ready again and no Registry row points to it. Its pool slot and cycles are lost to the pool, and Root draining stalls permanently at finalize_inventory with STATE_UNAVAILABLE.

Evidence

recycling_completion returns Ok(None) whenever asset.last_recycle.component == component, before looking at the current Recycling claim (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1630-1640). complete_recycling therefore changes nothing (1354-1362), and validate_complete_recycling returns Ok (1372-1377). Pool claims for children use the parent Component ID: CanisterPoolClaimKey{component, operation_id} in advance_child_creation (component_installation/mod.rs:51-54), called with request.component (component_registry/mod.rs:2319). Subtree-leaf removal validates and completes with request.component (component_registry/mod.rs:2088-2106). claim_smallest_sufficient_ready prefers the lowest-cycle Ready asset (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:386-403), which is usually the one just recycled. The stuck Recycling{Ready} status cannot be retried (retry_reset falls to conflict, 262-264) or handed off (begin_handoff 1075-1080; handoff_candidate 1137-1152). finalize_inventory requires non_store_asset_count()==0 (workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:386-388).

Recommendation

Make completion idempotent on the exact claim. Pass the operation_id (or the full CanisterPoolClaimKey) into complete_recycling and validate_complete_recycling, and act on the current Recycling{claim} first. Treat last_recycle only as a replay proof when it matches the full claim and the asset is no longer Recycling. Add a unit test that recycles the same asset twice under one component.

Verifier (confirmed): The finding holds as described. recycling_completion (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1630-1640) returns Ok(None) whenever last_recycle.component == component, and it does this before it looks at the current Recycling{claim}. Nothing ever clears last_recycle: it is written only at 1364, and neither claim_smallest_sufficient_ready (386-403) nor finalize_claim (449-466) resets it. So once an asset has been recycled under Component C and is then reclaimed by C, the old C/opX value survives. Child claims use the parent Component ID (component_installation/mod.rs:51-54, called with request.component at component_registry/mod.rs:2319). Ordinary subtree removal is allowed while the Component is Active (subtree_retirement/mod.rs:131), so C can create and remove children again and again. On the second recycle, register_recycled_pending (162) and mark_ready (191-196) produce Recycling{C/opZ, Ready}. validate_complete_recycling then passes (component_registry/mod.rs:2088), the Registry row is removed without checking pool state, and complete_recycling at 2102 does nothing. There is no way to recover the asset: - RetryReset returns a conflict (242-264). - Handoff requires Ready or Failed (1075-1080, 1146-1150). - Import rejects it because its origin is now Recycled (121-123). - No workflow code handles Recycling. The stuck asset still counts toward maximum_size (1275) and non_store_asset_count, so finalize_inventory stays unavailable for good (fleet_subnet_root.rs:386-388). The cycles remain under Root's control but can never be reused or handed off. The existing unit test (2353-2428) covers only a single recycle.

highreproducedcp-registry-ops-1 · robustness · medium confidence
Record growth is never checked against the 4096-byte Storable bound, so install or commit can trap after the paid creation effect and permanently wedge the allocation
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/mod.rs:3314

Failure scenario

A registered parent provisions a child with about 700 bytes of candid init args, and the child role's Wasm is about 5 MiB (5 chunk hashes). Reserve, creation intent and mark_child_created all fit, and a pool canister with initial cycles is claimed. begin_child_install or commit_verified_child then serializes a record above 4096 bytes, and `replace_child_allocation`/`commit_child` traps on insert. Every retry traps the same way. The claimed canister stays unregistered, holding its cycles, and reserved_descendants stays at 1. begin_component_draining then returns `unavailable` forever (component_retirement/mod.rs:134-142), so the Component and the Root can never retire. The top-level path fails the same way with roughly 15-25 chunk hashes, which is a 15-25 MiB Wasm, especially for peer origins that embed a second ComponentBinding.

Evidence

Allocation and child-allocation values are stored with `impl_storable_bounded!(..., 4_096)` (storage mod.rs:49,53,1125-1129,2322-2327). ic-stable-structures 0.7.2 `BTreeMap::insert` calls `into_bytes_checked`, which `assert!`s `len <= max_size`, so an oversized record traps. The ops charges only compare against configured limits: `install_charged_entry_bytes` checks `charged > plan.maximum_registry_bytes` (mod.rs:3574), `child_install_charged_entry_bytes` returns a sum that `child_install_capacity` compares with `record.maximum_registry_bytes` and the root limit (mod.rs:3314-3327, 3361-3369), and those limits are MiB-scale (for example 16_777_216). Neither checks the value bound. The one bound check, `validate_creation_capacity`, compares key+value against `4096 + 128` (mod.rs:6441), which still admits values above 4096. Records grow phase by phase. Install adds `chunk_hashes: Vec<Vec<u8>>` (one hash per 1 MiB chunk) and a full `ComponentBinding`. Commit adds commitment and membership receipts. `application_init_args: Option<Vec<u8>>` comes from the parent and is limited only by the 16 KiB command payload (child_allocation/mod.rs:96-120). All `Vec<u8>` and `[u8;32]` fields serialize as CBOR integer arrays, about 1.9 bytes per random byte (cdk/serialize.rs:26-34). Neither transition has an abandon path.

Recommendation

Compute the value-only encoded size of the terminal maximum record (as the charge functions already build it) and reject with a typed `resource_exhausted` when it exceeds `Storable::BOUND.max_size()`. Do this at reservation for init args and at creation/install admission before any pool claim or paid effect. Bound `application_init_args` and chunk count explicitly. Encode byte fields with `serde_bytes` (or fixed byte strings) to halve their size, and add a unit test that drives a maximal record (many 0xFF chunk hashes plus large init args) through every phase.

Verifier (confirmed): The defect is real. ComponentRegistryEntryRecord and RootComponentAllocationRecord are bounded at 4096 (storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:49,53,1125-1129,2322-2327). ic-stable-structures 0.7.2 BTreeMap::insert calls into_bytes_checked (btreemap.rs:501), which asserts the length is within bounds (storable.rs:38-63), so an oversized value traps. replace_child_allocation and commit_child insert ChildAllocation values (store mod.rs:4965-4967). No ops path checks the value bound. The charge functions (ops mod.rs:3236-3327, 3480-3574, 3112-3178) only compare against MiB-scale maximum_registry_bytes, and validate_charged_child_record_size (3180) only checks the value against the charge. application_init_args has no size check anywhere (child_allocation/mod.rs:96-120, workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1185). I modelled the CBOR encoding: structs become string-keyed maps, IDs become 64-character hex text, and [u8;32]/Vec<u8> become integer arrays. A realistic Committed child entry comes to about 3.2 KB with no init args. With about 450-500 random init-arg bytes it passes 4096 at commit, while Reserved, Created and InstallIntent still fit (about 3.1 KB). So the likeliest trap is commit or membership, after the child is created, installed and started. That is later than the begin_child_install the finding names. Nothing abandons the allocation, so reserved_descendants stays set and retirement returns unavailable (component_retirement/mod.rs:134-142). The cycles stay in a canister Root controls, so a reset can recover them and they are not burned. Two limits keep this at high rather than critical: a registered parent must trigger it, and a reset path exists. Top-level records have less headroom (roughly 3.4-4.0 KB for Component or FleetService origins) but no init args.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): It stands. I traced a working path from the entry point to the trap. Entry: application code on any registered parent Component calls the public `create_canister_request(op_id, role, parent, Some(init))` (canic-core api/rpc/mod.rs:65). That becomes root's CreateCanister capability. `component_child_provision_request` copies `req.extra_arg` into `application_init_args` without checking its size (execute.rs:164-170). `reserve_child_allocation` only checks that the caller is `registered_parent` (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1107). The ops charge functions compare only against MiB-scale `maximum_registry_bytes` (ops mod.rs:3141-3150, 3353-3362; child_allocation/mod.rs:206-219). Nothing checks the 4096-byte value bound (storage mod.rs:53, 2323-2327). ic-stable-structures 0.7.2 `insert` calls `into_bytes_checked`, which asserts (btreemap.rs:501, storable.rs:55-60). My own CBOR model gives a Committed-plus-membership child value of about 3.3-3.7 KB with no init args. About 300-500 bytes of init args pushes it past 4096 at `commit_child` or `activate_child_membership`. Reserved, Created and Verified still fit. So the trap is later than `begin_child_install`, but it comes after the paid creation, the install and the runtime activation. Variable-length `recovery_controllers` inside ComponentBinding also add to the size. Every retry is deterministic, and a trap skips `record_child_failure` (lifecycle_drivers:233-248). No abandon path exists. Retirement returns `unavailable` because the allocation is not terminal (component_retirement:134-142). Who triggers it: an ordinary app passing a modest Candid init struct. That is a routine action, not an actor who already holds the authority to wedge Component retirement. The parent's authority is supposed to be bounded by configured limits and typed failures. Why high and not critical: the cycles stay in a canister that root controls, whose principal is recorded, so they are not lost. A reset recovers. The wedge covers one Component and its retirement, not the whole fleet.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this. Nothing documents it as intended or lists it as a known limitation, and the project's own history treats this class of problem as a bug. docs/changelog/0.100.md:2072-2074 widened the draining record from 4 KiB to 8 KiB after "the complete production-sized authority measured 4,204 bytes". Lines 2117-2120 size bounds for the "fully precharged terminal shape", and 3592-3594 set the allocation record to 4 KiB "for exact chunk and binding evidence". The design intends the precharge to guarantee that the terminal record fits its bound. The mechanism holds up in code: - The macro serializes to CBOR (canic-core cdk/mod.rs:22-52, serialize.rs:26-33). - ic-stable-structures 0.7.2 checks bounds on insert (btreemap.rs:501) and asserts in storable.rs:62-67, so an oversized value traps. - The entry-byte helpers use unchecked to_bytes (storage mod.rs:5731-5763), so they measure without trapping. - child_install_charged_entry_bytes builds the maximal Committed record (ops mod.rs:3236-3327). Its result is compared only against the MiB-scale registry limits (3339-3369), never against the 4096-byte value bound. - validate_child_install_capacity runs only once the record is Created, after the paid creation (child_allocation/mod.rs:393-413; workflow component_installation/mod.rs:559). - application_init_args (canic-core rpc extra_arg, execute.rs:169; component_rpc/lifecycle.rs:90) has no size check. Only the 16 KiB command envelope limits it. Adding a typed resource_exhausted check at admission, before any paid effect, fits the reinstall-only rules on typed failures and bounded paid effects. Impact check: the cycles stay in a canister that Root controls, so cycle conservation holds. The wedge is limited to one Component partition. Retirement stays blocked (component_retirement/mod.rs:134-142) and nothing abandons the allocation, so same-release recovery cannot finish without a reset. The exact trap threshold comes from an estimate, not a measurement. The top-level path needs an unrealistically large Wasm. That fits "recovery that cannot complete": high, not critical.
Reproduction (reproduced): The fixture is the same single active partition used by child_reservation_is_parent_indexed_idempotent_and_capacity_bounded. The child test runs the real ops lifecycle: reserve, validate_creation, begin_creation, mark_created, validate_install, begin_install, installed, verified, commit, directory_prepared, runtime_activated and membership. It uses 5 pseudo-random chunk hashes and init args of 0 to 1536 bytes, runs each step under catch_unwind, and prints the stored value size after each step. It asserts that a step either finishes or returns a typed error at an admission check, and never traps. Every admission check passed, and every step after begin_creation (the paid creation effect) then trapped at the ic-stable-structures bound assert (storable.rs:63): membership at 512B of init args, commit at 768B, begin_install at 1024B and above. The wedge test starts from the 768B case. Retrying commit traps again with the same record size. The allocation stays Verified with reserved_descendants=1, and begin_component_draining returns unavailable (E140). The top-level test uses prepared_created_allocation: 32 chunks trap at activate_membership and 48 chunks trap at begin_install, both after the creation effect. So the finding holds in full: no ops path checks the 4096-byte value bound, the trap is deterministic, and the Component can no longer retire. The only difference from the finding is which phase traps first, which depends on size, as the verifier noted.

+//! Reproduction: allocation record growth versus the 4096-byte Storable value bound.
+
+use super::*;
+use crate::storage::stable::component_registry::ComponentRegistryEntryRecord;
+use canic_core::cdk::structures::storable::Storable;
+
+const VALUE_BOUND: usize = 4_096;
+
+enum Step<T> {
+    Done(T),
+    Rejected(InternalError),
+    Trapped(String),
+}
+
+fn step<T>(f: impl FnOnce() -> Result<T, InternalError>) -> Step<T> {
+    match std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(f)) {
+        Ok(Ok(value)) => Step::Done(value),
+        Ok(Err(error)) => Step::Rejected(error),
+        Err(payload) => Step::Trapped(
+            payload
+                .downcast_ref::<String>()
+                .cloned()
+                .or_else(|| payload.downcast_ref::<&str>().map(|s| (*s).to_string()))
+                .unwrap_or_default(),
+        ),
+    }
+}
+
+fn noise(seed: u32, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
+    (0..u32::try_from(len).expect("len"))
+        .map(|i| (i.wrapping_add(seed).wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761) >> 24) as u8)
+        .collect()
+}
+
+fn child_value_len(component: ComponentInstanceId, operation_id: [u8; 32]) -> usize {
+    RootComponentRegistryStore::child_allocation(component, operation_id).map_or(0, |record| {
+        ComponentRegistryEntryRecord::ChildAllocation(record)
+            .to_bytes()
+            .len()
+    })
+}
+
+fn top_level_value_len(operation_id: [u8; 32]) -> usize {
+    RootComponentRegistryStore::allocation(operation_id).map_or(0, |record| record.to_bytes().len())
+}
+
+struct ChildFixture {
+    root: FleetSubnetRootBinding,
+    component: ComponentInstanceId,
+    parent: candid::Principal,
+    binding: ComponentBinding,
+    decision: ComponentChildAllocationDecision,
+    registry: ComponentRegistryHead,
+}
+
+// Same single active top-level partition as
+// `child_reservation_is_parent_indexed_idempotent_and_capacity_bounded`.
+fn import_single_active_partition() -> ChildFixture {
+    RootComponentRegistryStore::import(RootComponentRegistryData::default());
+    let root = root_binding();

+        release_build_id: ReleaseBuildId::from_nonce(ReleaseBuildNonce::from_random_bytes([8; 32])),
+        manifest_digest: ReleaseSetDigest::from_bytes([9; 32]),
+    };
+    let binding = ComponentBinding {
+        authority: root.authority.clone(),
+        component,
+        component_spec: "projects".parse().expect("Component Spec"),
+        spec_hash: [6; 32],
+        role: CanisterRole::new("project_hub"),
+        placement_subnet: root.placement_subnet,
+        fleet_subnet_root: root.fleet_subnet_root,
+        canister_id: parent,
+    };
+    let origin = ComponentProvisioningOrigin::FleetAdministrator {
+        caller: candid::Principal::from_slice(&[11; 29]),
+    };
+    let mut partition = ComponentRegistryPartitionRecord {
+        binding: binding.clone(),
+        protocol_profile_digest: ProtocolProfileDigest::from_bytes([12; 32]),
+        provisioning_origin: origin.clone(),
+        release_set,
+        status: ComponentLifecycleStatus::Active,
+        revision: 2,
+        content_hash: component_partition_content_hash(
+            &binding,
+            ProtocolProfileDigest::from_bytes([12; 32]),
+            &origin,
+            release_set,
+            ComponentLifecycleStatus::Active,
+            2,
+            empty_component_descendant_content_hash(component),
+            0,
+        )
+        .expect("partition hash"),
+        descendant_content_hash: empty_component_descendant_content_hash(component),
+        directory_synchronized_at_ns: 33,
+        reserved_descendants: 0,

+/// Outcome of one lifecycle run: `Ok` is acceptable (completed, or rejected
+/// with a typed error at an admission check), `Err` is a trap.
+fn drive_child_lifecycle(init_len: usize, chunks: usize) -> Result<String, String> {
+    let fx = import_single_active_partition();
+    let op = [44; 32];
+    let component = fx.component;
+    let mut trace = Vec::new();
+    macro_rules! run {
+        ($label:expr, $admission:expr, $body:expr) => {
+            match step(|| $body) {
+                Step::Done(value) => {
+                    trace.push(format!("{}={}B", $label, child_value_len(component, op)));
+                    value
+                }
+                Step::Rejected(error) if $admission => {
+                    return Ok(format!(
+                        "rejected at admission {} ({:?}) trace=[{}]",
+                        $label,
+                        error.public_code(),
+                        trace.join(", ")
+                    ));
+                }
+                Step::Rejected(error) => {
+                    return Err(format!(
+                        "typed error {:?} at non-admission step {} trace=[{}]",
+                        error.public_code(),
+                        $label,
+                        trace.join(", ")
+                    ));
+                }
+                Step::Trapped(message) => {
+                    return Err(format!(
+                        "TRAP at {} ({message}) trace=[{}]",
+                        $label,
+                        trace.join(", ")
+                    ));
+                }
+            }
+        };
+    }
+
+    run!(
+        "reserve",
+        true,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::reserve_child_allocation(
+            fx.decision.clone(),
+            op,
+            Some(noise(7, init_len)),
+            fx.registry.clone(),
+        )
+    );
+    let plan = RootComponentCreationPlan {
+        wasm_store: candid::Principal::from_slice(&[50; 29]),
+        payload_hash: [51; 32],
+        payload_size_bytes: u64::try_from(chunks).expect("chunks") * 1_048_576,
+        initial_cycles: Cycles::new(5_000_000_000_000),
+        controller: fx.root.fleet_subnet_root,
+    };
+    run!(
+        "validate_creation",
+        true,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::validate_child_creation_capacity(component, op, &plan)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "begin_creation",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::begin_child_creation(
+            component,
+            op,
+            plan,
+            ReplayCostGuardSettlement {
+                quota_intent_id: IntentId(52),
+                reservation_intent_id: IntentId(53),
+            },
+        )
+    );
+    // Paid creation effect happens here in the workflow.
+    let canister = candid::Principal::from_slice(&[54; 29]);
+    run!(
+        "mark_created",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_child_created(component, op, canister)
+    );
+    let install_plan = RootComponentChildInstallPlan {
+        fixture_grant_revision: Some(3),
+        raw_module_hash: [56; 32],
+        protocol_profile_digest: ProtocolProfileDigest::from_bytes([59; 32]),
+        chunk_hashes: (0..chunks)
+            .map(|i| noise(1_000 + u32::try_from(i).expect("i"), 32))
+            .collect(),
+        binding: ComponentChildBinding {
+            component: fx.binding.clone(),
+            parent_canister_id: fx.parent,
+            role: fx.decision.child_role.clone(),
+            canister_id: canister,
+        },
+        maximum_registry_bytes: fx.decision.maximum_registry_bytes,
+    };
+    run!(
+        "validate_install",
+        true,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::validate_child_install_capacity(component, op, &install_plan)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "begin_install",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::begin_child_install(
+            component,
+            op,
+            install_plan,
+            ReplayCostGuardSettlement {
+                quota_intent_id: IntentId(59),
+                reservation_intent_id: IntentId(60),
+            },
+        )
+    );
+    run!(
+        "installed",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_child_installed(component, op)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "verified",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_child_verified(component, op)
+    );
+    let committed = run!(
+        "commit",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::commit_verified_child(
+            component,
+            op,
+            66,
+            fleet_directory(&fx.root),
+            None,
+        )
+    );
+    let RootComponentChildAllocationProgressView::Committed { commitment, .. } =
+        &committed.0.progress
+    else {
+        return Err("commit did not produce Committed".to_string());
+    };
+    let hash = commitment.directory_authority_hash;
+    run!(
+        "directory_prepared",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_child_directory_prepared(component, op, hash)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "runtime_activated",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_child_runtime_activated(component, op, hash)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "membership",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::activate_child_membership(
+            component,
+            op,
+            69,
+            fleet_directory(&fx.root),
+            None,
+        )
+    );
+    Ok(format!("completed trace=[{}]", trace.join(", ")))
+}

+fn drive_top_level_lifecycle(chunks: usize) -> Result<String, String> {
+    let (root, created, canister) = prepared_created_allocation();
+    let op = [12; 32];
+    let mut trace = vec![format!("created={}B", top_level_value_len(op))];
+    macro_rules! run {
+        ($label:expr, $admission:expr, $body:expr) => {
+            match step(|| $body) {
+                Step::Done(value) => {
+                    trace.push(format!("{}={}B", $label, top_level_value_len(op)));
+                    value
+                }
+                Step::Rejected(error) if $admission => {
+                    return Ok(format!(
+                        "rejected at admission {} ({:?}) trace=[{}]",
+                        $label,
+                        error.public_code(),
+                        trace.join(", ")
+                    ));
+                }
+                Step::Rejected(error) => {
+                    return Err(format!(
+                        "typed error {:?} at non-admission step {} trace=[{}]",
+                        error.public_code(),
+                        $label,
+                        trace.join(", ")
+                    ));
+                }
+                Step::Trapped(message) => {
+                    return Err(format!(
+                        "TRAP at {} ({message}) trace=[{}]",
+                        $label,
+                        trace.join(", ")
+                    ));
+                }
+            }
+        };
+    }
+    let plan = RootComponentInstallPlan {
+        fixture_grant_revision: Some(3),
+        raw_module_hash: [20; 32],
+        protocol_profile_digest: ProtocolProfileDigest::from_bytes([23; 32]),
+        chunk_hashes: (0..chunks)
+            .map(|i| noise(2_000 + u32::try_from(i).expect("i"), 32))
+            .collect(),
+        binding: ComponentBinding {
+            authority: root.authority.clone(),
+            component: created.component,
+            component_spec: created.component_spec.clone(),
+            spec_hash: created.spec_hash,
+            role: created.role.clone(),
+            placement_subnet: root.placement_subnet,
+            fleet_subnet_root: root.fleet_subnet_root,
+            canister_id: canister,
+        },
+        maximum_registry_bytes: 16_777_216,
+    };
+    run!(
+        "validate_install",
+        true,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::validate_install_capacity(op, &plan)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "begin_install",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::begin_install(
+            op,
+            plan.clone(),
+            ReplayCostGuardSettlement {
+                quota_intent_id: IntentId(23),
+                reservation_intent_id: IntentId(24),
+            },
+        )
+    );
+    run!("installed", false, ComponentRegistryOps::mark_installed(op));
+    run!("verified", false, ComponentRegistryOps::mark_verified(op));
+    let committed = run!(
+        "commit",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::commit_verified(
+            op,
+            31,
+            plan.maximum_registry_bytes,
+            fleet_directory(&root),
+        )
+    );
+    let RootComponentAllocationProgressView::Committed { commitment, .. } = &committed.0.progress
+    else {
+        return Err("commit did not produce Committed".to_string());
+    };
+    let hash = commitment.directory_authority_hash;
+    run!(
+        "directory_prepared",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_directory_prepared(op, hash)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "runtime_activated",
+        false,
+        ComponentRegistryOps::mark_runtime_activated(op, hash)
+    );
+    run!(
+        "membership",
+        false,

+}

+#[test]
+fn repro_child_record_growth_traps_after_paid_creation() {
+    println!("value bound = {VALUE_BOUND} bytes");
+    let mut violations = Vec::new();
+    for init_len in [0_usize, 256, 512, 768, 1_024, 1_536] {
+        let outcome = drive_child_lifecycle(init_len, 5);
+        println!("child init_args={init_len}B chunks=5: {outcome:?}");
+        if let Err(violation) = outcome {
+            violations.push(format!("init_args={init_len}B: {violation}"));
+        }
+    }
+    RootComponentRegistryStore::import(RootComponentRegistryData::default());
+    assert!(
+        violations.is_empty(),
+        "child record growth must be rejected with a typed error at admission, \
+         never trap on the Storable bound:\n{}",
+        violations.join("\n")
+    );
+}
