+#[test]
+fn repro_child_record_trap_is_deterministic_and_wedges_retirement() {
+    let component = ComponentInstanceId::from_generated_bytes([10; 32]);
+    let op = [44; 32];
+    let outcome = drive_child_lifecycle(768, 5);
+    println!("first run init_args=768B chunks=5: {outcome:?}");
+    let retry = step(|| {
+        ComponentRegistryOps::commit_verified_child(
+            component,
+            op,
+            67,
+            fleet_directory(&root_binding()),
+            None,
+        )
+    });
+    let retry_trap = match &retry {
+        Step::Trapped(message) => Some(message.clone()),
+        Step::Done(_) | Step::Rejected(_) => None,
+    };
+    println!("commit retry trapped: {retry_trap:?}");
+    let progress = ComponentRegistryOps::child_allocation(component, op)
+        .expect("child allocation read")
+        .expect("retained child allocation")
+        .progress;
+    let still_verified = matches!(
+        progress,
+        RootComponentChildAllocationProgressView::Verified { .. }
+    );
+    let partition = ComponentRegistryOps::partition(component)
+        .expect("partition read")
+        .expect("partition");
+    println!(
+        "after trap: still_verified={still_verified} reserved_descendants={} committed_descendants={}",
+        partition.reserved_descendants, partition.committed_descendants
+    );
+    let draining = ComponentRegistryOps::begin_component_draining(
+        component,
+        [90; 32],
+        ComponentRegistryHead {
+            component,
+            revision: partition.revision,
+            content_hash: partition.content_hash,
+        },
+        100,
+        16_777_216,
+        fleet_directory(&root_binding()),
+    );
+    let draining_unavailable = draining.as_ref().is_err_and(|error| {
+        error.public_code() == InternalError::unavailable().public_code()
+    });
+    println!(
+        "begin_component_draining after trap: {:?} (unavailable={draining_unavailable})",
+        draining.as_ref().map(|_| ()).map_err(InternalError::public_code)
+    );
+    RootComponentRegistryStore::import(RootComponentRegistryData::default());
+    assert!(
+        retry_trap.is_none(),
+        "an admitted child allocation must be able to finish (or fail typed) on retry, \
+         but the commit retry trapped again: {retry_trap:?}; still_verified={still_verified}, \
+         Component draining blocked as unavailable={draining_unavailable}"
+    );
+}
highreproducedcp-registry-workflow-3 · liveness · high confidence
The subtree removal timer spins forever at 1 s when it finds an already-Completed removal, which a routine RemoveSubtree retry triggers, and the perpetual timer blocks root authority snapshots
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:645

Failure scenario

The operator runs RemoveSubtree, the response is lost, and the CLI resends the identical command. Two chains now run, or the resend lands after completion. Once the removal reaches Completed, the surviving chain gets invariant every second, forever. It burns root cycles, and every PrepareAuthoritySnapshot fails with UnmanagedClaim until the root is upgraded or reinstalled.

Evidence

subtree_removal_action maps Completed to Err(InternalError::invariant()) (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:645-647). advance_existing_subtree_removal calls it with no Completed short-circuit (733-740). schedule_subtree_removal_after reschedules every error after Duration::from_secs(1), and stops only when a successful response is Completed (696-706). The RemoveSubtree endpoint schedules a chain after every successful begin (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:703-708). begin_subtree_removal returns the existing record on exact replay (mod.rs:1717-1727), and validation accepts Completed (authority_validation/mod.rs:469-478). Chains are also not deduplicated (lifecycle_drivers:679-681), so a duplicate chain that sees the Completed state produced by another chain loops too. Every iteration registers a lifecycle timer. suspend_root requires every registered timer to be a known claim (workflow/runtime/timer/mod.rs:174-176, 471-483), and prepare_root_snapshot depends on it (authority_restore.rs:45-50).

Recommendation

Make advance_existing_subtree_removal return the current response when the removal is Completed, and have the scheduler check the durable phase before advancing. Deduplicate subtree-removal chains with a scheduled set keyed by (component, operation_id). Add a test: schedule after completion and assert the chain terminates and no timer stays registered.

Verifier (confirmed): The finding holds. `subtree_removal_action` returns `Err(InternalError::invariant())` for `Completed` (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:645-647). `advance_subtree_removal_phase` calls it first (532), and `advance_existing_subtree_removal` (733-740) has no Completed short-circuit. The scheduler stops only when a successful response is Completed (696-700); every `Err` reschedules after 1 s (703-705). Completed records are kept: `ComponentRegistryOps::subtree_removal` still returns them (subtree_retirement/mod.rs:10-26) and new-removal admission filters them out (mod.rs:163-172). On exact replay, `begin_subtree_removal` returns the existing record (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1717-1727). Validation accepts Completed with the target membership absent (authority_validation 438-441, 469-477). The RemoveSubtree endpoint then schedules a new chain unconditionally (root.rs:706-707). Unlike `schedule_component_allocation` (lifecycle_drivers:20-27, which dedupes on a scheduled set), nothing dedupes these chains. Replay after completion is a tested path: baseline.rs:3905 replays RemoveSubtree after Completed and asserts Ok, but never checks the timer inventory. Each loop registers a `lifecycle-N` timer (timer/mod.rs:351-398). `require_observed_claims_resumable` rejects it with UnmanagedClaim (471-478), so `suspend_root` and `prepare_root_snapshot` fail (authority_restore.rs:45-50), which blocks the host authority_seal used by fleet ensure. Corrections: the CLI never sends RemoveSubtree; the caller is a controller issuing the root command directly (root.rs:243-255). A root code upgrade clears IC timers, so a recovery path exists and this is high, not critical.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): The finding holds. I traced it from the root's update endpoint `canic_root_command`. RemoveSubtree is a controller-only command (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:243, 254-257). The endpoint has no replay cache: the replay_protected manifest entry (replay_policy/role_command_manifest.rs:183-189) is only metadata, so idempotency lives in the workflow. On an exact replay, begin_subtree_removal returns the stored record before any admission gate (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1716-1727). Validation accepts a Completed record (authority_validation/mod.rs:410-425, 469-477). Completed records are kept (subtree_retirement/mod.rs:10-26; storage 4400-4416 relies on them). The endpoint then always schedules a new chain (root.rs:703-708). That chain calls advance_existing_subtree_removal (lifecycle_drivers 733-740), which reaches subtree_removal_action. That function returns Err(invariant) for Completed (645-647) without awaiting, and the Err arm re-arms after 1 s (703-705). Unlike schedule_component_allocation (20-27), these chains are not deduplicated. Lifecycle timers are not in the claimed set of require_root_resumable (timer/mod.rs:131-160). The scheduler always registers the next timer before the current one finishes, so require_observed_claims_resumable returns UnmanagedClaim every time (471-478). suspend_root therefore fails, which fails prepare_root_snapshot (authority_restore.rs:45-50) and the host's fleet-ensure SealAuthority step (canic-host fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:4842). The trigger is a root controller replaying its own idempotent command, for example after a lost response. The design supports and tests this replay (baseline.rs:3905), so this is an ordinary operation, not privilege abuse. Holding controller authority does not make an unintended liveness failure acceptable. The harm has two parts: roughly one paid timer message per second, which drains root cycles without bound, and snapshots blocked until upgrade. It is not critical because a recovery path exists. There is no pre_upgrade guard, the root post_upgrade (lifecycle/upgrade/root.rs) does not reschedule subtree removals, and an upgrade clears IC timers. The CLI never sends RemoveSubtree, so the trigger needs a direct controller call. That lowers likelihood but does not refute the finding.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this. Nothing in the docs or the code says the loop is intended, and several things show the chain is meant to end. - **The chain is meant to stop at Completed.** The scheduler stops only when a successful response is Completed (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:696-700). Every Err reschedules after 1 s (703-705). But subtree_removal_action returns Err(invariant) for Completed (645-647), and advance_existing_subtree_removal (733-740) never checks for Completed first. - **Replay is a supported, tested path.** begin_subtree_removal returns the stored record on exact replay (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1717-1727). The RemoveSubtree endpoint then schedules a chain every time (canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:703-707). baseline.rs:3905 replays after Completed and expects Ok, but never checks for leftover timers. - **Re-sending is the only way to restart a removal.** schedule_subtree_removal has no caller except that endpoint (grep finds only root.rs:707). So after an upgrade, an operator must re-send RemoveSubtree to resume. Re-sending without knowing the removal already finished is therefore a normal operator action. - **No runtime replay cache stops the resend.** The replay_protected manifest entry (replay_policy/role_command_manifest.rs:183-189) is only a classification. Nothing on this runtime path uses it. - **Chains are not deduplicated.** Component allocation keeps a set of scheduled chains (lifecycle_drivers:10-27); subtree removal has no equivalent. - **The design says removal should end.** The 0.100 design (0.100-design.md:2071-2076) describes idempotent, interruption-safe post-order removal. Nothing documents a retry that never ends. The impact is as claimed. Each loop iteration registers a lifecycle-N timer (timer/mod.rs:351-398). require_root_resumable accepts only known claimed timers (131-159) and returns UnmanagedClaim for anything else (471-478). So suspend_root and prepare_root_snapshot fail (authority_restore.rs:45-50). That blocks the SealAuthority step that fleet ensure uses (canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:4842). The loop also burns root cycles every second, indefinitely. A controller can recover by upgrading root with the same code, which clears the timers. So this is high, not critical.
Reproduction (partially reproduced): I added a test helper, repro_import_completed_subtree_removal, to the ops component_registry tests module. It runs the same production ops sequence as subtree_removal_target_finalization_is_terminal_and_releases_the_live_fence: drain, quiesce, fence, select, stop, delete, remove membership, sync the directory, finalize. That leaves one retained Completed subtree removal in the store. To make the helper reachable from workflow, I changed `mod tests` to `pub(crate) mod tests` in ops/component_registry/mod.rs. The workflow test first confirms that ComponentRegistryOps::subtree_removal still returns the Completed record, which is what a replay or duplicate chain sees. It then calls advance_existing_subtree_removal once with a noop waker. That is the exact call the schedule_subtree_removal_after timer body makes. The test asserts Ok with phase Completed, the only result that stops the chain. Observed: the future resolves straight away with Err(InternalError E137 STATE_INVALID, i.e. InternalError::invariant()). This confirms the core defect: advancing an already-Completed removal fails instead of reporting completion, and the scheduler re-arms after 1 s on any Err. Not exercised natively: the timer loop itself, the missing chain dedup, the endpoint replay scheduling a new chain, and suspend_root / prepare_root_snapshot failing with UnmanagedClaim. Those need real IC timers, so PocketIC. A PocketIC test would replay RemoveSubtree after Completed, then check that lifecycle timers stay registered and that PrepareAuthoritySnapshot fails.

+//! Repro: advancing an already-Completed subtree removal must terminate the driver chain.
+
+use super::*;
+use std::{
+    future::Future,
+    pin::pin,
+    task::{Context, Poll, Waker},
+};
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_completed_subtree_removal_advance_terminates() {
+    let (component, operation_id) =
+        crate::ops::component_registry::tests::repro_import_completed_subtree_removal();
+
+    // The terminal record is retained and readable, exactly what a replayed
+    // RemoveSubtree (or a duplicate driver chain) observes after completion.
+    let retained = ComponentRegistryOps::subtree_removal(component, operation_id)
+        .expect("subtree removal read")
+        .expect("Completed removal is retained");
+    println!("retained progress = {:?}", retained.progress);
+    assert!(matches!(
+        retained.progress,
+        crate::view::component_registry::RootComponentSubtreeRemovalProgressView::Completed(_)
+    ));
+
+    // This is the exact call the `schedule_subtree_removal_after` timer body makes.
+    let request = RootComponentSubtreeRemovalStatusRequest {
+        operation_id,
+        component,
+    };
+    let mut future = pin!(advance_existing_subtree_removal(request));
+    let mut context = Context::from_waker(Waker::noop());
+    let Poll::Ready(result) = future.as_mut().poll(&mut context) else {
+        panic!("advancing a Completed removal must not await any platform effect");
+    };
+    println!("advance_existing_subtree_removal(Completed) = {result:?}");
+
+    // The scheduler stops only on Ok(Completed); every Err re-arms a timer after 1 s.
+    let response = result.expect(
+        "advancing an already-Completed removal must return its Completed response so the \
+         driver chain terminates instead of re-arming every second",
+    );
+    assert!(matches!(
+        response.phase,
+        RootComponentSubtreeRemovalPhase::Completed(_)
+    ));
+    crate::storage::stable::component_registry::RootComponentRegistryStore::import(
+        crate::storage::stable::component_registry::RootComponentRegistryData::default(),
+    );
+}
highreproducedcp-root-admission-funding-1 · liveness · medium confidence
Root ledger retirement stores an immutable transfer intent and then requires an exactly-zero ledger balance, so dust, any later third-party deposit, or a retry after the 24-hour ledger window permanently wedges Root deletion
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:78

Failure scenario

The operator removes Root R. prepare_deletion persists intent {balance_before: 0}, or B, and then waits on Coordinator readiness, which normally takes retries. Any principal sends 1 cycle (plus the 100M fee) to R's Cycles Ledger account. Every later retry sees Duplicate or skip, then balance 1, and returns conflict. Alternatively, R's account holds a 50M leftover from pool creation (below the 100M fee), so InvalidTransfer repeats forever. Or the first dispatch fails at the cost-guard reservation because R's balance is below the retained target, and the operator retries more than 24 h later: TooOld, conflict forever. R stays Draining forever with its cycles stranded, and Fleet admission mutations and funding rotations are blocked permanently.

Evidence

On the first attempt, evacuate reads balance and fee and persists a FleetLedgerTransferIntent {balance_before, fee, created_at_time} through begin_root_ledger_transfer (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:28-45). Any later attempt must reuse it exactly: an existing intent that differs returns conflict (ops/component_registry/root_retirement.rs:1486-1492), and nothing ever clears ledger_transfer. Each retry re-dispatches the same intent (46-77). Duplicate counts as success, and every other ledger error maps to conflict (line 74): TooOld after 24 h, BadFee, InsufficientFunds. The infra layer computes amount = balance_before - fee and requires it to be > 0, otherwise it returns InvalidTransfer (canic-core/src/infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:204-213), which evacuate turns into invariant (line 63) on every retry. require_empty_source demands exactly zero after the transfer (82-91). Once a receipt exists it is re-checked on every prepare_deletion retry (24-26) until preparation completes. Anyone holding Cycles Ledger balance can icrc1_transfer to the Root's default account. A Root stuck in Draining keeps registry_accepts_admission_mutation false (ops/fleet_admission/mod.rs:1129-1141) and fails funding rotation's all_roots_active check (ops/fleet_coordinator/funding_rotation.rs:148-153, 203).

Recommendation

Model the sweep as sequential intents. Once a recorded intent reaches a proven terminal ledger outcome (block or Duplicate), or TooOld with no block, re-observe the balance and record a successor intent. When 0 < balance <= fee, record a reviewed terminal residual discard, as the conservation policy allows, instead of requiring zero. Treat later deposits by re-sweeping rather than failing with conflict. Add a PocketIC test that deposits into the Root account in the middle of preparation. Apply the same fix to the Coordinator retirement sweep (workflow/fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:26-99).

Severity adjusted from critical to high during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The main claim holds. begin_root_ledger_transfer stores an intent that can never change (root_retirement.rs:1486-1492; storage component_registry/mod.rs:3481-3494). Nothing clears it. evacuate requires the ledger balance to be exactly zero (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:78, 82-91), and it re-checks this on every retry once a receipt exists (24-26). The retry loop is guaranteed in normal operation: Coordinator readiness only appears after the Coordinator polls again following the Root's reclamation record (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:860-880). Meanwhile the Root's timer retries every second on any Err (fleet_subnet_root.rs:559-564). So one icrc1_transfer from anyone to (root, None), sent between intent persistence and record_root_deletion_preparation, gives a conflict on every retry. No in-protocol path spends the residual. The Root stays Draining, which blocks Fleet admission mutations (fleet_admission/mod.rs:1129-1141) and funding rotation (funding_rotation.rs:148-153, 203), and the retries burn cycles without end. Corrections: (1) The dust case never reaches InvalidTransfer. The store rejects balance_before<=fee at storage mod.rs:902-906, so nothing is persisted, and topping the account above the fee unblocks it. (2) TooOld needs a failure before dispatch that lasts more than 24h. (3) The Coordinator sweep returns early once it has a receipt (retirement/mod.rs:31-33), so its window is narrower and only the operator can trigger it. I rate this high, not critical. The trigger needs a rare Root removal that the operator starts, plus a deposit in a short window. The residual cycles stay in the Root's account. An out-of-band controller reset/reinstall (recovery_controllers, canic-host fleet_ensure) probably remains possible, though it is destructive.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): The core wedge holds, but the fleet-level impact described in the finding is partly wrong. How it is reached: the operator or Coordinator starts a removal (accept_root_removal, fleet_subnet_root.rs:281-298). The Root timer then retries advance_root_removal_once every second on any Err (559-564). prepare_deletion (951-1041) re-runs evacuate on each retry until record_root_deletion_preparation. Retries are normal, because the Coordinator only records readiness_intent on a later poll (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:860-870), and until then line 1011 returns unavailable. Once an intent exists, evacuate re-sends the same transfer, gets Duplicate, and require_empty_source fails (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:46-91). With a receipt it fails at 24-26. The intent can never be changed (root_retirement.rs:1486-1492). Any principal can icrc1_transfer 1 cycle plus the fee to the Root's public default account. Spamming Roots that show as Removed hits the window cheaply. Nothing in the protocol can spend the residual. Corrections: publish_removal runs before prepare_deletion (fleet_subnet_root.rs:654-697), and the Coordinator sets the Root to Removed there (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1868). registry_accepts_admission_mutation accepts Removed (fleet_admission/mod.rs:1129-1140), so admission is not blocked. Funding rotation's all_roots_active already fails for any Removed Root, wedged or not. Real harm: Fleet retirement requires a root_deletion_receipt for every Root (ops/fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:193-198). That receipt needs readiness, so Fleet retirement is wedged permanently. Both the Root and the Coordinator (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:806-813) retry every second forever and keep burning cycles. If the wedge hits before reclaim_root_deletion_cycles, those retries burn the Root's unreclaimed balance. The dust case (balance at or below the fee, which the store rejects) is recoverable by a top-up. The only recovery for the rest is a destructive, controller-driven reset. So this stays high, not critical.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this finding. Refusing to delete while a Ledger balance remains is intended. Having no way to drain again is not. Code: evacuate reuses the stored ledger_transfer and never replaces it (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:28-45). It then requires an exactly-zero balance (78, 82-91), and it re-checks that on every retry once a receipt exists (24-26). Once an intent is stored it cannot change: begin_root_ledger_transfer returns conflict on any mismatch (root_retirement.rs:1486-1492), and the storage transition requires request_is_retained (storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:3481-3494). prepare_deletion runs evacuate on every retry (fleet_subnet_root.rs:1004). Retries are normal here: the Coordinator's readiness_intent and readiness each show up only on a later Coordinator poll (fleet_subnet_root.rs:1008-1013, 1034-1038; fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:859-880), and the timer retries every second on Err (fleet_subnet_root.rs:559-564). I found no abort path for Root removal on the Root or the Coordinator. Intent: docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:326-330 says destructive delete steps keep their residual limits, and that "a late donation may require another drain or review so the additional cycles are not discarded". docs/status/current.md:3614-3616 says the same. So the design expects fail-closed behaviour followed by another drain. The Root sweep cannot drain a second time, because it has no successor intent. The recommended fix (sequential intents, then sweep again) matches the documented design. I found no known-limitation entry for this. The only PocketIC coverage is the ideal path (baseline.rs:14844-14866). Impact: cycles stay in the Root's own account, so conservation is not violated. The harm is liveness. Root stays Draining, which blocks Fleet admission mutations (fleet_admission/mod.rs:1129-1141) and funding rotation (funding_rotation.rs:148-153, 203). A deposit costs about one fee, and any holder of Cycles Ledger funds can send one, so griefing is cheap. I agree with the verifier's corrections. The dust case is rejected before anything is persisted (storage mod.rs:902-906) and a top-up clears it. The TooOld case needs a failure before dispatch that lasts more than 24 hours. A destructive controller reset or reinstall probably remains possible and is the normal pre-1.0 path, so this is high, not critical.
Reproduction (partially reproduced): The test runs the same production ComponentRegistryOps chain as the existing end-to-end root retirement test: prepare, draining, funding fence, final inventory, removal publication, Store reclamation, binding finalization, Store deletion, and begin_root_deletion_preparation for operation [10;32]. It then persists the first sweep intent the way evacuate does, with balance 100, fee 10, t=35. After a restart, the retry view still holds that same intent, and cycle reclamation without a receipt returns STATE_CONFLICT (E132). To model a third-party deposit, it tries to record a successor intent for the new balance of 200 at t=40, once with no receipt and once after recording the first transfer's block-7 receipt. Both return STATE_CONFLICT, and the stored intent stays at balance_before=100, so the assertion fails. This confirms the core defect natively. The recorded intent can never be replaced, so there is no durable way to sweep a later deposit. Because evacuate re-dispatches only the stored intent and require_empty_source needs a zero balance, every retry fails. The async parts could not be run natively: the Ledger Duplicate/TooOld responses, require_empty_source itself, and the fleet-level wedge. Those would need a PocketIC test that deposits into (root, None) partway through preparation. The dust case matches the verifier's correction: begin_root_ledger_transfer(50, fee 100) is rejected at the store with STATE_CONFLICT and never reaches InvalidTransfer, and a top-up can recover it.

Component operations bind the SHA-256 of the entire live Coordinator FleetRegistry, so a routine admission change blocks every existing and in-flight Component operation
crates/canic-host/src/component_operation/ops/transport/mod.rs:288

Failure scenario

The operator runs `canic component apply demo extra`. The Root reserves and creates the component, and the CLI's 60-second polling window ends before completion. Another operator then runs `canic admission apply demo` to add a browser user, which republishes the Coordinator registry with a new admission generation and revision. Every later `component status` or `component apply` (and `info env --component-operation`) fails with `Component operation authority changed: reviewed binding` or `live Registry`. A re-run Ensure that refreshes the retained registry does not help, because the record's registry_sha256 is immutable. If the Root restarts, its heap timer is gone and the allocation needs a host resubmission, which is now impossible through the CLI. Deleting the record and planning again creates a second allocation that also counts against the admission limit.

Evidence

authority() records `registry_sha256: Sha256::digest(serde_json::to_vec(registry)?)` over the Ensure-retained initial registry (transport/mod.rs:95,181). policy/mod.rs:28 includes registry_sha256 in the immutable AuthorityBinding. On every plan, apply and status, observe() queries the live registry and rejects any byte difference (transport/mod.rs:280-292, `Authority{"live Registry"}`). workflow/mod.rs:84-85 and 130-131 run observe before progress, so nothing can proceed. FleetRegistry contains `revision` and `admission` (canic-core dto/fleet_registry.rs:112-119). Admission publication replaces the Coordinator registry with the successor policy (canic-control-plane ops/fleet_coordinator/admission.rs:113-117). The admission CLI knows the live registry moves past the retained copy and compares only authority and fleet_subnet_roots (canic-cli admission/mod.rs:756-760). The component path does no such narrowing.

Recommendation

Bind only component-relevant registry facts: registry.authority, the component_specs entry for the selected Spec, and the selected Root's FleetSubnetRootEntry (status, admissions, topology digest, limits, funding, release set). Store these as a named struct in ComponentAuthorityRecord instead of the whole-registry hash, and compare the live values field by field as admission's validate_live_authority does. Add a regression test where the fake transport's live registry changes only admission or revision and apply/status still succeed, while a changed Root entry still rejects.

highreproducedhost-ensure-capacity-1 · liveness · high confidence
An approved capacity import has no abort path, and its 2-attempt per-step budgets are spent before local prechecks, so ordinary transient failures permanently wedge Root and the host Fleet.
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:90

Failure scenario

A Root-held running source takes more than 45 s to stop. 1. The host's '0:stop' Advance times out and returns Unresolved. 2. On rerun, '0:confirm_stop' (attempt 1) is rejected Unavailable because the first message still holds the execution guard. 3. On the next rerun (attempt 2) it is rejected Conflict because the source is still Stopping. 4. The next rerun fails with BudgetExhausted. The same end state follows from two Coordinator query timeouts inside verify_destination during 'reserve', or from two consecutive Root pool-maintenance conflicts at reserve time. The approved-but-unreleased journal then blocks every canic fleet ensure/reset/import. If the reservation succeeded, Root refuses all pool, allocation and provisioning work. No command exists to recover.

Evidence

Each Root step reserves a submission before the call. See finish_root at workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:86-95, settle at 97-100 and release at 68-73, plus reserve and handoff at handoff/mod.rs:94-99 and 171-172. publication/mod.rs:42 sets MAX_SUBMISSIONS=2, and consume (299-311) never refunds.

The spent attempt often never leaves the host:
- transport.submit runs verify_destination before update_signed (transport/mod.rs:124-132).
- root_command does the same before its update (transport/root/mod.rs:208-221).

Approval is saved before the Root reservation exists (handoff/mod.rs:50-53, 76-77). Once approved and unreleased, the import counts as in progress (operation_selection/mod.rs:120-133). While it is in progress:
- lock_operation and lock_completed_source refuse all Ensure, reset and reinstall work (ops/mod.rs:685-692, 707-716).
- New reviews are refused (review/mod.rs:71-76; journal/store/mod.rs:122-125).

There is no cancel: PoolImportCommand offers only Advance, Release, Reserve and Settle (canic-core/src/dto/pool_import/mod.rs:125-136). Root's fence (canic-control-plane ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:152-162) blocks allocation, provisioning and retirement.

Root legitimately rejects retries:
- claim_execution returns unavailable while an earlier Advance is still awaiting (canic-control-plane workflow/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:103).
- observe_source returns conflict while the source is Stopping (canic-control-plane ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:86-91).

Recommendation

Charge the submission allowance only after local and free prechecks pass. Do not count typed retryable Root rejections (unavailable/conflict) or observation-only steps against it; let Root's paid_calls bound the cost, and add backoff polling. Persist approval together with, or after, a successful reservation, or allow un-approval while no reservation or effect exists. Add a journalled abort: a Root Abandon command that releases the fence once every source is AwaitingHandoff or has a Ready receipt, plus a host command that proves non-execution before retiring the journal.

Severity adjusted from critical to high during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanics check out. finish_root (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:90-94) and reserve/settle/release charge a step with reserve_submission before root_command. root_command then runs verify_destination (Root and Coordinator queries plus verify_infrastructure) before the update (transport/root/mod.rs:208-221), and submit does the same (transport/mod.rs:124-129). MAX_SUBMISSIONS=2 (publication/mod.rs:42) and consume never refunds (299-311). The stop scenario holds: - Root holds PoolImportExecutionGuard across the stop_canister await (control-plane workflow capacity_import/mod.rs:103,128; transient guard drops only on completion), so a retry gets Unavailable. - observe_source returns conflict while the source is Stopping (ops .../capacity_import/mod.rs:87-91). Other claims also check out. Approval is saved before reserve (handoff/mod.rs:50-53,76-77). An approved, unfinished journal blocks ensure, reinstall, reset, bootstrap and operator_mint (ops/mod.rs:688,719; callers in workflow/*), and blocks re-review (review/mod.rs:71-76). PoolImportCommand has no abort (dto/pool_import/mod.rs:125-136). A deterministic Root reserve rejection, such as require_quiet_pool during pool creation (ops .../capacity_import/mod.rs:666-669), wedges the host even with no Root fence. This is intended-but-incomplete design. fleet-ensure.md says an exhausted allowance stops apply 'with the operation still fenced', but there is no recovery route. That contradicts the design's 'correct any confirmed reset/import recovery gap' and the same-operation recovery requirement. Why high, not critical: - The wedge needs two failures of the same step inside the bound, or a persistent Root rejection, not a single ordinary failure. - No cycles are lost and no control is compromised. - An unsupported recovery exists: the operator can drive Root's operator-authenticated Advance, Settle and Release by hand through the icp CLI, and remove the host journal. The docs forbid editing the journal, though.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): Reachable from a routine operator command. `canic fleet import --apply` (crates/canic-cli/src/fleet/import/mod.rs:44,123) reaches it, and so does clean reinstall, which sends unfinished Roots through the same apply (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:155-157,252-259). The operator's authority does not refute this. It is not an escalation: ordinary failures during a normal procedure trigger it. Path I traced: 1. finish_root charges `{index}:{step}` before root_command (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:90-94). 2. root_command runs verify_destination before the update, and times out with Unresolved at 45s (transport/root/mod.rs:208-221; transport/mod.rs:43). 3. consume never refunds and MAX_SUBMISSIONS=2 (publication/mod.rs:42,299-311). 4. Root's Advance commits StopIssued, then awaits stop_canister while holding the guard (control-plane workflow/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:103,127-128). A retry gets unavailable from claim_execution (ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:55), or conflict while the source is Stopping (:87-91). So a stop slower than 45s plus two reruns, which the docs tell the operator to repeat (fleet-ensure.md:1186), exhausts "0:confirm_stop". Reserve can also exhaust with no fence. require_quiet_pool (ops/.../capacity_import/mod.rs:666-669) is not checked by context(), so it fails only after the charge. After that, lock_operation and lock_completed_source refuse (ops/mod.rs:688,719), re-review is refused (review/mod.rs:71-76), and PoolImportCommand has no abort (dto/pool_import/mod.rs:125-136). The docs call the fenced stop intended (fleet-ensure.md:1200) but give no recovery. Not critical, because an out-of-band route exists: - The operator can send Advance or Settle to Root by hand, since Root authenticates the reservation operator (ops/.../capacity_import/mod.rs:59-66). - After a manual step, a host rerun computes new step names and no longer needs the spent one. - If there is no reservation, deleting the journal is effect-free, though the docs forbid it. - No cycles are lost. Rubric: recovery that cannot complete, so high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): Parts of this are intended, but the defect is real. fleet-ensure.md:1200 says an exhausted allowance "stops apply with the operation still fenced". FI1 in 0.110-design.md says "Ambiguous evidence stays blocked" and that restarting the CLI cannot reset the budget. The test publication/tests.rs:172-199 checks that budgets survive a reopen. So a durable, finite budget is deliberate. What the design does not intend: - Spending a budgeted attempt on host prechecks that never send anything. The budget is reserved first (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:90-94, handoff/mod.rs:97-99), then root_command runs verify_destination before the update (transport/root/mod.rs:208-209). - Spending it on typed rejections that say "retry later". claim_execution returns unavailable (control-plane ops/capacity_import/mod.rs:55), and Root holds that guard across stop_canister (workflow mod.rs:103,128). - Saving approval before the reservation exists (handoff/mod.rs:50-53). That last point matters. A deterministic Root reserve rejection wedges the host with no effect performed and nothing to reconcile. Examples are require_quiet_pool (ops mod.rs:201,666-669) and a sequence mismatch (193-195). After that, the approved journal blocks every lock_operation (ops/mod.rs:688), and a new review cannot replace it. The documented terminal state has no documented exit. The docs forbid editing the journal. AGENTS.md requires same-operation recovery, and FI1 says "Correct any confirmed reset/import recovery gap". So this is not only a documentation problem. The main fix does not contradict the design: charge only real submissions, retry typed-unavailable rejections, and approve together with the reservation. The proposed abort command is more debatable, because approved intents are elsewhere documented as non-cancellable. Impact check: - Two quick reruns while Root's stop is still pending use up confirm_stop's budget. - Step 3 of the scenario (a Conflict while Stopping) needs the IC stop timeout. I found a related Root gap: a failed stop leaves the source StopIssued. After that, require_observation expects stopped=true (ops mod.rs:827), and nothing re-issues the stop. It stays high, not critical, for three reasons: no cycles are lost, a manual Root drive with operator authentication is possible, and it needs repeated or deterministic rejections.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test runs the production workflow finish_root (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs) against a real ic-agent Agent. The Agent points at an in-process fake replica, and query-signature verification is off. The fake Root answers the PoolImport status query (source AwaitingHandoff, phase Reserved) and the PoolImportContext query. The Coordinator registry query returns HTTP 500. The journal is built with the existing ops helpers: bound, approved, Root-reserved, and custody-ready. Each finish_root call charges the "0:controllers" submission allowance first. It then calls advance_root, root_command and verify_destination, and fails with CoordinatorUnavailable before any update is sent. The fake replica recorded 0 /call requests. That fails the assertion that an allowance must not be spent when no update was submitted. - After exhaustion, staging a fresh review returned Conflict, because the approved journal was not released. This confirms the host is wedged. Not exercised natively: - The slow-stop path, where Root returns Unavailable and then Conflict. That needs PocketIC. - Root's allocation fence. - The lock_operation refusal. - The absence of an abort command, which I checked only by reading the code (PoolImportCommand has no abort variant). The core claim holds: the allowance is charged before free prechecks, so two failures that never reach Root permanently exhaust the step. The same pattern appears in reserve and release.

+//! Repro: Root step submission budgets are charged before local/free prechecks.
+
+use super::*;
+use crate::fleet_ensure::{
+    generate::capacity_import::tests::inputs,
+    model::capacity_import::{CapacityImportPlanRecord, CapacityImportReservationRecord},
+    ops::capacity_import::{
+        journal,
+        transport::tests::{
+            completion, repro_awaiting_handoff_status, repro_root_context,
+            repro_transport_with_agent, request,
+        },
+    },
+    policy::capacity_import::tests::{destination, plan, principal, sources},
+};
+use candid::{CandidType, Principal};
+use canic_core::dto::{
+    error::Error,
+    pool_import::{PoolImportContext, PoolImportIdentity},
+};
+use ic_agent::{Agent, Identity, Signature, agent::EnvelopeContent};
+use sha2_host::{Digest, Sha256};
+use std::{
+    io::{Read, Write},
+    net::{TcpListener, TcpStream},
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    sync::{
+        Arc, Mutex,
+        atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
+    },
+};
+
+// Unsigned identity that reports the reviewed operator principal; the fake replica does not
+// authenticate envelopes, so this only satisfies the host's local verify_agent check.
+struct ReviewedOperator(Principal);
+
+impl Identity for ReviewedOperator {
+    fn sender(&self) -> Result<Principal, String> {
+        Ok(self.0)
+    }
+
+    fn public_key(&self) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
+        None
+    }
+
+    fn sign(&self, _: &EnvelopeContent) -> Result<Signature, String> {
+        Ok(Signature {
+            public_key: None,
+            signature: None,
+            delegations: None,
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(CandidType, serde::Deserialize)]
+enum StatusRequest {
+    PoolImport(PoolImportIdentity),
+    PoolImportContext,
+}
+
+#[derive(CandidType)]
+enum StatusResponse {
+    PoolImport(Box<PoolImportStatus>),
+    PoolImportContext(Box<PoolImportContext>),
+}
+
+struct FakeReplica {
+    url: String,
+    updates: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
+    log: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>,
+}
+
+// Root answers status/context queries; the Coordinator registry query fails (HTTP 500),
+// which is a free, pre-update precheck failure inside verify_destination.
+fn spawn_fake_replica(
+    root: Principal,
+    status: PoolImportStatus,
+    context: PoolImportContext,
+) -> FakeReplica {
+    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
+    let url = format!("http://{}", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
+    let updates = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
+    let log = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
+    let (thread_updates, thread_log) = (updates.clone(), log.clone());
+    std::thread::spawn(move || {
+        for stream in listener.incoming() {
+            let Ok(stream) = stream else { continue };
+            serve(
+                stream,
+                root,
+                &status,
+                &context,
+                &thread_updates,
+                &thread_log,
+            );
+        }
+    });
+    FakeReplica { url, updates, log }
+}
+
+fn serve(
+    mut stream: TcpStream,
+    root: Principal,
+    status: &PoolImportStatus,
+    context: &PoolImportContext,
+    updates: &AtomicUsize,
+    log: &Mutex<Vec<String>>,
+) {
+    let mut buffer = Vec::new();
+    let mut chunk = [0_u8; 8192];
+    let header_end = loop {
+        if let Some(position) = buffer.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n") {
+            break position + 4;
+        }
+        match stream.read(&mut chunk) {
+            Ok(0) | Err(_) => return,
+            Ok(read) => buffer.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..read]),
+        }
+    };
+    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer[..header_end]).to_string();
+    let path = head.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
+    let length = head
+        .lines()
+        .find_map(|line| {
+            let (key, value) = line.split_once(':')?;
+            key.trim()
+                .eq_ignore_ascii_case("content-length")
+                .then(|| value.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())
+                .flatten()
+        })
+        .unwrap_or(0);
+    while buffer.len() < header_end + length {
+        match stream.read(&mut chunk) {
+            Ok(0) | Err(_) => return,
+            Ok(read) => buffer.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..read]),
+        }
+    }
+    let body = &buffer[header_end..header_end + length];
+    let (code, reply) = respond(&path, body, root, status, context, updates, log);
+    let reason = if code == 200 { "OK" } else { "Internal Server Error" };
+    let mut response = format!(
+        "HTTP/1.1 {code} {reason}\r\nContent-Type: application/cbor\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n",
+        reply.len()
+    )
+    .into_bytes();
+    response.extend_from_slice(&reply);
+    let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
+    let _ = stream.flush();
+}
+
+fn respond(
+    path: &str,
+    body: &[u8],
+    root: Principal,
+    status: &PoolImportStatus,
+    context: &PoolImportContext,
+    updates: &AtomicUsize,
+    log: &Mutex<Vec<String>>,
+) -> (u16, Vec<u8>) {
+    if path.contains("/call") {
+        updates.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        log.lock().unwrap().push(format!("UPDATE {path}"));
+        return (500, Vec::new());
+    }
+    if !path.ends_with("/query") {
+        log.lock().unwrap().push(format!("OTHER {path}"));
+        return (500, Vec::new());
+    }
+    let canister = path.split('/').nth(4).unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
+    if canister != root.to_text() {
+        log.lock()
+            .unwrap()
+            .push(format!("QUERY {canister} -> 500 (coordinator unavailable)"));
+        return (500, Vec::new());
+    }
+    let arg = envelope_arg(body);
+    let reply = match candid::decode_one::<StatusRequest>(&arg) {
+        Ok(StatusRequest::PoolImport(_)) => {
+            log.lock().unwrap().push("QUERY root PoolImport status".into());
+            Ok::<StatusResponse, Error>(StatusResponse::PoolImport(Box::new(status.clone())))
+        }
+        Ok(StatusRequest::PoolImportContext) => {
+            log.lock().unwrap().push("QUERY root PoolImportContext".into());
+            Ok(StatusResponse::PoolImportContext(Box::new(context.clone())))
+        }
+        Err(_) => return (500, Vec::new()),
+    };
+    let candid = candid::encode_one(reply).unwrap();
+    let value = ciborium::Value::Map(vec![
+        (
+            ciborium::Value::Text("status".into()),
+            ciborium::Value::Text("replied".into()),
+        ),
+        (
+            ciborium::Value::Text("reply".into()),
+            ciborium::Value::Map(vec![(
+                ciborium::Value::Text("arg".into()),
+                ciborium::Value::Bytes(candid),
+            )]),
+        ),
+    ]);
+    let mut out = Vec::new();
+    ciborium::ser::into_writer(&value, &mut out).unwrap();
+    (200, out)
+}
+
+fn envelope_arg(body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut value: ciborium::Value = ciborium::de::from_reader(body).unwrap();
+    while let ciborium::Value::Tag(_, inner) = value {
+        value = *inner;
+    }
+    let field = |map: &ciborium::Value, name: &str| -> Option<ciborium::Value> {
+        map.as_map()?
+            .iter()
+            .find(|(key, _)| key.as_text() == Some(name))
+            .map(|(_, value)| value.clone())
+    };
+    let content = field(&value, "content").unwrap();
+    field(&content, "arg")
+        .and_then(|arg| arg.into_bytes().ok())
+        .unwrap_or_default()
+}
+
+// Approved, Root-reserved journal whose only source has completed its host handoff.
+fn approved_journal(
+    plan: CapacityImportPlanRecord,
+) -> (PathBuf, EnsurePaths, CapacityImportJournalStore, CapacityImportJournalRecord) {
+    let directory = crate::test_support::temp_dir("capacity-import-repro-budget");
+    std::fs::create_dir_all(&directory).unwrap();
+    let paths = EnsurePaths::under(directory.as_path(), "staging", "test-fleet");
+    let (policy, seed) = inputs(&plan);
+    let policy = policy.replace("maximum_size = 3", "maximum_size = 4");
+    std::fs::write(directory.join("policy.toml"), policy).unwrap();
+    std::fs::write(directory.join("seed.toml"), seed).unwrap();
+    let store = CapacityImportJournalStore::open(&paths).unwrap();
+    let bound = publication::bind(
+        &paths,
+        &journal::reviewed(plan).unwrap(),
+        Path::new("policy.toml"),
+        Path::new("seed.toml"),
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    store.stage_review(bound).unwrap();
+    let staged = store.read().unwrap().unwrap();
+    let plan = staged.plan.clone();
+    let approved = journal::approve(
+        &staged,
+        plan.plan_sha256,
+        &destination(&plan),
+        &sources(&plan),
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    store.save(&approved).unwrap();
+    let mut record = journal::reserve(
+        &approved,
+        CapacityImportReservationRecord {
+            plan_sha256: plan.plan_sha256,
+            authority: plan.authority.clone(),
+            sources: plan
+                .sources
+                .iter()
+                .map(|source| source.binding.canister_id)
+                .collect(),
+        },
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    store.save(&record).unwrap();
+    for mut observed in sources(&plan) {
+        let id = observed.binding.canister_id;
+        let signed = request(&plan, id);
+        record = journal::prepare_handoff(&record, &observed, signed.clone()).unwrap();
+        store.save(&record).unwrap();
+        record = journal::issue_handoff(&record, id).unwrap();
+        store.save(&record).unwrap();
+        observed
+            .binding
+            .controllers
+            .clone_from(&plan.transitional_controllers);
+        observed.binding.canister_version += 1;
+        record =
+            journal::observe_handoff(&record, &observed, &completion(&plan, id, &signed)).unwrap();
+        store.save(&record).unwrap();
+    }
+    (directory, paths, store, record)
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_step_budget_not_spent_by_failed_free_precheck() {
+    let initial = plan();
+    // Default Agent root key is the IC mainnet key; bind the reviewed plan to it.
+    let probe = Agent::builder()
+        .with_url("http://127.0.0.1:1")
+        .build()
+        .unwrap();
+    let mut authority = initial.authority.clone();
+    authority.network_root_key_sha256 = Sha256::digest(probe.read_root_key()).into();
+    let plan = crate::fleet_ensure::ops::capacity_import::prepare_review(
+        authority,
+        initial.sources,
+        initial.root_budget,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let root = plan.authority.root;
+    let coordinator = plan.authority.coordinator;
+    let replica = spawn_fake_replica(
+        root,
+        repro_awaiting_handoff_status(&plan),
+        repro_root_context(),
+    );
+    let agent = Agent::builder()
+        .with_url(replica.url.clone())
+        .with_identity(ReviewedOperator(plan.authority.operator))
+        .with_verify_query_signatures(false)
+        .build()
+        .unwrap();
+    let transport = repro_transport_with_agent(agent);
+    let (directory, paths, store, mut record) = approved_journal(plan.clone());
+    assert!(record.approved && record.reservation.is_some());
+    assert!(journal::all_custody_ready(&record));
+
+    let runtime = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
+        .enable_all()
+        .build()
+        .unwrap();
+    let step = "0:controllers";
+    let mut outcomes = Vec::new();
+    for attempt in 1..=3 {
+        let result = runtime.block_on(finish_root(&store, &mut record, &transport));
+        let charged = store
+            .read()
+            .unwrap()
+            .unwrap()
+            .operation
+            .unwrap()
+            .submissions
+            .get(step)
+            .copied();
+        println!(
+            "attempt {attempt}: result={:?} persisted_submissions[{step}]={charged:?} updates_sent={}",
+            result.as_ref().err(),
+            replica.updates.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
+        );
+        outcomes.push(result);
+    }
+    println!("fake replica log: {:#?}", replica.log.lock().unwrap());
+
+    // Wedge evidence: with the approved journal unreleased, a fresh review is refused.
+    let mut next_sources = plan.sources.clone();
+    next_sources[0].binding.canister_id = principal(90);
+    let next = crate::fleet_ensure::ops::capacity_import::prepare_review(
+        plan.authority.clone(),
+        next_sources,
+        plan.root_budget.clone(),
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let next = publication::bind(
+        &paths,
+        &journal::reviewed(next).unwrap(),
+        Path::new("policy.toml"),
+        Path::new("seed.toml"),
+    );
+    let restage = next.map(|next| store.stage_review(next));
+    println!("stage fresh review after exhaustion: {restage:?}");
+
+    assert_eq!(replica.updates.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
+    for outcome in &outcomes[..2] {
+        assert!(matches!(
+            outcome,
+            Err(CapacityImportJournalError::CoordinatorUnavailable { coordinator: c }) if *c == coordinator
+        ));
+    }
+    std::fs::remove_dir_all(directory).ok();
+    // Correct behaviour: two precheck failures that never submitted a Root update must not
+    // exhaust the step's submission allowance; the third attempt should reach the precheck
+    // again rather than being permanently refused.
+    assert!(
+        !matches!(
+            outcomes[2],
+            Err(CapacityImportJournalError::BudgetExhausted { .. })
+        ),
+        "step {step} exhausted its {}-submission budget although 0 Root updates were sent: {:?}",
+        2,
+        outcomes[2].as_ref().err()
+    );
+}
highreproducedhost-ensure-capacity-3 · security · high confidence
Any credit to a source or the destination Root is treated as a conservation failure, so a permissionless deposit_cycles can block approval or permanently stall a reserved import.
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/policy/capacity_import/mod.rs:359

Failure scenario

After the Root reservation, anyone deposits 0.5T cycles into the Root. From then on, every Root Advance/Settle paid call fails reserve_call with conflict, and the host's per-step budget is exhausted within two runs. Alternatively, an attacker deposits a few billion cycles into a source after its handoff executed. Each rerun reaches observe_handoff, which returns Unresolved or ConservationUnproven and spends an inspection, until BudgetExhausted. The source's controllers have already been changed. In both cases the import is permanently stuck and Root stays fenced. A legitimate Coordinator refill or refund can trigger the same outcome.

Evidence

Host-side checks that reject any increase:
- retained_source_debit uses total_before.checked_sub(total_after) and returns ConservationUnproven whenever a source gained cycles (policy/capacity_import/mod.rs:351-362). It is used by admit_source (323), prepare_handoff (journal/mod.rs:211), observe_handoff (journal/mod.rs:298) and renew (journal/rejection/mod.rs:93).
- observe_handoff also returns Unresolved if the post-handoff total exceeds the pre-handoff total (journal/mod.rs:307-309).
- admit_handoffs computes the Root debit with checked_sub and returns InvalidCycleBounds when Root's live balance exceeds its reviewed balance (policy/capacity_import/mod.rs:249-257).
- validate_root_status rejects last_root_cycles > observed_cycles (evidence/mod.rs:25).

On the Root side, reserve_call returns conflict on every paid call once the current balance exceeds the reviewed observed_root_cycles (canic-control-plane ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:941-944). Bootstrap applies the same rule (ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:569-575).

Tests assert this as intended (policy/capacity_import/tests.rs:323-343). However, any canister can deposit cycles into any canister ID, and there is no path to review a credit. Each failed attempt spends the 4-inspection or 2-submission allowance.

Recommendation

Conservation only requires that no cycles are lost. Compute the debit as original.saturating_sub(current), and treat any excess as retained controlled credit recorded in the receipt, rather than as an error, on both the host and Root sides. At minimum, never make a credit terminal. Allow a reviewed rebase that keeps the original baseline as the lower bound.

Verifier (confirmed): The finding holds, with small corrections. In retained_source_debit (policy/capacity_import/mod.rs:351-362), total_before.checked_sub(total_after) rejects any balance above the reviewed baseline. The host calls it from observe_handoff (journal/mod.rs:298), which also returns Unresolved when the total rises (307-309). On Root, reserve_observation and budget (workflow/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:241-261) pass the live canister_cycle_balance to reserve_call. reserve_call (ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:941-944) and settle (509-514) return conflict once that balance exceeds reservation.observed_root_cycles, which the host sets to plan.root_budget.observed_cycles (host ops/capacity_import/mod.rs:152). The Root source transitions (297, 336, 360, 427, 473) reject source credits too. Corrections: only a deposit larger than the debit consumed so far trips the check. For a stopped source that debit is near zero, so almost any deposit does. The bootstrap check is in canic-host ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:569-575, not canic-control-plane. The stall is permanent. Every Advance or Settle attempt spends the host's 2-submission step allowance (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:88-99; publication MAX_SUBMISSIONS=2), and each observe_handoff retry spends one of 4 inspections. So even after Root burns back below its baseline, the host cannot finish. No abort path exists: capacity_import is never cleared except by release. An active import fences pool, allocation, provisioning and retirement through require_idle (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs and component_registry/*). deposit_cycles and Cycles Ledger withdraw are permissionless, and routine top-ups also trigger it. Cycles stay controlled, but recovery cannot complete, so this is high.

Every Advance or Settle call (workflow/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:87-196) first calls reserve_observation. That passes the live Root balance to reserve_call (241-251), and reserve_call returns conflict when `observed_root_cycles.checked_sub(live)` fails (ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:939-942). settle (509-514) and require_observation (839-841) reject in the same way, and so do the source transitions at 297, 336, 360, 427 and 463. Each Advance or Settle attempt spends a submission before the call is sent (workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:88-99). consume allows 2 per step (publication/mod.rs:42, 299-311). A new operation cannot be bound after approval (publication/mod.rs:83). The only thing that clears Root's capacity_import record is a replacing reserve() after Released (ops/.../capacity_import/mod.rs:185-191), and reaching Released requires a successful settle. In the meantime, require_idle fences pool, allocation, provisioning and retirement (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:108 and following, component_registry/*). The wider project intent points the other way, though: - The design (0.110-design.md:216) calls for accounting for "any separately approved credit". No such review path exists in the import code; grep finds none. - The maintainer's "Native donation tolerance" directive (docs/design/0.110-fleet-runtime-contraction/status.md:1162-1170) says native donations must not reject recovery. Accounting must accept them without creating payment authority, using net accounting. - docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:585 and :1384 accept outside top-ups as ordinary balance observations. - AGENTS.md requires that same-release recovery can complete. The recommended fix matches that existing donation-tolerance design, so it does not contradict it. The impact is real: - reserve_call (control-plane ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:941-944) rejects any Root credit as a conflict, before the paid call is counted. - The host still spends one of its two submissions per step (publication/mod.rs:42, 260-271; workflow/capacity_import/mod.rs:88-99). - observe_handoff also rejects credits (journal/mod.rs:298, 307-309). - Once an import is approved but unfinished, it blocks Fleet ensure (retained_contract/mod.rs:128; journal/store/mod.rs:328-341) and clean reinstall (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:180-181). Clean reinstall runs through this import path itself. - fleet-ensure.md:1191 and :1200-1202 forbid editing the journal, and a new review cannot replace an approved unfinished operation. Correction: the "legitimate Coordinator refill" trigger is mostly unreachable. The import requires minimum_root_cycles to be at least request_threshold (workflow capacity_import/mod.rs:232-240), and a funding request needs a balance at or below that threshold (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:63). A permissionless deposit to Root or a source, or a third-party auto top-up, remains a trivial trigger. Severity stays high rather than critical: no cycles are lost, existing workloads keep running, and reinstalling Root out-of-band is still possible before 1.0.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test reuses the existing publication fixture, which is a bound, operation-carrying journal on disk, and drives production code in three places. (1) It calls retained_source_debit with the source's reviewed balance plus a 500-cycle deposit. (2) It calls admit_handoffs with the destination Root's controlled_cycles raised by 500. (3) It follows the handoff workflow's own inspection spending: one inspection for the approval sample, then approve and reserve, one inspection for the intent sample, then prepare_handoff and issue_handoff. It then plays the workflow's Completed branch (reserve_inspection followed by observe_handoff) against a post-handoff sample whose controllers are already transitional, whose version is +1, and whose balance includes a 500-cycle third-party deposit. It asserts that a credit counts as zero debit, that approval is admitted, and that the handoff is recorded as Applied. All three checks fail as the finding claims. retained_source_debit returns ConservationUnproven. admit_handoffs returns InvalidCycleBounds. Both observe_handoff attempts fail with ConservationUnproven, and the third reserve_inspection fails with BudgetExhausted. So the handoff that was already executed can never be recorded, because the 4-inspection budget cannot be reset. The host-side claim holds in full. The Root-side reserve_call rejection was not run by this test. The existing control-plane test capacity_import_root_paid_attempts_survive_replay_without_budget_rebase already asserts that reserve_paid_call(identity(), 1, 10_001) errors, which corroborates it. The "no abort path" part of the permanence claim was not tested separately.

+// Reproduction for review finding host-ensure-capacity-3: a permissionless credit
+// (deposit_cycles, Cycles Ledger withdraw, routine top-up) loses no cycles, so it must
+// not be treated as a conservation failure that blocks approval or stalls an issued handoff.
+#[test]
+fn repro_third_party_credit_is_not_a_conservation_failure() {
+    use crate::fleet_ensure::policy::capacity_import::{admit_handoffs, retained_source_debit};
+    const DEPOSIT: u128 = 500;
+    let (directory, _paths, store) = fixture();
+    let staged = store.read().unwrap().unwrap();
+    let plan = staged.plan.clone();
+    let id = plan.sources[0].binding.canister_id;
+
+    // (1) Policy: a pure credit to a reviewed source is zero debit, not a conservation failure.
+    let source_credit = retained_source_debit(
+        &plan.sources[0],
+        plan.sources[0].observed_cycles + DEPOSIT,
+        plan.sources[0].observed_reserved_cycles,
+    );
+    println!("retained_source_debit(source +{DEPOSIT}) = {source_credit:?}");
+
+    // (2) Approval: someone deposits into the destination Root between review and approval.
+    let mut credited_root = destination(&plan);
+    credited_root.controlled_cycles += DEPOSIT;
+    let root_credit = admit_handoffs(&plan, &credited_root, &sources(&plan));
+    println!("admit_handoffs(root +{DEPOSIT}) = {root_credit:?}");
+
+    // (3) Journal: follow the handoff workflow's inspection spending exactly
+    // (one inspection for the approval sample, one for the handoff-intent sample).
+    let mut journal = reserve_inspection(&staged, id).unwrap();
+    store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+    journal = journal::approve(
+        &journal,
+        plan.plan_sha256,
+        &destination(&plan),
+        &sources(&plan),
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+    journal = journal::reserve(
+        &journal,
+        CapacityImportReservationRecord {
+            plan_sha256: plan.plan_sha256,
+            authority: plan.authority.clone(),
+            sources: vec![id],
+        },
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+    journal = reserve_inspection(&journal, id).unwrap();
+    store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+    let observed = sources(&plan).remove(0);
+    let handoff_request = request(&plan, id);
+    journal = journal::prepare_handoff(&journal, &observed, handoff_request.clone()).unwrap();
+    store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+    journal = journal::issue_handoff(&journal, id).unwrap();
+    store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+
+    // The controller update executed (source controllers already changed), then a third
+    // party deposits cycles into the source before the host samples it.
+    let mut after = observed;
+    after
+        .binding
+        .controllers
+        .clone_from(&plan.transitional_controllers);
+    after.binding.canister_version += 1;
+    after.cycles += DEPOSIT;
+    let done = completion(&plan, id, &handoff_request);
+    let mut attempts = Vec::new();
+    let mut applied = None;
+    loop {
+        match reserve_inspection(&journal, id) {
+            Ok(next) => {
+                journal = next;
+                store.save(&journal).unwrap();
+            }
+            Err(error) => {
+                attempts.push(format!("reserve_inspection -> {error:?}"));
+                break;
+            }
+        }
+        match journal::observe_handoff(&journal, &after, &done) {
+            Ok(next) => {
+                applied = Some(next);
+                break;
+            }
+            Err(error) => attempts.push(format!("observe_handoff -> {error:?}")),
+        }
+    }
+    println!("post-handoff attempts (source cycles {}): {attempts:#?}", after.cycles);
+    println!("handoff applied: {}", applied.is_some());
+    std::fs::remove_dir_all(directory).unwrap();
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        source_credit,
+        Ok(0),
+        "a source credit must count as zero debit, not a conservation failure"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        root_credit,
+        Ok(()),
+        "a Root credit must not block approval of the reviewed import"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        applied.is_some(),
+        "an executed handoff must be recorded Applied despite a third-party credit; attempts: {attempts:?}"
+    );
+}
highreproducedhost-ensure-core-1 · liveness · high confidence
Ledger effects reuse the review-time created_at_time, and the InProgress journal is written first, so applying a plan more than 24h after review (or resuming a lost Ledger reply after the window) permanently wedges the operation
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/mod.rs:1344

Failure scenario

An operator reviews a plan containing Create or Fund actions and applies its digest more than 24h later. Pre-apply verification passes, the InProgress journal is written, and the first Create returns TooOld. Every resume fails the same way, planning keeps returning the same in-progress plan, and --reinstall is refused, so there is no supported recovery. Variant: a Create is issued, the Ledger executes it, and the reply is lost. If the resume happens more than 24h later, the reissue returns TooOld. The new canister and the operator debit are never recorded in the journal, so terminal conservation can never be reached.

Evidence

The action timestamp is the review clock plus the action index: policy/mod.rs:380-384, fed from the CLI's now_nanoseconds (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:594-600). verify_fresh_plan recompiles with retained_plan.planned_at_time (workflow/mod.rs:2776, 2811), so the timestamp is frozen. The fresh InProgress journal is created and written at workflow/mod.rs:1344-1378, before any Ledger call. apply_create and apply_fund send Some(created_at_time) (ops/platform.rs:2742, 2763ff). A TooOld reply becomes a generic LedgerCreate/withdraw error (ops/platform.rs:5632, 5657). The executor then only bumps stalled_observations and returns (workflow/mod.rs:1776-1797). While the journal is InProgress, plan_with_observations returns the retained plan (workflow/mod.rs:519-561) and plan_reinstall returns RetainedOperationRecoveryRequired (workflow/reinstall/mod.rs:85-91). For an Intent Create after a lost reply, the only reconciliation is the Ledger Duplicate reply (ops/platform.rs:5500-5512, 4412-4423). By contrast, the runtime pool refill explicitly handles the 24h window (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/refill.rs:212-219, 322-337; canic-core TX_WINDOW_NANOS).

Recommendation

Before writing the fresh journal, reject a plan whose earliest Ledger created_at_time is older than the Ledger window minus a safety margin, using DriftedBeforeApply or a typed StalePlan error. Persist an 'issued at least once' marker before each Ledger call. When the first-ever issuance gets TooOld or CreatedInFuture (which proves the call never executed), close the journal as ReplanRequired. For already-issued Intent Ledger effects past the window, add typed reconciliation (Ledger block lookup or the pending principal) instead of blind reissue.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. Each action's timestamp is the plan clock plus the action index (policy/mod.rs:380-384; the Create/Fund fields are set at 947 and 1003). apply() takes no clock argument (workflow/mod.rs:1054-1061). verify_fresh_plan recompiles with retained_plan.planned_at_time (2776, 2811) and only compares digests, so a plan applied days after review passes. No plan-age or ledger-window check exists: verified_plan (4123-4134) checks only the hash, and a grep turns up no TX-window logic in fleet_ensure outside operator_mint. The InProgress journal is written at 1344-1378 before any effect. apply_create and apply_fund send the frozen time (ops/platform.rs:2742, 2767, 4861). TooOld only becomes the string-typed LedgerCreate/LedgerWithdraw error (5504-5512, 5632, 5657), and the executor just increments stalled_observations and returns (1776-1797). Once InProgress, plan returns the retained plan (519-561), and plan_reinstall refuses with RetainedOperationRecoveryRequired (reinstall/mod.rs:85-91). The CLI has no abandon path; cancel-mint only covers mint reviews. Funding reviews do get fresh times (funding/mod.rs:169-173), but main-plan effects do not. An estate-funding or mint pause lasting more than 24h before a later Create or Fund is a second way to reach this. The lost-reply variant matches the intended uncertain-TooOld block (0.106-design.md:215-218; 0.100-design.md:1872-1876), but the known-unapplied first issue has no ReplanRequired exit. Severity stays high, not critical: TooOld proves nothing was paid, the canisters keep running, and deleting the host journal by hand is an unsupported escape.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): The finding stands. Someone who can run `canic fleet ensure <fleet> --apply <digest>` on the host can reach it through an ordinary delay. No attack is needed. `plan` reads `now_nanoseconds()` (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:594). `--apply` calls `apply()`, which takes no clock (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:565-572; workflow/mod.rs:1054-1061). Each action gets planned_at_time plus its index as its timestamp (policy/mod.rs:379-383). `verify_fresh_plan` recompiles with retained_plan.planned_at_time (workflow/mod.rs:2811). It fails only when the digest differs and the bounded-observation check also rejects (2844-2848). That check limits cycle movement, not age (3377-3405). An idle or fresh-install Create plan therefore passes days later. No age or window check exists anywhere in fleet_ensure (grep: only operator_mint handles TooOld). The InProgress journal is written before any effect (1344-1378). apply_create and apply_fund send the frozen timestamp (ops/platform.rs:2742, 2763). TooOld comes back only as the string-typed LedgerCreate/LedgerWithdraw error (5512, 5632, 5657). The executor just bumps stalled_observations (1776-1797). After that there is no supported exit. `plan` returns the retained plan while InProgress (519-561). `--reinstall` fails with RetainedOperationRecoveryRequired (reinstall/mod.rs:85-91). clean_reinstall re-plans only after ReplanRequired (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:116-129). `--cancel-mint` covers only mint reviews. The lost-reply variant is an intended fail-closed choice (local-development-fleet.md:136-138; 0.106-design.md:215-218). Those docs allow a fresh request only when evidence proves the effect never happened, but a TooOld on a first-ever issuance has no ReplanRequired exit. Operator authority does not reduce the severity, because the harm is recovery that cannot complete for that operator, not an escalation. It is high rather than critical: TooOld proves nothing was paid, root and the canisters keep running, and deleting the journal by hand is a crude escape.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute the main claim. Only the lost-reply variant is intended behaviour. docs/features/operations/local-development-fleet.md:136-138 says an unresolved request "fails" once it is past the Ledger window, and Canic will not "silently submit a new timestamp". 0.106-design.md:215-218 also forbids turning TooOld into a fresh paid request unless there is proof the effect never happened. So blocking an uncertain request after 24h is by design. The known-unapplied case is not intended. The designs call for an exit here: 0.100-design.md:3424 says "known-unapplied `TooOld` rolls forward monotonically", and the runtime pool refill implements that. The host has the tools for it too: a ReplanRequired completion exists (model/mod.rs:1307) and is used for balance drift (workflow/mod.rs:1624). DriftedBeforeApply also exists as a check before the journal is written. The recommended fix therefore fits the design. No doc sets a limit on plan age or asks for a prompt apply. fleet-ensure.md only mentions a one-hour limit for catalogs (line 525), and its line 948 only says it does not check that the window is open. The code facts hold: - apply() takes no clock (workflow/mod.rs:1054-1061). - verify_fresh_plan recompiles with planned_at_time (2811). The drift check only bounds cycle movement, by default 1T (3383-3400; doc line 1217), so a plan applied a day later still passes. - The journal is written before any effect (1344-1378). - apply_create and apply_fund send the frozen timestamp (ops/platform.rs:2742, 2767). - TooOld only produces a string error (5504-5512, 5632, 5657), and the executor just increments stalled_observations (1776-1797). - While the journal is InProgress, plan returns the retained plan (519-561), and reinstall is refused (reinstall/mod.rs:85-91). The trigger is realistic. fleet-ensure.md:898-903 sends an operator with a shortfall off to buy ICP and run --operator-mint before applying, which can easily take more than 24h. It stays high, not critical: nothing is paid, and the fleet canisters keep running.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test uses the existing fleet_ensure fixture() and MockPlatform, with a Create for "created" and Funds for "app" and "replaced". It calls production workflow::plan with planned_at_time set to wall-clock now minus 48h. It then models the Cycles Ledger's TooOld rule in the mock: every Ledger action whose created_at_time is more than 24h old gets stall_before_mutation(u32::MAX), so it errors every time without executing. Then it calls production workflow::apply, applies again, re-plans with a fresh clock, and calls plan_reinstall. What happened: apply ran no plan-age check. It wrote the InProgress journal and sent one Ledger request carrying the timestamp from 48h earlier. That request was rejected, and the only effect was stalled_observations=1. The second apply returned Stalled, and the journal stayed InProgress. Planning with the fresh clock returned the same plan digest with the same frozen created_at_time values. plan_reinstall returned RetainedOperationRecoveryRequired. No real mutation ever happened, so the operation is wedged with no supported exit. The test asserts the correct behaviour: a stale plan must not reach InProgress, no out-of-window Ledger request may be sent, and fresh planning must give in-window timestamps. It fails on the first of these. The main claim holds in full. Two caveats: the Ledger's TooOld reply is simulated by the mock, because a real Ledger is not available natively, and the lost-reply-after-24h variant was not exercised.

FundEstate completion requires an untouched Root Ledger balance, so Root's own autonomous creation (or any third-party credit) after the transfer makes the paid effect permanently unprovable and wedges the operation
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:5366

Failure scenario

An active Root R has a WaitingForFunding pool creation and 1T in its Ledger account. The plan's FundEstate is 5T with expected_post 6T. Apply persists the intent (operator 100T, R 1T) and submits icrc1_transfer. Then the ICP CLI reply is lost (timeout or Ctrl-C), or the host's post-transfer reads fall after Root's next 30-60 s tick. Root sees 6T, creates its canister and debits about 4.1T. On rerun the Intent replays, gets a Duplicate receipt and becomes Issued. Observation then sees destination_after = 1.9T, a credit of 0.9T instead of 5T, so applied stays false for good. The operation hits Stalled on every resume, and the InProgress journal blocks new plans and reinstall (RetainedOperationRecoveryRequired). A stranger depositing a few cycles into the operator's or R's account inside the window has the same effect.

Evidence

`estate_funding_applied` (platform.rs:5344-5369) requires `source_debit == amount + fee`, `destination_credit == amount` and `destination_after == expected_destination_after`. Both `before` values are frozen in the intent by `prepare_effect` (effect_preparation/mod.rs:32-42, via action_cycles 5026-5031 and action_destination_cycles 5100-5103). `observe_effect` (4477-4506) re-reads live operator and Root Ledger balances on every observation. The Root Ledger account is not quiescent. Root's pool maintenance timer runs every 30 s (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:53, 263-267) and retries a WaitingForFunding creation from that same default account (refill.rs:35, 84-88, 142-147). That pending creation is exactly what the FundEstate was planned to fund. Anyone can also icrc1_transfer into either account. In the main effect loop an Issued, non-applied record is never replayed (workflow/mod.rs:1824-1837 allows replay only for ProvisionComponents) and only consumes the stall budget (1864-1899). The frozen baselines never change, so every resume reproduces the mismatch. The supplementary funding path explicitly accepts consumption (workflow/funding/mod.rs:448-449), and the doc promises recovery "including when the Root has already consumed the credit" (fleet-ensure.md:884-887). The primary-plan path does neither.

Recommendation

Prove FundEstate completion from the transfer itself: authenticate the receipt block through icrc3_get_blocks (from = operator, to = R, amount, fee, created_at_time). Treat live balances as bounded evidence (destination_after >= destination_before + amount - Root creation debits proven by R's pool creation receipts), and reconcile the remainder at terminal conservation, as the supplementary funding path already does. Add a regression test where the mock Root consumes the credit between apply and observation.
