highreproducedhost-ensure-platform-4 · liveness · medium confidence
Retirement Transfer requires an exact treasury credit with no allowance for the treasury's own burn, so routine idle charges turn a conserved drain into a permanent UnbalancedTransfer
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:4751

Failure scenario

Retire canister S with a 10T drain to treasury T, which holds 50T at intent. The drain call takes a few seconds, and in that window T is charged about 20k cycles of idle fees. Observation computes a credit of 10T - 20k, which is not 10T, so it returns UnbalancedTransfer. S is left running (fail-closed), and retirement can never complete on resume. After a lost reply the gap only grows.

Evidence

observe_effect for Transfer (platform.rs:4715-4793) reads the treasury's live liquid balance (4730-4738) and compares it with destination_pre_cycles frozen at intent (4745-4750, captured by action_destination_cycles 5104-5110). reconcile_retirement_transfer (model/mod.rs:1400-1413) requires destination_credit == transfer_amount exactly. If the treasury balance dropped below its baseline, it returns BalanceMovedInInvalidDirection. The source side gets a maximum_execution_burn allowance; the destination gets none. The treasury is an ordinary Present canister (policy/mod.rs:2156-2160). It pays periodic storage and compute charges, and pays for any execution (timers, heartbeat) between the intent read and the post-drain status read. Any such debit turns a correctly conserved drain into an UnbalancedTransfer error. The baseline is never refreshed, so every resume reproduces it; the doc explicitly requires an 'exact controlled-treasury credit' (fleet-ensure.md:1547).

Recommendation

Bound the destination side too. Either accept destination_credit in [amount - reviewed_treasury_observation_burn, amount] under an explicit reviewed treasury burn bound, or prove the credit through a receipt (the drain response plus a treasury-side deposit record) rather than raw balance deltas.

Severity adjusted from medium to high during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): `reconcile_retirement_transfer` (model/mod.rs:1393-1428) requires `destination_credit == transfer_amount` exactly. It returns BalanceMovedInInvalidDirection when the treasury balance falls below `destination_before`. `destination_pre_cycles` is captured once in `prepare_effect` (ops/effect_preparation/mod.rs:34-42) and is never refreshed: `merge_observed_cycles` (workflow/mod.rs:2397-2408) updates only the post fields. The observation at platform.rs:4715-4793 reads a fresh live treasury balance, because apply clears the snapshot at 4838. The source side gets a `maximum_execution_burn` allowance; the treasury gets none. On mainnet, every canister with memory pays periodic allocation and storage charges, applied roughly every 10 s, plus the cost of any messages it executes. The window from intent read to the post-drain read spans several icp CLI round trips, so a nonzero treasury debit in that window is likely on essentially every mainnet retirement. The result is UnbalancedTransfer, or InvalidTransferBalance before the drain is even issued. The baseline is frozen, the InProgress journal pins the plan (workflow/mod.rs:517-540), and there is no abandon command, so every resume reproduces the error. This path is routine: the planner emits Transfer for every material retiring canister (policy/mod.rs:1895-1947). Cycles remain conserved in the treasury, but retirement and the fleet-ensure operation cannot complete. That is 'recovery that cannot complete' on an ordinary path, so I upgrade it to high. The PocketIC tests are deterministic and would not expose it.

The treasury baseline is captured once, at intent (effect_preparation/mod.rs:34-42). merge_observed_cycles updates only the post fields (workflow/mod.rs:2397-2408). reconcile_retirement_transfer rejects any fall in the treasury balance (model/mod.rs:1402) and demands an exact credit (1413). The source gets an allowance, but the treasury gets none. The skeptic found that the failure is more deterministic than the finding says. Every treasury read is a fresh management `canister_status` update routed through the treasury's effective canister ID: `icp canister status` (icp/canister.rs:245-257), or on local, management_canister_status_candid (icp/management.rs:84-110). On the IC, the effective canister pays the ingress induction fee for such management-canister ingress, about 1.2M cycles or more. So each read costs the treasury cycles, on top of its idle storage charges. Apply clears the snapshot (platform.rs:4838), and the loop observes without one. After the intent is written, the first observe_effect runs before apply (workflow/mod.rs:1531-1540). Its fresh treasury read (platform.rs:4730-4738) already comes in below the frozen baseline, so it returns InvalidTransferBalance and the drain is never issued. action_destination_cycles at workflow/mod.rs:1547 adds another paid read. Even when the drain is issued, the post-drain read's own fee rules out an exact credit. The InProgress journal pins the plan (workflow/mod.rs:517-540), and I found no abandon command. Every resume therefore repeats the error. The only drain in the repo is a fake platform in tests.rs, so nothing exercises real IC fees. Cycles stay conserved, because the check fails closed. But retirement and the fleet operation cannot complete, which is recovery that cannot complete on a routine path: high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): Not refuted. The code does what the finding says. reconcile_retirement_transfer (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/model/mod.rs:1393-1428) gives the source a maximum_execution_burn allowance, but it requires destination_credit == transfer_amount exactly and returns BalanceMovedInInvalidDirection if the treasury balance dropped. prepare_effect captures destination_pre_cycles once (ops/effect_preparation/mod.rs:34-43). The observation reads a fresh treasury status with an ingress management call (platform.rs:1745-1760, 4730-4738), after apply has cleared the snapshot (4836-4838). Wording such as "exact controlled-treasury credit" appears in fleet-ensure.md:1546-1547 and changelog 0.109.md:1587-1590. It describes a conservation proof; it does not accept that routine retirement will never complete. The design itself recognises that observing a canister costs that canister cycles. fleet-ensure.md:1478-1500 has "measured execution and observation burn", and the funding margin covers "one observation" per target. workflow/mod.rs:3378 tolerates movement caused by observation. current.md:3612 says "Balance snapshots cannot distinguish donations from simultaneous consumption". The ideas design says balance deltas "cannot distinguish" an operation's credit "from Root burn" and calls for receipts (bounded-multi-fleet-estates/design.md:296-298). So the recommended fix fits the design direction. On a network that charges fees, the post-drain canister_status ingress is itself billed to the treasury (as the effective canister), and the treasury also pays periodic storage charges. The exact-equality check therefore fails on essentially every retirement. The mock tests (tests.rs:549-571, 781-805) credit exactly `amount` and never show this, and the repo contains no real drain endpoint. Cycles stay conserved, since the source keeps running and funded. However, the InProgress journal pins the plan (workflow/mod.rs:519-545) and the baseline is never refreshed, so retirement cannot complete. This is an intended feature path that cannot finish, which fits high.

Each test registers a "treasury" principal and gives the source "coordinator" 20T and the treasury 50T. After that it calls the real IcpEnsurePlatform::observe_effect. (1) Before the drain, the treasury pays a 20k idle charge and the source is untouched. The correct result would be Pending, but observe_effect returns Err(InvalidTransferBalance). This happens because destination_after < destination_before hits BalanceMovedInInvalidDirection. (2) After an exactly conserved drain, the source is debited 10T+1M, which is inside its allowance, and the treasury is credited 10T-20k. The correct result would be applied, but observe_effect returns Err(UnbalancedTransfer), because the destination credit must equal the amount exactly. This confirms that the destination side has no burn allowance and that the frozen intent baseline is what gets compared. I checked the resume claim by reading the code only; no test exercises it. merge_observed_cycles updates only the post fields, and the pre-apply observe_effect in the workflow (mod.rs:1531-1540) uses the same record. So re-observing would give the same error every time, and the core claim holds.

highreproducedhost-ensure-reinstall-1 · correctness · high confidence
After a clean reinstall completes, clean-reinstall.json keeps capturing all later Ensure invocations, so a changed desired can never be applied and --reinstall no longer starts a new reset
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:65

Failure scenario

A clean reinstall converges. The operator adds a deployment and runs `fleet ensure staging --desired new.toml`. Because the Fleet is completed, `selected` is false, so the ordinary planner writes plan X. `fleet ensure --apply X` is then routed to clean reinstall with the frozen desired and fails with DriftedBeforeApply. `fleet ensure` or `fleet ensure --reinstall` returns plan X with fleet_completed: true and no next command. No CLI command can apply the new desired or begin another reset. The only recovery is manually deleting clean-reinstall.json or plan.json, which the docs forbid.

Evidence

`selected` returns `reinstall || (applying && clean-reinstall.json exists)` only while `completed_fleet` holds. Otherwise it returns true whenever clean-reinstall.json exists (workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:60-65). That file is never removed after phase 3 converges; a later retirement is the only thing that archives it (writers and readers are only at ops/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:37,70). `completed()` returns None as soon as plan.json and journal.json stop matching (ops/operation_selection/mod.rs:39-43). That is exactly the state after an ordinary review writes a new plan. From then on:
- `retained_desired` returns the frozen reset desired, even with --reinstall (79-82).
- `apply` passes that frozen desired, together with the new plan's own desired_sha256, to workflow::apply (278-286). workflow::apply therefore uses the frozen desired as operation_desired (workflow/mod.rs:1098-1124), and verify_fresh_plan recompiles from it (workflow/mod.rs:2745-2850), giving DriftedBeforeApply.
- `review` (with or without --reinstall) skips retirement because prepare_bootstrap finds no completed operation, then returns the new plan as terminal (115-133).

Recommendation

Scope the selection to its own operation. Route to clean reinstall only when plan.json is the clean infrastructure plan, a clean import is pending, or plan.desired_sha256 == convergence_digest(record.desired, infrastructure plan); otherwise fall through to ordinary Ensure. Alternatively, archive clean-reinstall.json with the terminal receipt when phase 3 converges and let terminal replay read the archived selection. Add a test that runs an ordinary review and apply with a changed desired after a completed clean reinstall.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced this end to end and the defect is real. After phase 3 converges, clean-reinstall.json stays in place. Only retirement removes it, via archive capture of the whole estate directory (retirement/mod.rs:161-230), and retirement needs completed() to return Some. An ordinary review is not routed away because selected() returns false at workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:60-63. It always writes a new plan. The phase-3 plan's desired_sha256 is convergence_digest (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:158; ops/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:194-205), which never matches the file hash. So matching_prior is None, a new operation_id is computed (workflow/mod.rs:650-657), and write_plan runs at 672, 694 or 773. This happens even when the desired file is unchanged. completed() then returns None (operation_selection/mod.rs:39-43), so every later ensure is routed to the clean reinstall at mod.rs:65. That covers review, --apply and --reinstall, because run_if_selected runs first (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:508) and retire_if_selected is never reached. - review: prepare_bootstrap does nothing (retirement/mod.rs:35-38), and 115-133 reports plan X as terminal with fleet_completed:true even though X was never applied. - apply: 278-285 passes X's own desired_sha256, so the check at 1098-1101 passes trivially and the frozen desired becomes operation_desired. verify_fresh_plan then fails at 2848 because normalized_plan differs. The normalized-plan check means no wrong on-chain effect and no cycle loss. The docs say ordinary Ensure works after a reset (fleet-ensure.md:277-278), but the only recovery is deleting local state by hand. So this is recovery that cannot complete: high.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could reach the bug from the CLI with a routine operator action. `run_ensure` calls `clean_reinstall::run_if_selected` first (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:508). After phase 3 converges, `completed_fleet` is true, so a plain review gets `selected == false` (workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:60-63). `retire_completed_authority` returns early when `new_reinstall` is false (workflow/completed_reset/mod.rs:34-36). Completed_reset and completed_preparation do not select either. `load_ensure_authority` loads the new file because `retained_in_progress_plan` sees the journal as completed. `plan_with_observations` then falls through. The prior plan has no reinstall intent, and `reconcile_retained_planning_state` returns no `matching_prior` because the file hash differs from `convergence_digest`. It calls `write_plan` at workflow/mod.rs:773, and `write_plan` overwrites plan.json unconditionally (ops/mod.rs:939-955). Once plan.json is replaced, `completed()` returns None (operation_selection/mod.rs:39-43). From then on `selected` returns true because clean-reinstall.json still exists (mod.rs:65). The results: - `--reinstall`: `retained_desired` returns the frozen desired (79-82). `review` skips retirement (retirement/mod.rs:35-38) and reports X as terminal, since it checks only that the journal is Converged, not its plan_sha256 (mod.rs:130-133). - `--apply X`: this reaches `workflow::apply` with the frozen desired and X's own desired_sha256 (mod.rs:278-285). It fails before any effect (workflow/mod.rs:2846-2850). I checked the terminal replay test (repeat_reset/mod.rs:57-61), and it never runs an ordinary review after a reset. I found one accidental escape: if the operator leaves out `--environment`, the selection checks the `local` path (canic-cli/src/fleet/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:23), so the ordinary apply works. That escape is undocumented, and every printed next command includes `--environment` (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:630). Nothing is lost or wrongly changed on-chain. Still, the documented review, apply and reset commands for the Fleet are wedged, so this stays high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this. Nothing in the docs or designs says this behaviour is intended, and the design contradicts it. 0.110-design.md:37 requires that "another clean reset must work afterward". fleet-ensure.md:277-278 and 1640-1641 treat ordinary Ensure as the normal path after a reset. Neither docs/status/current.md nor CHANGELOG.md tracks it as a known limitation. The code trace holds. clean-reinstall.json is kept after completion on purpose. clean_reinstall/terminal/mod.rs:96 reads it for receipt replay, and the PocketIC journey (completed_reset/mod.rs:260-275) replays the infrastructure phase after the Fleet completes. Only a retirement triggered by completed() removes the file (retirement/mod.rs:35-38). An ordinary review after completion gets past every selector (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:60-63, completed_reset, completed_preparation). The prior desired_sha256 is the convergence_digest, so it never matches (workflow/mod.rs:861-865), and write_plan runs unconditionally (workflow/mod.rs:773). completed() then returns None (operation_selection/mod.rs:41-44), so line 65 routes every later ensure to the clean reinstall. That includes --reinstall, because retained_desired returns the frozen desired (79-82) and review returns plan X as terminal (130-133). The CLI's retire_if_selected is never reached (canic-cli fleet/mod.rs:508-511). No test covers ordinary Ensure after a clean reinstall. Impact: if the desired is unchanged, plan X can still be applied through the frozen desired. Any changed desired fails with DriftedBeforeApply, and the next release's reset cannot start. The on-chain state is not harmed and no cycles are lost. The only way out is to delete clean-reinstall.json by hand, which is undocumented. Since this blocks the normal release transition, high is right, not critical. Note on the fix: the alternative recommendation (archive the file at convergence) would break the tested earlier-phase replay. Operation-scoped selection is the fix that fits the design.
Reproduction (reproduced): The test reuses the MockPlatform fixture from the existing fresh_logical_controller test. It models a finished clean reset: ops::clean_reinstall::bind freezes the reset desired in clean-reinstall.json, then workflow::plan/apply converge phase 3 under a stand-in convergence digest. That run is terminal. Before any new plan exists, selected(review) is false, as the finding says. The operator then adds a canister and runs the ordinary workflow::plan with a new desired hash, which writes plan X (1 create). Next the test checks the routing the CLI's run_if_selected would do, with the platform bound to the changed desired (as the CLI does). The review, --apply and --reinstall calls all route to the clean reinstall. With --reinstall, retained_desired returns the frozen reset desired. clean_reinstall::review returns the never-applied plan X with terminal=true. clean_reinstall::apply(X) fails with DriftedBeforeApply and applies nothing. As a control on the same state, ordinary workflow::apply(X, changed desired) returns Ok(true), so the failure comes from the routing, not from the fixture. The finding holds in full: once a plan is written after a completed reset, clean-reinstall.json captures every later Ensure, the changed desired cannot be applied through the routed path, and --reinstall returns the stale plan instead of starting a new reset. The one step not driven here is the actual canic-cli binary. Its routing was reproduced by calling the same host selected/retained_desired/review/apply functions in the order the CLI calls them.

+    let reinstall_selected =

+    let reinstall_desired =

+    } else {

+            &root,
+            &changed,
+            &changed_sha256,
+            &fleet,
+            &plan_x,
+            &mut fixture.platform,
+        )
+        .map(|report| report.terminal)
+    };
+    println!(
+        "--apply X routed_to_clean_reinstall={apply_selected} result={:?}",
+        applied.as_ref().map_err(|error| format!("{error:?}"))
+    );
+    if apply_selected {
+        failures.push("--apply of ordinary plan X is routed to the completed clean reinstall");
+    }
+    if !matches!(applied, Ok(true)) {

+            "control: ordinary workflow::apply(X, changed desired) result={:?}",
+            control.as_ref().map_err(|error| format!("{error:?}"))
+        );
+    }

+    fs::remove_dir_all(&root).expect("remove test directory");
+    assert!(failures.is_empty(), "completed clean reinstall captured later ordinary Ensure: {failures:#?}");

highreproducedr2-activation-endpoint-fences-1 · liveness · high confidence
A root Fleet-state cascade that reaches a committed but still-Prepared Component records a prepared state-snapshot hash that activate_component_runtime rejects as obsolete evidence, so that Component can never be activated
crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:957

Failure scenario

1. The Coordinator sends ProvisionComponents to an Active root. Root commits member partitions one step at a time. 2. Before the publication phase delivers ConfigureRuntime (it waits on a Coordinator round trip), the controller calls RootCommand::SetCyclesFunding(false) or SetFleetStatus. Re-issuing the current value also cascades (the state_cascade PocketIC test replays it). 3. Root sends canic_command SynchronizeState to every partition. Each still-Prepared member stores prepared_state_snapshot_hash = Some(H). 4. Publication then sends ConfigureRuntime. prepare_directory commits DirectoryPrepared, and activate_component_runtime returns InvalidRecord('managed Component runtime retains obsolete cascade or credential evidence'). 5. Every later attempt fails the same way. The republication path sees DirectoryPrepared, and activate_group_member_runtime resends ConfigureRuntime. The provisioning operation, and the Coordinator operation waiting on it, never reach RuntimesActive. No in-product path clears the hash. Recovery needs a reinstall of the member canisters.

Evidence

Root's state fanout targets every Component Registry partition with no status filter: RootStateCascadeTargets::current uses ComponentRegistryOps::root_component_canisters (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/state/mod.rs:44-49; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/mod.rs:1134-1144). Partitions are inserted at registry commit (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:5163-5167). ProvisionComponents commits each member during its Accepted phase (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:1026-1120) but delivers ConfigureRuntime only later, in publication (component_provisioning.rs:783-856). commit_allocation likewise precedes prepare_component_directories (component_registry/mod.rs:2900-2941).

On the target, the Prepared fence admits canic_command (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/fleet_activation.rs:52-58). SynchronizeState skips the Fleet guard and checks only is_parent (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:590, 698-705).

nonroot_cascade_state always computes an activation hash in managed mode (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/cascade/state.rs:47-54, 76-78). prepare_applied_snapshot then sets prepared_state_snapshot_hash on any Prepared record without checking component_runtime (mod.rs:940-972).

activate_component_runtime rejects any record carrying that hash with InvalidRecord (mod.rs:431-441). The only code that clears it is FleetActivationOps::activate (mod.rs:782), which refuses Component runtimes (mod.rs:714). ConfigureRuntime is the sole activation command, and it always reaches that check (role.rs:624-646; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/component_runtime.rs:114-132, 277-298).

Recommendation

In prepare_applied_snapshot, return PreparedFleetActivationSnapshot(None) when record.component_runtime.is_some(). Components use Directory-bound activation, and FleetStateOps::import_input still applies the mode. Also make RootStateCascadeTargets tolerate non-runtime-activated partitions. Add a unit test in ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs: initialize a Component runtime, call record_state_snapshot, prepare the Directory, and assert that activate_component_runtime succeeds.

Verifier (confirmed): The chain holds as described. RootStateCascadeTargets::current (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/state/mod.rs:39-50) adds every Registry partition. root_component_canisters (ops/component_registry/mod.rs:1133-1143) applies no status filter. Partitions are inserted at commit (storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:5163-5167). Directory preparation and ConfigureRuntime come later, as separate awaited steps: commit_allocation versus prepare_component_directories (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:2900-2950), and the provisioning member commit versus publish_component_directory (component_provisioning.rs:1026-1112, 783-856). The trigger is RootCommand SetCyclesFunding or SetFleetStatus. Both are controller-only. They are deliberately exempt from the Fleet guard (root.rs:202, 248-249), take no operation lock, and always cascade (core workflow/state/mod.rs:42-57). On the target, SynchronizeState skips the guard and checks only is_parent (role.rs:590, 698-705). The Prepared fence admits canic_command (policy fleet_activation.rs:52-58). nonroot_cascade_state computes the hash in managed mode (cascade/state.rs:47-54, 77-79). prepare_applied_snapshot stores it without checking component_runtime (mod.rs:940-972), and validate_record_bound/fixture::validate do not reject it (mod.rs:898-910; fixture/mod.rs:24-65). activate_component_runtime then rejects the record (mod.rs:431-441). The field is only cleared in activate (mod.rs:782), which refuses Component runtimes (mod.rs:714-719). Retries fail the same way, because prepare_directory returns the existing, equal directory (mod.rs:299-302). The topology cascade can set prepared_topology_snapshot_hash the same way (topology.rs:40-60). Recovery requires removing and reinstalling the Component, so high is the right severity, not critical.

I traced the full path from the entry point to the harm. 1. **Entry point.** The trigger is a controller calling canic_root_command with SetCyclesFunding or SetFleetStatus. Both are exempt from the Fleet guard (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:202) and need only is_controller (root.rs:248-249). They take no operation lock (root.rs:761-788; crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/state/mod.rs:22-27). The host and CLI never issue them; only PocketIC tests use them. So they are manual operator commands, which fits the rubric's "routine operator action". 2. **Targets.** RootStateCascadeTargets::current adds every Registry partition (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/state/mod.rs:39-50). root_component_canisters applies no phase filter (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_registry/mod.rs:1133-1143). execute_command_to always builds a Fleet-state snapshot and fans it out (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/state/mod.rs:42-57). 3. **The window.** commit_allocation and prepare_component_directories are separate calls (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:2900-2950). ConfigureRuntime is delivered later, during publication (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:783-856). 4. **On the target.** canic_command skips the guard for SynchronizeState and checks only is_parent (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:590, 698-705). The Prepared fence admits canic_command (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/fleet_activation.rs:52-58). In managed mode, nonroot_cascade_state computes the hash (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/cascade/state.rs:47-54, 77-78). prepare_applied_snapshot stores it without checking component_runtime (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:940-972). fixture::validate does not reject it either (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/fixture/mod.rs:24-65). 5. **Harm.** activate_component_runtime rejects the record (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:431-441). A grep finds only one line that clears the hash, mod.rs:782 inside activate, and activate refuses Component runtimes (mod.rs:714-719). configure_with_runtime keeps the prepared Directory when it returns Err (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/component_runtime.rs:118-131), so every retry fails the same way. I found no abort path in component_provisioning.rs. The controller holds authority to reinstall, but it does not intend this wedge. A durable operation that cannot complete matches the rubric's "high" tier. Critical does not fit: the trigger is a race, and removing and reinstalling the Component recovers.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this. It is an unintended interaction between two design changes, not documented behaviour. History: 0.100.26 (docs/changelog/0.100.md:3418-3450) hard-cut cascade activation for Components. Managed Canisters "no longer export the obsolete Fleet cascade/topology" mutations, and Components switched to Directory-bound activation. The rejection in activate_component_runtime (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:431-441) was written to catch that obsolete evidence, on the assumption that Components could no longer receive cascades. Reproduction (reproduced): The test sets up a Prepared managed Component runtime with initialize_nonroot_prepared and an UngroupedOrdinary deployment. It then makes the same two calls that StateCascadeWorkflow::apply_state_with_activation makes in managed mode when a root SynchronizeState cascade reaches a node: prepare_applied_state_snapshot(H) followed by commit_prepared_snapshot. Next it runs the ConfigureRuntime ops sequence: prepare_component_runtime_directory succeeds with DirectoryPrepared, then activate_component_runtime is called twice (once, then as a retry). The test asserts that the first activation transitions to Active. Result: prepare_applied_state_snapshot accepts the Component-runtime record and stores prepared_state_snapshot_hash = Some(H). Both activation attempts return InvalidRecord("managed Component runtime retains obsolete cascade or credential evidence"), and the hash is still present afterwards. So the member is permanently unable to activate; the only code that clears the hash is FleetActivationOps::activate, which rejects Component runtimes. The core defect and the permanent wedge are both confirmed natively. The upstream reachability was checked by reading code, not by running it: - RootStateCascadeTargets::current adds every Registry partition, with no status filter (root_component_canisters). - The Prepared non-root fence admits CANIC_COMMAND updates. The downstream consequence, that provisioning never reaches RuntimesActive, needs PocketIC and was not exercised.

highreproducedr2-host-plan-compiler-1 · cycles · high confidence
Retirement leaves material_threshold + maximum_execution_burn_cycles in the source, but Delete allows at most material_threshold, so every drained retirement or replacement fails at Delete and cannot be replanned
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/policy/mod.rs:1956

Failure scenario

The desired marks an auxiliary canister Absent (or replace=true), with drain.maximum_execution_burn_cycles = 1T and material_cycle_threshold = 1M. The canister holds 10T. The plan transfers 10T - 1.000001T to the treasury, and the drain call burns about 20M. Stop succeeds, and Delete sees about 0.98T > 1M and fails with MaterialCycles on every resume. The journal stays InProgress, so no new plan can be reviewed. Any replan would target a Stopped canister whose drain method cannot run. The Fleet's ensure pipeline stays wedged until the operator starts and drains the canister by hand.

Evidence

append_retirement_actions sets reserved = material_threshold + drain.maximum_execution_burn_cycles and amount = live.cycles - reserved (policy/mod.rs:1913-1924). It then emits Delete { maximum_remaining_cycles: bounds.material_threshold } (1955-1959). apply_transfer asks the drain method for exactly `amount` and rejects any other amount (ops/platform.rs:3365-3384). reconcile_retirement_transfer accepts any source debit in [amount, amount + max_burn] (model/mod.rs:1404-1418), so after the transfer the source holds between material and material + max_burn. Delete refuses when live.cycles > maximum_remaining_cycles (ops/platform.rs:4874-4881). A real drain burns far less than its conservative bound, so Delete fails unless the actual burn exactly equals the bound. retire_plan never adds a Start before Transfer (policy/mod.rs:1858-1964), so a later replan of the now-Stopped canister issues a drain call that a stopped canister rejects. The unit-test mock hides the defect: it deducts exactly amount + maximum_execution_burn_cycles (fleet_ensure/tests.rs:793). The docs describe drain/delete as a maintained lane (docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:328-330).

Recommendation

Let Delete retain the bounded unspent drain reserve: maximum_remaining_cycles = material_threshold + maximum_execution_burn_cycles, which the plan already accounts as burn, so conservation still holds. Alternatively, compute the drain amount at apply time from the live balance minus the threshold. Also emit a Start before Transfer when the retiring source is Stopped, and change the mock so it burns less than the bound.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. The plan sets amount = observed - (material_threshold + maximum_execution_burn_cycles) (policy/mod.rs:1913-1924) and emits Delete { maximum_remaining_cycles: bounds.material_threshold } (1955-1959). Replacement uses the same helper (1579). apply_transfer requires transferred == amount (ops/platform.rs:3375-3384). Reconciliation accepts a source debit anywhere in [amount, amount + max_burn] (model/mod.rs:1411-1413). Delete returns MaterialCycles whenever live.cycles > material_threshold (platform.rs:4874-4881). So Delete passes only if the total burn from the planning observation to the delete observation (drain execution plus idle burn) reaches the full reserve. With a conservative bound, such as the documented 0.1B example (docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:1538) or the 1T values in audit evidence, it essentially never does. The mock hides this in two ways: it burns exactly amount + max_burn (tests.rs:793), and its Delete ignores the bound (tests.rs:662-666). No real drain endpoint exists in the repo, so nothing exercises the lane end to end. On failure, the workflow increments stalled_observations and returns the error (workflow/mod.rs:1776-1795). While the journal is InProgress, plan returns the retained plan and requires the exact desired input (workflow/mod.rs:521-535), so the operator cannot re-review a fix. Two corrections. First, a replan would already fail at plan time with NoSafeDrain, because residual < material + max_burn makes checked_sub underflow (1920-1926); that happens before the missing Start matters. Second, recovery is possible but manual (start, drain by hand, stop) or needs very long idle burn. Cycles stay controlled. So this is high (recovery cannot complete), not critical.

+        .find_map(|action| match action {

highreproducedr2-restart-driver-resumption-2 · liveness · medium confidence
One trap after an await permanently disables retained core timer owners (automatic cycle top-up, placement acknowledgement drain, Root issuer renewal, pool maintenance), because the watchdog recovers only the expired attempt and never re-establishes the stuck registration
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/cycles/mod.rs:135

Failure scenario

A non-root's automatic top-up callback traps after awaiting its parent funding call; for example a stable-memory grow failure or an evidence write traps. The lease stays active. About 5 minutes later the core watchdog runs one top-up attempt and finishes it, and its RetryAfter or ScheduleAt directive is dropped. Every later reconcile_after_transfer or reconcile_schedule on TOPUP_TIMER is silently absorbed. The canister never requests cycles again, drifts below its freezing threshold and is eventually uninstalled. The same happens on Root: prepare_authority_snapshot then fails with RunningClaim until an upgrade. If the stuck top-up had an automatic ICP refill active, Root post_upgrade traps in require_no_resumable_refill_for_upgrade, so no upgrade can clear the heap. Placement acknowledgements likewise stop draining after one recovered batch, leaving Root receipts unreleased.

Evidence

TOPUP_TIMER, ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_TIMER and RENEWAL_TIMER are Retained Once registrations, declared once per heap (cycles/mod.rs:743-754, placement/acknowledgement.rs:263-274, auth/renewal.rs:333-344). Pool maintenance is AfterCompletion (canister_pool/mod.rs:389-411). In ic-timers, dispatch_ordinary runs begin_ordinary (Running) and the callback's first segment in one message, with no Drop guard (runtime/mod.rs:1138-1177). After a trap past an await, the entry stays Running. TimerControl::request_deadline returns no action for Running (control.rs:154-168), and request_ordinary only stores a pending command that is applied at a completion that never comes (registry/mod.rs:913-930). A trap before the first await instead leaves the entry Scheduled with a provider task that ic-cdk-timers already deleted (global_timer.rs, reject-code handling). Earliest-selection ensure_scheduled then cannot replace it; the placement ack's schedule() uses exactly that (acknowledgement.rs:123-133). The recovery watchdog replays only an expired lease: recover_expired_timer spawns run_attempt and discards its TimerRunResult (`let _ = AsyncJobWorkflow::finish(...)`, cycles/mod.rs:135-138; acknowledgement.rs:101-104; renewal.rs:98-101). It never unregisters or re-declares the claim. On Root, the only watchdog belongs to pool maintenance, and it is cancelled on draining or on any non-transport maintenance error (canister_pool/mod.rs:139-145, 436-443). require_root_resumable rejects a Running claim (timer/mod.rs:479-481).

Recommendation

When the watchdog recovers an expired lease, apply the recovered TimerRunResult directive. Also detect a claim that is Running or dead-Scheduled with no live attempt, and unregister and re-declare it (or re-register under a fresh identity) before reconciling. Alternatively, move these owners to the Watchdog-plus-spawn pattern the fixture importer already uses. Give Root a core-owned watchdog that is independent of pool maintenance, and use reconcile_schedule (Exact) rather than ensure_scheduled for re-arming. Add a PocketIC test that traps the top-up callback after its first await and asserts that top-up resumes.

Verifier (confirmed): The core claim holds. In ic-timers 0.8.0, dispatch_ordinary (runtime/mod.rs:1138-1177) runs begin_ordinary (Running) and the callback's first segment in one message, and has no Drop guard. After a trap past an await, ic-cdk's cleanup (ic-cdk call.rs:1003-1037) cancels the task, so complete_ordinary never runs and the entry stays Running for the rest of that heap's life. request_ordinary (registry/mod.rs:913-930) only records a `pending` command for a Running entry and applies no action. cancel and unregister are also deferred (1064-1068, 1129-1175). The ic-timers README states that Once and AfterCompletion get "No automatic recovery". Canic's recover_expired_timer (cycles/mod.rs:123-139, acknowledgement.rs:88-105, renewal.rs:76-98, pool spawn_maintenance) finishes the leased attempt and throws away its directive. Nothing detects or re-declares the stuck claim, and no test covers this path (timer_authority.rs traps only the application watchdog). After that, reconcile_after_transfer, start() and schedule_if_pending are silently absorbed. On Root, require_root_resumable fails with RunningClaim (timer/mod.rs:479). If a resumable refill exists, it can resume only through the top-up timer (automatic.rs:58), and post_upgrade rejects the upgrade (runtime/root.rs:113). Corrections: the trap-before-await 'dead-Scheduled' case is recovered by Exact reconcile (start() through cascade or lifecycle). Only the Earliest paths (ensure_scheduled, KeepEarlier) are stuck. On non-root, an upgrade clears the stuck state. Likelihood depends on a trap after an await (resource or memory-grow failure, which is most likely when cycles are low), so it is not attacker-triggered.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): Not refuted. The trigger is the canister's own timer, so no caller authority is needed. An ordinary resource failure is enough; an attacker cannot cause it. Path: the TOPUP_TIMER callback (cycles/mod.rs:743-754) runs run_registered. That calls AsyncJobWorkflow::claim (a stable lease), then run_topup, which awaits request_parent_funding (cycles/mod.rs:617). In ic-timers 0.8.0, dispatch_ordinary (runtime/mod.rs:1138-1177) marks the entry Running in that first message. The only way out of Running is complete_ordinary, and there is no Drop guard (grep shows no `impl Drop` in ic-timers). If the response callback traps, for example when a stable write in CycleTopupEventOps::record_* or record_observation fails to grow memory, ic-cdk cleanup cancels the task (ic-cdk call.rs:1033-1036). Running stays committed. request_deadline returns None for Running (control.rs:154-168), and request_ordinary only stores a pending command (registry/mod.rs:913-930). declare_timer returns early because custody already exists (cycles/mod.rs:743-746). So every later reconcile is absorbed. The watchdog recovers only the lease. recover_expired_timer spawns one attempt and discards its directive (cycles/mod.rs:135-138). After finish, has_expired_attempt is false (async_job/mod.rs:29-31), and nothing reschedules. The runtime README (docs/features/runtime/README.md:85-99) says the watchdog "supplies liveness" for these recovery-critical owners. This path breaks that contract. Root: recovery goes through pool maintenance (canister_pool/mod.rs:319-321). A remaining Running claim blocks require_root_resumable (timer/mod.rs:479-480). An automatic refill resumes only through this timer (automatic.rs:58-78), and the manual path cannot take it over (manual.rs:51-78). A resumable refill also makes Root post_upgrade fail (root.rs:113). The trap is uncommon but tends to happen when cycles are low, which is exactly when top-up is needed. On non-root, an upgrade clears it. I would still keep this at high as a recovery path that cannot complete.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I found nothing showing this behaviour is intended, and the project's own docs treat the same failure mode as a defect. docs/status/current.md:6341 says "An ordinary once timer stranded work after a trap; the watchdog correction passes that same recovery journey." docs/audits/reports/2026-09/2026-09-11/canic165-consumer.md:21-24 says the same. That fix was applied only to the fixture importer (docs/features/build-and-evidence/fixture-artifacts.md:240-242). The core owners kept the Once/AfterCompletion registrations plus a lease-only watchdog. docs/operations/recovery-retry-runbooks.md:255-258 names exactly these four owners and this scenario ("after an inter-canister continuation traps"). It tells operators to "Allow the retained recovery watchdog to advance", which implies recovery completes. It never warns that the native claim then stays Running and scheduling ends. The code confirms the mechanism: - ic-timers-0.8.0 dispatch_ordinary (runtime/mod.rs:1138-1177) has no guard. The README (line 60) says Once gets "No automatic recovery". - request_deadline returns None for a Running entry (control.rs:154-168). - The core recovery code drops the recovered directive (cycles/mod.rs:135-138, acknowledgement.rs:101-104, pool spawn_maintenance canister_pool/mod.rs:421-425). - Every re-arm path goes through the same stuck registration: start() from cascade/state.rs:113, reconcile_after_transfer from nonroot_cycles.rs:427, and schedule(). The fix does not contradict the design. The 0.104 design says the watchdog must not reschedule *healthy* callbacks, and this callback is not healthy. The recommended Watchdog-plus-spawn pattern is the one maintainers already adopted for the importer. On impact: automatic top-up stops for the rest of the heap, so a canister can drift toward freezing. Placement acknowledgements stop draining. require_root_resumable fails with RunningClaim (timer/mod.rs:479). Upgrading non-root clears the stuck state, so this is not critical. The Root upgrade wedge (runtime/mod.rs:152-162) needs a second condition: the single recovered refill attempt must also fail transiently. It is not attacker-triggerable, but the runbook treats traps after awaits as an expected operational event. High is appropriate.
Reproduction (partially reproduced): canic-core cannot drive ic-timers natively: its non-test platform calls ic0, which panics off-wasm, and recover_expired_timer needs ic_cdk spawn plus a parent call. So I copied ic-timers 0.8.0 byte-for-byte into repro-vendor/ and pointed the workspace at it with a [patch.crates-io] entry. That makes its cfg(test) fake platform usable, and the test drives the real runtime on it. Test 1 sets up a Retained Once registration the way CycleWorkflow::declare_timer does, arms it, and dispatches it. The first callback suspends at an await. I then drop the suspended task, which is what ic-cdk's cleanup does after a trapped response callback. After that it calls the only re-arms Canic makes, reconcile_schedule(At(100)) and ensure_scheduled(At(100)). Both return Ok, but the claim stays Running and no provider task exists. A later wake-up never dispatches (calls=1), so the test fails. Test 2 deletes the provider task before the first await. It confirms that Earliest ensure_scheduled cannot replace the dead Scheduled entry. By code reading, all four recover_expired_timer owners use `let _ = AsyncJobWorkflow::finish(...)` and never touch the registration. That confirms the watchdog discards the directive and never re-declares the claim. Not exercised: Canic's own watchdog code, and the end effects (no further top-up, Root RunningClaim, post_upgrade trap). Those need PocketIC.

+//! Repro for finding r2-restart-driver-resumption-2.
+//!
+//! Canic's retained `Once` owners (automatic cycle top-up, placement
+//! acknowledgement drain, Root issuer renewal) keep one `OnceRegistration`
+//! in custody for the life of the heap and only ever re-arm it through
+//! `reconcile_schedule` (Exact, e.g. `CycleWorkflow::start`) or
+//! `ensure_scheduled` (Earliest, e.g. `reconcile_after_transfer`). Their
+//! recovery watchdog replays an expired business lease out-of-band and never
+//! touches the registration. These tests drive the real ic-timers runtime on
+//! its fake platform and model an IC trap exactly: the committed first
+//! message leaves whatever registry state it wrote, and the provider task is
+//! dropped without being polled again (ic-cdk cleanup after a trapped
+//! response callback, or ic-cdk-timers deleting a trapped self-call task).
+
+use super::*;
+use crate::platform::{discard_next_due, run_next_due, set_time, timer_count};
+use std::{cell::Cell, rc::Rc};
+
+fn identity(name: &str) -> TimerIdentity {
+    TimerIdentity::try_new("canic", "cycles", name).expect("fixture identity should be valid")
+}
+
+fn describe(timer: &TimerIdentity) -> String {
+    let snapshot = timer_snapshot(timer)
+        .expect("snapshot lookup should succeed")
+        .expect("retained declaration should exist");
+    format!(
+        "registration_status={:?} state={:?} next_deadline_ns={:?} work_started={} work_completed={} provider_tasks={}",
+        snapshot.registration_status(),
+        snapshot.state(),
+        snapshot.next_deadline_ns(),
+        snapshot.observability().counters().work_started(),
+        snapshot.observability().counters().work_completed(),
+        timer_count(),
+    )
+}
+
+/// Trap after the first await: the retained Once claim stays `Running`
+/// forever and every later Canic re-arm request is silently absorbed.
+#[test]
+fn repro_retained_once_trapped_after_await_is_never_rearmed() {
+    reset_for_test(10, 7);
+    initialize_runtime().expect("runtime initialization should succeed");
+    let timer = identity("topup");
+    let calls = Rc::new(Cell::new(0_u64));
+    let callback_calls = Rc::clone(&calls);
+
+    // Same shape as CycleWorkflow::declare_timer: Retained Once custody.
+    let registration = register_once(
+        timer.clone(),
+        DeclarationLifetime::Retained,
+        move |_context: OnceContext| {
+            let call = callback_calls.get() + 1;
+            callback_calls.set(call);
+            async move {
+                if call == 1 {
+                    // First segment commits (entry is Running), then the task
+                    // waits on the parent funding response that later traps.
+                    std::future::pending::<()>().await;
+                }
+                TimerRunResult::new(TimerCompletion::success(1), TimerDirective::Stop)
+            }
+        },
+    )
+    .expect("registration should succeed");
+
+    registration
+        .reconcile_schedule(Some(TimerSchedule::At(20)))
+        .expect("initial exact reconcile should arm");
+    set_time(20);
+    assert!(run_next_due(), "first top-up callback should dispatch");
+    println!("after first segment (awaiting parent): {}", describe(&timer));
+
+    // The response callback traps; ic-cdk cancels (drops) the task, so
+    // `complete_ordinary` never runs.
+    assert!(discard_next_due(), "the suspended task should be dropped");
+    println!("after trap past await:                 {}", describe(&timer));
+
+    // Watchdog recovery (recover_expired_timer) finishes only the lease and
+    // discards its directive; afterwards Canic re-arms only through these.
+    let exact = registration.reconcile_schedule(Some(TimerSchedule::At(100)));
+    let earliest = registration.ensure_scheduled(TimerSchedule::At(100));
+    println!("reconcile_schedule(At(100)) -> {exact:?}; ensure_scheduled(At(100)) -> {earliest:?}");
+    println!("after Canic re-arm requests:           {}", describe(&timer));
+
+    set_time(1_000_000_000);
+    let dispatched = run_next_due();
+    println!(
+        "later wake-up dispatched={dispatched} total_callback_calls={} {}",
+        calls.get(),
+        describe(&timer)
+    );
+
+    assert!(
+        dispatched && calls.get() == 2,
+        "retained Once top-up claim must resume after a trap past its first await \
+         (dispatched={dispatched}, calls={}, {})",
+        calls.get(),
+        describe(&timer)
+    );
+}
+
+/// Trap before the first await: the claim stays `Scheduled` on a provider
+/// task that no longer exists. Earliest-selection `ensure_scheduled` (used by
+/// `reconcile_after_transfer` and the placement acknowledgement `schedule`)
+/// cannot replace it; only an Exact reconcile with a different deadline can.
+#[test]
+fn repro_retained_once_trapped_before_await_absorbs_earliest_ensure() {
+    reset_for_test(10, 7);
+    initialize_runtime().expect("runtime initialization should succeed");
+    let timer = identity("topup-dead-scheduled");
+    let calls = Rc::new(Cell::new(0_u64));
+    let callback_calls = Rc::clone(&calls);
+    let registration = register_once(
+        timer.clone(),
+        DeclarationLifetime::Retained,
+        move |_context: OnceContext| {
+            callback_calls.set(callback_calls.get() + 1);
+            async { TimerRunResult::new(TimerCompletion::success(1), TimerDirective::Stop) }
+        },
+    )
+    .expect("registration should succeed");
+
+    registration
+        .ensure_scheduled(TimerSchedule::At(20))
+        .expect("initial ensure should arm");
+    set_time(20);
+    // The whole callback message traps and rolls back; the provider has
+    // already deleted its task.
+    assert!(discard_next_due(), "the trapped provider task should be deleted");
+    println!("after trap before await: {}", describe(&timer));
+
+    let earliest = registration.ensure_scheduled(TimerSchedule::At(50));
+    println!("ensure_scheduled(At(50)) -> {earliest:?}; {}", describe(&timer));
+    set_time(1_000_000_000);
+    let dispatched = run_next_due();
+    println!(
+        "later wake-up dispatched={dispatched} total_callback_calls={} {}",
+        calls.get(),
+        describe(&timer)
+    );
+
+    assert!(
+        dispatched && calls.get() == 1,
+        "an Earliest re-arm of a dead Scheduled claim must produce a live wake-up \
+         (dispatched={dispatched}, calls={}, {})",
+        calls.get(),
+        describe(&timer)
+    );
+}

canic-host, and therefore the canic CLI, does not compile on macOS: durable_io passes a u32 file mode where rustix expects the platform mode_t, which is u16 on Darwin
crates/canic-host/src/durable_io/mod.rs:619

Failure scenario

An operator on macOS follows INSTALLING.md and runs `cargo install --locked canic-cli --version <version>`, or a contributor runs any cargo command that builds canic-host. Compilation stops with E0308 (expected u16, found u32) at durable_io/mod.rs:619. On macOS the operator CLI cannot be built, and neither can canic-host, canic-testing-internal or canic-tests.

Evidence

create_sibling_temp takes `permissions: u32` (durable_io/mod.rs:605) and calls `Mode::from_raw_mode(permissions)` (mod.rs:619). In rustix 1.1.5, from_raw_mode takes RawMode, which is libc mode_t: u32 on Linux but u16 on macOS. The module is written to support Apple targets (cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android", target_vendor = "apple")) at mod.rs:115). Every CI job runs on ubuntu-24.04 (.github/workflows/ci.yml, security.yml), so nothing builds canic-host on macOS. git log -L dates the current form of these lines to 0.110.22.

Recommendation

Type the parameter as rustix::fs::Mode, or pass Mode::from_raw_mode(0o600) and Mode::from_raw_mode(0o666) literals, so the platform width is inferred. Add a macOS job to CI, at least `cargo check -p canic-cli --locked`, so platform-dependent libc types compile on every supported host OS.

Verifier (confirmed): Found while preparing the reproduction worktrees. The unmodified commit fails to compile canic-host on this Mac (Darwin 25.6.0, rustc 1.98.1, rustix 1.1.5). The one-line cast `permissions as _` fixes it, and every host and CLI reproduction in this review had to carry that change.
Reproduction (reproduced): On the unmodified commit, building canic-host on macOS fails with the type error below. With the one-line cast applied, canic-host, canic-cli and canic compile, and every host and CLI reproduction in this review ran with it.
$ cargo test -p canic-host --lib --no-run   (unmodified 06d73694d, macOS 26 / Darwin 25.6.0, rustc 1.98.1, rustix 1.1.5)
error[E0308]: mismatched types
   --> crates/canic-host/src/durable_io/mod.rs:619:37
    |
619 |                 Mode::from_raw_mode(permissions),
    |                 ------------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `u16`, found `u32`
note: associated function defined here
   --> rustix-1.1.5/src/backend/libc/fs/types.rs:197:18
    |     pub const fn from_raw_mode(st_mode: RawMode) -> Self {

Transport failures (PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE) are classified as permanent by the cycle top-up, pool maintenance, auth renewal and placement-ack retry classifiers, so one transient reject permanently stops those background workers
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/cycles/mod.rs:966

Failure scenario

A non-root child's timer calls its parent for cycles while the parent is briefly stopped or frozen, or while its input queue is full (SYS_TRANSIENT). The error is PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE, the top-up returns Stop plus InvariantFailure, and nothing re-arms it. The child drains to its freezing threshold and eventually loses its state. The same happens on Root. Root's bounded-wait RequestRootFunding to the Coordinator times out (fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:106-111), so Root's funding stops. The Coordinator's unresolved `current` grant then blocks its policy rotation and authority snapshots (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:231-242, funding_rotation.rs:204). One rejected management or Cycles Ledger call permanently disables pool maintenance. One issuer reject stops delegation-proof renewal until proofs expire. Unacknowledged placement receipts accumulate toward the 512 per-caller and 10k global replay caps (ops/replay/mod.rs:98-117).

Evidence

Every local call failure (CallRejected, CallPerformFailed, SYS_UNKNOWN) maps to `InternalError::public(PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE)` (crates/canic-core/src/infra/mod.rs:18-21, through ops/ic/call.rs:136-146). Decoded remote errors get internal code PLATFORM_FAILED (crates/canic-core/src/error.rs:66-72). The classifiers compare `err.code()` against PLATFORM_FAILED and STATE_FAILED only:
- top-up: cycles/mod.rs:966-970, which stops at 582-609;
- pool: canister_pool/mod.rs:492-500, where InvariantFailure sets MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=false and cancels the timers at 439-451;
- renewal: auth/renewal.rs:391-398, which stops at 242-247, with the transport cause kept at provisioning/mod.rs:263-265;
- placement ack: placement/acknowledgement.rs:278-281, which stops at 205-219 and 146-157.
The tests use `InternalError::platform_failure()` as the transport stand-in (cycles/mod.rs:1011-1023, acknowledgement.rs:312-319, provisioning/mod.rs:425-428), so this path is never exercised. The bootstrap classifier gets it right (lifecycle/mod.rs:37-49). Top-up is re-armed only by lifecycle start or a fleet-state cascade (workflow/runtime/mod.rs:68, cascade/state.rs:112).

Recommendation

Build one shared classifier that treats PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE and PLATFORM_INSUFFICIENT_LIQUID_CYCLES as retryable with backoff. Better still, classify on the typed IcInfraError (reject code SysTransient, SysUnknown, CanisterError or perform failure) before it is flattened. Do not treat an observed remote error as transport. Add tests that build the real transport error through `IcInfraError::CallFailed(...).into()` instead of platform_failure().

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. A failed `call.await` becomes IcInfraError::CallFailed (infra/ic/call.rs:139) and then public(PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE) (infra/mod.rs:18-21) through ops/mod.rs:103. That covers a reject, a SysUnknown timeout, a stopped or stopping target, or a perform failure. Only a decoded remote Err becomes PLATFORM_FAILED (error.rs:69-72, rpc/mod.rs:52-56). None of the four classifiers accepts PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE: - Top-up: cycles/mod.rs:966-970, then Stop at 603-609. The Root bounded-wait call (fleet_coordinator_client:106-111) is affected the same way. - Renewal: renewal.rs:391-398 and 242-247. Transport keeps cause.code() at provisioning/mod.rs:276-278. - Pool: canister_pool/mod.rs:492-500. CyclesLedgerOps::fee and balance_of pass CallFailed through unchanged (ops/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:75-77). InvariantFailure clears MAINTENANCE_ENABLED and cancels both the maintenance timer and the recovery watchdog (443-451). Only lifecycle or activation calls start() again. - Ack: acknowledgement.rs:278-281, then Stop at 146-157. The docs do not say this is intended, and the test named only_transport_and_in_flight_funding_failures_retry shows transport was meant to retry. A child's top-up is re-armed only by lifecycle or a fleet-state cascade (cascade/state.rs:113). reconcile_after_transfer re-arms the parent's own timer, not the child's. So a routine parent upgrade that coincides with the child's timer (a stopping or stopped reject) is enough to trigger this. Corrections: - The placement-ack stall is not permanent. The next placement allocation re-arms it (allocation.rs:219). - Renewal is re-armed by an operator template or policy upsert. - The cycles test at 1011-1023 does not use platform_failure(). It simply never covers transport.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. Every step from the entry point to the harm checks out in the code. Entry point: the child's top-up timer runs `run_registered` and then `run_topup` (cycles/mod.rs:212, 236). When the balance is below threshold it calls `request_parent_funding` (mod.rs:313), which reaches `RpcOps::call_rpc_result` via `CallOps::unbounded_wait(...).execute().await?` (ops/rpc/mod.rs:118-121). A reject becomes `IcInfraError::CallFailed` (infra/ic/call.rs:139), then `public(PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE)` (infra/mod.rs:21). The rejects that qualify are: parent stopped or stopping, parent frozen, a trap in the parent, or `SysTransient`. `is_retryable_funding_error` (mod.rs:966-970) accepts only PLATFORM_FAILED, STATE_FAILED and STATE_CONFLICT. So `finish_funding_failure` returns Stop (mod.rs:603-609) and records a Terminal disposition (mod.rs:560-564). The only re-arms are lifecycle start (runtime/mod.rs:68), a fleet-state cascade (cascade/state.rs:113), and on Root a SetCyclesFundingEnabled toggle (control-plane state/mod.rs:105-118). `reconcile_after_transfer` re-arms the parent's own timer, not the child's (nonroot_cycles.rs:427). No attacker is needed. The trigger is an ordinary failure or a routine operator action. A Member-scope backup of the parent stops it (backup/plan/build/phases.rs:33-60). The stop order is top-down and the restart order is bottom-up, so children keep running while their parent is stopped. A child that asks for cycles in that window loses automatic funding permanently. There is also a cascade: a parent that is itself frozen for lack of cycles permanently stops every child that asks it for funding in that window. Those children never resume after the parent is refilled. Root works the same way. Its bounded-wait call to the Coordinator (fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:106-111) turns a timeout into PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE, and that also leads to Stop. Pool maintenance is also confirmed (canister_pool/mod.rs:447-450, 492-500), and so is renewal (renewal.rs:391-398, where PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE matches none of the accepted codes). Recovery paths exist (upgrade, cascade, toggle), so this is not critical. Still, a single transient reject silently disables cycle funding, which is the fleet's safety net, and can leave canisters frozen. That fits high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this. The behaviour is not intended, and git history shows how it happened. Before 0.102.2, `is_retryable_funding_error` retried any error of class `Infra | Ops` (git show 439da1c8e and 0ec1bdb7f^, cycles/mod.rs:342-349). Commit 0ec1bdb7f (0.102.2) did two things together: - it rewrote the classifier as `code()==PLATFORM_FAILED || STATE_FAILED` (cycles/mod.rs:966-970); - it mapped `IcInfraError::CallFailed` to PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE (infra/mod.rs:18-21). That dropped transport from the retry set. It looks like a mechanical hard-cut slip, not a design choice. The test name `only_transport_and_in_flight_funding_failures_retry` (cycles/mod.rs:1011) shows the intent was to retry transport, but the test never builds a transport error. The renewal test uses `platform_failure()` as its transport stand-in (provisioning/mod.rs:425-428). The lifecycle classifier does list PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE (lifecycle/mod.rs:37-49), so the authors know the code. No document supports stopping here: - docs/features/runtime/README.md:80-83 lists top-up, renewal, acknowledgement and pool as "recovery-critical owners". - docs/status/current.md:6725-6727 treats a sampling timer that "permanently stopped" on a rejection as a defect that needed fixing. - AGENTS.md requires lost-response reconciliation. I confirmed the path end to end. The failed call goes through `CallOps::execute` (ops/ic/call.rs:136-146) and `call_rpc_result` (ops/rpc/mod.rs:118-121). It then hits `finish_funding_failure`, which stops the timer (cycles/mod.rs:603-608). The watchdog only recovers expired leases (timer/mod.rs:237-253), not stopped workers. Root's bounded-wait `request_root_funding` (fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:104-111) turns a SysUnknown lost response into a stop. That is a lost-response reconciliation that never completes. "Permanent" overstates it. Lifecycle start, a fleet command that reconciles funding (workflow/state/mod.rs:51), the cascade (cascade/state.rs:113), root policy rotation (root_funding/mod.rs:99,112,160) and the next allocation all re-arm it. None of these is automatic, though. A child whose top-up has stopped can silently drain to freezing. High still fits the rubric: "retries lost; recovery that cannot complete".
Reproduction (partially reproduced): In canic-core, the tests build the real transport error the way CallOps::execute builds it: InternalError::from(OpsError::from(IcInfraError::from(CallFailed::CallRejected(CallRejected::with_rejection(code, msg))))). They cover SysTransient (2), CanisterError (5), SysUnknown (6) and CallPerformFailed. Each one comes out as code E66 (PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE). - Top-up: CycleWorkflow::finish_funding_failure returns InvariantFailure/Stop for all four transport classes. - Renewal: RootIssuerRenewalWorkflow::failed_result, given the Transport projection that into_renewal_error uses, returns InvariantFailure/Stop. - Placement ack: is_retryable_root_failure returns false on the real transport error, so drain_batch returns Err and run_scheduled stops. - Pool (canic-control-plane): IcInfraError is crate-private there, so the test uses InternalError::public(PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE), which the canic-core From impl produces for CallFailed. maintenance_timer_result and timer_result_completion both give InvariantFailure, the completion that makes finish_maintenance_timer set MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=false and cancel the timers. Every test asserts retry or non-Stop, and every one fails. So the core defect holds in all four classifiers. Not exercised natively: that nothing re-arms the stopped timers, and the downstream harm (a child draining to its freezing threshold, receipts building up toward the replay caps). Those need PocketIC with the real timer registry. The verifier also noted that placement-ack is re-armed by the next allocation and renewal by a template or policy upsert, so those two are not strictly permanent.

highreproducedxc-cycles-1 · cycles · high confidence
Retirement and deletion intents freeze an observed balance and fail with a conflict forever when anyone deposits cycles or ledger credit, with no path to reclaim or sweep again
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs:1006

Failure scenario

The operator starts retiring a root. The root's delete_store records the Store deletion intent and reclaims cycles. An attacker who knows the public Store principal calls deposit_cycles(store) with 1B attached cycles, which is more than the Store's idle burn since reclamation. Every later delete_store retry fails in require_store_deletion_authority, and reclamation cannot run again, so retirement is stuck permanently. The same thing happens if the attacker makes a 1-cycle icrc1_transfer (paying about 100M cycles in fees) to the root's Cycles Ledger account after begin_root_ledger_transfer: every prepare_deletion retry resends the same transfer, gets Duplicate, and fails require_empty_source. The only recovery left is a destructive reset.

Evidence

Four retirement paths record a balance once and later treat any increase as a hard failure:
- Store deletion: the intent is reused without a fresh observation (fleet_subnet_root.rs:884-897). Reclamation fails with InvalidState when the live balance exceeds observed_cycles_before_reclamation (gc.rs:538-543) and refuses to run again once it is durable (gc.rs:519-526). Stop and delete require status.cycles <= observed_cycles_after_reclamation, otherwise "balance increased after cycle reclamation" (gc.rs:1003-1010, called at 1024, 1037, 1057, 1071).
- Root deletion: reclaim_root_deletion_cycles returns conflict if current_cycles > observed_cycles_before_reclamation (fleet_subnet_root.rs:1526), and that value is captured once at line 994.
- Root Cycles Ledger evacuation: the transfer intent is immutable (root_retirement.rs:1486-1492), and require_empty_source demands an exact zero balance on every retry, including after the receipt exists (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:24-26, 78, 82-88).
- Coordinator fleet retirement: the same exact-zero check applies (fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:88-94).

Anyone can deposit to these targets: management deposit_cycles has no caller restriction, and any account can make an ICRC-1 transfer to the root or Coordinator. The host code acknowledges this openness ("Native balances are open to third-party deposits", host workflow/mod.rs:3696; see also 3546).

Recommendation

Treat a later increase as work to sweep, not as a conflict: - Allow repeated, bounded reclamation passes that each record their own receipt; do not forbid re-running once durable. - For ledger accounts, after the recorded transfer is confirmed, allow a new sweep intent (fresh created_at_time, memo derived from operation_id plus a pass index) for any remainder above the fee, and treat a remainder at or below the fee as a reviewed terminal discard. - Compare the pre-stop and pre-delete native balance against the reserve target, not against the last observation. - Add PocketIC tests that deposit to the Store, the root, and the root's ledger account between steps.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed, with corrections. Store path: on retry, delete_store reuses the stored intent without a fresh observation (fleet_subnet_root.rs:884-897). Reclamation fails if the balance is above the frozen observation (gc.rs:538-543) and refuses to run again once durable (gc.rs:519-526). Stop and delete fail if the balance is above observed_after (gc.rs:1003-1010). Root native path: the balance is captured once (fleet_subnet_root.rs:994), and reclaim returns conflict on any increase (1526-1527). Ledger paths: intents cannot change (root_retirement.rs:1478-1484; coordinator ops/retirement/mod.rs:61-63). An exact zero balance is required after a transfer or a Duplicate (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:24-26, 78, 82-89; coordinator workflow/retirement/mod.rs:88-94). Management deposit_cycles, Cycles Ledger withdraw and ICRC-1 transfers are open to anyone. Neither a fresh sweep nor an abandon path exists, and no test deposits between steps. Docs (fleet-ensure.md:326-330) say fail-closed is intended but promise that a late donation 'may require another drain or review'; no such path is implemented, so recovery within the same operation cannot complete. Corrections: (1) Native-balance wedges are not strictly permanent. They clear once idle or execution burn eats the donation, but a cheap large deposit keeps them stuck for as long as the attacker likes. Ledger balances never decay, so those wedges are permanent. (2) The Coordinator returns early once its receipt exists (workflow/retirement/mod.rs:31-33). Its window is therefore the retirement call plus any retries after a failure. The root ledger window is wider, because every prepare_deletion retry calls evacuate (1003) before the Coordinator handshake. (3) Cycles are not lost, since they stay in controlled canisters. The harm is that recovery cannot complete, so high rather than critical.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. Here is the path I traced. An authorized caller accepts removal through the RemoveRoot endpoint (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:64). The private timer in workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:559-566 then drives it and retries every second on Err, forever. Because every retry re-reads the frozen values, a failure never self-heals within the operation. The actor who causes the wedge needs no Canic authority, only cycles and a public canister ID. Management deposit_cycles and ICRC-1 transfers to any account are open to anyone. The operator's own auto top-up service (CycleOps style) reaching a freshly drained Store also works, so this is an ordinary path, not only an attack. - Store: once reclamation is durable, it cannot run again (gc.rs:519-526). Stop and delete fail if the balance is above observed_after (gc.rs:1003-1010). delete_store reuses the intent (fleet_subnet_root.rs:884-897). About 1T cycles (roughly $1.35) exceeds a small Store's idle burn for years. - Root ledger: this is worse than reported. No timing window is needed. A 1-cycle transfer to the root's account at any point before evacuation leaves balance_before of 1, which is at or below the fee. The transfer then fails with InvalidTransfer (infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:205-213), which maps to invariant (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:61-64). The intent can never change (root_retirement.rs:1486-1492), so the wedge is permanent. A deposit after the intent exists hits require_empty_source instead (mod.rs:78, 82-88). The Coordinator path is the same (fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:37-51, 88-94). - Root native: the balance is captured once (fleet_subnet_root.rs:994), and reclaim returns a conflict on any increase (1526). Internal funding is fenced (fleet_subnet_root.rs:641-649), so these external deposits are the only trigger. The docs promise "another drain or review" (fleet-ensure.md:326-330), but no such path exists. The only way out is a destructive reset, so same-operation recovery cannot complete. That is high; it is not critical because a reset path exists and the cycles stay controlled.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): Not refuted. Refusing to continue when a balance goes up is intended. The docs require that "destructive drain/delete steps still require their reviewed residual limits" (docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:326-330), and the donation follow-up leaves deletion safeguards unchanged (docs/status/current.md:3613-3617; docs/design/0.110-fleet-runtime-contraction/status.md:1167-1181). But the same docs promise that "a late donation may require another drain or review", and no such path exists: - Store reclamation cannot run again once it is durable (gc.rs:519-526). - Stop and delete compare the balance with the frozen observed_after value (gc.rs:1003-1010). - The root's native baseline is captured once (fleet_subnet_root.rs:994) and checked at 1526-1527. - Ledger transfer intents cannot change (root_retirement.rs:1486-1492). - The Coordinator requires an exact zero balance (fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:88-94). - Only one draining operation_id is accepted (root_retirement.rs:1471-1473), so no fresh operation can replace a stuck one. AGENTS.md accepts a reviewed terminal residual discard, and nothing in the code implements one. The recommended fix follows the documented intent rather than contradicting it. The impact is if anything understated. CyclesLedgerInfra::transfer rejects any balance between 1 and the fee (crates/canic-core/src/infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:205-214), and the retained intent keeps that balance. So one dust credit to the root's or the Coordinator's ledger account, sent at any time before evacuation, wedges evacuation permanently. The attacker pays about 100M cycles in ledger fees. This is not critical. Cycles stay controlled, so conservation holds, and an explicit pre-1.0 reinstall or reset is still available. Whole-Fleet deletion is also described as an optional follow-up (status.md:2813-2814). Still, same-operation recovery cannot complete, and the rubric rates that high.
Reproduction (partially reproduced): The Store deletion path is confirmed. The other three paths are not. Setup: the test builds the terminal publication state and a single Store inventory. It gets the deletion cycle authority from production `store_deletion_cycle_authority` on a 2T-cycle status: retained target 330B. It then builds a durable intent with observed_after = 180B, the Store-side target. `validate_store_deletion_intent_lineage` accepts this fixture. Control: with no deposit, `require_store_deletion_authority` returns Ok. After a 1B third-party deposit, the Store holds 181B, still well under the 330B durable target. Two results: - `require_store_deletion_authority` returns an InvalidState error (E137). This check guards both stop and delete. - Polling `reclaim_single_finalized_root_store_cycles` again on the durable intent returns E137 at once, before any IC call. The lineage and the guard pass, so the error comes from the "already durable" refusal. So the test shows no way forward: stop/delete is refused and no second sweep is allowed. `fleet_subnet_root::delete_store` also skips reclamation once observed_after is set. The claim holds for the cited gc.rs:1006 path. Not exercised: the root native reclaim, the root Cycles Ledger `require_empty_source` and the Coordinator zero-balance check. All three need async IC or ledger calls, so they need PocketIC. Also not shown: whether the wedge is permanent, since idle burn can eventually eat the deposit on native balances. Test-enablement change: I re-exported CanisterSettingsSnapshot, MemoryMetricsSnapshot, QueryStatsSnapshot and LogVisibility from `canic_core::control_plane_support::ops::ic::mgmt`. Without them a CanisterStatus fixture cannot be built. This does not change behaviour.

After 300 s, two requests for K (user retries, or recover_entry racing resolve_or_create) both classify Resumable and send recover calls with the same operation. 3. Root commits B's allocation. C's request is handled after that commit, gets the same pid P, and its reply reaches the parent after B's. 4. B binds K to P. C sees Bound, calls recycle_canister(P), and root removes P's subtree. K now resolves forever to the destroyed canister P, whose application state is lost, and no API unbinds it.

Evidence

finalize_created_instance treats any failure of set_provisional_pid_if_claim_matches as 'claim lost' and recycles the pid through root (create.rs:45-55). The ops function returns Ok(false) for a Bound entry without comparing the bound pid (ops/storage/placement/index/mod.rs:230-238). Once a claim is older than PENDING_TTL_SECS with no provisional pid, any caller classifies it as Resumable (classification.rs:63-72). Both resolve_or_create and recover_entry then call resume_pending_instance, which runs recover_child and create_child on the same claim (create.rs:138-159). Each concurrent resumer gets an ExistingPending permit (allocation.rs:276-279), and root returns the same pid for the same operation id: a cached DuplicateSame receipt, or a re-execution against the existing allocation. The first callback binds the key and commits (create.rs:57-75). The second callback sees Bound, and recycle_abandoned_child passes its only guard, contains_pid (cleanup.rs:78-91), so root starts subtree removal of the bound child. Root does not know the parent's index binding (control-plane begin_subtree_removal only checks that the parent matches). The following finish_disposed_child fails with ReceiptBackedEvidenceConflict (ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:1083-1092), but the recycle has already happened.

Recommendation

In the claim-lost branch, re-read the entry. If it is Bound to exactly `pid`, treat the call as success: settle only if still pending, and return Bound without disposing of anything. Recycle only when the entry is Bound to a different pid or is held by a different claim. Settle-or-verify the intent state before any destructive effect, and add a two-resumer regression test.

The only guard there is contains_pid (cleanup.rs:78). That check passes because root syncs the parent's directory before it replies (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:293-330). Two resumers can run at once: classification marks the stale claim Resumable (classification.rs:63-72), begin_allocation hands every caller an ExistingPending permit with no lease (allocation.rs:274), and root authorizes recycle only by parent match (authorize.rs:141-156). begin_subtree_removal does not block P's own terminal allocation (subtree_retirement/mod.rs:186-198). Sharding assigns the key after the shard-creation await without re-checking, so a key assigned concurrently to another shard is silently moved
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/placement/sharding/assignment.rs:198

Failure scenario

All shards are full. Request R1 for key K plans CreateAllowed at slot 2 and awaits root. Meanwhile the shard at slot 3, created for another key, becomes available. Request R2 for K (a retry or a second client) takes the UseExisting path, K is assigned to shard 3, and the caller writes K's data there. R1's creation then completes and assign moves K to the new slot-2 shard. Routing now points K at slot 2 while K's data sits on shard 3.
