In the CreateAllowed branch, AlreadyAssigned is decided from a snapshot taken before the await (assignment.rs:106-128). allocate_and_admit(...).await then runs root creation (assignment.rs:185-194), and afterwards ShardingRegistryOps::assign(pool, partition_key, pid) is called unconditionally (assignment.rs:198). assign is documented as 'Assign (or reassign)': it decrements the old shard's count and moves the key to the new shard (ops/storage/placement/sharding.rs:230-264). The bootstrap path has the same pattern: assign after bootstrap_empty_active(...).await (bootstrap.rs:67-89). Other messages interleave at the await: a UseExisting assignment of the same key once another shard gains capacity (a new shard finishing, or release_partition_key), or a CreateAllowed at a different free slot.

After the await, re-read partition_key_shard(pool, key). If it is Some, return that shard (the new shard stays registered for future keys); otherwise assign. Use a create-only assign variant on this path so reassignment requires an explicit operation.

In the CreateAllowed branch it awaits allocate_and_admit (assignment.rs:185-188), which awaits a root RPC (allocation.rs:101-111). Afterwards it calls ShardingRegistryOps::assign unconditionally (assignment.rs:198), and that function explicitly reassigns: when the current assignment differs, it decrements the old shard's count and moves the key (ops/storage/placement/sharding.rs:206-264). The bootstrap path does the same after its await (bootstrap.rs:67-89). Nothing serializes calls per key. Allocation resources are per slot (model/placement/allocation.rs:111-121, resource_includes_subject=true), so creations for different keys at different HRW slots run concurrently. Two concurrent requests for the same key and the same free-slot set converge on one operation, but once another slot's creation completes, or release_partition_key frees capacity (release.rs:29-60), a second request for K takes the synchronous UseExisting path (assignment.rs:146-168) and gets shard 3 back. R1 then moves K to slot 2. The two callers receive different pids and routing silently changes after the first answer went out. That is a double effect under retry interleaving. ShardingApi::assign_to_pool is public (api/placement/sharding/mod.rs:46-53), and apps call it from update endpoints (apps/test/user_hub/src/lib.rs:30-32). Registry counts stay consistent; the harm depends on the app writing to the returned shard. highverifiedcp-fleet-coordinator-5 · correctness · medium confidence
Funding reconcile treats any Root error as a definite rejection, even when an earlier attempt may already have transferred the cycles
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1231

Failure scenario

The Coordinator sends AcceptFunding with X cycles and the Root accepts, but the bounded-wait response is lost and the Coordinator gets SysUnknown. When the Root retries RequestRootFunding, the Coordinator reconciles. The Root's replay now returns an error, for example from a transient authority or mirror validation or a command-variant fence. The Coordinator records RootRejected. X cycles have moved but are missing from the Coordinator's automatic and window accounting, so caps are bypassed. The Root's funding journal is permanently wedged, which blocks all future grants, its removal and snapshots.

Evidence

`request_root_funding` sends both `Invoke` and `Reconcile` dispositions through `call_root_funding_acceptance` (mod.rs:255-262). That function maps any `Err(_)` from the Root to `FleetRootFundingCallOutcome::Rejected` (1227-1233). `record_root_funding_rejection` then clears `current` and stores NoGrant(RootRejected) as `last`, charging no spend (root_funding.rs:427-461). Reconcile exists precisely because a previous attached-cycles call has an unknown outcome: the call is bounded-wait (mod.rs:1221), so a timeout gives SysUnknown. If that earlier call was accepted, the Root is in GrantAccepted, and its `record_response` rejects any NoGrant in that phase (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:478-486). Every later Root retry receives the replayed `last` NoGrant (root_funding.rs:134-138), and the Root can never clear its request. With a pending request the Root cannot fence funding for terminal removal (fleet_subnet_root.rs:642-647) or take an authority snapshot. Design 0.108 (lines 876-879) assumes the replay always converges to the receipt.

Recommendation

For a Reconcile disposition, treat a Root error as retryable: return the error and keep `current`. Record RootRejected only on a first Invoke with a definite, non-replay rejection, or first ask the Root for its journal state. Because refunds of attached cycles can be lost when a bounded-wait response is dropped, consider `unbounded_wait` for this value transfer.

Severity adjusted from medium to high during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. `call_root_funding_acceptance` (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1219-1234) turns every Candid `Err` reply into `Rejected`, for Reconcile as well as Invoke (255-275). `record_root_funding_rejection` (ops root_funding.rs:427-461) then clears `current` and charges no spend. On the Root, `accept` (workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:189-218) only replays a GrantAccepted receipt if every earlier guard passes. One realistic guard that can fail is the default fleet guard (canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:201-212), which returns Err when an operator has set the Root's fleet status to readonly or disabled. The Root's cycle timer keeps resuming its current request whatever the fleet status is (canic-core workflow/runtime/cycles/mod.rs:269-318, 896-903). After that, the Coordinator replays the NoGrant from `last` (root_funding.rs:134-138). The Root's `record_response` refuses NoGrant while in GrantAccepted (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:478-486), and no repair path exists. The Root journal is therefore wedged for this release: removal is fenced (fleet_subnet_root.rs:642-647), snapshots are blocked, and the grant of X cycles is missing from the Coordinator's caps. It takes two ordinary faults: a lost bounded-wait response, then a guard error on the replay. I rate it high because it is a recovery that cannot complete after a lost response. highverifiedcp-registry-workflow-1 · liveness · medium confidence
Allocation Directory authority is frozen at commit but re-validated against the live Fleet mirror and live partition head, so an ordinary Fleet publication or a sibling child commit permanently wedges in-flight allocations
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:4200

Failure scenario

Parent P runs two concurrent CreateCanister RPCs. Child A commits at revision r+1. Child B commits at r+2 while A's prepare_child_directories is awaiting root_store::status. From then on, A's convergence fails with conflict on every retry, and A is never terminal. Separately, a service scale-out or funding rotation advances the root mirror while top-level allocation X sits between commit and membership sync. The 1 s driver then fails with invariant forever. The Component stays Prepared and cannot be removed, its pool canister and cycles are stranded, and the perpetual timer blocks suspend_root.

Evidence

Top-level: prepared_component_runtime_plan_with_authority takes the CURRENT mirror directory (mod.rs:3894-3895). It hashes that directory together with the prepared partition head and returns invariant when the result differs from the commit-time hash, unless initial descendants are terminal (3946-3958). ops commit_verified also re-validates the hash against the current fleet (ops/component_registry/top_level_activation/mod.rs:39-47). Child: prepared_child_runtime_plan passes the current fleet (mod.rs:4019-4020) to committed_child_authority (4049-4054). That function checks the commit-time directory_authority_hash (ops/component_registry/mod.rs:4539-4563). Separately, prepare_child_directories converges the owning Component with the immutable committed authority (mod.rs:2635-2641, 4169-4191). On membership retry it uses the historical membership snapshot (ops mod.rs:4322-4366). active_component_direct_children_for_authority returns conflict whenever the live partition head differs from that authority (mod.rs:4197-4202), even though current_child_partition explicitly tolerates a later revision (4139-4143). No code serializes child commits (ops child_activation 31-136), and no code blocks mirror advances while allocations are in flight (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:315-352, 483-505). A non-terminal child allocation blocks draining and ancestor subtree removal (ops component_retirement/mod.rs:137-141; subtree_retirement/mod.rs:186-196). A committed but never-activated top-level Component stays Prepared, and begin_component_draining refuses it (component_retirement/mod.rs:124-129).

Recommendation

Treat committed and membership authorities as a lower bound. On each phase, rebuild the Directory request from the current partition and the current mirror, and accept progression when the new state covers the old one (the pattern in component_directory_progresses and fleet_directory_non_regressing). Keep the frozen hash only as historical evidence. If exactness is required, fence mirror advances and sibling commits while any allocation is between commit and terminal. Add unit tests: commit A then B before A's prepare; advance the mirror between commit and activation.

highverifiedcp-registry-workflow-2 · liveness · medium confidence
A scale-out Directory synchronization intent becomes permanently irreconcilable once the target's partition head moves past intent.registry (or the target stops being Active), wedging the root's single active synchronization slot
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_directory_synchronization/mod.rs:120

Failure scenario

The coordinator publishes a service scale-out. The root journals the intent for grouped member C, commits C's head to r+1, and awaits C's configure call. Meanwhile C's application provisions a child, whose commit moves C's head to r+2 before C's runtime is converged, so coverage validation fails with conflict. On every coordinator retry, directory_refresh_plan_for_intent sees r+2, which is neither r nor r+1, and returns conflict. The operation never completes. Every future SynchronizeComponentDirectories on this root is rejected with ActiveOperationConflict until the root is reinstalled.

Evidence

advance() unconditionally returns Reconcile(in_flight) while an intent is retained (ops/component_directory_synchronization/mod.rs:120-124). synchronize_target rebuilds the plan with directory_refresh_plan_for_intent (workflow/component_directory_synchronization/mod.rs:171-176). That function accepts only current == previous_registry or current == intent.registry, and otherwise returns conflict (ops/component_registry/directory_refresh/mod.rs:230-252). prepare_directory_refresh also requires the target to still be Active (118-120). The refresh commit happens before the awaited runtime calls (workflow:176-195). Post-call validation requires the Component's runtime authority to equal the CURRENT head exactly (workflow:210-231). Any concurrent head change during those awaits (child commit or membership activation in the grouped Component, a subtree-removal step) therefore makes the call fail with the intent kept. Every later retry then hits the conflict at directory_refresh 247-252. A new operation cannot be accepted while one is active (storage/stable/component_provisioning/mod.rs:612-617), and there is no abandon path.

Recommendation

Allow reconciliation to a successor head: if the current head is a later revision of the same Component and canister, re-plan from it (a new intent at the same index) or accept coverage when the runtime is at or beyond the current head. Alternatively, fence partition-head mutations of target Components while a synchronization is active. Record a typed skip disposition for targets that leave Active. Add a unit test that bumps the partition after commit_directory_refresh and then reconciles.

Anything else returns conflict (ops/component_registry/directory_refresh/mod.rs:231-253). The head can move through ordinary, allowed paths. commit_child_allocation_for_parent is called by the parent canister and is not fenced by any active directory synchronization (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:519-566). require_child_allocation_runtime_phase only checks the root and parent phase (4148-4167). committed_child_records derives revision+1 from the current partition, not from the reserved head (ops/component_registry/mod.rs:3615-3653). The 0.101 design explicitly keeps the direct-child lifecycle available for grouped members (0.101-design.md:2151-2154). The move can happen during the await at workflow:188-195. It can also happen after any failed or lost sync call, while the intent is retained at r+1. After that, every retry fails, the slot is never cleared (replace_directory_synchronization clears it only when complete, storage/stable/component_provisioning/mod.rs:677-684), and new operations get ActiveOperationConflict (612-617). There is no abandon path, and scale-out is forward-only, so the operation cannot reach RuntimesActivated. It stays high rather than critical because root otherwise keeps working.

highverifiedcp-root-admission-funding-4 · liveness · medium confidence
Every Coordinator retry of an in-progress admission phase starts a new self-rescheduling Root timer chain, which exhausts ic-timers' 64-registration limit and multiplies target calls
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:139

Failure scenario

A Root has about 30 enrolled participants and each target step takes about 2 s, so the Fence phase lasts over a minute. The Coordinator calls Fence at 1 Hz and each call adds a chain. After about 60 s roughly 60 chains issue duplicate Prepare calls, and the registry is full. From then on the Coordinator's Activate and Open calls trap, rolling back their commits. Running chains trap inside schedule, rolling back the receipt they just recorded. Every other Root lifecycle timer (pool maintenance, component lifecycle drivers, Registry sync, Store GC, Root removal) traps until the phase drains. If trapped callbacks leak their registrations (unverified), the Root cannot schedule lifecycle work at all.

Evidence

prepare (Fence), activate and open call schedule() whenever the phase is still in progress (workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:79, 92, 105). schedule() (139-147) calls TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required, which registers a new once-timer with a fresh `lifecycle-{id}` identity on every call, with no dedup (canic-core/src/api/timer.rs:81-89; workflow/runtime/timer/mod.rs:351-398). Each chain reschedules itself on Ok(false) or Err (143-144) and stops only on Waiting or Complete (153-155, 231-233); an operation-ID mismatch also retries every 1 s (160-161). The Coordinator re-issues the phase call every 1 s while the Root returns unavailable (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:598-605, 628-633). ic-timers allows 64 registrations per canister (ic-timers-0.8.0 src/registry/mod.rs:24, 728-731; global at runtime/mod.rs:19-21), and defer_lifecycle_required traps on failure (api/timer.rs:87-88). Chains race: losers of the compare-and-swap in record_target_receipt (ops/root_admission/mod.rs:267-270) retry after issuing duplicate bounded-wait target calls (workflow 245-248).

Recommendation

Keep a single owned convergence timer per Root, like TOPUP_TIMER with with_owned_once plus ensure_scheduled or reconcile_schedule, and make prepare, activate and open only ensure it is armed. End the chain on operation-ID mismatch. Add a test that asserts a bounded timer inventory during a slow convergence.

Verifier (confirmed): The finding holds. While a phase is still in progress, a replayed Fence/Activate/Open call returns no receipt: canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/fleet_admission_root/mod.rs:145, 231 and 276 return state.clone() with a None receipt. So every Coordinator retry reaches schedule() again (workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:79, 92, 105). schedule() registers a fresh `lifecycle-{n}` once-timer with no dedup (canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/timer/mod.rs:351-398). The endpoint layer adds no dedup either (canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:274-292, 395-406). A chain ends only at Waiting or Complete (root_admission/mod.rs:153, 231). Losing the record_target_receipt check (ops/root_admission/mod.rs:268-270), or any target error, reschedules it after 1 s. The Coordinator retries after 1 s plus the round-trip (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:598-605). ic-timers caps the registry at 64 (registry/mod.rs:24, 728-731), and defer_lifecycle_required traps when registration fails (api/timer.rs:86-88). The leak the finding left unverified is likely. dispatch_ordinary commits the Running state before `future.await` (runtime/mod.rs:1138-1167). ic-timers has no Drop guard, and its README:60 says Once timers get "No automatic recovery". So a continuation that traps after the target call stays registered. Once the registry is full, no receipt can commit, the phase cannot reach Waiting, and chains leak one by one. Root lifecycle scheduling stays blocked until an upgrade clears the heap. Corrections: one persistently failing participant makes chain growth unbounded, which is a stronger trigger than a slow phase (up to 4,096 participants). Operation-ID-mismatch chains do end at the next Waiting. Recovery by upgrade exists, so this is high, not critical.

highverifiedcp-root-admission-funding-5 · cycles · medium confidence
The Coordinator attaches whole grants to bounded-wait AcceptFunding calls, so a lost response on the zero-accept replay path burns the entire grant
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1221

Failure scenario

A 750T grant is accepted by the Root, but the Coordinator's bounded-wait response is lost. The Root retries and the Coordinator reconciles with another 750T attached. The Root accepts 0 and returns the receipt, but under cross-subnet backlog that response also times out. 750T is burned, recorded in neither ledger, and each further loss burns another full grant.

Evidence

call_root_funding_acceptance sends RemoteRootCommand::AcceptFunding with the full granted_cycles attached through CallOps::bounded_wait (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1217-1225). On every Root retry of an in-flight grant, the Coordinator returns Reconcile (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:130) and makes the same call again with cycles attached (workflow 244-278). After the first acceptance, the Root replays by accepting zero and returning the stored receipt (workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:197-199; ops/root_funding/mod.rs:392-396, 732-750), so the whole attached amount travels back as a refund in the response. The 0.108 design justifies zero-accept replay by the standard refund model (docs/design/0.108-coordinator-backed-root-funding/0.108-design.md ~858-864), which holds for unbounded-wait calls. With bounded-wait calls, a response that times out or is dropped produces SYS_UNKNOWN and the refund is not delivered. The Coordinator treats the `.await?` error as a plain retryable failure with no accounting. By contrast, the value-moving Cycles Ledger transfers use unbounded_wait (canic-core/src/infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:214).

Recommendation

Use unbounded_wait for AcceptFunding, which is a value transfer. Alternatively, on Reconcile first read the Root receipt with zero cycles attached and attach the grant only when the Root reports CoordinatorRequested.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. call_root_funding_acceptance (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1217-1225) sends AcceptFunding with the full granted_cycles over CallOps::bounded_wait, which uses a best-effort call with the default 300 s timeout (canic-core/src/infra/ic/call.rs:35). Any `.await?` error leaves the Coordinator's `current` grant in place. The next Root retry then gets Reconcile (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:128-131) and the call repeats with the whole grant attached (workflow 254-261). On replay the Root requires incoming == granted (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:388-390), accepts nothing and returns the receipt (workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:200), so the whole principal has to come back as a refund inside the response. For best-effort calls, DeadlineExpired and ResponseDropped map to SYS_UNKNOWN (ic-error-types lib.rs:130-132). A refund carried by a response that is dropped or arrives late is lost. No Coordinator ledger records that loss, and window limits never count it, so each repeat can burn another full grant. The design assumed refunds always come back (0.108-design.md:863-867). The M0 evidence tested only a trapped callback, never a timeout (audits/working/0.108.../README.md:33, 56-57). Cycles Ledger transfers use unbounded_wait (cycles_ledger.rs:214). Triggering this needs response loss, which is most likely under the same cross-subnet backlog that caused the first loss. That fits the rubric's high: a conservation violation on ordinary failure paths. The zero-attached-read fix also needs a Root change, because the Root rejects any amount that differs from the grant (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:388).

highverifiedhost-ensure-capacity-2 · robustness · medium confidence
Handoff lost-reply recovery stops working about 5 minutes after submission: the envelope expires in 240 s and the IC prunes the reply, yet renewal requires a certified rejection.
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/capacity_import/transport/mod.rs:105

Failure scenario

The operator's apply submits the handoff, and then the process is killed (Ctrl-C, crash, lost network or laptop sleep). Alternatively, the 12 s poll ends Unresolved. The operator reruns 10 minutes later. - request_status now returns Done, giving a permanent HandoffPruned, or Unknown. - On Unknown, the expired envelope is resubmitted, rejected at the HTTP layer and mapped to Unresolved, and the second resubmission ends in BudgetExhausted. The same happens if the crash falls between saving the Issued state and calling update_signed: the request never ran, but it can never be renewed. The approved import is wedged, as in the no-abort finding, with Root fenced.

Evidence

prepare() signs update_settings with expire_after(240 s) as soon as the source has been observed (transport/mod.rs:100-107; handoff/mod.rs:117-124).

Reconciliation uses only certified request_status (transport/mod.rs:138-154):
- Done maps to HandoffPruned.
- Unknown maps to Unresolved (transport/mod.rs:279-283).

On Unresolved, submit_or_reconcile reserves another submission and resends the identical, possibly expired bytes (handoff/mod.rs:159-185), then polls for only 12 s (188-207).

Renewal is allowed only when the current request has a retained certified rejection (journal/rejection/mod.rs:29-34, 80-82). The comment at handoff/mod.rs:164 says a retained reply stays useful after ingress expiry, but the IC drops terminal ingress statuses about 5 minutes after completion and refuses envelopes past their expiry. No code accepts the exact post-handoff management state, or proof of non-execution after expiry, as a resolution.

verify_destination also makes about 2N+1 certified reads after signing and before submission (transport/root/mod.rs:58-89), which eats into the 240 s window on large fleets.

Recommendation

Once ingress_expiry plus the permitted drift has passed, treat Unknown or Done as resolvable from certified management state. If controllers and version still equal the reviewed binding, the request provably did not execute, so allow one bounded renewal. If controllers equal the transitional set and version equals reviewed+1, mark the handoff Applied. Sign immediately before issuance, not before the observation, and fix the misleading comment.

So once the IC prunes the ingress entry, which it does about MAX_INGRESS_TTL after the terminal status, no code path can finish or renew. The same is true if a crash lands between saving Intent or Issued and submission. The rest of the system then stays blocked: lock_operation calls require_no_approved_import (ops/mod.rs:688), and Root's active import fences provisioning and retirement (component_provisioning/mod.rs:310; root_retirement.rs:541). highverifiedhost-ensure-capacity-4 · liveness · medium confidence
The bootstrap-initial import pins bootstrap-time pool and Root balances as immutable baselines, and bootstrap never checks pool headroom, so an underfunded pool or a later top-up leaves the Root hold unreleasable.
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/capacity_import/review/mod.rs:121

Failure scenario

Bootstrap completes with operator-held pools holding 0.5T each, while the pool policy's canister_cycles is 1T. 1. `fleet import` review fails with InsufficientCycles. 2. The operator tops the pools up, but the review keeps using the pinned 0.5T samples and still fails. 3. Even if it passed, approval would now fail ConservationUnproven because of the increase. Likewise, a Root top-up after the bootstrap receipt makes approval return InvalidCycleBounds on every attempt. The Root's bootstrap hold never clears, so Root and the fleet cannot progress.

Evidence

Baseline selection in plan_async (workflow/capacity_import/review/mod.rs:105-126):
- Operator-held pool sources always take the bootstrap survey's original sample.
- The Root always takes the bootstrap terminal-receipt sample (prior_root).
- Fresh or persisted samples are only a fallback.

convergence::verify_imports then requires imported.observed_cycles to equal the original sample (ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/convergence/mod.rs:172-181).

validate_plan requires observed_cycles >= minimum_ready_cycles + maximum_debit_cycles (policy/capacity_import/mod.rs:166-174), where minimum_ready is the pool policy's canister_cycles (admission/review/mod.rs:238-260).

Bootstrap compile skips Pool targets entirely (policy/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:62-64), and validate_source checks custody only, not balance (427-455). Nothing therefore guarantees that the pinned pool balances can pass the later import.

The Root bootstrap hold is cleared only by completing that import. Until then Root's pending()/is_active() fences pool, allocation and provisioning work, and the docs state that the first workload plan requires every held import to be complete.

Recommendation

At bootstrap review, require each operator-held pool's sampled balance to be at least canister_pool.canister_cycles plus a reviewed per-source debit bound, and bind that bound into the bootstrap record. Also permit a reviewed rebase or credit for bootstrap sources and the Root, with the original balance as a lower bound, so a top-up can repair headroom.

Bootstrap never checks pool balances: compile skips Pool targets (policy/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:62-64), and validate_source (427-455) checks custody only. highverifiedhost-ensure-funding-2 · liveness · high confidence
A credited operator mint permanently freezes its Estate or Native funding review: no second conversion and no refresh are allowed, so a short credit caused by a CMC rate move wedges the operation
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/operator_mint/mod.rs:184

Failure scenario

An Estate review needs 10T cycles, and the operator's balance is 0. The CLI quotes 200,000,000 e8s at a rate of 50,000. Before notify, the CMC rate updates to 49,900, so 9.98T cycles are minted and credited. Resume fails with OperatorFundingRequired. `--operator-mint` only shows the credited conversion, and prepare keeps returning the same review. Topping up outside Canic is tolerated only up to the prior debit and then breaks terminal accounting. The operation is stuck with the ICP already spent.

Evidence

review() accepts only the already-retained intent for a funding review and rejects any other with OperatorMintReviewConflict (operator_mint/mod.rs:184-189). The CLI shows the retained mint instead of preparing a new one (canic-cli/src/fleet/operator_mint/mod.rs:63-90). funding::prepare returns the review unchanged whenever operator_mint is Some; Native refresh only runs when operator_mint.is_none() (funding/mod.rs:139-145). The CLI sizes the mint to exactly the gap, required minus available (operator_mint/mod.rs:281-299). quote::amount_e8s adds no slippage margin beyond rounding up one e8 (policy/operator_mint/quote/mod.rs:15-25). The CMC mints at the rate current at notify time. Resume re-checks the full debit, and a short credit fails with OperatorFundingRequired (funding/mod.rs:396-397 and 456-470; native/mod.rs:547-548). A Native review that has a mint attached also cannot be re-quoted after the Root balance drops beyond the margin: validate_observation returns DriftedBeforeApply at native/mod.rs:492-501. By contrast, the Operator pause path creates a new review whenever the balance is still short (workflow/funding/operator/mod.rs:122-140).

Recommendation

Allow a supplementary conversion bound to the same funding review when the admitted net credit leaves a shortfall, matching the Operator-pause behaviour. Alternatively, allow a funding review whose mint is credited but which has no effect to be refreshed or replaced. Add an explicit rate-slippage margin to the quote, and check at admission whether the credit covers the gap, reporting the remaining shortfall.

The CLI calls prepare_review only when status() returns None (canic-cli/src/fleet/operator_mint/mod.rs:63,82-90), so a credited mint is only displayed. funding::prepare returns an Estate review with no effect unchanged, and it refreshes a Native review only when operator_mint is None (funding/mod.rs:124-145). The Operator-pause special case at :127-131 does not extend to Estate or Native. quote::amount_e8s rounds up by less than one e8 and adds no margin (quote/mod.rs:15-25). Apply is a separate later command, so the CMC rate can move before notify. execution/mod.rs:67-165 admits the credit without checking that it covers the gap. The resume check require_operator_funds (funding/mod.rs:396-397, 456-470; native/mod.rs:547) then fails with OperatorFundingRequired. Docs (fleet-ensure.md:925-929) say a changed rate never authorizes a second payment, forbid minting independently into a retained operation, and give no path for a short credit. One correction: a top-up outside Canic passes verify_balance while the observed balance stays at or below operator_source, i.e. up to the prior debit (funding/mod.rs:237-241). Terminal accounting (workflow/mod.rs:3653-3700) then treats it as a net credit, so it does not break accounting as claimed. It is still undocumented. When the prior debit is smaller than the gap, any top-up gives DriftedBeforeApply and nothing can recover the operation. No cycles are lost, so high, not critical.

highverifiedhost-ensure-funding-3 · liveness · medium confidence
Deposit authentication needs a certified hash chain from the current Cycles Ledger tip back to the deposit, at most 1024 blocks in one query, so a mint whose deposit read is interrupted can become impossible to admit
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/operator_mint/transport/mod.rs:350

Failure scenario

The operator applies a conversion. The transfer and notify succeed, and Minted is recorded. The process is then interrupted by a network error or Ctrl-C before read_deposit completes. The operator retries the next day, after the Cycles Ledger has appended more than 1024 blocks, and read_deposit returns BudgetExceeded on every retry. The ICP has been spent, the credit can never be admitted, and the retained operation is permanently fenced.

Evidence

read_deposit fetches the current tip certificate and requires tip - deposit + 1 <= DEPOSIT_LIMITS.blocks (1024); otherwise it returns BudgetExceeded (transport/mod.rs:42-48 and 341-354). It then issues a single icrc3_get_blocks query for the whole range (355-364). verify_chain requires exactly that many blocks, linked by phash (receipts/blocks/mod.rs:79-102). A ledger that truncates responses therefore fails as well; I did not verify the Cycles Ledger's per-request cap. Once the notification outcome is Minted, apply() always goes straight to read_deposit, with no alternative evidence path (execution/mod.rs:143-153). The conversion can no longer be cancelled (operator_mint/mod.rs:255-257), and the missing receipt fences all plan and apply calls through OperatorMintPending (workflow/mod.rs:4146-4155). The minted cycles are already in the operator account, outside operator_source (policy/operator_mint/mod.rs:120-128). The repository already authenticates a single Cycles Ledger block through a certified replicated icrc3_get_blocks read, with no tip-distance limit (ops/reinstall/debit/mod.rs:94-99). The docs acknowledge that over-budget history stays unresolved.

Recommendation

Authenticate the deposit block directly with a certified replicated icrc3_get_blocks read of length 1, as ops/reinstall/debit does. Alternatively, page backwards through the chain in bounded chunks under a total budget, and do not treat distance from the tip as a permanent failure.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. In transport/mod.rs:327-373, read_deposit verifies the certified tip, then requires tip - deposit + 1 <= 1024 (lines 350-354), or it returns BudgetExceeded. It then makes one icrc3_get_blocks query and passes the result to verify_chain. verify_chain (receipts/blocks/mod.rs:79-102) requires the exact contiguous chain back from the tip. The tip only grows, so once the distance passes 1024 the failure is permanent. The comment at transport:39 says these budgets are "not a payment validity window", but in practice they act as one. No other path exists. Once Minted is recorded, apply goes straight to read_deposit (execution/mod.rs:143-150). admit_credit is the only way to set a receipt. cancel_review is refused after approval (operator_mint/mod.rs:255-257). verify_journal fences plan resume with OperatorMintPending (workflow/mod.rs:4145-4155, used at 528 and elsewhere). The docs (fleet-ensure.md:925-929) say over-budget history "remain[s] unresolved" and also forbid resetting the journal, so the wedge is acknowledged but has no recovery path. Reachability is broader than a Ctrl-C. A notify call_and_wait timeout (120s, transport:250-263) or a transient read_deposit error, followed by a retry after more than 1024 new ledger blocks, also triggers it, because CMC returns the cached block index. The ledger's per-request block cap is unverified and could shrink the window further. No cycles are lost: the net credit sits in the operator's own account. The impact is recovery that cannot complete, so high is appropriate. The fix already exists nearby: ops/reinstall/debit/mod.rs:94-99 does a certified replicated length-1 read.

Intent check: the design admits the limit. It says old deposits "may exceed that budget" and offers no fallback (0.110-design.md:463-468). The user docs say over-budget receipt history "remain[s] unresolved" and forbid resetting the journal (fleet-ensure.md:925-929). So this is a known limitation. It is not a designed recovery outcome, for three reasons: - The same design promises that a restart can rebuild the receipt chain (0.110-design.md:405-407). - AGENTS.md is normative and requires same-release interruption recovery. "If code conflicts with this file, the code is wrong." - The docs name no path forward, because the operation stays fenced forever. The code and docs agree with each other, so this is not just a documentation problem. The recommended fix does not break any design rule. The same design already authenticates ICP blocks with a certified single-index replicated read (0.110-design.md:486-490). ops/reinstall/debit/mod.rs:94-99 does exactly that for one Cycles Ledger block. Nothing in the design says a replicated read is unacceptable for the Cycles Ledger. Impact check: no cycles are lost, because the net credit sits in the operator's own account, so conservation holds. But the retained Fleet operation, possibly with its own unresolved paid withdrawal, can never be resumed. That is recovery that cannot complete. It is reachable through an ordinary timeout or transient read error followed by a delayed retry, and possibly sooner if the ledger caps blocks per request (not verified). Severity stays high. The documented acknowledgement is the only mitigating factor.
highverifiedhost-ensure-reinstall-2 · correctness · medium confidence
Clean reinstall erases the old Root and Coordinator registries without checking that the seed covers every Root-controlled canister, so omitted or refill-created assets are silently stranded
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:96

Failure scenario

A mainnet Fleet has converged with pool assets P1 to P4. At runtime an allocation consumes P1 and the Root refill creates P5; alternatively, the operator's seed simply omits workload W. The operator builds the new release, generates from the seed (the pool check is skipped because the Root module differs) and runs --reinstall. Phase 1 reinstalls the Root, which erases its pool registry and any pending creation. Phase 2 clears only P1 to P4. P5 or W stays controlled by the Root principal but appears in no registry, no host state and no conservation equation. Their cycles are stranded, and the reset still reports fleet_completed.

Evidence

`review` first calls prepare_bootstrap (line 96). This archives and deletes the completed operation, including state.json, which is the last terminal inventory (ops/operation_selection/retirement/mod.rs:30-51, 146-216). Nothing compares that inventory to the new seed. After that, the estate is only what the operator-authored desired lists: automatic::custody observes only desired.canisters (ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/automatic/mod.rs:84-127), and review_import imports only desired Pool entries whose parent is the Root (workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:186-205). Generation has a live pool check that rejects an 'unseeded controlled pool asset' (generate/mod.rs:1963-1969), but it is skipped whenever a seeded Root module differs from the selected build (generate/mod.rs:1693-1701). That is the normal release transition, and even when the check runs it is not repeated before the Root install. The obsolete lane had an explicit membership and unsettled-creation check before any reset (ops/reinstall/terminal/inventory/membership/mod.rs:88-93; generate/completed_source/mod.rs:177-190). On mainnet, Roots keep creating pool assets from their recurring maintenance timer (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:110-124, 284-287).

Recommendation

Before prepare_bootstrap deletes state.json, require that the seed and desired principal set covers the retained terminal inventory (principals, pending_principals and topology descendants), with a typed error that names the missing IDs. Before the infrastructure install, page the old Root's pool through the maintained read-only pool contract. Reject undeclared members, pending creation and pending handoff, bind that membership digest into the reviewed plan, and recheck it immediately before the Root install.

Verifier (confirmed): The finding holds, with one correction that makes it worse than described. In the clean-reinstall path, generation never runs the live pool check at all. For a completed Fleet, generate/mod.rs:781-800 sets initialization=Initialize. completed_source::observe is then skipped (lines 919-929) and observe_estate is never called (lines 935-953), so observed is empty. The module-mismatch early return at lines 1693-1701 is not the gate that matters. review() calls prepare_bootstrap at clean_reinstall/mod.rs:96, which archives and removes state.json (retirement/mod.rs:30-51, 146-216). No membership comparison happens before that. BootstrapSurvey's retain_request then requires an empty state (survey/mod.rs:303-312). automatic::custody observes only desired.canisters (automatic/mod.rs:88-120). infrastructure_bootstrap::observe (ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:419-444) never queries the old Root pool. review_import imports only desired Pool entries (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:186-205). The old membership and unsettled-creation lane (membership/mod.rs:88-93) is reachable only through completed_source, which this route bypasses. The PocketIC fixture always supplies the full pool list (completed_reset/mod.rs:468-469); there is no omission test. This contradicts docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:481-485, which says omitting a pool import 'fails closed'. On mainnet, Root refill creates assets on its own (canister_pool/mod.rs:262-287), so the seed can go stale through ordinary operation. Mitigation: an omitted asset keeps the Root principal (plus any recovery controllers, fleet_topology/mod.rs:253-259) as controller. It can be adopted later with `fleet import` (docs lines 1108-1111), but only if the operator finds its ID outside Canic. The reset still reports success, and an omitted workload keeps its old code and state and keeps burning cycles, so high stands.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): Reachable from a routine operator CLI command. `canic fleet ensure <fleet> --reinstall` goes to clean_reinstall::run_if_selected first (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:508). On a completed Fleet, selected() returns true (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:59-63), and that leads to review(). review() calls prepare_bootstrap (line 96), which archives and removes the terminal state (retirement/mod.rs:30-51, 146-216). Nothing compares the membership first. retained_contract::check (retained_contract/mod.rs:122-176) inspects only side-operation metadata. Generation for a completed Fleet sets initialization=Initialize (generate/mod.rs:781-800) and skips both completed_source::observe and observe_estate (919-953). infrastructure_bootstrap::validate_seed only requires pool_imports to be non-empty (generate/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:49-57). The custody survey and observe() read only desired.canisters (automatic/mod.rs:88-120; ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:419-444). No Root pool query exists anywhere in the reinstall path; grep finds none. review_import imports only the desired Pool entries (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:186-205). The old Root does not need to misbehave for this to happen. Its maintenance timer refills the pool toward minimum_size after an ordinary allocation (canister_pool/mod.rs:262-287, started from fleet_activation/mod.rs:59). The host never learns those new IDs, so a seed written from host records goes stale through normal operation. This contradicts the documented guarantee that omitting a pool asset "fails closed" (fleet-ensure.md:481-485). The actor is the operator, who already has full authority. But this is a missing safety check on their own estate, triggered by a routine action, not an authorization issue. Mitigations: an omitted canister stays controlled by the Root principal, so the letter of "remains controlled" holds. `fleet import` can adopt it if its ID is known, and an omitted workload's ID survives in the archived history. A Root-refilled asset's ID was known only to the old Root's registry, which the reinstall erased. The flow still reports fleet_completed, and an omitted old workload keeps running old code, which is effectively mixed-version operation. High stands.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, medium): I could not refute the finding, but I would lower it from high to medium. What the design intends: the .45 amendment (docs/design/0.110-fleet-runtime-contraction/0.110-design.md:26-28) says reset is reviewed "from explicit inventory" with no predecessor adapters. The CLI help calls --seed "Explicit retained canister inventory" (crates/canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:445), and the operator guide tells the operator to "Select the complete physical inventory" (fleet-ensure.md:12-13). Completeness is therefore the operator's job. The second fix the finding recommends, paging the old Root's pool, goes against the design. The guide says explicit reinstall needs no current endpoints on old code (fleet-ensure.md:664), and ordinary generation deliberately skips the pool query when the Root runs a different module (generate/mod.rs:1694-1701). Why it is still a defect: the docs promise the check exists. fleet-ensure.md:481-485 says omitting a pool import "fails closed". CANIC-166 (0.110-design.md:325) requires fresh verification of the "full physical inventory". Follow-up 154, "complete retained-estate review before Root reset" (status/current.md:6941-6946), was accepted by the maintainer. The .45 amendment replaces only schema decoding and repair with the original CLI (0.110-design.md:16-17). It never drops the omission guarantee. The code confirms the gap. automatic::custody observes only desired.canisters (automatic/mod.rs:88-120), and review_import imports only desired Pool entries (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:186-205). Why the impact is smaller than claimed: - retirement/mod.rs:73-85 archives state.json rather than destroying it. - Omitted assets stay controlled by the Root principal. The cycle-conservation invariant covers observed cycles, so this is not a literal violation. - `fleet import` accepts sources the destination Root already controls (fleet-ensure.md:1108-1111). The real harm is narrower: a pool asset created by Root refill after the seed was written (canister_pool/mod.rs:284-287). Its ID lived only in the old Root registry, which the reinstall wipes. After that its cycles are practically unrecoverable, and the reset still reports success.
highverifiedr2-cross-root-trust-1 · liveness · high confidence
Coordinator Registry publications reach only the roots each flow calls, and an activated root has no resync path, so removing a root or a partial scale-out permanently strands the other roots' mirrors and wedges their removal, component operations and funding
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:841

Failure scenario

Roots R1 and R2 are on different subnets, both mirrors at v5. The operator removes R2: the Coordinator publishes R2 Draining (v6) and Removed (v7). R1 stays at v5. R1's next funding request names v5 and is rejected as RegistryStale, so R1's top-up timer stops. To retire the Fleet, the operator sends RemoveRoot for R1. The Coordinator reserves at v7 and commits, then R1 rejects because v7 is not covered by v5. Every retry fails the same way and the reservation is irrevocable, so R1 can never be removed and Fleet retirement, which needs every root Removed, never completes. Variant with R1-R3: a scale-out of service T, hosted only on R3, advances only R3 to v6. The next scale-out with a batch on R1 fails acceptance forever while holding the Coordinator's scale-out slot. A funding-policy rotation starts, then PrepareRoot on R1 is rejected forever. R3's new T members are rejected by ProvisionPeer at R1 and never appear in R1's Component Directories.

Evidence

Root removal publishes Draining and Removed in the Coordinator only (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:840-858). The only root whose mirror advances is the one being removed (fleet_subnet_root.rs:625). Scale-out confirmation roots are validated to be exactly the batch roots plus the roots that host that service (component_provisioning_plan/scale_out/mod.rs:284-305). No root-side path can resync after activation. The private timer stops once active (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:212-219). SynchronizeRegistry accepts only an exact replay of the Joining operation (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:103-114; root.rs:794-797). activate() has no endpoint. Every later check compares against the stale mirror: component acceptance requires mirror == plan registry (component_provisioning.rs:103-108); directory synchronization requires current == source (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:434-437); rotation prepare requires predecessor == mirror (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:171); funding sends the mirror version (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:92, workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:228), which the Coordinator matches exactly (root_funding.rs:500) and which leads to RegistryStale and then Stop (fleet_funding/mod.rs:99-101; cycles/mod.rs:922). Root draining requires coverage of the Coordinator version (fleet_subnet_root.rs:258-263), and the Coordinator commits the reservation before calling the root (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:497-512).

Recommendation

Make Registry adoption Fleet-wide. After every Coordinator publication (admission, draining, removal, scale-out), drive an idempotent 'advance mirror to exact version V' step on every non-Removed root, keep per-root acknowledgements, and refuse the next publication, or any plan or reservation that names a lagging root, until all Active roots acknowledge the current version. Add a Coordinator-authenticated root resync that jumps from the root's own validated mirror to the fetched current snapshot and republishes the derived Directory to local Components. Add a two-root PocketIC test: remove one root, then fund the survivor and remove it.

Severity adjusted from critical to high during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The core claim holds. Only a few functions in workflow/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs can advance an active mirror, and they sit at lines 348, 405 and 480 (commit_active). They run only from component publication (component_provisioning.rs:472), directory sync (component_directory_synchronization/mod.rs:59,106), funding rotation (root_funding/mod.rs:144) and a root's own draining (fleet_subnet_root.rs:625). Each one requires the local mirror to equal the source version the Coordinator names: component_provisioning.rs:103-108, fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:434-437 and 653-667, and ops/root_funding/mod.rs:171. The initial-activation timer stops once the mirror is active (mirror/mod.rs:212-219). The general controller endpoint `canic_fleet_registry_activate_mirror` was removed in 0.103.0 (commit 731cd2a2d), and LifecycleApi::activate_fleet_registry_mirror is now unused. The steady-state resync that the 0.100 design specifies (lines 1778-1795 and 2946-2953) no longer exists. What follows from that: funding sends the mirror version (root_funding/mod.rs:228), the Coordinator compares it exactly (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:500), and the result is RegistryStale, then Stop (cycles/mod.rs:922, 551). Draining coverage fails (fleet_subnet_root.rs:258). Each root can hold only one reservation and it cannot be cancelled (root_lifecycle.rs:360-362). Retirement needs every root Removed (retirement/mod.rs:193). The reach is wider than claimed: MutateAdmission, which the CLI supports, also publishes a new Registry version (admission.rs:111-116), and root admission never advances the mirror. So even a single-root Fleet loses funding and root removal after one admission change. Downgraded to high: controllers keep IC-level control and the pre-1.0 reset/reinstall path. RemoveRoot and ScaleOut have no CLI wiring, and I did not verify whether the scale-out slot is released on failure.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute it. Routine controller commands reach it, and one of those commands is wired into the CLI. Entry point: `canic admission` (canic-cli/src/admission/mod.rs:326) sends `MutateAdmission`. The Coordinator accepts it from a controller (fleet_coordinator.rs macro, lines 80-96) and publishes a new Registry version (ops/fleet_coordinator/admission.rs:111-116). The root-side handlers for Prepare/Activate/Open never touch the mirror (workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:65-108). None of the requests carry a Registry version (dto/fleet_admission.rs:214-221). The only functions that write an active mirror are `commit_active`, at fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:267, 295, 348, 405 and 480. Each one requires the current mirror to equal a source version the Coordinator names (mod.rs:647-664, 374, 440). The initial-sync timer exits once the mirror is active (mod.rs:212-219). `accept_synchronization` accepts only an exact replay (mod.rs:103-114). `LifecycleApi::activate_fleet_registry_mirror` has no caller. Harm after that one admission change: - Root funding sends the mirror version (workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:230). The Coordinator compares it exactly (root_funding.rs:500), which gives RegistryStale and then Stop (cycles/mod.rs:922, 546-551). - A RemoveRoot reservation is checked against, and committed at, the current Coordinator version before the root is called (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1714-1737; workflow mod.rs:497-512). The root then rejects it (fleet_subnet_root.rs:258-263 via registry_covers_preparation). The reservation can never be removed, and a different operation for the same root conflicts (root_lifecycle.rs:355-357). - That stuck reservation on an Active root also blocks every later admission transition (admission.rs:43-51). - Retirement needs every root Removed (retirement/mod.rs:193). The existing tests never combine these steps. The two-root admission test (baseline.rs:14243) never funds afterwards, and the only RemoveRoot journey uses a single root (baseline.rs:14605). The triggering actor is the operator, but this is a liveness defect caused by ordinary use, not an authority escalation, so operator authority does not excuse it. I keep it at high rather than critical because cycles stay controlled and manual top-up plus the pre-1.0 reset path remain available.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): The behaviour is not intended. The designs assume a steady-state, snapshot-convergent path that keeps root mirrors current. 0.100-design.md:1778-1795 describes later snapshots with a 5-minute poll, and 2946-2953 covers post-removal convergence of surviving roots. 0.101-design.md:1776-1777 and 2036-2041 say that "unrelated roots receive the new Fleet Registry revision through normal 0.100 mirror synchronization". The 0.103 hard cut (0.103-design.md:359) folded synchronize/activate into "one synchronization intent", but the code keeps it only for Joining. accept_synchronization rejects anything but an exact replay (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:103-114). The timer exits once the mirror is active (212-219). LifecycleApi::activate_fleet_registry_mirror (api/lifecycle.rs:461) has no caller. I found no doc, status or changelog entry recording this as a known limitation. 0.108-design.md:1032 treats a stale Registry as an invariant failure ("stop funding owner"), and current.md:2675 requires mirror == Coordinator head. Both presume the mirrors converge. The impact is real and reachable from the CLI, not only through the unwired RemoveRoot/ScaleOut. MutateAdmission (canic-cli/src/admission) republishes the Registry (ops/fleet_coordinator/admission.rs:108-116). Root admission never commits the mirror; it uses the mirror only as a fallback (root_admission/mod.rs:70,115). After that, funding sends the mirror version (workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:228), the Coordinator requires an exact match (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:500), and the root gets RegistryStale, then Stop with no ICP fallback (cycles/mod.rs:922,955). A later CLI funding-policy rotation starts at the Coordinator, which requires predecessor == head (funding_rotation.rs:159). PrepareRoot then requires predecessor == mirror (ops/root_funding/mod.rs:171), and I found no abort path. This is not critical. Direct top-up and the pre-1.0 reset/reinstall path still work: reset authority comes from physical inventory and controllers. It is still high under the rubric: routine operator actions leave recovery unable to complete. One note on the fix: the "block the next publication until every root acknowledges" part contradicts 0.101-design.md:2036-2041. The design-consistent fix is to restore Coordinator-authenticated snapshot-convergent resync.
Also reported as: cp-root-admission-funding-3
highverifiedr2-snapshot-restore-consistency-1 · correctness · high confidence
Restoring a Component that uses Fleet admission rolls its admission projection back: principals removed after the backup are admitted again, and the next admission change sticks at Prepare with no release path, blocking all provisioning and removal on that Root
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:94

Failure scenario

Component A uses Fleet admission. T0: A is backed up at generation 3, which includes principal X. T1: the operator removes X; generation 4 converges everywhere. T2: the operator runs `canic restore` of A from the T0 backup. A now returns contains(X)=true, so X regains every admission-gated endpoint on A. T3: the operator adds Y (generation 5). Root reserves, fences, and sends Prepare{expected_generation:4} to A. A is at generation 3 and returns conflict. Root retries every second indefinitely and the Coordinator never converges. Root's catalog fence now rejects ProvisionComponents, every child allocation, and RemoveComponent/RemoveSubtree for every Component on that Root, including A itself. Only a clean Fleet reinstall recovers. Live backups currently cannot be created with the CLI (see the preflight finding), so today this triggers when any other valid manifest is restored; once backup creation is re-enabled it becomes a routine operator path.

Evidence

Restore runs only upload, stop, load, start and a status check (crates/canic-backup/src/restore/apply/mod.rs:76-105); no step involves Root. A snapshot load runs no lifecycle hook. FleetAdmissionProjectionWorkflow::restore is called only from post_upgrade (workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:282,295), and it only checks the state's internal consistency (fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:71-74). contains() answers from the rolled-back local projection (mod.rs:94-101). On the next mutation, Root sends Prepare with the Fleet's current expected_generation (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:105-118). The target policy requires active.generation == expected_generation and Open phase (domain/policy/pure/fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:62-63,88-93), so it returns PhaseConflict. schedule() then retries every second forever (root_admission/mod.rs:80-88). A release is allowed only before the fence and while every participant is still Pending (domain/policy/pure/fleet_admission_root/mod.rs:181-192), so the transition cannot be abandoned. While current_transition exists, require_catalog_mutation_allowed rejects everything (ops/root_admission/mod.rs:383-396). That covers component provisioning (workflow/component_provisioning.rs:100), allocations and child allocations (component_registry/mod.rs:730,788,1125), and RemoveComponent and RemoveSubtree (component_registry/mod.rs:1359,1729). A member captured while Fenced stays Fenced after the load, so contains() is false for every caller (mod.rs:97-99).

Recommendation

Coordinate restore with Root. Before the load, fence the restored member's admission-gated ingress. After start, have Root push its current admission projection through a root-authenticated reconcile command that does not require the predecessor to match. Also make members detect a load, for example by persisting the last observed canister-history count or version and failing contains() closed until Root re-synchronizes. Give the Root admission transition a typed per-participant predecessor-mismatch outcome, or an abort after fence, instead of an infinite 1-second retry. Add a PocketIC test: capture member, converge Remove(X), restore, then assert X is rejected and the next mutation converges.

Verifier (confirmed): I could not refute the chain; each step holds in the code. Restore apply only uploads, stops, loads, starts and verifies (canic-backup/src/restore/apply/mod.rs:76-105). Nothing in it involves Root or admission: grep finds no admission references in canic-backup, and restore readiness checks only checksums and verification (restore/plan/summary.rs:81-84). Normal backup scopes exclude Root (plan/error.rs:47), so Root stays at the newer generation. FleetAdmissionProjectionWorkflow::restore runs only from post_upgrade (workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:282,295) and only validates. contains() backs the caller gate (access/auth/predicates.rs:30). Prepare returns PhaseConflict when the predecessor does not match (policy/pure/fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:62-63,88-93). call_target turns that into an error (root_admission/mod.rs:248-251), and schedule() retries every 1s (80-88). release_fleet_admission_root refuses once the fence is set (fleet_admission_root/mod.rs:181-192). The Coordinator issues Release only in its Releasing phase (ops/fleet_admission/mod.rs:352-368). require_catalog_mutation_allowed rejects while a transition is current (ops/root_admission/mod.rs:383-396). active_policy also returns conflict (375), so reinstalling the component cannot re-seed it either. Root and Coordinator have an AuthorityRestoreFence that detects restores through canister history (storage/stable/authority_restore). Components have none. Two points are overstated. First, reachability today: CLI backup creation fails closed (canic-cli/src/backup/create/executor/mod.rs:45-52,133-136), so triggering this needs an externally produced manifest or a native snapshot load. Second, 'no recovery': restoring a snapshot at the current generation, or the normal pre-1.0 clean reinstall, recovers. It stays high because restore produces a wrong authorization state and leaves recovery unable to complete.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, medium): The code chain holds, but only actors who already have more authority can reach it, and no supported Canic flow reaches it today, so I am downgrading it rather than refuting it. Chain confirmed. contains() answers from the local projection (fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:94-101), and restore() only validates it (71-74). Prepare returns PhaseConflict when the predecessor does not match (policy/pure/fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:62-63,88-93). schedule() retries every 1s (root_admission/mod.rs:80-88). Release is refused once fence_request_hash is set (fleet_admission_root/mod.rs:185). require_catalog_mutation_allowed then blocks catalog changes (ops/root_admission/mod.rs:383-396). Who can trigger it: - Loading a snapshot needs controller rights over A. Component controllers are exactly Root plus recovery_controllers (ids/fleet_topology/mod.rs:253-266, checked by component_registry/mod.rs:198-211). - That actor already controls both A and Root. They can install arbitrary code on A or clean-reinstall the Fleet, which is the normal pre-1.0 recovery. The supported path is dead today: - `canic backup create` always fails at preflight (canic-cli/src/backup/create/executor/mod.rs:45-52,133-136; runner/mod.rs:126-131). - Git history shows that stub arrived in 0.100.80, before Fleet admission existed (0.109.0). So no Canic release that has admission can produce a manifest for `canic restore`. - What remains is a hand-crafted manifest or a native `icp` snapshot load by a controller. Why I keep it at medium instead of refuting it: - Canic plainly treats native snapshot loads as a threat for authority canisters: Root and Coordinator get an AuthorityRestoreFence that detects loads via canister history (workflow/runtime/authority_restore.rs). Components get nothing equivalent. - A routine controller action can silently re-admit a removed principal on A. It also leaves Root's catalog frozen, with no typed abort after the fence. This is a realistic but uncommon operator path. The failure is recoverable by clean reinstall and is self-inflicted by fully privileged actors. It is medium, not high.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, high): I could not refute this finding on intent grounds. The design explicitly forbids the behaviour. 0.109-design.md:200-201 says "stale-generation or fenced local authority denies protected ingress". Security invariants 11 and 13 (0.109-design.md:651,653) say stale projection state denies and that no opened participant serves a predecessor. A Component restored to generation 3 while the Fleet is at 4 does the opposite. It returns contains(X)=true from its stale Open projection (workflow/fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:94-101). The only restore check is internal consistency (mod.rs:71-74, called only from runtime/nonroot.rs:282,295). The project treats native snapshot loads as in scope. The 0.100.94 changelog (docs/changelog/0.100.md:391-420) added an authority restore fence based on Canister history so that restored Roots and Coordinators stay fenced. The 0.109 design then put authority-derived projections on Components without extending that fence to them. No document lists this as a known limitation. AGENTS.md requires same-release restore, and the recommended fix mirrors the existing fence, so it does not contradict the design. Failure scenario

Root's total balance covers an approved grant, but the balance minus the freezing-threshold reserve does not. deposit_cycles fails synchronously with InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance, and the receipt becomes RecoveryRequired. The child retries the same operation ID, because the remote error has code PLATFORM_FAILED and is treated as retryable. Every retry gets REQUEST_INCOMPLETE. Each new operation gets FundingOperationInProgress. After Root is refilled, that child can still never be funded by Canic.

`execute_authorized_request_cycles` marks the costed effect in flight (nonroot_cycles.rs:419-420) and then awaits an unbounded-wait deposit_cycles call (424-425). On any Err, including synchronous InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance, CallPerformFailed or a clean reject, all of which are known not to have executed, it calls `preserve_request_cycles_recovery_required` with ExternalEffectStatusUnknown (432-438, 615-639). `abort_replay_after_failure` removes only Reserved receipts (replay.rs:521-528, ops/replay/mod.rs:270-271, receipt.rs:474-480).

On an exact retry, the receipt falls into the catch-all `RecoveryRequired { .. } => Err(ReplayDuplicateSame)` (handler/replay.rs:171-179). Any new operation from the same child is rejected by `reject_competing_funding_operation`, because RecoveryRequired counts as pending (nonroot_cycles.rs:380-410, storage/stable/replay.rs:401-416). The receipt survives expiry forever (storage/stable/replay.rs:411-416), and no endpoint resolves it.

Approval checks total balance, not liquid balance (nonroot_cycles.rs:365-373, 465-472), so a liquid-balance failure is reachable. The same no-exit applies to any ExternalEffectInFlight receipt whose callback traps after the effect (receipt.rs:546-548), for example ICP refill or provision.

Distinguish outcomes. For an unbounded-wait deposit_cycles, a reject or perform failure is known-not-executed. Restore the ledger snapshot, recover the cost guard, and abort the receipt (a new abort_after_known_unapplied_effect). Reserve ExternalEffectStatusUnknown for genuinely ambiguous cases, and give it a reconciliation path: re-execute idempotently, or add an operator-resolvable terminal. Add a trap-cleanup Drop guard that moves ExternalEffectInFlight receipts to RecoveryRequired.

Failure scenario

A root is configured with icp_refill.minimum_icp_balance_e8s = 0.1 ICP, and the operator funded its default ICP account with 5 ICP for emergencies. After one automatic refill, the operator retires the root. Store deletion, Cycles Ledger evacuation and native reclamation all succeed, the Coordinator issues PrepareRootDeletionExecution, and the root is deleted. The remaining ICP (at least the 0.1 ICP floor, 4 ICP here) sits in an account whose owner principal no longer exists and will never be reused, so it is permanently lost. The conservation evidence never mentions it.

Evidence

Root deletion preparation evacuates only the Cycles Ledger account (root_ledger_retirement::evacuate, which reads CyclesLedgerOps::balance_of and transfers from it at lines 31-55) and native cycles (reclaim_root_deletion_cycles, fleet_subnet_root.rs:1520-1570). The funding fence checks only that no refill operation is resumable (fleet_subnet_root.rs:642-650). The Coordinator's deletion-execution validation checks only the Cycles Ledger receipt (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_deletion/mod.rs:126, 452-456).

Meanwhile the root holds ICP by design. The automatic refill source is the root's default ICP account (workflow/ic/icp_refill/automatic.rs:157-167), and the refill policy requires a floor of amount + fee + minimum_icp_balance_e8s to remain (domain/policy/pure/icp_refill.rs:195-210). No Canic endpoint can move root ICP anywhere except the CMC top-up path, so an operator cannot empty the floor before retiring. The 0.110 design says retirement should "account for every controlled native and Ledger balance".

Recommendation

Add an ICP evacuation step to deletion preparation, alongside the Cycles Ledger step: - Observe icrc1_balance_of for the root's default account and any source subaccounts used by manual refills. - Transfer balance minus fee to a reviewed destination (for example the operator or treasury), with a durable intent and a created_at_time plus memo. - Require a zero balance, or a remainder at or below the fee recorded as terminal discard, before readiness. - Include the ICP receipt in root_deletion validation. The refill-policy floor should not apply to this evacuation.

highverifiedxc-robustness-1 · robustness · medium confidence
Lifecycle drivers each take a slot in ic-timers' 64-entry registry with no concurrency bound, and `defer_lifecycle_required` traps when the registry is full, so ordinary concurrency or command replays can kill every Root lifecycle driver and pin their slots until restart
crates/canic-core/src/api/timer.rs:87

Failure scenario

1. A removal or registry synchronization is waiting on a slow dependency. Its chains retry every 1 second (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:371-373; fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:200-201). 2. The operator re-runs `fleet ensure` or retries RemoveComponent/SynchronizeRegistry after lost responses. Alternatively, many components request distinct child or peer allocations at once. Each replay or operation adds a live chain. 3. After about 54 chains the registry is full. Every endpoint that schedules lifecycle work (ProvisionComponent/Peer/Child, RemoveComponent, RemoveSubtree, SynchronizeRegistry) now traps, which blocks fleet control. 4. Any running chain that tries to reschedule traps after its awaits. The step's post-await writes (including recorded effect responses) roll back, the chain dies, and its Running entry is never removed, so capacity falls further. For allocations, the op id stays in `SCHEDULED_COMPONENT_ALLOCATIONS`, so later re-arms are silently ignored. 5. Root lifecycle orchestration stays wedged until an upgrade or reinstall clears the heap. After that, only provisioning and the pool resume automatically (api/lifecycle.rs:977-986); everything else must be re-issued by hand.

Evidence

`defer_lifecycle_required` maps any registration error to `ic_cdk::trap("lifecycle timer rejected")` (api/timer.rs:81-88). `register_lifecycle_once` gives every call a fresh identity with `RemoveWhenStopped` (workflow/runtime/timer/mod.rs:351-396). ic-timers caps the registry at `MAX_TIMER_REGISTRATIONS = 64` and returns CapacityExceeded when full (ic-timers-0.8.0 registry/mod.rs:24,728). The registry is shared with about 10 fixed claims (intent, log, cycles, sampling, auth, placement, watchdogs, pool).

An entry is removed only after its callback future completes (runtime/mod.rs:1167-1176). A chain therefore holds its own slot while it registers its successor (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:40-42, 193-214, 368-374, 700-704).

There is no deduplication or concurrency limit:
- `schedule_component_removal` (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:352-354), `schedule_subtree_removal` (682-684), `schedule_registry_synchronization` (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:185-187) and `schedule_root_removal` (fleet_subnet_root.rs:555-557) start a new chain on every call.
- `accept_synchronization` explicitly accepts exact replays and still schedules again (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:98-121).
- RemoveComponent/RemoveSubtree replays return the existing draining record and then schedule (root.rs:690-711, component_registry/mod.rs:1350-1357).

Allocation drivers are deduplicated, but through a heap set that keeps the op id if the callback traps (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:20-26, 35-38).

Recommendation

Deduplicate every driver by operation key, as the allocation drivers already do, and remove the key in both the success path and the terminal-error path. Also clear it when a replay finds the chain gone. Bound the number of concurrent lifecycle chains below the registry capacity minus the fixed claims, and return a typed REQUEST_CAPACITY error instead of trapping. Make in-callback rescheduling non-trapping: return a TimerRunResult with a retry directive, or hand off to a single watchdog-driven reconciler that scans durable operations. Longer term, drive these state machines from one `Watchdog` or `AfterCompletion` claim per domain rather than one `Once` per operation.

It removes an entry only inside `complete_ordinary` after the future returns (runtime/mod.rs:1164-1176; registry/mod.rs:1271-1284), and its README says Once gives "No automatic recovery" on a trap. +//! Repro for xc-robustness-1: unbounded lifecycle deferrals against the
+//! 64-entry ic-timers registry, and the trap in `defer_lifecycle_required`.
+
+use super::*;
+use crate::api::timer::TimerApi;
+use std::panic::{AssertUnwindSafe, catch_unwind};
+
+fn panic_text(payload: &(dyn std::any::Any + Send)) -> String {
+    payload
+        .downcast_ref::<String>()
+        .cloned()
+        .or_else(|| payload.downcast_ref::<&str>().map(|s| (*s).to_string()))
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| "<non-string panic>".to_string())
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_lifecycle_deferrals_are_bounded_and_do_not_trap_when_registry_full() {
+    // Step 1: the shared ic-timers runtime must exist for any registration.
+    let init = catch_unwind(TimerAuthorityWorkflow::initialize_shared_runtime);
+    match &init {
+        Ok(result) => println!("initialize_shared_runtime -> {:?}", result.as_ref().map(|_| ())),
+        Err(payload) => println!("initialize_shared_runtime panicked: {}", panic_text(payload.as_ref())),
+    }
+    assert!(
+        matches!(init, Ok(Ok(()))),
+        "setup: ic-timers runtime could not be initialized natively"
+    );
+
+    // Step 2: register more one-shot lifecycle deferrals than the registry holds.
+    let mut first_failure = None;
+    for index in 0..=ic_timers::MAX_TIMER_REGISTRATIONS {
+        let result = TimerAuthorityWorkflow::defer_lifecycle_once(
+            Duration::from_secs(60),
+            format!("repro-{index}"),
+            async {},
+        );
+        if let Err(error) = result {
+            first_failure = Some((index, error));
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+    println!("first lifecycle registration failure: {first_failure:?}");
+
+    // Correct behaviour: Canic bounds its own lifecycle chains below the provider
+    // capacity so fixed claims keep their slots, and the endpoint adapter does not
+    // trap when that bound is reached.
+    let trapped = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
+        TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required(Duration::from_secs(60), "repro-overflow", async {});
+    }));
+    if let Err(payload) = &trapped {
+        println!("defer_lifecycle_required panicked: {}", panic_text(payload.as_ref()));
+    }
+    assert!(trapped.is_ok(), "defer_lifecycle_required trapped at registry capacity");
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn repro_defer_lifecycle_required_traps_on_any_registration_error() {
+    // No runtime on this fresh test thread: the provider rejects registration.
+    let typed = TimerAuthorityWorkflow::defer_lifecycle_once(
+        Duration::from_secs(60),
+        "repro-typed",
+        async {},
+    );
+    println!("defer_lifecycle_once without runtime -> {typed:?}");
+    assert!(matches!(
+        typed,
+        Err(TimerError::Provider(ProviderError::NotInitialized))
+    ));
+
+    // The endpoint-facing adapter converts that same rejection into a trap.
+    let trapped = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
+        TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required(Duration::from_secs(60), "repro-trap", async {});
+    }));
+    if let Err(payload) = &trapped {
+        println!("defer_lifecycle_required panicked: {}", panic_text(payload.as_ref()));
+    }
+    assert!(
+        trapped.is_ok(),
+        "defer_lifecycle_required trapped instead of surfacing the typed registration error"
+    );
+}
mediumunverifiedbackup-persistence-3 · correctness · medium confidence
Relative backup output paths are passed to `icp snapshot download`, which runs in the workspace root, while canic pre-creates and hashes the temp directory relative to its own working directory.
crates/canic-cli/src/backup/create/executor/mod.rs:33

Failure scenario

1. The operator runs `canic backup create prod` from `apps/prod/`. The workspace root, two levels up, becomes icp_root. 2. Canic creates `apps/prod/backups/deployment-prod-…/<id>.tmp`, empty. 3. icp, running in the root, writes to `<root>/backups/deployment-prod-…/<id>.tmp`. If icp creates the missing directories, canic hashes its own empty directory (the sha256 of an empty listing), commits it as Durable and publishes a manifest, and `backup verify` passes. The result is a verified backup with no data, noticed only at restore time. If icp refuses, the backup fails after the Stop, CreateSnapshot and Start effects have already run.

Evidence

backup_create uses `options.out` or default_backup_output_path, which is the relative `backups/deployment-<fleet>-<stamp>` (create/mod.rs:40-43, create/plan.rs:68-74). That path becomes BackupRunnerConfig.out unchanged (create/mod.rs:88-95), and temp paths are root.join("<id>.tmp") (runner/operations/path.rs:17-19). The executor builds IcpCli with `.with_cwd(&icp_root)` (executor/mod.rs:31-35). icp_root is found by walking up from the current directory (canic-host icp_config/mod.rs:230-237, config_discovery/mod.rs:54-63). IcpCli::command sets current_dir(cwd) (canic-host icp/command.rs:124-131), and snapshot_download passes `--output <artifact_path>` as-is (icp/snapshot.rs:37-41). Meanwhile canic itself creates an empty 0700 temp directory relative to its own working directory before the download (runner/operations/artifacts.rs:273-296). Afterwards it only checks that this directory still exists (299-325), then hashes it and records ChecksumVerified (340-369). Today the path is gated only by the preflight stub (executor/mod.rs:45-53).

Recommendation

Make the layout root absolute once in backup_create, for example with std::path::absolute(out) or by canonicalizing the created directory, before building BackupRunnerConfig. Alternatively, have the executor absolutize artifact_path against canic's working directory before spawning icp. Add a test that runs from a subdirectory of the workspace.
