mediumunverifiedbackup-persistence-4 · correctness · high confidence
The finalize manifest embeds the current wall-clock time and tool version, so a resumed FinalizeManifest can never adopt its own previously published manifest and stays stuck on ManifestConflict.
crates/canic-backup/src/runner/manifest.rs:22

Failure scenario

1. Finalize publishes the manifest with created_at `unix:T`. 2. The process is killed, or the execution-journal write fails with ENOSPC, before the Completed receipt is durable. 3. The operator resumes at T+5s. The rebuilt manifest has `unix:T+5`, so publish_manifest returns ManifestConflict and FinalizeManifest is recorded Failed. 4. Every retry repeats this. Result: `backup list` shows Failed, `backup verify` refuses with DryRunNotComplete, and only hand-deleting the manifest recovers the backup. The path is latent while the CLI preflight is stubbed.

Evidence

build_manifest sets `created_at: state_updated_at(config.updated_at.as_ref())` and `tool.version: config.tool_version` (runner/manifest.rs:19-26). state_updated_at falls back to current_timestamp_marker() (timestamp/mod.rs:15-17), and the CLI passes `updated_at: None` (backup/create/mod.rs:88-95). publish_manifest adopts an existing manifest only if its serialized bytes are identical, otherwise it returns ManifestConflict (persistence/layout.rs:76-124). A Pending FinalizeManifest has no command lock, so prepare_backup_operation returns Ok(None) (runner/mod.rs:279-290) and execute_finalize_manifest rebuilds and republishes (runner/operations/artifacts.rs:387-445). reject_premature_manifest allows Pending and Failed (runner/mod.rs:98-104). Every recovery test pins `updated_at: Some("unix:10")` (persistence/tests/operational_readiness/download_effect.rs:470-477), which masks the problem. pending_finalize_rejects_conflicting_manifest_without_replacing_it (manifest_publication.rs:72-99) shows that a created_at difference leads to ManifestConflict and a Failed finalize.

Recommendation

Derive the manifest's time-dependent fields from durable state, for example the finalize operation's state_updated_at, which is persisted when the operation is marked Pending, before the effect. Alternatively, compare all fields except provenance on adoption. Add a crash-recovery test with `updated_at: None`.

Verifier (): The verifier returned no result for this finding.
mediumconfirmedbackup-restore-3 · operability · high confidence
Snapshots created by backup and uploaded by restore are never deleted, so they keep billing storage and eventually exhaust the per-canister snapshot limit.
crates/canic-backup/src/runner/operations/artifacts.rs:54

Failure scenario

An operator backs up a fleet nightly and occasionally restores in place. Every member gains one retained snapshot per backup and one per restore, each as large as its heap plus stable memory, charged as storage continuously (for a few-GB canister this is a standing multiple of its storage burn). After the per-canister snapshot limit is reached, CreateSnapshot and UploadSnapshot fail. This triggers the mixed-window backup retry and the lost-baseline restore wedge described in the other findings.

Evidence

execute_create_snapshot calls `executor.create_snapshot(&target, ...)` (artifacts.rs:54-57). The host wrapper runs `icp canister snapshot create <canister> --json` with no replace argument (crates/canic-host/src/icp/snapshot.rs:13-19), and no backup phase deletes the source snapshot after download (plan/build/phases.rs:39-80). Restore's operation kinds are only Stop, Start, Upload, Load, VerifyMember and VerifyDeployment (restore/apply/journal/types.rs:416-423), so each uploaded snapshot stays on its target after load. A grep of canic-backup, canic-host and canic-cli finds no snapshot delete or replace path. The IC management API supports `replace_snapshot` on both take and upload (ic-management-canister-types TakeCanisterSnapshotArgs and UploadCanisterSnapshotMetadataArgs). The README's 'local pruning kept separate from live snapshot deletion' has no live-deletion counterpart.

Recommendation

After a verified durable download, delete the source snapshot, or pass replace for the previous Canic-created snapshot. After a successful load and verification, add a journalled DeleteUploadedSnapshot operation, or pass replace_snapshot on upload. At minimum, report retained snapshot counts and sizes in backup and restore status.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. execute_create_snapshot (crates/canic-backup/src/runner/operations/artifacts.rs:54-57) calls IcpCli::snapshot_create, which runs `icp canister snapshot create <canister> --json` with no `--replace` (crates/canic-host/src/icp/snapshot.rs:13-19). The restore upload command is `snapshot upload <target> --input <path> --json`, also without `--replace` (crates/canic-backup/src/restore/apply/journal/commands/mod.rs:151-172), and load is `snapshot restore` (lines 174-190). No backup phase deletes snapshots (plan/build/phases.rs:39-80), and a grep of canic-backup, canic-host and canic-cli finds no snapshot delete or replace path. The installed icp CLI offers `snapshot delete` and `--replace` on both create and upload, so the capability exists and Canic does not use it. No design or runbook says retaining live snapshots is intended. docs/features/backup-and-restore/README.md:15 only says local pruning is kept separate from live snapshot deletion, and nothing else performs that deletion. Result: each backup leaves one full heap-plus-stable-memory snapshot on every member, and each restore leaves one uploaded snapshot on every target. These keep billing storage, and once the IC per-canister snapshot limit is reached, later create or upload calls fail with a typed error. The failure is recoverable (delete snapshots with icp and start a new backup) and does not violate cycle conservation, so medium is right.
mediumconfirmedbackup-restore-4 · liveness · high confidence
The upload's sticky pre-effect inventory makes deleting an old snapshot, the natural fix for a snapshot-limit failure, permanently block the upload operation.
crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/execute.rs:554

Failure scenario

Upload of member 3 fails because the target already holds the maximum number of snapshots. Retained snapshots make this likely (see the snapshot-accumulation finding). The operator deletes an obsolete snapshot with icp, runs `--retry-failed` and then `--execute`. Every run returns SnapshotInventoryLostBaseline. The only way out is deleting the journal by hand and re-preparing, which re-uploads members 0-2 and leaves more orphan snapshots.

Evidence

The inventory is observed only when `snapshot_ids_before.is_none()` (execute.rs:193-208) and is stored at the first claim (212-218). Failed and retried states keep it (journal/types.rs:175-189 requires it for Failed; journal/mod.rs:292-303 does not clear it). On every later attempt reconcile_upload_operation returns `SnapshotInventoryLostBaseline` if any baseline ID is missing (execute.rs:550-559). That happens before the claim, so the op stays Ready and each rerun fails the same way. There is no journal operation that refreshes the baseline. The design forbids editing journals (0.94-design.md:272), and re-running prepare conflicts with the existing journal (restore/persistence/mod.rs:63-85). The backup runner has the same strictness (runner/mod.rs:622-633).

Recommendation

Distinguish baseline shrink from identity ambiguity. If baseline IDs are missing and no new ID appeared (or the previous attempt is known to have failed before metadata upload), allow a journalled baseline refresh, for example a typed `--refresh-upload-baseline` recovery action that records the old and new inventories. Apply the same fix to backup CreateSnapshot reconciliation.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed, with one correction: the restore as a whole is not permanently stuck. The inventory is observed only when `snapshot_ids_before.is_none()` (crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/execute.rs:193-208) and is stored at the first claim (212-218). transition_operation (restore/apply/journal/mod.rs:339-369) never clears it, and retry_failed_operation_at (292-303) only moves the op back to Ready. After that, reconcile_restore_operation still treats the op as recovering because `snapshot_ids_before.is_some()` (execute.rs:465-467), and reconcile_upload_operation returns SnapshotInventoryLostBaseline if any baseline ID is missing (550-559). That error is propagated with `?` before the claim (166-171), so every rerun fails the same way. Any deletion the operator makes to free space removes an ID that is in the baseline. The 0.94 design lets operators use documented platform operations but forbids editing journals (0.94-design.md:272-276), and it treats a permanently halted upload as a closeout failure. Correction: `restore prepare --journal-out <new>` followed by `restore run --journal <new>` (crates/canic-cli/src/restore/options.rs:105,148,224) re-prepares from scratch, redoing members that were already restored and leaving more orphan snapshots. So this is a confusing but recoverable failure, which is medium. The backup CreateSnapshot path has the same check (runner/mod.rs:622-633), and rearm_after_failure_containment (execution/mod.rs:222-267) does not reset it; there, a fresh --out avoids it.
mediumconfirmedbackup-restore-6 · contract · medium confidence
Restore is never bound to the current release, topology or target identity, so an old or foreign backup can be loaded in place with no check before the destructive load.
crates/canic-backup/src/restore/plan/mod.rs:43

Failure scenario

After an ID-preserving reset to release N+1, an operator restores a subtree backup taken under release N. Upload, stop, load and start all succeed, and verification passes because it compares against the old snapshot's module hash. The children now run release-N code and state under a release-N+1 root: a mixed-version fleet and a cross-release state restore, both of which policy forbids, achieved with no warning.

Evidence

RestorePlanner::plan uses only the manifest and mapping (plan/mod.rs:39-78). RestorePlan carries source_environment, root and topology_hash but no release or tool binding (plan/types.rs:57-72). Nothing in the planner, the dry-run or the runner compares manifest.tool.version, the release, or topology_hash with the live fleet, or checks target module hashes or controllers before the first stop or load. The only live checks are the stopped-status precondition and post-start verification (restore/runner/execute.rs:245-254, 414-427). A grep for tool version in restore and manifest code finds only non-empty validation (manifest/validation/sections.rs:25). Project policy says backup and restore are for same-release recovery only and designs must not produce mixed-version operation (AGENTS.md; docs/features/backup-and-restore/README.md).

Recommendation

Record the release identity (release set or build ID) and the fleet identity in the manifest and plan. At prepare and run time, compare them with the terminal Fleet Ensure inventory and each target's current module hash, and refuse a mismatch unless an explicit, journalled override is given.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed as described. RestorePlanner::plan (crates/canic-backup/src/restore/plan/mod.rs:39-78) validates only the manifest and mapping. It copies source_environment, root and topology_hash into the plan, and plan/validation.rs:29-31 only checks that they are non-empty or valid hashes. A grep for source_environment, topology_hash and tool.version in restore/ finds no comparison with live state. The CLI prepare path (crates/canic-cli/src/restore/mod.rs:111-156) reads the manifest, mapping and artifacts, and nothing else. restore run takes an operator-supplied --environment (options.rs:193) that is never compared with manifest.source.environment. Its only binding check is the journal backup_root path (io.rs:150-172). resolve_backup_reference (canic-cli/src/backup/reference/resolve.rs:27-66) accepts any listed backup. Load verification compares the status against the manifest's own module hash (execute.rs:401-427), so an old-release restore verifies as success. This conflicts with docs/features/backup-and-restore/README.md:29-32 (same-release recovery only) and with canic-cli/README.md, which says authority-bearing Fleet commands read the terminal fleet ensure inventory. It is reachable through a routine operator mistake: after an ID-preserving reset, `restore prepare` then `run --execute` with an old backup. Within one release, a stale topology_hash also lets a root restore drop registry rows for children created after the backup. The target must still be controlled (upload is controller-only), so this is a missing guardrail on an operator action, not an escalation. Medium fits.
mediumconfirmedcli-core-1 · correctness · medium confidence
fleet ensure picks a different reset/reinstall workflow depending on whether --environment was typed, because its three pre-selectors use three different environment defaults
crates/canic-cli/src/fleet/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:23

Failure scenario

Two cases: 1. A local Fleet `demo` has a completed-source reset review pending. The operator runs the documented form `canic fleet ensure demo --desired fleets/demo.toml --apply <reset-review-digest>` without `--environment`. `clean_reinstall::selected("local", reinstall=false, applying=true)` returns false because no `clean-reinstall.json` exists. The completed-reset and preparation selectors are skipped because no environment was typed. Ordinary `apply` then decodes the predecessor plan and fails with a decode error or PlanDigestMismatch. The identical command prefixed with `canic --environment local` routes to `completed_reset` and succeeds. 2. A completed `staging` Fleet (desired `environment = "staging"`). `canic fleet ensure staging --reinstall` checks the clean-reinstall selector against `.canic/fleet-ensure/local/staging`, which does not exist, skips retirement, and falls into `plan_reinstall` for staging. With `--environment staging` it would take the clean-reinstall path instead.

Evidence

`run_ensure` (fleet/mod.rs:506-517) runs three selectors before loading the desired document, and each resolves the environment differently:
- `clean_reinstall::run_if_selected` uses `options.environment.as_deref().unwrap_or("local")` (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:23).
- `completed_reset::retire_if_selected` and `run_if_selected` do nothing unless `--environment` was passed (completed_reset/mod.rs:21, 37-39).
- `completed_preparation::run_if_selected` also returns false when `--environment` is absent (completed_preparation/mod.rs:20-22).
- The ordinary path takes the environment from the desired file when the flag is missing (fleet/mod.rs:652-680).

The environment is only forwarded when the operator types it, because `apply_global_environment` returns early on `None` (cli/globals.rs:117-119). INSTALLING.md:153-162 and walkthrough:61,81-84 show `canic fleet ensure <fleet> --desired ... --apply <digest>` without `--environment`. When no selector claims the call, the ordinary `apply` decodes the retained plan (`verified_plan(retained_plan::read(..))`, canic-host fleet_ensure/workflow/mod.rs:1070-1074) and `plan_reinstall` decodes predecessor plans. The completed-reset and clean-reinstall owners are written specifically to avoid that decoding.

Recommendation

Resolve one effective environment before any selector runs: the explicit flag, else the desired file's `environment` (loaded only as far as needed), or refuse when neither exists. Pass that value to all three selectors and to `retire_if_selected`. Add a test asserting the same routing with and without an explicit, equal `--environment`.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. The top-level `--environment` has no default (cli/help.rs:196, globals.rs:51-56), and `apply_global_environment` returns early on None (globals.rs:117-119), so `options.environment` is None unless typed. `clean_reinstall::run_if_selected` falls back to "local" (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:23). `retire_if_selected` and both `run_if_selected` functions do nothing without the flag (completed_reset/mod.rs:21,37-39; completed_preparation/mod.rs:20-22). The ordinary path instead takes the environment from the desired file (fleet/mod.rs:662-680). For a completed staging Fleet, `fleet ensure X --desired .. --reinstall` without the flag checks `.canic/fleet-ensure/local/X` (host clean_reinstall/mod.rs:44-65) and gets false. It skips retirement and reaches `plan_reinstall`, which runs `verified_plan(read_plan)` on the predecessor plan (reinstall/mod.rs:65-68). That is exactly the predecessor decoding the .45 correction removed, so older-release plans fail to decode and same-release ones get the older preparation review. Impact is limited: every outcome is a typed refusal or a reviewed plan, with no effect before an approved digest. The documented staging reset commands include `--environment` (fleet-ensure.md:246-262), and completed_reset's printed apply command always adds it (completed_reset/mod.rs:225-238). The inconsistency is still real and reachable with the ordinary INSTALLING.md form (169-173). Medium.
mediumconfirmedcli-core-2 · performance · medium confidence
canic info list starts one OS thread and several icp subprocesses per registry entry with no concurrency bound, and each cycles cell triggers a Root update call
crates/canic-cli/src/list/live/mod.rs:214

Failure scenario

A Fleet with a few hundred canisters, and `canic info list prod` run on macOS (default `ulimit -n` of 256). Hundreds of concurrent `icp` children, each holding piped stdout/stderr, exhaust file descriptors. Spawns fail, and many CYCLES and CANIC cells print `error` even though the canisters are healthy. With thousands of entries, thread creation can fail and the CLI panics with exit 101. Meanwhile Root receives hundreds of simultaneous InspectCanister update calls from a command labelled read-only.

Evidence

`collect_visible_entry_values` calls `thread::spawn` once per visible entry and joins them all afterwards (list/live/mod.rs:208-222). It is called for canic versions (82-98), cycle balances (62-80) and, on local transport, readiness (170-196).

Each worker builds a fresh `IcpCli` via `live_icp` (262-269). The version-qualification cache is per instance (canic-host icp/version.rs:19-30), so every worker first runs `icp --version` before its real call.

Cycle balances go through `observe_fleet_canister`, which runs `preflight_inspection` and then an update call to the Fleet Subnet Root with `CANIC_ROOT_COMMAND` InspectCanister (canic-host observability/mod.rs:134-172).

Peak concurrency therefore equals the Fleet size, with no cap. `std::thread::spawn` panics if the OS refuses a thread. By contrast `canic observatory snapshot` bounds the same fan-out with `--maximum-canisters` (default 128, observatory/mod.rs:58).

Recommendation

Run the per-entry work through a bounded worker pool (for example 8-16 workers, or a `--jobs` option). Share one `IcpCli` across workers so version qualification runs once. Consider a shared maximum-canisters bound matching observatory, and document that cycle cells issue Root update calls.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. `collect_visible_entry_values` calls `thread::spawn` once per visible entry and only joins afterwards, with no bound (list/live/mod.rs:208-222). `run_list_options` calls it for readiness (local transport only; the remote path is sequential, 52-58), versions and cycles in sequence (list/mod.rs:88-92), so peak concurrency is the Fleet size in each phase. Each worker builds a fresh `IcpCli` (live/mod.rs:262-269), and its version cache is per instance (icp/version.rs:19-30). Each cycles cell runs `preflight_inspection` and then a `call_canister_with_arg` InspectCanister to Root (observability/mod.rs:133-170). `std::thread::spawn` panics when the OS refuses a thread, which aborts the CLI. Subprocess spawn failures from fd exhaustion become `error` cells. Observatory bounds the same kind of fan-out (`--maximum-canisters`, default 128, observatory/mod.rs:58). Some limits on impact: the damage stays on the operator host, and the total number of Root calls is the same whatever the concurrency. Only the burst and the fd/thread pressure are new. Exact fd thresholds depend on the host's ulimit. Medium stands, as resource exhaustion that makes a routine monitoring command unreliable as Fleets grow.
mediumconfirmedcli-ops-1 · correctness · high confidence
`canic cycles funding` always fails for a Fleet whose Registry contains a Removed Fleet Subnet Root, because it compares and queries every Registry Root without skipping Removed entries
crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/funding.rs:389

Failure scenario

An operator drains and removes one Root of a multi-subnet Fleet through fleet ensure, and the ensure converges. From then on, `canic cycles funding demo` exits with "live Registry authority or Root set conflicts with terminal current ensure authority". The operator loses the funding and headroom diagnostic, which is also what `docs/operations/fleet-funding.md` tells them to use, for the rest of that Fleet's life.

Evidence

`validate_registry_authority` (funding.rs:387-398) builds `expected_roots` from `current.topology.fleet_subnet_root_canister_ids`. It builds `live_roots` from ALL `live.fleet_subnet_roots` and requires `live_roots == expected_roots`. The topology excludes Removed Roots: `initial_active_registry` filters `status != Removed` before comparing with it (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/inventory/mod.rs:164-178, 440-456). Root removal keeps the Registry entry and only flips its status (crates/canic-core/src/ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:728), and nothing prunes such entries. So after any Root removal the live Registry has one more Root than the topology, and the check always returns FundingAuthority. Even without that check, the loop at funding.rs:256-265 would call `current_binding` and `query_root` on the Removed (deleted) Root, and `validate_coordinator_status` compares Root counts including Removed entries (funding.rs:421). Neighbouring commands filter Removed correctly: info_subnets/model.rs:108-113 and admission/mod.rs:367.

Recommendation

Filter `FleetSubnetRootStatus::Removed` out of `live_roots` in `validate_registry_authority`, out of the Root loop in `collect_funding`, and out of the Root count and matching in `validate_coordinator_status`, the same way info_subnets and admission do. Add a unit test with a Registry that contains a Removed Root.

Verifier (confirmed): The defect is real. `validate_registry_authority` (crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/funding.rs:381-404) compares every live `fleet_subnet_roots` principal against `current.topology.fleet_subnet_root_canister_ids`, and that topology excludes Removed roots (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/inventory/mod.rs:164-178, 446-456). `compile_removed` only changes the status to Removed (crates/canic-core/src/ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:728), and nothing prunes the entry (no retain/remove on fleet_subnet_roots). Removal can be reached through the controller-gated `CoordinatorCommand::RemoveRoot` (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:92; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1868), and the status doc lists autonomous Root removal as a maintained recovery case. The reviewer's path needs one correction: removal happens through the Coordinator command, not fleet ensure. That changes the route, not the outcome. If a later ensure converges, the topology leaves the Root out and the set check fails with FundingAuthority. If the operator uses the stale pre-removal ensure record, the set check passes, because both sides then include the Root and the Coordinator status also lists Removed entries (ops/fleet_coordinator/root_funding.rs:268-279). The loop at funding.rs:256-265 then calls `query_root` on the removed or deleted Root, and the whole command fails. Either way the command cannot run after a removal. info_subnets/model.rs:108-113 filters Removed correctly. Medium is right: this is a read-only diagnostic, but the failure is permanent for that Fleet.
mediumconfirmedcli-ops-3 · performance · medium confidence
`info cycles` and `info metrics` start one unbounded OS thread per canister, each running several `icp` subprocesses that are mostly Root update calls, which can exhaust thread or process limits (`thread::spawn` panics) and flood Root as Fleets grow
crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/transport.rs:128

Failure scenario

On a Fleet with around 3000 canisters, `canic info cycles prod` starts about 3000 threads and up to about 12000 `icp` processes at once. On macOS (default maxproc around 2666) or Linux with RLIMIT_NPROC, forks fail and many rows show spurious errors. Otherwise thread creation fails and the command panics. Root receives thousands of concurrent ingress updates, and boundary-node rate limiting turns the diagnostic into mostly errors.

Evidence

`collect_cycle_tracker_reports` calls `thread::spawn` once for every visible registry row with no concurrency limit (cycles/transport.rs:116-139). `collect_metrics_reports` does the same for every filtered entry (metrics/transport.rs:83-98). Fleets may hold up to MAX_FLEET_ENSURE_CANISTERS = 4096 canisters (canic-host fleet_ensure/model/mod.rs:25). Each cycles worker runs up to four `icp` subprocesses: balance, a history page (twice when total > limit) and top-ups. For non-root canisters, `observe_fleet_canister` makes every one of these an UPDATE call to Root's `canic_root_command` (InspectCanister or ObserveCanister, see canic-host observability/mod.rs:134-150, 178-188). Root then makes an inter-canister call to the child. `std::thread::spawn` panics if the OS refuses to create a thread. Worker panics are caught at join, but a spawn failure in the loop aborts the whole command. The same pattern exists in list/live/mod.rs:214 (outside this unit).

Recommendation

Use a bounded worker pool (for example 8 to 16 workers via `std::thread::scope` and a work queue, or `available_parallelism`) shared by cycles and metrics. Spawn with `thread::Builder::spawn` and map failures to per-canister errors. Consider batching observations through one Root call per subnet.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. `collect_cycle_tracker_reports` calls `thread::spawn` once per visible row, with no bound (crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/transport.rs:116-139). `collect_metrics_reports` does the same for each filtered entry (crates/canic-cli/src/metrics/transport.rs:83-98). `std::thread::spawn` panics if the OS refuses a thread, and that happens in the loop outside the join-time panic recovery, so the whole command aborts. Registry size is bounded only by `MAX_FLEET_ENSURE_CANISTERS = 4_096` (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/model/mod.rs:25). For non-Root rows, `observe_fleet_canister` makes each observation a preflight plus an update call to Root's `canic_root_command` (InspectCanister or ObserveCanister; crates/canic-host/src/observability/mod.rs:134-188; crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:189-196). `measure_canister_inspection` only records timing and does not limit concurrency (crates/canic-host/src/icp/timing/mod.rs:102-116). The host side already has a bounded pattern: `bounded_observations::MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 4` with `thread::scope` (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/bounded_observations/mod.rs:9-36), but the CLI diagnostics do not use it. Impact is limited to operator diagnostics and Root ingress load. No state is corrupted and total paid calls do not grow, so medium (bounded resource exhaustion that grows with fleet size) is appropriate. The same pattern is at list/live/mod.rs:214.
mediumconfirmedcli-ops-4 · correctness · medium confidence
The convert pending log reuses any old `pending_send` record with the same (environment, fleet, root, subaccount, amount), so a later new conversion can silently replay an already completed operation, and `--json` output hides the reuse
crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/convert/operation.rs:92

Failure scenario

1. The first `canic cycles convert demo R --icp-e8s 100000000` loses its response, so the record stays pending_send with id X. 2. The operator resumes with `--operation-id X`, which succeeds, but the record is never completed. 3. A week later, automation runs the same command with `--json` to convert another 1 ICP. The CLI reuses X, Root replays the old Completed result, and the output shows status Completed. 4. No ICP was converted, and Root stays underfunded with no signal in JSON.

Evidence

`reserve_pending_icp_refill_operation` returns the newest `pending_send` record whose operation_key matches (pending.rs:164-173). The key has no age limit and no per-intent nonce (pending.rs:366-378). A record is marked completed only when the default path's status read is non-resumable (mod.rs:118-120). The `--operation-id` resume path returns `Provided` with no log key (operation.rs:80-82), so `mark_pending_operation_completed` never touches the existing record (operation.rs:62). The reuse is only reported by `write_generated_operation_id_notice`, which returns immediately in JSON mode (operation.rs:107-109). The JSON status render has no `operation_id_source` (response.rs:47-57). Dry-run never reads the log and prints a freshly generated id, which is not the id the real run will send (operation.rs:89-91). Root replays a known operation id and does not execute it again (canic-core workflow/ic/icp_refill/manual.rs:65-76).

Recommendation

Include `operation_id_source` and `reused_pending_record` in the JSON outputs. When `--operation-id` matches a pending record's id, mark that record completed after a terminal status. Give pending records a staleness bound, or require explicit confirmation (`--resume` / `--new`) when a pending record is reused. Have dry-run consult the pending log and report the id it will actually use.

Verifier (confirmed): The code matches the claim. reserve_pending_icp_refill_operation reuses the newest pending_send record whose key matches (pending.rs:164-173). The key covers only env, fleet, root, subaccount and amount, with no age limit (pending.rs:366-378). The --operation-id path returns Provided with key None (operation.rs:80-81), so mark_pending_operation_completed does nothing (operation.rs:62). A record orphaned that way, or one left because the operator never re-ran after a lost status read (mod.rs:108-120), is picked up by the next identical conversion. Root's ICP-refill receipts never expire: icp_refill_replay_reserve_input (replay.rs:57-71) uses ReplayReceiptReserveInput::new, which sets expires_at_ns to None (receipt.rs:85), and classify returns ReturnCommitted (receipt.rs:559-566). So Root replays the old Completed response and no ICP moves. In JSON mode the reuse notice is suppressed (operation.rs:107-109), and response.rs:47-57 has no source field. Some of this is documented: changelog 0.61.md:385-395 says JSON output stays unchanged and --operation-id bypasses the log, and the runbook (recovery-retry-runbooks.md:188) says to repeat the exact command. The combination still produces a false Completed with no conversion. No funds are lost and the fix is to re-run, so medium is right.
mediumconfirmedcli-ops-6 · correctness · high confidence
A registered issuer whose local protocol binding or Candid file cannot be resolved is misreported as `issuer_unregistered`, and medic then recommends reinstalling the dependency closure
crates/canic-cli/src/auth/mod.rs:661

Failure scenario

An operator runs medic from a checkout whose `.icp/<env>/canisters/<issuer-role>/*.did` artifact is missing, for example after cleaning build outputs or on a fresh CI runner. The issuer is registered and healthy on chain. Medic warns `status=issuer_unregistered` and tells the operator to reinstall the dependency closure. Pre-1.0 releases are reinstall-only, so following that advice wipes the application state of those canisters.

Evidence

`resolve_auth_issuer_call_target` returns `Ok(None)` in three different cases: the issuer is missing from the registry, the entry has no role, or `resolve_registry_protocol_binding` fails for any reason, such as MissingBinding, MissingCandid or RoleMismatch (auth/mod.rs:647-662; errors listed at canic-host protocol_binding/mod.rs:119-149). `issuer_observation_with_runtime` maps every `Ok(None)` to the reason `issuer_not_in_component_registry` (auth/mod.rs:777-782). `renewal_status_code` then returns IssuerUnregistered (auth/mod.rs:858-859). For that status the medic summary's `next` says: "restore the registered topology for issuer ... by reinstalling the affected dependency closure; do not provision delegation proof state manually" (auth/mod.rs:913-917). Unreadable Candid, by contrast, is reported as `issuer_status_metadata_unavailable` (auth/mod.rs:783).

Recommendation

Return `Ok(None)` only when the issuer is absent from the registry. Map binding and Candid resolution failures to a separate reason, such as `issuer_status_metadata_unavailable` or `issuer_binding_unavailable`, with a remediation like 'rebuild or restore local artifacts'. Keep the reinstall advice only for a registry absence that has been confirmed.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. resolve_auth_issuer_call_target returns Ok(None) for any resolve_registry_protocol_binding error (auth/mod.rs:657-662). Those errors include MissingBinding, RoleMismatch, MissingCandid, CandidHashMismatch and ProfileDigestMismatch (canic-host protocol_binding/mod.rs:118-151, 185-218). issuer_observation_with_runtime maps Ok(None) to issuer_not_in_component_registry (auth/mod.rs:780-781). renewal_status_code then returns IssuerUnregistered (auth/mod.rs:858-859), and medic's next says to reinstall the dependency closure (auth/mod.rs:913-917). This contradicts the documented meaning in docs/operations/root-proof-provisioning.md:234 ("Issuer is absent from the root subnet registry"). resolve_current_fleet does not validate bindings (inventory/mod.rs:278-323), so the path is reachable. Correction to the scenario: a fully cleaned checkout or fresh CI runner usually fails earlier, because root's own binding goes through the same strict resolver and returns Err CandidUnavailable (auth/mod.rs:615-621), which gives a medic Fail rather than issuer_unregistered. The realistic trigger is issuer-specific: the issuer role's .did rebuilt locally with changed Candid (CandidHashMismatch) or missing, while root's artifact is intact. The misdiagnosis, plus advice that would wipe state, justifies medium.
mediumconfirmedcore-access-endpoints-2 · security · high confidence
auth::authenticated accepts delegated tokens minted for the anonymous principal, so anonymous ingress passes authenticated endpoints
crates/canic-core/src/access/auth/token.rs:34

Failure scenario

An anonymous agent calls the issuer's canic_command(PrepareDelegatedToken{grants: [{target: user_shard, scopes: ["verify"]}]}), then queries canic_auth_status(DelegatedToken{claims_hash}), also anonymously. It then calls user_shard `hello(token)`, which is guarded by auth::authenticated(cap::VERIFY) (apps/test/user_shard/src/lib.rs:25). The check passes with msg_caller() == anonymous. Any application that keys per-user state or quotas by caller now treats every unauthenticated visitor as one shared authenticated account.

Evidence

Issuing a token to anonymous:
- PrepareDelegatedToken is dispatched without any caller check (role.rs:675-680).
- The managed inspector accepts any decodable CanisterCommand from any caller (role.rs:562-580).
- The workflow uses msg_caller as prepared_by (workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/mod.rs:72, 114-119).
- ops/auth/delegated/prepare.rs:146-149 sets presenter = subject = prepared_by.
- The public prepare policy lets any caller self-grant cap::SESSION, cap::VERIFY and declared application scopes (domain/policy/pure/auth/mod.rs:147-159).
- The token is fetched through the public canic_auth_status query, keyed by caller (role.rs:257, 272-276; api/auth/token.rs:36).

Verification never rejects anonymous:
- access/auth/token.rs:26-35 hands the transport caller to AuthOps::verify_token.
- verify_claims only checks presenter == caller and presenter == subject (ops/auth/delegated/verify.rs:211-216).
- There is no Principal::anonymous() check anywhere in ops/auth, workflow/runtime/auth or access/auth/token.rs.

By contrast, the local-application path rejects anonymous (access/auth/mod.rs:51), and sessions reject it via validate_application_subject (api/auth/application_session.rs:78, 270-273; access/auth/identity.rs:17-19).

Recommendation

- Reject Principal::anonymous() (and preferably the other infrastructure subjects that validate_application_subject rejects) in RuntimeAuthWorkflow::prepare_delegated_token before reserving a replay receipt. - Also reject it in the verifier, in verify_claims or delegated_token_verified. - Add unit and PocketIC tests for an anonymous presenter.

Verifier (confirmed): The finding is real, and I found no guard that rejects anonymous at any step. canic_command is `public` (role.rs:584-588). Its only pre-check is eval_default_fleet_guard, which looks at fleet state, not the caller (access/fleet.rs:34-44). The managed inspector accepts any decodable CanisterCommand (role.rs:562-580). PrepareDelegatedToken reaches AuthApi::prepare_delegated_token with no caller predicate (role.rs:675-680; api/auth/token.rs:23-30). The workflow takes msg_caller with no anonymity check (prepare/mod.rs:72). Claims set presenter = subject = prepared_by (ops/auth/delegated/prepare.rs:146-149). Retrieval through the public query is keyed only by caller (api/auth/token.rs:33-38; ops/auth/token/mod.rs:159-171). The verifier checks only presenter == caller and presenter == subject (verify.rs:211-216). ops/auth/token/mod.rs:181-216 has no anonymity check either. The contract says prepare derives claims from "the authenticated update caller" (AUTH_DELEGATED_SIGNATURES.md:288-291), while both session paths explicitly reject anonymous (access/auth/mod.rs:51; application_session.rs:77, 270-273). So the gap contradicts the stated intent. Impact is limited: any visitor can already mint a verify token for a fresh self-authenticating key. The extra harm is that authenticated endpoints accept one principal shared by everyone, which can also self-grant declared application scopes. Medium is fair.
Also reported as: xc-security-1
mediumverifiedcore-auth-2 · liveness · high confidence
One invalid issuer template or narrowed policy fails every renewal batch non-retryably, stopping the renewal timer and lazy repair for all issuers
crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegation/chain_key_batch/mod.rs:410

Failure scenario

The operator upserts issuer B's template with scopes ["write","read"]; the policy allows both, so the upsert succeeds. Alternatively, the operator later disables B's issuer policy but leaves B's template enabled. B is due immediately (no state yet) or after refresh_after. From then on every timer sweep and every GetOrCreate from issuers A, C and others fails with SECURITY_INVALID or AUTHORITY_UNAUTHORIZED, and the timer stops. Once each cert expires (at most one cert TTL), PrepareDelegatedToken fails for every user on every issuer until someone finds and fixes B's template.

Evidence

validate_root_issuer_policy_upsert never re-checks existing templates (domain/policy/pure/auth/root_provisioning.rs:32-46). Template upsert checks only policy subset and TTL (root_provisioning.rs:101-135). It does not check the canonical sorted-unique ordering, the scope-label grammar or the 16/32 bounds that validate_role_grants enforces (delegated/audience.rs:56-92). Template grants are stored verbatim (ops/storage/auth/mapper.rs:206-221). At batch time all due templates are processed together. Approvals are collected with `?`, and any policy error becomes forbidden (workflow/runtime/auth/root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:30-51). Leaves are built with collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()? (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:406-411), where prepare_delegation_cert re-runs validate_role_grants (delegated/delegation_cert.rs). A single failure aborts the whole batch. AUTHORITY_UNAUTHORIZED and SECURITY_INVALID are not retryable, so the timer stops (workflow/runtime/auth/renewal.rs:240-246, 391-398). Lazy repair for any issuer prepares the same due set (selection.rs:20-38), so it fails the same way.

Recommendation

Validate template grants with validate_role_grants (or canonicalize them) at upsert. When a policy upsert makes existing templates invalid, reject it or auto-disable those templates. During planning, drop templates that fail approval or leaf construction and record the failure per issuer, instead of failing the whole batch.

Severity adjusted from high to medium during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. Policy upsert (workflow/runtime/auth/root_issuer/mod.rs:63-78) runs validate_root_issuer_policy_upsert and the fleet-binding check only (root_provisioning.rs:32-46). It never re-checks existing templates, so disabling or narrowing B's policy leaves B's enabled template in place. Template upsert (root_provisioning.rs:124-135) checks only TTL, non-empty grants and the policy subset. The request conversion copies grants without canonicalizing them (root_issuer_renewal/mod.rs:222-235), so unsorted scopes pass admission. Later, prepare_delegation_cert runs validate_role_grants (audience.rs:56-139), which rejects them as NonCanonicalScopes, mapped to SECURITY_INVALID (errors.rs:11-21). due_chain_key_templates filters only on template.enabled (selection.rs:20-38). The required_issuer_pid lazy path still pulls in every other due template. A failed approval becomes forbidden, i.e. AUTHORITY_UNAUTHORIZED (root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:30-51, error.rs:119). Both errors abort the batch before B's state changes, so B stays due indefinitely. Neither code is in is_retryable_renewal_error (renewal.rs:390-397), so failed_result returns Stop (renewal.rs:240-246). Lazy GetOrCreate for any issuer fails the same way (provisioning/mod.rs:82-90). No docs or tests say whole-batch fail-closed is intended; install failures are already isolated per issuer (tests.rs:912). Caveats: the trigger needs a controller (root.rs:253-255). A later upsert that fixes B recovers, because it calls reconcile. Diagnostics record only the error code and never name B (renewal.rs:329-345). A second, smaller effect: in the non-canonical case the proof epoch advances before the build fails (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:271-275). High is borderline: this is a routine action (revoking an issuer) that causes a fleet-wide auth-renewal outage, but it is recoverable, so medium is also defensible.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, medium): The mechanism is real, but only a root controller can trigger it. UpsertIssuerPolicy and UpsertIssuerRenewalTemplate are controller commands gated by is_controller (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:253-258). Templates enter state only through that workflow (workflow/runtime/auth/root_issuer/mod.rs:81-99). The path holds up when traced. Template conversion copies scopes verbatim (ops/auth/delegation/root_issuer_renewal/mod.rs:222-231, root_issuer_policy.rs:84-89). Upsert admission checks only TTL, non-empty grants and the policy subset (domain/policy/pure/auth/root_provisioning.rs:124-135, 158-180). A policy upsert never re-checks templates (root_issuer/mod.rs:63-78). Every due template is selected, including B when A is the required issuer (chain_key_batch/selection.rs:20-38). Either the approval `?` (root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:30-51) or validate_role_grants in prepare_delegation_cert (delegated/delegation_cert.rs:105, audience.rs:124-133) aborts the whole batch (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:406-411). The error codes are outside is_retryable_renewal_error, so the timer stops (renewal.rs:240-246, 390-397). The lazy GetOrCreate path hits the same failure (provisioning/mod.rs:82-90). The policy upsert also advances the registry epoch, so batches already in flight are no longer reused (mod.rs:302). Why this is a downgrade from high: no untrusted, child or issuer actor can reach it. The controller who causes it already holds strictly greater authority, so this is not an authorization weakness. No cycles are burned, because the batch fails before sign_with_ecdsa. No state is corrupted. The same controller can recover by fixing or disabling B's template, since that upsert calls reconcile. The outage is fleet-wide and diagnostics do not name B, which makes it confusing. That is exactly the rubric's medium case: "missing validation that produces confusing but recoverable failures", amplified from one misconfigured issuer to the whole fleet.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, medium): Not refuted. No document says this behaviour is intended, and the archived design expects the opposite. The mechanics hold. 1. Policy upsert does not re-check existing templates. It runs only validate_root_issuer_policy_upsert (root_provisioning.rs:32-46), which checks audiences and grants only when the policy is enabled. It then commits and advances the registry epoch (root_issuer_policy.rs:16-19), so disabling B while B's template stays enabled is accepted. 2. Template admission (root_provisioning.rs:124-135, 195-208) checks only that each scope is a member of the policy. grant_policies copies grants verbatim (root_issuer_policy.rs:31). Ordering is first enforced at issuance, where validate_role_grants returns NonCanonicalScopes (audience.rs:56-139), which maps to SECURITY_INVALID (errors.rs:11-21). 3. due_chain_key_templates filters only on template.enabled and always includes other due issuers (selection.rs:20-38). A single approval failure becomes forbidden and is propagated with `?` (root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:30-51). Leaves are collected with `?` (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:406-411). 4. The timer stops on these codes (renewal.rs:240-246, 390-397). The lazy path fails the same way (provisioning/mod.rs:82-90). Intent check: authentication.md:307-331 requires canonical grants at issuance. It also says partial issuer install failure is retried per issuer (authentication.md:358-363). No document calls whole-batch fail-closed at prepare intended. The archived 0.74 design (docs/design/archive/0.74-root-managed-delegation-proof-renewal/0.74-design.md:600-606) records `PolicyRejected` per issuer when a template no longer satisfies policy. That supports the recommended fix rather than contradicting it. No tests or audits track this as a known limitation. Severity calibration: the trigger needs a controller (endpoints/root.rs:253-257). It is recoverable: a single corrective template or policy upsert calls reconcile and re-arms the timer (root_issuer/mod.rs:63-98). No cycles, authority or state are lost. The operator can still find the cause, because it follows their own recent change, even though diagnostics show only the error code (renewal.rs:329-345). This matches the rubric's medium entry, "missing validation that produces confusing but recoverable failures". The fleet-wide auth outage after cert TTL makes high defensible, but under the strict rubric it is not a conservation, authorization or unrecoverable-state defect.
mediumconfirmedcore-auth-3 · liveness · medium confidence
The renewal timer stops with an invariant failure after any issuer policy or template upsert while no template is due
crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegation/mod.rs:141

Failure scenario

Issuers A and B both have installed proofs. The operator upserts B's policy, or A's template. reconcile schedules the timer at now. The sweep finds no due template, records STATE_INVALID and stops. No proactive renewal happens at refresh_after, the proofs expire, and liveness falls back to lazy repair on the next login. Issuers whose proof is missing are never repaired (see the separate finding).

Evidence

commit_root_issuer_policy and commit_root_issuer_renewal_template advance the registry epoch (root_issuer_policy.rs:16-19; root_issuer_renewal/mod.rs:29-35), which changes the registry hash (chain_key_registry.rs:95-101). root_issuer_renewal_timing then returns Some(now_ns) whenever any enabled issuer's installed batch does not match the new registry (delegation/mod.rs:128-143; root_issuer_renewal/mod.rs:151-194). Due selection ignores registry identity. chain_key_template_due compares only the template fingerprint, next_attempt_after and refresh_after (selection.rs:46-63), so templates still inside their refresh window are not due. plan_due then returns Complete with no batch (chain_key_batch/mod.rs:214-223), and the sweep reports zero work. completed_result treats 'deadline <= now and work_count == 0' as an invariant failure and returns TimerDirective::Stop (workflow/runtime/auth/renewal.rs:219-230). reconcile runs only on upserts and at root startup (workflow/runtime/mod.rs:91-95; root_issuer/mod.rs:64-100), which lead back into the same state. There is no test of timing after a registry change.

Recommendation

Make due selection registry-aware: treat a template whose last installed cert is not in a batch matching the current registry as due. Alternatively, have timing return the earliest template deadline when nothing is due. Do not turn 'passed deadline with no work' into Stop without recomputing a future deadline.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. Both upserts call advance_delegated_auth_registry_epoch (root_issuer_policy.rs:18, root_issuer_renewal/mod.rs:35). The epoch is part of the registry snapshot (chain_key_registry.rs:103), so every installed batch stops matching. root_issuer_renewal_timing (delegation/mod.rs:127-142) finds no in-flight batch for the current registry, and all_enabled_root_issuer_proofs_match_registry (root_issuer_renewal/mod.rs:151-180) returns false, so the timing is Some(now_ns). Due selection (selection.rs:46-63) checks only the fingerprint, next_attempt_after_ns and refresh_after. The fingerprint does not cover the registry (identity.rs:16-27), and install success sets next_attempt_after_ns to refresh_after (install.rs:262-274). A session lasts up to maximum_session_ttl_secs (at most 1,800 s) and only its own caller can clear it (398-409). Count only receipts inside the 60 s retrieval window against the global prepare quota, and lower the replay TTL cap. Failure scenario

An operator runs `canic blob-storage fund <fleet> backend --cycles 5000000000000`. The Cashier on another subnet is slow and the bounded-wait call returns SysUnknown after the Cashier has already credited 5T. The canister returns an internal error and the CLI exits 2 with TRANSPORT_FAILED, giving no hint that the transfer happened. The operator retries and 10T leaves the project. Variants: Cashier returns InternalError after accepting (as the mock does), or returns Ok with a negative total for an account in debt. Canic reports failure while the cycles are gone. If the Cashier did not accept and the best-effort response is dropped, the refund is lost and the cycles are burned, which violates cycle conservation.

The top-up uses `CallOps::bounded_wait(...).with_cycles(cycles)` (ops/cashier/client.rs:51-56). billing/mod.rs:197-205 maps every call failure through `.await?` to a generic Internal error, and the ic-cdk default 300 s timeout (SysUnknown) takes the same path. A Cashier Err becomes CashierTopUp (:206-210). After an Ok, a negative or oversized returned total becomes a CashierDecode error (:212-213), although Cashier has already credited the account. No path reads msg_cycles_refunded or persists an intent. The guard is transient and is dropped on return (ops/blob_storage/funding.rs:12-14, 59-63), and the endpoint argument has no idempotency key, so a retry runs again. The repo's own mock accepts all attached cycles before returning a forced Err (canisters/test/blob_storage_cashier_mock/src/lib.rs:171-188). The failure tests assert only the error code and `mock_last_top_up == None`, never the project's balance delta (pic_blob_storage.rs:1127-1184). The Cashier inventory requires that "all errors preserve project reserve accounting" (BLOB_STORAGE_CASHIER_INVENTORY.md:443-445).

Recommendation

On every reply path, compute transferred = attached - msg_cycles_refunded() and return it in both the report and the typed errors (for example CashierTopUpAfterTransfer { transferred }). Persist a funding intent (amount, Cashier id, pre-call Cashier balance) before the call. Return a typed OutcomeUnknown on SysUnknown and require reconciliation through account_balance_get_v1 before admitting a new funding. Use unbounded_wait for the cycles-bearing top-up so refunds cannot be dropped. Assert project balance deltas in the PocketIC error tests.

Every call failure goes through `.await?` into the generic Internal error (billing/mod.rs:197-205, 111-135; api billing.rs:127). A Cashier Err maps to CashierTopUp (:206-210). After an Ok, a negative or oversized `total` (the Candid type is `int`, and there is a debt_target) becomes CODEC_INVALID even though the Cashier has already credited the account (:212-213). No path reads msg_cycles_refunded or reports the amount transferred. Under IC best-effort semantics, a response dropped or timed out (SysUnknown) loses any unaccepted refund, so cycles can burn when the Cashier did not accept them. That is a real conservation gap, but it needs a rare failure combined with non-acceptance. Corrections: (1) Keeping no persisted intent record is intended. The 0.70 design (archive/0.70-blob-storage-billing/0.70-design.md:452-455, 483-484) says the guard is transient and nothing is persisted. (2) A double-fund on retry is not a loss. The cycles go to the project's own Cashier account (account = canister_self, :196), which get_blob_storage_status reports, so the operator can reconcile before retrying. The inventory also documents negative-to-decode-error mapping (CASHIER_INVENTORY.md:435-437). What remains is a misreported completed transfer. Medium fits: a less common but realistic path, with a bounded, operator-initiated amount.

Failure scenario

(a) A Component with sharding initial_shards=8 and limits.maximum_descendants=4 passes the build and fleet ensure. At runtime the 5th allocation fails with ComponentDescendantCapacityExhausted and the Component never becomes ready. (b) A self-recursive initial shard pool is accepted by canic::build! and caught only by fleet-ensure planning. If that planner misses it, for example on a runtime provisioning path it does not vet, shards keep creating shards until maximum_descendants (default 20,000 canisters at 5T initial cycles each).

Build-time checks are per pool and per grant only:
- validate_sharding and validate_scaling (config/validation/component_spec.rs:336-450) compare each pool only with its own spawn grant.
- A child role may own a pool, since a grant parent may be any child role (:198). A shard role with a sharding pool targeting itself (grant shard->shard) is therefore accepted.
- configured_initial_instances (topology/mod.rs:1007-1033) sums initial counts per grant, and InitialSpawnGrantExceedsMaximum (:132-140) is also per grant.
- Nothing compares the transitive initial tree (Component, its initial children, their initial children, and so on) with limits.maximum_descendants or detects non-convergence.

At runtime every canister bootstraps its own configured initial shards (workflow/placement/sharding/bootstrap.rs:30-55), and allocation stops at maximum_descendants (component_child_allocation.rs:369).

Move the initial-tree computation into ConfigModel::validate or ComponentTopology::compile. Reject non-convergent initial graphs and trees whose total exceeds limits.maximum_descendants. Share the helper with the member-limit check and the host planner so there is a single definition.

Topology compile checks initial <= maximum per grant (topology/mod.rs:132-140), and validate_spawn_grants (:77-100) has no transitive or cycle check. No code compares the transitive initial tree with maximum_descendants, in core or in the host: host uses of maximum_descendants are observation bounds only (current_inventory/mod.rs:1527,1541). At runtime validate_capacity (component_child_allocation.rs:369) rejects the 5th allocation, and bootstrap then never reaches mark_ready (nonroot.rs:42-49). Part (b) is overstated. Self-recursive grants are intentionally allowed for dynamic spawning. Only positive initial cycles are invalid, and the host rejects them for every deployed spec, both in fleet generate (generate/mod.rs:1087 via initial_workload_count) and in the ensure and startup-funding paths (policy/mod.rs:3123-3166, startup_funding/mod.rs:162; test at startup_funding/tests.rs:262-275). The only plausible bypass is a Spec reached solely through runtime peer provisioning (component_allocation.rs:151-190). Even there, recursion stops at maximum_descendants and at the root pool and funding budgets; the '5T per canister' figure is unverified. The replay slot key omits the actor, so any authorized fleet member can pre-occupy another member's deterministic placement or top-up operation IDs and block them (permanently for placement)
crates/canic-core/src/ops/replay/receipt.rs:526

Failure scenario

1. A compromised fleet member B computes victim A's next sharding or scaling operation ID from A's principal, pool and generation. 2. B sends AllocatePlacementChild with that request_id and a role B may create. Root reserves the slot for actor B, creates B's child and commits a placement receipt that waits for B's acknowledgement. B never acknowledges. 3. When A allocates, root returns ReplayConflict (CODEC_CONFLICT) forever. A's pool allocation for that generation is permanently wedged, because A's next_sequence only advances on commit. The same squat on A's next cycle-top-up operation ID makes A's top-up stop with a non-retryable error.

Evidence

- **Global slot:** `ReplayReceiptOps::slot_key` hashes only command_kind and operation_id (ops/storage/replay.rs:35-44).
- **First writer wins:** `classify_existing_receipt` returns `ActorMismatch` whenever the stored actor differs (receipt.rs:526-528). The root maps this to DuplicateConflict / ReplayConflict (guard.rs:219-221, handler/replay.rs), before any expiry check.
- **Predictable IDs:** placement operation IDs are SHA-256 of public inputs (owner principal, placement kind, pool, subject, generation; model/placement/allocation.rs:124-143) and are sent unchanged as the root request_id (dispatch.rs:60-75). Cycle top-up IDs are SHA-256(domain, caller, sequential generation) (async_job_recovery/mod.rs:47-58).
- **No binding check:** root authorizes AllocatePlacementChild for any member whose provision parent is itself (handler/authorize.rs:109-131) and never checks that request_id is derived from the caller.
- **Retention:** a committed placement receipt is kept until the *owning actor* acknowledges it (`record_survives_replay_expiry`, storage/stable/replay.rs:413-418; `acknowledge_placement_receipt` actor check, receipt.rs:292-294).

Recommendation

Scope the replay namespace to the actor: include `ReplayActor` in `slot_key`. Or, for root capabilities, recompute and require that the request_id is bound to the direct caller (for example, reject IDs not derived from `ctx.caller`). Add a test in which a second actor's receipt with the same operation ID does not block the owner.

Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is real and I found no guard against it. `ReplayReceiptOps::slot_key` hashes only a domain, command_kind and operation_id (ops/storage/replay.rs:35-44). `classify_existing_receipt` returns ActorMismatch before any expiry check (receipt.rs:526-528), and guard.rs:219-221 maps that to DuplicateConflict, which becomes ReplayConflict (handler/replay.rs:185-199). Placement IDs are SHA-256 over owner, kind, pool, subject and generation (model/placement/allocation.rs:124-143), and dispatch.rs:60-75 sends them unchanged as request_id. Neither the control-plane admission (canic-control-plane/.../component_rpc/mod.rs:42-56, 110-146) nor authorize_provision (authorize.rs:109-131) nor the structural proof (capability/proof.rs:42-58) binds request_id to the caller. A committed placement receipt survives expiry (storage/stable/replay.rs:413-418). Only the stored actor can acknowledge it (receipt.rs:292-294), and root self cannot either. Victim A reuses the same generation because `next_sequence` is committed_qty (workflow/placement/allocation.rs:85-87), and scaling/mod.rs:239-265 and sharding/allocation.rs:61-86 simply return the error. The Fleet Coordinator entrypoint defines no post_upgrade, so a same-release upgrade is not rejected and leaves a Coordinator whose every Canic endpoint traps, recoverable only by a destructive reinstall.
crates/canic/src/macros/start.rs:721

Failure scenario

An operator runs `icp canister install <coordinator> --mode upgrade` with the identical Coordinator Wasm, for example to restart it. The IC accepts the upgrade because no post_upgrade exists to trap. Every later Coordinator command (RequestRootFunding, ProvisionComponents, snapshot acknowledgements) and status query traps in preflight with "Fleet activation fence rejected endpoint". Upgrading again changes nothing. The only way out is reinstall, which wipes the Coordinator Fleet Registry (ID 15), the funding journal (ID 62) with any in-flight grant reconciliation state, and admission (ID 64). The upgrade is also not blocked while a funding grant is in flight.

Evidence

`start_fleet_coordinator!` (start.rs:711-731) emits only `#[init] fn init(args)`, which delegates to `FleetCoordinatorApi::init`. There is no `#[post_upgrade]` export and no `pre_upgrade` anywhere in the workspace (grep). `FleetCoordinatorApi::init` (canic-control-plane/src/api/fleet_coordinator.rs:86-101) performs all of the volatile setup: `initialize_shared_runtime_required`, `MemoryRuntimeApi::bootstrap_registry`, `EnvOps::initialize_fleet_coordinator_runtime()` (heap only: sets `runtime_kind` whose default is `Managed`, model/runtime_kind/mod.rs:22), and `ReadyApi::mark_ready()`. After an upgrade none of this is re-established. Every `canic_update`/`canic_query` calls `dispatch::preflight_endpoint` (dispatch/mod.rs:54-58). That call lazily bootstraps memory and then runs `FleetActivationWorkflow::require_endpoint_allowed` (workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:413-418): `is_fleet_coordinator_runtime()` is now false, so it calls `EnvOps::canister_role()?`, and the Coordinator never imports an EnvRecord role. The result is Err, and preflight `panic!`s. `AuthorityRestoreWorkflow::authority_command_endpoint` fails the same way (authority_restore.rs:209-214). The 0.110 design (0.110-design.md:1141-1145) requires the actor lifecycle to reject upgrades before interpreting state. The 0.108 design (line 1671) requires restart to resume same-release work and upgrades to fail closed while a grant is current.

Recommendation

Emit a `#[post_upgrade]` from `start_fleet_coordinator!`. Either (a) trap unconditionally with a typed "Coordinator is reinstall-only" message so the IC rolls the upgrade back, or (b) implement a real same-release restore: initialize the shared timer runtime, bootstrap memory, set the runtime kind, check the release-build identity, restore snapshot suspension from `AuthorityRestoreFenceOps::is_sealed_for`, reject while a grant is current, and mark ready. Add a PocketIC case that upgrades the Coordinator and asserts rejection or continued operation.

Severity adjusted from high to medium during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is real. `start_fleet_coordinator!` (crates/canic/src/macros/start.rs:711-731) exports only `#[init]`. `FleetCoordinatorApi::init` (crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/fleet_coordinator.rs:86-101) sets the heap-only runtime kind, which defaults to `Managed` (crates/canic-core/src/model/runtime_kind/mod.rs:22-23). The Coordinator never stores an Env role (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:182-199). After an upgrade, every generated endpoint runs `preflight_endpoint` (canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:120,137-149; dispatch/mod.rs:54-58), including the public Health query. There, `require_endpoint_allowed` (fleet_activation.rs:413-418) reaches `EnvOps::canister_role()?`, gets Err, and panics (dispatch/mod.rs:106-113). Nothing rejects the upgrade itself, and all timers are lost. This conflicts with 0.110-design.md:1142-1146 (the actor lifecycle rejects the upgrade before interpreting state) and 0.108-design.md:1669-1670 (upgrades fail closed). I downgraded it to medium. No Canic tool ever upgrades a canister: the host installs only with `install` or `reinstall` (canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:2861-2865), and no runtime or CLI code issues an upgrade. The trigger is therefore a manual, out-of-band `--mode upgrade` by a controller. The working audit also records this state as "no supported post_upgrade" (docs/audits/working/0.104-timer-ownership/README.md:126). Recovery exists: the normal clean-reinstall path (fleet_ensure/generate/mod.rs:800), or loading an earlier snapshot. Cycles survive reinstall, so this is an outage and a policy violation, not a permanent wedge or a cycle loss. The fix is still worth making: a `post_upgrade` that traps.

Every managed endpoint call deep-clones the up-to-2 MiB activation record and re-encodes and hashes the Directory authority twice.
crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/fleet_activation/mod.rs:459

Failure scenario

A Component in a large Fleet holds a Fleet Directory snapshot of several hundred KB (many subnet roots, services and members). Each application query or update first clones that record and Candid-encodes and SHA-256-hashes the directory twice. Near the 2 MiB bound that can cost hundreds of millions of instructions per call, and the fixed cost grows with Fleet size, not with the request. That burns cycles on every user call and eats into the 5B query budget.

Evidence

`FleetActivation::get()` returns `store.get().clone()` (storage/stable/fleet_activation/mod.rs:458-460). The record is bounded at `MAX_FLEET_ACTIVATION_RECORD_BYTES = 2_097_152` (line 29) and contains the Fleet Directory snapshot, service members, Component Group directory, cascade manifest and credential manifests. `dispatch::preflight_endpoint` (dispatch/mod.rs:54-58) runs on every macro-generated query and update and calls `FleetActivationWorkflow::require_endpoint_allowed` (workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:413-426). That calls `FleetActivationOps::status` → `FleetActivation::get()` → `mapper::record_to_status` (mapper.rs:27-31). For an Active Component runtime, `validate_active_component_runtime` (mapper.rs:141-160) calls `validate_component_runtime_directory_record` twice (for `directory` and `activation.directory`). Each call converts the record to a DTO and computes `directory_authority_hash` = `candid::encode_one(authority)` + SHA-256 (ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:1124-1133; ops/component_runtime.rs:21-31). Non-infrastructure endpoints then also call `fixture_provisioning::require_ready()`, which reads activation state again. The root path converts the full cascade and credential manifests on every call (mapper.rs:103-107).

Recommendation

Give the endpoint fence a cheap projection: read only the phase and identity through a borrow (`with_borrow(|s| s.get().as_ref().map(|r| phase_of(r)))`) without cloning. Validate the Directory hashes once when the record is written (activation, synchronization) and at post_upgrade restore instead of on every read. Cache the validated status in heap, invalidated on `replace`.

Verifier (confirmed): The path is as described. `FleetActivation::get()` deep-clones the cached record (storage/stable/fleet_activation/mod.rs:458-460), even though `BoundedCell::get` hands out a borrowed reference (cdk/bounded_cell/mod.rs:25-29). Every macro endpoint except the four Store data-lane methods gets `preflight_endpoint` (canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:138-151; dispatch/mod.rs:54-58). That calls `require_endpoint_allowed` (workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:413-434), which calls `FleetActivationOps::status` (ops mod.rs:202-207) and then `record_to_status`. For an Active Component, that runs `validate_active_component_runtime` (mapper.rs:141-160). Each of its two `validate_component_runtime_directory_record` calls (ops mod.rs:1124-1145) converts the record to a DTO, runs `candid::encode_one`, and computes a SHA-256 (ops/component_runtime.rs:21-31). The caller then uses only `status.phase`. For non-infrastructure endpoints, `fixture_provisioning::require_ready()` then reads the record again, and `component_fixture_assignment` also calls `FleetActivation::get()` (ops mod.rs:234-237). The magnitude is overstated for typical fleets: `FleetDirectorySnapshot` holds subnet-root entries and services with members (dto/fleet_registry.rs:500-544), usually a few KB. Even at the 2 MiB bound the cost stays below the 5B query limit. It is still a fixed per-call cost, paid on every application query and update, that grows with Fleet size, which matches the rubric's medium for hot-path cost.

Each counting helper in `ReplayReceiptStore` (replay.rs:244-343: `active_len_for_actor`, `active_len_for_actor_command_kind`, `active_len_for_command_kind`, `pending_len_for_actor`, `pending_len_for_command_kind`, `has_pending_for_actor_command_excluding_operation`) iterates the entire B-tree and calls `entry.value()`, deserializing the full `ReplayReceiptRecord` including `response_bytes` and `staged_response_bytes`. `list_by_actor_operation_excluding_command` (211-226) and `collect_expired` (345-363) do the same, and `collect_expired` restarts from the first key each time. Admission calls these per request: `reserve_root_replay` (ops/replay/mod.rs:103-116) and `pending_receipt_quota_decision`/`retained_receipt_quota_error` (ops/replay/receipt.rs:322-365), about five scans per new receipt. The root allows up to `MAX_ROOT_REPLAY_ENTRIES = 10_000` receipts (512 per caller; workflow/rpc/request/handler/mod.rs:38-39). The record's `response_bytes: Option<Vec<u8>>` fields (replay.rs:91-93) lack `serde_bytes`, so ciborium encodes every byte as a separate CBOR integer and decodes it element by element. `to_bytes` also clones the whole record (line 155).

Recommendation

Add small secondary indexes (actor → count, command kind → count, pending set, expiry-ordered key) maintained on upsert/remove, as the intent store already does for expiry and pending. At minimum, scan keys with lazily decoded compact metadata instead of full values. Annotate the byte fields with `#[serde(with = "serde_bytes")]`. This is a stable-layout hard cut, which is acceptable pre-1.0.

Verifier (confirmed): Every counting helper does a full scan: replay.rs:211-226 and 244-343 iterate the whole map and call `entry.value()`. Keys are opaque 32-byte slot hashes (replay.rs:38), so nothing can be filtered by key. A fresh root request runs `list_by_actor_operation_excluding_command` (guard.rs:153), then `purge_expired`/`collect_expired` (guard.rs:146, replay.rs:345-363). That scan starts from the first key every time, so with few expired receipts it covers the whole map. Then comes `active_len_for_actor` (ops/replay/mod.rs:103). That makes 3 full scans on the generic path. The RequestCycles path adds `has_pending_for_actor_command_excluding_operation` (nonroot_cycles.rs:395) and `pending_for_actor_command` (funding_usage/mod.rs:39), for about 5. `response_bytes` and `staged_response_bytes` (replay.rs:91,93) have no serde_bytes annotation, even though serde_bytes is a dependency (canic-core/Cargo.toml:53). Ciborium therefore encodes them as integer arrays, and the `[u8;32]` fields are encoded as tuples too. `to_bytes` clones the whole record (155). Two corrections: the store is capped at `MAX_ROOT_REPLAY_ENTRIES = 10_000` (handler/mod.rs:38), and other command kinds are capped at 512 (receipt.rs:22, retention/mod.rs:22). So cost stops growing at the cap and probably stays below 40B unless responses are large. Reaching about 10k needs 20 or more authorized children near their 512 cap, for example through unacknowledged placement receipts that outlive expiry (replay.rs:410-415). Medium fits: bounded cost amplification of several billion instructions per request on root, which every fleet request goes through.
