mediumconfirmedcore-placement-fleet-2 · liveness · high confidence
Index claim is persisted before capacity admission, so an admission failure leaves an untracked claim that stays unrecoverable forever
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/placement/index/create.rs:95

Failure scenario

The receipt-backed intent store is momentarily full (1,000 records, shared with application intents), or the resource-total store is full (see the separate finding). A caller resolves a new key K: claim_pending succeeds and begin_allocation returns StoreCapacityReached, so the call errors. After the store drains, every resolve_or_create(K) returns Pending for 5 minutes and then STATE_CONFLICT forever, and recover_entry(K) also returns STATE_CONFLICT. K can never be created. Each distinct failed key also leaves a permanent Pending registry row.

Evidence

claim_and_create_instance writes the Pending claim first (create.rs:95-103) and only then calls create_and_finalize_claim → PlacementAllocationWorkflow::create_child, whose first statement is begin_allocation(&request)? (allocation.rs:101-104). begin_allocation maps CapacityExceeded and StoreCapacityReached to resource_exhausted (allocation.rs:285-289). The error is returned before any await. The API returns Result as a normal reply (api/placement/index.rs:39-46), so the claim is committed with no intent behind it. After the TTL the entry is Resumable (classification.rs:63-72). recover_child then rejects any operation without a stored intent with STATE_CONFLICT (allocation.rs:115-124). release_stale_pending_if_claim_matches refuses to release claims whose provisional_pid is None (ops/storage/placement/index/mod.rs:300-308). The existing test stale_pending_without_provisional_child_remains_claimed_for_exact_resume (index/tests.rs:291-316) confirms that untracked claims fail closed permanently, yet this code path creates exactly that state from an ordinary failure.

Recommendation

Admit the intent before writing the claim: derive the claim id, call begin_allocation, then claim_pending, all within the same synchronous section. Alternatively, remove the claim in the same message when begin_allocation fails. Optionally let recover_entry release a stale claim that has no provisional pid and no stored intent.

Severity adjusted from high to medium during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The defect is real and happens as described. claim_and_create_instance persists a Pending claim with provisional_pid None (create.rs:95; ops/storage/placement/index/mod.rs:190-198). It then reaches create_child, whose first statement is begin_allocation(&request)? (allocation.rs:104), with no await in between. create_receipt returns StoreCapacityReached when there are 1,000 receipt records or 1,000 resource totals, and CapacityExceeded otherwise (ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:1562-1587). begin_allocation maps both to resource_exhausted (allocation.rs:285-289). The API returns this as a normal Err reply (api/placement/index.rs:39-46; apps/test/index_hub/src/lib.rs:14-19), so the claim is committed. After the 300 s TTL the entry is classified Resumable (classification.rs:63-72). recover_child then fails with STATE_CONFLICT because no intent exists (allocation.rs:118-124). Both release callers (cleanup.rs:59,120) handle only NeedsCleanup, and release refuses a claim with no provisional pid (mod.rs:302). No test covers admission failure. Severity is medium, not high: no root call is made, so no cycles or effects are lost. The blast radius is one key per failed attempt. The trigger needs the 1,000-record store to be saturated. There is also a manual escape: bind_instance lets the app bind a Pending entry to a direct child of the right role (mod.rs:356-366; index/mod.rs:312-331), so 'forever' is overstated. A reinstall also clears it. Related, not claimed here: committed_qty is never decremented, so index resource totals persist and saturation eventually becomes routine. Each failed distinct key also leaves a permanent registry row.
mediumconfirmedcore-rpc-ic-4 · cycles · medium confidence
ICP refill becomes final after 5 notify attempts, which strands already-transferred ICP at the CMC, and attempts are counted before any CMC call is made
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/execution.rs:302

Failure scenario

Root is at its emergency threshold and the ICP transfer succeeds. The CMC answers Processing, or returns a transient Other error such as a minting limit, on each of 5 quick retries by the automatic timer; some of those attempts may also be lost to cost-guard rejections while Root is low on cycles. The operation becomes final with the ICP already paid to the CMC but no cycles minted. Root stays underfunded, and the value is lost unless an operator notices and calls CMC notify_top_up by hand before the block ages out.

Evidence

notify_operation increments notify_attempts first (execution.rs:302-303, ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:1250-1257). Only afterwards does it reserve the cost guard (execution.rs:309) and mark the notify effect (execution.rs:311). If either step fails, an attempt is used up without calling the CMC. Both NotifyTopUpError::Processing and Other count as failures (execution.rs:407, 415-422). Once notify_attempts reaches MAX_NOTIFY_ATTEMPTS = 5 (icp_refill/mod.rs:40), the operation is marked Failed{NotifyMaxAttempts} (execution.rs:430-435, 446-447; ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:1368-1376). That state is not resumable (domain/icp_refill.rs:59-81), and advance_operation returns it as final (execution.rs:262-266). The ledger block index is already recorded, so the ICP sits in the CMC top-up subaccount, and nothing in Canic calls notify_top_up for it again. The operation also stops counting as resumable (root_funding/mod.rs:69), so new refills can start while the value stays unconverted until the CMC reports TransactionTooOld.

Recommendation

Keep an operation with a recorded ledger block resumable until the CMC returns Refunded, InvalidTransaction or TransactionTooOld. Use backoff instead of a fixed attempt cap. Increment notify_attempts only after the call is actually issued, and do not count Processing as a failure. Expose an explicit resume-notify path for operators.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. notify_operation increments notify_attempts first (execution.rs:302-303, store icp_refill.rs:1250-1257). Only then does it reserve the cost guard and mark the effect (309-311). An Err from those steps returns without a trap, so the increment persists. That cost-guard path is rarely reachable, though: it needs under about 2B cycles (cost_guard.rs:28-29) or more than 60 operations per minute. Transport failures in the Err branch (318-325) also consume attempts without applying the cap. When Processing or Other arrives with attempts at 5 or more, the record becomes Failed{NotifyMaxAttempts} (425-451). That state is not resumable (domain/icp_refill.rs:59-81), and neither can_retry_notify nor advance_operation (257-266) will retry it. No trigger check exists, so the automatic timer path, which retries every RETRY_INITIAL (1 minute), is capped the same as the manual path. This contradicts the archived design (docs/design/archive/0.58-convert-icp/0.58-design.md:274-279), which scopes the cap to manual mode and says to keep it independent of timer-driven self-refill. Nothing in Canic re-notifies a block that is already recorded. Two points temper the claim. First, the ICP is not immediately lost: anyone can call CMC notify_top_up out-of-band until the CMC purges the block. Second, CMC minting-limit failures likely come back as Refunded, not Other, so reaching the cap needs repeated Processing, FailedToFetchBlock or transport failures. Medium is right.
mediumconfirmedcore-runtime-metrics-1 · correctness · high confidence
ICP-refill status metrics are keyed per automatic sequence and error code but projected without them, producing duplicate rows that permanently reject Root's public `operations` family and inflate protected Core metrics
crates/canic-core/src/ops/runtime/metrics/icp_refill.rs:33

Failure scenario

1. A Root has an automatic ICP refill policy and `public_metrics = ["operations"]`. 2. Automatic refills with sequence 1 and 2 both complete, leaving two status keys: (Automatic{1}, Completed, None) and (Automatic{2}, Completed, None). 3. At the next 5-minute sample, `operation_metrics` emits `cycles_funding.icp_refill.automatic.notify.status.completed` twice. `replace` returns `invalid_input` and the operations snapshot stops refreshing. 4. The public state goes Stale six minutes later and stays Stale for the rest of the release, and the timer records a retryable failure every slot. 5. Two failed manual refills with BadFee and LedgerTransferFailed collide in the same way (`manual.transfer.status.failed`). 6. Protected Core metrics list one row per refill record, each with count 1, instead of aggregated counts.

Evidence

The derived index keys status counts by `(record.trigger, record.status, record.error_code)` (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:757-761). `trigger` is `IcpRefillTriggerRecord::Automatic { sequence: u64 }` (crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/icp_refill.rs:86-89), and every automatic refill gets a new sequence from `next_automatic_sequence` (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/automatic.rs:192). `entries_from_snapshot` emits one row per key, with labels `[icp_refill, trigger_label, record_phase(status,error), "status", status_label]` and `principal: None` (icp_refill.rs:30-45). `trigger_label` drops the sequence (86-91), and `record_phase` folds many error codes into `transfer` or `notify` (113-145). Distinct keys therefore map to identical labels. On Root, `bounded_core_entries` adds these rows to the public `operations` sample (ops/runtime/metrics/mod.rs:89-98). `operation_metrics` names each row `labels.join(".")` with `canister_id: None` (public_metrics/mod.rs:352-384). `PublicMetricsCache::replace` then rejects the whole family on any duplicate name and canister pair (model/public_metrics/mod.rs:81-86). Records are retained up to 4,096 and never pruned (ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:999). `bounded_metric_snapshot(257)` takes BTreeMap order, so `Automatic{1..}` keys also crowd out all `Manual` statuses (ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:907-922).

Recommendation

Aggregate in the projection. In `entries_from_snapshot`, sum counts into a BTreeMap keyed by the emitted label tuple (trigger kind, phase, status label) before building rows. Alternatively, key `status_counts` by a trigger kind without the sequence, and either add the error code as a label or keep only the separate error rows. Add a regression test with two automatic Completed records, and two Failed manual records with different transfer-phase error codes, asserting one row with count 2 and a successful public operations sample.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. `IcpRefillDerivedIndex.status_counts` is keyed by `(IcpRefillTriggerRecord, status, error_code)` (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:124-131, 757-761). `IcpRefillTriggerRecord::Automatic { sequence }` (storage/stable/icp_refill.rs:86-89) takes a fresh monotonic sequence on every automatic refill (`next_automatic_sequence`, ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:1094-1100; workflow/ic/icp_refill/automatic.rs:192). `entries_from_snapshot` emits one row per key. `trigger_label` drops the sequence (ops/runtime/metrics/icp_refill.rs:86-91) and `record_phase`/`status_label` fold error codes, while the row has `principal: None` (30-45, 93-99). Two completed automatic refills therefore both produce `cycles_funding.icp_refill.automatic.notify.status.completed`. On Root, `bounded_core_entries` adds these rows (ops/runtime/metrics/mod.rs:89-98), `operation_metrics` names them with `labels.join(".")` (public_metrics/mod.rs:342-384), and `PublicMetricsCache::replace` rejects the whole family on the duplicate name and canister_id pair (model/public_metrics/mod.rs:84-89). The failure repeats every sample (`sample_selected`, workflow/metrics/publication/mod.rs:60-70), because records are never pruned (cap 4,096, fail-closed). The existing test (ops/runtime/metrics/tests.rs:518-535) uses only one automatic sequence, so it misses this. No cycles are affected, so medium is right: an ordinary production path permanently breaks a public observability family and inflates protected rows.
mediumconfirmedcore-runtime-metrics-2 · security · high confidence
Unauthenticated callers can flush the count-bounded runtime log, because every denied update call commits a Warn log entry into the same FIFO that holds operator history
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/log.rs:56

Failure scenario

1. An anonymous principal sends about 10,000 free ingress update calls to any access-gated update. Examples: an application `#[canic_update(requires(caller::is_controller()))]` method, or `canic_root_command` while the Fleet is Readonly. 2. Each call passes `inspect_message`, is denied, and appends one Warn entry, evicting the oldest. 3. Afterwards every earlier operator-relevant entry is gone: bootstrap failures, funding and refill errors, capability rejections. 4. The attacker can repeat this continuously to hide the trail of a later incident. The victim canister pays for every execution.

Evidence

`record_access_failure` increments a metric and calls `log!(Topic::Auth, Warn, "access denied ...")` (crates/canic-core/src/access/expr/mod.rs:498-509). Denied endpoints return `Err` rather than trapping; the macro requires access-gated endpoints to return `Result` 'to avoid traps' (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:29-32). The write therefore commits. `log!` persists every level through `LogRetentionWorkflow::append_runtime_log` (crates/canic-core/src/log.rs:124-160; workflow/runtime/log.rs:56-74). The store is a single FIFO: at `max_entries` it removes the oldest entry for each append (crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/log.rs:107-117). The default is 10,000 entries (crates/canic-core/src/config/schema/log.rs:13-15). Ingress inspection only checks payload size, not authorization (crates/canic-core/src/ingress/payload.rs:73-84), and inter-canister calls bypass inspection entirely. The same path runs when the fleet guard on public `canic_root_command` rejects callers while the Fleet is Readonly (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:202-213; access/expr/mod.rs:341-366).

Recommendation

Do not persist per-request access-denial lines. The access metric already counts them, so use `IcOps::println` only, or aggregate denials into a periodic summary. Alternatively, give untrusted-triggerable topics or levels (Auth/Warn denials) a separate small quota or ring so they cannot evict Error and Init history, or rate-limit denial logging per endpoint and predicate.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. Denials from both `eval_access_selected` and `eval_default_fleet_guard` go through `record_access_failure`, which calls `log!(Topic::Auth, Warn, ...)` (crates/canic-core/src/access/expr/mod.rs:326-366, 498-520). `log!` persists every level through `__append_runtime_log` → `LogRetentionWorkflow::append_runtime_log` → `LogOps::append_runtime_log`, with no level or topic filter (log.rs:115-150; workflow/runtime/log.rs:56-74; ops/runtime/log.rs:37-62). The store evicts the oldest entry at `max_entries` (storage/stable/log.rs:107-117; default 10,000, config/schema/log.rs:13-15). Generated guards return `Err` instead of trapping (canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/access.rs:57-88; expand/mod.rs:29-32), so the append commits. Every public update gets at least the default fleet guard (access.rs:154-168). `inspect_update_message` checks only payload size (ingress/payload.rs:73-84). Correction: direct `access::auth::is_controller`/`is_root` checks inside `canic_command` dispatch do not log (role.rs:624-665). The vector needs expression-gated application updates, or any default-guarded update while the Fleet is Readonly or Disabled. The impact is limited to non-authoritative diagnostic history; durable journals and the recent-failure ring are separate. That still fits medium as a cheap, repeatable, unauthenticated bounded DoS on operator observability.
Also reported as: xc-security-6, xc-efficiency-10
mediumconfirmedcp-fleet-coordinator-6 · performance · medium confidence
Every Coordinator read and write re-derives and re-validates the whole history, at a cost quadratic in root count and linear in history length
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/registry_history.rs:855

Failure scenario

As a Fleet grows to a few hundred roots, or accumulates many admission publications, one `current()` call approaches billions of instructions. Queries (5B limit) fail first, including the Registry reads Roots use to sync their mirrors. Then updates (40B limit, with at least two validations each) fail, including RequestRootFunding. Because history cannot be compacted, the Coordinator permanently stops serving grants and every other command.

Evidence

`current()` clones the entire record and runs `validate_current` (ops mod.rs:1917-1948), and every command and query calls it. `historical_joining_registry` loops over all join receipts. For each one it calls `compile_joining`, which validates the whole Registry, and `FleetRegistryOps::version`, which validates, canonically encodes and SHA-256 hashes the whole Registry again (registry_history.rs:855-897; fleet_registry/mod.rs:379-390, 479-485, 733-744). That is Θ(N²) in roots, and it runs twice per validation (registry_history.rs:71 and 830). `canonical_registry_lifecycle_history` replays every admission publication, service publication, rotation checkpoint and lifecycle receipt, hashing a full Registry at each point (114-177, 612-657). It also clones the whole funding cell (73, 277). `validate_root_draining_reservations` rebuilds that history once per reservation (root_lifecycle.rs:225 → registry_history.rs:460-471). Each commit clones and deep-compares the record twice and rewrites a cell of up to 32 MiB (storage mod.rs:810-829), and it first clones the funding cell (ops mod.rs:2027-2029). `validate_funding_record` is O(N²) through `exact_registry_root` (root_funding.rs:739-744, 532-546). The public operation-status query runs `current()` three times (workflow mod.rs:159-180), and the Registry query twice (api/fleet_coordinator.rs:64-71, 257-261). Validation accepts up to 4,096 roots and 4,096 admission publications (ops mod.rs:1972-1976), and history is append-only.

Recommendation

Validate incrementally on write: check only the transition against the committed head, and trust the committed state on read. Cache derived history versions and the head version in the record instead of recomputing them. Drop the per-reservation history rebuild by storing the reservation's source root entry. Read `rotation_current` without cloning the funding cell. Add an instruction-count benchmark at the declared maxima.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed, with one correction. `current()` (ops mod.rs:1917-1948) runs `validate_current_registry` on every call. That rebuilds the join history twice: once in `validate_root_join_receipts` via `historical_joining_registry` (registry_history.rs:855-897), and once in the lifecycle history (71). Each step validates, canonically encodes and SHA-256 hashes a whole Registry (canic-core ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:379-390, 733-744). `apply_admission_publication_to_registry` computes two full versions per publication (admission.rs:209-273). The history is rebuilt again for each draining reservation (root_lifecycle.rs:225) and for a scale-out source registry (1933-1937). Correction: the number of roots is realistically small. Validation requires strictly increasing, unique placement subnets (canic-core fleet_registry/validation/mod.rs:144-147), so the N-squared-in-roots term matters only at the declared 4,096-root maximum. The dominant growth driver is up to 4,096 admission publications (MAX_FLEET_ADMISSION_PUBLICATIONS). These are append-only within a release, with no compaction, and each one costs roughly two full-Registry hashes per rebuild. The 0.109 bounds (design lines 565-590) measure bytes, not instructions. At a few thousand publications this plausibly exceeds the 5B query limit, and then update budgets, after several rebuilds. Reinstalling at a release boundary resets the history, so the risk is bounded to one release's lifetime. Medium is right.
mediumconfirmedcp-fleet-coordinator-7 · robustness · high confidence
Retirement's Ledger transfer intent is immutable, so a later deposit, a fee change or a retry after 24 h makes retirement permanently uncompletable
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:84

Failure scenario

(a) After the intent commits, anyone sends 1 cycle plus the fee to the Coordinator's default Cycles Ledger account. The transfer succeeds or deduplicates, but the balance stays non-zero, so every retry returns conflict forever. (b) The first transfer succeeds but the final balance read fails transiently, and the operator retries more than 24 h later. The ledger returns TooOld, so retirement never records Complete even though the funds moved. (c) The ledger fee changes between intent and transfer, so BadFee makes the conflict permanent and the balance stays stranded in the account.

Evidence

`retire` reads the Cycles Ledger balance and fee across awaits (retirement/mod.rs:37-44). It then commits an intent that fixes `balance_before`, `fee` and `created_at_time` (ops retirement/mod.rs:54-83). Later calls return the stored intent unchanged (61-64, 34-40). The transfer amount is `balance_before - fee` with a fixed `created_at_time` (infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:205-226). Every transfer error other than Duplicate and TemporarilyUnavailable, including TooOld, BadFee and InsufficientFunds, maps to `conflict` (retirement/mod.rs:76-85). Completion also requires a post-transfer balance of exactly 0 (88-94). No path re-plans or sweeps a residual.

Recommendation

After a transfer, re-read the balance. If a residual remains, allow a bounded follow-up sweep intent with its own memo. On TooOld, look up the original transfer by memo or created_at_time; if it is absent, re-plan with a fresh created_at_time. On BadFee, re-plan with the new fee. Map these errors to typed, retryable results instead of a permanent conflict.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. `begin_retirement_transfer` (ops retirement/mod.rs:54-84) commits an intent that fixes `balance_before`, `fee` and `created_at_time`, and returns that stored intent on every later call (60-63). `CyclesLedgerInfra::transfer` (canic-core infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:201-227) always sends `balance_before - fee` with that fixed `created_at_time`. Only Ok, Duplicate and TemporarilyUnavailable are handled; TooOld, BadFee and InsufficientFunds all map to `conflict` (workflow retirement/mod.rs:76-85). Completion requires a post-transfer balance of exactly 0 (88-94). (a) Anyone can credit the Coordinator's default Cycles Ledger account for about one fee. Any deposit that lands after the intent's balance read leaves a residual, so every retry deduplicates and then hits conflict forever. (b) If the first transfer failed or its outcome went unconfirmed, a retry after the ledger's deduplication window (about 24 h) gets TooOld. When the original never executed, the balance cannot be evacuated through this path at all. (c) BadFee is rare because the ledger fee rarely changes, but it is also permanent. The 0.110 design (lines 819-824) requires retirement to reconcile interrupted effects. Mitigating factors: Retire is controller-only (canic macros fleet_coordinator.rs:93-101), host/CLI do not invoke it yet, and the stranded cycles stay controlled. Medium stands.
mediumconfirmedcp-fleet-coordinator-8 · liveness · medium confidence
RemoveRoot commits an irrevocable reservation before the Root validates it, so a definite Root rejection permanently blocks admission and further removal of that root
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:501

Failure scenario

An operator names a Root pool canister as `asset_recipient`. The Coordinator validates only anonymous, management and the root itself, and commits the reservation. The Root rejects with REQUEST_INVALID. Every retry replays the same request and gets the same rejection, and a corrected request conflicts on the root identity. Admission is now blocked for the whole Fleet and the root can never be removed.

Evidence

`accept_root_removal` commits the reservation durably through `prepare_root_draining_reservation`, then calls the Root (mod.rs:500-513). If the Root rejects, the error goes back to the operator and the reservation stays. The identity rules reject any different request for the same root or operation (ops mod.rs:1701-1709), so the operator cannot correct it, and no cancel command exists. The Root checks conditions the Coordinator cannot see, for example rejecting an `asset_recipient` that is one of its pool canisters (`CanisterPoolOps::contains_asset(recipient)`, fleet_subnet_root.rs:336), or a `root_entry` that differs from its own view (345-352). While the reserved root stays Active, `require_admission_transition_start_allowed` blocks every admission mutation (admission.rs:43-52), and `require_component_plan_roots_unreserved` excludes the root from provisioning plans (root_lifecycle.rs:49-64).

Recommendation

Add a controller command to cancel a reservation that has no draining receipt, after confirming through the Root's operation status that the Root never accepted it. Alternatively, make the Root validate the reservation before the Coordinator commits it. Classify a definite Root rejection separately from an uncertain call failure.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. `accept_root_removal` (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:497-513) commits the reservation through ops `prepare_root_draining_reservation` (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1690-1738) before it calls the Root. The identity check matches on the same root OR the same operation id (root_lifecycle.rs:360-371). Any request that differs from the stored one therefore returns conflict (ops mod.rs:1701-1709). RetryReset moves Failed to PendingReset (ops 254). prepare_reinspection then picks Reinspect for PendingReset/Failed whenever cycles > 0 (ops 326-331). Record that a full destructive reset is still owed: clear asset.cycles on a failed Reset or add an explicit reset-required flag, and have prepare_reinspection choose Reset for it. RetryReset moves Failed to PendingReset (ops 254). prepare_reinspection then picks Reinspect because cycles > 0 (ops 326-331). Only the reviewed capacity import enforces snapshots_size_bytes == 0 (ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:836). Backups create canister snapshots of Fleet canisters (crates/canic-host/src/icp/snapshot.rs:13-19), and nothing deletes them.

Recycling and Reinspect should read the snapshot inventory (or memory_metrics.snapshots_size) and either delete snapshots under the pending claim before uninstall, or mark the asset Failed and exclude it from Ready while snapshots_size != 0, matching capacity import. The 0.110 design (0.110-design.md:176-180) itself says uninstall does not erase snapshots. Recycling is reached from Component and leaf deletion (component_registry/mod.rs:5851-5883). Backups create snapshots and never delete them (canic-host/src/icp/snapshot.rs:13-19; the canic-backup runner has no delete path), and recovery controllers can take them. After a reset the controllers are root plus the recovery controllers (canic-core ids/fleet_topology/mod.rs:253-259), the same set that already controlled the old Component. No command lets the operator supply ledger evidence (for example a burn-block lookup or an observed canister ID) to settle it.

Add an operator-reviewed resolution command that takes exact evidence (a Cycles Ledger ICRC-3 block matching the created_at_time/amount, or an explicit no-effect attestation) and then either adopts the canister or closes the record as a reviewed terminal discard with conservation accounting. TooOld after an uncertain result blocks with UnresolvedAfterLedgerWindow (refill.rs:322-333). retry_blocked_creation refuses exactly that failure (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:893-895). It is excluded from cancel and rollover (1604-1624), and the only creation-clearing sites are 879, 901, 921 and 941, so the record persists forever. begin_handoff refuses while any creation exists (1058-1060), has_pending_lifecycle_work stays true (960-965), and finalize_inventory refuses both while it is set and while any non-Store asset remains (fleet_subnet_root.rs:386-392). That part is intended, and should not be reported as a bug on its own. What the design does not cover, and the later drain and retirement flow does not address, is the knock-on: an unrelated Ready asset cannot be handed off and Root can never be retired. No evidence-based resolution or reviewed-discard exists, which falls short of AGENTS.md's 'recovery must complete' and conservation-accounting requirements. Reaching this state needs more than 24h of stalled retries after an uncertain reply, for example maintenance disabled by another invariant failure or a frozen Root. That is uncommon but realistic, so medium.

`validate_removed_component_authority` calls `removed_component_allocation_for_receipt`, which collects and decodes every allocation record (`RootComponentRegistryStore::allocations()`, mod.rs:5114-5126). Root-wide loops call it once per Component. `terminal_root_component_history` does so for every allocation (mod.rs:1626-1644). That runs inside `terminal_root_inventory_plan`, which is invoked by prepare/begin root final inventory and again by `validate_root_final_inventory_record` on every later root-retirement step (root_retirement.rs:217-243, 674-691, 741-779). `require_admission_catalog_stable` does the same for every removed draining record (mod.rs:1199-1208). That feeds root admission projection compile (workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:277) and pool capacity import. It also decodes every entry in the registry map just to list partitions (`registry_components`, storage mod.rs:3707-3722). Removed allocations are never deleted, so N grows with churn and is bounded only by registry bytes, not by `maximum_component_instances`.

Pass the already-collected allocation map, or add a component-to-allocation index, into `validate_removed_component_authority`. Use a keyed or range lookup instead of a full principal-index scan: store a per-component principal count, or range-scan a composite key. Collect partitions via key ranges instead of decoding every entry. Add a bounded-cost test that seeds hundreds of removed Components.

Recovery commits the quota (ops/cost_guard.rs:254-256), and the quota is 64 operations per 60 s per command kind (workflow/deployment.rs:16-17, 48-51). The Root Timer Ownership step 5 (~905) says 'after any terminal outcome, resamples before selecting its next deadline', and the failure table gives 'balance above normal threshold -> schedule next observation'. A transport failure on the Coordinator's accept call keeps the same request resumable across backoff, which widens the window. The timer comes back only through CycleWorkflow::start (lifecycle, or SetCyclesFundingEnabled only: control-plane workflow/state/mod.rs:105; SetFleetStatus does not re-arm it), rotation reconcile, or a child transfer (nonroot_cycles.rs:427). Finalization never compares exports or package identity against the role (artifact_io/mod.rs:73-117).

Recommendation

Before any compilation, reject duplicate package or library names across all specs. Alternatively give each Cargo workspace or batch its own target subdirectory, or capture each group's outputs right after its batch, as is already done for the infrastructure artifacts. Locate artifacts from Cargo's `--message-format=json` compiler-artifact filenames rather than by package-name convention.

Specs are grouped by `cargo_workspace_root` (artifact.rs:469-480), but every Cargo command gets CARGO_TARGET_DIR from `context.workspace_root` (cache.rs:23-27, declarations cache.rs:181-184). The ordering matches the report: all declaration batches run first (artifact.rs:365-371), Candid is read from `<target>/declarations/.../<pkg>.wasm` (461-464), then all runtime batches run (396-416), and each finalizer reads `built_canister_wasm_path` (934-943), where the last group wins. `encode_protocol_build_context` rejects duplicate packages only within one group (canic-core role_contract/build_context/mod.rs:96-104). Nothing checks names across specs. Finalization only confirms that the embedded Candid equals the sidecar (artifact_io/mod.rs:84-86), and both come from the partner package, so this passes. Role a's recorded profile digest (role a plus partner Candid) will differ from the digest embedded in the shipped runtime (role b), so a post-install protocol check probably catches it, but only after the wrong code is installed. It needs an unusual config (same-named role packages in separate workspaces), so it stays medium.
mediumconfirmedhost-canister-build-2 · correctness · high confidence
Artifact paths are derived from `package_name.replace('-', "_")` instead of Cargo's library target name, so a role with a custom `[lib] name` fails confusingly or silently ships a stale Wasm left in the target directory.
crates/canic-host/src/canister_build/artifact.rs:942

Failure scenario

Package `app` declares `[lib] name = "app_canister", crate-type = ["cdylib"]`, so Cargo emits `app_canister.wasm`. On a clean target, extraction fails with a missing-file error that does not mention the library name. If `app.wasm` survives from a build before the library was renamed, Canic extracts Candid from the stale declaration Wasm, finalizes the stale runtime and reports success. The published release artifact then does not contain the current source.

Evidence

The declaration input path (artifact.rs:461-464), the single-role declaration path (806-809) and the runtime path (934-943) are all `format!("{}.wasm", package_name.replace('-', "_"))`. Cargo names the cdylib after the `[lib] name` target, which cargo metadata exposes as `CargoMetadataTarget.name` (cargo_metadata.rs:83-89). The builder never consults it. Role package validation constrains build scripts and dependencies but never the library target name (role_contract/package/mod.rs; there is no lib-name check). Nothing verifies that this invocation produced the file: there are no JSON artifact messages and no freshness check. Finalization simply reads whatever bytes are at the path (artifact_io/mod.rs:125, 351-357), and Candid extraction likewise hashes whatever file exists (candid_cache/mod.rs:154).

Recommendation

Resolve the cdylib target name from cargo metadata, or better, read `compiler-artifact.filenames` from `cargo build --message-format=json`. Fail when the expected file was not emitted by this invocation. Alternatively reject custom library names during role validation.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. All three artifact paths use `package_name.replace('-', "_")`: artifact.rs:464 for declarations, 809 for single-role declarations, and 942 for the runtime. Nothing consults the cdylib target name. `CargoMetadataTarget.name` exists (cargo_metadata.rs:83-89), but role validation never checks it. The only target-name comparison is in the dependency-tree resolver (role_contract/package/graph/mod.rs:302), which does not constrain the role's own library name. There is no JSON artifact capture, and no stale-file removal of the target-dir Wasm: `prepare_canister_artifact_output` (artifact.rs:538-544) only clears the ICP sidecars in artifact_root. Candid extraction hashes and uses whatever file exists (candid_cache/mod.rs:154-170). Finalization copies `source_wasm_path` without any identity check (artifact_io/mod.rs:121-125). With a custom `[lib] name`, a clean build fails at Candid extraction with a missing-file error that never mentions the library name. If an `app.wasm` from a pre-rename build survives in `target/canic-wasm`, Cargo does not delete the old uplifted file, and Canic silently extracts and ships the stale declaration and runtime. Medium fits: the path is less common, the clean case fails confusingly, and the stale case silently ships wrong bytes.

`input_snapshot` runs one catalog, for `context.workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml")` (reuse/mod.rs:347-352). For those workspaces the only coverage is the `.d` scan (dependencies/mod.rs:56-72). It scans only the directories of packages in that catalog and the config directory (368-393), and adds Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, toolchain and `.cargo/config` files only along the ancestors of the context and metadata workspace roots (399-412). Those manifests are derived from inputs that are already covered (App lock, canic sources, config). The retained journal evidence in docs/audits/reports/2026-09/2026-09-09/toko-feedback-evidence/retained-terminal-journal.json shows pre_canister_version values of 390, 422 and 1910. The unit tests keep canister_version constant (comparison/tests.rs:74,157).

Expose that epoch version in PublicHistorySnapshot in place of the live value, or drop canister_version from same_window and the timer check and rely on heap_started_at_ns plus registration identity. Add a fixture where the live canister_version advances between snapshots and results stay Available.

The result is SourceWindowChanged, or NonAdvancingWindow if the sampler did not advance. Timer rows fail within one snapshot once any message has run after init. crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/capacity_import/admission/observer/inventory/mod.rs:188

Pages::push rejects any page with pending_creation or pending_handoff. It also rejects any asset whose status is not Store, Ready or Workload, which covers Claimed, PendingReset, Recycling, HandingOff, StoreDeletionPending and Failed (admission/observer/inventory/mod.rs:185-209). finish additionally requires pending_reset == 0 (239-243).

The workflow reserves an inspection before each observer.source call (handoff/mod.rs:118-120, 128-130, 141-143), and MAX_INSPECTIONS is 4 (publication/mod.rs:43). These free membership reads can fail after the allowance is already spent.

Root's own quiet-pool check accepts Failed assets and fences only the destination Root (canic-control-plane ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:666-681). Other Roots keep running pool maintenance and component claims during the import.

Require quiescence only for the destination Root, which is already fenced. For other Roots, collect membership IDs for every status without requiring a quiet state, and accept Failed. Reserve the paid allowance after the free pre-reads succeed, immediately before the management call.

A bootstrap review cannot be retried after a failed first attempt, because the inspection record binds the first attempt's time-dependent plan hash.
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/infrastructure_bootstrap/inspection/mod.rs:84

The new timestamp produces a different plan hash, so inspection::reserve fails with Integrity. Changing the declarations fails at retain_request. The plan hash covers planned_at_time and per-action times (policy/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:71-75, 322, 335). The CLI passes now_nanoseconds() on every review (canic-cli/src/fleet/bootstrap/mod.rs:266). review_source reuses the retained plan's time only if a plan was already written (workflow/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:306).

plan() reserves the Review inspection before the live observation and verify_initial, and writes the plan only afterwards (workflow/infrastructure_bootstrap/mod.rs:99-109). The survey file pins the original desired fleet and declarations, and a different request fails with Integrity (survey/mod.rs:294-300).

The code comment claims 'A second round permits recovery of one lost response' (inspection/mod.rs:27).

Plan read/write round-trips every inline Store/fixture chunk byte through serde_json::Value, giving a roughly 32x memory blow-up that grows with release size and Root count
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/plan_content/mod.rs:100

Failure scenario

A release union of about 40 MiB of wasm.gz published to 3 Roots puts about 120 MiB of chunk bytes into plan/phase actions. Each read_plan/read_journal/write_plan builds a Value tree of about 4 GiB or more (at least 32 bytes per element), which can exhaust memory on an operator laptop or CI runner and makes plan/apply/resume slow.

Evidence

read_plan parses plan.json into a Value, then plan_content::hydrate reinserts each chunk as serde_json::to_value(bytes), a JSON array with one Value per byte (ops/plan_content/mod.rs:98-104; fixture/mod.rs:191-196), before serde_json::from_value (ops/mod.rs:754-771). write_plan first builds super::json::to_value(plan) with all inline bytes (ops/mod.rs:939-947) and only then strips them in remove_inline_bytes. Chunks go up to CANIC_WASM_CHUNK_BYTES (1 MiB) and are repeated per Root's Store sequence (ops/current_protocol/mod.rs:2389-2437). read_journal hydrates every successor phase the same way (ops/continuation/mod.rs:236-253), and apply reads both the plan and the journal on every invocation. The report path already avoids this by clearing bytes before to_value (json/mod.rs:137-152), but the durable path does not.

Recommendation

Project chunk payloads before building a Value: clone the action with publication bytes cleared and insert bytes_sha256/bytes_size directly (as report_json_value already does). On read, deserialize the hashed projection into a typed struct and load bytes straight into Vec<u8>, or encode bytes as hex/base64 strings, so no Value exists per byte.

Verifier (confirmed): plan_content::hydrate (ops/plan_content/mod.rs:98-104) inserts each chunk as serde_json::to_value(Vec<u8>), a Value::Array holding one Value::Number per byte. With default serde_json features, a Value is 32 bytes. This happens inside read_plan (ops/mod.rs:754-771) before from_value. write_plan (ops/mod.rs:939-947) calls json::to_value(plan) with all inline bytes, then remove_inline_bytes decodes each array back with from_value::<Vec<u8>> (plan_content:54-56). read_journal hydrates every successor phase through read_plan (ops/continuation/mod.rs:233-245), and retain_phase re-reads the phase too (continuation:220-226). Chunks come from append_chunk_actions (current_protocol/mod.rs:2389-2435) at 1 MiB (canic-core/src/lib.rs:83). The number of actions is bounded only by MAX_FLEET_ENSURE_PROTOCOL_STEPS = 4096 (model/mod.rs:26). The report path shows the intended fix already exists: action_json_value clears publication bytes before to_value (json/mod.rs:136-163). Peak transient memory is about 32x a plan's chunk bytes (at least 0.5 GiB for 15 MiB of release chunks, and several GiB for the multi-Root case described). This is host-side and transient, and not a canister limit. It fits 'resource cost that risks memory limits as fleets grow': medium.

It also requires the recomputed expected balance to equal that value (261-270). For the last Estate review, prepare() returns the retained review unchanged and never re-observes it, because only Native reviews are routed to refresh (funding/mod.rs:139-145). resume() with the plan digest returns EstateFundingRequired while that review has no effect (390-395). With the review digest it fails in verify_balance with DriftedBeforeApply (396). The Native path has exactly the missing mechanism: native::refresh replaces an unapproved review when the live balance drifts (native/mod.rs:322-372). Anyone can call icrc1_transfer to the Root's default account.

Mirror native::refresh for Estate reviews that have no effect and no operator_mint. When the observed Root account or pending creation differs, discard the unapproved review from a disposable journal copy, re-derive estate_funding_required from a fresh observation, and prepare a new review with a new timestamp.

Only Native reviews reach native::refresh (native/mod.rs:322-372). resume() with the plan digest returns EstateFundingRequired at funding/mod.rs:390-395. The main loop, which could re-derive the pause through retain_estate_funding_pause (workflow/mod.rs:1561-1580), runs only after funding::resume at workflow/mod.rs:1384 and is never reached. With the review digest, verify_balance needs balance_cycles == pause.available_cycles (211-214). Root's balance is a plain icrc1_balance_of on its default account (ops/platform.rs:1263-1273), and any principal can credit that account. The docs only tell the operator "Do not credit the account outside Canic or discard the journal" (docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:882). Tests restore the exact balance to recover (funding_tests/mod.rs:444-450), which cannot be done in production. So a Native-style refresh alone would not fix the third-party-credit case; the fix also needs a bounded rule for accepting credits. Kept at medium rather than high: it needs an uncommon Estate FundingRequired pause, no cycles are lost, and deleting the journal by hand is an unsupported way out.

Every fleet-a retry now fails with DriftedBeforeApply at native/mod.rs:569. While a Native Intent has no receipt, retry is allowed only if the operator balance equals exactly pre or pre - amount - fee (native/mod.rs:561-570). After the receipt it must equal exactly pre - amount - fee (600-602). Estate applied() requires pre - post == shortfall + fee exactly (funding/mod.rs:480-494), and a failure repeats on every retry once the receipt is stored (434-447). The prior_debit bounds treat any credit above operator_source as drift (native/mod.rs:489-501; funding/mod.rs:237-241; operator/mod.rs:114-121). All fleets and environments that use one identity share the default account (from_subaccount None, ops/platform.rs:2769-2772 and 2800-2808; balance read at 4234). The operation lock, however, is per environment and fleet (ops/mod.rs:547-561). The Cycles Ledger also has a FailedToWithdraw outcome with fee_block, in which the amount is refunded and only the fee is charged (platform.rs:587-591). It is mapped to a generic error (2790-2792) and leaves the balance at pre - fee, which neither admissible value matches.

Reconcile retained intents by authenticated ledger evidence. Look up the withdraw or transfer block from its receipt, or search by the created_at_time identity, and verify amount, fee, from and to, instead of relying on global balance equality. Handle FailedToWithdraw and its fee_block as a typed outcome that has been definitively refunded. Consider a per-operation subaccount or a cross-fleet operator lock, and document that the operator account must be used exclusively while an operation is in progress.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. native::resume accepts only operator_cycles == pre or pre - shortfall - fee (native/mod.rs:561-570), and after the receipt only pre - shortfall - fee (600-602). validate_observation rejects any credit above operator_source (489-501). Estate resume stores post_cycles from identity_cycles_balance (ops/platform.rs:5026-5031). applied() then needs an exact pre - post debit (funding/mod.rs:480-494). A failure is returned before the write at 451, so every retry repeats it. The balance is the operator's default account (platform.rs:4282, cycles_ledger_balance with subaccount None, 1263-1273). The lock covers only .canic/fleet-ensure/<env>/<fleet>/operation.lock (ops/mod.rs:547-561, 726-742), so another fleet or any other use of the same identity changes that balance unseen. FailedToWithdraw{fee_block} (platform.rs:587-591) becomes a generic LedgerWithdraw error (2790-2792), leaves the Intent with no receipt and leaves the balance at pre - fee, which matches neither admitted value. The fail-closed rule is deliberate: tests assert drift for 995/899/1001 and recover only by setting the balance back exactly (funding_tests/mod.rs:661-671). But no recovery is documented, and the docs never require exclusive use of the account while an operation is in flight. That conflicts with the required lost-response and interruption recovery. Kept at medium: no cycles are lost, FailedToWithdraw against a Root verified as running is rare, and an exact manual top-up can sometimes restore an admissible balance.
mediumconfirmedhost-ensure-platform-3 · correctness · medium confidence
FailedToCreate/FailedToWithdraw are resubmitted with the same dedup identity, and the resulting Duplicate is misread as a pending creation or a successful withdrawal receipt
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:5508

Failure scenario

A Create targets a subnet the CMC rejects, or the CMC fails transiently: the Ledger returns FailedToCreate and refunds everything except the fee. When the operator reruns, the Ledger answers Duplicate{canister_id: None}. The host reports LedgerCreatePending on every attempt until the window turns it into TooOld, and never gives a typed 'known failed' outcome. Similarly, a withdraw whose deposit_cycles is rejected returns FailedToWithdraw. The rerun gets Duplicate, the host adopts it as a receipt, and observation fails with NativeFundingBalanceDrift, reporting a refunded payment as balance drift.

Evidence

`create_canister_response_outcome` (platform.rs:5490-5515) maps FailedToCreate{fee_block, refund_block} to LedgerCreate(String) and Duplicate{canister_id: None} to LedgerCreatePending ('duplicate does not yet identify its created canister'). `apply_fund` (2779-2793) treats any Duplicate{duplicate_of} as a successful receipt. A failed first attempt leaves the record in Intent, and it is resubmitted with identical arguments (workflow/mod.rs:1707-1812), so the Ledger's duplicate detection answers the retry with the original failed and refunded burn. For Create, canister_id is then permanently None. For withdraw, the host records the burn block as proof of issuance, and native_funding_completion (5315-5328) then raises NativeFundingBalanceDrift because no cycles arrived. The Root control plane tells these apart: Duplicate{None} is uncertain-pending (refill.rs:202-211) while FailedToCreate becomes Blocked LedgerCreationFailed (246-251).

Recommendation

Persist the typed failure (fee_block, refund_block) in the EffectRecord and mark the intent KnownFailed so it is not resubmitted. Treat Duplicate{canister_id: None} as pending only while no failure has been recorded. Cross-check a withdraw Duplicate against the Ledger blocks (burn followed by refund) before adopting it as a receipt.

Verifier (confirmed): The code matches the claim. `create_canister_response_outcome` (platform.rs:5490-5515) maps `Duplicate{canister_id: None}` to `LedgerCreatePending` and every other error, including FailedToCreate, to `LedgerCreate(String)`. `apply_fund` (2763-2795) adopts any `WithdrawError::Duplicate` as a receipt. When `platform.apply` fails (workflow/mod.rs:1775-1795), the record stays `Intent` and nothing records the definite failure. `created_at_time` is fixed inside the action (platform.rs:2742, 2772), so a rerun sends the byte-identical request. The failed original's burn block holds that dedup identity. The Cycles Ledger contract says Duplicate carries `canister_id` only 'if the original created a canister', so after a failed create a duplicate answer with None is expected. For withdraw, the adopted receipt marks the record Issued, and `native_funding_completion` (5315-5328) then returns NativeFundingBalanceDrift on every resume. Root handles this correctly: refill.rs:246-251 blocks FailedToCreate as a known failure and never resubmits. Impact: the command fails closed, and the refund (minus fee) returns to the operator account, so no cycles are lost. But the InProgress journal pins the plan (workflow/mod.rs:517-540, 1316), and I found no abandon path, so the operation cannot complete and the operator gets a misleading diagnosis. It needs a definite CMC or deposit failure, which is rare but realistic, so medium holds. The Ledger dedup behaviour after failure comes from the Ledger contract; this repo does not contain the Ledger source to confirm it.
mediumconfirmedhost-ensure-platform-5 · cycles · medium confidence
Ordinary live observation drops reserved_cycles, so Delete's material-cycles guard and controlled-cycle accounting ignore reserved balances that deletion destroys
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:4875

Failure scenario

A retiring canister on a subnet above the storage-reservation threshold holds 0.05T liquid, within maximum_remaining_cycles, plus 3T reserved. Drain and Stop succeed, Delete passes the guard, and 3T of controlled cycles are burned without ever being observed or reviewed as terminal residual discard.

read_status_with (platform.rs:1777-1812) builds LiveCanister.cycles from the liquid `cycles` field only, although IcpCanisterStatusReport exposes reserved_cycles (icp/model.rs:91). direct_local_status_optional (1841-1847) likewise decodes only `cycles`. The Delete effect (4868-4891) checks maximum_remaining_cycles against live.cycles, then calls delete_canister_without_cycle_recovery, which also destroys the reserved balance. The drain endpoint cannot move reserved cycles. A retiring canister's reserved balance is therefore discarded without appearing in the reviewed residual bound or in observed controlled cycles. Other Canic flows do count reserved cycles as controlled (ops/completed_preparation/mod.rs:475-503 adds reserved_cycles to the balance; the capacity-import and startup-funding views carry them too).

Recommendation

Carry reserved_cycles in LiveCanister and fail if the status report omits it. Include it in controlled-cycle observations and in the Delete guard (liquid + reserved <= maximum_remaining_cycles), and report it explicitly as a reviewed terminal discard.

Verifier (confirmed): `read_status_with` (platform.rs:1744-1813) builds LiveCanister from the liquid `cycles` field only, although `IcpCanisterStatusReport` carries `reserved_cycles` (icp/model.rs:91). `ManagementCanisterObservationResponse` (platform.rs:115-121), used by direct local status, does not decode it at all. The policy uses only liquid `live.cycles` for the material check (policy/mod.rs:1895). A canister with low liquid cycles and a large reserved balance therefore gets no drain and goes straight to Stop plus Delete. The only reviewed burn it gets is `maximum_remaining_cycles = material_threshold` (1955-1960). The Delete apply (platform.rs:4868-4891) checks liquid cycles only, then runs `icp canister delete --no-recover-cycles` (icp/canister.rs:287-294), which discards the reserved balance too. `controlled_cycles` (workflow/mod.rs:4092+) also sums only liquid cycles, so the reserved balance never enters the conservation equation. Other Canic flows do treat reserved cycles as controlled: `validate_debit` sums native and reserved (ops/completed_preparation/mod.rs:497-510), and completed_reset does the same (mod.rs:454). Reserved cycles cannot be drained, so the loss is unavoidable once the canister is deleted. The defect is that the discard is never observed or reviewed as a terminal residual. It needs a subnet above the storage-reservation threshold, and each canister is capped by `reserved_cycles_limit` (5T by default). Medium is right.
mediumconfirmedhost-ensure-reinstall-3 · robustness · medium confidence

crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/completed_preparation/mod.rs:204

Failure scenario

An operator applies the documented v0.110.44 preparation, which seals the Coordinator and Roots. They then upgrade the CLI to 0.110.46, as the docs require in order to build against the current release. From then on, `fleet ensure`, `fleet ensure --reinstall`, `--apply <preparation review>` and `fleet generate` all fail. The sealed, non-functional Fleet cannot be reset without the old CLI or manual file deletion that the docs forbid. This contradicts the policy that a release transition must not require the old CLI.

Evidence

In v0.110.44, `fleet ensure --reinstall` on a completed Fleet was dispatched to completed_preparation (the tag's CLI dispatch has only completed_reset and completed_preparation). Preparation seals the Coordinator and Root mutation and timer owners and writes completed-preparation-journal.json. In 0.110.46 that leftover journal blocks every path:
- Every lock_operation calls require_no_intent, which returns CompletedPreparationInProgress for any plan or apply (ops/mod.rs:685-693; ops/completed_preparation/mod.rs:515-525).
- Clean reinstall goes prepare_bootstrap → begin → require_terminal_side_effects, which rejects a preparation whose source is the completed operation (ops/operation_selection/retirement/mod.rs:90-132, `source == operation` at 125).
- The only consumer, preparation::review → verify, rejects any review whose cli_release or operation_id differs from env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") (192-220, cli_release check at 204). So `--apply <review>` and `fleet generate` both fail with Conflict (generate/completed_source/mod.rs:40).
- publication::retirement::retire removes only consumed preparations (ops/reinstall/adoption/publication/retirement/mod.rs:27-45).

The 0.110.46 CLI can no longer create or finish a preparation, because clean reinstall is dispatched first (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:508-518).

Recommendation

Seals are not paid effects, and the clean infrastructure reinstall clears them. Let clean-reinstall retirement take ownership of a non-consumed preparation from any CLI release: archive its review and journal bytes into the retirement archive instead of rejecting them, and remove the require_no_intent gate from lock_operation. Alternatively, hard-cut the obsolete lane together with its gates.

Severity adjusted from high to medium during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is real. v0.110.44's dispatch (cli fleet/mod.rs run_ensure) sent `--reinstall` on a completed supplied-estate Fleet to completed_preparation. In 0.110.45 and .46, clean_reinstall runs first (canic-cli/src/fleet/mod.rs:508). For a converged full plan, workflow::selected returns `reinstall` (clean_reinstall/mod.rs:60-63). The review path is prepare_bootstrap -> begin -> require_terminal_side_effects, which rejects any preparation whose source is the completed operation, even when prepared=true (retirement/mod.rs:109-132, line 125). `--apply <old review>` then falls through to completed_preparation::run_if_selected, and verify rejects it on the cli_release/operation_id binding (completed_preparation/mod.rs:197-204). Plain ensure hits require_no_intent through lock_operation (ops/mod.rs:690). Correction: `fleet generate` fails earlier than claimed, at retained_contract::check -> require_terminal_side_effects (generate/mod.rs:781-799, retained_contract/mod.rs:137-143), not at completed_source:40. Blocking a prepared same-source preparation is deliberate and is tested (retirement/tests.rs:67-95). It still breaks AGENTS.md's rule that a completed previous release must not require its old CLI. Severity lowered to medium. No cycles are at risk and application canisters keep running. Recovery is still possible with the published 0.110.44 CLI (finishing its reset in the same release) or by removing the two files. Only operators who applied the ≤0.110.44 preparation and upgraded before the reset can reach this.
mediumconfirmedhost-ensure-reinstall-4 · correctness · medium confidence
The Root reinstall prerequisite stops and reinstalls a running Root after checking completeness only against stale host state, orphaning pool assets the Root created after the last ensure
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/policy/root_reinstall/mod.rs:85

Failure scenario

After the last terminal ensure, the mainnet Root's refill creates P5, or a Cycles Ledger creation is still pending. A new release changes the Root Wasm. Ordinary `fleet ensure` plans Stop → Install(Reinstall) → Start, and require_complete_estate passes because P5 is not in host state. The reinstall wipes the Root's pool and pending-creation records. The following Full plan imports only canister_pool_imports. P5's cycles, or the in-flight creation's Ledger debit, are stranded with no conservation failure reported.

Ordinary planning compiles this Root reset from management status alone, before any protected observation (workflow/mod.rs:664-701). Its only completeness gate, require_complete_estate (policy/root_reinstall/mod.rs:85, 233-288), has three gaps:
- It walks only state.principals and state.topology from the last terminal publication.
- It skips principals that have no topology entry (255-258).
- It ignores pending_principals.

At apply, root_reinstall::verify_effect_authority checks only the management binding, the Stopped status and funding (workflow/root_reinstall/mod.rs:263-350). No Root pool page and no pending Cycles Ledger creation is read before Stop. root_reinstall::complete measures conservation over Root balances only (105-133). Generation also skips live pool enumeration when the Root module differs (generate/mod.rs:1693-1701). The activation lane shows the intended guard: it re-inventories every asset before its Stop (workflow/reinstall/activation/mod.rs:180-196). Meanwhile, mainnet Roots refill their pools from a recurring timer (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:284-287).

crates/canic-host/src/fleet_package/mod.rs:112

The next `canic build` rebuilds, but root, wasm_store and fleet_coordinator still resolve the old transitive version from their preserved generated locks, and cargo metadata keeps compatible locked versions. Evidence

Each generated manifest declares its own `[workspace]` (fleet_package/mod.rs:85), so Cargo uses `.canic/generated/<pkg>/Cargo.lock`. materialize copies the workspace lock only when that file is absent: `if !lock.is_file() && workspace.join("Cargo.lock").is_file() { fs::copy(...) }` (lines 111-114). Build-mode package validation then runs cargo metadata without `--locked`, because `PackageValidationMode::locked()` is false for Build (role_contract/package/mod.rs:90-92, 578-596). That rewrites the generated lock while preserving previously locked versions. The infrastructure builds use `--locked` against this lock (bootstrap_store/mod.rs:197-201). Nothing re-seeds it from the workspace; `fleet_package` is the only Cargo.lock writer in the host. The audit record calls lock preservation intentional (docs/audits/reports/2026-09/2026-09-08/generated-fleet-artifacts.md: "preserves unchanged source files and existing locks"), while the feature doc promises the packages "bind the exact Canic dependency" and "exact dependency graph". `fs::copy` is not atomic.

Recommendation

Re-derive the generated lock from the workspace lock on every materialization (copy atomically, then let cargo prune it), or fail when the generated lock's shared package versions diverge from the workspace lock. Include the generated locks in the reported provenance and cache inputs, and write the seed through durable_io's atomic writer.

Each generated manifest is its own workspace (line 85). Build-mode validation then runs unlocked cargo metadata against it (role_contract/package/mod.rs:90-92, 587-603; the Store calls it at bootstrap_store/mod.rs:121-125), and cargo keeps existing locked versions. The Store build uses `--locked` against that lock (bootstrap_store/mod.rs:197-201). Root is materialized the same way (canonical_root/mod.rs:71), as is the coordinator (bootstrap_coordinator/mod.rs:124). No code re-seeds the lock or compares it with the workspace lock, and fleet_package is the only Cargo.lock writer in canic-host. The result is that `cargo update` in the workspace never reaches root, wasm_store or coordinator transitive dependencies on a persistent checkout, which contradicts the audit's "exact dependency graph" claim (generated-fleet-artifacts.md:10-11). Mitigating factors: `.canic` is gitignored (.gitignore:45), so fresh CI and release checkouts seed from the current workspace lock. Root build provenance already hashes the generated lock (build_provenance/inputs.rs:53-55); non-root roles hash the workspace lock. A truncated seed is low-probability, and cargo would fail loudly on it rather than build silently. Drift on long-lived operator workstations is still a realistic supply-chain gap for the most privileged canisters, so medium stands.

canic_root_command runs eval_default_fleet_guard(AllowsUpdates) on every variant except SetCyclesFunding and SetFleetStatus (root.rs:201-213). guard_fleet_update rejects both Readonly and Disabled (crates/canic-core/src/access/fleet.rs:34-44).

The Prepared-root variant list omits SetCyclesFunding and SetFleetStatus (root.rs:371-394). require_root_command_variant_allowed(false) therefore returns Fenced while root is Prepared (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:482-499). BootstrapStore, PrepareComponentRegistry, PrepareFleetActivation and ResumeFleetActivation all fail at the guard, while SetFleetStatus(Enabled) fails at the Prepared fence.

Non-roots inherit the same init_mode (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:238-240). Their ConfigureRuntime, ActivateFleet and PrepareFleetCredential are Fleet-guarded too (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:590-601; wasm_store.rs:67-78). They could only be unlocked by a SynchronizeState cascade, which triggers finding 1 on Components.

Recommendation

Either reject non-enabled init_mode at build validation, or: add SetFleetStatus and SetCyclesFunding to the Prepared-root allowlist; exempt root-owned bootstrap and activation variants and the root-to-child control commands (ConfigureRuntime, ActivateFleet, PrepareFleetCredential) from the application Fleet guard; and add a PocketIC case with init_mode = "readonly".

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. Root init creates Prepared activation state (root.rs:48-55), then sets Fleet state from config (root.rs:93-94). CONFIG.md:86 documents readonly and disabled, the schema accepts both (schema/mod.rs:445-452), and ConfigOps::app_init_mode maps them directly (ops/config/mod.rs:272-279). No validation rejects either value. canic_root_command applies the AllowsUpdates guard to every variant except SetCyclesFunding and SetFleetStatus (endpoints/root.rs:201-213), and guard_fleet_update rejects both Readonly and Disabled (access/fleet.rs:34-44). The prepared allowlist at root.rs:371-394 omits SetCyclesFunding and SetFleetStatus, so while root is Prepared require_root_role_variant_allowed returns Fenced (fleet_activation.rs:482-499). Root exposes no other bootstrap update endpoint: every other root endpoint is status or observability. post_upgrade does not re-run init_mode (root.rs:101-130), so an upgrade cannot clear the state. Recovery requires a rebuild and a reinstall, both routine before 1.0. No cycles are lost, and a controller can still reinstall, so this is a recoverable wedge rather than a permanent one: medium, not critical. The comment 'State recovery must remain reachable' at root.rs:200 shows the fence contradicts the stated intent.
mediumconfirmedr2-cross-root-trust-2 · contract · high confidence
Delegated-token and role-attestation trust anchors are one App-wide root, so every issuer and attestation subject under any other Fleet Subnet Root permanently fails, even inside its own subtree
crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/token/verifier_config.rs:9

Failure scenario

canic.toml pins root_canister_id to R1, as offline derivation requires. An issuer Component is placed on R2. Its lazy repair calls R1, which rejects it as not a local member, so the issuer never gets a proof and no tokens are minted in R2's subtree. Role attestations R2 signs for its own children fail every verifier, including R2's sibling canisters. If root_canister_id is left unset with an explicit key, R2 signs with its own derived tECDSA key, which does not match the configured public key, so the batch is discarded and delegated auth never works under R2.

Evidence

The verifier root is the configured root_canister_id, or EnvOps::root_pid() if unset (verifier_config.rs:9-14). The chain-key policy pins one public_key_hex (verifier_config.rs:37-121). Offline derivation requires an explicit root_canister_id before the build (docs/contracts/AUTH_DELEGATED_SIGNATURES.md:421). All roots must run the same release build (ops/fleet_registry/validation/mod.rs:154-160), so every subtree compiles the same anchor. Root signing uses canister_self with the App-wide public key (ops/auth/delegated/chain_key_signing.rs:117-162), and signatures that do not verify against that key are discarded. Issuers repair their proofs by calling verifier.root_canister_id (workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/mod.rs:349-359). That root serves GetOrCreateDelegationProof only to its own active Component members (root.rs:295-311; api/component_auth/mod.rs:31-52). Role-attestation proofs are checked against the single configured root id (ops/auth/attestation.rs:156-170). No build-time or plan-time check stops an issuer or attestation-using Spec from being admitted on more than one root.

Recommendation

Carry per-root trust anchors through protected authority: give each Component its root's canister id and derived chain-key public key at install, or verify proofs against the issuing root once it is authenticated as an Active Registry root. Until then, reject at build or plan time any delegated-token issuer, or any Spec that uses role attestations, that is admitted on a root other than the pinned root_canister_id. Document that auth is single-root.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. The verifier root is the one configured `root_canister_id`, or `EnvOps::root_pid()` when it is unset (verifier_config.rs:9-14). root_pid is set per subtree to that subtree's own Fleet Subnet Root (workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:172-175, root.rs:75). The chain-key policy pins a single `public_key_hex` (verifier_config.rs:42-43, 102-121). Every root signs as `IcOps::canister_self()` (ops/auth/delegation/mod.rs:168-172, 216, 240) and checks the returned signature against the configured key (chain_key_signing.rs:196-203). A second root's tECDSA key is derived from a different canister id, so its batches always fail. Issuer lazy repair calls `verifier.root_canister_id` (workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/mod.rs:349-358), and that root admits only its own active Component members (control-plane workflow/component_auth/mod.rs:25-31). There is a single App-wide AuthConfig (config/schema/mod.rs:171). The runbook assumes one Root identity (root-proof-provisioning.md:28), but nothing documents or rejects issuers on other roots: the host only projects auth flags (release_set/config/projection/details.rs:44-50). One correction: if root_canister_id is unset, role attestations still verify inside each root's own subtree (canister-signature check against the per-subtree root_pid, attestation.rs:156-166). The attestation failure applies only when root_canister_id is pinned, although cross-subtree tokens and attestations fail in both modes. The failure is fail-closed, not a bypass, so medium stands.
mediumconfirmedr2-group-provisioning-pipeline-1 · liveness · high confidence
A Root whose pool refill is waiting for Estate funding can never be recorded as Provisioned, and the funding requirement is never shown to the host
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1166

Failure scenario

On a mainnet install, the Root pool holds exactly the batch's ready assets (for example imported capacity). The batch claims them, and the maintenance timer starts a refill to minimum_size. The Root's Cycles Ledger balance is short, so the refill goes WaitingForFunding. The Root then finishes and reports Provisioned with estate_funding_required set. Every Coordinator poll now fails with invariant and is retried every second. The Coordinator status shows only a pending_root_failure, not a funding request, so the host never funds. The operation, and with it Fleet admission, funding rotation and scale-out, stays blocked until someone deposits into the Root's Cycles Ledger account out of band.

Evidence

status_response copies the Root-wide CanisterPoolOps::estate_funding_required() into every provisioning status (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:3457). That value is Some whenever any pool creation is WaitingForFunding (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1016-1045). The maintenance timer refills to minimum_size independently of the batch (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:230-288), so once a batch claims ready assets the refill can wait for funding even though the batch needs nothing more. advance_component_root_provisioning sends every response carrying the flag to record_component_provisioning_estate_funding_pause, whatever its phase (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1165-1172). For a Provisioned response, validate_estate_funding_pause_progress sees progress, so the response is stored as `current` (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1128-1134). validate_current then runs validate_current_root_provision_record, which requires `current` to be an Accepted, result-free response (component_provisioning_validation/mod.rs:341-359; reconciliation/mod.rs:294-301), so the commit fails with invariant. The normal record path also rejects any response carrying the flag (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1030-1032). Because the pause never commits, the Coordinator status never shows estate_funding_required. The host requests funding only from that field (canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/mod.rs:1563-1587). Automatic refill is disabled off mainnet (workflow/canister_pool/refill.rs:40-45), so PocketIC never reaches this path.

Recommendation

Take the pause path only for an Accepted response whose remaining claims are not covered by ready assets. For Provisioned or claim-complete responses, strip the flag and record them normally, and let record_component_provisioning_root accept the flag once claims are complete. Consider scoping the Root's reported flag to the batch's own remaining demand. Add a test with a Provisioned response that carries the flag.

The Coordinator sends any flagged response to the pause path (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1166-1171). validate_estate_funding_pause_progress accepts Provisioned as progress (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:2567-2589; reconciliation/mod.rs:246-263) and stores it as `current` (mod.rs:1128-1134). validate_current_root_provision_record then requires an Accepted, result-free `current` (validation/mod.rs:341-359; reconciliation/mod.rs:294-301), so the commit fails with invariant. The normal path would reject the response anyway (mod.rs:1030). Each retry first clears the Coordinator's estate_funding_required when it commits the intent (mod.rs:988) and later takes the Reconcile path, so the host never sees funding (current_protocol/mod.rs:1304-1306). Nothing in the Root clears WaitingForFunding except a deposit or draining (refill.rs:394-411, 90-107). No test covers a Provisioned response that carries the flag. I downgraded severity because reachability is narrower than stated. The observed-pool host plan pre-funds workloads plus minimum_size ready assets (policy/mod.rs:3095-3107; workflow/mod.rs:2886-2910), so the tail refill falls short only after drift, for example a failed attempt that cost a fee. The full wedge needs the Root's first flagged observation to be Provisioned. Out-of-band funding recovers it, although the host tells operators not to do that (workflow/mod.rs:82).
mediumconfirmedr2-group-provisioning-pipeline-2 · liveness · medium confidence
The Root records a Provisioning-stage failure while it waits for Estate funding, and the Coordinator turns that failure into an error before it reads estate_funding_required, so the designed funding pause is almost never retained
crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:337

Failure scenario

A batch is accepted while the pool is WaitingForFunding, or its ready assets are taken by an unfenced child allocation after acceptance. The Root's claim step waits and records an UNAVAILABLE Backoff failure. From then on every Coordinator poll is an error that is retried every second. In AcceptingRoots this also triggers the batch re-sends described in the next finding. The host sees only a generic pending failure and never gets a funding request.

Evidence

When a claim is waiting for funding, require_ready_pool_capacity returns Ok (component_provisioning.rs:1533-1535) and ensure_remaining_claim_capacity returns Ok(false) (1544-1556). advance then returns the unchanged status (429-432). advance_scheduled_provisioning treats a no-progress Ok as `unavailable`, tags it with stage Provisioning and Backoff, and calls record_failure (337-350). The failure is cleared only when progress changes (319-328). The Coordinator reads Root status through query_root_component_provisioning, which applies observed_root_failure first (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1287-1295). observed_root_failure returns an error for any Provisioning-stage failure while the Root is Accepted (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:160-172), so the funding check at workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1166 is never reached. A pause captured in the short window before the first failure is dropped by the next Begin, which clears estate_funding_required (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:988). The host then clears its own pause when the field disappears (host workflow/mod.rs:1588-1593). The unit tests build Root responses with last_failure None (workflow/fleet_coordinator/tests.rs:3554-3630), which hides this. Acceptance also admits a batch without ready capacity when funding is required, and it does not reserve the ready assets it checked; child allocations are not fenced by the active batch (component_registry/mod.rs:1093-1125).

Recommendation

Do not record a failure for a pure funding wait, or give it a distinct non-error disposition. In the Coordinator, check estate_funding_required before observed_root_failure, and handle funding pauses during acceptance as well. Reserve or recheck the batch's ready assets against concurrent child claims.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed as described. On the Root, require_ready_pool_capacity returns Ok when estate_funding_required() is Some (component_provisioning.rs:1533-1535). ensure_remaining_claim_capacity then returns Ok(false) (1553-1555), and advance returns the unchanged view (429-432). In advance_scheduled_provisioning, progress_changed is false and failure_changed is false. The unchanged Ok result is then turned into UNAVAILABLE with stage Provisioning and retry Backoff (337-344), and record_failure stores it (347-353). Only progress clears it (319-328). status_response sends last_failure and estate_funding_required together (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:3450-3458). query_root_component_provisioning runs observed_root_failure first (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1287-1295), and that returns an error for a Provisioning-stage failure in the Accepted phase (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:160-172). So `?` at 1164 returns before the funding branch at 1166. That branch is reachable only in the short window before the Root's first failed claim attempt. Begin then clears the retained pause (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:988). The host reads estate_funding_required only from Coordinator status (host current_protocol/mod.rs:1304-1306). It sees a Backoff pending_root_failure and gets ReplayExactIssuedCommand (1320-1322), not EstateFundingRequired. The only funding-pause tests I found are Coordinator unit tests that inject funding directly (workflow/fleet_coordinator/tests.rs:3554ff). Medium is right: the paused operation livelocks and stays recoverable only outside the protocol.
