Failure scenario

A two-Root fleet on subnets A and B runs out of Ready assets through normal scaling. Both Roots start refills and move to WaitingForFunding. Every later `fleet ensure` review fails with MixedSubnetCreationFees before it can plan a FundEstate for either Root, so neither pool ever refills and later Component or child allocations fail CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT. In a second case, a Root sits on a 34-node subnet where cost_create_canister is about 1.3T but the seed says 500B. The host funds 500B-based creations, Root waits for funding, and every review then fails with 'pending creation amount differs'.

validate_creation_fee_scope counts the subnet of every domain whose required_creation_count or pending_creation_count is nonzero, and fails with MixedSubnetCreationFees when more than one subnet appears (creation_fee/mod.rs:22-44). compile_plan calls it unconditionally (policy/mod.rs:679). pending_creation_count is 1 for any unmaterialized Root refill, including WaitingForFunding (policy/mod.rs:2957-2965). Root refill derives its fee at runtime from ic0.cost_create_canister (canister_pool/refill.rs:374-379; canic-core ops/ic/mod.rs:49-55). The host instead requires pending.creation_amount_cycles == floor + margin + desired.management_creation_fee_cycles and otherwise fails compile_plan with EstateFundingTopology (policy/mod.rs:2943-2956), even when creation is deferred. During apply, a Root funding requirement that carries a different fee becomes PlanIntegrity (workflow/mod.rs:2945-2958). The fee comes only from `--management-creation-fee-cycles`, and the CLI rejects that option unless `--fresh` is given (canic-cli fleet/mod.rs:201-210), so a retained estate cannot correct it. Root has no other way to fund its Cycles Ledger account.

Recommendation

Bind the creation fee per Root subnet, taking it from the Root's own reported pool creation authority or a per-subnet fee catalog, rather than one seed scalar. Check the fee scope only against creations this plan actually funds, not against unrelated pending Root refills. Allow a reviewed fee refresh on non-fresh estates.

(a) validate_creation_fee_scope adds the Root's subnet for every domain with a nonzero pending_creation_count (creation_fee/mod.rs:27-43). compile_plan calls it unconditionally (policy/mod.rs:679). Even the deferred or reconciliation-only path still counts pending.unmaterialized (policy/mod.rs:2700-2733), so reuse and reinstall plans are rejected too. Retained apply re-checks the scope (workflow/mod.rs:1198-1203). On mainnet, Roots refill on their own maintenance timer (canister_pool/mod.rs:262-287) and move to WaitingForFunding when their account is short (refill.rs:148,221,406). Two Roots on different subnets can therefore block every Fleet Ensure compile, and FundEstate is the only reviewed way to fund them. The test at funding_tests/mod.rs:334-342 pins this behaviour. It is a documented CANIC-141 limitation (fleet-ensure.md:685-693; toko-upstream-feedback.md:30). The documented workaround, one subnet per operation, does not help here, because the operator cannot control when a Root starts a refill. Draining or out-of-band funding (which the guidance tells operators not to do) are the only ways out. No cycles are lost and Root keeps running, so this is medium, not high. crates/canic-host/src/component_topology/mod.rs:192

Failure scenario

The pool has canister_cycles 5T and margin 1T. The Component Spec has initial_cycles 5T, and its child role has initial_cycles 20T (as in canisters/audit/root_probe/native-child-recovery.toml). Generation and planning pass. During ProvisionComponents the Component asks Root for its initial child. validate_root_pool_capacity compares only component_specs[spec].initial_cycles with pool_target_cycles (component_topology/mod.rs:184-200). Both generation and protocol_actions rely on this check (generate/mod.rs:870; ops/current_protocol/mod.rs:399-408). On Root, child_creation_plan takes initial_cycles from ConfigOps::try_get_canister_by_role(child_role), which is the child's own initial_cycles and defaults to 5T (component_registry/mod.rs:5441-5458; config/schema/component_spec/mod.rs:21-23, 263-301). Root then claims only a Ready asset whose cycles are at least that value (component_installation/mod.rs:51-57; ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:386-392). The fallback maintain_ready_capacity_once(1) returns Maintained whenever any Ready asset exists (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:284-286), and refill funds only floor + creation_execution_margin (refill.rs:368-374). Extend validate_root_pool_capacity to cover every role that can be created initially (Component and child), using the same role-based initial_cycles resolution Root uses. Alternatively, have Root top up a claimed floor-sized asset to the role's initial_cycles, and forecast that demand in startup funding.

crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:4322

A Root reset of a recycled asset fails after stop_canister but before uninstall_code. The asset becomes Failed with its old cycle count and a module still installed. protocol_actions returns only the pool-reconciliation actions whenever any exist, which suppresses Store, Registry, ProvisionComponents and readiness actions (ops/platform.rs:4316-4324). compile_pool_reconciliation selects every PendingReset or Failed asset with no filter on the failure reason (ops/current_protocol/mod.rs:413-457). compile_plan then adds a paid Fund for each asset below floor + margin, ordered before the import (policy/mod.rs:860-958, 653-655, 676). Root's ImportPoolCanister on a Failed asset with nonzero recorded cycles takes the non-destructive Reinspect path (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:326-331). That path requires exact Root controllers and no installed module, and otherwise fails with conflict (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:657-664). Reconcile only assets whose failure funding can fix (for example, underfunded ones), or run reconciliation alongside other work instead of exclusively. ReconcilePoolAsset calls Root `admin Import` (canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:467-487). For any existing row whose origin is not Imported, `initialize_imports` returns conflict immediately (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:120-124), before the Reinspect path is reached. The finding's state is reachable: `mark_failed` keeps a recycled asset as Recycling{Failed} (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:223-227), and `recycling_completion` converts it to Failed, origin Recycled, with the old cycle count retained (1647-1651). An ordinary underfunded recycle reaches the same Failed/Recycled state (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:630-643), so reachability is broader than claimed. The host maps any non-Imported response to an error (current_protocol/mod.rs:1352-1362). The Intent effect is retried from the InProgress journal on every resume (workflow/mod.rs:1316-1318). A narrow escape exists for the underfunded case: after the host funds the asset, Root RetryReset makes it Ready, and the effect observation then counts it as satisfied (current_protocol/mod.rs:1114-1117). mediumconfirmedr2-recycled-principal-authority-2 · correctness · medium confidence

Failure scenario

B registers Q, now a pool asset or another tenant's canister, as its worker, and never obtains a real one. Case (b): A left a RecoveryRequired root.request_cycles receipt (core-rpc-ic-1). Placement receipts awaiting acknowledgement, ExternalEffectInFlight receipts and RecoveryRequired receipts never expire (storage/stable/replay.rs:401-416).

Operation IDs derived by a workload restart after reinstall. Placement IDs hash actor = canister_self, kind, pool, slot and a generation read from local intent totals (model/placement/allocation.rs:137-143; workflow/placement/allocation.rs:85-87; scaling/mod.rs:237-240; sharding/allocation.rs:53-70). crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/mod.rs:185

Failure scenario

A compromised or buggy active Component, or any of its children, calls canic_root_command PrepareRoleAttestation about 34 times a second, each call with a fresh request_id and ttl_ns set to 300 s. Every call succeeds, because the pending counts stay at 0. About 10,000 unexpired Committed receipts accumulate. From then on, every ProvisionCanister, AllocatePlacementChild, RecycleCanister and RequestCycles call from every Component on that root fails with ReplayStoreCapacityReached, because the 256-per-request purge finds nothing expired. Automatic cycle top-ups and child placement stop fleet-wide on that root while the flood lasts. Each prepare also scans and decodes the whole receipt map twice. Without any attack, a Component that legitimately prepares more than 512 attestations in 5 minutes locks its own root-capability calls with CallerCapacityReached.

Evidence

The manifest labels PrepareRoleAttestation replay_protected with ROOT_CANISTER_SIGNATURE_PREPARE_QUOTA_V1 (replay_policy/role_command_manifest.rs:128-134). At runtime the root arm only requires ActiveComponentMemberPredicate (macros/endpoints/root.rs:314-330, :613-616), which admits Components and ComponentChildren (prepare/admission.rs:84-99). The workflow calls reserve_or_replay_receipt (prepare/mod.rs:185). That function applies only pending_receipt_quota_decision (ops/replay/receipt.rs:191-199, :222-238, :317-338). Pending means Reserved, InFlight or RecoveryRequired (storage/stable/replay.rs:401-409), and the prepare reserves and commits inside one message with no await (prepare/mod.rs:185-244), so its pending count is always 0. The resulting Committed receipts carry a TTL of up to 300 s (prepare/replay.rs:28, :55-70). No purge runs on this path. The only purge is in the root-capability guard, at 256 receipts per fresh request (ops/replay/guard.rs:145-147). The receipts sit in the same REPLAY_RECEIPTS map that reserve_root_replay caps globally by len() >= 10,000 and per actor by active_len_for_actor >= 512, counting every command kind (ops/replay/mod.rs:103-116; handler/mod.rs:38-39; storage/stable/replay.rs:239-253). This is distinct from core-auth-4, which is about heap maps.

Recommendation

Give role-attestation prepares the retained-receipt path: reserve_or_replay_receipt_with_retention, with explicit per-actor and per-command-kind limits and purge_expired_for_command_kind, as PrepareDelegatedToken already does. Or add a real cost-guard quota keyed by the calling member. Count only root-capability command kinds against MAX_ROOT_REPLAY_ENTRIES and MAX_ROOT_REPLAY_ENTRIES_PER_CALLER, for example with per-command-kind counters, so other receipt families cannot exhaust root-capability admission. Add a test that a synchronous prepare flood is rejected.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. The root arm only evaluates ActiveComponentMemberPredicate (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:313-329). It then calls ComponentAuthApi::prepare_role_attestation (component_auth/mod.rs:83-88), whose admission only binds subject, role and subnet to the caller (prepare/admission.rs:44-76). The workflow uses plain reserve_or_replay_receipt (prepare/mod.rs:185). That function applies only pending_receipt_quota_decision (ops/replay/receipt.rs:191-199, 222-238, 317-338). record_is_pending counts Reserved only before expiry, plus InFlight and RecoveryRequired (storage/stable/replay.rs:401-409). Reserve, stage and commit all happen in one message with no await (prepare/mod.rs:185-237, 255-277; commit at receipt.rs:429-451), so pending counts from earlier calls stay at 0. The receipt TTL comes from metadata.ttl_ns and is capped at 300 s (prepare/replay.rs:28, 53-68). Nothing enforces the manifest label: grep finds ROOT_CANISTER_SIGNATURE_PREPARE_QUOTA_V1 and RootCanisterSignaturePrepare only in the manifest, in the tests and in a cost-key label (ops/cost_guard.rs:394). The only purges are in the root guard (guard.rs:145-147) and in the retention path (receipt.rs:209). reserve_root_replay counts every command kind: a per-actor active count of 512 and a global len() of 10,000 (ops/replay/mod.rs:98-117; handler/mod.rs:37-39). Both the self-lockout and the fleet-wide ReplayStoreCapacityReached scenarios therefore hold. crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:173

Failure scenario

During a Fleet scale-out, the Coordinator's accept call succeeds, but its follow-up query_root_component_provisioning call gets a transient reject. The next Coordinator tick reconciles and re-sends ProvisionComponents. Root returns the retained receipt and starts a second provisioning chain, and each further transient failure adds another. The parallel chains call advance with the same expected cursors, duplicate Coordinator status calls and record spurious Backoff failures that delay the operation. Each chain also holds an ic-timers registration. With enough replays, defer_lifecycle_required traps (xc-robustness-1), taking down other Root drivers. The same happens for every host resend of an in-progress SynchronizeRegistry.

Evidence

ProvisionComponents is manifested response_idempotent (role_command_manifest.rs:150-153). accept returns the retained status on an exact replay (component_provisioning.rs:87-97). accept_and_schedule nevertheless calls schedule_provisioning on every call (component_provisioning.rs:163-175). schedule_provisioning registers a new defer_lifecycle_required timer each time, with no scheduled-set guard (component_provisioning.rs:190-198). The chain re-arms itself whenever progress changes or a Backoff failure is recorded (component_provisioning.rs:325-376). The Coordinator re-sends ProvisionComponents on its Reconcile disposition, for example when the follow-up status query after a successful accept fails (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:406-420, :1191-1209). SynchronizeRegistry is replay_protected (role_command_manifest.rs:223-229). accept_synchronization returns the receipt for an exact replay but still calls schedule_registry_synchronization (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:100-122). That function also has no deduplication and retries forever, at 1 s on errors and immediately otherwise (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:186-206). By contrast, component allocation deduplicates through SCHEDULED_COMPONENT_ALLOCATIONS (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:10-27).

Recommendation

Deduplicate both schedulers by operation ID, as lifecycle_drivers does: insert into a thread-local scheduled set and remove on terminal completion, or claim through an AsyncJobRecoveryOps owner. Make the replay path return the retained receipt without scheduling when a chain is already live. Add a unit test showing that N exact replays leave exactly one registration.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. On an exact replay, accept returns the retained status (component_provisioning.rs:95-99), and accept_and_schedule then calls schedule_provisioning without any check (163-175). schedule_provisioning registers a fresh defer_lifecycle_required timer with no scheduled-set guard (190-198). By contrast, lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:10-27 deduplicates through SCHEDULED_COMPONENT_ALLOCATIONS. Chains re-arm on progress (344-351) and on Backoff (360-366). They die only when failure_changed is seen, or on completion or ReviewRequired, so duplicates persist through normal progress. The Coordinator re-sends on Reconcile: after an OperationAccepted, a failed status query fails the whole call (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:413-420, 1192-1209; ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:820-825). When a parallel chain's advance hits a conflict before the other chain commits, it records a Backoff failure (352-366). That delays the operation, and the other chain exits at 345-346. accept_synchronization also schedules on an exact replay (fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:100-122). Its chain retries every 1 s until activation (186-205). The host re-sends SynchronizeRegistry routinely: the ActivateRegistryMirror action sends the same command (canic-host/.../current_protocol/mod.rs:1449-1456). Sync chains end once activation is done, so the harm is duplicate pollers while the sync is incomplete, and indefinitely if it is stuck. crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:288

Failure scenario

The Root has begun draining: canister_pool::stop() has run and the funding fence is set. The removal driver then traps after an await, for example on the registry-full trap in its 1 s reschedule, or on instruction exhaustion in the O(N^2) removed-Component validation. Alternatively, the operator performs a same-release Root upgrade mid-removal. The host replays RemoveRoot, the Coordinator forwards it, and the Root returns OperationAccepted but schedules nothing. The Coordinator's loop then polls query_root_removal at 1 s forever. The Root never reaches its final inventory or Store deletion. Root and Store cycles, pool assets pending handoff and the Coordinator's draining reservation, which fences admission, stay held with no command able to resume them.

accept_root_removal (fleet_subnet_root.rs:281-299) takes the `if let Some(existing) = root_draining_if_present(...)` branch on every replay (288-296). That branch validates and returns `Ok(OperationReceipt)` without calling schedule_root_removal. Only the first acceptance calls it (298). schedule_root_removal_after (559-567) is a RemoveWhenStopped Once chain whose only other arms are its own reschedules. The public LifecycleApi::schedule_fleet_subnet_root_removal (api/lifecycle.rs:559-561) is never wired to any endpoint; grep finds no caller outside the file. Root post_upgrade (api/lifecycle.rs:959-989) resumes only canister_pool and component_provisioning. resume_authority_snapshot (api/lifecycle.rs:167-183) resumes only the pool and core owners. The Coordinator's root-removal loop (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:818-883) only queries Root status and publishes what it observes; it never drives Root steps. The RemoveRoot endpoint arm (canic macros endpoints/root.rs:698-701) maps straight to accept. ic-timers keeps a trapped Once registration Running, and defer_lifecycle_required traps when the 64-entry registry is full (api/timer.rs:81-89, registry/mod.rs:728-731). Either event, or a heap wipe from an upgrade, ends the chain for good.

Recommendation

In accept_root_removal's existing-draining branch, call schedule_root_removal after the exact-retry validation, deduplicated by a heap set cleared on terminal completion. On Root post_upgrade and in resume_authority_snapshot, scan for a non-terminal root draining record and re-arm its driver. Add a PocketIC test: upgrade the Root mid-removal, replay RemoveRoot, and assert that removal completes.

Severity adjusted from high to medium during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The core claim holds. accept_root_removal (fleet_subnet_root.rs:288-296) returns a receipt on replay without calling schedule_root_removal. Only first acceptance arms the driver (298), and the chain is kept alive only by self-reschedules (559-567). The RemoveComponent arm is different: it always calls schedule_component_removal after the idempotent begin (canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:690-697). RemoveRoot maps straight to accept (698-701). Root post_upgrade (api/lifecycle.rs:966-988) and bootstrap_post_upgrade_root_canister (bootstrap/root.rs:205-261) re-arm only the pool and provisioning. The changelog entry at docs/changelog/0.110.md:2422 shows restart resumption is an intended property. There is no manual escape. The per-step LifecycleApi functions (finalize/publish/reclaim/delete/prepare, lifecycle.rs:350-430) are not wired to any endpoint, and the Coordinator loop (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:817-883) only observes. Corrections that lower severity. First, the authority-snapshot vector is not real. require_root_resumable, via timer/mod.rs:471-483, rejects any unmanaged lifecycle timer, including a Running one, so no snapshot can be taken mid-removal. Second, host tooling never upgrades a Root; it issues only install or reinstall (fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:2861-2864). Third, the trap triggers are speculative: the 64-entry registry limit is far above Root's roughly 10 claims while provisioning is closed, and the instruction exhaustion was not demonstrated. What remains reachable is an out-of-band same-release Root upgrade by a controller, or a rare trap, and either leaves the removal permanently stranded. The cycles stay Root-controlled, so conservation holds, but the draining fence stays in place. That makes this a medium-severity recovery gap, not high.

A top-level allocation has created its canister and recorded an InstallIntent. The driver's reschedule then traps because 64 ic-timers entries are live, or the commit traps. The operation ID stays in SCHEDULED_COMPONENT_ALLOCATIONS. The host polls the allocation status, sees it non-terminal and replays ProvisionComponent. Each replay returns OperationAccepted and schedules nothing, so the created canister and its cycles stay unowned by any Component until an operator happens to upgrade the Root and replay again. SCHEDULED_COMPONENT_ALLOCATIONS and SCHEDULED_COMPONENT_CHILD_ALLOCATIONS are thread_local sets (lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:10-15). schedule_component_allocation inserts the operation ID and returns early when it is already present (21-26). The driver removes it only on `Ok(true)` (35-39). The child path behaves the same (161-171, 188-192). The insert commits with the command message, after reserve_allocation's awaits (canic endpoints/root.rs:641-661). ic-cdk-executor handles a callback trap by cancelling the task without completing it, and nothing in the driver or in ic-timers removes the set entry on drop. The driver's awaits (root_store::status, install and commit steps) are followed by operations that can trap: the Storable-bound trap after a paid creation from round one, instruction exhaustion, and the registry-full trap in defer_lifecycle_required (api/timer.rs:87-88). Replays reach schedule_component_allocation through reserve_allocation's idempotent existing-record branch (component_registry/mod.rs:714-728). Initial-bootstrap child replays go through component_rpc/lifecycle.rs:106-117. Root post_upgrade never re-arms allocations (api/lifecycle.rs:959-989), so only an upgrade followed by a replay recovers.

Recommendation

Make the dedup entry prove liveness. Store the lifecycle timer identity and treat the entry as stale when ic-timers reports no Scheduled registration for it; the alternative, clearing it from a watchdog that checks for no live registration, is racier. Also re-arm non-terminal allocations and child allocations from Root post_upgrade by scanning ComponentRegistryOps.

Verifier (confirmed): The dedup gap is real. lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:20-26 and 164-171 insert into heap sets, and only the Ok(true) arms (35-39, 188-192) remove entries. No other code touches either set (grep finds only these lines). Replays go through the endpoint at root.rs:634-661 and the idempotent branch at component_registry/mod.rs:714-728, so they return OperationAccepted and arm nothing. Root post_upgrade (api/lifecycle.rs:959-989) resumes only component_provisioning and the pool. Two corrections on the trigger. First, the Suspended trap is not reachable: a seal fails while any lifecycle once exists (timer/mod.rs:471-483, UnmanagedClaim). Second, the realistic trap is ic-timers MAX_TIMER_REGISTRATIONS=64 (registry/mod.rs:24, 728), hit in defer_lifecycle_required (api/timer.rs:87-88). A driver that reschedules still holds its own RemoveWhenStopped entry, so it needs one extra slot. That becomes likely once about 55 allocations or child allocations are non-terminal at the same time. The ic-timers README says Once gets no automatic recovery after a trap, so each trapped driver also leaks a Running slot. That makes further traps more likely, and it blocks require_root_resumable. The parent bootstrap cap of 64 attempts is real (lifecycle/init/nonroot.rs:20). A Root upgrade followed by a replay recovers, so medium, not high.

Each executes as a replicated update, scans the whole Component Registry, and is billed to root: ingress induction, the update base fee and every scan instruction. The sender pays nothing. The same applies to the treasury-holding Coordinator's operation-status query. Registry growth increases the drain per message, and the only bound is the subnet's ingress rate.

The installed hooks route every method other than the command union to inspect_update_message (start.rs:452-455, 461-464, 470-473; root.rs:164-170; fleet_coordinator.rs:29-35; role.rs:562-568; wasm_store.rs:27-38). inspect_update_message looks up a registered limit, falls back to DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES (16 KiB) for unregistered methods, and calls accept_message whenever the payload fits (payload.rs:73-84). It never checks whether the method is an update. Public queries are exported with plain #[ic_cdk::query] (canic-macros expand/mod.rs:290-298), and no code rejects replicated execution: a grep for in_replicated_execution finds no match. Examples of public queries whose cost grows with state and that run before or without caller authorization: root canic_root_operation_status (root.rs:1020-1053), which scans every Component's child allocations for an operation id (child_allocation/mod.rs:49-58, cf. xc-efficiency-4); Coordinator canic_coordinator_operation_status, which for a non-controller calls FleetCoordinatorOps::current() and re-derives the history (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:217-225, cf. cp-fleet-coordinator-6); and _immutableObjectStorageBlobsToDelete (blob_storage.rs:23-29). Round-one findings covered command variants only.

Recommendation

In the shared inspect hook, accept only methods that are real update endpoints: an allowlist built from the registered update limits plus the command methods, generated by the endpoint macros. Reject everything else, which covers query and composite-query names. Alternatively, have canic_query wrappers reject replicated execution with a typed error before any state access. Either way, fix the O(N) public lookups already reported.

That function falls back to the 16 KiB default and calls accept_message without checking whether the method is an update (canic-core/src/ingress/payload.rs:73-84). Query wrappers carry a plain cdk::query attribute (canic-macros expand/mod.rs:290-298). `advance_root_store_removal` rebuilds the request on every driver iteration through `root_deletion_preparation_request`. That function takes a fresh canister_status of self and copies idle_cycles_burned_per_day, reserved_cycles and freezing_threshold, plus a target derived from them (fleet_subnet_root.rs:696-699, 713-738).

When an intent already exists, `retry_is_exact` requires those fresh values to equal the ones recorded on the first attempt; otherwise it returns conflict (968-988).

The first attempt normally cannot finish: Root needs the Coordinator's readiness_intent (1007-1011). The Coordinator records that only after it observes Root's deletion_readiness_intent in its own driver (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:861-872). A retry is therefore the normal path.

idle_cycles_burned_per_day follows memory usage. Between attempts, Root writes the preparation intent, the ledger-transfer intent, logs and metrics. A single new 64 KiB heap or stable page changes the reading, and every later attempt then conflicts. The driver retries every 1 s forever (559-566). Separately, a nonzero reserved_cycles is rejected outright (1426), which can permanently block deletion on subnets using storage reservation.

Once the intent exists, resume from its persisted observations and skip the live canister_status comparison (keep only the operation ID and store_deletion_hash for identity). Once the intent exists, prepare_deletion requires idle_cycles_burned_per_day, reserved_cycles, freezing_threshold and the derived target to equal the first attempt's values, and returns conflict otherwise (968-988). A retry is effectively guaranteed. After record_root_deletion_cycle_reclamation, Root immediately asks the Coordinator for `readiness` (1030-1035), which the Coordinator can record only after it polls Root (fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:874-883), so that attempt returns unavailable and the driver loops (559-566). The prepare endpoint API (api/lifecycle.rs:423) is not wired to any endpoint, so no operator path can supply the persisted observations. Root is created with memory_allocation None, so idle burn tracks live memory and message-memory usage. A mismatch then produces an unbounded conflict loop. Corrections: - Drift is probabilistic, not systematic. The PocketIC autonomous-removal journey (canic-testing-internal/.../baseline.rs:14680-14880) finishes through several retries, including a lost ledger reply. - Stable growth under MemoryManager is bucket-sized, not per 64 KiB page. - The zero-reserved-cycles rejection (1426) is a documented fail-closed design choice (0.100-design.md:2853-2856), not a bug. The wedge is realistic on mainnet (heap high-water growth, concurrent message memory), so medium is correct.

Serialize reset per asset with a durable reset-attempt token checked after every await, or route all resets through the maintenance lease. That fence is one of fixture/mod.rs:45, mod.rs:674, 686 or 627. crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/execution.rs:303

Failure scenario

The root's automatic refill transfers 2 ICP to the CMC. The CMC is then unreachable or returns Other (for example while its ledger fetch is degraded) for about 5 minutes, and each 1-minute retry uses up an attempt. The fifth attempt ends the operation as Failed/NotifyMaxAttempts. The root's top-up timer stops, the root receives no cycles, and the 2 ICP stay unconverted at the CMC until someone runs notify_top_up by hand before the CMC rejects the block as TransactionTooOld.

Evidence

notify_operation increments notify_attempts before every CMC call (execution.rs:302-303; ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:1250-1256), including calls that fail at transport level (execution.rs:318-325). A Processing or Other reply when attempts >= MAX_NOTIFY_ATTEMPTS (5, icp_refill/mod.rs:40) sets NotifyMaxAttempts (execution.rs:426-450). That state is not resumable (domain/icp_refill.rs:59-81), so advance_operation returns it as final (execution.rs:262-266). The Root timer then stops as an invariant failure (runtime/cycles/mod.rs:433-442), with a fixed 1-minute retry between resumable attempts (mod.rs:417-431). At this point the ledger block is recorded and the ICP sits in the CMC top-up subaccount; only an out-of-band notify_top_up can credit it. Separately, mark_transfer_window_stale releases the budget (budget_reserved=false, ops/storage/icp_refill.rs:1343-1356) even after a transfer attempt whose outcome was unknown (Err path at execution.rs:216-223), because the record does not track that an attempt was made.

Recommendation

Because notify_top_up is idempotent, keep retrying with backoff until a definite outcome (Completed, Refunded, InvalidTransaction, TransactionTooOld). Count only definite CMC replies, not transport failures, toward any cap. If a cap stays, make NotifyMaxAttempts resumable by an operator command. For a stale window after an uncertain transfer, check ledger evidence before releasing the budget or classifying the transfer as never applied.

Verifier (confirmed): Confirmed. mark_notify_attempt_started commits the increment before the await (execution.rs:302-303; storage icp_refill.rs:1250-1256), so a transport failure (execution.rs:318-325) uses up an attempt. With the post-increment count at 5 or more, a Processing or Other reply becomes NotifyMaxAttempts (execution.rs:411-451). That state is non-resumable (domain/icp_refill.rs:59-81), and advance_operation returns it as final (execution.rs:262-266), including for manual retries under the same operation_id. finish_automatic_refill then stops the Root top-up timer as an invariant failure (runtime/cycles/mod.rs:430-439). Resumable replies retry after a fixed RETRY_INITIAL of 1 minute (mod.rs:64, 414-428). Transport errors back off (mod.rs:582-592). The archived 0.58 design explicitly says to keep this cap independent of timer-driven self-refill (docs/design/archive/0.58-convert-icp/0.58-design.md:274-279), yet the automatic path uses the same capped notify_operation. A realistic trigger is roughly 5 minutes of FailedToFetchBlock or reject replies during an NNS ledger or CMC upgrade. Impact: a root at its emergency threshold loses automatic funding, and the ICP sits at the CMC subaccount with no in-product retry. The ICP is not destroyed, because anyone can call notify_top_up out of band for the recorded block, so medium rather than high. The secondary budget-release claim (storage icp_refill.rs:1344-1356) is technically true but weak. Transfers use unbounded_wait (infra icp_refill.rs:344), so an Err almost always means the transfer was not applied, and within 24h a retry deduplicates.

Every sharding assign exports and linearly scans all partition-key assignments across all pools, so onboarding costs O(N^2) and assign traps once a few million keys exist
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/placement/sharding/assignment.rs:106

Failure scenario

Take a user_hub pool of 64 shards x 50,000 capacity, with one partition key per user as in apps/test/user_hub/src/lib.rs:30-32. At 1M assigned users, each create_account decodes about 1M keys plus BTree traversal and String allocation (about 10-20k instructions each), roughly 10-20B instructions per call. Between about 2M and 4M assignments every assign exceeds the 40B update limit and traps, so onboarding halts for everyone, including already-assigned users who hit the same path. Onboarding N users costs O(N^2) instructions in total. partition_keys for one 50k-key shard returns about 3.5 MB, which exceeds the reply limit.

Evidence

assign_with_policy (assignment.rs:60-218) always calls ShardingRegistryOps::assignments_for_pool(pool) at :106 (and again in plan_assign_to_pool at :250). ShardingRegistry::assignments_for_pool (crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/sharding/registry.rs:98-105) calls export_assignments() (:131-136), which collects ShardingCore::all_assignments (storage/stable/sharding/mod.rs:245-253): a full decode into a Vec of every (ShardKey, Principal) entry in every pool. ShardKey is CBOR with field-name map keys, up to 192 bytes (sharding/mod.rs:52-71). assignment.rs:107-113 then clones every key again into views. ShardingPolicy::plan_assign finds an existing assignment with a linear find (domain/policy/pure/placement/sharding/mod.rs:87-95,107). All of this runs even for keys that are already assigned. The O(log n) lookup ShardingRegistry::partition_key_shard (registry.rs:70-74) exists but is unused on this path, and the storage comment at registry.rs:113-115 itself says assignments are unbounded. ShardPoolPolicy has no upper bound on capacity or max_shards (config/schema/component_spec/mod.rs:835-849). ShardingApi::partition_keys (registry.rs:77-84, api/placement/sharding/mod.rs:40-43) also scans all assignments and returns every key in one unpaginated reply.

Recommendation

First look up the key with partition_key_shard and return early if it is assigned. Plan new assignments from the ShardEntryRecord rows only: counts are already maintained by assign/release, and HRW selection needs only entries. Never materialize assignments. If per-pool iteration is ever needed, use a fixed-width, non-CBOR key encoding with a pool-prefix range. Paginate partition_keys.

The result is a full decode and clone of every (ShardKey, Principal) row across ALL pools, and the pool filter is applied only afterwards. The keys are serde-serialized through impl_storable_bounded (cdk/mod.rs:31-47). The views are cloned again (assignment.rs:107-113), and ShardingPolicy::lookup_partition_key does a linear find (domain/policy/pure/placement/sharding/mod.rs:87-95, 107). None of this is skipped for keys that are already assigned. The O(log n) ShardingRegistry::partition_key_shard (registry.rs:71-74) exists but this path does not use it. Config validation bounds max_shards only by the spawn grant (config/validation/component_spec.rs:367-385), and capacity is an unbounded u32 (config/schema/component_spec/mod.rs:835-839). Correction: the query plan_assign_to_pool has the 5B limit, so it fails roughly 8x earlier than assign does. partition_keys_in_shard (registry.rs:78-85) is also an unpaginated full scan. An early-return lookup must still respect the routable_active filter (assignment.rs:108). Medium fits the rubric's category of hot-path cost that grows with the fleet and risks the instruction limit.

The inspect_message hooks never check the caller, so controller- and canister-only command methods accept megabyte ingress from anyone, and the treasury-holding Coordinator, root and store pay the induction cost
crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:29

Failure scenario

An anonymous sender repeatedly submits roughly 2 MB `canic_coordinator_command(ProvisionComponents(..))` messages that decode. inspect_message accepts them, and the Coordinator pays about 2K cycles per byte plus the cost of decoding a 2 MB plan before `is_controller` rejects each one (fleet_coordinator.rs:98-101). At the subnet ingress byte limit this drains tens of trillions of cycles per day from the Fleet treasury and crowds out legitimate root funding traffic. Root and the store can be drained the same way.

Evidence

`__canic_inspect_fleet_coordinator_update_message` accepts any ingress that decodes as a `CoordinatorCommand` within the size limit of its variant, and `ProvisionComponents` is allowed up to MAX_FLEET_COMPONENT_PROVISIONING_PLAN_CANONICAL_BYTES = 8 MiB (fleet_coordinator.rs:12-26, 29-54; crates/canic-core/src/ops/component_provisioning_plan/mod.rs:49). Every Coordinator variant is either controller-only or authorized for root canisters (fleet_coordinator.rs:75-102), so the only legitimate ingress senders are controllers. Root's hook works the same way and admits `ProvisionComponents` up to 8 MiB + 64 KiB (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:164-187). All of root's non-controller variants are called only by canisters (coordinator or components), which never pass through inspect_message. The store forwards publish-chunk ingress to `inspect_update_message`, which checks size only (wasm_store.rs:27-38; crates/canic-core/src/ingress/payload.rs:73-84), with a limit of about 1.06 MiB (crates/canic-core/src/lib.rs:83-85), although the only legitimate ingress sender is the installation controller (crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/template/mod.rs:53-60). On the IC, accepted ingress is inducted at the receiving canister's expense (per-message plus per-byte fee); ingress rejected in inspect_message is not charged.

Recommendation

Make inspect_message caller-aware on the specialized roles. For `canic_root_command`, `canic_coordinator_command` and the store publish/command methods, accept ingress only when `is_controller(msg_caller())`; for the store, the retained installation controller. All legitimate non-controller callers of these methods are canisters, which bypass inspect_message. Keep the size checks for controllers. Add a test that anonymous ingress to these methods is rejected at inspect.

Verifier (confirmed): The Coordinator hook accepts any decodable `CoordinatorCommand` up to 8 MiB with no caller check (endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:29-54). Every variant is either controller-only or root-authorized, and those checks run only in the update (fleet_coordinator.rs:73-102). Root does the same up to about 8 MiB + 64 KiB (endpoints/root.rs:164-187). Root's non-controller variants are sent by canisters. The store's publish_chunk and publish_fixture go through `inspect_update_message` (wasm_store.rs:29-34; ingress/payload.rs:73-84) with a limit of about 1.06 MiB (canic-core/src/lib.rs:83-85), yet only root or the installation controller may call them (canic-control-plane/src/api/template/mod.rs:53-60). The IC ingress limit is 2 MiB, so 8 MiB is unreachable. Still, each accepted anonymous message costs the receiver an induction fee of about 1.2M + 2K cycles per byte, roughly 4B cycles at 2 MiB, plus the decode during execution. Messages rejected at inspect are not charged. Caveats: (a) The base 16 KiB exposure exists on every public update anywhere on the IC. At subnet saturation the large messages amplify it only about 6x. (b) The maintainer has recorded this as deferred. See docs/design/ideas/inspect-message-admission/design.md:5-8 and 27-29, which list exactly this caller/method filter. This is a known but real bounded cycle-drain DoS on treasury-holding roles, so medium stands.

Positional backup references are re-resolved on every mutating restore call, so `restore run <N> --execute` can run a different prepared restore after the list shifts.
crates/canic-cli/src/backup/reference/resolve.rs:40

Failure scenario

1. The operator prepares backups X (#1) and W (#2) to compare readiness, intending to restore W. 2. A teammate or cron job runs `canic backup create prod`, even a dry run or one that fails preflight. A new layout appears as #1, so X becomes #2. 3. The operator runs `canic restore run 2 --execute`. It resolves to X, whose journal passes the backup-root check. Result: X's snapshots are loaded onto the production targets instead of W's, a wrong-state restore.

resolve_backup_reference_in (resolve.rs:31-50) treats an all-digit reference as an index into the current output of backup_list. That list is sorted newest-first by created_at (reference/list.rs:26-31) and includes DryRun, Running, Failed and invalid entries (entry.rs:14-24). Plan-only entries take created_at from the run_id stamp (entry.rs:62-67), so any new create attempt immediately becomes #1. This includes one that fails at preflight, because persist_backup_create_layout writes the plan and journal before the runner starts (backup/create/mod.rs:76, create/persistence.rs:34-36). `restore run` and `restore status` resolve the reference again on each call (restore/io.rs:86-96, 120-134). verify_prepared_journal_backup_root only checks that the journal found in the resolved directory names that same directory (io.rs:98-110, 150-172). Nothing binds the call to the backup_id the operator prepared. The help text promotes numeric references for mutation: `canic restore run 1 --execute --max-steps 1` (restore/mod.rs:19-23, restore/options.rs:23-27).

Recommendation

For prepare, run --execute and run --retry-failed, reject numeric references or require an exact BACKUP_ID or path. Alternatively, store the prepared backup_id in the restore journal and require a matching `--backup-id` before any mutation. At minimum, print and confirm the resolved backup_id before executing.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is as described. resolve.rs:40-49 indexes the live backup_list, which sorts newest-first (list.rs:26-31). Plan-only layouts are listed too (entry.rs:19-20, 51-76), and backup_create persists the plan before the runner starts (create/mod.rs:76). Every non-dry-run create currently fails at the stubbed preflight (executor/mod.rs:45-53) but still leaves a layout, so any attempt shifts the row numbers. restore_runner_config resolves the ref again on each call (restore/mod.rs:224-228, io.rs:120-134). verify_prepared_journal_backup_root only checks that the journal sits in the directory the ref resolves to right now (io.rs:98-110, 150-172). Nothing binds the call to a backup_id. I downgrade it to low for three reasons. Numeric row references are documented, intended UX (changelog 0.34.md:306-312; 0.110.md:2999-3000 says restore and backup share the displayed row ordering), and the help text shows them (options.rs:23-27). The scenario needs an operator error: reusing a stale index across separate invocations while two backups are already prepared, so X had already been deliberately prepared for restore. And the current release cannot produce restorable manifests: the only production writer is execute_finalize_manifest (artifacts.rs:439), which sits behind the stubbed preflight, so restore needs externally supplied layouts. It is still a real footgun for a destructive command. Binding --execute to an exact BACKUP_ID, or echoing the resolved backup_id, is a cheap hardening.

crates/canic-backup/src/artifacts/secure.rs:96

Failure scenario

1. On macOS, the operator runs `canic backup create prod --out /tmp/prod-bk` (or `--out ./bk`). 2. Stop, CreateSnapshot, Start and DownloadSnapshot all succeed. 3. VerifyArtifact fails with Io(ENOTDIR), or UnsupportedEntry for `./`, on every retry. Result: the layout can never complete, after paid snapshot effects have already run. The path is latent while the CLI preflight is stubbed.

checksum_path splits an absolute path into root "/" plus its components, and a relative path into "." plus its components (secure.rs:92-114). open_relative rejects any non-Normal component (secure.rs:144-150) and opens every intermediate component with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY (secure.rs:161-172). The runner calls ArtifactChecksum::from_path(root.join("<id>.tmp")) for VerifyArtifact and for reconciliation (runner/operations/artifacts.rs:217, 364). As a result:
- `--out ./backups/x` fails (CurDir component).
- `--out ../x` fails (ParentDir component).
- An absolute path through a symlink fails. On macOS /tmp, /var and /etc are symlinks and $TMPDIR is /var/folders/...; a read-only openat(fd('/'), 'var', O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) on this host returns ENOTDIR.

ensure_expected_temp_path binds the journaled temp path to the exact spelling of the root (runner/operations/path.rs:21-36), so a resume cannot use a normalized path. Unit tests such as artifacts/tests/mod.rs:39-56 hash under std::env::temp_dir() and cannot pass on macOS. CI runs only on ubuntu-24.04 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:23).

Recommendation

Hash the temp tree with ArtifactChecksum::from_relative_path_no_follow(layout.root(), "<id>.tmp"). This opens the root the way verify_durable_artifact does and keeps no-follow inside the artifact tree. Alternatively, canonicalize the layout root once at run start. Add a CI job or test with a symlinked ancestor and a `./` root.

Verifier (confirmed): The defect is real, but the shipped CLI can't reach it today. secure.rs:96-103 splits an absolute path into "/" plus its components. open_relative (secure.rs:144-150) rejects any component that isn't Normal. A read-only probe on this Mac confirms openat(fd('/'), 'var'/'tmp', O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) returns ENOTDIR. A resume with a normalized spelling therefore gets ArtifactTempPathMismatch. By contrast, verify_durable_artifact uses from_relative_path_no_follow(layout.root(), ...) (integrity/artifacts.rs:100), which only no-follows inside the tree. Tests using temp_path() (test_support.rs:229-230, under $TMPDIR=/var/folders) cannot pass on macOS. CI runs only on ubuntu-24.04. It becomes medium once preflight is implemented.

VerifyArtifact records a checksum of whatever tree exists after the download, with no check of content or size, so an empty or truncated download becomes a Durable, verified backup.
crates/canic-backup/src/runner/operations/artifacts.rs:364

The `icp` download exits 0 but writes nothing or only part of the snapshot into the expected directory, for example because of the working-directory mismatch in finding 3, or a partial write that still exits successfully. The backup reaches Complete, verify passes, and prune may later remove older good backups. The problem is discovered only when restore upload or load fails.

prepare_download_temp_directory creates an empty temp directory before the command runs (artifacts.rs:273-296). require_download_temp_directory only checks that it is still a non-symlink directory (299-325). execute_verify_artifact hashes the tree and stores that hash as the expected checksum while advancing to ChecksumVerified (340-369). There is no independent expectation. snapshot_total_size_bytes is journaled (journal/types.rs:64-65; artifacts.rs:112) but never compared with the downloaded bytes. The checksum of an empty directory is simply the sha256 of an empty listing (artifacts/mod.rs:114-128). Finalize then publishes it and `backup verify` re-derives the same hash.

Recommendation

Before ChecksumVerified, require a non-empty tree containing the expected snapshot files, for example the icp metadata file. Compare the total regular-file bytes with snapshot_total_size_bytes when it is known, and fail closed otherwise.

Neither expires_at nor the topology hash is re-validated on resume.

Recommendation

Persist expires_at (and the topology hash) in the execution journal. On resume past expiry, re-run preflight before the next mutating operation, or reject the resume. If the TTL is not meant to gate anything, remove the fields.

B's delayed write then replaces A's execution journal with a fresh one that has no receipts, and B fails on the lock. 4. If A crashes before its next journal write, the durable receipts for its completed paid effects are gone.

Evidence

persist_backup_create_layout checks `backup_plan_path().is_file()`. If the file is absent, it writes the plan and a fresh execution journal with write_json_durable, which replaces existing files, and holds no lock (create/persistence.rs:18-42). The JournalLock is first acquired later, inside backup_run_execute_with_terminal_writer (runner/mod.rs:62-63). Default output directories use per-second stamps (create/plan.rs:68-74), so two creates of the same fleet in the same second share a directory.

Recommendation

Acquire the JournalLock in persist_backup_create_layout and hold it across the runner call, which means passing it in. Use create-only semantics (create_json_durable) for the initial plan and journal.

The newest backup's artifact directory is damaged or partially removed, but its manifest and journal remain, so it still lists as Complete. `canic backup prune --keep 1` deletes the only intact older backup and keeps the corrupt one. Separately, if removal fails partway through, the operator gets an error with no record of which backups were already deleted.

backup_prune keeps the newest `--keep` entries with status Complete (prune.rs:14-19). Complete means only that a manifest file exists and every execution operation is completed or skipped (backup/labels.rs:8-26, reference/entry.rs:78-96). BackupLayout::verify_integrity, which runs the checksum checks, is never called for the retained set. The deletion loop uses `?` (prune.rs:33-35), so an error on the k-th entry returns without a report even though entries 1 to k-1 are already gone.

Recommendation

Verify the integrity of the backups that would be retained. Refuse to prune when fewer than `keep` verified backups would remain, or count only verified ones. Collect per-entry outcomes and always emit the report, including partial failures.

lowunverifiedbackup-persistence-10 · performance · high confidence
read_json deserializes directly from an unbuffered File, costing one read syscall per byte on journals the runner re-reads several times per target.
crates/canic-backup/src/persistence/json.rs:42

Failure scenario

For a fleet of about 1000 targets the download journal is roughly 0.5 MB. About 5 reads per target gives about 5,000 reads of a 0.5 MB file, around 2.5×10^9 single-byte read syscalls. That is minutes of host CPU, growing quadratically with fleet size.

Evidence

read_json opens the file and calls serde_json::from_reader(file) (json.rs:37-43). serde_json's IoRead reads byte by byte and documents that callers must add their own buffering for a File. The runner re-reads the whole download journal several times for each target: snapshot receipt lookup and persistence, download, reconcile, verify and finalize (runner/operations/artifacts.rs:66, 104, 155, 173, 202, 346, 391). `backup list` reads the plan, execution journal and manifest of every directory, several times per entry (reference/entry.rs:26-96).

Recommendation

Use `serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(path)?)` or wrap the file in a BufReader.

Apply the resolver's rule, Normal components only (a single segment for runner-produced layouts), in SourceSnapshot::validate and in journal validation. Drop CurDir from the journal validator.

Newly created layout directories are never fsynced into their parent, so the backup root's own directory entry is not durable.
crates/canic-backup/src/persistence/json.rs:55

Failure scenario

After Stop and CreateSnapshot receipts are durably written inside a new backup directory, a power loss on a filesystem without ordered metadata journaling (or a weaker network or FUSE filesystem) loses the `deployment-…` entry itself. The journals recording stopped canisters and created snapshots disappear, and the next run cannot reconcile them.

create_bytes_at_barriers and replace_bytes_at_barriers call fs::create_dir_all(parent) (json.rs:55, 94) and then fsync only the immediate parent after the rename (json.rs:74, 113). When the layout root is first created, fsync each newly created directory's parent: create the root explicitly, then open and fsync its parent.

lowconfirmedbackup-restore-7 · liveness · medium confidence
The restore runner has no authority preflight, failure containment or abort path, so a failed stop or a permanently failing load leaves members already stopped down, with no journalled way to finish or roll back.
crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/execute.rs:119

Failure scenario

Stopping member 4 hangs in Stopping because of outstanding call contexts, or the load for member 4 fails permanently (for example the partial-upload case). Root and members 0-3 are already stopped, and 0-3 may already hold restored state. The journal offers only retry-failed. The operator has to start canisters by hand outside the journal, after which the journal no longer matches reality (a later load fails its stopped precondition). The fleet stays down or mixed until someone intervenes by hand.

Evidence

On a failed step the runner records the failure and returns (execute.rs:119-137). Later runs refuse to proceed while any op is Failed (status.rs:63-72), and retry only re-arms that same op (preview.rs:41-57). Ops advance strictly in sequence (journal/mod.rs:372-393), and phases stop every member, root first, before any load (apply/mod.rs:82-99). So no StartCanister row can run until every load completes. The backup runner has explicit containment that restarts stopped canisters (runner/mod.rs:317-466); restore has no equivalent and no abort command. Nothing observes controllers before mutation either: RestorePlanMember has no authority data and the runner never reads status settings.

Recommendation

Add a journalled containment or abort mode. During the stop phase it restarts every member this journal stopped. After loads have begun, it either restarts all members as a recorded partial-restore state or completes the remaining loads. Also add a pre-mutation preflight of every target's status and controllers before the first stop.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): Partly right; consequences overstated. (1) There is effectively an authority preflight. apply/mod.rs:75-86 uploads a snapshot to every target before the first stop, and `icp canister snapshot upload` (journal/commands/mod.rs:151-173) is a controller-only management call, so a controller gap fails before any availability effect. (2) In the stop-phase scenario, members 0-3 cannot hold restored state: every StopCanister precedes every LoadSnapshot (apply/mod.rs:81-92). A failed stop is journalled and retry-failed re-arms it (preview.rs:41-57), and a canister stuck in Stopping clears once its call contexts close. (3) For failures after a load, the design forbids what the recommendation proposes. 0.94-design.md:691-705 says that after the first committed load, automatic restart or rollback is forbidden and recovery completes the remaining loads, and :707 accepts permanent load failure as fail-closed. The real remaining gap: the design allows a journalled abort before the first load (:694-696, 'may be restarted ... may abort incomplete'), and the backup runner implements containment (runner/mod.rs:317-466), but restore has none (grep finds no abort or containment in restore/). An operator who abandons a restore during the stop phase has to start root and the stopped members by hand, and a later load then fails its stopped precondition (commands/mod.rs:189). That is a recoverable operator inconvenience, so low.

The restore takes hours of local IO and CPU, which lengthens the window in which the fleet is stopped.

Evidence

RESTORE_RUN_OUTPUT_RECEIPT_LIMIT is 64 KiB per stream, so each receipt can carry about 128 KiB of stdout and stderr (constants.rs:38; receipts/mod.rs:288-296). validate() runs on every transition and receipt (journal/mod.rs:124-180, 222-233, 339-369) and calls validate_against for each receipt, which scans all operations linearly (receipts/mod.rs:155-161), giving O(ops x receipts) work. Recommendation

Index operations by sequence (for example a Vec indexed by sequence) inside validate_against. Cap each receipt's output much lower or store it in per-attempt sidecar files referenced by hash. Validate only the changed operation and receipt on each transition.

`run_topup` calls `icp.canister_top_up_output(&target.canister_id, options.amount_cycles)` straight after resolving the target (wallet.rs:400-411). `canister_top_up_output` runs `icp canister top-up --amount N <canister>` with no deduplication or journal (canic-host icp/canister.rs:231-243). If the `icp` process fails after the Cycles Ledger withdraw commits, for example on a network timeout, the command reports an error even though the effect happened.

Recommendation

Record a pending top-up intent (target, amount, created_at) before the effect and show it on rerun. Alternatively, observe the target balance and the operator ledger balance before and after, and ask for confirmation when a matching recent intent exists. Document that `topup` is not idempotent.

lowunverifiedcli-ops-8 · security · medium confidence
The convert status read that decides whether the journal record is completed is an uncertified `--query` issued right after the update
crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/convert/mod.rs:108

Failure scenario

A refill leaves operation X in the Transferred state because the CMC notify is pending. The status query is answered by a faulty replica that reports Completed, and the CLI marks the pending record completed. The operator believes the refill is done. The ICP sent to the CMC stays unnotified until someone notices `resume_required` in `canic cycles funding`.

Evidence

After the RefillCycles update, `run_options` calls `canister_query_arg_output_with_candid(... CANIC_ROOT_OPERATION_STATUS ...)`, which adds `--query` (canic-host icp/canister.rs:164-189, 193-203). Recommendation

Read operation status with a replicated call (omit `--query`, or use a certified read) whenever the result updates the local journal. Treat 'operation not found' right after an accepted command as retryable rather than rejected.

The Not arm of eval_access_inner returns Ok(()) for any non-terminal failure of its operand (expr/mod.rs:400-404). It does not distinguish a genuine denial from a dependency failure.

Custom predicates return AccessError, which includes the Internal variant (expr/mod.rs:170; access/mod.rs:64-65). env predicates return BuildNetworkUnavailable when the build network is unknown (access/env.rs:49-57).

- In the Not arm, invert only explicit denials. - Treat AccessError::Internal and the *Unavailable variants as terminal, and propagate them.

- LifecycleApi authorize_* helpers.

Route inline checks through a helper that builds an AccessContext and calls eval_access(&caller::is_controller(), ..) or record_access_failure, so each inline denial emits exactly one metric, as eval_access does.

Root does not re-install either: its renewal state still records the old install, so the template is not due until refresh_after (selection.rs:46-63). Include the Missing status (SECURITY_UNAVAILABLE from active_delegation_proof_unavailable_error) in delegated_token_prepare_error_allows_lazy_repair, or change the contract to say that provisioning after a reinstall is required.

lowconfirmedcore-blob-storage-5 · correctness · high confidence
Content-addressed roots have no reference counting, and the documented product flow queues shared content for gateway deletion when one referencing asset is deleted.
crates/canic-core/src/ops/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:114

Failure scenario

Users A and B upload the same PDF, which yields a single root H; B's create_certificate returns Ok as AlreadyLive. A deletes their asset and the backend calls mark_pending_delete(H) as documented. B's asset now fails require_live. The gateway lists H, deletes the bytes and confirms, so B's content is permanently lost. B's attempt to re-upload in the meantime is rejected with STATE_CONFLICT.

Evidence

A second `register_live` of the same root returns `AlreadyLive` and records nothing extra (lifecycle.rs:77-91). `create_certificate` throws that outcome away (api/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:39-40). `mark_pending_delete` queues the root for deletion whenever it is live (lifecycle.rs:114-130). Once pending, the root is no longer live (lifecycle.rs:97-100), and re-registration is refused with BlobPendingDeletion (lifecycle.rs:81-83). Roots are content hashes (model/blob_storage/hash.rs), so identical files share one root. The integration guide's Product Flow says "When deleting the product asset, call mark_pending_delete" and never mentions shared references (docs/operations/blob-storage-integration.md, Product Flow step 4).

Recommendation

Add per-root reference counts: registration increments, a release API decrements, and deletion is queued only at zero. At minimum, expose the inserted versus already-live outcome from the certificate path and document that products must count references before calling mark_pending_delete.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The facts hold. register_live returns AlreadyLive for a root that is already stored and records no second reference (crates/canic-core/src/ops/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:76-91). mark_pending_delete queues any stored root (114-130), which makes it non-live (94-111). Re-registration is then refused until the gateway confirms (81-83, 133-136). create_certificate drops the outcome (crates/canic-core/src/api/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:39-40). The integration guide's Product Flow says to call mark_pending_delete when deleting the asset, with no warning about shared roots (docs/operations/blob-storage-integration.md:155). The missing reference counting is intended, though. The 0.69 design copies the Toko reference semantics: one canonical live record per root (docs/design/archive/0.69-blob-storage/0.69-design.md:388) and "marks the same root hash pending deletion when remote assets are deleted" (0.69-design.md:431-436; docs/contracts/BLOB_STORAGE_INVENTORY.md:711-736). Consumer ownership helpers are an explicit non-goal (0.69-design.md:74-81). The 0.111 extraction design moves tenant references and reference release to a future service (docs/design/0.111-standalone-blob-service-extraction/0.111-design.md:75, 104-107). Consumers already store the root on their own records, so they can count references before deleting. The defect that remains is the unqualified guide instruction, which can lose user content if a product follows it literally. That is a documentation and API-usability hazard. It is not a lifecycle correctness bug that breaks a Canic invariant, so I downgrade it to low. Fix: warn in the guide that shared roots must be reference-counted by the product. Optionally, return the inserted-versus-already-live outcome to backend callers.

`transferable_cycles = project_cycles_available.saturating_sub(project_cycles_reserve)`, and `requested_cycles` is attached whenever it is at most that amount (policy mod.rs:136-142). Recommendation

Pass the estimated call cost (method and argument bytes) plus a fixed callback-reservation margin into the policy, and compare against available minus reserve minus overhead.

Gateway confirmation deletes a root that is live but not pending, so a gateway retry arriving after re-registration drops live state (ABA).
crates/canic-core/src/ops/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:135

Failure scenario

H is pending. The gateway confirms H but loses the reply on its side. A user re-uploads the same content: create_certificate registers H as live and the bytes are re-stored. The gateway then retries its confirm and H's live row is removed. `_immutableObjectStorageBlobsAreLive(H)` now returns false, the gateway can garbage-collect the re-uploaded bytes, and the product record points at missing content.

`confirm_deleted_by_gateway` removes the pending row and then the stored row unconditionally, with no pending check and no generation check (lifecycle.rs:133-136). It is called for every well-formed root in a registered gateway's batch (api/blob_storage/gateway.rs:24-37). `register_live` re-inserts a root after confirmation (lifecycle.rs:77-91). The inventory records the same live-but-not-pending deletion in Toko (BLOB_STORAGE_INVENTORY.md:499-501), so the behaviour is contract-conformant but not idempotent across re-registration.

Recommendation

Treat confirmation of a root with no pending row as a no-op, or bind confirmation to the pending record's marked_at generation. Record the decision in the inventory, because it deviates from the Toko source.

crates/canic-core/src/ops/fixture_importer/mod.rs:187

The application's apply_chunk rejects chunk 7 with Application { code: 12 } because of a schema mismatch in the release. `require_callback` traps on any Err from begin, apply_chunk or validate_step (ops/fixture_importer/mod.rs:140-165, 181-189). The `Application` arm of permanent_failure (mod.rs:241) is reachable only from the read-only progress callback. This behaviour is documented in docs/features/build-and-evidence/fixture-artifacts.md ("A trapped callback retains uncertain work for watchdog recovery").

In the claim message, persist a consecutive-trap counter keyed by next_chunk. After N traps at the same position, record a FixtureImportFailure and stop. Expose the attempt count in FixtureProvisioningStatus::Pending.

`create_certificate` validates the hash and calls `register_live` with no caller argument, no per-caller count and no global limit (api/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:36-46; ops/blob_storage/lifecycle.rs:77-91). lowconfirmedcore-config-2 · security · high confidence
auth.role_attestation.min_accepted_epoch_by_role keys are free strings checked only for emptiness, so a mistyped or non-canonical role silently disables the configured revocation floor
crates/canic-core/src/config/validation/auth.rs:290

Failure scenario

After rotating role attestations, an operator sets `[auth.role_attestation.min_accepted_epoch_by_role] "user-hub" = 7` intending to reject user_hub attestations with epoch < 7. The build succeeds. Every verifier keeps accepting epoch 1-6 attestations for role user_hub, for example a leaked pre-rotation attestation, until they expire naturally.

Evidence

The schema types the map as BTreeMap<String, u64> (config/schema/mod.rs:625-626). RoleAttestationConfig::validate only rejects keys that are empty after trim (validation/auth.rs:290-297). It never calls validate_canister_role_name and never checks that the key names a declared role. The renderer copies the raw strings into the runtime authority (bootstrap/render.rs render_role_attestation_config).

At runtime the lookup is exact, `.min_accepted_epoch_by_role.get(attestation.payload.role.as_str())` (workflow/runtime/auth/mod.rs:272-275). resolve_min_accepted_epoch falls back to 0 when nothing matches (:319-325).

So keys such as "UserHub", "user-hub", " user_hub", or a role that is not declared at all, all pass build validation and never match any attestation. CONFIG.md:142 presents the field as the per-role floor for rejecting older attestations, which is a revocation control.

Recommendation

Deserialize the map as BTreeMap<CanisterRole, u64>. Validate each key with validate_canister_role_name and require it to be a declared role or an implicit infrastructure role, rejecting anything else with a typed ConfigSchemaError that names the offending key.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The defect is real, but it needs operator error and its impact is bounded, so I downgraded it from medium to low. The schema types the map as BTreeMap<String, u64> (config/schema/mod.rs:625-626). RoleAttestationConfig::validate only rejects keys that are empty after trim (validation/auth.rs:290-297). No code runs validate_canister_role_name (schema/role.rs:43, lowercase snake_case) on these keys or checks them against declared roles. render_role_attestation_config copies the raw strings (bootstrap/render.rs:1019-1023). At runtime the lookup is an exact .get(attestation.payload.role.as_str()) (workflow/runtime/auth/mod.rs:272-275). resolve_min_accepted_epoch then falls back to 0 unless the caller passes an explicit floor (:319-325). So a key like "user-hub" or "UserHub" silently never matches, and CONFIG.md:142 presents this field as the revocation floor. Why low: - The operator has to mistype the key. - An explicit endpoint min_accepted_epoch still wins over the config value. - Issuance caps attestation lifetime at auth.role_attestation.max_ttl_secs (prepare/admission.rs:29-35; default 900 s). A leaked pre-rotation attestation therefore stays usable for minutes, not indefinitely. The fix is still cheap and worth doing: type the keys as CanisterRole and require each one to be a declared or implicit role.

- RootConfigOps::validate_protected_component_deployment (ops/config/mod.rs:121-128) calls ConfigModel::validate_protected_component_deployment. That compiles the full deployment configuration digest (component_deployment_configuration.rs:216-218) and then compiles the deployment topology again (:223-226).
- Along that path, ComponentGroupTopology::canonical_bytes flattens every group each time it runs (component_group/mod.rs:157-160), and it runs several times inside compile, validate and digest.

Compute ComponentTopology, ComponentDeploymentConfiguration and its digest once in Config::init_from_model and store them in InstalledConfig. Have RootConfigOps return Arc or references, and validate protected contexts against the cached projections.

crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/auth/mod.rs:153

An App configures `allowed_scopes = ["admin", "my_app:read"]` for sessions on role `project_hub`. Its issuer policy grants `project_hub/admin` for a privileged issuance flow, and a privileged endpoint on that role is guarded by `delegated_token(scope = "admin")`. Any principal can then call PrepareDelegatedToken with the grant {project_hub, [admin]}. The prepare policy accepts it as a declared application scope, and the resulting token passes the admin guard.

`public_delegated_token_prepare_scope` (auth/mod.rs:142-160) lets any caller self-issue `session`, `verify`, and any scope that parses as an ApplicationScope and appears in the target role's `local_application_authorization.allowed_scopes`. The ApplicationScope grammar (model/auth/application_authorization/scope.rs:209-241) accepts bare single-segment names such as `admin`, `read` and `write`, the same strings as Canic's capability constants (ids/capability.rs:7-11). Config validation (config/validation/component_spec.rs:145-156) checks only grammar, ordering and uniqueness; it has no reserved-name or namespace requirement. The endpoint delegated-token guard matches any required scope string against the token's grants (access/auth/token.rs:46-54), so a self-issued application-scope token satisfies a `delegated_token(scope = X)` guard whenever X is also a declared application scope. Separate the namespaces. Require application scopes to be namespaced (at least one ':' segment) or reject reserved capability names (read, write, verify, session, admin) in `ApplicationScope::parse` and config validation.
