lowconfirmedcore-intent-replay-2 · correctness · medium confidence
Replay receipts expire TTL after reservation regardless of commit time, and expired Committed receipts are purged, so a same-operation retry after purge is treated as Fresh and re-executed
crates/canic-core/src/ops/replay/guard.rs:110

Failure scenario

1. A child claims a CycleTopup attempt at time T and requests cycles with op X. Root reserves at T+2 s (expires T+302 s), transfers, and commits. 2. The child's callback traps, or its call is delayed past the lease, so the result is never recorded. 3. The watchdog takes over at about T+300 s to T+330 s with the same op X. 4. If the receipt is still present, the takeover gets `ReplayExpired` (EVIDENCE_EXPIRED, not retryable) and top-up stops instead of receiving the cached response. 5. If any other fresh root request has purged it in the meantime, root treats X as Fresh and transfers again while the child's balance is still below threshold. The same applies to any caller retrying `create_canister(operation_id)` or `recycle_canister(operation_id)` more than 300 s after the first attempt.

Evidence

- **Expiry is set once:** `evaluate_root_replay` sets `expires_at_ns = now_ns + ttl_ns` at reservation (guard.rs:110-121). Commit never changes it (`commit_staged_receipt_response`, receipt.rs:429-451). The root TTL cap is 300 s (handler/mod.rs:40) and `operation_request_metadata` always sends 300 s (ops/rpc/request/dispatch.rs:27, 332-337).
- **Expired means rejected:** once past expiry, a non-placement Committed receipt is classified `Expired` (receipt.rs:548-556), even if it was committed after its expiry.
- **Expired means purgeable:** on every Fresh decision, `purge_expired` deletes such receipts (guard.rs:145-147; storage/stable/replay.rs:345-363). Only in-flight, recovery or unacknowledged placement receipts survive.
- **No memory after purge:** a missing slot is Fresh (receipt.rs:245-270). There is no issued-at bound or tombstone, so the retry re-executes.
- **Retry timing:** cycle top-up reuses its operation generation on takeover (async_job_recovery/mod.rs:320-331), but takeover only happens after the 5-minute lease (workflow/runtime/async_job/mod.rs:15, 49-58), which is typically past the 300 s receipt TTL.

Recommendation

Make receipt retention cover the caller's retry horizon. - Keep Committed receipts (or a compact tombstone with the response digest) until at least commit time + the maximum TTL, and never purge a receipt whose `updated_at_ns + max_ttl` is in the future. - Or bind admission to caller-supplied issued-at metadata and reject stale IDs instead of treating them as Fresh. - Also align the async-job lease with the replay TTL so takeover still finds the cached response.

Severity adjusted from high to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The replay-layer mechanism is real. Expiry is set once at reservation (guard.rs:110-121), and commit never extends it (receipt.rs:429-451). An expired non-placement Committed receipt is classified Expired (receipt.rs:548-556) and purged on any later Fresh decision (guard.rs:145-147; stable/replay.rs:345-363). The sender re-stamps issued_at_ns on every send (ops/rpc/mod.rs:219-229), so nothing ties a retry to the original operation's time. The harm is overstated, though: - **create/recycle claim is wrong:** root re-execution is idempotent in the domain layer. Component Registry child allocations are keyed by operation_id, retained, and returned when they already exist (control-plane workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1111-1123; lifecycle.rs:94-104). Recycle resumes through existing_subtree_removal (lifecycle.rs:152-167). - **RequestCycles re-execution is harmless in practice:** calls are unbounded-wait (ops/rpc/mod.rs:117), so a committed reply is lost only if the child's callback traps or the reply is delayed past the lease. On takeover, run_topup re-samples the balance and requests only if balance <= threshold (cycles/mod.rs:274-310; policy/pure/cycles.rs:41). A Fresh re-execution is fully re-authorized under the funding policy, and the cycles stay in a controlled child. No conservation violation. - **Residual defect:** if the receipt is still present, takeover gets EVIDENCE_EXPIRED (rpc/mod.rs:107). That code is non-retryable (cycles/mod.rs:966-970), so automatic top-up stops. The 5-minute lease equals the 300 s TTL, and the watchdog runs every 30 s. Rare trigger with small impact, so severity is low.
Also reported as: core-rpc-ic-8
lowconfirmedcore-intent-replay-4 · robustness · high confidence
Terminal local intent records are never deleted, so the intent record map grows without bound; the cost guard adds two permanent records per costed operation
crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:1991

Failure scenario

A busy root processes many cycles grants, provisions and refills per day. Each leaves two permanent `IntentRecord`s. An application calling `LocalIntentApi::begin` per user action adds one record per action. Over a release's lifetime these maps grow monotonically, raising stable-memory cost and any full-map export or validation cost, with no operator-visible bound or cleanup.

Evidence

- **Insert only:** `IntentStore` exposes `insert_record` and has no remove (storage/stable/intent.rs:703-705).
- **Terminal records re-inserted:** `commit_at`, `abort` and `settle_pair_at` write the Committed/Aborted record back to the primary map via `remove_pending_and_apply` (mod.rs:1991-2001) and settle_pair_at's update loop (mod.rs:865-868). Only the pending and expiry indexes are cleaned.
- **Cleanup only aborts:** the cleanup timer aborts expired pending intents but never deletes terminal primaries (workflow/runtime/intent.rs:412-470).
- **Growth rate:** `CostGuardOps::reserve` allocates two fresh IntentIds and records per costed operation (ops/cost_guard.rs:195-222), and `LocalIntentWorkflow::begin` one per application reservation. None of these are ever reclaimed within a release.

By contrast, receipt-backed application rows have an explicit reclamation index.

Recommendation

Delete the primary record when an intent reaches a terminal state, or retain terminal records only for a bounded window with an ordered reclamation index like application receipts. Callers such as `observe_transfer_reservation` already treat a missing or terminal record as zero outstanding, so deletion or a tombstone suffices. Add a capacity metric for the record map.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The growth claim holds. `IntentStore` has `insert_record` but no remove for INTENT_RECORDS (storage/stable/intent.rs:699-705). Only `import_records` and `reset_for_tests`, under cfg(test), touch it otherwise (intent.rs:990-1096). `remove_pending_and_apply` re-inserts the terminal record (ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:1986-1996). The cleanup timer only aborts due pending intents (workflow/runtime/intent.rs:414-446). `CostGuardOps::reserve` allocates two records per costed operation (ops/cost_guard.rs:195-222), and the public `LocalIntentApi::begin` adds one per call (api/intent/mod.rs:29-31). Severity is overstated, though. The claimed full-map export or validation cost does not exist in production: `export_records` is cfg(test) only, and production code accesses records only by key (O(log n) StableBTreeMap). Each record is at most 229 bytes (intent.rs:285), so the only impact is slow stable-memory growth and the matching storage-fee cycles. That growth resets at every pre-1.0 reinstall boundary. There is no functional failure, and no instruction limit is at risk. A tombstone or bounded retention would still be good hygiene, especially for application use of LocalIntentApi.

At about 1.2 mints per second, terminal rows alone (at least 15 minutes each) exceed 1,000. 3. `begin_placement_or_load` then returns StoreCapacityReached, so the hub can no longer allocate shards or scale children until application traffic subsides. Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The behaviour is real, but it is largely the documented design. `create_receipt` compares the total `ReceiptBackedIntentStore::len()` against the limit (ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:1557-1569). `begin_placement_or_load` passes the same RECEIPT_BACKED_INTENT_RECORD_LIMIT that application admission uses (mod.rs:911-926). A shared ceiling was an explicit choice: 0.96-design.md:103 says a new operation is rejected once "the shared primary receipt map contains 1_000 rows", and 0.96 status.md:210 counts "application and Canic-owned rows against the shared primary ceiling". Neither document, nor the active adapter guide (docs/operations/receipt-backed-intent-adapter.md), discusses application traffic starving placement, so a gap remains. Reasons to downgrade: exact retained retries stay readable at capacity (0.96-design.md:100-101), so in-flight placements continue. Application admission is throttled too, so this acts as backpressure. Terminal application rows are reclaimed once eligible (model/intent/mod.rs:28-43), at most about 60 minutes of replay window plus the 15-minute grace. The "permanent" case needs the application to leak its own unsettled pending rows. That is a consumer bug that also wedges the consumer's own admission. Scope: this affects only canisters that host both a busy receipt adapter and placement. It is a bounded, recoverable liveness trade-off.
lowunverifiedcore-intent-replay-7 · correctness · medium confidence
Local intent begin and cost-guard reserve return an error after reservations are already committed, leaking unaddressable pending reservations
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/intent.rs:134

Failure scenario

The timer registry rejects scheduling during a transient custody conflict. A cost-guarded request returns Err, but its quota slot and cycle reservation stay pending for up to one hour. The caller retries and immediately hits QuotaExceeded or CycleReserveRejected. For application local intents, the caller cannot commit or roll back the reservation it never learned about.

Evidence

`LocalIntentWorkflow::begin` persists the reservation via `try_reserve` (intent.rs:112-127), then calls `IntentCleanupWorkflow::schedule_intent(intent_id)?` (intent.rs:134). If scheduling fails, the error returns to the caller without the IntentId. Scheduling can fail through `require_active` (TimersSuspended), `register_once` or custody errors (intent.rs:492-517; timer/mod.rs:400-420).

`CostGuardWorkflow::reserve` does the same with two intents (workflow/cost_guard/mod.rs:18-26). The persisted pending quota and cycle reservations still count toward `enforce_quota` and `enforce_cycle_reserve` (ops/cost_guard.rs:316-349).

No trap follows, so IC does not roll back the reservation. It lingers until TTL, and cleanup was not armed for it; it is only rearmed at the next successful reconcile or lifecycle start.

Recommendation

Schedule before mutating, or trap (or roll back the reservation) when scheduling fails after `try_reserve`, so the message is atomic. Alternatively return the IntentId together with a non-fatal scheduling warning and rely on lifecycle reconstruction.

Init enforces `binding.role == compiled_role && canister_id == self` (workflow/env/mod.rs:70-74, 92-96), but post-upgrade has no equivalent check. `init_role_runtime_authority` compares compiled against compiled (bootstrap/mod.rs:104). `require_release_build` (fleet_activation/mod.rs:210-222) compares a ReleaseBuildId that is embedded identically into every Wasm of a release (ids/release_build.rs:44-47). `restore_nonroot_after_upgrade` (workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:372-380) validates the stored deployment against the stored binding. For GroupMember it checks only component_spec/spec_hash (config/runtime.rs:436-444), and for ComponentChild it checks the owning Component, never the child's role. The fleet-admission restore checks only that the stored binding is self (fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:216-231). So a same-release wrong-role Wasm passes and the role is rewritten. Severity is lower than claimed: only a controller can trigger this, by hand, because Canic host tooling never performs upgrades (no Upgrade install path in canic-host/core). Controllers can already install arbitrary code. Re-upgrading with the correct Wasm fixes the recorded role. It is a missing defensive fence that is inconsistent with the init-time check, not a reachable authority weakness.

It then calls `BootstrapStatusOps::mark_failed(...)` even for retryable errors. Nothing reschedules the post-upgrade bootstrap. Readiness is load-bearing: root's `require_component_runtime_ready` (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:4275-4302) requires `ReadinessStatus::Ready`. docs/features/runtime/README.md:77 requires activation and readiness to expose an explicit retry path. Alternatively keep retrying with a capped backoff rather than terminating. Give the wasm_store ActivateFleet replay the same unconditional `schedule_init_nonroot_bootstrap()` that managed ConfigureRuntime has.

If it awaits indefinitely, `$after` never runs either. For managed post_upgrade this means `bootstrap_post_upgrade_nonroot_canister` (PlacementAcknowledgementWorkflow::start, initial shards/workers, `ReadyOps::mark_ready`) is never scheduled. lowunverifiedcore-lifecycle-memory-11 · performance · high confidence
The sequence allocator for cycle top-up events scans the entire event map on every insert.
crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/cycles.rs:459

Failure scenario

A long retention window holds tens of thousands of top-up events. Every new event write pays a linear key scan, which inflates the instruction cost of the automatic top-up path on every canister that runs it.

`CycleTopupEvents::next_sequence` (cycles.rs:459-466) runs `self.map.iter().filter(|entry| entry.key().timestamp_secs == timestamp_secs).map(|e| e.key().sequence).max()` over the whole B-tree. Keys are ordered `(timestamp_secs, sequence)` big-endian (lines 240-270), so the answer is the last key in the range `(ts,0)..=(ts,u32::MAX)`. `record` calls it on every event (lines 373-394): scheduled, ok and err events for every automatic top-up. Retention purges only in bounded batches (purge_inner, lines 434-457), so the map can hold the full retention window.

Recommendation

Use `self.map.range(CycleTopupEventKey::new(ts, 0)..=CycleTopupEventKey::new(ts, u32::MAX)).next_back()` to find the last sequence in O(log n).

lowunverifiedcore-placement-fleet-7 · correctness · medium confidence

crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/placement/sharding.rs:255

Only the UseExisting plan checks count < capacity (domain/policy/pure/placement/sharding/mod.rs:114-122, 165-167). After the await, re-check count < capacity on the target shard. If it is full, re-plan (take the UseExisting or next CreateAllowed path) or return a retryable capacity error.

lowunverifiedcore-placement-fleet-9 · robustness · medium confidence
A late concurrent completion of the same placement operation returns an invariant error once the first caller's terminal record has been acknowledged and removed
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/placement/allocation.rs:194

Failure scenario

Two assign_to_pool requests for different keys both trigger creation at the same slot. The first completes and is acknowledged. The second's root reply (cached, same pid) arrives later, settle returns NotFound, and the caller gets an invariant error with its key unassigned. A retry works, but the invariant-class error and metric are misleading.

Evidence

Concurrent callers deliberately share one operation (next_sequence, allocation.rs:84-91). The first caller settles and schedules the acknowledgement drain, which removes the terminal record after root acknowledges (acknowledgement.rs:222). A slower caller holding the same permit then gets NotFound from settle_canic_owned_if_pending, which settle_allocation maps to InternalError::invariant (allocation.rs:189-196). In sharding this happens after the shard is registered but before the caller's key is assigned (sharding/allocation.rs:88-97 returns Err, so assignment.rs:198 never runs). In scaling it happens after the worker is registered (scaling/mod.rs:270-274).

Recommendation

Treat NotFound as success when the domain registry already holds the same child under the same identity, or keep terminal evidence until no permit could still be outstanding. Return a retryable error instead of an invariant error.

lowunverifiedcore-rpc-ic-7 · robustness · medium confidence
The public Call builder records per-(target, method) metrics in a heap HashMap with no size bound, at construction time
crates/canic-core/src/ops/ic/call.rs:43

An application canister uses Call to reach user-supplied canisters or methods, for example a token canister chosen by the user. CallOps::bounded_wait and CallOps::unbounded_wait call InterCanisterCallMetrics::record_call(canister_id, method) as soon as the builder is created, before anything executes (ops/ic/call.rs:41-60). record_call inserts a key built from the target Principal and method.to_string() into a thread-local HashMap with no cap or eviction (ops/runtime/metrics/inter_canister_call.rs:13-19, 56-66, 72-77), and snapshot() clones the whole map (lines 81-88). lowunverifiedcore-rpc-ic-9 · performance · medium confidence

If one mid-tree canister is slow, for example because its subnet is congested, propagation to all later siblings stalls.

Evidence

fanout awaits send_snapshot for each child in turn (state.rs:141-163). Each non-root recipient applies the snapshot and then runs the same sequential fanout over its own children before replying (state.rs:73-98). The response is the aggregated subtree report (ops/cascade.rs:291-322), sent through RpcOps::call_rpc_result, which always uses unbounded wait (ops/rpc/mod.rs:118-121). One slow or stuck subtree therefore delays every later sibling indefinitely, and root keeps an outstanding call open for the whole traversal. Fleet state, including the cycles_funding_enabled kill switch that parents read locally (nonroot_cycles.rs:328), reaches the last canisters only after about one round trip per canister in the fleet.

Recommendation

Fan out to children concurrently with a bounded concurrency limit (for example join_all over chunks), or have children acknowledge before recursing and report asynchronously. Consider a per-hop deadline so one slow subtree cannot hold back its siblings.

lowunverifiedcore-runtime-metrics-4 · correctness · high confidence
Endpoint and checkpoint instruction accounting uses canister-global PERF_STACK and PERF_LAST across interleaved call contexts, misattributing instruction totals in protected and public performance metrics
crates/canic-core/src/perf.rs:161

Failure scenario

1. Async update A enters with a frame start of 40k, then awaits a call. 2. Update B enters with a start of 45k (at least A's start, so it is pushed), then awaits. 3. A resumes and exits at 2.0M on its own counter. It pops B's frame and records 1.955M, and 1.955M is added to A's frame as child time. 4. B resumes and exits at 300k. It pops A's frame: total 260k minus 1.955M child time saturates to 0, so B's endpoint is recorded with 0 instructions. 5. Checkpoints spanning awaits likewise take deltas against another message's counter.

Evidence

`enter_endpoint_at` and `exit_endpoint_at` push and pop one thread-local `PERF_STACK` shared by all messages (perf.rs:23-27, 161-196). Frame starts are `performance_counter(1)` values, which are per call context (perf.rs:55-59), yet they are compared and subtracted across contexts. The trap heuristic `start < last.start` clears other in-flight frames (166-170). `exit` pops whatever frame is on top and charges its total to the frame below as child time (187-194). The `perf!` macro computes `now - PERF_LAST`, where `PERF_LAST` is a global last set by whichever message ran last (crates/canic-core/src/lib.rs:120-134). Production checkpoints span awaits, for example `delegated_token_fetch_root_proof` after an unbounded call (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/auth/prepare/mod.rs:352-358). The first checkpoint of each message is measured against the previous message's counter. These rows are published as `perf.endpoint.*` and `perf.checkpoint.*` counters in the public `performance` family (public_metrics/mod.rs:409-456, 275-289) and in protected Runtime metrics.

Recommendation

Make accounting per call context. For endpoints, capture `start = perf_counter()` in a local in the generated wrapper and record `end - start` at exit. Exclusive nesting cannot be meaningful across async interleaving, so drop it for async endpoints or scope it to synchronous nesting. For `perf!`, reset `PERF_LAST` at endpoint and timer entry, and document that checkpoints spanning awaits are unreliable, or carry the checkpoint base in a local. Consider bounding PERF_TABLE cardinality for dynamic `perf!` labels.

lowunverifiedcore-runtime-metrics-5 · performance · high confidence
Paged observability and public reads materialize whole stable collections before paging (logs, cycle history, public children), and the 1,000-entry log page can exceed the reply limit
crates/canic-core/src/ops/runtime/log.rs:118

Failure scenario

1. A canister holds 10,000 log entries, some with multi-KiB Debug-formatted messages. 2. A controller requests `Logs` with the default 1,000-entry page. 3. The query decodes the whole log, then fails with an oversized reply. Through the Root relay it fails at the 2 MiB response bound, which is confusing because the operator must guess a smaller page size. 4. On a hub with thousands of children, every anonymous Children query decodes the full child set.

Evidence

`page_filtered` iterates `Log::snapshot()`, which decodes every stored entry into a Vec (`self.entries.iter().map(|e| e.value()).collect()`, crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/log.rs:157-159, 203-205), before filtering and paging (ops/runtime/log.rs:107-131). Defaults allow 10,000 entries of up to 16 KiB each (config/schema/log.rs:13-19), and the page limit is 1,000 (ops/runtime/log.rs:18, 135-137). A full page of large entries is about 16 MiB, beyond the query reply limit and beyond the Root relay's inter-canister response limit. `CycleTrackerQuery::page` and `topups` also load all entries (`entries(0, usize::MAX)`) before `paginate_vec` (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/cycles/query.rs:18-25; ops/storage/cycles.rs:69-71, 214-216). The anonymous `canic_public_status(Children)` path decodes every child record for each query (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/topology/children/query.rs:28-32; ops/storage/children/mod.rs:47-57).

Recommendation

Iterate the stable BTreeMap lazily (`iter().rev()`), skipping `offset` matching entries and stopping after `limit`. Also cap cumulative response bytes, for example at 1.5 MiB, and return a continuation marker. Apply the same range-iterator paging to the cycle tracker, top-up events and children instead of `paginate_vec` over a full Vec.

lowunverifiedcore-runtime-metrics-6 · performance · medium confidence
Every `log!` call performs several full-record stable decodes plus timer reconciliation, including in queries where the work is discarded
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/log.rs:76

Failure scenario

1. A busy Root at log capacity, with `max_age_secs` set and multi-KiB messages, handles a burst of funding requests and denials. 2. Each log line performs three full CBOR decodes of up to 16 KiB plus a timer reconcile, adding hundreds of thousands of instructions per logged line to hot update paths. 3. Query endpoints that log on access denial pay the same cost for no durable effect.

Evidence

`log!` runs `__append_runtime_log`, then `append_runtime_log` (crates/canic-core/src/log.rs:124-152), then `LogStore::append`. `append` calls `last_key_value()`, which decodes the whole newest entry just to compare `created_at` (storage/stable/log.rs:92-100). At capacity it calls `first_key_value()`, decoding the whole oldest entry to obtain its key, then removes and inserts (112-121). `reconcile` then calls `next_deadline_ns` → `oldest_created_at`, which decodes the oldest entry again (workflow/runtime/log.rs:161-168; storage/stable/log.rs:161-165), followed by `ensure_declared`, `require_active` and `reconcile_schedule` (76-89). Entries may be 16 KiB. Logging sits on hot paths: every access denial, every RequestCycles authorization (rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:252-289) and root-capability envelope errors. The append also runs in query contexts, where the stable write and timer reconciliation are rolled back but still cost instructions.

Recommendation

Store `created_at` in the key, for example `(created_at, sequence)`, or keep heap-cached `last_created_at` and `oldest_created_at` that are rebuilt on restore. Use `first_key_value` only when capacity is reached. Skip `reconcile` when the oldest timestamp is unchanged. Skip persistence when not in replicated update or timer execution, for example with `ic_cdk::api::in_replicated_execution()` plus a query-context check.

lowunverifiedcore-runtime-metrics-7 · robustness · high confidence
`log.max_age_secs` is not validated, so a very large value makes the retention deadline overflow and fails runtime start or traps managed-canister activation

Failure scenario

1. An operator sets `[log] max_age_secs = 99999999999` intending 'effectively forever'. 2. The build validates successfully. 3. On a managed non-root the first activation runs `start_all`. The log already contains init lines, so `next_deadline_ns` overflows and returns an invariant error. 4. `activate_nonroot` traps with 'could not establish runtime services', and Fleet activation cannot complete. The opaque invariant code gives no hint that the log configuration is the cause.

`LogConfig::validate` checks only `max_entries` (config/schema/log.rs:56-66). `max_age_secs: Option<u64>` is unbounded (41-42). `next_deadline_ns` computes `age_expiry_at(created_at, max_age)` and then `seconds_to_nanos`, both with checked arithmetic that returns `InternalError::invariant` on overflow (workflow/runtime/log.rs:161-175). Values above about 1.66e10 seconds overflow nanoseconds. `LogRetentionWorkflow::start()` propagates this error. `RuntimeWorkflow::start_all` calls it first among the runtime services (workflow/runtime/mod.rs:57-63), and init and post-upgrade paths propagate with `?` (workflow/runtime/nonroot.rs:190, 259). `activate_nonroot` traps when `start_all` fails (workflow/runtime/fleet_activation.rs:272-278). When the log is empty the error is swallowed at append time, so age retention silently never arms.

Recommendation

In `LogConfig::validate`, reject `max_age_secs` values whose `(u64::MAX / 1e9) - now` margin cannot hold, for example with a documented cap of 100 years. Alternatively, saturate the deadline to 'no deadline' instead of failing runtime start.

1. A short burst of transient series names briefly exceeds the 256-series cap, for example many pending lifecycle timers sampled during a busy upgrade window. 2. staging_status_response reads and SHA-256-hashes every chunk to build stored_chunk_hashes (chunked.rs:145-150), then reads and hashes every chunk again, concatenates the full payload and hashes that too (158-179). The host polls this through the canic_wasm_store_catalog query (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/wasm_store.rs:354-356).

Compute the chunk hashes once and reuse them for completeness. Verify the payload hash incrementally with a streaming Sha256 instead of concatenating. Reject preparations whose payload_size_bytes exceeds chunk_count x CANIC_WASM_CHUNK_BYTES or the Store limit, or cap the capacity hint.

So a re-entry on an active root with a complete receipt leaves Overview.bootstrap.ready=false (api/ready.rs:34-36; root.rs:864). PrepareFleetActivation then returns unavailable, because the phase is not ACTIVATION_PREPARED (root.rs:103-107; fleet_activation/mod.rs:24-26). That contradicts its `response_idempotent` manifest row (replay_policy/role_command_manifest.rs:113). Corrections: (1) The Active early return is not dead. When Active is committed but the receipt is incomplete (for example, `mark_root_runtime_activated` failed after the awaits in resume_root), complete_or_wait sets ACTIVATION_PREPARED (root.rs:130-138) and prepare_root finishes the receipt. (2) Reachability is narrow. canic-host and canic-cli never issue Prepare/ResumeFleetActivation (grep finds nothing). The root-internal driver calls them only while the observed phase is Prepared (component_provisioning.rs:694-722). Only a manual controller command reaches this path. (3) The impact is diagnostic only. Functional gates use `ReadyOps::is_ready`, which stays true; readiness is misreported by `canic list live` and the observatory until the next upgrade. (4) Metrics are recorded again, not reset.

Because the label contains the shard id, PERF_TABLE also grows by one row per distinct shard for as long as the canister runs.

The facade prelude exports core `perf!` (crates/canic/src/prelude/mod.rs:12 -> api/mod.rs:111). It records `PerfKey::Checkpoint { scope: module_path!(), label: format!(..) }` into the heap `PERF_TABLE` BTreeMap with no size cap (canic-core/src/perf.rs:23,124-129,141-149), so a label that includes an id creates a new row on every call. `bounded_entries` returns `InternalError::invalid_input()` if any of the first `limit` keys has a scope or label longer than 128 bytes (perf.rs:220-244). `performance_metrics()` also calls `metric_name(&row.labels, 6)`, which requires the joined `perf.checkpoint.<scope>.<label>` to fit in 128 bytes (public_metrics/mod.rs:341-349,409-421); that leaves roughly 105 bytes for scope plus label. The error propagates with `?` and fails the whole Performance family (public_metrics/mod.rs:265-268). lowconfirmedhost-canister-build-3 · performance · high confidence
Configured-role finalization spawns one unbounded thread per role, each running ic-wasm and multi-threaded wasm-opt -Oz, so memory and CPU use grow linearly with fleet size.
crates/canic-host/src/canister_build/artifact.rs:425

Failure scenario

Consider a release build of an App with 30 deployable roles on a 16 GB, 8-core CI runner. After the runtime batch, 30 concurrent wasm-opt -Oz processes start, each needing hundreds of MB to over 1 GB and each spawning 8 threads, next to 30 walrus parses and gzip-best passes. The runner thrashes, or the OOM killer terminates wasm-opt or canic. The release build fails only once the fleet has grown past the machine's headroom.

Evidence

`build_workspace_canister_artifacts_from_specs_with_toolchain` calls `scope.spawn` once for every spec (artifact.rs:421-439) with no limit. Candid extraction, by contrast, is bounded to MAX_EXTRACTORS = 4 (candid_cache/mod.rs:26, 50). Each finalizer runs `ic-wasm shrink` (a full walrus parse), `ic-wasm metadata`, `wasm-opt --print-features` twice and `wasm-opt -Oz` once (artifact_io/mod.rs:75-99, 465, 471, 586). It also performs three in-process `Compression::best()` gzip passes (466, 596, 103). Binaryen parallelizes each process across all cores by default. The Coordinator and Store finalizers may still be running concurrently (artifact.rs:163-182). The build doc limits infrastructure finalizers to two workers but sets no bound for configured roles.

Recommendation

Run finalization through a bounded worker pool, for example min(available_parallelism, 4) or chunks like `extract_configured_candids`. Consider setting BINARYEN_CORES per child so the process count and thread count do not multiply.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is real. artifact.rs:419-439 calls `scope.spawn` once per spec with no bound, while Candid extraction chunks by MAX_EXTRACTORS = 4 (candid_cache/mod.rs:26, 50). Each finalizer runs ic-wasm shrink and metadata, and for Release also `--print-features` plus `wasm-opt -Oz` (artifact_io/mod.rs:74-98, 454-471, 529, 613) and gzip-best passes (376). There is no BINARYEN_CORES or worker knob anywhere in canic-host or canic-cli, and the CLI caller (canic-cli/src/build.rs:560) passes all roles at once. The impact is overstated, so I downgrade it to low. Cost scales with the number of distinct deployable roles, not fleet or canister count. The repo's apps have 2-9 roles (apps/test/canic.toml has 9), so 30 concurrent Release finalizers is atypical. The -Oz pass runs only for the Release profile (artifact_io/mod.rs:429-433). The Coordinator and Store finalizers start before the configured Cargo batches (artifact.rs:159-182), so they have usually finished before configured finalization begins. The failure is host-side, operator-scoped and recoverable (a bigger runner or fewer roles), with no effect on canister state or cycles. Bounding the pool is still a sensible fix.

It runs many domain owners with `?`, for example wasm_store_adoption_operation_status, which calls validated_root_authority()? (canic-control-plane workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:155-165), and FleetActivationWorkflow::status()? (workflow/root_status/mod.rs:111). Only the final select_unique_match maps an empty result to unavailable (root_status/mod.rs:233-236). Recommendation

Use the typed single-owner status that already exists (a component-allocation status endpoint analogous to component_child_provisioning_status) whose only unavailable case is 'not found'. Alternatively, return a distinct transient error when record.progress is Some and the status is unavailable.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is real, but the example scenario is wrong and the finding overstates how often this can happen. archive/mod.rs:26 fixes the budget at 256 MiB. Snapshot::retain (186-203) charges every estate file plus each referenced content object, and failure returns an opaque InvalidTerminalSource (221). capture cannot be skipped: retirement/mod.rs:76-77 calls it, and clean reinstall reaches that through prepare_bootstrap (workflow/clean_reinstall/mod.rs:96). There is no typed size error. Correction: "60 roles at 5 MB" on one App cannot converge. Every wasm store is hard-capped at 40,000,000 bytes across templates, chunks and fixtures (canic-control-plane/src/schema.rs:1, config.rs:32-39, ops/storage/template/chunked.rs:328-343). The host also rejects a root projection whose unique artifact plus fixture bytes exceed maximum_wasm_store_bytes (release_set/application/mod.rs:525-559). Objects are deduplicated by digest (archive/mod.rs:157-160), so a single root, or several roots with overlapping specs, stays near 38 MiB, far below the cap. Going over 256 MiB takes 7 or more roots with nearly disjoint, near-capacity projections. The step bound (per_root counts the full union, times roots, must be at most 4096; continuation/mod.rs:75-107) caps that at about 10 roots. So the case is reachable in a narrow window. When it happens it blocks the normal reinstall with no supported workaround, but the fleet shape is unusual. Low severity. Deriving the cap from roots times the store limit, plus a typed error, would fix it.

Decode the reply with the method's return type and compare IDLValues or typed values rather than bytes. Use a replicated (update) status read for the completion predicate. Require {{operation_id}} or {{operation_id_blob}} in command templates, or make command idempotency a validated contract.

The only test covers `local` and `ic` (replica_query/tests.rs:6-11). Reachability is narrow, though. Only two places use it: `canic list` readiness (canic-cli/src/list/live/mod.rs:47, 170-196, where failures become `ReadyStatus::Error`) and the `canic status` replica row (canic-cli/src/status/mod.rs:185-204). `query_canister_ready` has no caller in fleet ensure or in any other mutation path. lowunverifiedhost-icp-network-4 · performance · high confidence
Every authenticated query and every management status call builds a new Agent, re-exporting and decrypting the private key and spawning 2–4 `icp` subprocesses, which adds roughly a second per call and multiplies copies of the key in memory.
crates/canic-host/src/icp/management.rs:163

Failure scenario

On a Fleet with several hundred pool assets, or many component members, planning makes hundreds of authenticated queries. Each spawns about three `icp` processes and decrypts an encrypted PEM through the password file or session, adding minutes of wall time. The key is decoded and held in memory hundreds of times.

Evidence

`query_candid_readonly` calls `build_authenticated_agent` on every call (icp/query/mod.rs:126-133), and so does `management_canister_status_candid` (management.rs:101). `build_authenticated_agent` runs `icp network status --environment <env> --json` unless a direct local target is set (186-200), `icp identity default` when the identity is unbound (identity.rs:20-35), `icp identity export <name>` (206-211) and `icp identity principal` (218). It then builds a fresh Agent, which must fetch subnet keys again to verify query signatures. `QueryTransport` caches only the HTTP client and runtime (query/mod.rs:52-58). Callers loop: Root pool paging (fleet_ensure/ops/current_inventory/mod.rs:1418-1430), per-member partition checks (1083-1098), and per-canister direct-local status (platform.rs:1821). fleet-ensure.md:378-380 documents re-resolving per query as intended. The retained attribution report shows about 0.43–0.48 s per identity lookup.

Recommendation

Cache the exported identity and the network status in the `IcpCli` context. Keep the per-query authority check cheap: compare the cached identity's `sender()` with the bound Principal, and compare the cached root key with the enrolled canonical network, without re-exporting. Or reuse one Agent per context and rebuild it only when the bound identity or environment changes.

lowunverifiedhost-icp-network-5 · robustness · medium confidence
The durability path on Apple platforms syncs the parent directory with plain `fsync`, which does not flush the device write cache, so a published rename can be lost on power failure even though the call succeeded.
crates/canic-host/src/durable_io/mod.rs:477

Failure scenario

On a macOS operator laptop, the journal of an intent-before-effect step is published and the directory fsync returns. The paid effect runs, then power is lost before the drive cache flushes. After reboot the directory entry has reverted to the previous journal, so the effect is not recorded as intended. Reconciliation then relies on external observation, or the effect repeats.

Evidence

The temp file's data is synced with `temp_file.sync_all()` (durable_io/mod.rs:449), which on macOS std maps to `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)`. The parent-directory syncs that make the rename and created directories durable use `rustix::fs::fsync` (477, 590, 598), and on Apple platforms plain fsync does not flush the drive cache. rustix 1.1.5 in Cargo.lock provides `rustix::fs::fcntl_fullfsync` (fs/fcntl_apple.rs:24). Callers treat a successful `write_bytes` as durable intent before paid effects; for example local_fleet `reserve` persists the allocation intent before `create_canister` (local_fleet/ops/mod.rs:205).

Recommendation

On `target_vendor = "apple"`, call `rustix::fs::fcntl_fullfsync(&parent_fd)` (falling back to fsync on ENOTSUP) at all three directory-sync points, matching std's `sync_all` semantics for files.

lowunverifiedhost-icp-network-7 · liveness · high confidence
The raw replica HTTP client used by `canic list` and `canic status` sets no connect, read or write timeout and reads the whole response unbounded, so a wedged or hostile local gateway hangs the command forever.
crates/canic-host/src/replica_query/transport/mod.rs:102

Failure scenario

The PocketIC gateway process is suspended (SIGSTOP, debugger, or a stuck replica) but its socket still accepts connections. `canic status` or `canic list --environment local` blocks in `read_to_end` indefinitely, with one hung thread per registry entry in `list`. A misbehaving endpoint named through an `http://` environment can also stream an unbounded body into memory.

Evidence

`get_http_status` (transport/mod.rs:37-47) and `post_cbor` (100-113) call `TcpStream::connect` with no `connect_timeout`, never call `set_read_timeout` or `set_write_timeout`, and call `read_to_end` into an unbounded Vec. Errors are handled only as I/O errors; timeouts are never raised. `local_replica_status_reachable_from_root` (status/mod.rs:5-14) is a boolean probe used by `canic status` (canic-cli/src/status/mod.rs:192) and `canic replica` (canic-cli/src/replica/mod.rs:437). `split_http_body` does not handle chunked encoding (129-149). Contrast the agent query path, which enforces 10 s per attempt and 30 s overall (icp/query/mod.rs:18-20).

Recommendation

Use `TcpStream::connect_timeout` and set read and write timeouts of a few seconds. Cap the response with `Read::take` to the CBOR envelope limit plus the header size. Treat a timeout as unreachable. Consider reusing the reqwest client with an explicit deadline.

lowunverifiedhost-icp-network-13 · robustness · medium confidence
Workspace-root discovery recursively scans the `apps/` tree of every ancestor directory and aborts on the first error in any of them, including an unrelated ancestor's duplicate App names or unreadable directories.
crates/canic-host/src/config_discovery/mod.rs:72

Every `canic` command run from `~/work/ws` fails with `DuplicateApp` about files outside the workspace. A large `apps/**/target` tree also makes every command walk thousands of directories.

`discover_canic_workspace_root_from` loops over `start.ancestors()`. For each one it calls `discover_workspace_canic_config_choices(candidate)?` (config_discovery/mod.rs:67-89) and only returns early on a candidate that has `icp.yaml`. That helper recurses into every non-symlink subdirectory of `candidate/apps` with no depth or entry bound. This covers `target/`, `node_modules/` and `.canic/generated/` (166-199). lowconfirmedhost-release-set-2 · contract · high confidence
Evidence envelope `payload_sha256` is never verified against the payload, and `canic evidence compare` ignores the payload body and trusts that field
crates/canic-host/src/policy_gate/evaluation/mod.rs:308

Failure scenario

A CI envelope is edited or partially regenerated so that `payload.source.dirty` becomes false and `payload.artifacts[].sha256` changes, while `payload_sha256` is left as it was. `canic evidence gate` passes the edited body with no evidence_conflict. `canic evidence compare` against the reviewed reference reports Matched, because only the unchanged `payload_sha256` is compared. The two passive commands vouch for contradictory evidence.

Evidence

EvidenceEnvelopeV1 carries `payload_sha256: Option<String>` beside `payload: serde_json::Value` (evidence_envelope/mod.rs:24-25). The producer computes it with `json_payload_sha256(&payload)` over the typed BuildProvenanceV1, serialized in struct field order, and stores `serde_json::to_value(&payload)` (build_provenance/envelope.rs:36-37). serde_json is built without preserve_order (Cargo.lock:4329-4339 has no indexmap), so the stored Value re-serializes with sorted keys and a generic recomputation never matches. evaluate_policy_gate passes the parsed envelope straight to evaluate_policy (policy_gate/mod.rs:36-59). evaluate_build_provenance decodes `envelope.payload` and applies the clean-source, lock, gzip and sha rules to the body (evaluation/mod.rs:308-338) without comparing it to `payload_sha256`. The manifest gate behaves the same way (manifest_gate/mod.rs:79-93). The CLI's compare lists `payload_sha256` as compared and `payload` as ignored (canic-cli/src/evidence/compare.rs:17-28), and its help states this (evidence/command.rs:107).

Recommendation

Define the payload digest over a canonical encoding that verifiers can reproduce, either the exact payload JSON bytes stored in the envelope or a sorted-key canonical form. In evaluate_policy and the manifest gate, recompute it and emit an `evidence_conflict` finding on mismatch or absence. In compare, either compare the payload body or verify both digests first.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The facts are correct, but the impact is overstated. evaluate_build_provenance decodes envelope.payload and applies its rules (policy_gate/evaluation/mod.rs:308-338) without ever checking payload_sha256. The manifest gate does the same (manifest_gate/mod.rs:79-93). Compare lists payload_sha256 as compared and payload as ignored (canic-cli/src/evidence/compare.rs:17-28). The producer hashes the typed struct (build_provenance/envelope.rs:36) but stores a sorted-key Value (line 37; serde_json has no preserve_order, Cargo.lock:4330-4340). This deviates from the 0.51 design rule that the digest covers "the serialized payload bytes used in the envelope" (0.51-design.md:511-512). Mitigating factors: envelopes are explicitly unsigned and "not attestations" (0.51-design.md:621-625), and the payload is declared the evidence authority (617-619). Anyone able to edit the body can also recompute an unkeyed SHA-256 with the public json_payload_sha256 (evidence_envelope/mod.rs:320-325), so verifying the digest would catch only accidental inconsistency, not tampering. The gate report also records the fingerprint of the evaluated envelope file (policy_gate/mod.rs:48-54). Compare comparing payload_sha256 instead of the payload is documented and was accepted (evidence/command.rs:107; 0.51-closeout.md:86). This is a real but low-impact contract gap: the digest is unverified and cannot be reproduced from the envelope.
Also reported as: cli-ops-11
lowunverifiedhost-release-set-4 · architecture · medium confidence
Release-set loaders return unbound child evidence, so each consumer must re-implement the finalized digest chain, and several bind it only partially
crates/canic-host/src/release_set/application/persistence/mod.rs:220

Failure scenario

A retained union or infrastructure manifest under `.canic/release-builds/<id>/` is replaced with different but canonical JSON, for example copied from another build with the id rewritten. Other paths reject the same release, so behaviour becomes inconsistent across commands.

load_persisted_application_artifact_union validates only shape and topology (application/persistence/mod.rs:220-228). load_persisted_canic_infrastructure_artifact_manifest validates only canonical shape (infrastructure/persistence/mod.rs:261-269). load_persisted_current_release_set_manifest does not check the finalized plan digest (current/mod.rs:209-215). The only binding is manual digest comparison at each call site. ProtocolCatalog::load loads both children and the finalized record but never compares child digests to the current manifest (fleet_ensure/ops/current_inventory/mod.rs:257-268). registration::bind_state trusts an unbound infrastructure manifest (infrastructure_bootstrap/registration/mod.rs:103-107). compile_current_store_sequence binds the union to the current manifest but not the current manifest to the finalized plan (current_protocol/mod.rs:2217-2232). On the writer side, compile_and_persist_current_release_set_manifest re-reads the fixture manifest but trusts the caller's `application.digest` and `infrastructure.digest` (current/mod.rs:163-176), and the Persisted* structs have public, freely constructible fields (application/persistence/mod.rs:63-68).

Recommendation

Add one release_set-owned `load_finalized_release_authority(root, id, topology)`. It should load and validate the finalized plan, the current manifest, all three children and their digests, and return an opaque verified type with private fields. Have every consumer use it, and have the writer recompute child digests from retained bytes.

lowunverifiedhost-release-set-7 · security · medium confidence
Clean-source provenance relies on `git status` defaults that user or repository git config can override, so untracked sources can be reported as `clean`
crates/canic-host/src/build_provenance/source.rs:19

Failure scenario

A repository sets `status.showUntrackedFiles = no`, a common speed setting in large repos, or CI exports GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS with that setting. A new untracked module or build-script input is compiled into the artifact. Provenance records `dirty: false` and `dirty_policy: clean`, and `canic evidence gate` with require_clean_source passes an artifact built from uncommitted source.

Evidence

Dirty detection is `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` with no `--untracked-files` or `--ignore-submodules` override (source.rs:19). The result is `dirty = !status.is_empty()` with `dirty_policy: Clean` when empty (source.rs:32-43). clear_git_environment removes GIT_DIR-style variables but not GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT or GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS (source.rs:92-106), and the command inherits the user's and the repository's git config. Porcelain status honours `status.showUntrackedFiles=no` and per-submodule `ignore` settings. The policy rule `require_clean_source` passes exactly on `dirty == Some(false)` and `dirty_policy == Clean` (policy_gate/evaluation/mod.rs:341-347).

Recommendation

Invoke git with explicit flags: `-c status.showUntrackedFiles=all -c core.fsmonitor=false status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --ignore-submodules=none`. Also clear the GIT_CONFIG_* variables, or record the effective settings in the provenance.

lowunverifiedhost-release-set-8 · contract · high confidence

crates/canic-host/src/release_set/application/mod.rs:801

Failure scenario

lowunverifiedr2-application-session-authz-1 · correctness · high confidence
Session establishment rejects proofs whose issue time is ahead of the verifier clock, ignoring the 60 s skew the verifier itself accepts, and reports the transient condition as SECURITY_INVALID
crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/auth/application_authorization.rs:192

Failure scenario

The issuer runs on subnet A and the verifier on subnet B, whose block time lags A by 6 s (for example under load). The client prepares a 30 s token on A (issued_at = T_A), fetches it and submits Establish to B about 3 s later, when B's time is T_A - 3 s. verify_token accepts the token because of the 60 s skew. Eligibility then fails with NotCurrentlyValid and the client receives SECURITY_INVALID. That is indistinguishable from an invalid proof, so a conforming client treats the login as failed rather than retrying a few seconds later. The same token also passes auth::authenticated token-lane endpoints on the same canister at the same instant.

Evidence

The verifier deliberately tolerates clock skew between subnets. verify_cert_time accepts cert.not_before up to AUTH_TIME_SKEW_ALLOWANCE_NS ahead of now (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/verify.rs:194), and verify_claims does the same for claims.issued_at (verify.rs:243). The allowance is 60 s (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/mod.rs:42). verify_delegated_token_material then sets proof_not_before = cert.not_before_ns.max(claims.issued_at_ns) (verify.rs:178). After verification succeeds, establish_verified calls validate_application_proof_eligibility (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/auth/application_sessions.rs:147). That check rejects `now_ns < proof_not_before_ns()` as NotCurrentlyValid with no skew allowance (application_authorization.rs:192-194). map_workflow_error maps NotCurrentlyValid to SECURITY_INVALID, the same code as a forged proof (crates/canic-core/src/api/auth/application_session.rs:403-407), and the rejection metric records ProofInvalid (application_session.rs:371-375). issued_at is the issuer subnet's time at prepare (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/prepare.rs:151), and cert.not_before is the root subnet's time at batch planning (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegation/chain_key_batch/mod.rs:429). The verifier can be on a third subnet whose clock lags.

Recommendation

Apply the same AUTH_TIME_SKEW_ALLOWANCE_NS tolerance to proof_not_before in validate_application_proof_eligibility, or clamp the stored not-before to verifier time. Alternatively, return a distinct typed 'proof not yet valid' diagnostic (for example AUTH_PROOF_PENDING, which already exists for root proofs) so clients can retry. Add a unit test with issued_at slightly ahead of now.

lowunverifiedr2-application-session-authz-2 · robustness · medium confidence
Session admission counts expired, unpruned sessions and replay tombstones, and pruning is gated behind unrelated intent-cleanup errors, so a cleanup outage becomes a permanent login lockout
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/intent.rs:449

Failure scenario

A verifier canister retains a receipt-backed intent whose expiry index entry makes abort_intent_if_pending return Ok(false). Every cleanup run then fails with an invariant error before reaching session cleanup. Replay tombstones, one per login and each dead after 60 s, are never removed. Once 4,096 logins have occurred, every Establish fails with CAPACITY_LIMIT, although no live tombstone remains. An upgrade restores the same state and the same failing batch, so login stays blocked until reinstall.

Evidence

application_session_occupancy returns raw index sizes: session_by_caller.len() and replay_by_fingerprint.len(), which include expired records (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/auth/application_sessions.rs:320-337). commit_application_session enforces the 4,096-replay and 2,048-session caps against those raw counts (application_sessions.rs:367-382). The pure policy documents its input as 'Target-local post-cleanup occupancy' (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/auth/application_authorization.rs:291), but establishment never prunes inline. Pruning happens only in IntentCleanupWorkflow::cleanup_due_batch, and only after receipt reclamation and local intent aborts, each of which returns early with `?` on error (intent.rs:412-447). Session cleanup at intent.rs:449-452 is therefore skipped whenever an earlier step fails. On any batch error run_due_batch_at returns TimerDirective::Stop (intent.rs:342-358). The API re-arms the timer only on successful Establish or Clear (crates/canic-core/src/api/auth/application_session.rs:104, 155, 169). A rejected Establish never re-arms it (application_session.rs:66-71). Separately, if the cleanup timer cannot be declared at all (for example the ic-timers registry is full, per xc-robustness-1), nothing ever prunes these records.

Recommendation

Prune expired sessions and replays for the admission check inside establishment, bounded by a small limit, before computing occupancy. Alternatively, compute occupancy from records whose expiry is still in the future (count only live tombstones), as the policy's 'post-cleanup' contract describes. Run application-session cleanup independently of receipt and intent cleanup errors, and re-arm the cleanup timer on capacity rejection as well.

lowunverifiedr2-application-session-authz-3 · robustness · medium confidence
Delegated tokens carry the issuer certificate's full grant set twice, and no validation keeps a policy-valid token within the fixed 16 KiB canic_command cap that session establishment must fit in
crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:504

Failure scenario

An operator registers an issuer policy and renewal template covering 10 roles with about 20 scopes of about 30 bytes each, which passes all root checks. That is roughly 6 to 7 KB per grant copy, so tokens are roughly 17 to 18 KB even with minimal claims. Users can prepare and retrieve tokens, and token-lane endpoints with a raised payload cap accept them. Every Establish ingress is silently refused at inspect_message with a generic rejection, so application sessions can never be opened and nothing tells the operator why.

Evidence

Establish travels only as CanisterCommand::ApplicationSession inside canic_command. canic_command's inspect_message and macro guard cap the payload at DEFAULT_UPDATE_INGRESS_MAX_BYTES = 16 KiB (role.rs:570-586; crates/canic-core/src/ingress/payload.rs:9), and the application cannot raise this cap. Every DelegatedToken embeds the root-signed grant vector twice: DelegationCert.grants (crates/canic-core/src/dto/auth/proof.rs:238) and ChainKeyDelegationCertV1.grants inside the root proof (proof.rs:165). Verification requires the two to be equal (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/chain_key.rs:380). The user can narrow only claims.grants; the certificate grants are the issuer's whole template. Policy allows up to 16 role grants of 32 scopes each (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/audience.rs:14-15), with scopes up to 64 bytes (crates/canic-core/src/model/auth/application_authorization/mod.rs:25). That is roughly 33 KB per copy, far above the cap. On top of this come the issuer canister-signature certificate (typically 1.5 to 3 KB on mainnet) and an optional caller ext of up to 4,096 bytes (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/canonical.rs:28). Neither issuer-policy upsert nor renewal-template validation bounds the encoded grant size (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/auth/root_provisioning.rs:31-46, 125-136).

Recommendation

Bound the encoded size of certificate grants when issuer policies and renewal templates are upserted, keeping a whole token (two grant copies, issuer proof and maximum ext) within the Establish payload budget. Alternatively, give the ApplicationSession variant a larger explicit per-variant limit. Document the size budget, and add a test that measures the encoded size of a worst-case policy-valid token against the cap.

The refusal is typed and happens before any effect, with no corruption or partial snapshot. It remains a real gap: AGENTS.md lists same-release backup/restore as required, multi-root Fleets are a maintained topology, and they currently cannot be backed up at all. The concrete fixable defects are the misleading error and the needless refusal of a single-root subtree.

Only then does FleetServicePeerOps::resolve look up the caller (line 918). validated_current clones the candidate, active and synchronization records (storage/stable/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:97-103) and calls validate, manifest, version and directory_for_root (ops/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:69-94). Those amount to about six full validations and three canonical encodings plus SHA-256 of a Registry of up to 2 MiB (ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:362-407, 733-757). crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:329

Failure scenario

A Root with 2,000 group members does 2,000 publication steps, each transferring and re-validating a Registry of up to 2 MiB from the Coordinator. The Coordinator re-derives its whole history for each call. Publication for large groups becomes very expensive and slow, and any unrelated Registry advance mid-publication wedges an already-mirrored Root.

So on every call it runs fetch_snapshot, an unbounded-wait call that returns the whole FleetRegistry (fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:53-63), recomputes the manifest and directory twice, and validate_target requires the live Coordinator version to equal expected (343; 585-587). Only after that does classify_active_transition notice the mirror is already current (344-346). The Root timer publishes one member per invocation, and each invocation first issues query_coordinator_provisioning (component_provisioning.rs:255-275). Each member step therefore costs a Coordinator status read, a Store status read (cp-runtime-api-4), a full Registry transfer, and two full Coordinator record validations (cp-fleet-coordinator-6). Because the live check comes first, a Root whose mirror already matches still fails publication if the Coordinator Registry advances (for example the draining publication in cp-fleet-coordinator-3).

Recommendation

In advance_for_component_publication, return early when the validated local active mirror already equals expected_registry and its directory. Better, advance the mirror once per publication in begin_publication and persist the result, so later member steps skip the Coordinator entirely. Stop re-querying Coordinator status on each member step once published_fleet_registry is recorded.

That value is the acceptance-time record field: begin_publication stores the published version only in publication.fleet_registry (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:821-822). So the short-circuit at fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:322-328 never fires on the normal path. Every call runs root_store::status (321), then fetch_snapshot, which sends an unbounded-wait CANIC_COORDINATOR_REGISTRY call returning the full FleetRegistry (fleet_coordinator_client/mod.rs:53-63), recomputes the manifest (494-495), and runs directory_for_root twice (330, 589). The Coordinator serves each read through current(), which runs validate_current (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:464-472, 1917-1942). Only after all that does classify_active_transition return Current (659-661), even though commit_active already stored the full snapshot locally. publish_component_directory delivers one member per call (783-856), and the timer adds query_coordinator_provisioning on every step (255-275). That makes about three overhead calls per useful delivery. Downgraded to low: the cost is aggregate cycles and latency in a one-time, operator-started operation. Per-message cost stays far below the 40B limit, and the Registry holds specs, roots and services, not instances, so 2 MiB is only a cap. The heavy Coordinator validation is a separate finding (cp-fleet-coordinator-6). The wedge claim is overstated: validate_target (585-587) fences not-yet-mirrored roots in the same way, so an early return would not unwedge the operation. The live check may also be a deliberate stale-directory fence.
lowunverifiedr2-group-provisioning-pipeline-6 · robustness · high confidence
The Coordinator treats an unchanged Root cursor as a STATE_CONFLICT failure, so normal polling between Root steps records pending root failures, retries every second and makes the host replay ProvisionComponents
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/component_provisioning_reconciliation/mod.rs:242

Failure scenario

A Root takes several seconds per install step. Most Coordinator polls land between steps, and each one records STATE_CONFLICT, writes a full Coordinator commit and logs a warning. Host runs observe a 'failure' during normal progress and replay the command, adding Coordinator timer chains. The operator sees spurious failures throughout a healthy provisioning run.

Evidence

After each successful record, the Coordinator re-polls immediately with zero delay (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:934-938, 976-986). It then begins a new intent and queries the Root. validate_root_provision_response requires strictly_advances_to, which is false when the counts are equal (reconciliation/mod.rs:241-244; root_progress/mod.rs:83-91). replay_recorded_root_provision also requires strict progress (ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:2652-2665), so an unchanged Accepted cursor becomes Err(conflict). Runtime activation behaves the same way (component_provisioning_validation/mod.rs:400; component_provisioning_progress/mod.rs:447-466). Directory confirmation, by contrast, accepts equality (validation/mod.rs:645). The error is recorded as last_root_failure against the still-open intent, so it appears as pending_root_failure (component_provisioning_retry/mod.rs:55-67). A Warn line is logged and the next attempt runs after 1 s (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:940-971). The host maps any pending failure on an unapplied operation to ReplayExactIssuedCommand (current_protocol/mod.rs:1320-1322), and each replay re-enters accept_component_provisioning and starts another Coordinator timer chain (cp-fleet-coordinator-10).

Recommendation

Treat an observation equal to the recorded cursor as Current or pending: keep the intent and schedule a bounded backoff poll without recording a failure. Apply the same change to runtime activation. Only a regression or an identity mismatch should count as a conflict.

lowunverifiedr2-group-provisioning-pipeline-7 · robustness · low confidence
The Root status reply embeds the full per-member provisioned result with no size bound, so a large batch that fits in the request can produce a reply above the cross-subnet limit, which the Coordinator can never read
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:3468

Failure scenario

One Root holds about 3,500-4,096 members, for example one deployment with large member counts and several recovery controllers. The Provisioned status reply exceeds 2 MiB, so the Root's reply fails. The Coordinator records a transport failure and retries every second forever, and the operation never advances past ProvisioningRoots.

Evidence

status_response includes the entire result from Provisioned onward (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:3447-3478). Each result member is a RootProvisionedGroupMember with a full ComponentBinding (dto/component_provisioning.rs:384-409). That binding carries a FleetRegistryAuthority, which includes the Fleet key, app, coordinator subnet and principal, and every recovery controller (ids/fleet_topology/mod.rs:242-248, 340-349). That comes to roughly 420-600 Candid bytes per member, about three times a plan entry. The only bounds are on the request side: 4,096 entries per plan and 8 MiB of canonical bytes (component_provisioning_plan/mod.rs:49-63). No reply bound exists. The Coordinator reads this reply cross-subnet on every provisioning, confirmation and activation poll (workflow/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:1277-1300). It also stores each Root's result in its single record, where it is re-validated on every load.

Recommendation

Bound the encoded status reply at plan-validation time (members per Root times the maximum encoded result size), or return results in pages or as a hash-bound digest the Coordinator fetches in pages. Keep the full ComponentBinding authority out of each member, since it repeats the batch-level authority.

lowunverifiedr2-host-plan-compiler-5 · correctness · high confidence
Pool Fund authority takes Root from live.controllers.first(), which is the lexicographically first controller and can be a recovery controller rather than the Root
crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/policy/mod.rs:1807

Failure scenario

A configured Idle pool asset has cycles below its desired minimum_cycles, and recovery controller '2vxsx-…' sorts before Root 'rrkah-…'. The plan's Fund names the recovery principal as Root. Effect preparation calls query_estate_pool_page on it, and the call fails deterministically. Every re-review produces the same plan, so the Fund never applies.

append_target_funding builds PoolFundingAuthority { root: live.controllers.first() } for Pool targets (policy/mod.rs:1803-1813). Observed pool controllers are synthesized as sorted(configured.controllers + root), which includes the recovery controllers (ops/platform.rs:2497-2503, 2616-2622). The executor then pages the pool inventory of authority.root (ops/platform.rs:2441-2458, 5033-5044), and the retained-plan sufficiency check looks up the domain by that principal (workflow/mod.rs:3427-3431). If any recovery controller's text sorts before the Root's, the query targets a user principal and fails before the withdraw. The path is latent with generated desired, because Root records Ready cycles at or above the floor and desired minimum_cycles equals the floor. Resolve the Root from configured.parent through the observed Root principal (as ReconcilePoolAsset funding does), not from controller order.

lowconfirmedr2-recycled-principal-authority-1 · security · high confidence
Root issuer policies and renewal templates stay keyed to a retired issuer's principal, so Root keeps signing and installing delegation certs for whichever Component next claims that canister
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/auth/root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:33

Failure scenario

The operator upserts an issuer policy and renewal template for user_hub Component A at principal P, with grants on project_instance scopes and a Fleet audience. The operator then runs RemoveComponent(A); P is reset and completed as Ready. The next renewal sweep still includes P's enabled template, the install to the empty P fails, and the renewal timer stops for every issuer. An allocation for Component B then claims P; B is another tenant's user_hub, or any role compiled with canic_capability_delegated_token_issuer. Root signs A's cert again, either lazily through B's GetOrCreateDelegationProof or through renewal, and installs it on P. B's open PrepareDelegatedToken now mints Fleet-audience tokens with A's operator-approved grants, and every verifier accepts them, although the operator never authorized B.

Evidence

Issuer authority is keyed only by principal. RootDelegationStateOps offers get, list and upsert for issuer policies and renewal templates but no removal (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/auth/mod.rs:135-197). Nothing in canic-control-plane references them (grep for RootDelegationStateOps or issuer_policy finds nothing). Neither retirement (workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:1555-1627, 1981-2115) nor pool reset (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:672-689) revokes them.

Batch approval checks only the stored policy for template.issuer_pid (root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:29-49). The signed registry snapshot lists policies by issuer_canister_id (ops/auth/delegation/chain_key_registry.rs:55-90). Root then pushes each proof to issuer_pid (workflow/runtime/auth/provisioning/mod.rs:175-187). The issuer-side InstallDelegationProof checks only that the caller is a controller, which Root always is (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:648-656), plus a valid root proof for this canister (ops/auth/delegation/active.rs:26-45). GetOrCreateDelegationProof admits any active Component member and uses msg_caller as issuer_pid (endpoints/root.rs:296-311; api/auth/root.rs:60-67).

While the principal is empty in the pool, the install fails with CallFailed, which maps to PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE (infra/mod.rs:21; provisioning/mod.rs:271-279). is_retryable_renewal_error rejects that code (renewal.rs:391-398), so failed_result stops the renewal timer (renewal.rs:240-247).

Recommendation

Bind issuer policies and templates to the managed binding (ComponentInstanceId, role and install id), and verify that binding at batch approval and in GetOrCreateDelegationProof. Alternatively, make Component retirement atomically disable or delete the retired principal's policy, template, renewal state and batch entries before complete_recycling, and add an operator removal API. Treat an install to a principal that is not a current member as skip-and-disable, not as a failure that stops the whole batch.

Severity adjusted from high to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The mechanism is real, but the impact is overstated. Issuer policies and templates are keyed only by principal (model/auth/root_issuer.rs:20-37). Storage has get and upsert but no delete (storage/stable/auth/mod.rs:247-382). Nothing in canic-control-plane touches them on delete_component or remove_component_membership (component_registry/mod.rs:1555-1627). complete_recycling returns P to Ready (canister_pool/mod.rs:1647-1648). So a later issuer role at P would be approved under A's policy (root_delegation_batch/mod.rs:29-49; selection.rs:28). No principal gains authority from this, though. Every token is self-issued: subject = presenter = the caller (ops/auth/delegated/prepare.rs:146-156). The open prepare endpoint (role.rs:676-680) can only grant session, verify, or scopes the target role declares as self-grantable (prepare/admission.rs:108-128; policy/pure/auth/mod.rs:142-160; AUTH_DELEGATED_SIGNATURES.md:287-293). No privileged issuance API exists (api/auth/token.rs). While A was live, any caller could already get the same A-grant token for themselves from P, and grants are per role, not per tenant. Root controls P and installs only release-set code there. The operator can also disable P with an enabled=false upsert (root_issuer/mod.rs:64-79). What remains is lifecycle hygiene: a retired issuer stays in the signed registry. A side effect is plausible: an install to an empty P fails as PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE, which is not retryable (provisioning/mod.rs:271-279; renewal.rs:391-398), so the renewal timer stops (renewal.rs:240-247). Issuers still recover lazily (prepare/mod.rs:330-361).
lowconfirmedr2-recycled-principal-authority-3 · cycles · high confidence
Root's per-child lifetime funding ledger is keyed by principal and never cleared, so a Component that reuses a recycled canister inherits the previous Component's consumed max_per_child budget
crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:344

Failure scenario

Long-lived Component A at P receives 98 TC of Root top-ups over months, against the 100 TC default cap, and is then removed. P is recycled with its residual balance and claimed by a new top-level Component B. B's first top-up is clamped to 2 TC, and every later request is denied as MaxPerChild; B also inherits A's cooldown. B runs only on its initial pool cycles, cannot be refilled by Root, and eventually freezes and is uninstalled by the IC, although B itself consumed no budget.

Evidence

Root authorizes a top-level Component's RequestCycles with the role taken from its current Registry binding (nonroot_cycles.rs:338-341, 479-490). It evaluates the grant against CyclesFundingLedgerOps::snapshot(ctx.caller) (nonroot_cycles.rs:344) and charges record_child_grant(ctx.caller, ...) (nonroot_cycles.rs:421).

The ledger accumulates granted_total per principal (ops/runtime/cycles_funding.rs:23-30; test at 49-61). Policy treats that total as lifetime headroom: remaining = max_per_child - granted_total, with a default cap of 100 TC and a 60 s cooldown on last_granted_at (domain/policy/pure/cycles_funding.rs:5-7, 16-27, 49-52).

The only writers are record_child_grant and restore_child_snapshot. A grep across crates finds uses only at nonroot_cycles.rs:344, 420, 421 and 435, so no retirement or recycle path clears or rebinds the entry. Pool recycle (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:578-586) and membership removal (component_registry/mod.rs:1594-1627) leave it intact. The same holds for a Component parent's ledger when a child principal it funded is later reassigned to it.

Recommendation

Key the funding ledger by the managed binding (ComponentInstanceId or install id). Otherwise, clear the principal's ledger entry on the funding parent atomically with membership removal and complete_recycling, together with its root.request_cycles replay receipts.

Severity adjusted from medium to low during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): Factually correct. The ledger is keyed by principal (ops/runtime/cycles_funding.rs:23-35). Policy computes lifetime headroom as max_per_child - granted_total, with a 100 TC default and a 60 s cooldown (domain/policy/pure/cycles_funding.rs:5-7, 49-52). Root evaluates against snapshot(ctx.caller) (nonroot_cycles.rs:344) and charges record_child_grant(ctx.caller) (421). The only other stable writer is the canonical *Data import at storage/stable/cycles.rs:207, which is backup restore. Nothing on the recycle or membership-removal path clears the entry. Top-level component deletion recycles P into the pool (component_registry/mod.rs:5868-5882, 1626; canister_pool/mod.rs:578-586), and Ready assets are reclaimed (canister_pool/mod.rs:1647-1648). Downgraded to low: the error is conservative and typed (MaxPerChild), and no cycles are lost or stranded. P keeps its residual balance through reset (uninstall retains cycles; the pool selects assets by recorded cycles), so B also inherits part of what was granted to A. Anyone can deposit cycles directly, so the effect is recoverable out of band. The lifetime cap would strand a long-lived A in the same way, so the inheritance only shortens B's configured budget. It is a real policy-scope defect (budget bound to the principal rather than the ComponentInstanceId), but its impact is bounded.
lowunverifiedr2-recycled-principal-authority-6 · security · medium confidence
A recycle whose reset failed before uninstall still completes membership removal, and Root draining then hands that un-reset canister, with the retired workload's module and stable memory, to the asset recipient
crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1649

Failure scenario

uninstall_code during Component A's recycle hits a transient management rejection. Membership removal still completes, so A disappears from the Registry, while P keeps A's Wasm, stable memory (user data, sessions, keys) and snapshots, and the asset stays Failed. On Root removal, fleet_subnet_root.rs:601-617 hands P to the draining asset_recipient. The recipient becomes a controller of a canister holding tenant A's full state, and its own recovery or import flow may start it.

Evidence

The reset sequence is stop, then update_settings, then uninstall_code (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:672-688). Any error before uninstall completes goes to mark_failed, which stores Recycling{reset: Failed} (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:645-647; ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:223-227). recycling_completion accepts Failed and maps it to pool status Failed (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1647-1651), so validate_complete_recycling passes. remove_component_membership (component_registry/mod.rs:1607-1626) and remove_subtree_leaf_membership (component_registry/mod.rs:2088-2106) then erase the Registry entry while the module and state remain.

A retry cannot reset the asset: prepare_reinspection sends PendingReset or Failed assets with nonzero recorded cycles to Reinspect, which rejects a present module (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:326-331; workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:657-663; see cp-pool-provisioning-3). During Root draining, handoff_candidate selects Ready or Failed assets (ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:1137-1152). handoff only adds the recipient as controller (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:544-553), with no uninstall and no snapshot deletion.

Recommendation

Make validate_complete_recycling fail unless the reset reached Ready or an underfunded Failed state that is proven post-uninstall. Mark dirty assets and re-run the destructive reset on retry. Exclude dirty Failed assets from handoff_candidate, or uninstall and delete snapshots before the handoff controller change.

lowunverifiedr2-replay-manifest-conformance-3 · contract · high confidence
The replay-policy manifest is never consumed at runtime, and its cost, quota and reserve labels have already drifted from the handlers' actual cost guards
crates/canic-core/src/replay_policy/role_command_manifest.rs:367

Failure scenario

A reviewer or a release check that relies on the manifest concludes that PrepareRoleAttestation is quota-bounded, that deployments reserve cycles and that RespondCapability on managed canisters is deployment-bounded. None of these hold at runtime. The drift has already hidden the unbounded role-attestation path reported in the first finding. Any future handler change can drift further with every test still green.
