Placement, sharding and scaling, fleet registry, service binding, admission and funding policy, fleet activation, provisioning plan

core-placement-fleet3 high2 medium4 low

This unit covers child placement and the Fleet evidence compilers. Placement has three strategies: scaling (worker pools), sharding (partition keys routed to shard canisters by HRW over slots) and index (one child per logical key). All three go through one shared admission primitive, PlacementAllocationWorkflow. It reserves capacity in the receipt-backed intent store under a deterministic operation id (owner, pool, subject, generation), replays the same root `allocate_placement_child` operation on retry, and settles Committed or RolledBack only after the domain registry owns or has disposed of the child. Terminal receipts are then released at root by a durable acknowledgement drain. The Fleet side (fleet_registry, fleet_service_binding, component_provisioning_plan/receipt, fleet_admission_policy, fleet_funding_policy, fleet_activation, admission projection) is mostly pure validation and canonical hashing. It carries exact authority checks, bounded plans, append-only service publication and idempotent state-machine transitions. Overall quality is high. The intent-before-effect and replay design is careful, canonical encoders are length-prefixed and domain-separated, and the Fleet Registry and provisioning validators are thorough about ordering, bounds and cumulative root capacity. The main risks sit in the placement workflows, where durable state and the allocation intent can come apart across awaits and on error paths. (1) The index claim-lost branch recycles the child it just received even when the key is now Bound to that same child. Two concurrent resumers of a stale claim can therefore destroy a live, bound instance. (2) The index claim is written before capacity admission. If admission fails, the claim is left untracked, which the code deliberately fails closed on forever. (3) Every index key permanently uses one of the 1,000 global intent resource-total records, so index creation, and every other new intent resource in that canister, stops working after about 1,000 keys. (4) Sharding assigns a key after the shard-creation await without re-checking whether the key was assigned meanwhile, so a key can silently move between shards. Secondary issues: sharding assignment scans every assignment in every pool on each call (unbounded instruction cost); `ScalingApi::create_worker` can never grow a pool beyond min_workers, although max_workers is documented as the cap; creation-path assignments skip the capacity check; the acknowledgement drain stops on transient root errors it classifies as non-retryable; a late concurrent caller gets an invariant error after the first caller's record is removed; and several canonical digests leave out authority fields they claim to bind. I found no defects in the funding-policy hashing, the service-binding compiler or the scale-out plan validator within the time available.

Strengths
  • Shared receipt-backed allocation identity (crates/canic-core/src/model/placement/allocation.rs:124-173) binds owner, kind, pool, subject and generation into the operation id, and role and extra_arg into a separate payload binding. Concurrent callers and retries therefore converge on one root operation rather than creating duplicate children.
  • Scaling and sharding keep placement bounded by construction: sharding identities are per slot, so concurrent creation is capped at max_shards (workflow/placement/sharding/allocation.rs:53-71), and scaling reuses committed_qty as the sequence, so only one worker is in flight per pool (scaling/mod.rs:237-245).
  • Terminal placement receipts are released through a durable, paged, backoff-bounded acknowledgement drain with a recovery watchdog (workflow/placement/acknowledgement.rs:87-133, 283-290), rather than being dropped.
  • Fleet Registry validation is exhaustive and fail-closed: exact authority equality, canonical root and service ordering, per-spec admission totals checked against the fleet maximum, service members restricted to Active admitting roots, and append-only scale-out that forbids removing members or adding Authority members (ops/fleet_registry/validation/mod.rs:71-176, ops/fleet_registry/mod.rs:572-667).
  • Scale-out provisioning validation seeds the ledger with committed placements before checking cumulative root placement, component and spec-admission capacity, density and spread (ops/component_provisioning_plan/scale_out/mod.rs:41-80, 201-238).
  • Fleet-service binding compilation re-derives each root receipt's content hash, checks exact phase, counts and time evidence, and rejects duplicate component identities and principals across published and new members (ops/fleet_service_binding/mod.rs:512-557, 588-630).
  • Funding policy digests bind every field of the coordinator, root and ICP-refill policies, and tests assert each field changes the hash (ops/fleet_funding_policy/mod.rs:70-100, 377-401).
  • Root-side recycle maps an InProgress subtree removal to a retryable error, so parent cleanup never releases a claim while a disposal is only partly done (workflow/rpc/request/handler/execute.rs:256-266).
Not covered

I read these only partly: ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs (about the first 1,100 of 2,573 lines; mapper.rs and the fixture submodule not read), ops/fleet_admission_policy/mod.rs past line 560, the fleet_funding_policy test module, and the tests.rs files of fleet_registry, fleet_service_binding and component_provisioning_plan (skimmed). I did not verify the domain-policy model validators the ops layer calls (model::fleet_funding_policy rotation limits, model::fleet_admission_projection transitions). Root-side replay and receipt semantics (ops/replay, the control-plane component registry) were followed only as far as needed to confirm the child-side findings. The realistic timing window for the index recycle race was reasoned from the replay-decision code, not reproduced. The cost of the O(N) sharding scan was estimated, not measured. I ran no build or test commands.

Domain, DTO, model, IDs, views, protocol and error types

core-data-model1 medium4 low5 info

This unit holds canic-core's passive and pure layers: layer-neutral IDs (`ids/`), boundary DTOs (`dto/`), authoritative model shapes and invariant validators (`model/`), pure policy decisions (`domain/policy/pure/`), read-only views, the error envelope and protocol method names. Most identifiers are carefully built newtypes. 32-byte identities (FleetId, CanonicalNetworkId, ReleaseBuildId, ComponentInstanceId) accept only canonical lowercase hex, and this is enforced at FromStr and at serde/Candid decode. Derived identities use domain-separated, length-prefixed SHA-256. The multi-phase journals (Fleet admission root, target projection, Coordinator mutation) re-validate the whole state before and after every transition and support exact replay. Cycle and ICP arithmetic uses checked or saturating operations and fails closed. Overall quality is high. No command DTO derives `Default`, and model and policy do not import DTOs (only `view/` does). I found no critical or high defect in these paths. The main risk is a policy-level DoS on local application sessions. Establishing a session is open to any non-infrastructure principal holding a self-issued delegated token, while `decide_application_session_admission` enforces one global cap of 2,048 active sessions and 4,096 replay records. An attacker with cheap self-authenticating principals can therefore block new users from logging in on a target canister. The other findings are latent or hygiene issues. ComponentInstanceId declares a Storable bound (64) smaller than its own CBOR encoding (66 bytes). Fleet-wide admission removal can leave redundant, non-canonical narrower rules. Application scopes share a namespace with delegated-token guard scopes. Several validated newtypes derive unvalidated Deserialize or have an infallible FromStr. There are also small contract drifts: logic inside a DTO, a view that depends on DTOs, a boundary type alias, and stale dead-code lint expectations.

Strengths
  • Canonical ID parsing is enforced at every decode path, not only FromStr: FleetId, CanonicalNetworkId, ReleaseBuildId and ComponentInstanceId implement Deserialize via the strict lowercase-hex parser (crates/canic-core/src/ids/fleet/mod.rs:62-101, ids/network.rs:86-125, ids/component/mod.rs:165-204), with tests rejecting uppercase and removed wire shapes (ids/fleet/mod.rs:291-349).
  • Derived identities are domain-separated and length-prefixed: ComponentInstanceId::from_root_allocation (ids/component/mod.rs:125-140), CanonicalNetworkId (ids/network.rs:17-34), ReleaseBuildId (ids/release_build.rs:53-59), placement allocation identities (model/placement/allocation.rs:128-175) and the replay payload hasher (model/replay/mod.rs:323-416).
  • Journal state machines validate full invariants before and after each transition and support exact replay with conflict detection: fleet_admission_root (domain/policy/pure/fleet_admission_root/mod.rs:393-476), target projection transitions (domain/policy/pure/fleet_admission_projection/mod.rs:45-172), Coordinator mutation planning (domain/policy/pure/fleet_admission/mod.rs:142-297).
  • Funding and refill arithmetic fails closed: window accounting treats overflowing spent+reserved as zero allowance (domain/policy/pure/fleet_funding/mod.rs:216-228), the automatic refill derives exact ceil(e8s) = deficit / xdr_permyriad (domain/policy/pure/icp_refill.rs:131-155), and funding policy validation uses checked_mul and is_none_or (model/fleet_funding_policy/mod.rs:401-424).
  • The error envelope maps every policy error variant exhaustively to a registered diagnostic code (crates/canic-core/src/error.rs:246-322), and public errors can only be created from registered codes (dto/error.rs:20-40).
  • The data-boundary contract largely holds: no command/request DTO derives Default, and model and policy do not import dto (only view/fleet_activation.rs does).
  • Bounded heap caches with conservative byte accounting and total admission caps (model/public_metrics/history/mod.rs:192-266, 379-392).
Not covered

I only skimmed the largest passive DTO files beyond their type outlines: dto/component_registry.rs past line 160, dto/fleet_subnet_root.rs, dto/fleet_registry.rs, dto/pool.rs, dto/pool_import, dto/runtime.rs, dto/component_provisioning.rs, dto/fleet_funding and dto/auth/{proof,renewal,application_session}.rs. I did not deeply review model/auth/application_authorization/authority.rs or domain/runtime.rs. I did not verify the stable-record size bounds in storage/** that embed these IDs (owned by another unit), Candid .did conformance, or host-side ordering consistency for Principal (ic_principal Ord is length-then-bytes, while some Canic code orders by as_slice()). No build or test was run, and every claim comes from reading the code. The session-capacity finding depends on issuer-side token issuance having no global rate limit, which I did not trace.

Blob storage, cashier billing, fixture content and import

core-blob-storage5 medium6 low1 info

This unit has two parts. The first is Canic's Caffeine/Toko-compatible blob-storage gateway. Content-addressed `sha256:<hex>` roots live in three stable BTreeMaps (live roots, pending deletions, gateway principals). Four gateway endpoints are macro-emitted. Only create-certificate has a guard the host supplies; the gateway-only list and confirm endpoints check the caller against the stored principal set. The optional billing layer adds Cashier integration: a stored config, gateway-principal sync (all-or-nothing with typed validation), a read-only status call, and project-cycle funding. Funding attaches cycles to a bounded-wait `account_top_up_v1` call behind a transient single-flight guard. The second part is the fixture-import consumer. A timer-owned, lease-fenced step fetches one chunk from the Store, checks every durable and heap fence again after the await, verifies length and digest, and asks the application importer to apply it. Importer errors trap so a partial write rolls back. Code quality is high in the core invariants. Hashes are canonicalised with typed errors. Nat/Int boundary conversions are checked. Policy is pure. Gateway sync keeps the previous set on every failure. The fixture consumer's post-await fencing is careful and correct. The main risks are at the protocol and accounting edges. (1) The gateway-facing endpoints return `Result<_, Error>` and reply with a certified `Err` on denial. The pinned Toko contract expects plain records, with traps on failure. Against the real gateway this either breaks certificate decoding or turns a denial into a certified reply. (2) Funding never observes how many cycles actually left the canister on error or unknown-outcome paths, and has no intent record, so a routine retry double-funds. (3) The confirm-deletion ingress is silently capped at 16 KiB, while the pending list is unbounded and has no pagination. Together they can wedge deletion. (4) Content-addressed roots have no reference counting, and the documented product flow deletes content that other assets still share. Smaller issues: the `sync-gateways` CLI reports success when the canister returns `Err`; a Candid decode failure is reported as "unavailable" rather than "malformed"; the funding reserve ignores call overhead; a confirm-deletion retry can remove a live root (ABA); there are no registration quotas; and a deterministic importer rejection retries forever without ever reaching a Failed status (this last one is documented design). Everything here is based on reading the code; I ran no tests or builds.

Strengths
  • Root-hash canonicalisation is strict and typed (prefix, length, hex, lowercase). Stable keys use the normalised form, so upper- and lowercase inputs collapse to one row (crates/canic-core/src/model/blob_storage/hash.rs:102-120; crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/blob_storage.rs:619-658).
  • Gateway sync validates the Cashier list before any mutation. It rejects empty lists, anonymous and management principals, and over-limit lists, deduplicates entries, and keeps the previous set on every error path (crates/canic-core/src/ops/cashier/conversion.rs:96-123; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/blob_storage/billing/mod.rs:138-151).
  • The funding single-flight guard is RAII and is released on return and on unwind, with tests covering both (crates/canic-core/src/ops/blob_storage/funding.rs:29-63, 110-127).
  • Billing decisions are pure functions using saturating arithmetic, with all-or-nothing attachment and no cycles attached on refusal (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/blob_storage/mod.rs:131-154).
  • Boundary numeric conversions reject negative and oversized Cashier Int values and oversized Nat config fields with typed errors instead of truncating (crates/canic-core/src/ops/cashier/conversion.rs:91-94; crates/canic-core/src/ops/blob_storage/conversion.rs:27-33).
  • The fixture consumer checks the heap lease, the durable attempt fence, activation, the exact assignment and the exact progress again after the Store await, then verifies chunk length and digest before any application callback (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/fixture_provisioning/mod.rs:105-118).
  • The fixture content identity is domain-separated and uses fixed-width fields, with a bounded chunk count, bounded chunk size and an exact length-sum check (crates/canic-core/src/ops/fixture_content/mod.rs:15-47).
  • CLI target resolution fails closed for unregistered principals and ambiguous roles, and derives the query/update mode from the Candid sidecar (crates/canic-cli/src/blob_storage/target.rs:95-187).
Not covered

The Caffeine storage gateway source is not available on this machine (there is no ../toko checkout), so how the gateway verifies the OwnerEgressSignature certificate, how it batches confirm-deletion calls, and how it uses the liveness query were inferred from the inventory, not confirmed. The Store-side fixture read path (canic-control-plane FixtureStoreApi authorize_read and read) and the ic_timers watchdog internals were not reviewed. Fleet-activation fixture validation was only checked for the content_id comparison. The PocketIC suites (pic_blob_storage.rs, fixture_provisioning tests), canic-cli blob_storage/tests.rs and model.rs were read only in part. No tests or builds were run. Instruction and reply-size thresholds are estimates. The real Cashier's behaviour (whether it accepts cycles before returning Err, and debt semantics) is unknown. The IC rule that refunds are lost on a dropped bounded-wait response comes from IC spec knowledge; ic-cdk 0.20.3 docs were checked and do not state it.

Component registry state machines and their stable storage

cp-registry-ops1 high3 medium4 low

The root-local Component Registry is a set of explicit, append-mostly state machines stored in six stable structures (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:87-190). The pieces are a meta Cell, the top-level allocation map, a normalized entries map (partitions, children, traversals, child allocations, subtree removals, parent/role counts), a principal index, subtree-removal history and per-Component draining records. The ops layer (ops/component_registry/*) builds each next record synchronously and hands exact expected/next pairs to store compare-and-commit functions. Allocation goes Reserved -> CreationIntent -> Created -> InstallIntent -> Installed -> Verified -> Committed (-> Removed for top-level). Membership activation, subtree removal (post-order, step-keyed history) and top-level retirement (draining -> quiescence -> final inventory -> delete -> membership removal) are similarly journalled, and a byte ledger (meta.encoded_bytes / partition.encoded_bytes) pre-charges terminal maximum sizes before paid effects. Quality is high. Every transition uses checked arithmetic and typed errors, replays are mostly idempotent, and fences between child reservation, subtree removal and draining are enforced in both directions. The code does not rely on state across awaits. The unit tests are extensive (idempotent replay, capacity exhaustion before mutation, export/import restart). The main risks are liveness and resource bounds, not authorization. (1) The byte ledger is checked only against multi-MiB configured limits and never against the 4096-byte Storable bounds of the stable maps. Records grow at later phases (chunk hashes, bindings, commitment and membership receipts, parent-supplied init args encoded about 1.9x as CBOR integer arrays), so a record that fit at reservation can trap on insert after the paid creation effect. That permanently wedges the allocation, which cannot be abandoned, and blocks Component and Root retirement. (2) Several replay paths recompute directory hashes from the caller's current Fleet directory or the current (advanced) partition and return `invariant` on a lost-response retry. (3) Top-level membership activation does not require the Prepared partition to be free of in-flight initial-bootstrap reservations. (4) Removed-Component validation is O(N) per Component inside root-wide loops, giving O(N^2)/O(R*P) messages on terminal Root inventory and admission. There are also smaller issues: ledger drift on grouped directory preparation, weaker guards on the top-level creation path than on the child path, and globally scoped by-operation lookups over per-Component-unique IDs.

Strengths
  • Every stable mutation is a compare-and-commit against the exact expected meta, partition and operation record (storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs:4180-4215, 4247-4333, 4822-4906, 5091-5114). All ops functions are synchronous, so no await splits a transition.
  • Terminal maximum sizes are pre-charged before paid effects: creation_charged_entry_bytes/install_charged_entry_bytes (ops/component_registry/mod.rs:3457-3578), component_quiescence_terminal_entry_bytes fixed-point (2820-2880), and child_allocation_entry_bytes always reserves the largest diagnostic slot (storage mod.rs:5749-5763). Retries and diagnostics therefore never move the ledger.
  • Subtree removal is post-order, bounded per message (SUBTREE_REMOVAL_TRAVERSAL_BATCH_SIZE=64, ops mod.rs:118; subtree_retirement/mod.rs:286-310) and keyed by traversal step in immutable history. Every phase recognises its completed-leaf receipt for effect-free replay (subtree_retirement/mod.rs:357-360, 441-448; storage mod.rs:4551-4695).
  • Fences run in both directions. Child reservation rejects parents inside a live subtree removal (child_allocation/mod.rs:156-177). Subtree removal rejects non-terminal child allocations in the target subtree (subtree_retirement/mod.rs:186-198). Draining requires zero reserved descendants and a terminal child/subtree history (component_retirement/mod.rs:134-153).
  • Unique canister IDs are enforced through the principal index at both top-level and child commit (storage mod.rs:5156-5161, 5265-5281). The child creation path also rejects protected and already-indexed principals (child_allocation/mod.rs:349-360).
  • Stale workflow decisions are caught in ops: reserve_allocation re-checks next_allocation_sequence (top_level_allocation/mod.rs:125-127), so a policy decision computed from a snapshot taken before an await cannot over-admit.
  • Terminal root accounting recomputes exact retained bytes and a history hash from durable records rather than trusting counters (ops mod.rs:1563-1651, 1727-1762).
  • Broad unit coverage of idempotency, capacity exhaustion before mutation and restart (tests/mod.rs:311, 1468, 1630, 2524, 4240, 4356, 5279).
Not covered

I did not read these closely: root_retirement.rs beyond about line 1100 (Store deletion, ledger transfer and root deletion cycle arithmetic), the view module, and most of tests/mod.rs, which I sampled only. I sampled workflow ordering only where it was needed to confirm a finding. I did not check how journalled directory-refresh intents interact with a later begin_component_draining, or whether require_catalog_mutation_allowed covers pending refreshes. The CBOR record sizes and instruction costs in findings 1 and 4 are estimates from reading the structure definitions; I did not run code to measure them. No code was executed.

Component registry orchestration, directory synchronization, component RPC and auth

cp-registry-workflow3 high5 medium3 low1 info

This unit is the root-side orchestration for the Component Registry. It covers top-level and child allocations (reserve, pool claim, install, verify, commit, Directory preparation, runtime activation, membership activation). It also covers Component draining and quiescence, deletion, and membership removal, post-order subtree removal (fence, traverse, stop, delete by recycling into the pool, membership removal, Directory sync, finalize), coordinator-driven scale-out Directory synchronization, and the root capability RPC and component-auth predicates. Work is driven by private lifecycle timers (schedule_*), by operator RootCommands (ProvisionComponent, RemoveComponent, RemoveSubtree), and inline by member RPCs (CreateCanister, RecycleCanister). The local code quality is high. Every paid or destructive effect has a durable intent before it runs. Management effects are re-observed after lost responses. Controller and module-hash checks are exact. Retired canisters go back to the pool with their cycles, so cycle conservation holds. RPC authority comes from protected Registry evidence, not from the request. The main risks are in liveness and recovery, not authorization. (1) Allocations freeze a Directory authority (the Fleet Directory snapshot plus the Component registry head) at commit time. Every later phase re-checks that frozen hash against the live Fleet mirror and the live partition. One Fleet publication or funding rotation, or a sibling child commit, arriving mid-allocation wedges it permanently. A wedged allocation also blocks removal of the Component and of its ancestor subtrees. (2) The scale-out Directory sync keeps one in-flight intent that can become impossible to reconcile. That wedges the root's only sync slot. (3) The timer drivers retry every 1 s forever with no backoff and no dedup. The subtree driver even loops forever on an already-Completed removal. Each perpetual lifecycle timer makes suspend_root fail, which blocks root authority snapshots (backup). (4) Retirement needs a live, still-installed, responsive workload, and there is no way to abandon a child allocation. So broken or abandoned workloads can make a Component unremovable.

Strengths
  • Intent-before-effect journalling with cost-guard permits for pool claims and installs, including recovery of the permit on failure (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/component_installation/mod.rs:73-102, 544-652, 771-871).
  • Lost-response reconciliation on every runtime configure/activate call: after a call error the code re-queries and accepts converged state (component_registry/mod.rs:4372-4392, 4436-4458, 4610-4630, 3071-3086).
  • Stop effects are independently re-observed with exact root-controller and module-hash checks before a receipt is committed (component_registry/mod.rs:5792-5849, 5914-5952).
  • Cycle-conserving retirement: removed workloads are uninstalled and retained in the local pool with their cycles, never deleted (component_registry/mod.rs:5851-5883; workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:578-586, 652-690).
  • Root capability authority is resolved only from protected Registry membership. Parent selection is structural only (ThisCanister). Recycle-recovery authority is bound to the caller's own durable removal journal and parent, and the lifecycle executor re-checks identity after each phase (workflow/component_rpc/mod.rs:42-171; workflow/component_rpc/lifecycle.rs:167-200).
  • Directory paging is bounded (limit <= 100, cursor <= 2048 bytes), and the opaque cursor is bound to the exact head and filters (component_registry/mod.rs:3755-3757, 5378-5419).
  • Scale-out Directory synchronization fans out to exactly one target per coordinator call and journals the in-flight intent before the Component call (ops/component_directory_synchronization/mod.rs:107-154; workflow/component_directory_synchronization/mod.rs:81-95).
  • Child allocation failures record typed diagnostics with backoff (ops/component_registry/child_failure/mod.rs:72-103; lifecycle_drivers/mod.rs:198-215).
Not covered

I did not review ComponentRegistryOps/store internals beyond the functions my paths call. In particular I only spot-checked the store commit functions, traversal and partition byte accounting, and root retirement. I did not verify pool reset and recycle state-machine concurrency in depth: concurrent reset_asset for the same canister is only noted, not proven. Group provisioning (workflow/component_provisioning.rs), the fleet_subnet_root retirement driver, core replay and authorize internals, placement workflows, and all PocketIC and integration tests were not reviewed. The IC behaviour of uninstalling a canister that runs out of cycles was applied from platform knowledge, not checked in code. Nothing was built or run, because this was a read-only review.

Fleet coordinator: deployment ledger, provisioning validation, progress and reconciliation, root deletion, service publication

cp-fleet-coordinator4 high5 medium3 low1 info

The Fleet Coordinator keeps one stable-cell record: the canonical Fleet Registry, every join, activation, admission, service-publication and lifecycle receipt, the Component provisioning and scale-out journals, the deployment ledger, and the root removal and deletion history. A second cell holds the funding ledger. Every command and query calls `current()`, which clones the whole record and validates all of it. That includes replaying join and registry-lifecycle history, recomputing the canonical version hash for each historical snapshot, and re-deriving the deployment ledger. Transitions are compare-and-swap commits of the complete record. Multi-step work (admission, funding-policy rotation, Component provisioning, root removal) is driven by self-rescheduling lifecycle timers. Each step writes a durable intent before it calls a Root, then records the Root's authenticated response. Single-operation code quality is high. Intents come before effects. Retries and replays compare exact identities. Receipts are hash-bound. Root-side cycle acceptance is atomic, and replays accept zero cycles. The main risks are in how operations interact and in the recovery paths. (1) The root-removal timer uses the Registry version captured at reservation time as its compare-and-swap version. Any unrelated Registry revision therefore wedges that removal permanently, along with all admission mutations. Such revisions include a second removal, a scale-out publication, a funding rotation, or an admission change. (2) A root reservation during an active Component operation wedges that operation's service publication. (3) The funding-rotation fence applies to the whole Fleet and cannot be aborted. It deadlocks with any Root that has an unresolved local funding request, which freezes all Root funding and all Registry commits. (4) Several operations whose Root call or Ledger transfer failed have no abort or re-plan path: removal reservations, retirement transfers, and funding grants that failed on reconcile. All the timer loops retry forever at a fixed 1 s interval, so every wedge keeps burning treasury cycles. Cost and exposure: whole-record validation grows quadratically with root count and linearly with history. Queries run it two to three times and updates at least twice. It will hit IC instruction limits well below the declared 4,096-root and 4,096-admission-publication bounds, and history is append-only. The Coordinator's `inspect_message` accepts ingress from any caller, including multi-MiB controller-only payloads and root-only variants. Anonymous senders can therefore make the Fleet treasury pay ingress-induction fees and full validation on every message.

Strengths
  • Intent-before-effect journaling on every Root effect: `advance_component_provisioning_root_acceptance` and `advance_component_provisioning_root` commit `in_flight` intents before the call (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:850-867, 978-1001), and `prepare_root_funding` persists `current` before the attached-cycles call (root_funding.rs:187-199).
  • Stable commits are compare-and-swap against the exact prior record, which prevents lost updates across awaits and interleaved timer loops (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:810-829, 751-770).
  • Root-side grant acceptance does not await between `msg_cycles_accept` and receipt persistence, traps if persistence fails, and replays with zero accepted cycles (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:189-216), as design 0.108 requires.
  • Root-deletion lifecycle records are hash-bound, canonically ordered and exact-retry only, and the retained-cycle target is bounded by the freezing reserve plus an execution reserve (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_coordinator/root_deletion/mod.rs:485-529, 544-745).
  • Endpoint authorization is enforced before dispatch. Controller commands check `is_controller` first. Root funding callers are matched against raw Registry membership before any treasury read, and anonymous callers and the Coordinator itself are rejected (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/fleet_coordinator.rs:74-102; root_funding.rs:67-89).
  • Retirement requires every root to be Removed with a deletion receipt, requires exact asset-recipient ownership, and puts the transfer under a value-transfer cost guard (ops/fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:182-219; workflow/fleet_coordinator/retirement/mod.rs:56-75).
  • Scale-out reserves its placement ordinals before any effect, and every read validates the deployment ledger against a full replay of history (deployment_ledger/mod.rs:126-168, 337-391).
Not covered

These parts were only spot-checked or grepped: the 2,022-line component_provisioning_validation module, most of component_provisioning_directory and component_provisioning_projection, the scale-out directory synchronization and publication validators, and the deployment_ledger tests. Most of the 7,065-line workflow tests file was not read; only the reservation and removal tests were. Root-side counterparts (root_funding ops, fleet_subnet_root removal, admission participant code) were read only as far as needed to confirm or refute Coordinator-side hypotheses. I did not read the 0.110 design doc in depth. Instruction-count claims come from code structure (quadratic join replay, per-point full-registry hashing, repeated `current()`). They were not measured. IC ingress fee figures and the refund behaviour of bounded-wait calls with attached cycles come from IC pricing and spec knowledge, not from code in the repo. Nothing was built or run.

Canister pool, component provisioning, templates, wasm store, fixture store and grants

cp-pool-provisioning2 high4 medium2 low

This unit covers Root's prepaid Canister pool and the Store's executable-template and fixture storage. On the Root side, a durable asset table moves each canister through PendingReset/Ready/Claimed/Workload/Recycling/Failed/HandingOff. Refill goes through the Cycles Ledger with deduplication on created_at_time. Recycling runs grant revocation, then stop, controller reset, uninstall_code and a cycle observation. Reviewed capacity import is a separate intent-before-effect journal. On the Store side, template chunk sets are hash-bound before any upload, and every chunk is verified on write and again on read. Fixture sources are content-addressed and uploaded in sequence under an exact byte ledger. Target grants are compare-and-set revisions that the Store checks against the exact caller Principal on every read. Store GC is a one-way state machine tied to one operation ID. Cycle reclamation only happens from an empty, GC-complete Store and only to the authenticated Root. The code is careful and heavily fenced. Admission is mostly all-or-nothing before any write, retries are exact, and lost responses are reconciled by observation. Module-hash verification before install is sound: Root supplies the payload hash from its own protected release set, and the IC's install_chunked_code enforces it. The Store's catalog is never trusted for that hash. Chunked upload integrity and fixture read authorization held up under review. The main risks sit in the recycling state machine, where ordinary histories leave assets or the whole maintenance loop stuck. (1) Grant revocation rejects the retained disabled tombstone of a previous allocation. A canister that served a fixture role and is later reused by a non-fixture role can then never be recycled again. Because that conflict is classed as an invariant failure, it also turns off the pool maintenance timer. (2) Recycling completion is made idempotent by comparing only the component ID. One component's children share that ID, so a second recycle of the same asset under the same component silently does nothing. The asset stays in Recycling forever and Root's final inventory can never pass. (3) A transient management-call failure during a recycle reset becomes a terminal Failed state. Because the asset still carries its old cycles value, every retry takes the non-destructive Reinspect path and can never uninstall. Secondary issues: recycling does not check for or clear canister snapshots, which uninstall does not erase and which backups create and never delete. Also, a pending refill is bound to live fee values, and an unresolved refill has no way out; either can permanently block pool maintenance and Root retirement.

Strengths
  • Chunk-set metadata is immutable once prepared: a changed re-preparation is rejected as a conflict, and exact retries keep the original timestamp and uploaded chunks (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/storage/template/chunked.rs:251-257). Every write is hash-verified (536-562), and every read re-verifies the chunk hash (386-391).
  • Combined preparation plus first-chunk admission projects every capacity limit before any write, and commits happen with no await in between (ops/storage/template/chunked.rs:269-295).
  • Install hash authority stays with Root: resolved_root_store_module_source passes Root's own release-set payload_hash to install_chunked_code, so a Store or installation controller cannot substitute a different module (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/mod.rs:62-98).
  • Fixture reads require the exact target Principal and the full current enabled grant revision. The check is repeated at the read boundary and closes once Store GC is prepared (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fixture_store/mod.rs:138-162).
  • The fixture byte ledger is exact: projected bytes are computed before mutation and committed together with the entries, and clearing removes one bounded entry at a time with its exact charge (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/fixture_store/mod.rs:126-180).
  • Recycling revokes the Store grant before reset and re-validates the pending recycling claim and Root authority after each Store await (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/fixture/mod.rs:33-70). Each destructive management call is fenced on that same claim (workflow/canister_pool/mod.rs:669-688).
  • Reviewed capacity import is rigorous: intent is recorded before each effect, controller and uninstall effects are confirmed from exact canister history, non-zero snapshots are rejected, and paid calls are bounded against a debit ceiling (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/capacity_import/mod.rs:262-494, 804-846, 931-971).
  • Refill never invents a new paid request after an uncertain Cycles Ledger outcome; it reuses created_at_time for deduplication and blocks terminally only after the ledger window closes (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/refill.rs:138-177, 322-338).
Not covered

Only read in part: the full RootComponentProvisioningOps state machine (ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs, about 3.5k lines), especially the publication and activation validators and failure/mod.rs. Only skimmed: the component-provisioning and fixture-store unit tests, capacity_import/history decoding, and storage/stable/canister_pool/capacity_import. Root-side Store publication and rotation workflows (workflow/runtime/template/publication) and the Root driver's retry cadence for GC Complete requests are outside these paths and were not traced. Fleet-activation and RPC capability verification behind StoreCommand::RespondCapability, ActivateFleet and SynchronizeState were not assessed. The claim that uninstall_code keeps snapshots rests on the repo's own design note (0.110-design.md:180), not on independent checking against the IC specification. Instruction counts are estimates only; nothing was measured. No code was run.

Root admission, root funding, fleet admission, registry mirror, service peers, ledger retirement, root status

cp-root-admission-funding5 high2 medium1 low

This unit covers the Root side of Coordinator-backed funding (0.108), the Root side of fleet-wide ingress admission (0.109), the Root Registry mirror, cross-root service-peer resolution, Root ledger retirement and the consolidated Root status lane. Root funding works as a single-slot journal: the Root persists request N with an ID derived from its identity before calling the Coordinator. The Coordinator attaches the grant to an AcceptFunding call, which the Root validates and accepts in one message with no await, then commits a receipt or traps. Replays accept zero and return the stored receipt. Root admission is a durable journal driven by timers (reserve/release, fence, activate, open) over the Root's participant catalog. The Registry mirror stores one validated Coordinator snapshot. The code is careful: every read revalidates the whole stored state, commits are compare-and-swap, and callers are authenticated at the endpoint against the exact protected Coordinator. The main risks are in liveness across the Root/Coordinator protocol, not in local state handling. (1) Root mirrors are only refreshed by component-publication, rotation and draining flows. After a routine admission mutation raises the Coordinator Registry revision, every Root's funding request is rejected as RegistryStale, which the Root treats as a terminal Stop. The same stale version also makes funding-policy rotation impossible to prepare. (2) Funding-policy rotation cannot be aborted. While it runs, the Coordinator rejects even exact replays of already-decided Root requests. A Root with an unresolved request therefore can never prepare, which deadlocks the Coordinator: Registry commits, grants and snapshots are all fenced. (3) Root ledger retirement stores an immutable transfer intent and then requires an exactly-zero balance. Dust at or below the fee, a later third-party deposit, or a retry after the ledger's 24-hour window wedges Root deletion permanently. A Root stuck in Draining blocks every future admission mutation and rotation for the whole Fleet. (4) Every Coordinator retry of an in-progress admission phase starts a new self-rescheduling Root timer chain. At the Coordinator's 1 Hz retry cadence this hits ic-timers' 64-registration limit. After that, Root lifecycle scheduling traps and duplicate target calls burn cycles. Secondary issues: the Coordinator grants cycles through bounded-wait calls, so the full-refund replay path can burn a whole grant when a response is lost. A designed, harmless Root rejection (balance already relieved) stops the Root top-up timer. Admission journal revalidation costs O(participants x principals) per load, which puts the status query and per-step convergence at risk of instruction limits at the documented maximums. Two mirror commits after awaits lack compare-and-swap. No authentication bypass, double acceptance, or double grant under retries was found on the Root side: exact-sequence, exact-request and phase checks hold.

Strengths
  • Intent before effect: RootFundingOps::prepare_request commits the exact request (sequence-derived operation ID) before any outbound call, and request_coordinator refuses any request that does not exactly equal the durable current one (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/root_funding/mod.rs:81-106, crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:173-183).
  • Atomic acceptance: validation, msg_cycles_accept and receipt commit run in one message with no await, and a failed commit after acceptance traps so the cycles are refunded (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:189-222).
  • Exact replay: an existing GrantAccepted or terminal Granted receipt is returned while accepting zero, and the per-Root operation sequence is strictly monotonic (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/root_funding/mod.rs:392-396, 587-592, 732-750).
  • Every read of the funding and admission journals fully revalidates the stored state against protected authority, and all commits are compare-and-swap on the exact expected record (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/root_funding/mod.rs:161-179, crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/root_admission/mod.rs:702-739).
  • Endpoint authentication binds AcceptFunding, the rotation commands and the admission phases to the exact protected Coordinator and rejects anonymous callers (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:274-293, crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:41-48).
  • Admission catalog reservation can be released before any target effect, and every retained hash is re-derived on load (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/root_admission/mod.rs:598-627, 842-979).
  • Mirror activation re-reads and reclassifies the active mirror after its awaits and enforces monotonic revisions under the same authority (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:258-275, 654-675).
  • Service-peer resolution requires a unique Registry service membership for the raw caller, a remote and Active owner Root, and an exact topology binding (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fleet_service_peer/mod.rs:36-96).
Not covered

Coordinator-side state machines (fleet_coordinator funding_rotation and root_funding ops, admission.rs) were read only far enough to confirm cross-protocol behaviour. The canic-core cycle top-up workflow and async-job claim internals were read only for the Root funding classification. The ic-timers trap/rollback semantics (whether a trapped lifecycle callback leaks its registration) were not verified. The IC bounded-wait refund-loss semantics behind finding 5 are stated from platform knowledge and not tested. Coordinator-side validation helpers in ops/fleet_admission/mod.rs:741-1070 and the CLI admission planner were only skimmed. PocketIC tests were only skimmed for coverage; no code was executed (read-only review). The rest of component_registry root_retirement, beyond the ledger-transfer intent, belongs to other units.

Control-plane runtime workflows, bootstrap, API, DTO/view, state and storage layout

cp-runtime-api1 high1 medium7 low2 info

This unit covers the root control-plane runtime. The root command, status and operation-status endpoints are emitted by crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs and delegate to api::lifecycle::LifecycleApi. Behind that API sit the Fleet activation wrapper (workflow/runtime/fleet_activation), the root bootstrap (workflow/bootstrap/root.rs) and the one-shot BootstrapStore/fixture flow (workflow/bootstrap/root_store). Store publication has two parts: catalog import and binding pinning, and the final-inventory GC, reclamation, binding finalization and physical deletion state machine (workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs). The unit also includes the Fleet-state fanout (workflow/state), the root-owned Store state cell (storage/stable/state/root_wasm_store.rs plus its ops facade), and the state-contract descriptors. Overall quality is high. Most effects follow intent-before-effect. Durable state transitions check generations and monotonicity. Store deletion checks the exact module hash and controllers, requires no reserved cycles, and records typed absence. Store client responses are matched by operation ID. Today every one of the 41 RootCommand variants has an authorization rule. Most in-memory guards release correctly under ic-cdk 0.20 cleanup. The main risks are liveness and cost, not direct authorization bypass. (1) The Store-deletion step fails permanently when anyone deposits cycles into the Store after the deletion intent is durable. Because the intent is immutable, root retirement wedges and the root's remaining cycles stay stranded. (2) The root's inspect_message accepts unauthenticated ingress up to the platform maximum for a variant that only the Coordinator canister can use. (3) Running the init bootstrap again on an already-ready root silently resets the reported bootstrap readiness. It also makes PrepareFleetActivation return `unavailable` instead of replaying. (4) root_store::status re-downloads, re-hashes and re-parses the full release-set manifest (up to 16 MiB) on every per-member provisioning step. Smaller issues: the post-upgrade bootstrap runs once with no retry, the authority-snapshot timer suspension is ordered before the await, the root subnet identity is never checked against the protected placement subnet, the root command authorization classification is default-open, and some storage metadata is inaccurate.

Strengths
  • Store physical deletion is a lineage-validated, intent-before-effect state machine: exact module hash and controller-set checks, reserved-cycles rejection, bounded retained-cycle target, and completion only on typed live absence (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs:575-623, 818-864, 1019-1078).
  • Every RootCommand variant currently has an explicit authorization rule: a controller list, Coordinator/admission/funding predicates, component-member and capability predicates, plus separate authority-restore and Fleet-activation fences (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:223-397).
  • The BootstrapStore manifest check rejects non-canonical JSON by round-trip comparison, verifies the digest, checks the exact topology projection with ordered entries, rejects conflicting duplicate artifacts, and applies overflow-checked byte totals (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/bootstrap/root_store/mod.rs:139-252).
  • Publication-binding transitions assert a single generation increment and slot distinctness. GC reconciliation is monotonic and validated (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/state/root_wasm_store.rs:181-304, 591-685).
  • fixture::prepare re-checks the protected root authority and store-admin-open state after its awaits, before issuing the Store effect (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/bootstrap/root_store/fixture/mod.rs:44-48).
  • Store client effect adapters match response variants and operation IDs exactly. Publication effects require an unforgeable CostGuardPermit threaded from reservation (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/client/mod.rs:129-148; publication/cost_guard.rs:38-86).
  • The authority-snapshot resume traps inside the same execution as the core fence opening, so a failure to rebuild the pool timer leaves authority sealed rather than half-open (crates/canic-control-plane/src/api/lifecycle.rs:167-182).
Not covered

Read deeply: the root endpoint macro, api/lifecycle.rs, fleet_activation, bootstrap/root.rs, root_store and fixture, the publication modules (mod, store, lifecycle/*, release/*, snapshot, cost_guard, client), workflow/state, stable and ops root_wasm_store state, ids, state_contract.rs, config.rs, schema.rs, lib.rs, runtime/*, transient storage, and allocation_tests. Only skimmed: ops/storage/template/mod.rs and chunked.rs (Store-side staging and publish mutation paths), dto/template, publication/error.rs and metrics.rs, ops/storage/state/mapper.rs, and view/* (view/component_registry is about 1,000 lines of plain structs, not audited field by field). Not audited: dto/fleet_coordinator.rs in depth. Followed callers only far enough to confirm or refute hypotheses: component_registry seal/converge inventory, fleet_subnet_root removal steps other than store deletion and prepare_deletion, root_status, canister_pool, and the canic-core fleet activation, authority restore and bootstrap status. Cycle and instruction magnitudes are estimates from IC fee schedules and code shape; nothing was run or measured. Whether the IC's management chunk store can lose chunks after bootstrap (no repair path exists) was not established.

Fleet ensure: reinstall, root reinstall, clean reinstall, completed reset and preparation

host-ensure-reinstall2 high4 medium1 low

This unit covers the host-side reset lanes of `fleet ensure`. There are four of them. (1) Clean reinstall (workflow/ops clean_reinstall) is the maintained pre-1.0 release transition. It retires and archives the completed operation, surveys current custody, reinstalls the Coordinator, Root and Store through the infrastructure-bootstrap journal, clears the held Root children through a reviewed capacity import on the new Root, and then converges fresh workloads with an ordinary Full plan. Its terminal receipt allows offline replay. (2) The Root reinstall prerequisite (policy/workflow root_reinstall) runs Stop → [Fund] → Install(Reinstall) → Start on a running Root whose module differs. An ordinary `fleet ensure` can produce it. (3) The activation-reset lane (policy/workflow reinstall/activation plus ops/reinstall/source and adoption) repairs a partial activation through an unfunded preparation followed by a Root reset. (4) Older completed-source lanes: the `plan_reinstall` completed/terminal-retirement branches, completed_preparation, completed_reset and generate/completed_source. Local durability is carefully built. Retirement and adoption archive exact bytes as content-addressed objects before any replacement or removal, and they are resumable. Effects record intent before issue. Reinstall lost responses are reconciled through a Root history witness. The Root prerequisite requires the exact management binding and a Stopped Root before paying or installing. The clean-reinstall terminal receipt is bound to the plan, the normalized journal, the state and the selection digests. The main risks are about which state the tool trusts: - **Estate completeness:** both the clean reinstall and the Root prerequisite wipe the Root's registry without proving that the import set covers every canister the Root controls. The clean lane archives and deletes the last terminal inventory without comparing it. Generation skips its live pool check whenever the Root module changes, which is the normal release case. The Root prerequisite checks only stale host state. Assets the operator left out of the seed, or created by Root refill after the last ensure, are silently stranded. - **Selection logic:** the persistent clean-reinstall.json keeps capturing later ordinary operations. It routes them to the frozen reset desired, so ordinary desired changes after a completed reset cannot be applied, and a new `--reinstall` does not start. Separately, the clean-reinstall review never checks that the shared journal belongs to the current plan, so an unapplied workload phase can be reported as `fleet_completed: true`. - **Obsolete lanes:** the completed-preparation/reset lanes are now unreachable from the CLI, but their leftover journal still gates `lock_operation` and clean retirement. Their only consumer rejects reviews made by another CLI version, so a Fleet prepared under 0.110.44 is wedged under 0.110.46. - **Pre-effect selection files:** several are written create-once before they are validated, so a correctable operator mistake becomes permanent.

Strengths
  • Activation-reset adoption archives byte-exact source plan/journal/state and the replacement before a two-file replace; recovery accepts either the before or after digest per file and completes idempotently (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/reinstall/adoption/mod.rs:65-181).
  • Completed-operation retirement snapshots every Fleet file as content-addressed objects, rehashes sources before publishing the manifest, and removes only files whose bytes still match the archive, never the lock (ops/operation_selection/archive/mod.rs:30-83; ops/operation_selection/retirement/mod.rs:146-223).
  • Root reinstall prerequisite orders Stop before any credit or install, requires the exact management binding with the Root observed Stopped for Fund/Install, keeps the original Ledger withdrawal identity on retry, and returns typed headroom errors (workflow/root_reinstall/mod.rs:263-350; policy/root_reinstall/mod.rs:126-175).
  • Lost-response reconciliation of reinstalls uses a Root history witness and admits the replacement binding only for the Root's own pending Intent/Issued reinstall with the target module (policy/reinstall/mod.rs:466-615).
  • Clean-reinstall terminal receipt binds plan, normalized journal, state and selection digests and re-verifies reviewed conservation bounds, enabling effect-free offline replay (ops/clean_reinstall/terminal/mod.rs:51-158).
  • Certified custody reads use read_state certificates with a delegation-derived subnet, strict CBOR controller decoding and duplicate/empty rejection (ops/reinstall/terminal/inventory/custody/mod.rs:168-185, 305-342).
  • Activation reset re-inventories the complete physical estate before its Stop while the Root still runs, and verifies preparation evidence byte-exactly before the Root reset (workflow/reinstall/activation/mod.rs:180-196, 336-369).
  • External retirement debits are authenticated through replicated reads with a strict ICRC-3 burn-block shape, bounded CBOR memo and destination-controller check (ops/reinstall/debit/mod.rs:77-230).
Not covered

Not read in depth: ops/reinstall/terminal/{documents, receipt_audit, inventory/ledger, parentage, coordinator, protocols}; adoption/publication/archive; the full test files. Capacity import and infrastructure-bootstrap internals, which other units own, were followed only where clean reinstall depends on them (custody survey, declarations, convergence handoff). The generic effect driver in workflow/mod.rs and the platform adapters (observe_effect/apply for Install, SealAuthority and Stop) were sampled, not audited. I did not check whether the IC chunk store, snapshots or logs survive the reinstall/uninstall paths. Nothing was executed; every finding is static code tracing. Finding confidence depends on runtime facts I did not confirm: whether reinstall-lane successors can create canisters, and whether Root refill runs between terminal ensures.

Fleet ensure: startup funding, funding observation, operator mint, balance observation

host-ensure-funding3 high2 medium2 low

This unit covers the host-side Fleet Ensure funding machinery. There are four parts. Supplementary Root funding reviews come in two kinds: Estate (FundEstate, an icrc1_transfer into the Root's Cycles Ledger account) and Native (Fund, a Cycles Ledger withdraw that tops up the Root canister). Operator ICP-to-cycles conversion (operator mint) runs an ICP transfer, then CMC notify_mint_cycles, then an authenticated Cycles Ledger deposit. The bounded descendant funding-observation pass is the third part. The fourth is the advisory startup-funding forecast. Every paid effect keeps its intent in the local journal before submission and reuses one fixed ledger dedup identity (created_at_time, amount, account) across retries. The code adopts Duplicate replies as receipts. Journal verification rebuilds every review, digest and authority binding from the retained plan. Receipt authentication for mints is thorough: a certified replicated ICP block read with exact protobuf field matching, and a certified-tip hash chain to a memo-bound deposit block. Arithmetic is checked everywhere and the unit conversions are correct. One e8 at xdr_permyriad_per_icp yields exactly rate cycles, and the CMC subaccount and account-id derivation match upstream. The main weakness is liveness, not theft. In several places the design freezes a review or intent and admits no replacement path. Stale ledger timestamps are persisted into irreversible intents without a freshness check. A credited operator mint freezes its Estate or Native funding review: there is no refresh and no second conversion, and the quote has no rate-slippage margin. Deposit verification only works while the Cycles Ledger tip is within 1024 blocks of the deposit. Unapproved Estate reviews cannot be refreshed after any Root-account balance change, even though the Native path has exactly this refresh. Reconciliation of retained withdrawals relies on exact equality of the operator's shared default-account balance. Concurrent activity breaks that equality, and so does a FailedToWithdraw fee-only debit. Each of these can wedge a retained operation permanently. verify_journal then fences both plan and apply behind the unresolved record, so the Fleet cannot be managed through Canic without manual journal surgery. No double-funding or cycle-theft path was found in these paths. Retries reuse identical ledger arguments, CMC notification is bound to an authenticated block, and duplicate ICP and deposit receipts are rejected. Cycle losses on failure paths are bounded to single ledger fees. The residual risks are operational: an ordinary delay, a rate move, a network interruption or a third-party ledger transfer can leave the operation unrecoverable. The documentation acknowledges some of these cases ("expired identities", "over-budget receipt history ... remain unresolved"), but none has a supported recovery.

Strengths
  • Intent is persisted before every paid submission, and retries reuse the exact ledger identity. Estate: crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/funding/mod.rs:396-401 and 420-424. Native: workflow/funding/native/mod.rs:547-555. Mint: approve() persists the transfer bytes before transport.transfer in workflow/operator_mint/execution/mod.rs:104-116.
  • ICP transfer receipts are authenticated through a certified replicated query_encoded_blocks read. The code checks a canonical prost round-trip and compares from, to, amount, fee, memo and created_at_time exactly (ops/operator_mint/receipts/icp/mod.rs:239-289 and 359-415). The archive redirect is limited to one hop (transport/mod.rs:274-293).
  • The deposit memo is a domain-separated hash over the operation, plan, funding-review and network identities, the four principals and the amounts (ops/operator_mint/mod.rs:208-238). admit_receipt rejects reuse of an ICP block or deposit block across admitted mints (policy/operator_mint/mod.rs:88-104).
  • Journal integrity rebuilds each funding review from the plan authority, the pause record and the digest. It does not trust stored digests (workflow/funding/mod.rs:82-90, workflow/funding/native/mod.rs:164-197, workflow/funding/operator/mod.rs:63-83).
  • An unapproved Native quote is refreshed on a disposable journal copy, and an approved intent never enters that path (workflow/funding/native/mod.rs:357-371).
  • The funding-observation pass persists each attempt before its paid Root commands, and an interrupted attempt counts as consumed rather than inferred unpaid (workflow/funding_observation/mod.rs:113-123 and 147-154; ops/funding_observation/validation/mod.rs:41-49).
  • Checked u128 arithmetic is used consistently. The advisory quote rounds up correctly: one e8 at a permyriad rate equals rate cycles (policy/operator_mint/quote/mod.rs:15-25). The startup forecast uses checked add and multiply (policy/startup_funding/mod.rs:276-288).
  • The CMC mint account derivation matches upstream: the principal subaccount has a length prefix, the account identifier is CRC32 plus SHA-224, and the memo is MINT (ops/operator_mint/mod.rs:21 and 240-259).
Not covered

I did not read ops/operator_mint/receipts/test_support and the icp/tests directory, ops/startup_funding/observation/inventory/pages, or the policy/startup_funding allowance, local_demand and live_binding modules in detail. Most of the *_tests files I only skimmed. I did not audit terminal conservation or estate_funding_requirement in workflow/mod.rs beyond the call sites relevant here, because the cycles lens covers them. I did not assess the runtime-side grant semantics in canic-core that the startup forecast models. I did not assess whether the plan's own original Fund, FundEstate and Create actions have the same stale-timestamp exposure; they probably do, since apply() takes no timestamp. Fleet ensure: capacity import, current inventory, infrastructure bootstrap, independent effects

host-ensure-capacity4 high4 medium1 low1 info

This unit is the host side of supplied-capacity enrollment. `fleet import` works in stages. The review captures certified custody plus one paid management sample per source and for the Root. Samples are keyed durably by a request digest and are never rebased. Declarations are bound byte for byte, and each observation is checked against the exact current Registry and every Root pool page. Apply then approves on fresh observations, has Root reserve an allocation fence, and gives each operator-held source a pre-signed update_settings envelope (retained before submission, reconciled only through certified request_status). Root is then driven through stop/controllers/uninstall/settle. The two generator inputs are published as a paired write, and the fence is released last. `fleet bootstrap` surveys explicitly supplied infrastructure, compiles a Coordinator-first, reinstall-only plan through the ordinary Ensure driver, retains a terminal receipt and publishes the estate seed. The initial held import then reuses the bootstrap samples as its immutable baselines. The independent-effects and bounded-observation helpers run up to 4 Store-chunk/pool-reconcile effects or reads at once. They persist every intent first and join every worker. Local integrity is strong. Every record is re-validated on read and save, transitions are enforced to be monotonic, envelopes are decoded and their request IDs recomputed, and adoption requires that the operator is a controller (or that Root already is) and that custody is certified. I found no path that adopts a canister the operator does not control. The main risk is liveness and recovery. Every retry allowance is small (2 submissions per step, 4 inspections per canister) and is spent before local prechecks. There is no abort or cancel command on the host or on Root. An approved, unfinished journal blocks every Fleet Ensure, reset and new import (lock_operation / lock_completed_source), and once reserved, Root fences all pool, allocation, provisioning and retirement work. Several ordinary failures therefore become permanent wedges with no supported recovery: transient query errors, a slow stop, a handoff interrupted for more than about 5 minutes (the 240 s ingress expiry plus IC reply pruning), and any cycle credit to a source or Root, which anyone can cause with deposit_cycles. Other defects: - The bootstrap-initial import pins bootstrap-time balances and bootstrap never checks pool headroom, so an underfunded pool or a later top-up can hold a Root fenced forever. - Capacity import breaks permanently once any Root has been Removed from the Registry. - The inventory check demands that every Root in the fleet be quiet (and rejects Failed assets) during each paid observation. - A bootstrap review cannot be retried after a failed first attempt, because the plan hash depends on the current time. - Imported canisters keep their prior compute/memory allocation, freezing and log-visibility settings.

Strengths
  • Intent-before-effect and monotonic persistence: CapacityImportJournalStore::save re-validates and require_monotonic forbids rebasing cycle baselines, dropping Issued intent or rewriting approval/reservation (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/capacity_import/journal/store/mod.rs:157-168, 265-325).
  • The exact signed ingress is retained and validated. The CBOR envelope is decoded with a recursion limit, the request ID is recomputed, and sender, target, method, argument and expiry are all bound before any resubmission (ops/capacity_import/transport/mod.rs:219-270, 296-331).
  • Controller verification is layered. The operator must be a controller unless Root already is (policy/capacity_import/mod.rs:155-162). Review compares certified custody with declared controllers and module (ops/capacity_import/admission/review/mod.rs:364-409). Every paid status sample is bracketed by certified read_state custody reads (admission/observer/management/mod.rs:145-187).
  • Rejection is only accepted as a non-serializable certified witness. Renewal requires fresh, unchanged custody and rejects reused request IDs (ops/capacity_import/transport/rejection/mod.rs:23-68; journal/rejection/mod.rs:72-122).
  • Pool inventory reads are complete and stable: each page is bounded, the cursor is monotonic, the summary is checked for stability, and Store uniqueness and counts are enforced (admission/observer/inventory/mod.rs:185-246). Root re-checks pool and component membership at reserve time as defence in depth.
  • Paired generator-input publication is recoverable. Before/after hashes are bound in the review, intent is persisted before writes, and a partial write of either file is accepted only if it matches the exact original or replacement (ops/capacity_import/publication/mod.rs:353-414).
  • The size preflight require_completion_fits reserves worst-case journal size before approval, so a small record cannot strand a paid effect later (journal/store/mod.rs:185-263).
  • The bounded parallel helpers drain every worker, even after a failure or panic, and persist all intents before submission. Every outcome and observation is retained in plan order (ops/bounded_observations/mod.rs:11-37; ops/independent_effects/mod.rs:56-72; workflow/independent_effects/mod.rs:44-121).
Not covered

- ops/current_inventory/mod.rs (3038 lines): only terminal_inventory, query_entries, append_pool_assets, the descendant observation and query_all_children were read closely. The component-partition and provisioning-status validators (lines ~661-1257) and the embedded tests were only skimmed, and ordinary/mod.rs was only partly read. - Not read: generate/*/tests.rs, most capacity-import unit tests, model/infrastructure_bootstrap, view/*, and ops/current_inventory/tests. - Root/control-plane import semantics were read only as far as needed to confirm host-side scenarios (the reserve_call credit rejection, the execution guard, the Stopping conflict, the absence of an abort command). Root-side correctness itself belongs to another unit. - IC timing facts were not reproduced: that terminal ingress statuses are pruned about 5 minutes after completion and that expired envelopes are refused. - Whether later workload allocation normalizes inherited canister settings was not traced beyond a grep. - Parallel icp-CLI invocation with encrypted identities was not assessed. - Nothing was executed; all findings come from reading code.

Fleet ensure: top-level workflow, continuation, current protocol, init, authority seal, plan content, operation selection, readiness, model/dto/json/view/generate

host-ensure-core1 high3 medium4 low1 info

Fleet ensure is a host-side, file-journaled reconciler. `plan` locks the Fleet directory, observes the live estate, compiles an immutable plan and writes `plan.json`. The plan digest is a domain-separated SHA-256 of the canonical decimal-u128 JSON, and Store/fixture chunk bytes are moved out to content-addressed objects. `apply` checks the digest and the journal, and before the first effect it recompiles against fresh observation with the plan's frozen `planned_at_time`. It then writes an InProgress journal and drives `ordered_actions` plus retained successor phases one index at a time: it persists an Intent, observes, issues the effect, records Issued, and marks Applied only on a typed terminal observation. After all effects it replans once, read-only, and either appends a bounded protocol-only successor phase (retained under `phases/<digest>.json` before the journal refers to it) or verifies the terminal inventory and conservation, then publishes state and a Converged journal. Operation selection and clean-reinstall retirement read only completion envelopes. Before removing files, retirement archives the exact bytes into `history/`. Code quality is high. Invariants are enforced by named predicates, typed errors, bounded reads, create-new object semantics and consistent intent-before-effect ordering. Continuation is carefully bounded by action count and burn. The main risks are liveness and operability problems at the journal boundary, not missing checks. (1) The InProgress journal is created before the first Cycles Ledger call, but Ledger `created_at_time` values are frozen at review time. A plan applied more than 24h after review, or a lost Ledger reply resumed after the window, can never progress, and the workflow offers no supported way out. (2) Any unrelated operator-account activity during an in-progress operation makes terminal conservation and funding reviews fail permanently. The error tells the operator to "review a new plan", which planning refuses while the journal is InProgress. (3) An ordinary no-effect review over a completed Fleet overwrites `plan.json` without archiving it. That cuts the Converged journal off from its plan, so completion selection, clean-reinstall selection, `--reinstall` and completed replay all stop working. The TerminalReplayBalanceChanged message itself tells operators to do exactly this. Efficiency is the other real concern. Plan read and write round-trip every inline chunk byte through `serde_json::Value`, a roughly 32x memory blow-up that grows with release size and number of Roots. The clean-reinstall archive has a hard 256 MiB cap, far below the publication capacity a plan allows. Smaller issues: a seal-replay retry hint that the executor rejects as JournalIntegrity, ProvisionComponents replays that are unbounded across invocations and reset the stall budget, and a clean-reinstall terminal receipt that binds a state digest which a failed read-only plan can change.

Strengths
  • Intent-before-effect is consistent: prepare_effect's record is pushed and write_journal'd before any observation or issuance (workflow/mod.rs:1486-1495), and Issued/Applied transitions are each persisted before state publication; Applied create/funding authority is re-derived idempotently on resume (workflow/mod.rs:1511-1530).
  • Paid retry bounds are durable: fixture publication attempts are reserved and journalled before the external call (workflow/mod.rs:1696-1706, ops/mod.rs:919-930), and pool maintenance attempts are persisted before each update (workflow/mod.rs:1739-1747); EffectRecord::attempts_match re-validates them on every journal load (model/mod.rs:1341-1356).
  • Plan digest binding is canonical and domain-separated (policy/mod.rs:3735-3744); verified_plan also cross-checks scope vs infrastructure_bootstrap (workflow/mod.rs:4123-4134), and pre-first-effect recompilation uses the frozen planned_at_time and normalized comparison with bounded balance movement (workflow/mod.rs:2745-2851, 3377-3405).
  • Successor phases are immutable, digest-addressed and written before the journal exposes them (ops/continuation/mod.rs:218-233, workflow/continuation/mod.rs:296-299); verify_records re-proves digest, binding, protocol-only effects, uniqueness, monotone burn and the action ceiling on every load (workflow/continuation/mod.rs:43-104).
  • Content-addressed chunk retention validates size/hash on both write and read, rejects mixed inline/referenced projections and prepared-hash mismatches, and uses create-new with byte comparison (ops/plan_content/mod.rs:25-47, 120-137, 262-315).
  • Completion selection decodes only envelope fields, bounds reads to 32 MiB, refuses to treat a converged label with non-applied effects as history, and never retires a newer pending plan (ops/operation_selection/mod.rs:21-62); retirement removes only files whose bytes still match the archived digest and fsyncs before clearing its intent (ops/operation_selection/retirement/mod.rs:140-215).
  • Authority seal admits only the maintained Candid contract (ops/authority_seal/contract/mod.rs:32-67) and requires fence receipts to be complete or absent, rejecting a Sealed fence owned by a different operation (ops/authority_seal/mod.rs:136-181).
  • Every durable/report u128 is decimal text (json/mod.rs DecimalU128Serializer; model u128_text helpers), and report projection externalizes chunk payloads with exact path/hash/size (json/mod.rs:128-168).
Not covered

Only spot-checked ops/platform.rs (10k lines), for Create/Fund/Install observation and apply. Not reviewed: policy/mod.rs compile_plan internals; workflow/funding, independent_effects, reinstall (except plan_reinstall's entry), root_reinstall, infrastructure_bootstrap, capacity_import, completed_preparation/completed_reset; generate submodules (capacity_import, completed_source, infrastructure_bootstrap, startup_funding); view/terminal_source and model submodules beyond serde attributes; durable_io internals (atomic rename and fsync assumed as documented); CLI dispatch beyond run_ensure and clean_reinstall::selected. Nothing was executed, so the Cycles Ledger 24h window behaviour is inferred from the in-repo runtime's TX_WINDOW_NANOS/TooOld handling, not reproduced. Memory numbers assume serde_json::Value is at least 32 bytes per element.

Fleet ensure: platform effects layer (IC calls from the host)

host-ensure-platform3 high2 medium7 low

`IcpEnsurePlatform` (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs) is the production adapter behind the `EnsurePlatform` trait (ops/mod.rs:192-530). It does all IC reads and writes through the ICP CLI and ic-agent. Reads cover management status, Root `InspectCanister` updates, Root pool pages (authenticated queries), Cycles Ledger balance and fee queries, and declarative protocol status queries. Paid effects are Cycles Ledger `create_canister`, `withdraw` and `icrc1_transfer`, each with a fixed `created_at_time` and `Duplicate` receipt adoption. Management effects (install, settings update, start, stop, uninstall, delete) and the configured drain endpoint also go through here. `effect_preparation` captures fresh pre-balances and the canister version into an unpersisted intent. The workflow persists that intent, then calls `apply`. It resubmits any record still in `Intent` after a failed or lost call, and observes `Issued` records through `observe_effect` until a terminal predicate holds or the stall budget runs out. `protocol.rs` runs user-declared Candid transitions whose completion is a byte comparison of a query reply against an expected value. The code is careful overall. Observation snapshots are scoped and dropped before every effect. Pool inspections require exact Root-plus-recovery controllers, and only validated responses are cached. Pagination authority is checked for consistency across pages and against declared lifecycle totals. Batches are drained in order so error precedence is kept. Install preparation takes a fresh, dedicated status. Native funding completion requires a receipt but tolerates donations. Ledger duplicates are adopted as receipts. The main risks sit in the terminal predicates and in how Ledger outcomes are classified. The FundEstate and retirement-Transfer predicates demand exact balance deltas on accounts that are not quiescent: Root's own 30-second maintenance loop spends the Root Ledger account, and the treasury pays idle charges. After a lost reply, or just a slow observation, the paid effect can never be proven and the operation wedges. The documentation promises the opposite for FundEstate. Separately, paid Ledger effects take `created_at_time` from the plan clock. TooOld, FailedToCreate and FailedToWithdraw are collapsed into strings, and the host has no typed resolution when the 24-hour deduplication window expires, even though Root's own control plane models this case (UnresolvedAfterLedgerWindow). Ordinary observation also drops `reserved_cycles`, so Delete can destroy reserved balances outside the reviewed bound. Lesser issues: completion evidence that relies on uncertified queries or self-reported balances, lenient status parsing, a Wasm hash-then-reread gap, and misleading error variants.

Strengths
  • Every paid Cycles Ledger call carries a stable created_at_time and adopts Duplicate receipts on replay (platform.rs:2785-2789, 2824-2828, 5500-5507); Create additionally requires the created principal from the duplicate.
  • apply() and apply_independent_effects() drop the observation snapshot and staging cache and re-check the operator identity before any effect (platform.rs:4837-4840, 4813-4816); Install preparation uses its own fresh snapshot (3501-3514); pacing invalidates cached evidence (3616-3648).
  • Root-owned inspections require the exact Root plus recovery controller set and an empty module where appropriate (validate_root_controlled_inspection 5432-5476, validate_pending_fresh_pool_inspection 5398-5430); only validated responses enter the cache (2430-2439).
