Panics, traps and overflow (cross-cutting)

xc-robustness1 high3 low1 info

Canic's canister code is unusually defensive about panics and arithmetic. Amounts, times and counters are handled almost entirely with checked_* operations, fallible TryFrom conversions and typed errors. Nat-to-u128/u64 conversions return errors instead of truncating. The expect/unreachable sites I traced act on values validated earlier in the same synchronous span or on immutable local snapshots, so none of them can be reached by callers. Window divisions are guarded (window_secs == 0 is rejected by policy validation or special-cased). u32-to-usize casts are sound on wasm32. Stable-record decoding fails closed by design. Host code follows the same discipline: checked u128 cycle arithmetic, u128_text serde for journal amounts, and panic-draining thread collection. A grep-driven survey of about 1,500 unwrap/expect/panic/unreachable/as-cast/unchecked-operator sites across canic, canic-core, canic-control-plane, canic-macros, canic-host, canic-cli and canic-backup found no caller-reachable arithmetic overflow, truncating conversion or panic in paths that move cycles or ICP. The main robustness risk is at a boundary between crates: Canic and the external ic-timers crate. Every multi-await lifecycle driver (Component allocation, child allocation, Component and subtree removal, Root removal, Registry synchronization, Fleet admission, Root provisioning, non-root bootstrap) runs as a chain of ic-timers `Once` registrations. Each registration gets a fresh identity in a volatile registry capped at 64 entries, which it shares with about 10 fixed claims. `TimerApi::defer_lifecycle_required` traps whenever registration fails. Several drivers are not deduplicated, and exact command replays spawn extra chains. So ordinary concurrency or retries can fill the registry. Once it is full, both endpoint scheduling and in-callback rescheduling trap. ic-timers only completes (and so removes) a `Once` entry after the consumer future returns. A trap after an await (explicit `ic_cdk::trap`, an expect, or instruction exhaustion) therefore leaves the entry Running for good. That kills the driver, permanently uses up a registry slot, and makes the Root authority-snapshot precondition fail until the heap is reset. Smaller issues: generic endpoints and inspect_message decode untrusted Candid with only a skipping quota. The release profile disables overflow checks, so the few invariant-guarded unchecked operations would wrap silently rather than trap. Several singleton records declare fixed-size storable bounds on variable-length CBOR; this is harmless only because plain `Cell` ignores bounds.

Strengths
  • Cycle-amount parsing is exact and overflow-checked: `Cycles::from_str` rejects sub-cycle precision and uses checked_mul/checked_add (crates/canic-core/src/cdk/types/cycles.rs:263-351). Human config requires quoted unit strings, and float and integer forms are rejected (cycles.rs:147-187).
  • Cost-guard reservations are range-checked before any use: reservations above u64::MAX are rejected (crates/canic-core/src/ops/cost_guard.rs:309-311), and balance arithmetic saturates the safe way (cost_guard.rs:333-349).
  • Cycle acceptance is trap-atomic: `accept` calls `msg_cycles_accept` and commits the receipt in one synchronous span with no await, so a failed commit traps and refunds the attached cycles (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:190-218).
  • The raw update adapter checks `msg_arg_data_size` against the per-method limit before allocating or decoding (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:365-376). Delegated-token decoding sets a decoding quota, a max type length and terse errors (crates/canic-core/src/access/auth/token.rs:86-96).
  • Ledger and management Nat values go through fallible conversions: `CyclesLedgerOps::checked_cycles` / `checked_block_index` (crates/canic-core/src/ops/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:66-72) and `status_nat_as_u128` (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_subnet_root.rs:740-742).
  • Validated expects operate on immutable snapshots. For example, `delete_single_finalized_root_store` checks `require_durable_store_cycle_reclamation(intent)` before the later `.expect("validated Store cycle reclamation")` on the same borrowed intent (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs:575-620).
  • `BoundedCell` checks the complete encoding before writing and fails closed on reopen (crates/canic-core/src/cdk/bounded_cell/mod.rs:30-64). Fixture ingestion checks chunk index, length and hash before any cursor arithmetic (crates/canic-core/src/ops/fixture_content/mod.rs:15-67; crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/fixture_store/mod.rs:61-85).
  • Host conservation and funding math uses checked u128 arithmetic with typed Conservation errors (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/mod.rs:4093-4119). Parallel host observations drain every worker and re-raise panics deterministically (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/bounded_observations/mod.rs:11-37).
Not covered

Not audited line by line: every expect inside the 6k-line component_registry ops and storage modules and root_retirement.rs (I sampled them and confirmed they follow the synchronous validate-then-expect pattern). Not assessed: whether each public DTO admits a zero-width Candid element, so the decoding-bomb cost is not quantified. Not deeply reviewed: backup and restore journaling, the ic-memory crate, or the Coordinator-side drivers beyond scheduling structure. I did not measure realistic concurrent lifecycle-driver counts or instruction costs, and I did not check whether the CLI automatically re-sends RemoveComponent/RemoveSubtree/SynchronizeRegistry. No tests or builds were run (read-only lens).

Architecture and layering (cross-cutting)

xc-architecture2 medium5 low1 info

Canic's layering is enforced mostly by convention plus a grep-based guard (scripts/ci/run-layering-guards.sh), and inside canic-core it largely holds. I checked the use crate:: imports for every core layer. domain/policy/pure is pure: it imports no storage, ops, dto, serde, async or timers. model does not depend on dto, ops, workflow or storage. The only workflow-to-storage and ops-to-api references are in tests. DTOs carry no logic, no command DTO derives Default, and there are no boundary type aliases. Host-only dependencies (toml, serde_path_to_error, quote, ic-secp256k1) are gated to non-wasm32 targets, and no canister manifest pulls in host crates. The host crate's fleet_ensure tree has its own dto/model/ops/policy/workflow split, and its policy layer is pure too. The real architectural risks sit at the crate and macro boundaries, not inside layers. The wire contracts for root and managed commands exist only inside macro_rules! bodies in the facade. They have no canonical .did, and about 60 hand-written partial mirror enums (the *Fragment and Remote* types) re-declare them across core, control-plane, host and CLI. Endpoint macros hold authorization matrices, orchestration and DTO translation. Payload bounds are also set in two uncoordinated places: the fixed 16 KiB on the target endpoint and the unbounded payload builders on root. Two concrete defects come from this. First, root sends each Component Group member a single ConfigureRuntime carrying the whole group directory and the whole Fleet directory, but the managed canic_command traps on any payload over 16 KiB, from any caller. By my size estimate (not measured), groups of roughly 40 or more members can never publish their directories. Second, the ConfigureRuntime arm calls an admission open_fresh step after committing the runtime change. After any admission transition, that step fails on every replay, and the bootstrap-recovery path that replay is meant to provide is skipped. Everything else is maintainability debt with latent security or correctness risk. Root, Coordinator and Store command authorization uses non-exhaustive matches! lists, so a new variant fails open. A dead module-source resolver path remains wired through core ops. Caller authorization for capability envelopes happens inside workflow through implicit msg_caller reads. The layering guard covers only canic-core, so the control-plane, the host and a config-to-ops upward call are unchecked.

Strengths
  • The core layering is checked mechanically by scripts/ci/run-layering-guards.sh. It has self-test fixtures (docs/audits/fixtures/layering) and guards ops->policy, workflow->storage records, api->replay orchestration, model/domain/storage->dto and record re-exports.
  • domain/policy/pure is genuinely pure: no storage, ops, dto, serde, async or timer imports. Time is passed in as now_ns or now_secs (e.g. domain/policy/pure/fleet_funding/mod.rs, cycles_funding.rs).
  • DTOs are passive. The only functions in dto are const constructors, accessors and tests. No command or request DTO implements Default, and there are no boundary type aliases.
  • Host-only parsing and codegen dependencies are gated to non-wasm32 targets (crates/canic-core/Cargo.toml [target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'], bootstrap/mod.rs:7-16, config/mod.rs:15-16), and no canister or app manifest depends on host crates.
  • Workflow avoids partial commits where it matters: activate_with_runtime traps if runtime services cannot start after a committed activation (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/component_runtime.rs:299-305).
  • Root-side callers reconcile lost or failed target responses by re-querying target status before failing (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_registry/mod.rs:4610-4630).
  • Replay-policy manifests are cross-checked against the macro-declared command variants by tests that derive membership from source (crates/canic-core/src/replay_policy/tests/mod.rs:119-147), and the 16 KiB envelope for PrepareFleetAdmission is pinned by a test (canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_admission/mod.rs:411-418).
  • The host reuses canister policy and ops code instead of re-implementing it: cycles_funding policy in startup_funding, FleetRegistryOps for registry hashing, and canic_core::CANIC_WASM_CHUNK_BYTES for chunking. Each of these facts has a single authority.
Not covered

I did not audit the internal state machines of the 53k-line canic-control-plane ops tree, which has no policy layer of its own. So I could not say how much business decision logic sits in ops (component_registry/mod.rs alone is 6.5k lines). The host fleet_ensure workflow and ops internals, canic-backup and most CLI commands were checked only at the import and ownership level. I did not measure Candid-encoded sizes; the ConfigureRuntime size threshold is estimated by hand from the field layout. Wasm size was not measured: I did not quantify the cost of the dead resolver path or of serde_json in root. I did not verify the IC semantics of msg_caller in timer contexts. The docs and API lens (CLI help ordering, public facade surface) was not reviewed.

IC instruction-count and wasm-size efficiency (cross-cutting)

xc-efficiency5 medium9 low1 info

Canic's canister runtime is unusually bounds-conscious: almost every stable singleton carries an explicit encoded-byte bound (BoundedCell, impl_storable_bounded), timers retire state in fixed batches with exact deadlines, public metrics history, cascade reports and page requests are clamped, host-only TOML/YAML/codegen dependencies are target-gated out of wasm32, and the endpoint surface is consolidated into a few command/status enums, which keeps per-endpoint macro expansion and exported-method count small. Instruction cost and wasm size were clearly designed for, not left to chance. Most of the remaining risk comes from code that is correct but whose per-message cost grows with state and is paid on hot paths. Five patterns recur. (1) A whole-structure copy-on-write compare-and-swap: the complete record is exported or cloned, fully re-validated, and often re-hashed and deep-compared, then the entire CBOR value is rewritten on every step. This appears in the Fleet Coordinator registry and funding cells (bounded at 32 MiB each), the root provisioning journal (8.65 MB per operation), the application-session cell (8 MiB), and the FleetActivation record that endpoint preflight clones on every call. (2) Linear full-decode scans of stable BTreeMaps where an index or range lookup would do: every sharding assign exports all partition-key assignments, replay quotas and purges scan every receipt, the root operation-status lookup decodes the whole Component Registry entry map, and the log page and cycle top-up sequence scans do the same. (3) Payload bounds that do not match the transport. The 16 KiB canic_command cap limits how much Directory the root can ship, far below the configured fleet and group maxima, while 8 MiB plan bounds exceed the IC's roughly 2 MiB ingress and cross-subnet message limits. (4) inspect_message accepts ingress based only on payload size and decodability, so anonymous senders can make the root and Coordinator pay ingress and decode costs for multi-MB messages. (5) Every log! call writes to stable memory, with no level filter. None of these is a cycle-conservation or authority defect. The most important are the O(total assignments) sharding assign path, which traps at a few million users; the 16 KiB Directory ceiling, which wedges provisioning and directory synchronization as fleets or groups grow; and the O(N^2) or O(R^2) control-plane journals and funding validation. Numbers below are derived from the code's own bounds and typical wasm costs (roughly 20 to 60 instructions per byte for ciborium and Candid encode or decode and SHA-256). They are not measured.

Strengths
  • Singleton stable records use BoundedCell, which validates the encoded size before writing and serves reads from the cached value without decoding (crates/canic-core/src/cdk/bounded_cell/mod.rs:11-66); most maps use bounded Storable records (impl_storable_bounded).
  • Log age retention runs in fixed batches of 256, and the timer is rescheduled to the exact next deadline instead of polling (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/runtime/log.rs:21,105-173); cycle-tracker and top-up retention are likewise batched at 128 (workflow/runtime/cycles/mod.rs:63,786-788).
  • Public metrics history is capped at 256 series x 288 slots, accounted against an 8 MiB byte budget, projected without sorting, and paged per series (crates/canic-core/src/model/public_metrics/history/mod.rs:23-27,95-150).
  • State-cascade reports carry at most MAX_REPORTED_STATE_TARGETS target details, with explicit omitted counts, so recursive fan-out replies stay under the 16 KiB cascade bound (crates/canic-core/src/ops/cascade_report/mod.rs:22-25,80-107).
  • Host-only configuration parsing and code generation (toml, serde_path_to_error, quote, proc-macro2) are target-gated out of canister wasm (crates/canic-core/Cargo.toml [target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'], config/mod.rs:15-61, bootstrap/mod.rs:7-8), as AGENTS.md requires.
  • Role endpoints are consolidated into single command, observability and status enums (crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/role.rs:78-200,490-590), which reduces exported methods and per-endpoint wrapper monomorphization.
  • The raw update adapter rejects oversized payloads before decoding and sets a Candid skipping quota (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:335-372).
  • The intent store keeps dedicated pending and expiry index maps, so expiry work does not scan the intent records (crates/canic-core/src/storage/stable/intent.rs:83-128).
Not covered

No builds, benchmarks or PocketIC runs were done, so wasm sizes and instruction counts are estimates derived from code bounds, not measurements. Not reviewed in depth: blob-storage and billing paths, ICRC-21, the wasm-store chunk publication pipeline beyond its occupancy accounting, the ic-memory and ic-timers crates' internals (for example whether reconcile_schedule is a no-op when the deadline is unchanged), the costs of the delegated-token and canister-signature crypto paths (only noted that the positive cache in ops/auth/delegated/cache.rs cannot be populated by queries), root post-upgrade and bootstrap cost, and host-side performance (canic-cli, canic-host, canic-backup). Whether Candid decoding without a decoding_quota admits zero-sized-element vector bombs on specific DTOs was not verified per type.

Documentation and public API (cross-cutting)

xc-docs-api1 medium9 low1 info

This lens compared the user-facing documentation with the code: README.md, INSTALLING.md, CONFIG.md, TESTING.md, the getting-started guides, docs/features/**, the main docs/operations runbooks and the crate READMEs. The code checked includes the CLI help and dispatch in canic-cli (clap definitions, global-option handling, scaffold, app, build, fleet, cycles, token, backup, restore and network), the canic facade (lib.rs, prelude, api, access, start/finish macros) and the canic-macros endpoint DSL (parse, validate, expand). Overall the configuration reference is accurate: every default and bound I checked in CONFIG.md matches the schema code. The runbooks are careful and consistently tell operators to keep journals and never bypass typed blockers. The endpoint macro has strong secure-by-default rules: access must be explicit, negated identity predicates are rejected, and gated endpoints must be async and fallible. The main risks show up where the CLI help, the facade API and the ledger/cycles semantics meet. First, the `canic cycles transfer` and `canic token transfer` help examples show sending Cycles Ledger or ICP ledger funds to application canisters, or to `aaaaa-aa`. No Canic runtime code can spend those balances, and the Fleet's cycle accounting treats them as uncontrolled. Second, the recommended `canic::api::call::Call` builder merges every call failure into one public code. A clean reject therefore looks the same as an unknown outcome (SysUnknown) on bounded-wait calls, even with cycles attached, so downstream code cannot retry safely. Third, `canic backup prune` removes backup directories without checking the restore plan and journal stored inside them. It can therefore destroy an in-progress restore that is being stepped with `--max-steps`. Several documented workflows are broken but fail safely. The primary INSTALLING/walkthrough quickstart fails at `scaffold canister`. The getting-started and macro README examples use bare `#[canic_query]`/`#[canic_update]`, which the macro rejects. Several runbooks put `--environment` after the subcommand, which the CLI refuses. Smaller API footguns are listed individually: the undocumented `internal` marker removes the Fleet-state guard; `attested_local_subnet()` has no way to require a role; `RpcApi::request_cycles` has no retry identity; restore runs are not bound to an environment; and the network-enrollment docs compute the fingerprint from the file being enrolled.

Strengths
  • Endpoint macros cannot silently open access: they reject endpoints with neither requires(...) nor public (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/validate/mod.rs:73-82), not(...) around caller/auth predicates (84-89), gated endpoints that are not async or not Result-returning (59-71), and unknown predicate paths (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/parse/mod.rs:486-501).
  • Global option handling fails closed: a top-level --environment/--icp placed after the command is rejected with a clear message (crates/canic-cli/src/cli/globals.rs:66-84, crates/canic-cli/src/lib.rs:210-216), and conflicting environments are detected (globals.rs:133-146).
  • Network trust enrollment refuses mainnet, symlinked or non-regular key files and conflicting re-enrollment, and it is write-once (crates/canic-host/src/network/mod.rs:171-260).
  • `canic cycles topup` deliberately accepts only the Coordinator or an explicit current Root Principal (crates/canic-cli/src/cycles/wallet.rs:371-398, 689-695). This is the right model for native funding.
  • The config schema uses deny_unknown_fields throughout, and the CONFIG.md defaults (log limits, topup, cycles_funding, limits, scaling/sharding policy) match the code exactly (crates/canic-core/src/config/schema/log.rs:12-23, component_spec/mod.rs:17-58, 758-767, 845-846).
  • The operator runbooks consistently say to preserve journals and evidence and never to bypass typed blockers with raw commands (docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md:1592-1623, INSTALLING.md:196-201).
  • The frontend handoff requires an independently retained digest, and the SDK consumer never fetches a root key from the gateway (docs/features/operations/frontend-handoff.md:70-75, crates/canic-host/examples/frontend-consumer/handoff.mjs:41-74).
  • RpcApi::create_canister_request requires a caller-owned, durable, nonzero operation id and documents reusing it after uncertain results (crates/canic-core/src/api/rpc/mod.rs:60-77).
Not covered

I did not check every command and flag in the 1716-line docs/features/operations/fleet-ensure.md or every docs/operations runbook; I sampled the command lines and verified them against the clap definitions. I could not verify icp-cli's behaviour when `-e` is omitted, because its source is not in the workspace. I did not review docs/contracts/* in depth (only ACCESS_ARCHITECTURE.md), docs/design, docs/architecture beyond the operator walkthrough, the CHANGELOG, docs/status, the canic::testing API, the stable-memory macros or the blob-storage billing API docs. Rendered clap help was checked from source only; nothing was built or run. cargo audit belongs to another unit.

Cycle conservation and paid effects (cross-cutting)

xc-cycles2 high5 medium

Only a few canister paths move cycles, and each has a guard. A root grants cycles to a child with a management deposit_cycles call behind a replay receipt and a cost-guard permit (nonroot_cycles.rs). The Coordinator attaches grants to a Root AcceptFunding command, and the Root accepts the exact amount synchronously and writes a receipt without awaiting (root_funding/mod.rs). The root refills its canister pool through Cycles Ledger create_canister, deduplicated by created_at_time. Automatic and manual ICP refill runs an ICP Ledger transfer, then CMC notify_top_up, from a durable operation record. Wasm Store and Root deletion reclaim native cycles to the parent before stop and delete, and keep only a freezing reserve plus reviewed headroom. Root, and separately the Coordinator, evacuate their Cycles Ledger accounts with an exact transfer intent. On the host side, fleet ensure uses withdraw, create_canister and icrc1_transfer with created_at_time deduplication, treats native balances as open to donations, and refuses to delete a canister holding material cycles. The arithmetic is checked, Nat values convert with overflow checks, and the Cycles parser is exact. The main risks sit where durable evidence is frozen and later compared against balances that other parties can change or that change over time. Store deletion, Root deletion preparation, Root Cycles Ledger evacuation and Coordinator retirement all store an observed balance, fee or created_at_time once and then fail with a conflict forever if the live value differs. There is no path to observe again or sweep the remainder, and anyone can deposit cycles or ledger credit to a known principal. Root retirement never evacuates the root's ICP Ledger account at all, and the ICP refill policy deliberately keeps an ICP floor there, so deleting a root destroys that ICP. The Coordinator's grant call is the only cycle-bearing inter-canister call that uses bounded wait (the blob Cashier top-up in canic-core is the other one). Under SYS_UNKNOWN the attached cycles can be lost, and the design assumes they are refunded. Lower-severity risks are about classification and liveness. The Coordinator treats every typed Root error as a terminal RootRejected, even though the Root checks authority before it looks up an earlier receipt. If an earlier grant was accepted but never acknowledged, this can leave the two journals disagreeing permanently. Pool refill checks a pending creation against fees it has just recomputed, so a Cycles Ledger or subnet fee change leaves an uncertain creation that can never be reconciled. ICP refill counts transport failures toward five notify attempts, then gives up terminally while the ICP sits at the CMC. Overall quality is high: journalling happens before effects, retries are deduplicated, and typed errors are used throughout. The defects cluster around edge-of-lifecycle conservation, not everyday funding.

Strengths
  • Root attached-cycle acceptance is atomic: it checks that msg_cycles_available equals the grant, accepts exactly that amount, traps if the receipt write fails, and a replay accepts zero so the Coordinator is refunded (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:189-216; ops/root_funding/mod.rs:381-413).
  • Child grants record intent before the effect: the cost-guard permit and the replay effect marker are written before deposit_cycles, the budget ledger snapshot is restored if the call is rejected, and competing pending operations for the same child are blocked (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:382-445).
  • Ledger effects are deduplicated with created_at_time and a memo, and Duplicate replies are handled: pool creation (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/refill.rs:193-211), ICP refill transfer (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/execution.rs:365-381), Root and Coordinator evacuation (root_ledger_retirement/mod.rs:66-70), and host withdraw, create and transfer (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs:2779-2835, 5490-5514).
  • Store deletion returns excess cycles to root before stopping it, keeps only a freezing reserve derived from status plus a named execution reserve, rejects reserved cycles, and treats deletion as done only when the canister is observed absent (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs:866-898, 1019-1078).
  • Arithmetic and conversions fail closed: Nat to u128/u64 conversions report overflow (crates/canic-core/src/infra/ic/mgmt/cycles.rs:50-55; infra/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:253-264; infra/ic/icp_refill.rs:285-289), freezing-reserve maths is checked (gc.rs:883-897), and the Cycles parser rejects sub-cycle precision (crates/canic-core/src/cdk/types/cycles.rs:263-346).
  • Every other cycle-bearing management and ledger call uses unbounded wait (deposit_cycles in infra/ic/mgmt/cycles.rs:43, sign_with_ecdsa in infra/ic/mgmt/signing.rs:40, and all ICP Ledger and CMC calls in infra/ic/icp_refill.rs:312-371).
  • Host conservation accounting explicitly allows third-party donations and computes net debit and credit against reviewed bounds; retirement drains to the reviewed treasury and deletes only when the remaining balance is at or below the material threshold (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/mod.rs:3546, 3696-3707; policy/mod.rs:1886-1956; ops/platform.rs:4867-4891).
  • Cost-guard permits limit quota and native reservations for value transfers, and the permit type is required at the ops boundary for paid calls (crates/canic-core/src/ops/cost_guard.rs:183-229; ops/ic/cycles_ledger.rs:31-54; ops/ic/mgmt/cycles.rs:17-31).
Not covered

I did not trace these in depth: - Host operator-mint receipt and certificate verification (ops/operator_mint/receipts/**). - Host completed_reset, reinstall adoption, terminal inventory custody and ledger evidence, and capacity-import transport. - Component provisioning claim and install paths that consume pool assets. - Fixture store, and the blob-storage Cashier protocol semantics. - The canic-backup crate (it moves no cycles). The claim that attached cycles can be lost on a bounded-wait SYS_UNKNOWN comes from IC platform documentation as I recall it; I could not check it against the spec text in this environment. The realistic frequency of CMC `Other` responses and of Cycles Ledger or subnet fee changes is inferred, not measured. No tests were run; the review was read-only as required.

IC async interleaving, lost responses and retries (cross-cutting)

xc-async3 high4 medium

Canic's canister-side async design is unusually deliberate. Root RPC capabilities reserve a durable replay receipt and switch it to ExternalEffectInFlight before any effectful await. Aborts only remove receipts that are still Reserved. Value transfers go through cost-guard permits whose settlement identity is persisted. Ledger and Cycles Ledger effects are deduplicated with created_at_time and memo. Timer work is serialized by durable leases, and a watchdog takes over leases that expire. Transient in-memory locks are Drop-based. Most workflows re-read durable state after each await and fail closed on mismatch. Explicit TOCTOU bugs (state checked before an await and trusted after it) were rare in the code I read. The main risks are in the recovery layer that sits on top of these journals. (1) Retry classifiers disagree with the error mapping. Every local transport failure (reject or perform failure) becomes internal code PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE, but the classifiers for cycle top-up, pool maintenance, auth renewal and placement acknowledgement retry only on PLATFORM_FAILED or STATE_FAILED. One transient reject therefore permanently stops funding, maintenance or renewal. (2) Some journal states have no exit. A clean deposit_cycles failure leaves a RequestCycles receipt in RecoveryRequired. That receipt never expires, is never reconciled, and blocks all further funding for that child. (3) Root removal is gated on exact, immutable balance snapshots and on retry identities that include live canister_status readings. A third-party cycle deposit, or ordinary drift in those readings, turns an expected retry into a permanent conflict. (4) Almost every private lifecycle driver retries at a fixed 0–1 s with no backoff and no permanent/transient split. A permanent error therefore becomes an endless paid retry loop that also blocks authority snapshots. (5) Cycles are attached to bounded-wait calls in two places. (6) Pool asset resets have two unsynchronized executors: the removal driver and the maintenance timer. Overall quality is high, and the intent-before-effect discipline is real. The defects are liveness and conservation problems that show up on ordinary failure paths and interleavings, not missing journals. Several of them chain across canisters: a Root top-up stops, the Coordinator grant stays unresolved, and Coordinator rotation and snapshots are blocked.

Strengths
  • Replay receipts are marked ExternalEffectInFlight before effectful awaits and are never expired or aborted from that state; abort only removes Reserved receipts (crates/canic-core/src/ops/replay/receipt.rs:474-480,546-548; crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/execute.rs:117-121).
  • Transient in-memory exclusion uses Drop guards that release on trap/cleanup (crates/canic-core/src/ops/blob_storage/funding.rs:58-62; crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/transient/capacity_import/mod.rs:22-34; crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/runtime/template/publication/lifecycle/gc.rs:124-150).
  • Ledger effects carry created_at_time + memo and handle Duplicate/TooOld explicitly, making lost-response retries effect-free (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/execution.rs:186-240,346-370; crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/refill.rs:176-212,327-341).
  • Root funding acceptance is synchronous accept-exact-or-replay-zero, so Coordinator reconcile retries cannot double-grant (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:193-219).
  • Post-await re-validation is thorough in fixture import and Store GC (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/fixture_provisioning/mod.rs:104-114; gc.rs:168-190) and mirror activation re-reads current state before commit (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/fleet_registry_mirror/mod.rs:262-280).
  • Cycle top-up attempts keep a replay-safe operation generation across lease takeover and retryable failure (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/async_job_recovery/mod.rs:305-370).
  • Pool creation fences stale attempts by persisted cost-guard settlement identity (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/canister_pool/mod.rs:607-639,774-790).
  • The Root component-provisioning driver persists failure/backoff, preserves review-required fences, and is resumed after restart (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/component_provisioning.rs:176-186,300-360).
Not covered

Host-side concurrency was only surveyed. That covers two operators running fleet ensure or backup on different machines; per-workspace file locks exist in crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/mod.rs:685-740. canic-backup restore interleaving, the auth prepare/attestation replay flows, the wasm_store endpoint macros, and most of the 6.5k-line component_registry workflow and ops were not traced end to end; I spot-checked delete, removal, draining and recycle paths. No code was executed. Timing claims were not reproduced dynamically: the probability of idle-burn drift, stop_canister durations, and race windows are all estimates. IC best-effort semantics were applied from platform knowledge, specifically that refunds carried in a dropped or timed-out bounded-wait response are not guaranteed to return. Trap reachability after awaits (instruction limits, expect sites) was not audited per path.

Strengths

  • Intent before effect is consistent across canister and host code. Root capability handlers mark the replay receipt ExternalEffectInFlight with its cost-guard settlement ids before the await (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/rpc/request/handler/nonroot_cycles.rs:418-424, crates/canic-core/src/ops/replay/receipt.rs), fleet ensure persists each Intent before observing or issuing (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/workflow/mod.rs:1486-1495), and the restore runner claims each operation Pending and records the target's snapshot inventory before the command runs (crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/execute.rs:210-222).
  • Root accepts Coordinator grants atomically. Validation, msg_cycles_accept and the receipt commit run in one message with no await, a failed commit traps so the cycles are refunded, and a replay accepts zero (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/root_funding/mod.rs:189-222).
  • Ledger effects are deduplicated with a fixed created_at_time (with a memo in ICP refill and pool refill), and Duplicate replies are adopted as receipts, in ICP refill (crates/canic-core/src/workflow/ic/icp_refill/execution.rs), pool refill (crates/canic-control-plane/src/workflow/canister_pool/refill.rs:193-211) and every host Cycles Ledger effect (crates/canic-host/src/fleet_ensure/ops/platform.rs). The management-canister and ledger adapters in canic-core use unbounded wait (crates/canic-core/src/infra/ic/mgmt/cycles.rs:43, infra/ic/mgmt/lifecycle.rs).
  • State machines commit by compare-and-swap against the exact prior record, and Component Registry ops transitions are synchronous, so no await splits a transition (crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/component_registry/mod.rs, crates/canic-control-plane/src/storage/stable/fleet_coordinator/mod.rs:810-829). Intent-store mutations finish every check and compute new totals before touching storage (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/intent/mod.rs:400-878).
  • The delegated-auth chain is complete and fails closed. Encoding is length-prefixed and domain-separated, Merkle leaves and nodes are separated, the root proof pins the key, key id, derivation hash and key version and rejects high-s signatures, and verification requires presenter, subject and transport caller to be equal (crates/canic-core/src/ops/auth/delegated/canonical.rs, chain_key.rs, verify.rs:203-290). No reviewer found a way to forge a token, and the session probe found that caller and subject cannot diverge.
  • Endpoint access is secure by default. Every endpoint must declare public or requires(...), not(...) cannot wrap identity predicates, the raw adapter checks the argument size before decoding, and every Root, Store and Coordinator command variant is authorized before any effect (crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/validate/mod.rs:70-89, crates/canic-macros/src/endpoint/expand/mod.rs:364-376, crates/canic/src/macros/endpoints/root.rs:222-397). The Fleet activation fence is injected unconditionally and its allowlists match exact name and call kind (crates/canic-core/src/domain/policy/pure/fleet_activation.rs:32-115).
  • Configuration is parsed on the host only. TOML and YAML parsers are target-gated out of canister Wasm, every schema struct uses deny_unknown_fields, cycle amounts parse exactly with typed overflow and sub-cycle errors (crates/canic-core/src/cdk/types/cycles.rs:127-351), and the topology, group and deployment projections are length-prefixed, domain-separated and hashed.
  • Stable memory and the reinstall-only policy are enforced in code. crates/canic-core/src/memory/policy.rs pins key namespaces to memory-ID ranges, BoundedCell validates the full encoding before a write, managed and Root post_upgrade reject a different release-build ID (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/fleet_activation/mod.rs:210-222), and a sealed Root or Coordinator loaded from a snapshot can never resume (crates/canic-core/src/ops/storage/authority_restore/mod.rs:67-91). scripts/ci/check-pre-1-0-hard-cut.sh keeps every product schema at v1.
  • Panic and overflow hygiene holds. A survey of about 1,500 unwrap, expect, cast and unchecked-operator sites across canic, canic-core, canic-control-plane, canic-macros, canic-host, canic-cli and canic-backup found no caller-reachable overflow, truncating conversion or panic on paths that move cycles or ICP, and Nat conversions are fallible throughout.
  • Host file durability is careful. durable_io writes a sibling temp with O_EXCL, syncs it, renames with no-replace and syncs the parent (crates/canic-host/src/durable_io/mod.rs:421-512). Backup locks reject symlinks and use flock, the command-lifetime lock proves child processes have exited, and restore staging hashes the exact bytes it copies (crates/canic-backup/src/persistence/command_lifetime_lock/mod.rs:71-90, crates/canic-backup/src/restore/runner/artifact.rs:89-158). The crash-barrier tests are thorough.
  • The release trust chain is bound to bytes. Release-set documents are create-new and must re-serialize to identical canonical JSON, artifact evidence is derived from the Wasm itself, and Binaryen is pinned by both archive and executable SHA-256 (crates/canic-host/src/release_set/application/persistence/mod.rs:403-412, crates/canic-host/src/binaryen/mod.rs:348-395). CI Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and every downloaded tool is checked against a digest (scripts/ci/check-release-integrity-contract.sh).
  • Host and canister wire contracts agree. The second-round probe compared about 45 hand-written Candid envelopes in canic-host and canic-cli with the macro unions and found variant names, routing and payload types consistent apart from one Result-wrapping drift in `canic cycles funding`. Coordinator provisioning hops use unbounded wait with no attached cycles, and member allocation identities are deterministic (crates/canic-control-plane/src/ops/component_provisioning/mod.rs:250-265).

Method and limits

Round one split the workspace into 31 subsystem areas and 8 cross-cutting lenses: security, contract conformance, panics and overflow, architecture and layering, IC instruction count and wasm size, documentation and API, cycle conservation, and async interleaving. Each reviewer read the code statically, with no edits and no builds, and reported findings with a file and line, evidence, a concrete failure scenario and a recommendation. Round-one reviewers reported reading 2,447 files.

Every critical, high and medium finding then went to an adversarial verifier told to refute it. Critical and high findings went one at a time, mediums in batches of up to three from the same area. Critical and high findings that survived went to two more skeptics with fresh context. One traced reachability from a real entry point (an endpoint, timer, callback or CLI command). The other checked intent against AGENTS.md, the contracts and the current designs. Verified means a finding survived all three. Low and info findings were not verified and are marked unverified. Verifiers refuted 8 findings. Across verification and the skeptic checks, 53 severities were lowered and 2 raised. None of the 104 skeptic checks refuted a finding outright.

A completeness critic then named the ten areas round one had covered least, mostly multi-hop protocols no single area owned. Round two probed each of them with the same verification, and those findings carry ids starting r2-. A dedup pass merged 67 duplicate reports into 44 primary findings.

Finally, 28 findings were retested. They were chosen by severity and by whether a native test could reach the defect. For each one, a focused test asserting the correct behaviour was written in its own throwaway git worktree and run with cargo against commit 06d73694d. Only the named tests ran, never the full suite, and the main checkout was never touched. Every worktree carried a one-line cast in crates/canic-host/src/durable_io/mod.rs, because canic-host does not compile on macOS at this commit (repro-build-1).

The reproduction pass also checks the static review. Of 28 findings retested, 27 reproduced in full or in part and none were disproved. That suggests the verified findings that were not retested are also reliable, though each still deserves its own test before it is fixed.

Limits: nothing was measured on the Internet Computer, so instruction and cycle figures in findings are estimates from reading code. No PocketIC test was run. Inter-canister awaits, real ic-timers behaviour and management-canister effects were exercised only where a native seam exists, and partial outcomes mark where that stopped. The dependency advisory scan (cargo audit) found no vulnerabilities and two unmaintained crates.
